name: Sparse encrusting community on Atlanto-Arctic upper bathyal coarse sediment
description: This broad community includes all biotopes that are characterised by encrusting species including deep-sea sponges, serpulid worms, cup corals and Anoniimid bivalves. Associated species can include squat lobsters, holothurians and ophiuroids. This community is widespread and occurs on coarse sediment and rock where erect coral species are absent. The species composition of the biotopes belonging to this broad community will vary with depth and location, and associated species will vary with sediment type.

source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Serpula vermicularis reefs on very sheltered circalittoral muddy sand
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Mytilus edulis beds in variable salinity infralittoral mixed sediment
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Sheltered Modiolus (horse-mussel) beds
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Modiolus modiolus beds with hydroids and red seaweeds on tide-swept circalittoral mixed substrata
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Modiolus modiolus beds on circalittoral mixed sediment
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Modiolus modiolus beds with fine hydroids and large solitary ascidians on very sheltered circalittoral mixed substrata
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Modiolus modiolus beds with Chlamys varia, sponges, hydroids and bryozoans on slightly tide-swept very sheltered circalittoral mixed substrata
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Lophelia reefs
source: JNCC, 2026. Marine habitat correlation tables v2026.02, sheet 'Correlation Data', columns 'JNCCv9706 Codes / Names / Levels'

name: Coastal and halophytic communities
description: Oceanic, inshore and offshore waters and their open-water and bottom communities; marine communities of the littoral zone and of coastal lagoons, bays, inlets, estuaries and tidal rivers; coastal and azonal interior halophyte or gypsophyte communities of saltmarshes, salt steppes, salt scrubs and gypsum scrubs; coastal sand dunes, sand beaches, shingle beaches, sea cliffs, rocky shores, coastal islets, rock stacks, reefs, banks and shoals; characteristically coastal agrosystems incorporating seminatural elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ocean and seas, marine communities
description: Oceanic and continental shelf waters of the world ocean and its connected seas, their associated open-water and bottom communities, and marine vascular vegetation beds; marine communities of the littoral zone and of coastal lagoons. Included within the Palaearctic realm are the waters of the Northeast Atlantic, of the northern part of the West African Atlantic, south to the latitude of the Cape Verde Islands, of the Arabian Sea and of the eastern and northern Red Sea, of the Mediterranean, of the Baltic Sea, of the Arctic Ocean east of Greenland and west of the Bering Strait, and of the northwest Pacific (Marine Region as used by the IUCN Commission on National Parks and Protected Areas, Kelleher & al., 1995: ii).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Open marine waters
description: Pelagic biocoenoses of the world ocean, its connected seas and coastal lagoons. They can be characterized by their planktonic communities and by the composition of their nektonic or surface-feeding faunas of cephalopods, fish, sea mammals and seabirds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oceanic waters
description: Waters beyond the continental shelf. In the Palaearctic region they occupy the greatest part of the Arctic, Atlantic and Pacific oceans, of the Barents Sea,  the Sea of Okhotsk, the Sea of Japan, the Arabian Sea, the Mediterranean Sea, the Ligurian Sea, the Tyrrhenian Sea, the Ionian Sea, as well as the central part of the Aegean Sea, the Red Sea, the Black Sea, the southern Adriatic Sea, the eastern part of the northern North Sea, the southern Bering Sea. They are absent from the Baltic Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Blue ocean waters
description: Oceanic waters of tropical and subtropical regions, generally of low productivity and high species diversity. In the Palaearctic, they include oceanic waters of the Atlantic north to about 40øN latitude, of the Mediterreanean, the Black Sea, the Red Sea, the Arabian Sea, the Pacific north to about 32øN latitude.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cool ocean waters
description: Oceanic waters of boreal, subarctic and arctic regions. In the Palaearctic, they include oceanic waters of the Arctic Ocean and its satellite seas, of the  Atlantic south to about 40øN latitude, of the North Sea, the Bering Sea, the Sea of Okhotsk, the Sea of Japan, of the Pacific south to about 32øN latitude.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ocean upwellings
description: Oceanic areas over which the warmer surface water is displaced, allowing cooler water rich in nutrients to rise to the surface. They are characterized by higher biological productivity and lower diversity.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shelf and slope waters
description: Waters of the continental shelf, underwater plateau extending from the coast to a depth of about 100 fathoms, beyond which the continental slope falls steeply toward the ocean bottom.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inshore waters
description: Waters within the strong influence of land masses, both in terms of physical parameters and of fauna, often arbitrarily defined as waters less than 5 km from low water mark, waters between the continent and islands or islets well in sight of shore, and any seas of depth less than 6 metres. They include the inshore waters of the Eurasian and African continents and their nearshore islands, south to Mauritania in the Atlantic, Egypt in the Red Sea, the Arabian peninsula and Iran in the Indian Ocean, China in the Pacific, and of Greenland, Iceland, the Azores, the Madeiran archipelago, the Canaries, the Cape Verde Islands, Soccotra, the Bonin, Volcano and Marcus islands, the Commander Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Offshore waters
description: Waters of the continental shelf comprised between the limits of inshore waters and the continental slope.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High Arctic offshore waters
description: Continental shelf waters of the high Arctic zone, bordering middle and northern Greenland, Spitzbergen, Franz Josef Land, Novaya Zemlya, Severnaya Zemlya, the New Siberian Islands, Wrangel Island and the nothern Siberian mainland from the north coast of the Yamal peninsula eastwards.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low Arctic offshore waters
description: Continental shelf waters of the low Arctic zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic low Arctic offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the low Arctic region of the North Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean, off southern Greenland, Iceland, Jan Mayen, Bear Island, northern Scandinavia, northwestern mainland Russia, southern and middle Novaya Zemlya.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific low Arctic offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the Chukchi Sea, the Bering Strait, the Bering Sea, the Commander Islands, Kamchatka, the northern and central Kuriles, the Sea of Okhotsk and the Tatar Straits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal offshore waters
description:
Continental shelf waters of the boreal (temperate, subarctic) maritime zone of the Atlantic, including the North Sea, the Baltic, the English Channel, the Irish Sea, the Bay of Biscay, bordering the coasts of Scandinavia south of the Arctic Circle, those of the Faeroes, of the British Isles and of their outlying archipelagoes, and those of mainland Europe south to Galicia, and of 
the Pacific, bordering the coasts of the southern Kuriles, Honshu, Hokkaido, Shikoku and continental Korea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Atlantic offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the Atlantic temperate region, including the North Sea, the English Channel, the Irish Sea and the Bay of Biscay, bordering the coasts of Scandinavia south of the Arctic Circle, those of the Faeroes, of the British Isles and of their outlying archipelagoes, and those of mainland Europe south to Galicia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the Baltic Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Pacific offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the southern Kuriles, Honshu, Hokkaido, Shikoku and continental Korea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical offshore waters
description: Continental shelf waters of the subtropical maritime zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical Atlantic offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the subtropical zone of the Atlantic, bordering the Canary Islands, Madeira, the Azores, the Mediterraneo-Atlantic coasts of Iberia, the Mediterraneo-Atlantic and Saharo-Atlantic coasts of Africa, south to Cap Blanc.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the Mediterranean Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Black Sea offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the Black Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical Pacific offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of peninsular Korea, the Yellow Sea, the East China Sea, Kyushu, the Ryukyu Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical offshore waters
description: Continental shelf waters of the tropical zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical Atlantic offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the tropical zone of the Atlantic, bordering the Cape Verde Islands and the southern coast of Mauritania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical western Indo-Pacific offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the tropical Indian Ocean and its connected seas, comprising, in the Palaearctic region as here defined, those of the northern Red Sea, of the continental shelf of Asia in the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden,  the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Oman, the Persian Gulf, and of the African continental shelf around Socotra.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical central Indo-Pacific offshore waters
description: Offshore waters of the Asian continental shelf in the northern South China Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental slope
description: Waters situated over the continental slope, the steep descent from the continental shelf to the ocean bottom, an area where upwellings, water mixing or shearing and other anomalies often develop.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Offshore and coastal upwellings
description: Zones of the continental shelf where the warmer surface water is displaced, allowing cooler water rich in nutrients to rise to the surface, often generating much increased biological productivity.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Major offshore and coastal upwellings
description: Coastal and offshore waters of the major upwelling areas of the world ocean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwest African upwelling zone
description: Waters of the continental shelf off the desert and tropical coasts of northwest Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arabian upwelling zone
description: Waters of the continental shelf of the southern Arabian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Minor offshore and coastal upwellings
description: Waters of the continental shelf in which local upwelling conditions are generated by features of the sea floor or the circulation of water masses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shoals
description: Shallow waters over permanently submerged elevated features of the continental shelf sea-floor, whether shoals, banks or reefs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Benthic communities
description: Communities of marine animals and algae occupying the sea floor. Included are all communities of animals and algae of the infralittoral, circalittoral and deeper zones, situated below the level of average low spring tides, or of regular emergence through wind or atmospheric pressure variations. Also  included are communities of marine animals and algae occupying the mediolittoral zone, comprised between the low and high tide levels of average spring tides or within the regular range of wind or atmospheric pressure induced sea-level fluctuations, as well as marine assemblies installed in the supralittoral zone, reached only by spray, exceptional waves or exceptional high tides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Deep sea floor
description: Bathyal, abyssal, hadal and hydro-thermal benthic communities of the continental slope, the abyssal plain and its features.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bathyal benthic communities
description: Benthic communities of the continental slope, developed on blue, coral, green or red oceanic muds, and of relatively high diversity.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Abyssal benthic communities
description: Benthic communities of abyssal plains and abyssal hills, large relatively level areas of the deep ocean floor, covered by thin layers of biogenic or nonbiogenic oozes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hadal benthic communities
description: Benthic communities of the oceanic trenches, deep elongated subduction troughs of the ocean floor.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oceanic ridge benthic communities
description: Benthic communities occupying raised features of the deep sea-floor; they include assemblages colonizing active or nonactive constructive midocean ridges, as well as those developed on asismic ridges, but with the exception of hydrothermal communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hydrothermal benthic communities
description: Highly distinctive benthic communities inhabiting the vicinity of oceanic hydrothermal vents, mostly localized along the central rift of the mid-oceanic ridges and along submerged volcanic chains of lesser ocean basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic hydrothermal benthic communities
description: Hydrothermal vent communities of the Central Atlantic Ridge, highly distinctive from those of other known ridges, distributed in widely separated areas strewn along the ridge from Iceland (Reykjanes Ridge) to the Azores and the Kane fracture zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Red Sea-Indian Ocean hydrothermal benthic communities
description: Hydrothermal vent communities of the Indian Ocean Ridge, represented within the Palaearctic region as here defined, in the Red Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pacific hydrothermal benthic communities
description: Hydrothermal vent communities of the Marianas-Japan Ridge, represented in the Palaearctic region, as here defined, along the extreme southeastern boundaries.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic hydrothermal vent communities
description: Hydrothermal vent communities of the Nansen-Gakkel, Knepivich and Mohns ridges, extending in Arctic seas from the Kolbeinsey Ridge, at the northern margin of Iceland to the Laptev Shelf, separated from the Central Atlantic Ridge communities by the Iceland-Greenland and Iceland-Scotland sills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cold-seep benthic communities
description: Highly distinctive benthic communities of large bivalves, sponges and bryozoans, inhabiting the vicinity of oceanic methane-laden seeps, mostly localized in subduction trenches.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sublittoral soft seabeds
description: Mostly animal communities colonizing soft sediments such as mud, sand or gravel of the infralittoral and circalittoral zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sublittoral pebbly seabeds
description: Communities of mostly annual algae and invertebrates developing on pebble deposits of the infralittoral and circalittoral zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sublittoral rocky seabeds and kelp forests
description: Varied, strongly stratified communities colonizing underwater cliffs, reefs and rocky continental shelf seabeds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sublittoral organogenic concretions
description: Continental shelf colonies of lower plants or animals resulting in concretions and encrustations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corallogenic concretions
description: Communities forming and colonizing corallogenic concretions of calcified red algae in the circalittoral zone of the Mediterranean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Encrusting algae pavements
description: Mediterranean communities associated with mediolittoral pavements of encrusting algae ([Lithospermum tortuosum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gastropod and polychaete ledges
description: Infralittoral ledges built by gastropods or polychaetes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mussel beds
description: Communities of Atlantic, Baltic and Mediterranean mussel beds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gas vent communities
description: Communities of bacteria and invertebrates colonizing the vicinity of hot or cold gas seeps of the continental shelf, often forming encrusted tubes or chimneys.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coral reefs
description: Infralittoral communities of coral reefs of the Red Sea, the Arabian Sea, the Persian Gulf, the South China Sea and the East China Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Indian Ocean coral reefs
description: Infralittoral communities of coral reefs of the Red Sea, the Arabian Sea and the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Pacific coral reefs
description: Infralittoral communities of coral reefs of the South China Sea and the East China Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sublittoral cave communities
description: Communities of marine invertebrates and algae colonizing the bottom and sides of caves (unit 12.7) situated under the sea or the sublittoral part of caves having an entirely, periodically or partly submerged opening.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Soft sediment littoral communities
description: Invertebrate and algal communities colonizing soft sediments such as mud, sand or gravel of the intertidal zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pebbly shore littoral communities
description: Communities of mostly annual algae and invertebrates developing on pebble deposits of the intertidal zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rocky shore littoral communities
description: Communities of algae, invertebrates and lichens colonizing the mediolittoral and supralittoral zones of rocky shores and cliffs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediolittoral fringe rocks
description: Cliffs and rocks of the lowest part of the mediolittoral zone, occupied by communities transitional to those of the infralittoral zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lower mediolittoral rocks
description: Cliffs and rocks of the lower part of the mediolittoral zone, occupied, in particular, by encrusting algae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Upper mediolittoral rocks
description: Cliffs and rocks of the higher part of the mediolittoral zone, occupied by communities characterized, in particular, by cirriped crustaceans and soft algae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediolittoral cave and overhang communities
description: Communities of marine animals and lower plants colonizing mediolittoral overhangs and crevices, and the mediolittoral level of sea-caves (unit 12.7).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediolittoral rock pools
description: Permanent saline pools of the mediolittoral zone, fed by flood tides (tide pools).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supralittoral rocks
description: Cliffs and rocks of the supralittoral spray zone, mostly occupied by lichens such as [Verrucaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supralittoral rock pools
description: Pools of the supralittoral spray zone, of variable salinity, fed by rainwater, spray and occasionally waves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Littoral communities of organogenic concretions
description: Littoral colonies of lower plants or animals resulting in concretions and encrustations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea-grass meadows
description: Beds of submerged marine vascular vegetation of the oceans, seas and coastal lagoons, except those of brackish seas and lagoons.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic eelgrass meadows
description: Eelgrass beds dominated by [Zostera marina], established between the base of the intertidal zone and a depth of about 10 metres in Palaearctic waters of the Atlantic, the North Sea, the Baltic and adjacent seas of the northern basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Atlantic eelgrass meadows
description: [Zostera marina]-dominated eelgrass beds of eastern Atlantic, North Sea, Irish Sea, Norway Sea and Baltic coasts of the Eurasian mainland and its continental shelf islands, north to the Faeroe Islands and northwestern Finmark.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Barents-White Sea eelgrass meadows
description: Isolated [Zostera marina]-dominated eelgrass beds of Barents Sea and White Sea coasts of northeastern Finmark and Karelia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic eelgrass meadows
description: [Zostera marina]-dominated eelgrass beds of Iceland, distributed in the western gulfs and in scattered fjords of the northwestern, northeastern and southeastern coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland eelgrass meadows
description: [Zostera marina]-dominated eelgrass beds of southwestern Greenland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic dwarf eelgrass meadows
description: Eelgrass beds dominated by [Zostera noltii] or [Zostera angustifolia], mostly characteristic of the low part of the intertidal zone in Atlantic, North Sea and Baltic waters, sometimes permanently submerged.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mainland Atlantic dwarf eelgrass meadows
description: Formations of [Zostera noltii] or [Zostera angustifolia] of the Atlantic, North Sea and Baltic shores of continental Europe and of its continental shelf islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian dwarf eelgrass meadows
description: Very local [Zostera noltii] formations of Fuerteventura and Lanzarote.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: African Atlantic dwarf eelgrass meadows
description: Formations of [Zostera noltii] of the subtropical Atlantic shores of northwest Africa, south to Cap Blanc.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Pontic [Cymodocea] and [Zostera] beds
description: Beds of [Cymodocea nodosa], [Zostera noltii] or [Zostera marina] [s.l.] of the Mediterranean and the Black Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Cymodocea] beds
description: [Cymodocea nodosa] formations of the Mediterranean, permanently submerged in waters down to 10 metres deep, often in sheltered areas behind [Posidonia] reefs, monospecific or associated with either the alga [Caulerpa prolifera] or the phanerogam [Halophila stipulacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Zostera] beds
description: Formations of [Zostera noltii] or [Zostera maritima] [s.l.] of the Mediterranean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean dwarf eelgrass beds
description: Usually sparse meadows formed, on muddy sands of the upper part of the infralittoral zone of Mediterranean coasts, by [Zostera noltii] and the alga [Giraudya sphacelarioides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean eelgrass beds
description: Formations of the Mediterranean endemic [Zostera hornemanniana], vicariant of [Zostera marina], often confined to coastal lagoons, recorded also from the Istrio-Dalmatian archipelago.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic [Zostera] meadows
description: [Zostera marina] and [Zostera noltii] formations of Black Sea shores, particularly luxuriant in the limans of the northern Black Sea and the Azov Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Posidonia] beds
description: Beds of the Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic endemic, [Posidonia oceanica], permanently submerged in waters down to 100 metres deep.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermo-Atlantic [Cymodocea] beds
description: Formations of [Cymodocea nodosa] of the Atlantic shores of southern Iberia, northwestern Africa and the Macaronesian Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian [Cymodocea] beds
description: Formations of [Cymodocea nodosa] or [Cymodocea] and [Caulerpa spp.], in particular [Caulerpa prolifera], occupying large surfaces, on sandy substrates at depths of 1-15 metres, around the Macaronesian Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lusitanian [Cymodocea] beds
description: Formations of [Cymodocea nodosa] of the southernmost Atlantic coasts of the Iberian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: African Atlantic [Cymodocea] beds
description: Formations of [Cymodocea nodosa] of the shores of northwestern Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate [Halophila] and [Thalassia] beds
description: Deep water colonies of [Halophila spp.] or [Thalassia spp.] of the Mediterranean and the Macaronesian Atlantic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian [Halophila] beds
description: [Halophila decipiens] colonies of Tenerife, at depths between 10 and 14 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Halophila] beds
description: Colonies of [Halophila stipulacea] invading the Mediterranean as a result of the opening of the Suez Canal; they have been reported from continental Greece, the Cyclades, Crete, Rhodes, Samos, the Maltese Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Pacific [Zostera] meadows
description: [Zostera marina], [Zostera caespitosa], [Zostera asiatica], [Zostera caulescens], [Zostera japonica] beds of the shores of the Kamchatka Basin, the Sea of Okhotsk, the Japan Sea, the Yellow Sea, the East China Sea and the low Arctic, boreal and subtropical Pacific.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Phyllospadix] beds
description: [Phyllospadix iwatensis] or [Phyllospadix japonicus] sea-grass meadows of the temperate Pacific and its connected seas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical sea-grass meadows
description: Beds of submerged vascular vegetation of tropical seas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical Hydrocharitaceae seagrass beds
description: Beds of seagrasses of genera [Halophila], [Enhalus], [Thalassia], in particular [Halophila ovalis], [Halophila stipulacea], [Halophila ovata], [Enhalus acoroides] and [Thalassia hemprichii], of the Red Sea and Indo-Pacific continental shelf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical Atlantic seagrass meadows
description: Formations of [Zostera marina], [Zostera noltii], [Cymodocea nodosa] and [Halodule wrightii] of the northwestern tropical Atlantic, transitional towards Mediterranean communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Indian Ocean Cymodoceaceae beds
description: Beds of seagrasses of genera [Cymodocea], [Halodule], [Syringodium], [Thalassodendron], in particular [Cymodocea rotundata], [Cymodocea serrulata], [Halodule uninervis], [Syringodium isoetifolium] and [Thalassodendron ciliatum], of the coasts of the Red Sea and of the Indian Ocean coasts of the southern Arabian peninsula and Baluchistan. They constitute the main foraging habitat of [Dugong dugon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical Pacific eelgrass meadows
description: [Zostera marina] formations of the South China Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brackish sea vascular vegetation
description: Beds of submerged or slightly emergent vascular vegetation of brackish seas, sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia maritima], [Ruppia cirrhosa], [Zannichellia pedicellata], [Chara spp.], [Tolypella nidifica] of brackish seas, sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia maritima], [Ruppia cirrhosa], [Zannichellia pedicellata], [Chara spp.], [Tolypella nidifica] of brackish seas, sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of Atlantic, North Sea and Baltic coasts of boreal and temperate Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic coastal tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia maritima], [Ruppia cirrhosa], [Zannichellia pedicellata], [Potamogeton pectinatus], [Chara spp.], [Tolypella nidifica] of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of the temperate and boreal coasts of the temperate and low Arctic North Atlantic, from Iceland and nortwestern Norway to central Portugal, of the North Sea, the English Channel, the Irish Sea, from northern Iceland and nortwestern Norway in the north, south to central Portugal.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of vascular vegetation of the Baltic dominated by [Ruppia spp.] or [Zannichellia palustris]. Included are formations of the open inner Baltic, composed of [Ruppia maritima] var. [maritima] and [Najas marina], of [Ruppia maritima] var. [brevirostris], and [Zannichellia palustris] ssp. [polycarpa], or of [Ruppia cirrhosa] and [Zostera marina], as well as communities of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons; beds of [Chara spp.], [Tolypella nidifica] may accompany or replace the vascular vegetation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia maritima] or [Ruppia cirrhosa] and of [Chara spp.]  of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of the Mediterranean, the Black Sea and the subtropical Atlantic, north to southwestern Iberia, south to 27øN.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Tethyan marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia maritima], including [Ruppia maritima] ssp. [rostellata], or [Ruppia cirrhosa] ([Ruppia drepanensis], [Ruppia spiralis]) and of [Chara spp.] of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats and coastal lagoons of Mediterranean coasts and of thermo-Atlantic coasts of southwestern Iberia, of norhwestern Africa, south to 27øN, and of the Macaronesian islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia maritima] or [Ruppia cirrhosa], accompanied by [Zannichellia palustris], [Potamogeton pectinatus] and [Chara spp.]  of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of the Black Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Sindian marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia maritima] or [Ruppia cirrhosa] and of [Chara spp.]  of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of the desert coasts of the North Atlantic, between 27øN and 18øN, and of the Indian Ocean and its connected seas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific temperate marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia spp.] and [Chara spp.]  of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of the boreal, temperate and subtropical western Pacific and its connected seas, distributed along all coasts, north to the northern coasts of the sea of Okhotsk and northern Kamtchatka in the Bering Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical marine tasselweed communities
description: Submerged beds of [Ruppia spp.] and [Chara spp.]  of sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons of tropical coasts of west Africa and of the Indo-Pacific.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marine spike-rush beds
description: Emergent [Eleocharis parvula] or [Eleocharis acicularis] formations of brackish seas, sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons, occurring in the open sea only in the Baltic, limited to coastal waterbodies elsewhere, and very rare.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf spike-rush beds
description: Emergent [Eleocharis parvula]-dominated formations of brackish seas, sea inlets, estuaries, permanent pools of mud or sand flats, and coastal lagoons. They occur in the open sea only in the inner Baltic, in particular in middle Sweden, southern Finland and Estonia; they are very rare elsewhere, noted in particular on a few points of the coasts of Norway and in closed limans of the northern Black Sea and Azov Sea coasts, probably extinct in France and Germany.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bothnian needle spike-rush beds
description: Emergent [Eleocharis acicularis]-dominated formations of the open Baltic in the Gulf of Bothnia (Bothnia Sea, Bothnia Bay) and the Gulf of Finland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal brackish water crowfoot communities
description: [Ranunculus spp.]-dominated communities developed in shallow-waters of very low salinity of coastal lagoons, coastal basins and coastal waters of the Palaearctic region, including the Atlantic, North Sea, Baltic Sea, Mediterranean Sea and Black Sea. The most widespread characteristic species is [Ranunculus baudotii]. Locally, other crowfoots may be typical, as, in particular, in the Gulf of Bothnia, [Ranunculus trichophyllus] ([Ranunculus confervoides]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea ice
description: Ice formations floating on sea water, usually constituting an incomplete cover, variable in form and structure, unstable and dynamic under the influence of surface air and water currents.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Permanent ice pack
description: Semicontinuous ice sheets covering the sea throughout the year, limited to the Arctic Ocean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Seasonal ice pack
description: Semicontinuous ice sheets forming on the sea for part of the year, characteristic of the Arctic Ocean, Baffin Bay, Davis Strait, the Greenland Sea, the Denmark Strait, the Norwegian Sea, the Barents Sea, the Kara Sea, the Laptev Sea, the East Siberian Sea, the Chukchi Sea, Bothnia Bay, the Bothnia Sea, and coastal areas of the Aland Sea, the Gulf of Finland and the Gulf of Riga, exceptional in other areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ice floes
description: Discontinuous formations of floating ice blocks, rafts and hummocks detached from the sea pack, remaining after the break-up of seasonal ice packs or drifting to more southern regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icebergs
description: Floating and drifting blocks of ice detached from coastal glaciers (unit 63.3).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea inlets and coastal features
description: Bays and narrow channels of the oceans and their connected seas, including sea lochs or loughs, fiords or fiards, rias and straits but excluding estuaries and lagoons. Detailed habitats can be coded by combining subdivisions of unit 11 with the relevant physiographic subdivisions of unit 12.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Open linear coasts
description: More or less straight coasts, devoid of deep indentations, characteristic of concordant coasts, of soft-sediment coastlines, and of the contour of isolated promontories.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Semienclosed coasts
description: Coastlines of wide, curved indentations of the sea into the land, with a wide or fairly wide opening, including bays and gulfs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sounds and straits
description: More or less narrow stretches of water connecting two larger bodies of water; channels between islands and the mainland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Enclosed enbayments
description: Bodies of water, such as coves, communicating with the sea by a relatively narrow but unobstructed opening.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fiords, fiards, sea lochs
description: Sea inlets dug by glacial action, usually characterized by the presence of an entrance moraine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fiords, fiordic lochs
description: Deep, long, narrow inlets in the coast, with high, rocky, parallel sides, smoothed by ice action, and a rocky floor often deeper than the sea floor and separated from it by a sill near the entrance, formed by the submergence of glacial valleys.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fiards, fiardic lochs
description: Irregular, often branched or islet-studded, shallow or deep, inlets in the coast, with low banks and a usually narrow entrance.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Open sea lochs
description: Sea inlets of glacial origin, communicating more broadly with the sea than fiords or fiards and lacking a shallow entrance sill.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rias, voes, abers
description: Funnel-shaped sea inlets formed, in particular, by drowned river valleys, particularly along discordant coasts, as a result of a rise in sea-level.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea-caves
description: Caves situated under the sea or opened to it, at least at high tide. Their marine part harbours benthic communities of units 11.26 and 11.294. They may be connected to terrestrial cave systems (unit 65) or to the underground water network through anchihaline environments (unit 65.451).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Submerged sea-caves
description: Sea-caves situated entirely below low-tide level.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Complex sea-caves
description: Sea-caves situated in part above low-tide level, comprising mediolittoral (unit 11.294), and, in some cases, supralittoral (units 12.72 x 11.296, 12.72 x 11.297), communities; they may be in contact with, or grade into, terrestrial caves (unit 65), and contain sand or pebble beaches (units 12.72 x 16.1, 12.72 x 17).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Estuaries and tidal rivers
description: Broadening of rivers entering the oceans or their connected seas and river channels below the tidal limit. Included are all marine or marine-related pelagic and benthic communities, which can be specified by use of subdivisions of unit 11, and all river course and riverbed communities, which can be specified by subdivisions of unit 24. The belts of fringing vegetation are excluded and indicated separately by use of units 53, 44, 15 and their subdivisions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tidal rivers
description: Portions of rivers subject to the tide, upstream from the estuary. Their banks may be colonized by communities of units 24.52, 37.71, 44.12, 53.1, in particular of units 37.711, 37.712, 44.121, 53.114, 53.13, 53.16, 53.17.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brackish water tidal rivers
description: Brackish portions of rivers subject to the tide, upstream from the estuary.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Freshwater tidal rivers
description: Freshwater sections of rivers subject to the tide.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Estuaries
description: Broadening of rivers entering the sea. Detailed habitats can be coded by combining subdivisions of prefix 11 with the relevant physiographic subdivisions of unit 13.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal plain estuaries
description: River-dominated, allochthonous deltaic estuaries formed by rivers accumulating sediments beyond the river mouth, often complex and constituted by many channels, with a salt wedge in the main channel; they are characteristic of microtidal shorelines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bar-built estuaries
description: Wave- and current-dominated autochthonous estuarine systems constituted by shallow, often extensive, embayments separated from the sea by offshore bars of current-transported sand and with a very reduced tidal range; they are characteristic of mesotidal shorelines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Complex estuaries, firths
description: Composite river- and sea-dominated estuarine systems, including estuaries of macrotidal shorelines, subjected to tide-currents, devoid of protective littoral bars, and often accompanied by very developed tidal flats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intertidal and littoral flats
description: Extensive, flat or nearly flat, surfaces of sands, muds or rocks of the coasts of the oceans, their connected seas and associated lagoons, submerged for part of every tide or for part of the annual cycle, devoid of terrestrial vascular plants. They are of particular importance as feeding grounds for wildfowl and waders. The diverse intertidal communities of invertebrates and algae that occupy them can be precised by use of the subdivisions of units 11.27 to 11.2A, phanerogamic marine vegetation communities that may be exposed for a few hours in the course of every tide by use of those of unit 11.3, brackish water vegetation of permanent pools by use of those of unit 11.4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mud flats and sand flats
description: Sands and muds of the coasts of the oceans, their connected seas and associated lagoons, submerged for part of every tide or for part of the annual cycle, devoid of terrestrial vascular plants, but usually coated by blue algae and diatoms. They are particularly well developed in the Wadden Sea, in the large bays of the North Sea, Atlantic and Channel coasts, in estuaries, in the Mediterranean Gulf of Gabes and along some subtropical coasts, among others, those of Mauritania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intertidal rock pavements
description: Bedrock platforms or terraces washed by the tides, broad wave-cut rock platforms situated in the intertidal zone, but nearer low tide, with a more or less plane surface, rough in detail, dotted by tidepools.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saltmarshes, salt steppes, salt scrubs
description: Communities of phanerogamic plants, for the most part halophytes, colonizing sites submerged by high tides at some stage of the annual tidal cycle of oceans and their connected seas. Similar halophyte communities colonizing the fringes and emersed beds of inland permanent or temporary saline, hypersaline or brackish waterbodies, including inland closed seas, lakes, pools, sebkhas, rivers, springs, seeps. By extension, azonal, strongly differentiated, communities developing on habitually dry, alkali, chlorid or gypseous soils of the nemoral, middle Eurasian steppe, Irano-Anatolian, Mediterranean, Saharo-Mediterranean and Macaronesian zones. Zonal communities of the desert and semidesert areas, composed, to varying degrees, of halophytes or gypsophytes, are listed under 7. Some saline communities with strong physionognimic similarity to fresh water ones into which they may merge, have been listed in other sections, together with their freshwater counterparts; it is the case in particular of saline tamarisk stands (44.83 ff.) and of tall helophyte beds (53). More generally, halophile forests and their related thickets have been listed with other forests under 4; in particular mangrove forests and thickets are in 4C.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Annual salt pioneer swards
description: Formations composed mostly or prominently of annuals, in particular Chenopodiaceae of genus [Salicornia] or grasses, colonizing periodically inundated muds and sands of marine or interior saltmarshes of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.], [Microcnemum coralloides]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]), or sometimes saltwort ([Salsola spp.]), formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of coastal saltmarshes and inland salt-basins of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Atlantic glasswort swards
description: Swards of annual [Salicornia spp.] and [Suaeda maritima] of the coastal saltmarshes of the North Sea, the Baltic, the northern Atlantic and the western Eurasian polar basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low shore samphire flats
description: Colonies of nonreddening tetraploid glassworts [Salicornia dolichostachya], [Salicornia fragilis], [Salicornia decumbens] and of [Suaeda maritima] ssp. [flexilis], occupying the lowest, dampest areas of northern and western European coastal flats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Seablite-samphire communities
description: Colonies of often much-branched, diploid glassworts [Salicornia ramosissima], [Salicornia europaea], [Salicornia obscura] [i.a.] and/or of [Suaeda maritima], occupying higher, drier areas of European coastal flats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Eurasian arctic glasswort swards
description: Swards of annual [Salicornia spp.] of the coastal saltmarshes of the western Eurasian polar basin, in particular, [Salicornia dolichostachya] ssp. [pojarkovae] swards of northern Norway and northern Russia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western European continental glasswort beds
description: Glasswort formations of inland saltmarshes of nemoral middle Europe, in particular of Germany, Poland, France and England (unit 15.4).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western European continental glasswort seeps
description: Colonies of the orange-turning [Salicornia emerici] var. [vicensis], of unstable, fluid, seeping muds of inland western European saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western European continental glasswort swards
description: Colonies of the reddening [Salicornia ramosissima] or of [Salicornia europaea], of firmer muds of inland western and central European saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean glasswort swards
description: Glasswort swards of saltmarshes, lagoons and deltas of the coasts and coastal regions of the Mediterranean and of the subtropical Atlantic, including those of southwestern France, the Iberian peninsula, mediterranean North Africa south to the Oued Tensift at 32øN and mediterraneo-Saharan Africa between 32øN and 27øN.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low-shore Mediterranean glasswort swards
description: Glasswort swards occupying long-inundated basins of coastal saltmarshes of the western Mediterranean basin, including those of Spain, southern continental France, the Gulf of Tarento, Corsica, Sardinia and Sicily, with Atlantic representatives in southwestern Europe, between southern Brittany and central Portugal, dominated by the reddening tetraploid glasswort [Salicornia emerici].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Venetian glasswort swards
description: Endemic, threatened [Salicornia veneta] swards of long-inundated muds of basins of the Venice lagoon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean glasswort-seablite-saltwort swards
description: [Salicornia spp.], [Suaeda spp.], [Salsola spp.], [Halopeplis amplexicaulis]  swards, often monospecific, occupying muds of coastal saltmarshes of the Mediterranean Sea and of the warm-temperate Atlantic, from central Portugal to 27øN, restricted, in the western Mediterranean basin, to firmer, drier muds with shorter inundation periods than those occupied by the communities of unit 15.1131.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Upper shore Mediterranean glasswort swards
description: Glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) swards occupying muds of coastal saltmarshes of the Mediterranean Sea, including both western and eastern basins, and of the Atlantic, from central Portugal to 27øN, dominated by diploid glassworts, in particular, by the reddening [Salicornia patula], also by [Salicornia ramosissima] and probably other diplo‹d taxa of the [Salicornia europaea] aggregate, limited in the western Mediterranean basin to firmer, drier muds than those colonized by the tetraploid [Salicornia emerici].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean annual seablite and saltwort swards
description: [Suaeda spp.] or [Salsola spp.]-dominated swards of exposed muds of coastal saltmarshes of the Mediterranean Sea and the warm-temperate Atlantic, mostly characteristic of the eastern Mediterranean basin and of muds on which organic material, in particular detritus of marine phanerogams, has accumulated; more species-rich formations characteristic of more substantial debris accumulations are listed as unit 15.56.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Halopeplis] swards
description: [Halopeplis amplexicaulis] swards, often monospecific and ephemereal, occupying hypersaline long-inundated muds of saltmarshes of arid Mediterranean coasts, appearing at the beginning of severe summer dessication, distributed in Egypt, Libya, Tunisia, northwestern Algeria and, very locally, in Morocco,  Sicily, Sardinia (Cagliari) and southern Italy (Metaponto). The formation is threatened in Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior Iberian glasswort swards
description: Annual [Salicornia spp.] and [Microcnemum coralloides] formations of interior Iberian salt basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian [Microcnemum] swards
description: Formations of the endemic [Microcnemum coralloides] ssp. [coralloides], associated or not with [Salicornia europaea] [s.l.], of interior salt basins of central and east-central Spain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian interior [Salicornia] swards
description: Formations of [Salicornia europaea] [s.l.] of interior salt basins of Iberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.], [Microcnemum coralloides]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) solonchak formations, colonizing periodically inundated muds of Black Sea coastal saltmarshes and of inland salt-basins of central Eurasian and Irano-Anatolian steppe and cold desert zones. Annual glasswort communities of salt steppes and saltmarshes of areas of extreme continentality within the boreal zone of Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic glasswort-seablite-saltwort swards
