description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola soda]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of inland salt-basins associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the Pannonic Plain (unit 15.A1) and its satellite basins. Similar communities restricted to isolated intermontane basins of the southwestern Balkan peninsula, related to both the Pannonic and western Pontic formations, are included in this unit, to parallel the treatment of the steppes and saltmarshes of unit 15.A1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic glasswort swards
description: Formations dominated by the reddening [Salicornia prostrata] or [Salicornia simonkaiana] colonizing periodically inundated muds of salt-basins associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the Pannonic Plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic seablite swards
description: Formations dominated by [Suaeda pannonica], [Suaeda maritima] ssp. [prostrata] or [Suaeda maritima] ssp. [salsa] colonizing periodically inundated muds of salt-basins associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the Pannonic Plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic saltwort communities
description: Formations of [Salsola soda] colonizing periodically inundated silty, nitrogen-rich muds of the lower levels of salt-basins of the Pannonic Plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonian seablite swards
description: Annual formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of inland saltmarshes of isolated intermontane basins of the southwestern Balkan peninsula, in particular, of the middle Vardar trough, northwest of the Pelagonian mountains, with [Suaeda maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Sarmatic glasswort-seablite-saltwort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola soda]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the coastal saltmarshes of the Black Sea and Azov Sea, and of the inland salt-basins associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the western and northern Black Sea and Sea of Azov plain, of the basins of the lower Danube, the middle Maritsa and the Tundzha, the Prut, the Dniestr, the Dniepr, the Don, and of the southern Russian hills, north of the Caspian depression and west of the Urals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic glasswort-seablite-saltwort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola soda]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the saltmarshes of the western Black Sea coast and adjacent inland waterbodies and of the inland salt-basins associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the western Black Sea plain, west of the Dniestr, of the basin of the lower Danube, and, in very fragmentary form, of the northern Thracian basin of the middle Maritsa and the Tundzha. Typical species include [Salicornia prostrata], [Suaeda maritima], [Bassia hirsuta], [Limonium gmelinii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic glasswort swards
description: Formations dominated by [Salicornia prostrata] ([Salicornia ramosissima] auct. eur. orient., non J. Woods) or [Salicornia europaea], often in association with [Puccinellia festuciformis] ssp. [convoluta], [Crypsis aculeata], [Puccinellia distans], colonizing periodically inundated muds of saltmarshes and salt-basins of the western Black Sea coast, the western Black Sea plain, west of the Dniestr, and the lower Danube plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic seablite swards
description: Formations, often monospecific, of [Suaeda maritima], colonizing periodically inundated muds of saltmarshes and salt-basins of the western Black Sea coast, the western Black Sea plain, west of the Dniestr, the lower Danube plain and, in very fragmentary form, the northern Thracian basin of the middle Maritsa and the Tundzha.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic saltwort communities
description: Formations, often monospecific, of [Salsola soda], colonizing periodically inundated muds of saltmarshes and salt-basins of the western Black Sea coast, the western Black Sea plain, west of the Dniestr, the lower Danube plain and, in very fragmentary form, the northern Thracian basin of the middle Maritsa and the Tundzha.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia europaea]) and seablite ([Suaeda maritima]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of inland salt-basins associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the southern edge and valleys of the Podolian plateau, of the Central Russian plateau, of the Volga plateau, of Orenburg and of Bachkiria north of the Pontic and Caspian plains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) and seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the coastal saltmarshes of the northern Black Sea and the Sea of Azov and of the inland salt-basins associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain, of the basins of the Dniepr and the Don.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxinian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) and seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of saltmarshes of the southern and eastrn Black Sea coasts, south of the Kuban basin limit between the steppe zone and the peri-Caucasian submediterranean broad-leaved deciduous woods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of salt steppes and saltmarshes of the Transvolgan, Kazakh, Kourgan, Ichim, Koulounda, Baraba, Barnaul steppe regions and of saltmarshes of the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea and other inland waterbodies of the northern Aralo-Caspian, Kura basin, western Kazakh, Dzungarian, Oust-ourt, Kyzyl Koum and Kara Koum middle Asiatic deserts and semideserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the salt steppes and saltmarshes of Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, the Songnen Plain of Northeast China, the western Loess Plateau of North China and of the saltmarshes of the inland waterbodies of the Gobi, Takla Makan, Tarim, Lop-nor, Bei-shan, Ala-shan, Ordos, Tsaidam and Pamyro-Tibetan Central Asiatic deserts and semideserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the salt steppes and saltmarshes of steppic areas of the Anatolian Plateau, of the Iranian Plateau and of northern Mesopotamia, as well as of the saltmarshes of the cold desert or subdesert areas of the Iranian Plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.], [Microcnemum coralloides]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the western Anatolian Plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Microcnemum] swards
description: Formations of the endemic [Microcnemum coralloides] ssp. [anatolicum] of interior salt-basins of western-central Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Salicornia] swards
description: Formations of annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) colonizing periodically inundated muds of the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the western Anatolian Plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Irano-Anatolian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of salt steppes and saltmarshes of eastern Anatolia and northwestern Iran.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Afghan glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the salt steppes and saltmarshes of steppic areas of the Central and Eastern Iranian Plateau in Iran and Afghanistan, and of the saltmarshes and temporary waterbodies of the cold desert or subdesert areas of Iran and Afghanistan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North Mesopotamian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]), [Halopeplis amplexicaulis], seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) and saltwort ([Salsola spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the salt steppes and saltmarshes of the Mesopotamian steppic region bordering the Near Eastern Saharo-Sindian deserts, extending north to southeastern Turkey and to Khuzestan in western Iran.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Yakutian boreal glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of the salt  meadows, salt steppe meadows, swamp meadows, alases and salt marshes of the middle Lena basin of eastern Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Sindian glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) and seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) formations developed on periodically inundated muds of inland saltmarshes and temporary waterbodies of the Saharo-Sindian subtropical desert belt and of coastal saltmarshes and lagoon fringes of desert and subdesert coasts of Africa and western Asia, including the oceanic desert coasts of the Atlantic Sahara between 27øN and 18øN, the extreme southeastern Mediterranean coasts of the Sinai peninsula, the coasts of the Red Sea, the Arabian Sea and the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far-Eastern continental glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) and seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) formations developed on periodically inundated muds of inland salt-basins of the Far Eastern nemoral and warm-temperate humid zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific glasswort swards
description: Annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) and seablite ([Suaeda spp.]) formations colonizing periodically inundated muds of Pacific coastal saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical glasswort swards
description: Formations of annual glasswort ([Salicornia spp.]) and other Chenopodiaceae colonizing periodically inundated muds of coastal and inland saltmarshes of tropical regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean halo-nitrophilous pioneer communities
description: Formations of halonitrophilous annuals ([Frankenia pulverulenta], [Suaeda splendens], [Salsola soda], [Cressa cretica], [Parapholis incurva], [Parapholis strigosa], [Hordeum marinum], [Sphenopus divaricatus], [Polypogon maritimus], [Spergularia spp.], [Vella annua]) colonizing salt muds of Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coastal regions, of Iberian and North African endoreic basins, susceptible to temporary inundation and extreme drying; they are more species-rich or richer in non-chenopodids than the communities of unit 15.113; they are particularly developed in the Iberian peninsula, secondarily in the large Mediterranean islands, in coastal regions and endoreic basins of North Africa, in southern Italy and Mediterranean France; they occur as irradiations on thermo-Atlantic coasts, notably on the Atlantic coast of France. Somewhat similar communities occur in the steppe zones of Eurasia and their regions of influence, as well as in Saharo-Mediterranean steppes of North Africa; they are included in units 15.14 and 15.15.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Frankenia pulverulenta] communities
description: Halophile and weakly to moderately nitrophile, predominantly non-gramino‹d, communities of annuals developing throughout the period of vegetation on solonchaks of Iberia, the Mediterranean basin and interior North Africa, dominated by [Frankenia pulverulenta], with [Suaeda splendens], [Salsola soda], [Cressa cretica], [Parapholis incurva], [Parapholis strigosa], [Hordeum marinum], [Sphenopus divaricatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean aestival halo-nitrophile grass swards
description: Halophile and weakly nitrophile predominantly gramino‹d swards developing usually in early summer on long-inundated solonchaks of Iberia, the western Mediterranean and North Africa, dominated by relatively small grasses, particularly [Sphenopus divaricatus], also [Parapholis filiformis], [Parapholis incurva], [Polypogon maritimus] ([Polypogon subspathaceus]) with [Hymenolobus procumbens], [Frankenia pulverulenta], [Hordeum marinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Cressa] swards
description: Halophile and weakly to moderately nitrophile aestival and postaestival solonchak communities of coastal, mostly endoreic or percolation, lagoons, coastal saltmarsh ponds and interior endoreic basins of Sicily, the Maltese Islands, Sardinia, Corsica, Iberia, North Africa and, very locally, Mediterranean France, Calabria, Mediterranean western Asia, dominated by the Convolvulaceae [Cressa cretica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Hordeum marinum] swards
description: Dense halonitrophilous meadows dominated by robust, spring-developing annual grasses, among which [Hordeum marinum] is often prevalent, forming at the upper margin of Iberian and North African endoreic depressions and of Mediterranean and warm-temperate Atlantic saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean nitrophilous solonchak chenopodid mats
description: Halonitrophilous, often polyspecific, annual communities dominated by Chenopodiaceae ([Chenopodium spp.], [Suaeda splendens]) colonizing solonchaks of Iberian and North African endoreic basins and of western Mediterranean and warm-temperate Atlantic coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean sea-pearlwort communities
description: Formations of annual pioneers, small geophytes and sometimes sparse chamaephytes occupying, in the Mediterranean basin, on thermo-Atlantic shores and around Iberian and North African endoreic basins, sands subject to variable salinity and humidity, notably in the transition zone between salt scrubs and dry grasslands. Dominant species include [Sagina maritima], [Spergularia spp.], [Mesembryanthemum crystallinum], [Mesembryanthemum nodiflorum], [Evax rotundata], [Evax pygmaea]; accompaniers comprise [Romulea bulbocodium], [Romulea rollii], [Anagallis arvensis], [Bellis annua].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic sea-pearlwort communities
description: Formations of annual pioneers occupying sands subject to variable salinity and humidity, on the coasts, in the dunal systems and in the saltmarshes of the Atlantic, the North Sea and the Baltic. They are usually limited to small surfaces and best developed in the zone of contact between dune and saltmarsh.  Characteristic species include [Sagina maritima], [Sagina nodosa], [Cochlearia danica], [Gentiana uliginosa], [Centaurium littorale], [Bupleurum tenuissimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian crypsoid communities
description: Sparse solonchak formations of annual grasses of genus [Crypsis] ([Heleochloa]), accompanied by [Cyperus pannonicus] ([Acorellus pannonicus]), [Spergularia media] ([Spergularia marginata]), [Spergularia marina] ([Spergularia salina]), [Salicornia spp.], [Lepidium latifolium], [Chenopodium spp.], [Atriplex spp.], colonizing drying muds of humid depressions of the salt steppes and saltmarshes (15.A) of Eurasia, from Pannonia to the Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Pannonic [Acorellus] community
description: Pioneer community of the salt basins of the Pannonic Plain, of Muntenia, the Danube delta, the Dobrogea, the northern Black Sea and Azov Sea coastlands and steppes, characteristic of sandy soils, with [Cyperus pannonicus] ([Acorellus pannonicus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian [Crypsis] communities
description: Sparse formations of annual grasses of genus [Crypsis], [Crypsis aculeata], [Crypsis schoenoides] ([Heleochloa schoenoides]), [Crypsis alopecuroides] ([Heleochloa alopecuroides]), accompanied by [Cyperus fuscus], [Cyperus difformis] and other monocotyledonous species, colonizing drying silty or clayey muds of humid depressions of the salt steppes and saltmarshes (unit 15.A) of Eurasia, from Pannonia to the Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian solonchak goosefoot mats
description: Formations of often prostrate [Atriplex] and [Chenopodium] species colonizing drying muds of humid depressions of the salt steppes and saltmarshes (unit 15.A) of Eurasia, from Pannonia to the Far East.  Western formations are dominated by [Atriplex prostrata] ([Atriplex hastata] agg.) or by [Chenopodium chenopodioides], accompanied by [Chenopodium glaucum], [Suaeda maritima] ssp. [prostrata], [Crypsis aculeata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian sea spurrey communities
description: Open or almost closed formations dominated by [Spergularia media] ([Spergularia marginata]) or [Spergularia marina] ([Spergularia salina]), colonizing small depressions inundated or humid in late spring, dessicated, often with salt efflorescences in summer, associated with the salt steppes and saltmarshes (unit 15.A) of Eurasia, in particular in the eastern Pannonic and western Pontic regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic [Bassia hirsuta] communities
description: Formations of [Bassia hirsuta] colonizing very humid, highly chloridic muds of saltmarshes and salt-basins of the western Black Sea coast and the lower Danube plain, often on the outskirts of [Salicornia europaea] and [Suaeda maritima] communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic halo-nitrophilous pioneer communities
description: Formations of halonitrophilous annuals ([Frankenia pulverulenta], [Suaeda confusa], [Salsola acutifolia], [Parapholis incurva], [Hordeum marinum], [Cressa cretica]) colonizing solonchak salt muds susceptible to temporary inundation and extreme drying, caracteristic of lagoon systems of the western Black Sea coast and of the Danube Delta, somewhat similar ecologically and in species composition to the Mediterranean formations of the [Frankenietea pulverulentae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic [Frankenia pulverulenta] communities
description: Formations of halonitrophilous annuals dominated by [Frankenia pulverulenta] colonizing salt muds susceptible to temporary inundation and extreme drying in openings within [Artemisio austriacae-Poetum bulbosae] or [Obionetum pedunculatae] communities of lagoon systems of the Black Sea, the Azov Sea and the Danube Delta.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic [Cressa] swards
description: Saltmarsh formations constituted by [Cressa cretica], often accompanied by [Crypsis spp.], [Puccinellia festuciformis] ssp. [convoluta], [Aster tripolium], [Salicornia spp.] of western Black Sea coastal areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic [Hordeum marinum] swards
description: Closed halonitrophilous annual communities dominated by [Hordeum marinum], with [Plantago coronopus], [Lotus tenuis], [Juncus gerardi], [Lepidium latifolium], [Spergularia media], [Puccinellia distans], colonizing moderately salted muds of the western Black Sea coast and the Danube delta, susceptible to heavy autumn and spring inundation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic mouse-ear sea-pearlwort communities
description: Formations of small annual caryophyllid pioneers, in particular [Sagina maritima] and [Cerastium spp.], notably [Cerastium gracile] ([Cerastium ramosissimum]) or [Cerastium dubium] ([Cerastium anomalum]), of the western Black Sea coast and the Danube delta, developed on sands subject to variable salinity and humidity, in particular in the zone of contact between dune and saltmarsh.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Perennial salt pioneer swards
description: Perennial pioneer grasslands of coastal salt muds of the Palaearctic, formed by [Spartina spp.] or similar grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Flat-leaved cordgrass swards
description: Perennial pioneer grasslands of coastal salt muds dominated by flat-leaved [Spartina maritima] ([Spartina stricta]), [Spartina townsendii], [Spartina anglica], [Spartina alterniflora], distributed along Atlantic and North Sea coasts of middle Europe north to Denmark and south to northwestern Iberia, with outposts on the Atlantic coast of Africa around Tangier, Rabat and Cap Blanc, extending east to the Danish archipelago and with isolated areas of occurrence in the Mediterranean basin, located in the northern Adriatic, in the Venice Lagoon and nearby coasts, from the mouth of the Po to Trieste and Slovenia, and in estuaries of the coasts of northwestern Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rush-leaved cordgrass swards
description: Perennial pioneer grasslands of southern Iberian coastal salt muds, dominated by the junciform-leaved [Spartina densiflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-nemoral coastal salt meadows
description: Salt meadows of the shores of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans and connected seas, including the Baltic, the North Sea and the English Channel, within the nemoral and boreal zones. [Aster tripolium] can be present or abundant in most western subdivisions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saltmarsh grass lawns
description: Communities of the lower and middle schorre of the shores of the Atlantic ocean and connected seas with an overwhelming dominance of [Puccinellia maritima], often in almost monospecific stands forming bright green lawns characteristic, in particular, of pioneer stages of the lowest levels and of intensely grazed areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic lower schorre communities
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas codominated by [Puccinellia maritima] and other physiognomically important species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea purslane-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas codominated by [Puccinellia maritima] and [Halimione portulacoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea aster-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas codominated by [Puccinellia maritima] and [Aster tripolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Glasswort-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas codominated by [Puccinellia maritima], annual [Salicornia spp.] and [Suaeda maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic stalked orache beds
description: Formations dominated by the rare, threatened [Halimione pedunculata], developing very locally in the [Puccinellion maritimae] of Denmark, Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium and France, extinct in the British Isles.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Pelvetia]-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Species-poor salt meadows restricted to the shores of northern Norway and southwestern Iceland in the vicinity of the Reykjanes peninsula, codominated by [Puccinellia maritima] and the brown alga [Pelvetia canaliculata], accompanied by [Agrostis stolonifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Catabrosa]-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Salt meadows of Iceland and northern Norway, mostly of the lower shore, dominated by [Puccinellia maritima], with [Catabrosa aquatica], [Carex mackenziei], [Carex subspathacea], [Stellaria crassifolia], [Glaux maritima], [Gentianella detonsa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Glaux]-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas codominated by [Puccinellia maritima] and [Glaux maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Plantago]-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas codominated by [Puccinellia maritima] and [Plantago maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Limonium]-saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas codominated by [Puccinellia maritima] and [Limonium vulgare], characteristic of undrained depressions on lightly grazed salt meadows of the Netherlands and the British Isles.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic upper schorre communities
description: Often relatively species-rich, grassy, flowery formations characteristic of the upper levels of the salt meadows of the Atlantic and its connected seas, with [Armeria maritima], [Glaux maritima], [Plantago maritima], [Frankenia laevis], [Artemisia maritima], [Festuca rubra], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Juncus gerardi], [Carex extensa], [Blysmus rufus], [Eleocharis spp.]. Similar communities occupying the lower levels of brackish meadows, in particular of the Baltic, are included, while formations restricted to brackish conditions are listed under unit 15.34. The dominance of various species induces distinctive facies, the most important of which are individualised in subunits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Juncus gerardii] saltmeadows
description: Often species-rich, closed, flowery, upper level salt meadows of the Atlantic and its connected seas, dominated by, or rich in, [Juncus gerardi]. [Glaux maritima] can dominate facies, forming thick carpets, in particular, in pioneer situations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Plantago maritima] saltmeadows
description: Communities of upper saltmarshes of the Atlantic, the North Sea and the Baltic, dominated by [Plantago maritima] or [Plantago maritima] and [Bupleurum tenuissimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Festuca rubra]-[Agrostis stolonifera] swards
description: Upper saltmarsh communities of the Atlantic and its connected seas dominated by, or rich in, [Festuca rubra] and [Agrostis stolonifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic thrift swards
description: Communities of salt meadows of the Atlantic and its connected seas dominated by, or rich in, [Armeria maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Carex distans] beds
description: Communities of Atlantic salt meadows dominated by [Carex distans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Carex extensa] saltmeadows
description: Upper saltmarsh communities of the Atlantic and its connected seas dominated by, or rich in, [Carex extensa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic sea lavender meadows
description: Upper saltmarsh communities of the Atlantic and its connected seas dominated by, or rich in, [Limonium vulgare].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Blysmus] salt meadows
description: Upper saltmarsh communities of the Atlantic and its connected seas dominated by, or rich in, [Blysmus rufus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Eleocharis] salt meadows
description: Atlantic saltmarsh or brackish marsh communities dominated by [Eleocharis uniglumis] or [Eleocharis palustris], associated with [Agrostis stolonifera] or [Carex paleacea]. They constitute a common upper shore community in Scotland; they are also very prevalent on the lower levels of the brackish marshes of the Baltic, east and north of southeastern Sweden and Estonia; in western Scandinavia they are restricted to estuaries and fjord heads. They occur on saline littorals in Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Juncus maritimus] beds
description: Saltmarsh communities of the Atlantic, the North Sea and the southern Baltic, dominated by, or rich in, [Juncus maritimus], with [Oenanthe lachenalii] and, locally, in Poland in particular, [Samolus valerandi], mostly characteristic of the upper shore, in moderately salty or brackish conditions, of the sandy-clayey transition to green beaches, also occurring, in the southern Baltic, on brackish lower shores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic sea wormwood salt meadows
description: Atlantic saltmarsh communities dominated by, or rich in, [Artemisia maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Potentilla anserina] carpets
description: Upper saltmarsh communities of the Atlantic and its connected seas dominated by, or rich in, [Potentilla anserina], including both [Potentilla anserina] ssp. [anserina], and, in Fennoscandia, Iceland and Greenland, [Potentilla anserina] ssp. [egedii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic sea-heath communities
description: Atlantic upper saltmarsh communities of the English Channel and the Franco-Iberian coasts of the Atlantic, with an isolated station on Anglesey, dominated by, or rich in, [Frankenia laevis], associated with [Limonium spp.], in particular with [Limonium lychnidifolium] in France, or [Limonium vulgare] in southern England, characteristic of the sandy transition zone between saltmarshes and dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic upper schorre sea aster beds
description: Atlantic upper schorre communities dominated by [Aster tripolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic strawberry clover swards
description: Atlantic upper saltmarsh communities dominated by [Trifolium fragiferum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic black sedge salt meadows
description: Atlantic upper saltmarsh communities dominated by [Carex nigra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian bogrush shore communities
description: Upper and middle saltmarsh communities of the Baltic and the northwest Atlantic, dominated by [Schoenus nigricans] or [Schoenus ferrugineus], with [Molinia caerulea] and [Campylium polygamum], developed on calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern [Agrostis-Festuca-Leontodon] communities
description: Upper shore swards of northern Norway, Iceland and the Faeroes dominated by [Agrostis stolonifera], [Festuca rubra], [Plantago maritima] and [Leontodon autumnalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Calamagrostis stricta]-sedge swards
description: Upper saltmarsh tall graminoid communities of the Gulf of Bothnia and the northern Atlantic coasts of Scandinavia, south of Finnmark, dominated by [Calamagrostis stricta], [Carex aquatilis], [Carex juncella], [Eriophorum angustifolium], rich in arctic halophytes, transitional towards fens which form flood belts near fresh water. This unit is replaced northwards by the truly arctic formations of unit 15.B26.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic [Carex scandinavica] swards
description: Communities of the middle levels of exposed shores of the southern Baltic dominated by [Carex scandinavica] ([Carex serotina] ssp. [pulchella], "[Carex pulchellum]", [Carex oederi] ssp. [pulchella], [Carex viridula] var. [pulchella]), characteristic, in particular, of southeastern Sweden.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic brackish saltmarsh communities
description: Communities of saltmarshes of the Atlantic and its connected seas developed in areas of varying salinity and humidity, such as estuaries, in coastal basins with fresh water input and along brackish seashores, such as those of the inner Baltic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pearlwort-saltmarsh grass swards
description: Communities of saltmarshes of the Atlantic, North Sea and Baltic coasts of Europe, from the Iberian peninsula to Scandinavia, developed in areas of varying salinity and humidity, in particular, in estuarine saltmarshes, in saltmarsh inner basins, in dike-enclsoed saltmarshes, with [Spergularia marina], [Puccinellia distans], [Puccinellia fasciculata], [Puccinellia retroflexa], [Puccinellia maritima], [Triglochin maritima], [Potentilla anserina] and [Halimione portulacoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic [Carex paleacea] swards
description: Formations of the brackish shores of the inner Baltic, dominated by [Carex paleacea], with [Eleocharis uniglumis] and [Agrostis stolonifera], accompanied by [Triglochin maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic [Carex mackenziei] swards
description: Communities of brackish lower shores of the northern and eastern Baltic dominated by [Carex mackenziei].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic salt basin [Agrostis]-[Triglochin] swards
description: Baltic [Agrostis stolonifera]-[Triglochin palustre] formations of depressions submitted to marine salt precipitation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic [Deschampsia bottnica] swards
description: Communities of the lower levels of the brackish marshes of the Gulf of Bothnia, characteristic of exposed coasts, dominated by the endemic [Deschampsia cespitosa] ssp. [bottnica] ([Deschampsia bottnica]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic saltmarsh and drift rough grass communities
description: Nitrophilous tall grass communities of Atlantic saltmarshes, green beaches and beach drift accumulations, dominated by [Elymus pycnanthus] ([Agropyron pungens]), [Elymus repens], [Festuca arundinacea] or sometimes tall perennial forbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saltmarsh and drift sea couch beds
description: Saltmarsh rough tall grass beds formed by [Elymus pycnanthus] ([Agropyron pungens]), limited to the coasts of Iberia, France and southern Britain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saltmarsh and drift common couch beds
description: Rough tall grass beds formed by [Elymus repens] in saltmarshes, on green beaches and on northern sand, gravel or pebble beaches of the coasts of the Atlantic, the North Sea and the Baltic, in areas of accumulation of organic material.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saltmarsh and drift bindweed-couch beds
description: Nitrophilous communities of older accumulations of organic drift on sand, gravel or pebble beaches of southern Norway dominated by [Calystegia sepium], [Elymus repens] and [Galeopsis bifida], accompanied by [Potentilla anserina], [Rumex crispus], [Cirsium arvense], [Vicia cracca], [Galium aparine], [Geranium pratense], [Sonchus arvensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Festuca arundinacea] drift communities
description: Beds of tall [Festuca arundinacea] colonizing shores of southern Baltic and Baelts coasts and archipelagoes on pebble or sand substrates rich in drift material, often forming a belt along high water line, above saltmarsh communities of unit 15.33. Accompanying grasses and forbs include [Agrostis gigantea], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Elymus repens] ([Elytrigia repens]), [Festuca rubra], [Potentilla anserina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern European [Lepidium] drift communities
description: Uncommon [Lepidium latifolium]-dominated communities of the shores of southern Scandinavia and the Baltic States, developed on older drift banks and sands with diffuse drift layers. [Elymus repens] ([Elytrigia repens]) is sometimes subdominant. Accompanying species include [Galium aparine], [Galium verum], [Linaria vulgaris], [Rumex crispus], [Solanum dulcamara].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic saltmarsh driftline annual communities
description: Annual formations of pioneers colonizing driftlines forming within Atlantic saltmarshes, with [Atriplex littoralis], [Atriplex hastata], [Beta maritima], [Matricaria maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific lower schorre communities
description: Communities of the lower part of the coastal saltmarshes of the Pacific and its connected seas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific upper schorre communities
description: Communities of the upper levels of the salt meadows of the Pacific and its connected seas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific oligo-haline communities
description: Communities of saltmarshes of the Pacific and its connected seas developed in areas of varying salinity and humidity, such as estuaries, in coastal basins with fresh water input and along brackish seashores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific saltmarsh rough grass communities
description: Nitrophilous tall grass communities of Pacific saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific saltmarsh driftline communities
description: Annual formations of pioneers colonizing driftlines forming within Pacific saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral inland salt meadows
description: Salt meadows of inland salt basins of the nemoral zones of western Europe and eastern Asia. Continental saltmarshes of interior middle Europe are remarkable, extremely threatened communities occurring in a few isolated stations of Saxony and Lower Saxony, Schleswig-Holstein, Thuringe, Hesse, Lorraine, Auvergne, the Midlands and southeastern Poland (lower Nida valley). They comprise this unit and continental glasswort swards (unit 15.112).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior European saltmarsh grass meadows
description: Meadows of [Puccinellia distans] occupying the lower levels of inland salt basins of the nemoral zone of western Europe, with fairly extended periods of inundation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior European saltmarsh rush and couch beds
description: Formations dominated by [Juncus gerardi] or [Elymus repens], with [Triglochin maritima], [Glaux maritima], [Melilotus dentata], of the upper levels of inland salt basins of the nemoral zone of western and central Europe, on damp, less saline soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior European stalked orache beds
description: Formations dominated by the threatened [Halimione pedunculata] restricted to saltmarshes east and south of the Harz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian travertine swards
description: Closed halo-hygrophile swards of [Scirpus pumilus], [Triglochin maritima], [Glaux maritima], [Centaurium littorale] ssp. [uliginosum], [Plantago maritima] ssp. [salsa] with [Pinguicula vulgaris], [Parnassia palustris], [Primula farinosa], endemic to the inner Carpathian Zipser valley of Slovakia, where they colonize travertine concretions permanently washed by mineralized spring waters.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pacific saltmarshes
description: Salt meadows of inland salt basins of the nemoral zone of eastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic salt meadows
description: Salt meadows of saltmarshes, lagoons and deltas of the coasts and coastal regions of the Mediterranean and of the subtropical Atlantic, including those of southwestern France, the Iberian peninsula, the Macaronesian Islands, mediterranean North Africa south to the Oued Tensift at 32øN and mediterraneo-Saharan Africa between 32øN and 27øN, and of endoreic interior basins of mediterranean Iberia and mediterranean North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean tall rush saltmarshes
description: Beds of tall [Juncus maritimus], [Juncus rigidus] ([Juncus maritimus] var. [arabicus], [Juncus arabicus]) or [Juncus acutus] of saline grounds of Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coastlands and of endoreic interior basins of mediterranean Iberia and mediterranean North Africa, forming, in particular, in periodically inundated depressions , where they may associate with [Carex extensa], [Iris spuria], [Gladiolus communis], [Aster tripolium], [Sonchus maritimus], [Sonchus crassifolius] or other elements of units 15.52 and 15.54, and in sandy dunal depressions, where they may alternate with stands of [Schoenus nigricans] or other formations of unit 15.53.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Mediterranean coastal tall rush saltmarshes
description: Beds of [Juncus maritimus] or [Juncus acutus] of saltmarshes, periodically inundated saline basins and humid dunal depressions of the Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts and coastlands of Europe and western Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior Iberian tall rush saltmarshes
description: Beds of [Juncus maritimus] or [Juncus acutus] of periodically inundated depressions of the endoreic interior basins of Mediterranean Iberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afro-Mediterranean tall rush saltmarshes
description: Beds of tall rushes, mostly [Juncus rigidus] ([Juncus maritimus] var. [arabicus], [Juncus arabicus]), sometimes [Juncus maritimus] or [Juncus acutus], of saltmarshes, periodically inundated saline basins and humid dunal depressions of the Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts and endoreic interior basins of North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean short rush-sedge-barley-clover coastal saltmeadows
description: Humid meadows of low vegetation dominated by [Juncus gerardi], [Carex divisa], [Carex extensa], [Schoenus nigricans], [Triglochin maritima], [Hordeum marinum] or [Trifolium spp.] and [Lotus spp.] of the edges of brackish lagoons of Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts of Europe, western Asia and North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean halo-psammophile meadows
description: Drier, dense formations of sandy soils at the foot of dunes, or between dunes and lagoons of the Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts of Europe and North Africa, and of the endoreic interior basins of Mediterranean Iberia, with [Plantago crassifolia], [Schoenus nigricans], [Juncus littoralis], [Spartina versicolor] ([Spartina patens], [Spartina juncea]), [Elymus elongatus], [Inula crithmoides], all of which may dominate and form physiognomically distinct, sometimes almost monospecific, facies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Mediterranean coastal halo-psammophile meadows
description: Psammo-halophile swards of the foot of dunes and of dune hollows of the Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts of Europe. [Plantago crassifolia], [Schoenus nigricans], [Juncus littoralis], [Spartina versicolor] ([Spartina patens], [Spartina juncea]), [Scirpus holoschoenus] may associate in communities or dominate stands that occur alone or in mosaics, often interspersed with psammophile tall [Juncus] stands of unit 15.51.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior Iberian halo-psammophile meadows
description: Psammo-halophile swards of endoreic interior basins of Mediterranean Iberia, with [Plantago crassifolia] and [Schoenus nigricans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afro-Mediterranean halo-psammophile meadows
description: Psammo-halophile swards of the foot of dunes and of dune hollows of the Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts of North Africa. [Plantago crassifolia], [Schoenus nigricans], [Spartina versicolor] ([Spartina patens], [Spartina juncea]), [Sporobolus pungens] are important elements of various communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior Iberian salt basin grass and small rush swards
description: Salt meadows peculiar to the lowest, wettest parts of interior Iberian depressions, dominated by [Puccinellia fasciculata] or [Aeluropus littoralis] in the very lowest areas, or, slightly higher, by [Juncus gerardi]. The higher, drier ground that surrounds them is occupied either by other salt meadow communities that are less differentiated from the coastal communities (units 15.512, 15.532) or by salt scrubs (unit 15.615).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean coastal-saltmarsh grass swards
description: Dense formations of perennial halophile grasses, in particular, [Puccinellia festuciformis] ([Puccinellia palustris]) or [Aeluropus littoralis], of Mediterranean coasts and their coastal lagoons.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean saltmarsh driftlines
description: Communities of annuals forming on accumulations of organic debris in saltmarshes and saline depressions of the Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts and of endoreic basins of the Mediterranean interior, in particular, of mediterranean Iberia, with [Atriplex hastata], [Suaeda splendens], [Suaeda maritima], [Bassia hirsuta], [Salsola soda], [Rumex pulcher].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean saltmarsh couch-wormwood stands
description: Formations of [Elymus] or [Artemisia] fringing Mediterranean and interior Iberian saline wetlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean saltmarsh couch stands
description: Formations of [Elymus] of Mediterranean and interior Iberian saline wetlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean saltmarsh wormwood fringes
description: Formations of [Artemisia] fringing Mediterranean and interior Iberian saline wetlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean fine-leaved rush beds
description: Medium-tall [Juncus subulatus] beds, often forming facies within [Arthrocnemum] scrubs of Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-nemoral saltmarsh scrubs
description: Scrubby formations of woody glassworts ([Arthrocnemum]), seablites ([Suaeda]), [Halimione], [Halocnemum] or [Limoniastrum] of saltmarshes and salt basins of mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic regions of the western Palaearctic, distributed in coastal saltmarshes of the Mediterranean, in endoreic interior basins of Iberia and mediterranean North Africa, and in warm temperate Atlantic coastal saltmarshes of Iberia, mediterranean and Saharo-mediterranean North Africa, the Macaronesian Islands and southwestern France, north locally to the English Channel and the southern North Sea. Scrubby formations of saltmarshes of the temperate coasts of the western Pacific and its connected seas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean saltmarsh scrubs
description: Low shrubby expanses of woody glassworts, seablites, sea purslanes or [Halocnemum], characteristic of temporarily inundated saltmarshes of Mediterranean coasts, southwestern Iberian and northwestern African Atlantic coasts and interior Iberian basins. They can be further subdivided according to dominant species, generally associated with patterns of inundation. [Cistanche lutea] characterises many southern formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Creeping glasswort mats
description: Low shrubby carpets of prostrate [Arthrocnemum perenne] of wettest areas of coastal marshes of Mediterranean, southwestern Iberian and northwestern African Atlantic coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shrubby glasswort thickets
description: Stands of robust [Arthrocnemum fruticosum], capable of forming extensive low, dense thickets in coastal marshes of Mediterranean, southwestern Iberian and northwestern African Atlantic coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Glaucous glasswort thickets
description: Shrubby formations of [Arthrocnemum glaucum]. Along northern Mediterranean shores, they often occupy somewhat drier sites such as shell banks in saline lagoons; in the North African coastal marshes of Cyrenaica, Tripolitana, Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco, they constitute the only [Arthrocnemum] formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shrubby seablite thickets
description: Shrubby formations of [Suaeda vera] occupying drier elevations of coastal saltmarshes of Mediterranean, southwestern Iberian and northwestern African Atlantic coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior Iberian salt scrubs
description: Formations of woody glassworts and seablites of Iberian interior salt basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior woody seablite scrubs
description: [Suaeda pruinosa] ([Suaeda fruticosa] var. [brevifolia]) formations of Iberian interior salt basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior glaucous glasswort scrubs
description: [Arthrocnemum glaucum] formations of Iberian interior salt basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior creeping glasswort scrubs
description: [Arthrocnemum perenne] formations of Iberian interior salt basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean sea-purslane-woody glasswort scrubs
description: [Halimione portulacoides]-rich facies within [Arthrocnemum] communities of coastal saltmarshes of Mediterranean, southwestern Iberian and northwestern African Atlantic coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Halocnemum] scrub
description: Salt scrubs of Mediterranean coastal saltmarshes dominated by [Halocnemum strobilaceum], characteristic of arid African coasts, with a few outposts on dry coasts of European peninsulas and islands. Formations of the desert coasts of the Sinai Mediterranean and the Red Sea and of endoreic basins of the Anatolian and North African transition regions between Mediterranean and desert or steppe zones are included under units 15.A and 15.C.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Mediterranean [Halocnemum] scrub
description: Rare and local formations dominated by the often sparse clumps of [Halocnemum strobilaceum], usually associated with [Arthrocnemum glaucum], sometimes with [Arthrocnemum fruticosum], limited to southeastern Spain, southern Sardinia, western Sicily, Toscany, Emilia-Romagna, Albania, Greece and Cyprus, apparently extinct in the Maltese Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afro-Mediterranean [Halocnemum] scrub
description: Salt scrubs of saltmarshes of the North African coasts of the Mediterranean dominated by [Halocnemum strobilaceum], characteristic of arid coasts between Egypt and Tunisia, occuring west to Tunis. Formations of the desert coasts of the Sinai Mediterranean and of endoreic basins of the North African transition regions between Mediterranean and desert or steppe zones are included under units 15.A and 15.C.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hypersaline [Limonium ferulaceum] scrubs
description: Salt scrubs of hypersaline Mediterranean coastal saltmarshes dominated by the leafless scaly [Limonium ferulaceum], characteristic of northwestern Africa, with irradiations in Algarve and western Andalucia and in Sicily, at Trapani and on the Isola Grande of the Marsala marshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic salt scrubs
description: Sea purslane, glasswort and seablite scrubs of northern Atlantic and North Sea coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Silver scrubs
description: Shrubby [Halimione portulacoides] communities of middle levels of Atlantic schorres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic creeping glasswort mats
description: [Arthrocnemum perenne]-dominated formations of the British Isles, the Atlantic coasts of France and of Iberia, except for the extreme southwest of the peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic shrubby seablite scrubs
description: [Suaeda vera]-dominated formations of the British Isles, where they are limited to the coast of Norfolk, and of the Atlantic coasts of France and of Iberia, except for the extreme southwest of the peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Franco-Iberian shrubby seablite scrubs
description: [Suaeda vera]-dominated formations of the Atlantic coasts of France and of Iberia, except for the extreme southwest of the peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Norfolk shrubby seablite scrubs
description: [Suaeda vera]-dominated formations of the British Isles, limited to the coast of Norfolk, with [Halimion portulacoides], [Limonium binervosum], [Limonium bellidifolium], [Frankenia laevis], [Puccinellia maritima], [Armeria maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic shrubby glasswort scrubs
description: [Arthrocnemum fruticosum]-dominated formations of the Atlantic coasts of France and of Iberia, except for the extreme southwest of the peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Limoniastrum] scrubs
description: Formations of often large, silver-glaucous shrubs of [Limoniastrum monopetalum] with showy pink flowers in late spring, of drier parts of Mediterranean and Iberian saltmarshes, distributed locally in North Africa, the Iberian peninsula, the southern Italian peninsula, western Sicily, Lampedusa, Sardinia and Crete.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian saltmarsh scrubs
description: Low shrubby expanses of woody glassworts, seablites, sea purslanes or [Zygophyllum], characteristic of temporarily inundated saltmarshes of Canary Island coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian creeping glasswort scrubs
description: Formations of [Arthrocnemum perenne] occupying the lowest level of the saltmarshes of the coasts of Fuerteventura, Lanzarote and Isla de Lobos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Zygophyllum] saltmarshes
description: Formations of the Canario-Saharan halophyte [Zygophyllum fontanesii], associated with [Arthrocnemum glaucum], of the higher level of the saltmarshes of the eastern islands and, very locally, of Alegranza and La Graciosa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian [Salsola] saltmarshes
description: Formations of [Salsola longifolia], often dense and sometimes up to 2 metres high, of Canary Island coastal marshes, barranco openings and lagoons.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific saltmarsh scrubs
description: Scrubby formations of saltmarshes of the temperate coasts of the western Pacific and its connected seas.
