description: Communities dominated by grasses, chenopods or sea-lavenders, formed on solonetz or solonchak-solonetz soils in the rills of salt steppes of the Sarmatic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Puccinellia] solonetz swards
description: Grassy formations of Sarmatic solonetz and solonchak-solonetz soils constituted by [Puccinellia distans] ([Puccinellia limosa]) or [Puccinellia festuciformis] ssp. [convoluta], accompanied by [Plantago maritima], [Spergularia media], [Aster tripolium], [Juncus gerardi], [Scorzonera austriaca] and [Camphorosma annua].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Camphorosma] hollows
description: Communities of solonetz or solonchak-solonetz soils of river terraces of the Sarmatic region dominated by [Camphorosma annua], often accompanied by [Puccinellia distans] or [Puccinellia festuciformis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Carex distans] solonetz hollows
description: Communities of solonetz or solonchak-solonetz soils of the Sarmatic region dominated by [Carex distans], with [Aster tripolium], [Juncus compressus], [Taraxacum bessarabicum] and [Agrostis stolonifera] ([Agrostis stolonizans]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic solonchak hollows
description: Communities dominated by perennial grasses and herbs or by steppe and semidesert zone annuals, developed on solonchak soils of the Sarmatic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Lepidium] solonchak hollows
description: Solonchak swards, of Ponto-Pannonic affinities, of northern Moldavia, massively dominated by [Lepidium cartilagineum] ssp. [crassifolium], with [Puccinellia distans] ssp. [limosa] ([Puccinellia limosa]), [Camphorosma annua], [Agropyron elongatum], [Plantago maritima], [Spergularia media], [Dianthus guttatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Puccinellia convoluta] solonchak hollows
description: Communities of solonchak depressions of the Sarmatic region dominated by [Puccinellia festuciformis] ssp. [convoluta] ([Puccinellia bilykiana]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Beckmannia]-[Agrostis] solonchak hollows
description: Communities of solonchak depressions of the Sarmatic region, with a strongly fluctuating water regime that may include acute periods of drought, dominated by [Beckmannia eruciformis], [Agrostis stolonifera] ([Agrostis stolonizans]), [Puccinellia distans], [Juncus compressus], characteristic, in particular, of the middle Don region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain, of the basins of the Dnieper, the Don, the Kouban, the Manytch, the upper Kuma and upper Terek, associated with the steppes of unit 34.923. Coastal saltmarshes of the northern Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, except those of southern Crimea, of mediterranean affinities and included in unit 15.A24.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic saline steppes
description: Communities dominated by low tufted grasses and subshrubs, in particular [Festuca pseudovina] and [Artemisia spp.], occupying higher, drier solonetz ground in salt steppes of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic saline meadows
description: Salt-meadow communities of medium tall often tussock-forming grasses, sedges or rushes of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic solonetz hollows
description: Communities dominated by grasses, chenopods or sea-lavenders, formed on solonetz or solonchak-solonetz soils in the rills of salt steppes and other inland saline flats subject to inundation and dessication of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain, as well as on the higher ground of northern Black Sea coastal saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic solonchak communities
description: Communities dominated by Ponto-Pannonic perennial grasses and herbs, or by Ponto-Caspian steppe and semidesert zone annuals and perennials, developed on solonchak or solonchak-solonetz soils of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain and of northern Black Sea coastal saltmarshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic salt scrubs
description: Scrubby formations colonizing saltmarshes and salt basins of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxinian saltmarshes
description: Saltmarshes of the southern Black Sea coast, west and north to the seaward fa‡ade of the Istranca-Stranja, of the eastern Black Sea coast, northwest to the northern limit of the peri-Caucasian deciduous woodland zone in the Kouban basin, and of the mediterranean or submediterranean woodland zone of extreme southern Crimea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of the steppe and wooded steppe belts of extreme eastern Europe and western Siberia, extending from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east, associated with the Transvolgan (Orenburg and Bachkiria), Kurgan, Ishim, Baraba, Kulunda, Barnaul, Kirgiz, Kazakh, Tarbagatai and Altai steppes of unit 34.93. Saltmarshes of the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea and other inland waterbodies of the northern Aralo-Caspian, Kura basin, western Kazakh, Dzungarian, Oust-ourt, Kyzyl Koum and Kara Koum middle Asiatic deserts and semideserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian saline steppes
description: Communities dominated by low tufted grasses and subshrubs, in particular [Festuca pseudovina] and [Artemisia spp.], occupying higher, drier solonetz ground of extreme eastern European and western Siberian salt steppes, from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian saline meadows
description: Salt-meadow communities of medium tall often tussock-forming grasses, sedges or rushes of extreme eastern European and western Siberian salt steppes, from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian solonetz hollows
description: Communities dominated by grasses, chenopods or sea-lavenders, formed on solonetz or solonchak-solonetz soils in the rills of salt steppes and other inland saline flats subject to inundation and dessication of extreme eastern European and western Siberian salt steppes, from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the eastas well as on the higher ground of saltmarshes of the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea and other inland waterbodies of the northern Aralo-Caspian, Kura basin, western Kazakh, Dzungarian, Oust-ourt, Kyzyl Koum and Kara Koum middle Asiatic deserts and semideserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian solonchak communities
description: Communities dominated by steppe perennial grasses and herbs, or by steppe and semidesert zone annuals and perennials, developed on solonchak or solonchak-solonetz soils of the saltmarshes of the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea and other inland waterbodies of the northern Aralo-Caspian, Kura basin, western Kazakh, Dzungarian, Oust-ourt, Kyzyl Koum and Kara Koum middle Asiatic deserts and semideserts, and of the salt basins of extreme eastern European and western Siberian salt steppes, from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian salt scrubs
description: Scrubby formations of [Halimione verrucifera], [Halocnemum strobilaceum] and [Nitraria schoberi], accompanied by [Artemisia spp.], [Limonium spp.], [Petrosimonia spp.], colonizing saltmarshes and salt basins of of the saltmarshes of the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea and other inland waterbodies of the northern Aralo-Caspian, Kura basin, western Kazakh, Dzungarian, Oust-ourt, Kyzyl Koum and Kara Koum middle Asiatic deserts and semideserts, and of the salt basins of extreme eastern European and western Siberian salt steppes, from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, the Songnen Plain of Northeast China, the western Loess Plateau of North China, of the Tien Shan, from the rim of the Naryn and Isyk-K”l basins eastwards, of the Sayan and Tannu mountains, associated with the steppes of unit 34.94. Saltmarshes of the inland waterbodies of the Gobi, Takla Makan, Tarim, Lop-nor, Bei-shan, Ala-shan, Ordos, Tsaidam and Pamyro-Tibetan Central Asiatic deserts and semideserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of steppic areas of the Anatolian Plateau, of Transcaucasia, of the eastern cis-Caucasian hills of Daghestan and the Terek basin, of the Iranian Plateau, the Kopet Dagh, the Pamir-Alai, the extreme western Tien-Shan, around the rim of the Ferghana basin and along the spur of the Karatau, and of northern Mesopotamia, associated with the steppes of unit 34.95. Saltmarshes of the cold desert or subdesert areas of the Iranian Plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of the western Anatolian Plateau, mostly characteristic of Lycaonia, particularly around Tuz Golu and in the region of Nigde. They are rich in endemic as well as Asiatic species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Halocnemum] steppes
description: Almost monospecific formations of [Halocnemum strobilaceum] forming the inner belt of vegetation around western Anatolian salt lakes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Artemisia]-[Salsola] steppes
description: Formations of [Artemisia fragrans], [Aeluropus lagopoides], [Camphorosma monspeliaca], [Limonium iconium], [Salsola inermis], [Salsola anatolica], [Salsola kali] forming the outermost belt of vegetation of western Anatolian halophile complexes, in contact with nonhalophile [Artemisia] steppes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian rosette steppes
description: Communities of rosette-forming sea-lavenders, prostrate perennial [Frankenia], annual [Petrosimonia] and related genera occupying clearings of Anatolian grassy or shrubby salt steppes, in particular on hypersaline soils with extreme regimes of inundation and dessication.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Frankenia hirsuta] salt steppes
description: Communities of [Frankenia hirsuta], [Limonium iconium], [Limonium gmelinii], [Camphorosma monspeliaca] forming on gently sloping rises in the vicinity of Anatolian salt lakes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Petrosimonia] salt steppes
description: Formations of [Petrosimonia nigdeensis], [Petrosimonia brachiata], [Halanthium kulpianum] ([Petrosimonia birandii]) occupying muddy sand soils in the vicinity of Anatolian salt lakes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Puccinellia]-[Limonium] salt steppes
description: Communities [Puccinellia distans] [s.l.], [Limonium gmelinii], [Limonium globuliferum] of western Anatolian halophile complexes, forming on sandy clay soils with brief periods of inundation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian [Juncus maritimus] formations
description: Saltmarsh meadows of water-logged depressions, puddles and small waterbodies of Anatolia, with [Juncus maritimus] dominant, [Limonium globuliferum], [Aeluropus lagopoides], [Puccinellia distans], [Halimione portulacoides], [Lepidium cartilagineum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Irano-Anatolian salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of Transcaucasia, the eastern cis-Caucasian hills of Daghestan and the Terek basin, eastern Anatolia and northwestern Iran, including the communities of the edges of Lake Van and Lake Urmia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Afghan salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of steppic areas of the Central and Eastern Iranian Plateau in Iran and Afghanistan, of the Kopet Dagh, the Pamir-Alai and the extreme western Tien-Shan, around the rim of the Ferghana basin and along the spur of the Karatau, associated with the steppes of unit 34.953. Communities of saltmarshes and temporary waterbodies of the cold desert or subdesert areas of Iran and Afghanistan, in particular the Dasht-i-Kewir and Dasht-i-Lut.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Mesopotamian salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and saltmarshes of the Mesopotamian steppic region bordering the Near Eastern Saharo-Sindian deserts, extending north to southeastern Turkey and Khuzestan in western Iran. Among characteristic species are [Suaeda palaestina], [Seidlitzia rosmarinus], [Alhagi maurorum], [Bassia eriophora], [Suaeda fruticosa], [Atriplex leucoclada], [Atriplex halimus], [Suaeda aegyptiaca], [Juncus maritimus] var. [arabicus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt steppes and interior saltmarshes of the steppic regions of the North African transition zone between the Mediterranean region and the Sahara ("Mauritanian Steppe").
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Yakutian boreal salt steppes and saltmarshes
description: Salt meadows, salt steppe meadows, swamp meadows, alases and salt marshes of the middle Lena basin of eastern Siberia, formed in regions of extreme continentality near the southern edge of the permafrost and the northern limit of the taiga belt, associated with the steppes of unit 34.96.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic salt meadows
description: Coastal saltmarshes of the Arctic zone, along the coasts of Greenland, the Norwegian Sea, Greenland Sea, Barents Sea, Kara Sea, Laptev Sea, East Siberian Sea, Chukchi Sea and Glacial Ocean coasts of northern Iceland, Jan Mayen, Spitsbergen, Bear Island, Finnmark in northern Norway, Franz Josef Land, northern continental Russia, Kolguyev Island, Novaya Zemlya, continental Siberia and the Siberian archipelagoes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lower shore arctic salt meadows
description: Species-poor communities of the lower shores of arctic Eurasia and Greenland, submitted to winter sea ice.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Puccinellia phryganodes] salt meadows
description: Open, sparse communities of the lower, intertidal, sector of saltmarshes of arctic coasts of Eurasia, from northern Troms and Finnmark eastwards, of the archipelagoes of the Eurasian polar basin, including Spitzbergen, Nova Zemlya,  and the New Siberian archipelago, of Jan Mayen and of Greenland, dominated by [Puccinellia phryganodes] [s.l.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Carex subspathacea] salt meadows
description: Lower shore salt meadow communities of northwestern Greenland, northeastern Greenland, Iceland, Spitzbergen, arctic Norway, the Kola peninsula, Yakutia, developed on clay substrates, dominated by [Carex subspathacea], often accompanied by [Puccinellia maritima] and [Puccinellia phryganodes]. In Iceland, [Puccinellia phryganodes] is absent and [Puccinellia capillaris] may codominate with [Carex subspathacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic [Puccinellia maritima] salt meadows
description: Salt meadows of the lower and middle shores of the coasts of arctic Eurasia, in particular, of western Iceland, western Finnmark, the Kola peninsula and Yakutia, dominated by [Puccinellia maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic [Carex ursina] salt meadows
description: Salt meadow communities of the lower and middle shores of arctic coasts, in particular of northeastern Greenland, Spitzbergen, Nova Zemlya, Yakutia, dominated by [Carex ursina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Upper shore arctic salt meadows
description: Coastal saltmarshes of the upper shores of arctic Eurasia and Greenland submitted to winter sea ice.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Carex glareosa-Festuca rubra] salt meadows
description: Upper shore salt meadow communities of arctic coasts of northern Norway, the Kola peninsula, Iceland and Greenland, extending locally along boreal-Atlantic coasts in Iceland and northwestern Norway, as well as in the Gulf of Bothnia, dominated by [Carex glareosa] and [Festuca rubra], often with [Gentianella detonsa], [Potentilla egedii], [Stellaria humifusa], [Carex subspathacea] and with abundant [Drepanocladus uncinatus] in the ground layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Kobresia] salt meadows
description: Middle and upper shore communities of Iceland dominated by [Kobresia myosuroides], with [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] often very prominent, occupying relatively dry, high, stony areas of coastal banks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Puccinellia capillaris] salt meadows
description: Usually open saltmarsh communities of upper shores of arctic Eurasia dominated by [Puccinellia capillaris] ([Puccinellia distans] ssp. [borealis]) with [Festuca rubra] and [Cochlearia officinalis], characteristic, in particular, of exposed wet shingle beaches with little fine material in northern Norway and northern Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic saltmarsh [Festuca rubra] swards
description: Saltmarsh communities of upper shores of arctic Eurasia, in particular, of northern Norway and northern Iceland, constituting a fescue-dominated facies of unit 15.B23.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic moss-[Dupontia] salt meadows
description: Communities of arctic coasts dominated by [Dupontia fisheri], [Dupontia pelligera] or [Dupontia psilosantha], characteristic, in particular, of brackish upper shores of Greenland, Spitzbergen, the New Siberian archipelago, Yakutia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Carex rariflora] salt meadows
description: Salt meadow communities of brackish upper shores of Finnmark dominated by [Carex rariflora], often with [Carex salina], [Calamagrostis stricta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic [Carex mackenziei] salt meadows
description: Saltmarsh communities of northern Norway, northern Russia and northern Iceland dominated by [Carex mackenziei] with [Agrostis stolonifera], accompanied by [Drepanocladus aduncus], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], characteristic of brackish basins of the upper shore.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Carex salina] salt meadows
description: Low swards of middle and upper shores of northern Iceland, northern Norway and the Kola peninsula dominated by [Carex salina], developed, in relatively exposed situations, on substrates of coarse material.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sulphurous arctic salt meadows
description: Communities of the arctic coasts of Eurasia developed in brackish water on sulphurous gleys, in particular, [Hippuris tetraphylla] beds of brackish shores of Finnmark and northern Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Sindian saltmarshes
description: Frutescent and herbaceous halophilous communities of inland saltmarshes and temporary waterbodies of the Saharo-Sindian zone, and of coastal saltmarshes and lagoon fringes of the desert coasts of the African Atlantic, of the extreme southeastern Mediterranean, of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Sea and of the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai saltmarshes
description: Frutescent and herbaceous halophilous communities of coastal saltmarshes, lagoon fringes and inundatable depressions of the Sinai coasts of the extreme southeastern Mediterranean and of the adjacent northern Sinai plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai [Halocnemum] saltmarshes
description: Frutescent halophilous communities of coastal saltmarshes, lagoon fringes and inundatable depressions of the northern Sinai dominated by [Halocnemum strobilaceum], usually occupying the wettest ground.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai [Arthrocnemum] saltmarshes
description: Frutescent halophilous communities of coastal saltmarshes, lagoon fringes and inundatable depressions of the northern Sinai dominated by [Arthrocnemum glaucum], usually forming a girdle on the drier side of [Halocnemum] formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai [Nitraria] saltmarshes
description: Frutescent halophilous communities of coastal saltmarshes, lagoon fringes and inundatable depressions of the northern Sinai dominated by [Nitraria retusa], associated with [Suaeda vermiculata], [Suaeda vera], [Limoniastrum monopetalum], [Frankenia hirsuta], [Halogeton alopecuroides], [Limonium pruinosum], usually forming on higher ground adjacent to [Halocnemum] and [Arthrocnemum] communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai [Zygophyllum] saltmarshes
description: Frutescent halophilous communities of coastal saltmarshes, lagoon fringes and inundatable depressions of the northern Sinai dominated by [Zygophyllum album], usually forming on the lower parts of dune scarps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai [Juncus rigidus] saltmarshes
description: Tall rush communities of coastal saltmarshes, lagoon fringes and inundatable depressions of the northern Sinai dominated by [Juncus rigidus] ([Juncus maritimus] var. [arabicus]), often occupying the central, wettest parts of less salty depressions, surrounded by [Halocnemum] and [Arthrocnemum] belts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic desert saltmarshes
description: Frutescent and herbaceous halophilous communities of coastal saltmarshes and lagoon fringes of the desert coasts of the African Atlantic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Red Sea-Indian Ocean saltmarshes
description: Frutescent and herbaceous halophilous communities of coastal saltmarshes and lagoon fringes of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Sea and of the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior Saharan saltmarshes
description: Frutescent and herbaceous halophilous communities of inland saltmarshes and temporary waterbodies of the Sahara.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interior Arabian saltmarshes
description: Frutescent and herbaceous halophilous communities of inland saltmarshes and temporary waterbodies of the Arabian Desert.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical salt meadows
description: Formations of [Paspalum vaginatum], [Sesuvium portulacastrum], [Sporobolus virginicus], [Philoxerus vermicularis] of intertidal or inundatable areas of tropical coasts of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal sand dunes and sand beaches
description: Sand-covered shorelines of the oceans, their connected seas and associated coastal lagoons, fashioned by the action of wind or waves. They include gently sloping beaches and beach-ridges, formed by sands brought by waves, longshore  drift and storm waves, as well as dunes, formed by eolian deposits, though sometimes refashioned by waves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sand beaches
description: Gently sloping sand-covered shorelines fashioned by wave action along the coasts of the oceans of the Palaearctic region, their connected seas and associated coastal lagoons.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Unvegetated sand beaches
description: Sandy beaches of the oceans of the Palaearctic region, their connected seas and associated coastal lagoons, devoid of phanerogamic vegetation. Mediolittoral (intertidal) and supralittoral invertebrate communities listed under 11.27 can be combined with 16.11 to record detailed habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sand beach driftline communities
description: Formations of the coasts of the Palaearctic region, composed mostly of a few annual species, occupying accumulations of drift material and sands rich in nitrogenous organic matter, usually comprising [Cakile maritima], [Salsola kali], [Atriplex spp.], [Polygonum spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic sand beach annual communities
description: Annual communities of sand beaches of the low Arctic and high Arctic oceanic zones of the Palaearctic Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic oceans, with [Cakile edentula] ssp. [islandica] ([Cakile arctica]), [Atriplex lapponica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eurasian Arctic sand beach annual communities
description: Annual communities of sand beaches of the Polar Basin coasts of continental Eurasia, from Finnmark eastwards, with [Atriplex lapponica] ([Atriplex longipes] ssp. [praecox] [p.]), [Polygonum norvegicum] and [Cakile edentula] ssp. [islandica] ([Cakile arctica]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic sand beach annual communities
description: Annual communities of Icelandic sand beaches, on fine sands, with [Cakile edentula] ssp. [islandica] ([Cakile arctica]) and [Atriplex glabriuscula]. Outlying stations occur within the boreal zone in southern Iceland and the Faeroe Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European sand beach annual communities
description: Annual halonitrophilous communities of the sand beaches of the temperate North Atlantic, the North Sea, the English Channel, the Irish Sea and the Baltic, with [Suaeda maritima], [Bassia hirsuta], [Cakile maritima], [Salsola kali], [Beta maritima], [Atriplex spp.], [Glaucium flavum], [Polygonum spp.], [Mertensia maratima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic sand beach annual communities
description: Annual driftline communities of the sand beaches of the temperate North Atlantic, the North Sea, the English Channel and the Irish Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic sand beach annual communities
description: Annual driftline communities of central and southern Baltic sand beaches, with [Cakile maritima] ssp. [baltica], [Atriplex littoralis], [Atriplex calotheca], [Atriplex hastata], [Salsola kali], [Polygonum aviculare], [Polygonum oxyspermum], [Senecio vulgaris], [Matricaria perforata], [Matricaria maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Bothnian sand beach annual communities
description: Annual driftline communities of the sand beaches of the Gulf of Bothnia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan sand beach driftline communities
description: Annual communities of sand beaches of the Mediterranean, Black Sea and Mediterraneo-Atlantic coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Tethyan sand beach annual communities
description: Annual communities of sand beaches of the Mediterranean and the subtropical Atlantic, between Portugal and the southern limit of the Mediterraneo-Saharan transition zone at 27øN.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic sea rocket communities
description: Sparse annual communities of weakly to moderately nitrogenated upper levels of sand beaches of the Mediterranean and of the subtropical Atlantic, from southwest Iberia to Safi in northwestern Africa, and in the Canary Islands, dominated by prostrate [Cakile maritima] ssp. [aegyptiaca], or, in northern areas, [Cakile maritima]  ssp. [maritima], and [Salsola kali].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Cakile susica] communities
description: Communities of sand beaches of the Atlantic coasts of northwestern Africa, between Essaouira and Tiznit, dominated by the giant annual [Cakile maritima] ssp. [susica], with [Salsola kali] and sometimes [Ononis tournefortii], [Lotus pseudocreticus], [Mesembryanthemum crystallinum], [Cyperus capitatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic sand beach composite communities
description: Annual communities of sand beaches of the Mediterranean and the subtropical Atlantic dominated by, or rich in, composites, in particular, formations, mostly of the Adriatic and Aegean, dominated by the anthropogenic [Xanthium strumarium] ssp. [italicum], formations of eastern Iberia dominated by tall knapweeds [Centaurea sonchifolia], [Centaurea seridis] ssp. [maritima], [Centauria aspera], [Centaurea albuferae], with [Cakile maritima] ssp. [aegyptiaca] and [Sporobolus pungens], formations of the eastern basin, including Cyprus, dominated by [Anthemis tomentosa] ([Anthemis muenteriana]) or [Centaurea aegialophila], communities of the western Mediterranean and the warm temperate Atlantic dominated by [Matricaria maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic sand beach chenopodid communities
description: Strongly nitrophile annual communities of sand beaches of the Mediterranean and of the subtropical Atlantic dominated by chenopodids, in particular, [Atriplex spp.], [Salsola kali], [Salsola soda], [Suaeda splendens], [Kochia hirsuta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic sand beach annual communities
description: Annual halonitrophilous communities of sand beaches of the Black Sea, with [Cakile maritima] ssp. [euxina], [Salsola kali] ssp. [ruthenica], [Salsola kali] ssp. [tragus], [Atriplex hastata], [Polygonum maritimum], [Euphorbia peplis], [Euphorbia paralias], [Glaucium flavum], [Xanthium strumarium] ssp. [italicum], [Convolvulus lineatus], [Convolvulus persicus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic sand beach perennial communities
description: Halonitrophilous communities of Black Sea sand beaches dominated by perennial herbs, including [Crambe maritima] ssp. [pontica], [Argusia sibirica], [Lactuca tatarica], [Petasites spurius] or [Trachomitum venetum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic sand beach [Crambe] communities
description: Halonitrophilous communities of Black Sea sand beaches, dominated by [Crambe maritima] ssp. [pontica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Pontic sand beach [Crambe] communities
description: Halonitrophilous communities of sand beaches of the southwestern Black Sea coasts of Turkey in Europe and Bulgaria, dominated by [Crambe maritima] ssp. [pontica], with [Lepidotrichum uechtritzianum], [Cakile maritima] ssp. [euxina], [Salsola kali] ssp. [ruthenica], [Euphorbia peplis], [Polygonum maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Pontic sand beach [Crambe] communities
description: Halonitrophilous beach communities of the northwestern Black Sea coasts and the Danube delta, dominated by [Crambe maritima] ssp. [pontica] and [Eryngium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic sand beach [Crambe] communities
description: Halonitrophilous communities of northern Black Sea and Azov Sea sand beaches dominated by [Crambe maritima] ssp. [pontica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic sand beach [Lactuca] communities
description: Halonitrophilous communities of Black Sea sand beaches dominated by [Lactuca tatarica], with [Glaucium leiocarpum], [Glaucium flavum], [Apera spica-venti] ssp. [maritima], [Salsola soda], [Euphorbia peplis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic sand beach [Argusia] communities
description: Halonitrophilous communities of Black Sea sand beaches dominated by [Argusia sibirica] ([Tournefortia sibirica]), with [Cakile maritima], [Salsola soda], [Elymus sabulosus], [Eryngium maritimum], [Gypsophila perfoliata], [Aeluropus littoralis], [Puccinellia distans] ssp. [limosa], [Plantago maritima], [Cynodon dactylon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic sand beach [Petasites] communities
description: Halonitrophilous communities of Black Sea sand beaches dominated by [Petasites spurius] with [Argusia sibirica], [Bromus squarrosus], [Corispermum nitidum], [Lactuca serriola], [Trifolium fragiferum], [Salsola kali] ssp. [tragus], [Eryngium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Pacific sand beach annual communities
description: Annual communities of driftlines of the temperate and subtropical western Pacific and its connected seas, including those of southern Amurland, Japan, Korea and China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic sand beach perennial communities
description: Perennial halonitrophilous communities of sand, gravelly sand and gravel cordons of upper beaches of the arctic and boreal sea coasts of Eurasia formed by [Leymus arenarius] ([Elymus arenarius]), [Ammophila arenaria], [Honkenya peploides], [Elymus farctus], [Elymus repens], [Mertensia maritima], accompanied by [Atriplex spp.] ([Atriplex prostrata], [Atriplex longipes] ssp. [praecox], [Atriplex glabriuscula]), [Polygonum aviculare], [Cakile maritima], [Cakile arctica], [Petasites spurius], [Potentilla anserina]. Representatives of these communities occur very locally within the nemoral zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North Sea sand beach perennial communities
description: [Leymus arenarius]-dominated perennial halonitrophilous communities of upper beaches of North Sea coasts of southern Norway, Jutland, Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony, the Netherlands, England, Scotland and Orkney, and of the Danish coast of the Kattegat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic sand beach perennial communities
description: [Leymus arenarius]-dominated perennial halonitrophilous communities of southern and central Baltic upper beaches, often with [Petasites spurius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Bothnian sand beach perennial communities
description: Perennial halonitrophilous communities of the upper beaches of the Gulf of Bothnia dominated by [Leymus arenarius] and [Festuca rubra] ssp. [arenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic sand beach perennial communities
description: Perennial halonitrophilous communities of upper beaches of Iceland dominated by [Leymus arenarius] or [Mertensia maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic sand beach [Leymus] communities
description: [Leymus arenarius]-dominated perennial halonitrophilous communities of upper beaches of Iceland, with irradiations in the Faeroe Islands. Accompanying plants include [Honkenya peploides], [Potentilla anserina], [Cakile arctica], [Silene uniflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Mertensia] mats
description: Upper shore communities of Iceland and the Faeroe Islands dominated by [Mertensia maritima], often in almost pure stands, characteristic of gravelly-stoney substrates. They represent an irradiation into the boreal zone of the arctic unit 16.1352.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic sand beach perennial communities
description: Perennial halonitrophilous communities of upper beaches of arctic, mostly low arctic, coasts of the Polar Basin, except of those of Iceland, recorded in particular from Greenland, Lapland and Russia, dominated by [Leymus arenarius] or [Leymus mollis], by [Festuca rubra] ssp. [arenaria], or by [Mertensia maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic upper beach fescue-lymegrass swards
description: Perennial halonitrophilous communities of upper beaches of the Polar Basin, in particular of Lapland and Greenland, dominated by grasses, notably [Leymus arenarius] or [Leymus mollis] and [Festuca rubra] ssp. [arenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic [Mertensia] mats
description: Upper shore communities of arctic shores dominated by [Mertensia maritima], often in almost pure stands. On the arctic coasts of Scandinavia, they form a belt between annual driftline communities and the [Festuca]-[Leymus] formations of unit 16.1351; in Greenland they are of local occurrence, particularly on the southwestern coast, with isolated occurrences in Thule and in the Ammassalik area of the east coast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Pacific sand beach perennial communities
description: Perennial halonitrophilous communities of the boreal beaches of the Pacific Basin, including those of southern Amurland, the Kuriles, Sakhaline, Hokkaido, extending to northern Honshu.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Sindian sand beach communities
description: Formations of annuals or perennials colonizing sand beaches of the desert coasts of the African Atlantic, of the extreme southeastern Mediterranean, of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Sea and of the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai sand beach communities
description: Communities colonizing sand beaches of the Sinai and Nile delta coasts of the extreme southeastern Mediterranean dominated by [Cakile maritima] ssp. [aegyptiaca] and [Silene succulenta], sometimes accompanied by [Convolvulus secundus], which may also compose alone a very sparse driftline belt.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic desert sand beach communities
description: Formations of annuals or perennials colonizing sand beaches of the desert coasts of the African Atlantic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Red Sea-Indian Ocean sand beach communities
description: Formations of annuals or perennials colonizing sand beaches of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Sea and of the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical sand beach communities
description: Formations of tropical beaches, comprising herbaceous, shrubby and arborescent communities, in particular those dominated by [Hippomoea pes-caprae], [Sporobolus virginicus], or the ligneous [Scaevola plumieri]. They are restricted, within the Palaearctic zone as here defined, to the southern Mauritanian coast, the Indian Ocean area and the tropical Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dunes
description: Onshore wind-carried sand deposits arranged in cordons of ridges parallel to the coast and often colonised and stabilised by communities of coarse maritime grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shifting dunes
description: Mobile sands of the coasts of the boreal, nemoral, steppe, Mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones, unvegetated or occupied by open grasslands; they may form tall dune ridges or, particularly along the Mediterranean and the Black Sea, be limited to a fairly flat upper beach, still subject in part to inundation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Embryonic dunes
description: Formations of the coasts of the nemoral, steppe, Mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones of the Palaearctic region, representing the first stages of dune construction, constituted by ripples or raised sand surfaces of the upper beach or by a seaward fringe at the foot of the tall dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic embryonic dunes
description: Embryonic dunes of the Atlantic, south to southern Iberia, of the North Sea and of the Baltic coasts of Denmark, Germany, southern Sweden, Poland, the Baltic States, Russia and southwestern Finland, with [Elymus farctus] ([Agropyron junceum]) accompanied by [Leymus arenarius] in the north, by [Euphorbia paralias] on middle and southern Atlantic shores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Tethyan embryonic dunes
description: Embryonic dunes of the Mediterranean coasts, on which [Elymus farctus] is accompanied by [Sporobolus pungens], [Euphorbia peplis], [Otanthus maritimus], [Medicago marina], [Anthemis maritima], [Anthemis tomentosa], [Eryngium maritimum], [Pancratium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Tethyan sand couch dunes
description: Embryonic dunes of the Mediterranean coasts dominated by [Elymus farctus] ([Agropyron junceum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic sand couch dunes
description: [Elymus farctus] embryonic dunes of southeastern and eastern Iberia, of the Mediterranean coasts of the Maghreb and of Atlantic Africa, south to Safi.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Mediterranean sand couch dunes
description: [Elymus farctus] embryonic dunes of Tyrrhenian, Adriatic and Ionian coasts of Europe, from northeastern Iberia to the western Peloponnese, including the east coast of Corsica, and with outposts in northern Algeria, with [Echinophora spinosa] and [Anthemis maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyrno-Sardinian sand couch dunes
description: [Elymus farctus] embryonic dunes of Sardinia and the west coast of Corsica, with [Silene succulenta] ssp. [corsica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegeo-Levantine sand couch dunes
description: [Elymus farctus] embryonic dunes of the Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean Levant Basin, with [Diotis maritima], [Eryngium maritimum], [Euphorbia paralias], [Verbascum pinnatifidum], [Cyperus capitatus], [Leymus racemosus] ssp. [sabulosus] ([Elymus giganteus]), of Pontic affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Mediterranean sand couch dunes
description: [Elymus farctus] embryonic dunes of arid Mediterranean coasts of North Africa, from Tunisia to the Nile, with [Silene succulenta] ssp. [succulenta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesio-Saharan sand couch dunes
description: [Elymus farctus] embryonic dunes of the Atlantic coast of Morocco, between Safi and Agadir, mostly characteristic of the relatively cool coast between Essaouira and Cape Rhir, southernmost outpost of the sand couch dunes, with the Macaronesian [Polycarpaea niveae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Tethyan [Sporobolus] dunes
description: Embryonic dunes of Mediterranean and North African Atlantic coasts dominated by [Sporobolus pungens] ([Sporobolus virginicus] ssp. [arenarius], [Sporobolus arenarius]) most characteristic of the seaward fringes of embryonic dunes on arid coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arid Mediterranean embryonic dunes
description: Embryonic dunes and upper beaches of the Mediterranean coasts, most characteristic of the eastern Mediterranean, dominated by grasses, sedges or dicots of continental steppic, subdesert or subtropical affinities, adapted to the most severe conditions of aridity.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Cyperus capitatus] dunes
description: Embryonic dunes and upper beaches of the Mediterranean coasts dominated by [Cyperus capitatus] ([Cyperus kallii]), well developed in particular in the Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean, also present, notably, in Italy, on the Maltese Islands, in Languedoc, extinct in the Bouches-du-Rh“ne.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Ipomaea] dunes
description: Embryonic dunes and upper beaches of the eastern Mediterranean, in southwestern Anatolia, Cyprus, the Levant and extreme western Crete, dominated by, or rich in, the subtropical [Ipomoea stolonifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Alhagi] dunes
description: Embryonic dunes of the eastern Mediterranean, in particular, of southwestern Anatolia and Cyprus, dominated by [Alhagi mannifera] ([Alhagi maurorum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Elymus giganteus] embryonic dunes
description: Embryonic dunes of the Aegean dominated by [Leymus racemosus] ssp. [sabulosus] ([Elymus giganteus]), of Pontic affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic embryonic dunes
description: Formations of Black Sea coasts, transitional between Pontic white dune and driftline communities, characterized by the adjunction to [Elymion gigantei] species assemblies of [Cakile maritima] ssp. [euxina], [Salsola kali] ssp. [ruthenica], [Euphorbia peplis] and other sand beach annual species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific embryonic dunes
description: Embryonic dunes of the Pacific basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: White dunes
description: Mobile dunes forming the seaward cordon or cordons of dune systems  of the coasts of the nemoral, steppe, Mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic white dunes
description: White dunes of the Atlantic, south to Aquitaine, of the North Sea and of the Baltic coasts of Denmark, southern Sweden, Germany, Poland, the Baltic States and Russia, dominated, when vegetated, by marram grass ([Ammophila arenaria]) accompanied by, among others, [Eryngium maritimum], [Euphorbia paralias], [Calystegia soldanella].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Tethyan white dunes
description: White dunes of the Mediterranean coasts and of the subtropical Atlantic coasts of Iberia and mediterranean North Africa, south to Safi at 32øN, dominated, when vegetated, by the marram grass [Ammophila arenaria] ssp. [arundinacea]  ([Ammophila australis]), accompanied by, among others, [Otanthus maritima], [Echinophora spinosa], [Eryngium maritimum], [Euphorbia paralias], [Cutandia maritima], [Medicago marina], [Anthemis maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic marram grass dunes
description: [Ammophila arenaria] white dunes of southeastern and eastern Iberia, of the Mediterranean coasts of the Maghreb and of Atlantic Africa, south to Safi at 32øN, where they reach the natural southern limit of marram grass. The range of marram grass dunes has been extended by plantations to Essaouira, at 31øN; the new communities have a cortŠge of Macaronesian affinities ("[Polycarpaeo niveae-Ammophiletum australis]").
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Mediterranean marram grass dunes
description: [Ammophila arenaria] white dunes of Tyrrhenian, Adriatic and Ionian coasts of Europe, from northeastern Iberia to the western Peloponnese, including the east coast of Corsica, with [Medicago marina], [Echinophora spinosa], [Cutandia maritima], [Anthemis maritima], [Euphorbia paralias].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyrno-Sardinian marram grass dunes
description: [Ammophila arenaria] white dunes of Sardinia and the west coast of Corsica, with [Silene succulenta] ssp. [corsica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegeo-Levantine white dunes
description: White dunes of the Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean, for the most part dominated by [Ammophila arenaria], sometimes by species of Pontic or Irano-Turanian affinities, in particular [Leymus racemosus] ssp. [sabulosus] ([Elymus giganteus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegeo-Levantine marram grass dunes
description: [Ammophila arenaria] white dunes of the Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean, recorded, in particular, from the northern Aegean, the western coasts of Anatolia and from the Levantine coasts, with [Cyperus conglomeratus], [Medicago marina], [Silene succulenta], [Lotus creticus], [Eryngium maritimum], [Diotis maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean subcontinental white dunes
description: White dunes of the Aegean dominated by species of Pontic or Irano-Turanian affinities, in particular [Leymus racemosus] ssp. [sabulosus] ([Elymus giganteus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Mediterranean white dunes
description: White dunes of arid Mediterranean coasts of North Africa, from Tunisia to the Nile, for the most part dominated by [Ammophila arenaria], sometimes by desert grasses of genus [Stipagrostis] ([Aristida]) or [Imperata cylindrica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Mediterranean marram grass dunes
description: [Ammophila arenaria] white dunes of arid Mediterranean coasts of North Africa, from Tunisia to the Nile, with [Silene succulenta], [Euphorbia paralias], [Pancratium maritimum], [Lotus creticus], [Lotus polyphyllos], [Cyperus capitatus], [Launea resedifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Mediterranean subdesert white dunes
description: Mobile dunes of arid or subdesert coasts of central and eastern North Africa, between Tunisia and Egypt, dominated by desert grasses of genus [Stipagrostis] ([Aristida]), in particular, [Stipagrostis pungens], [Stipagrostis coerulescens], [Stipagrostis scoparia], sometimes associated with [Imperata cylindrica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Iberian marram grass dunes
description: [Ammophila arenaria] white dunes of the Atlantic coasts of the Iberin peninsula with [Otanthus maritimus], [Euphorbia paralias], [Polygonum maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canario-Saharan white dunes
description: Mobile dunes of the Canary Islands and of the mediterraneo-Saharan coasts of Atlantic North Africa, with [Traganum moquini], [Euphorbia paralias], [Polycarpaea nivea], [Cyperus capitatus], [Ononis natrix], [Convolvulus caput-medusae], [Polygonum maritimum], [Lotus spp.] and the threatened Lanzarote endemic lily [Androcymbium psammophilum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic white dunes
description: Mobile dunes of the Black Sea coasts, with [Leymus racemosus] ssp. [sabulosus] ([Elymus giganteus]), [Elymus farctus] ssp. [bessarabicus], [Elymus pycnanthus], [Artemisia tschernieviana], [Eryngium maritimum], [Convolvulus persicus], [Petasites spurius], [Corispermum marschallii], [Lactuca tatarica], [Crambe maritima] var. [pontica], [Cynanchum acutum], [Centaurea arenaria] ssp. [odessana], [Argusia sibirica] ([Tournefortia arguzia]) and, in western formations, [Ammophila arenaria] ssp. [arundinacea], [Euphorbia paralias], [Calystegia soldanella].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific white dunes
description: Mobile dunes of the Pacific basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic dunes
description: Young dunes of the arctic and boreal latitudes of the Palaearctic region colonized by halonitrophilous perennial vegetation similar to that of unit 16.13, including [Leymus arenarius] ([Elymus arenarius]), [Ammophila arenaria], [Honkenya peploides], [Elymus farctus] ([Elytrigia juncea]), [Elymus repens], [Mertensia maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic dunes
description: Halonitrophilous perennial communities of young dunes of arctic, mostly low arctic, coasts of the Polar Basin, except of those of Iceland, recorded in particular from Greenland, Lapland and Russia, dominated by [Leymus arenarius] or [Leymus mollis], by [Festuca rubra] ssp. [arenaria], or by [Calamagrostis stricta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic foredunes
description: Halonitrophilous perennial communities dominated by [Leymus arenarius] colonizing young dunes of the coasts of Iceland, sometimes forming very broad belts, with irradiations in the Faeroe Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bothnian foredunes
description: Halonitrophilous perennial communities of young dunes of the Bothnian Gulf dominated by [Leymus arenarius] and [Festuca rubra] ssp. [arenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Pacific dunes
description: Halonitrophilous perennial communities of young dunes of the boreal coasts of the Pacific Basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Grey dunes
description: Fixed or semifixed dunes of the coasts of the boreal, nemoral, steppe, mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones of the Palaearctic region, with the perennial grasslands, chamaephyte-dotted grasslands, forblands, subshrub or succulent communities that stabilize them and the therophyte communities that may occupy the grassland clearings.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Atlantic grey dunes
description: Grasslands of Baltic, North Sea, English Channel and northern Atlantic fixed dunes, including those of the British Isles, the Faeroes, southern Norway, the North Sea and Baltic coasts, the Channel coasts of France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crested-hairgrass dune communities
description: Calciphile communities of fixed dunes of the North Sea, the English Channel, the north Atlantic and, locally, of the southwestern Baltic, with [Koeleria albescens], ([Koeleria glauca], [Koeleria arenaria]), [Galium verum] var. [maritimum], [Viola curtisii], [Ononis repens], [Festuca rubra], [Festuca polesica], [Anthyllis vulneraria] ssp. [maritima] and moss (e.g. [Tortula ruraliformis]) and lichen carpets.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Grey-hairgrass dune communities
description: Communities of less calcareous or decalcified dunes of the North Atlantic, the English Channel, the North Sea and the Baltic north to southern Norway, northern Jutland, southern Sweden, the Kalinin district and the Gulf of Riga, often rich in [Corynephorus canescens] and [Viola canina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mouse-ear dune communities
description: Short-lived, warmth-loving communities of the dunes of the North Atlantic and its connected seas north to extreme southern Sweden, with [Cerastium diffusum] ssp. [diffusum], [Cerastium diffusum] ssp. [subtetrandrum], [Cerastium semidecandrum], [Erodium lebelii], [Phleum arenarium], [Silene conica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Biscay grey dunes
description: Fixed dune grasslands infiltrated by dwarf bushes of French Brittany and the coasts of the Bay of Biscay, with [Helichrysum stoechas], [Artemisia campestris], [Ephedra distachya].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic grey dune communities
