description: Fixed dunes of the western and central Mediterranean and of the thermo-Atlantic coasts of Portugal, southwestern Spain and North Africa, colonized by communities mostly composed of fruticose species, with [Crucianella maritima], [Artemisia crithmifolia], [Armeria pungens], [Armeria welwitschi], [Helichrysum decumbens], [Helichrysum italicum], [Teucrium spp.], [Ephedra distachya], [Pancratium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-Atlantic [Crucianella] communities
description: Fixed dunes of the Galician, Lucitanian and Andalusian coasts of the subtropical Atlantic, with [Crucianella maritima], [Iberis procumbens], [Artemisia campestris] ssp. [maritima], [Artemisia crithmifolia], [Armeria welwitchii], [Armeria pungens], [Corema album].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tyrrhenian [Crucianella] communities
description: Fixed dunes of the Mediterranean coasts of Spain, France, Tyhrrenian Italy, Corsica, Sardinia and Sicily, with [Crucianella maritima], [Artemisia crithmifolia], [Armeria pungens], [Helichrysum decumbens], [Helichrysum italicum], [Teucrium spp.], [Ephedra distachya], [Pancratium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Mediterranean [Crucianella] communities
description: Fixed dunes of the mediterranean Maghreb and northern Atlantic Morocco with [Crucianella maritima], [Teucrium polium] var. [maritimum], [Artemisia campestris], [Calendula suffruticosa], [Lotus creticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean grey dune communities
description: Coastal dune communities of the Adriatic, the Ionian, the Aegean and the eastern Mediterranean, dominated by dwarf shrubs and subshrubs of genera [Ephedra], [Ononis], [Artemisia], and, very locally, [Crucianella], by tall canes or by succulents; they are usually rich in species of genus [Silene].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Adriatic grey dunes
description: Fixed dune communities of the Adriatic coasts of Italy, Istria and Dalmatia, generally without [Crucianella maritima]. Dunal systems are mostly limited to the northeastern Adriatic coasts of Italy, from Ravenna to the northern Gulf of Trieste, with more isolated occurrences in the Otanto, on the north coast of Gargano, around Pescara and Conero, on the island of Rab, around Split, Kastel-Novi, the Neretva estuary and on the Montenegrine coast. Grey dune communities appear to be lacking or poorly developed in most of them, absent, in particular, in the Dalmatian ones. Italian communities, in particular northeastern Italian ones, are dominated by the ligneous, much branched biennial [Scabiosa argentea] var. [alba], with [Euphorbia paralias], [Phleum arenarium], [Silene conica] ssp. [conica], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [angustifolia] and a more developed bryophyte cover, with [Tortula ruraliformis], then other mediterranean dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Ionian [Ephedra] dune communities
description: Coastal dune communities of the southern Adriatic and Ionian coasts of Albania, of the Ionian coasts of the Hellenic peninsula, of the western Peloponnese, of the Ionian archipelago, dominated by [Ephedra distachya], [Euphorbia terracina], and the otherwise mostly west-Mediterranean [Silene nicaeensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean [Ephedra] dune communities
description: Coastal dune communities of the Aegean coasts of continental Greece, Turkey and the archipelagoes, dominated by [Ephedra distachya], [Euphorbia terracina], [Silene conica] ssp. [subconica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Mediterranean rear dune communities
description: Coastal dune communities of Anatolian, Levantine, Cyprian and North African coasts of the eastern Mediterranean, west to arid Tunisia, dominated by dwarf shrubs and subshrubs of genera [Ononis], [Artemisia], locally associated with [Crucianella], by tall canes or by succulents.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Mediterranean [Ononis] dune communities
description: Coastal dune communities of Anatolian, Levantine, Cyprian and North African coasts of the eastern Mediterranean, west to arid Tunisia, dominated by dwarf shrubs of genus [Ononis], in particular, [Ononis natrix] ssp. [hispanica] in southern Anatolia, [Ononis vaginalis] between the Nile and north-east Lybia, [Ononis angustissima] in Tunisia, associated with [Lotus creticus], [Euphorbia paralias], and with canes of unit 16.22443, or, locally, in particular in the Levantine area and Egypt, with [Crucianella maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Mediterranean [Artemisia] dune communities
description: Coastal rear dune communities of Levantine and northeastern African coasts of the eastern Mediterranean dominated by [Artemisia monosperma], with [Cyperus capitatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Mediterranean tall cane dune communities
description: Coastal dune communities of North African coasts of the eastern Mediterranean, west to arid Tunisia, dominated by [Imperata cylindrica], associated with elements of unit 16.22441 and sometimes with desert grasses of genus [Stipagrostis] ([Aristida]), in particular, [Stipagrostis pungens], [Stipagrostis coerulescens], [Stipagrostis scoparia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Mediterranean [Nitraria] dunes
description: Semi-fixed dunes of arid or subdesert coasts of central and eastern North Africa, between Tunisia and Egypt, dominated by the chenopodid [Nitraria retusa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic dune [Mesobromion] grasslands
description: Dunal grasslands, in particular of northern Brittany, rich in species characteristic of dry calcareous grasslands (unit 34.32).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic dune thermophile fringes
description: [Geranium sanguineum]-rich forb and grass communities, related to hem formations of unit 34.4, developed within grey dune systems of western Ireland, southwestern England, Wales, Brittany and southwestern Norway.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune fine-grass therophyte communities
description: Sparse pioneer formations of fine grasses rich in spring-blooming therophytes characteristic of oligotrophic, superficial soils in grey dune systems of the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. They are closely related to grasslands of units 35.2 and 35.3.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan dune deep sand therophyte communities
description: Therophyte communities of the coasts of the western Mediterranean basin and the subtropical Atlantic colonizing deep sands in clearings of perennial communities of fixed or semi-fixed dune systems, and sometimes deflation depressions of white dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic dune malcolmia communities
description: Communities rich in small annuals, often generating an abundant ephemeral spring bloom, with [Malcolmia lacera], [Malcolmia ramosissima], [Evax asterisciflora], [Evax lusitanica], [Anthyllis hamosa], [Linaria pedunculata], of deep sands in dry interdunal depressions of the Mediterranean coasts of Iberia, southern France, Italy, the Maghreb and of the Atlantic coasts of southern Iberia and northern northwest Africa. They are coastal dune representatives of unit 35.4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesio-African dune therophyte communities
description: Therophyte communities of the Saharo-mediterranean and Macaronesian coasts of the subtropical Atlantic colonizing deep sands in clearings of perennial communities of fixed or semi-fixed dunes and deflation depressions of white dunes, with [Ononis tournefortii], [Cyperus capitatus] ([Cyperus kallii]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune Mediterranean xeric grasslands
description: Therophyte communities of shallow, calcareous fixed sands of the coastal dune systems of the Mediterranean basin, coastal dune representatives of unit 34.5. Subdivisions of unit 34.5 can be used to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermo-Atlantic succulent and semi-fixed dunes
description: Fixed or semi-fixed dunes of the Canary Islands and of the Saharo-mediterranean zone of the Atlantic coasts of North Africa, between Essaouira and Tan-Tan, dominated by the tall shrubby chenopod [Traganum moquinii] or by dwarf shrubs or subshrubs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Traganum] dunes
description: High dunes of the thermo-Atlantic coasts of North Africa and the Canary Islands dominated by the tall shrubby chenopod [Traganum moquinii], with [Suaeda vera], [Atriplex halimus], [Atriplex glauca] var. [ifniensis], [Salsola longifolia], [Salsola vermiculata], limited on the continent to the Saharo-mediterranean zone, between Essaouira and Tan-Tan, mostly characteristic, in the islands, of the centre and east of the archipelago, where they may form extensive systems (jables), penetrating well inland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermo-Atlantic [Ononis] dunes
description: Fixed or semi-fixed dunes of the Canary Islands and of the Saharo-mediterranean zone of the Atlantic coasts of North Africa, between Essaouira and Tan-Tan, dominated by dwarf shrubs or subshrubs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic fixed dunes
description: Fixed dunes of the coasts of the Black Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic fixed dunes
description: Fixed dunes of the western coasts of the Black Sea, north of the Bosphorus and west of the Dniester.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Pontic fixed dunes
description: Fixed dunes of the southwestern coasts of the Black Sea, between the Bosphorus and Cape Caliacra, harbouring the psammophytes [Cionura erecta], [Peucedanum arenarium], [Jurinea albicaulis] ssp. [kilaea], [Silene thymifolia], [Medicago marina], [Secale sylvestre], [Pancratium maritimum], [Convolvulus persicus], [Scabiosa argentea] ([Scabiosa ucranica]), [Euphorbia seguierana] and the Balkan endemic [Lepidotrichum uechtritzianum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Pontic fixed dunes
description: Dunes of the northwestern Black Sea coast, in particular, those associated with the mouth of the Danube.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Pontic [Ephedra]-[Carex] fixed dunes
description: Formations with [Ephedra distachya] and [Carex colchica] of dry fixed dunes OF the northwestern Black Sea coast, in particular, those associated with the mouth of the Danube.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Pontic [Alyssum]-[Secale] fixed dunes
description: Formations of windswept fixed dunes oriented perpendicularly to the shore of the northwestern Black Sea coast, in particular, those associated with the mouth of the Danube, dominated by [Alyssum borzaeanum], and [Secale sylvestre], with [Cynanchum acutum] and [Astragalus virgatus] as codominant elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Pontic [Calamagrostis]-[Scirpus] fixed dunes
description: Formations of northwestern Pontic dunes dominated by [Scirpus holoschoenus] and [Calamagrostis epigejos], of the more humid situations within fixed dune systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Pontic moss-sedge dunes
description: Pioneer formations of [Syntrichia ruralise] and [Carex nitida] on fixed dunes of the Danube Delta.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic fixed dunes
description: Fixed dunes of the northern and eastern Black Sea coasts, east of the Dniester, southeastwards to the Kuban basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Pontic fixed dunes
description: Fixed dunes of the southern and southeastern coasts of the Black Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic grey dunes
description: Communities of fixed dunes of the boreal and arctic coasts of Atlantic Eurasia, characterized by the dominance of species of the [Honkenyo-Elymetea] and the presence of arcto-alpine species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic grey dunes
description: Communities of inner coastal dunes of Iceland, developed on fixed sands. They are for the most part dominated by [Festuca richardsonii] ([Festuca cryophila], [Festuca rubra] ssp. [arctica]), with [Silene uniflora], [Equisetum boreale], [Leymus arenarius], [Armeria maritima], [Potentilla anserina], [Plantago maritima], [Galium verum], [Botrychium lunaria], [Sedum acre], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Erigeron borealis], [Draba incana], [Poa alpina], [Trisetum spicatum], [Carex capillaris], [Myosotis arvensis], [Rhinanthus minor], [Gentiana aurea], [Euphrasia arctica]. They can be invaded and eventually dominated by [Kobresia myosuroides], then supporting communities very similar to those of unit 15.B22, which can be indicated by combination of the two codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Russo-Scandinavian boreo-arctic grey dunes
description: Communities of fixed dunes of the boreal and arctic coasts of Norway and Russia, with [Leymus arenarius], [Achillea millefolium], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Oxytropis campestris], [Dianthus superbus], [Primula stricta], [Pedicularis septrum-carolinum], [Coeloglossum viride], [Pyrola minor], [Carex maritima], [Juncus arcticus], [Festuca rubra] [s.l.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland grey dunes
description: Fixed dune communities of Greenland with [Armeria scabra] ssp. [siberica], [Artemisia borealis], [Epilobium latifolium], [Carex maritima], [Calamagrostis purpurescens], [Honkenia peploides], [Leymus mollis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific grey dunes
description: Fixed dunes of the coasts of the Pacific fa‡ade of Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crowberry brown dunes
description: [Empetrum nigrum] or [Empetrum hermaphroditum] colonizing dunes of the Arctic Ocean, the North Atlantic, the North Sea and the southern Baltic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Germanobaltic crowberry brown dunes
description: [Empetrum nigrum] heaths occupying decalcified dunes of the North Sea and the southern Baltic; they are scattered around the North Sea in northern and eastern Scotland and from North Holland and Frisia to Jutland and the Kattegat coast of Sweden, and along the Baltic from Denmark to Poland, the Kalinin district, the gulf of Riga and Estonia, in Scania, on ™land, on Gotland and around the land Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreoarctic crowberry brown dunes
description: [Empetrum hermaphroditum] heaths colonizing dunes of the northern boreal and arctic coasts of Europe, recorded in particular from northern Norway and Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Heather brown dunes
description: [Erica], [Calluna] and [Ulex] heaths colonizing decalcified dunes of France, Iberia, Britain and Scandinavia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Anglian ling coastal dune heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris]-[Carex arenaria] heaths of inner coastal dunes of East Anglia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: French ling coastal dune heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris]-[Carex trinervis] heaths of northern French inner coastal dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British bell heather coastal dune heaths
description: [Erica cinerea]-[Carex arenaria] heaths of decalcified coastal dunes of the western British Isles, mostly dominated by [Erica cinerea], sometimes by [Calluna vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: French bell heather coastal dune heaths
description: [Erica cinerea]-[Festuca vasconcensis] heaths of dry coastal dunes of southwestern France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: French Dorset heath coastal dune heaths
description: [Erica ciliaris]-[Pseudarrhenatherum longifolium] ([Arrhenatherum thorei]) heaths of more humid coastal dunes of southwestern France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian green heather coastal dune heaths
description: [Erica scoparia]-[Ulex parviflorus] ssp. [eriocladus] ([Ulex australis]) heaths of southwestern Iberian coastal dunes, dunal fraction of the thermo-Mediterranean heaths of unit 32.2C1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian Dorset heath coastal dune heaths
description: [Erica ciliaris]-[Ulex parviflorus] ssp. [eriocladus] heaths of more humid southwestern Iberian coastal dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern ling coastal dune heaths
description: Open heathlands of inner coastal dunes of Denmark, of the southern and southeastern Baltic coast, of southern Scania, the Kattegat coast of Sweden, ™land, Gotland and the land-Archipelago Sea dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], with [Empetrum nigrum], [Carex arenaria], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Hieracium umbellatum], [Lotus corniculatum], [Polypodium vulgare], [Salix repens], and a ground layer constituted mostly by [Dicranum scoparium] and [Pleurozium schreberi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern bell heather coastal dune heaths
description: Low, open heaths dominated by [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], sometimes with [Juniperus communis], of inner coastal dunes of western Norway and the Faeroe Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune nemoral thickets
description: Dense formations of large, mostly deciduous, shrubs of nemoral affinities of the coastal dunes and dune-slacks of the boreal, nemoral, steppe, mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones of the Palaearctic region; they include sea-buckthorn, privet, elder, willow, gorse or broom, often festooned with creepers such as honeysuckle or white bryony ([Bryonia cretica]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea-buckthorn dune thickets
description: Thickets dominated by [Hippophae rhamnoides] ssp. [rhamnoides] colonizing dry or humid dune depressions of the coasts of the North Sea, the eastern English Channel and the southern Baltic, mostly in Denmark, Germany, Poland, the Kalinin district, the Netherlands, Belgium, Northern France and southeastern and eastern England and southeastern Scotland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western nemoral mixed dune thickets
description: Dunal preforest thickets of nemoral affinities of the coastal dunes of the western Palaearctic region formed of species of genera [Ulex], [Sarothamnus], [Rubus], [Ligustrum], [Daphne], [Sambucus]. Codes of subdivisions of unit 31.8 can be used, in addition to unit 16.252, to specify the habitat. Listed elsewhere are dunal formations of heaths (units 16.23, 16.24), sea-buckthorn ([Hippophae rhamnoides], unit 16.251) or creeping willow ([Salix arenaria], unit 16.26).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Palaearctic dune thickets
description: Dunal preforest thickets of nemoral affinities of the coastal dunes of the eastern Palaearctic region. Codes of subdivisions of unit 31.9 can be used, in combination with unit 16.253, to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Creeping-willow mats
description: Mats of [Salix arenaria] colonizing dry or humid dune depressions of Atlantic, North Sea, English Channel, Irish Sea and Baltic coasts of western and northwestern Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune juniper thickets
description: Juniper heaths and thickets formed by [Juniperus phoenicea], [Juniperus "lycia"], [Juniperus macrocarpa], [Juniperus transtagana], [Juniperus communis] in dune slacks and on dune slopes of the coasts of the boreal, nemoral, steppe, mediterranean or warm-temperate humid zones of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune prickly juniper thickets
description: [Juniperus oxycedrus] ssp. [macrocarpa] thickets and low woods of the outer belt of the juniper woods of fixed Mediterranean and Mediterraneo-Atlantic dunes. Well-developed woods and forests are placed in unit 16.29, with the habitat specified by unit 42.A92 (16.29 x 42.A92).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lycian juniper thickets
description: [Juniperus phoenicea] ssp. [lycia] thickets of the inner belt of the juniper woods of fixed Mediterranean and Mediterraneo-Atlantic dunes. Well-developed woods and forests are placed in unit 16.29, with the habitat specified by unit 42.AA12 (16.29 x 42.AA12).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rufescent juniper thickets
description: Scrubs of the fastigiate [Juniperus oxycedrus] ssp. [transtagana] of the dunes of southwestern Portugal.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Common juniper dune thickets
description: [Juniperus communis] scrubs of the calcareous dunes of northwest Jutland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific juniper dune thickets
description: Dune thickets of the coasts of Sakhalin, Hokkaido, Honshu, Kyushu, formed by the prostrate [Juniperus conferta], and of Kyushu and the Bonin Islands, dominated by the spreading, procumbent [Juniperus procumbens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune sclerophyllous scrubs and thickets
description: Sclerophyllous, lauriphyllous or drought-deciduous scrubs, thickets and brushes established on dunes of the mediterranean or warm-temperate humid regions of the Palaearctic region. Codes of subdivisions of units 32, 33 or 15.9 may be used in addition to 16.28 to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune sclerophyllous retam brushes
description: Sclerophyllous, lauriphyllous or drought-deciduous scrubs, thickets and brushes established on dunes of the mediterranean or warm-temperate humid regions of the Palaearctic region. Codes of subdivisions of units 32 and 33 may be used in addition to 16.28 to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune sclerophyllous thickets
description: Tall sclerophyllous, lauriphyllous or drought-deciduous thickets and brushes established on dunes of the mediterranean or warm-temperate humid regions of the Palaearctic domaine. Codes of subdivisions of units 32.1, 32.2, 32.31, 32.32, 32.37, 32.8, 32.A, 32.D may be used in addition to 16.28 to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune sclerophyllous low scrubs
description: Low sclerophyllous scrubs established on dunes of the mediterranean or warm-temperate humid regions of the Palaearctic domaine. Codes of subdivisions of units 32.2, 32.3, 32.4, 32.5, 32.8, 32.9, 32.B, 32.C, 32.D or 15.9 may be used in addition to 16.283 to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune phryganas and bathas
description: Cushion-forming thermo-mediterranean sclerophyllous formations, often thorny and summer deciduous, established on dunes of the mediterranean regions of the Palaearctic, or of their regions of transition towards deserts. Codes of subdivisions of unit 33 may be used in addition to 16.284 to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wooded dunes
description: Dunes of the coasts of the boreal, nemoral, steppe, mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones of the Palaearctic region, colonised by woodland or riparian thickets. Codes of units 41.5, 41.7, 42, 44, 45 can be used, in addition to that of unit 16.29, to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Sindian coastal dunes
description: Coastal sand dune communities of the desert coasts of the African Atlantic, of the extreme southeastern Mediterranean, of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Sea and of the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai coastal dunes
description: Coastal sand dune communities of the desert coasts of the extreme southeastern Mediterranean, in the northern Sinai and the Nile delta.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai [Aristida] coastal dunes
description: Coastal sand dune communities of the desert coasts of the northern Sinai and the Nile delta, dominated by desert grasses of genus [Stipagrostis] ([Aristida]), in particular [Stipagrostis scoparia] or [Stipagrostis ciliata], or by other species of Saharo-Sindian affinities, accompanied by desert psammophytes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai marram grass coastal dunes
description: Coastal sand dune communities of the desert coasts of the northern Sinai dominated by [Ammophila arenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sinai sand couch and silene coastal dunes
description: Coastal sand dune communities of the desert coasts of the Nile delta, dominated by Elymus farctus] or by [Silene succulenta], or by both in association.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic desert coastal dunes
description: Coastal sand dune communities of the desert coasts of the African Atlantic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Red Sea-Indian Ocean coastal dunes
description: Coastal sand dune communities of the desert coasts of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Sea and of the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical coastal dunes
description: Dune communities of tropical coasts of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Humid dune-slacks
description: Humid depressions of the coastal dunal systems of the Palaearctic region. The most important habitats are included in the subordinate units. If the divisions proposed are not sufficient, appropriate codes from units 22.4, 22.3, 54.2, 54.4, 53 can be used in conjunction with them. Humid dune-slacks are extremely rich and specialized habitats, very threatened by the lowering of water tables.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune-slack pools
description: Fresh-water aquatic communities (cf. unit 22.4) of permanent dune-slack water bodies of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune-slack pioneer swards
description: Pioneer formations of humid sands and dune pool fringes of the Palaearctic region, on soils with low salinity; communities can be specified by use of codes from unit 22.3, in particular unit 22.322 and unit 22.3132.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune-slack fens
description: Calcareous and, occasionally, acidic fen formations of coastal dune-slacks of the Palaearctic region (cf. units 54.2, 54.4, in particular units 54.21, 54.2H, 54.49), often invaded by creeping willow, occupying the wettest parts of dune-slacks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune-slack grasslands and heaths
description: Humid grasslands and rushbeds (units 37.218, 37.21F, 37.31, 37.4 [i.a.]), wet heaths and swamp-heaths (unit 31.112 [i.a.]) of dune-slacks of the Palaearctic region, also often with creeping willows ([Salix rosmarinifolia], [Salix arenaria]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune-slack reedbeds, sedgebeds and canebeds
description: Reedbeds, tall-sedge communities and canebeds (cf. units 53.1, 53.2, 53.3, 53.6) of dune-slacks of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shingle beaches
description: Beaches of the oceans, of their connected seas and of their associated coastal lagoons, covered by pebbles, or sometimes boulders, usually formed by wave action.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Unvegetated shingle beaches
description: Shingle beaches devoid of phanerogamic vegetation of the Palaearctic region. Codes of mediolittoral (intertidal) and supralittoral invertebrate communities listed under unit 11.28 can be combined with code 17.1 to record detailed habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shingle beach drift lines and pioneer swards
description: Very open formations of annuals or, particularly in Mediterranean, and mostly East Mediterranean, representatives, of annuals and perennials, occupying accumulations of drift material and gravels rich in nitrogenous organic matter; characteristic are [Cakile maritima], [Salsola kali], [Atriplex spp.] (particularly [Atriplex glabriuscula]), [Polygonum spp.], [Euphorbia peplis], [Mertensia maritima], and, particularly in Mediterranean formations, [Glaucium flavum], [Matthiola sinuata], [Matthiola tricuspidata], [Euphorbia paralias], [Eryngium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic gravel beach annual communities
description: Beach and upper beach formations, mostly of annuals of the low Arctic and high Arctic oceanic zones of the Palaearctic Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic oceans, occupying accumulations of drift material and gravels rich in nitrogenous organic matter; characteristic are [Cakile edentula], [Polygonum norvegicum] ([Polygonum oxyspermum] ssp. [raii]), [Atriplex longipes] [s.l.], [Atriplex glabriuscula], [Mertensia maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic shingle beach drift lines
description: Formations, predominantly of annuals, occupying accumulations of drift material and gravels rich in nitrogenous organic matter on nemoral and boreonemoral beaches of the Atlantic, the North Sea and the Baltic; characteristic are [Cakile maritima] ssp. [maritima], [Cakile maritima] ssp. [baltica], [Salsola kali], [Atriplex spp.] (particularly [Atriplex glabriuscula]), [Polygonum spp.], [Euphorbia peplis], [Mertensia maritima], [Glaucium flavum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan gravel beach communities
description: Very open, low formations of annuals and perennials of Mediterranean, thermo-Atlantic and Black Sea gravel and shingle beaches, occupying accumulations of drift material, sandy gravels and gravels rich in nitrogenous organic matter; characteristic are [Cakile maritima] ssp. [aegyptiaca], [Cakile maritima] ssp. [euxina], [Enarthrocarpus arcuatus], [Matthiola sinuata], [Matthiola tricuspidata], [Salsola kali], [Atriplex spp.], [Polygonum spp.], [Euphorbia peplis], [Euphorbia paralias], [Glaucium flavum], [Eryngium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific shingle beach drift lines
description: Formations of perennials or annuals occupying accumulations of drift material and gravels rich in nitrogenous organic matter on shingle beaches of the Pacific Basin, including those of southern Amurland, the Kuriles, Sakhaline.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea kale communities
description: Halonitrophilous perennial communities of the upper beach of the great shingle bars of temperate seas, characteristic in particular of northwestern Europe, mostly formed by [Crambe maritima], [Honkenya peploides] and a few specialized species characteristic of regional entities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic sea kale communities
description: Perennial communities of the shingle beaches and bars of the southern Baltic, east to Mecklenburg, where they are represented by fragmentary, endangered formations, of the Swedish, Finnish and Estonian coasts and islands of the land-Gotland basin, of the coasts of the Kattegat, the Oresund and the Baelts, dominated by [Crambe maritima], with [Leymus arenarius] ([Elymus arenarius]), [Euphorbia palustris], [Honkenya peploides], [Angelica archangelica] ssp. [litoralis], [Atriplex spp.], [Beta vulgaris] ssp. [maritima], [Elymus repens], [Geranium robertiana] ssp. [rubricaule], [Glaucium flavum], [Isatis tinctoria], [Ligusticum scoticum], [Mertensia maritima], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [maritima] ([Silene uniflora]), [Tripleurospermum maritimum], [Valeriana salina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Channel sea kale communities
description: Perennial communities of the shingle beaches and bars of the southern North Sea and Channel coasts of southeastern England and, very locally, the Channel coast of France, dominated by [Crambe maritima], with [Lathyrus japonicus] and [Honkenya peploides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic sea kale communities
description: Perennial communities of the shingle beaches and bars of Brittany, the Cotentin peninsula and Anglesey, dominated by [Crambe maritima], with [Crithmum maritimum] and a sparse representation of other nitrophiles, in particular, [Beta vulgaris] ssp. [maritima], [Matricaria maritima], [Rumex crispus], [Glaucium flavum], [Solanum dulcamara] var. [maritima], [Sonchus oleraceus], [Galium aparine].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gravel bank heaths, scrubs and grasslands
description: Grasslands, scrubs and heaths of the landward expanses of large coastal gravel banks of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian gravel bank grasslands
description: Dense perennial grasslands of boreal and nemoral coastal gravel banks of the Palaearctic region, in particular, swards of [Arrhenatherum elatius] of large Channel gravel banks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian gravel bank heaths
description: Low heaths of boreal and nemoral coastal gravel banks of the Palaearctic region, in particular, prostrate [Cytisus scoparius] formations of large Channel gravel banks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan gravel bank scrubs and heaths
description: Relatively closed or closed, stable, communities of shrubs, subshrubs, forbs or grasses colonizing landward expanses of large coastal gravel banks of the Mediterranean, the subtropical Atlantic and the Black Sea, related to grey dune, garrigue, maquis or phrygana communities. Codes of units 16.22, 32 or 33 can be used to define communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gravel bank thickets
description: Dense formations of large shrubs of coastal gravel banks of the Palaearctic region, in particular, thermo-mediterranean brushes of Mediterranean gravel banks. Codes from units 31.8, 32.2 can be used to specify habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gravel bank woods
description: Gravel banks of the coasts of the Palaearctic region, colonised by woodland or riparian thickets, in particular, Mediterranean gravel banks colonized by [Quercus ilex] low woods, by [Tamarix africana] or [Vitex agnus-castus] formations. Codes of units 32.1, 41, 42, 44, 45 can be used, in conjunction with that of unit 17.6, to specify the habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Rock exposures adjacent to the oceans, their connected seas and associated coastal lagoons, or separated from them by a narrow shoreline. The faces, ledges and caves of sea-cliffs and the expanses of rocky shore are important as reproduction, resting and feeding sites for seabirds, sea-mammals and a few groups of terrestrial birds, composing regionally distinct assemblies listed under unit 18.1. The presence of major sea-caves can be indicated by addition of codes of unit 12.7. Sea-cliffs may also harbour highly distinctive, specialized aerohaline plant communities with associated terrestrial faunas, listed under unit 18.2. Other terrestrial plant communities may belong to units 62, 61, 31, 32, 33, 34. The mediolittoral (intertidal or wave-washed) and supralittoral (spray) zones are inhabited by rich and diverse communities of invertebrates, fish and algae that have been listed under unit 11.29.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea-cliff faces, seaside rocks
description: Palaearctic hard rock sea-cliffs, their faces, ledges and associated caves, rocky shores and isolated seaside rocks, their associated seabird, sea mammal, wader and, in a few cases, terrestrial passerine, communities. The presence of vascular aerohaline vegetation should be indicated by use of the appropriate code from unit 18.2, that of mediolittoral (intertidal or wave-washed) and supralittoral (spray) zone communities of marine invertebrates, lower vertebrates and algae, by use of codes from unit 11.29. Less salt-influenced communities, in particular of units 62, 61, 31, 32, 33, 34, may contribute to the colonisation of the cliffs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High Arctic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs and their associated features, rocky shores and isolated seaside rocks of the High Arctic seas bordering middle and northern Greenland, Spitzbergen, Franz Josef Land, Novaya Zemlya, Severnaya Zemlya, the New Siberian Islands, Wrangel Island and the northern Siberian mainland from the north coast of the Yamal peninsula eastwards. Together with floating ice (unit 11.5), they constitute the main hauling-out places for [Odobenus rosmarus]. [Fulmarus glacialis], [Larus glaucoides], [Larus hyperboreus], [Cepphus grylle], [Plautus alle], [Uria lomvia], [Branta bernicla] are among characteristic bird species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic Low Arctic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs, cliff-faces, ledges and caves, rocky shores and isolated seaside rocks of the Low Arctic region of the North Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean, in southern Greenland, Iceland, Jan Mayen, Bear Island, northern Scandinavia, northwestern mainland Russia, southern and middle Novaya Zemlya. They constitute the principal breeding, resting or feeding areas of multitudes of seabirds and sea-mammals during at least part of the year.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Atlantic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs, their faces, ledges and associated caves, rocky shores and isolated seaside rocks of the Atlantic temperate region, including the North Sea, the English Channel, the Irish Sea and the Bay of Biscay, along the coasts of Scandinavia south of the Arctic Circle, of the Faeroes, of the British Isles and their outlying archipelagoes, of mainland Europe south to Galicia. They are the breeding, resting or feeding places of great numbers of seabirds and sea-mammals, of which [Halichoerus grypus], [Sula bassana], [Uria aalge], [Alca torda], [Rissa tridactyla], [Phalacrocorax aristotelis aristotelis] are characteristic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs, their faces and ledges, rocky shores and isolated seaside rocks of the Baltic Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical Atlantic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs, their faces, ledges and associated caves, rocky shores and isolated seaside rocks of the subtropical zone of the Atlantic, including the Canary Islands, Madeira, the Azores, the Mediterraneo-Atlantic coasts of Iberia, the Mediterraneo-Atlantic and Saharo-Atlantic coasts of Africa, south to Cap Blanc. A major zone of upwelling developed along the north African coast and the Canary Islands enhances their value as important breeding and resting places for marine birds and mammals. Their caves harbour the two remaining Atlantic subpopulations of the gravely endangered Monk Seal [Monachus monachus], endemic to this region and the next, those of  Madeira and of the Cap Blanc coasts. [Calonectris diomedea borealis], [Larus cachinnans atlantis], [Phalacrocorax carbo maroccanus], [Phalacrocorax aristotelis riggenbachi] are sea-birds endemic to the region for which cliffs and rocky shores provide an important breeding habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Pontic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs, their associated faces, ledges and caves, rocky shores and isolated rocks of the Mediterranean Sea and the Black Sea. The endangered [Monachus monachus] depends on their caves for reproduction. [Calonectris diomedea diomedea], [Puffinus yelkouan mauretanicus], [Puffinus yelkouan yelkouan], [Phalacrocorax aristotelis desmarestii], [Falco eleonorae], [Larus audouinii] are characteristic breeders. Their vascular aerohaline communities, as well as the rock communities of unit 62 that colonize their less salt-influenced reaches, are particularly diverse and rich in endemics. They are indicated by combination of appropriate units of 18.2 and/or 62 with unit 18.16.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical Atlantic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs, their faces, ledges and associated caves, rocky shores and isolated seaside rocks of the tropical zone of the Atlantic, including the Cape Verde Islands and the southern coast of Mauritania, along which extends the major upwelling zone of the Canary Current. Tropical seabirds such as [Phaethon aethereus], [Sula leucogaster], [Phalacrocorax carbo lucidus] are characteristic. [Calonectris edwardsii] is endemic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Indo-tropical sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs and rocky shores of the tropical Indian Ocean and its connected seas, comprising, in the Palaearctic region as here defined, those of the Red Sea, of the Arabian peninsula coast of the Gulf of Aden, of Socotra, of the Arabian Sea, of the Gulf of Oman and of the Persian Gulf. A major area of upwellings developed along the southern coast of the Arabian peninsula and Socotra inhances their importance as breeding sites for sea-birds. [Bulweria fallax], [Puffinus persicus], [Phalacrocorax socotranus], [Larus leucophthalmus], [Larus hemprichii] are endemic or near-endemic species of the region which do or may use sea-cliffs or rocky shores as breeding sites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific Low Arctic sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs and rocky shores of the Chukchi Sea, the Bering Strait, the Bering Sea, the Commander Islands, Kamchatka, the northern and central Kuriles, the Sea of Okhotsk and the Tatar Straits, harbouring an exceptionally rich community of alcids, gulls and cormorants, in particular.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Pacific sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs and rocky shores of the southern Kuriles, Honshu, Hokkaido, Shikoku and continental Korea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical Pacific sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs and rocky shores of peninsular Korea, the Yellow Sea, the East China Sea, Kyushu, the Ryukyu Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical Pacific sea-cliffs and rocky shores
description: Sea-cliffs and rocky shores of the South China Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea-cliff and rocky shore aerohaline communities
description: Palaearctic sea-cliffs, or parts of sea-cliffs, and rocky shores colonized by disjunct assemblages of aerohaline chasmophytes or by more or less closed aerohaline grasslands with associated terrestrial invertebrate and vertebrate faunal communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs of the northern Atlantic, the English Channel, the Irish Sea, the North Sea, the Baltic Sea, the Arctic Ocean and its seas, the northwest Pacific and its seas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Atlantic sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs of the nemoral middle Atlantic, the English Channel, the Irish Sea and the North Sea, along the coasts of Iberia, France, Ireland, England, Wales, southern Scotland and Helgoland, colonized by relatively thermophile communities variously formed by [Crithmum maritimum], [Armeria maritima], [Armeria pubigera], [Limonium occidentale], [Limonium ovalifolium], [Brassica oleracea] ssp. [oleracea], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [maritima], [Plantago maritima], [Festuca rubra] ssp. [pruinosa], [Daucus carota] ssp. [gummifer], [Daucus carota] ssp. [gadecaei], [Matricaria maritima], [Asplenium marinum], [Spergularia rupicola], [Inula crithmoides], [Sedum anglicum], [Lavatera arborea], [Frankenia laevis], [Anthyllis vulneraria] ssp. [corbierei], [Anthyllis vulneraria] ssp. [iberica], [Dactylis glomerata] ssp. [marina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs of the northern Atlantic, the northern North Sea, the Baltic, the Arctic Ocean and its seas, the Bering Sea, the Sea of Okhotsk, the northern and western Sea of Japan colonized by relatively cryophile communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North Atlantic sea-cliff communities
description: Usually open, lacunar, relatively cryophile, moderately nitrophile aerohaline communities of sea-cliffs of the northern Atlantic and northern North Sea coasts of Scotland, the Faeroe Islands, Iceland and Scandinavia, mostly dominated by [Cochlearia officinalis], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [maritima] ([Silene uniflora]), [Matricaria maritima], [Festuca rubra] ssp. [pruinosa], with [Armeria maritima], [Plantago maritima], [Cochlearia groenlandica], [Cochlearia fenestrata], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Poa pratensis], [Ligusticum scoticum], [Cerastium fortanum], [Rhodiola rosea], [Plantago maritima], [Sedum acre], [Asplenium marinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern boreo-nemoral sea-cliff communities
description: Uncommon, species-poor, often [Cochlearia officinalis]-dominated, communities occupying wet, shadowy recesses near the foot of cold, shaded cliffs in southwestern Britain and Brittany constitute extralimital, highly specialized representatives of unit 18.2121.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic seabird cliff communities
description: Species-rich, nitrophile, meadowlike or tall-herb communities colonizing seabird nesting cliffs of the northern Atlantic and the northern North Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic seabird cliff meadow communities
description: Species rich, nitrophile, often meadowlike communities of broad rock ledges and clifftops of the west coast of Norway, Iceland, the Faeroe Islands, characteristic of sites with seabird colonies; dominant species include [Cochlearia officinalis], [Festuca rubra] ssp. [pruinosa], [Matricaria maritima], [Rumex acetosa], with [Armeria maritima], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [maritima] ([Silene uniflora]), [Silene dioica], [Saxifraga rivularis], [Saxifraga cespitosa], [Plantago maritima], [Oxyura digyna], [Anthriscus sylvestris], [Ligusticum scoticum], [Ranunculus acris], [Cerastium arcticum], [Cerastium fortanum], [Rhodiola rosea], [Plantago maritima], [Hieracium spp.], [Taraxicum spp.], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Puccinellia distans] ssp. [borealis], ([Puccinellia coarctata]), [Leymus arenarius], [Poa pratense] [s.l.], [Poa alpina], [Poa glauca], [Poa annua].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic seabird cliff tall-herb communities
description: Luxuriant, nitrophile tall-herb communities of rock fissures and ledges of sea-cliffs occupied by seabirds, of Norway, southwest Sweden and the Faeroe Islands, dominated by [Angelica archangelica], [Anthriscus sylvestris], [Rumex acetosa], [Silene dioica], [Rhodiola rosea], [Achillea milletolium], with [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [maritima] ([Silene uniflora]), [Valeriana sambucifolia], [Viola tricolor], [Oxyria digyna], [Cochlearia officinalis], [Ligusticum scoticum], [Matricaria perfoliata], [Festuca rubra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs of the Baltic Sea, with [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [maritima] ([Silene uniflora]), [Ligusticum scoticum], [Armeria maritima], [Odontites litoralis] ssp. [litoralis], [Odontites litoralis] ssp. [fennica], [Matricaria maritima], [Senecio viscosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs of the Arctic Ocean and its seas, the Bering Sea and the Sea of Okhotsk.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Pacific sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs of the northern and western Sea of Japan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate Pacific sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs of the southern and eastern Sea of Japan, the Yellow Sea, the northern East China Sea and the temperate West Pacific.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan sea-cliff communities
description: Vegetated cliffs and rocky shores of the Mediterranean, of the Black Sea and of the subtropical eastern Atlantic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Tethyan sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of the Mediterranean, as well as of the southwestern Iberian and northwestern African Atlantic, with [Crithmum maritimum], [Plantago subulata], [Silene sedoides], [Sedum litoreum], [Limonium spp.], [Armeria spp.], [Euphorbia spp.], [Daucus spp.], [Asteriscus maritimus]. Mediterranean sea-cliffs harbour numerous endemics of of extremely local occurrence, in particular, of genus [Limonium], which comprises at least 43 and probably closer to 120-150 Mediterranean cliff species species, many of them restricted to a few stations, and several threatened, such as, for instance, [Limonium remotispiculum] of southern Italy and [Limonium strictisissimum] of Corsica and Caprera.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Iberian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of southern Portugal and southwestern Spain, north to Extremadura and east to Punta Marroqui, including, in particular, the large cliff systems of Cape San Vicente in Algarve, and of Barbate in Andalucia, with [Limonium algarvense], [Limonium emarginatum], [Limonium virgatum] ([Limonium oleifolium]), [Limonium ovalifolium], [Limonium auriculae-ursifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallo-Iberian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Gibraltar, eastern peninsular Spain and its nearshore islands, Roussillon, with [Limonium malacitanum], [Limonium cossonianum], [Limonium furfuraceum], [Limonium virgatum], [Limonium gibertii], [Limonium girardianum], [Limonium dufourei], [Limonium tremolsii], [Armeria ruscinonensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balearic sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of the Balearics, with [Limonium caprariense].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallo-Italic sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Provence and Liguria, and their nearshore islands, with [Limonium minutum], Provence endemic and [Limonium cordatum], Proven‡o-Ligurian endemic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Toscano-Cyrno-Sardian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Sardinia, Corsica, the Toscan archipelago and Mte. Argentario, in an area of very high endemism of sea-cliff colonisers, in particular, of genus [Limonium], with [Limonium hermaeum], [Limonium lausianum], [Limonium dictyocladum], [Limonium articulatum], [Limonium dolcheri], [Limonium tibulatium], [Limonium acutifolium], [Limonium obtusifolium], [Limonium nymphaeum], [Limonium tenuifolium], [Limonium herculis], [Limonium planesiae], [Limonium savianum], [Limonium gorgonae], [Limonium multiformae], [Limonium argentarium], [Limonium sommierianum], [Limonium trojae], [Limonium dianum], [Limonium ilvae], [Limonium divaricatum], [Limonium racemosum], [Limonium dictyocladum], [Limonium virgatum] var. [majus], [Limonium lausianum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Campanian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of the Circaeo peninsula, the Gulf of Gaita, the Gulf of Naples, the Sorrento peninsula, the Gulf of Salerno and their associated archipelagoes, an area of high endemism of genus [Limonium], with [Limonium joannis], [Limonium pontium], [Limonium pandatariae], [Limonium circaei], [Limonium amynclaeum], [Limonium remotispeculum], [Limonium inarimense], [Limonium tenoreanum], [Limonium virgatum] var. [majus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italo-Sicilian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Calabria, Sicily, the Lipari Islands, the Egadi Islands, Pantelleria, Linosa, Lampedusa and the Maltese Islands, an area including several centers of radiation of endemic sea-lavenders, with [Limonium parvifolium], [Limonium cosyrense], [Limonium bocconei], [Limonium syracusanum], [Limonium flagellare], [Limonium ponzoi], [Limonium tenuiculum], [Limonium minutiflorum], [Limonium calabrum], [Limonium ionicum], [Limonium furnarii], [Limonium tauromenitanum], [Limonium albidum], [Limonium panormitanum], [Limonium lopadusanum], [Limonium hyblaeum], [Limonium intermedium], [Limonium mazarae], [Limonium divaricatum], [Limonium zeraphae], [Limonium virgatum] var. [majus], [Limonium sibthorpianum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calabro-Sicilian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Calabria, northeastern Sicily and the Lipari Islands, with [Limonium minutiflorum], [Limonium calabrum], [Limonium ionicum], [Limonium tauromenitanum], [Limonium sibthorpianum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Sicilian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of western Sicily, Ustica and the Egadi Islands, with [Limonium bocconei], [Limonium flagellare], [Limonium ponzoi], [Limonium tenuiculum], [Limonium furnarii], [Limonium panormitanum], [Limonium mazarae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cosyrian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Pantelleria, with [Limonium parvifolium], [Limonium cosyrense].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyblaeo-Maltese sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of southeastern Sicily and the Maltese Islands, with the sea-lavenders [Limonium syracusanum], [Limonium hyblaeum], [Limonium zeraphae], and with the Maltese endemics [Anthemis urvilleana], [Allium lojaconoi], the Hybleo-Maltese endemics [Desmazeria pignattii] and [Senecio pygmaeus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of the Pelagian archipelago (Lampedusa, Linosa, Lampione), with [Limonium albidum], [Limonium lopadusanum], [Limonium intermedium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Adriatic sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Puglia, the Gargano, the Tremiti Islands and the Adriatic coast of central Italy, with [Limonium peucetium], [Limonium cancellatum], [Limonium virgatum] var. [majus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Triesto-Liburnian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of the Triestine Karst, Istria, the Velebit coast south to the Zrmanja estuary, and the Quarnero islands (Kvarner islands) of Krk, Cres, Rab, Losinj, Pag, with [Limonium cancellatum] and [Plantago scopulorum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dalmatian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of the Svilaja and Biokovo coasts of Dalmatia, between the Zrmanj and the Neretva estuaries, and of the islands of the Dalmatian archipelago from Silba to Hvar.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Vardean sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of the Ragusan coast of extreme southern Croatia, from the Peljesac peninsula southwards, the coast of Montenegro and the southeastern islands of the Dalmatian archipelago, including the Mljet, Korcula, Elafiti archipelagoes, with [Limonium anfractum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Ionian sea-cliff communities
