description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Albania, mostly limited to the southern, Keravnes, coast, western peninsular Greece, the western Peloponnese and the Ionian archipelago, with [Limonium anfractum] and [Limonium cancellatum], [Limonium oleifolium] ssp. [oleifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Aegean Greece, Aegean Turkey, the Aegean archipelagoes, Crete, Karpathos and Rhodes, with [Limonium oleifolium] ssp. [oleifolium], [Limonium aucheri], [Limonium frederici], [Limonium hyssopifolium], [Limonium pigadiense], [Limonium sieberi], [Limonium sinuatum], [Centaurea huljakii], [Malcolmia flexuosa], [Sedum atratum], and a number of narrow endemics, including [Limonium graecum], [Limonium carpathum], [Limonium sitiacum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Mediterranean sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Mediteranean southern Turkey, Cyprus, the Levant and Cyrenaica, with [Limonium oleifolium] ssp. [oleifolium], [Pancratium maritimum], [Frankenia pulverulenta], [Senecio joppensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Maghrebian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Tunisia, Algeria, Mediterranean Morocco, Melilla, Ceuta and the islands of the Sea of Alboran, with [Limonium gougetianum], [Limonium minutiflorum], [Limonium oleifolium], [Limonium spatulatum], [Limonium virgulatum], [Limonium aspagoides] and [Limonium gummiferum] of northwestern Algeria, [Limonium zembrae] of Zembra Island, [Brassica radicata], [brassica scopulorum], [Crithmum maritimum], [Asplenium marinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mauretano-Atlantic sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs and rocky shores of Atlantic Morocco, south to 27øN, with [Limonium mucronatum], [Chenolea tomentosa], [Polycarpaea nivea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic sea-cliff communities
description: Communities of the cliffs of the Black Sea, the Sea of Azov and the Sea of Marmara.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic sea-cliff communities
description: Communities colonizing sea-cliffs of the western Black Sea coast, including both typical hard-rock tall cliff communities, restricted to Cape Kaliakra and the maritime fa‡ade of the Istranca-Stranja, and more widespread low-cliff formations, related to sand beach communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic herbaceous sea-cliff communities
description: Herbaceous aerohaline communities of the sea-cliffs of the maritime fa‡ade of the Stranja and of the Cape Kaliakra area of Bulgaria, with [Limonium gmelinii], [Goniolimon collinum], [Crithmum maritimum], [Elymus pycnanthus], [Cichorium intybus], [Atriplex hastata], [Kochia prostrata], [Melilotus officinalis], [Convolvulus lineatus] and the local endemic [Silene caliacrae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic sea-cliff [Ficus] thickets
description: Thickets of [Ficus carica] and [Ulmus minor] of the cliffs of the western Black Sea coast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic low cliff communities
description: Low cliffs and neighbouring sands of the southern Romanian Black Sea coast (between Constanta and Vama Veche), harbouring communities dominated by [Scolymus hispanicus] and [Ecbalium elaterium], with [Atriplex tatarica], [Xanthium spinosum], [Lactuca saligna], [Lolium perenne] and [Polygonum aviculare].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs of the northern Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, with [Crithmum maritimum], [Kochia prostrata], [Elymus farctus] ssp. [bessarabicus], [Holosteum umbellatum], [Puccinellia distans], [Limonium meyeri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Pontic sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the cliffs of the southern coasts of the Black Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the sea-cliffs of the Canaries and Madeira, with [Crithmum maritimum], [Astydamia latifolia], [Schizogyne sericea], [Andryala glutinosa], [Plantago coronopus], [Tolpis fruticosa], [Aizoon canariense], [Campylanthus salsoloides], [Limonium pectinatum], [Frankenia ericifolia], [Reichardia ligulata], [Argyranthemum frutescens], [Lotus spp.], [Asplenium marinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean sea-cliff communities
description: Communities of the sea-cliffs of the Azores dominated by the endemic [Festuca petraea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cape Verde sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the sea-cliffs of the Cape Verde Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Atlantic sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the sea-cliffs of the coastal desert zone of northwest Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Desert sea-cliff communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the sea-cliffs of the Saharo-Sindian subtropical desert regions, along the Red Sea, the Arabian Sea and the Persian Gulf.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical sea-cliff and rocky shore communities
description: Aerohaline communities of the sea-cliffs and rocky shores of tropical regions.  [Sesuvium portulacastrum], [Philoxerus vermicularis], [Sporobolus virginicus] are characteristic. These communities are only represented, within the Palaearctic Region as here defined, along the west coast of Africa, in the Indian Ocean region and in the tropical Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal lagoon cliff communities
description: Communities of vascular chasmophytes and animals colonizing the cliffs of coastal saline or hypersaline bodies of water of the Palaearctic region, listed here only when they differ very significantly from the cliff communities of unit 18.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pantellerian lagoon cliff communities
description: Endemic [Limonium secundirameum]-dominated formations of the cliffs overlooking Bagno dell' Acqua, Pantelleria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic saline lagoon cliffs
description: Halocalcareous cliff communities of coastal lagoons of the Black Sea at Cape Dolosman (Romania), dominated by [Artemisia santonicum], [Limonium gmelinii], [Halimione verrucifera] ([Obione verrucifera]) and [Lepidium cartilagineum], with Irano-Turanian species such as [Camphorosma annua], [Halocnemum strobilaceum], [Leuzea salina] and [Taraxacum bessarabicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Deposit sea-cliffs
description: Sea-cliffs composed of relatively soft, unconsolidated or incompact mineral particle deposits, carved by wind and wave action, of the Palaearctic region. They often support a vegetation of dune shrubs (units 16.25, 16.26, 16.27), notably, [Hippophae rhamnoides], [Salix arenaria], [Sorbus aucuparia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Islets, rock stacks, reefs, banks, shoals
description: Permanently emerging, periodically uncovered, surface-breaking or near-surface raised features of the oceans, their connected seas and coastal waters, with their associated marine and terrestrial communities. The associated marine habitats can be coded by combining subdivisions of prefix 11 with the relevant physiographic subdivisions of 19, the terrestrial habitats by adding codes from units 3 and 4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lithogenic rock stacks and islets
description: Small islands in the sea or coastal waters of the Palaearctic region, mostly important as sites for seabird colonies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Surface and underwater rocks
description: Palaearctic lithogenic reefs, raised rocky features of the continental shelf and its inshore waters, covered by shallow water or reaching and breaking the surface, or uncovered by tides or strong wave action.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Barrier islands, spits
description: Palaearctic spits, barrier beaches, barrier islands, tombolos, features formed of sands and gravels deposited by longshore drift in narrow ridges attached to the land at one end and extending into the sea at the other, or separated from land by channels and lagoons, or linking an offshore island to the coast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Banks and shoals
description: Deposits of muds, sands or gravels of the continental shelf permanently covered by shallow (banks), or very shallow (shoals), water of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coral reefs
description: Organogenic features of oceans, seas or coastal waters, formed by coral, coral sands and other coral derivatives, with a crest often rising just above low spring tide level. Characteristic of clear, warm tropical waters, they are limited within the Palaearctic region, as here defined, to the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf, the Arabian Sea, the Ryukyu Islands, Taiwan, the Pescadores, Hainan, the Gulf of Tong king and the South China Sea islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fringing reefs
description: Coral reefs bordering the land, forming close inshore on rocky coastlines by the growth of corals and associated hydrozoans, alcyonarians and calcareous algae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Barrier reefs
description: Coral reefs separated from the land by lagoons.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atolls
description: Annular coral reefs formed round subsiding volcanic islands, sometimes interrupted by channels, enclosing a lagoon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Seamounts and guyots
description: Elevated features of the floor of the oceans and their connected seas (unit 11.214) raising close enough to the surface to create neritic conditions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal agrosystems
description: Complex ecosystems, restricted to coastal areas of the Palaearctic region, and combining natural or seminatural habitats characteristic of units 11, 15, 16, 17 or 18 with agropastoral landscapes otherwise listed in unit 8, as well as more minor elements borrowed from other units.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Machair
description: Plains behind dunes especially characteristic of the western seaboard of the Outer Hebrides. Windblown calcareous sands deposited on peat support a flower-rich, and correspondingly insect-rich, dune grassland studded with shallow lochs and cultivated on a strip rotation. The grassland is dominated by [Poa pratensis] and [Festuca rubra], accompanied by [Thalictrum minus] ssp. [arenarium], [Thymus praecox] ssp. [arcticus] ([Thymus drucei]), [Bellis perennis], [Prunella vulgaris], [Erodium cicutarium], [Trifolium spp.], [Euphrasia spp.] and many orchids, among which [Dactylorhiza fuchsii] ssp. [hebridensis], [Dactylorhiza purpurella], [Gymnadenia conopsea], [Coeloglossum viride], [Platanthera chlorantha] and [Orchis mascula] are the most prominent. This grassland harbours a plant community of very restricted distribution comprising vulnerable species; [Cochlearia scotica], [Euphrasia marshallii] and [Dactylorhiza fuchsii] ssp. [hebridensis] are endemic. Other elements of the ecosystem, such as pools and fallow fields, can be noted by addition of codes from other units (units 22, 16.2, 34, 37, 53, 54, 82, 87). As a whole, machair is an essential habitat for breeding waders such as [Haematopus ostralegus], [Vanellus vanellus], [Charadrius hiaticula], [Calidris alpina], [Tringa totanus] and [Gallinago gallinago]; it supports the healthiest European population of the threatened corncrake [Crex crex].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Non-marine waters
description: All inland and landlocked waters of natural origin, standing or flowing, saline, brackish or fresh, and the aquatic or amphibious, nonmarine, communities associated with them; seminatural aquatic communities occupying manmade water bodies. Included are coastal lagoons, freshwater lakes, ponds or pools, the waters of athalassal saline, hypersaline or brackish pools, lakes and inland seas, permanent or temporary streams and rivers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal lagoons
description: Saline or hypersaline waters of the vicinity of the oceans and their connected seas, often formed from sea inlets by silting and cut off from the sea by more or less effective obstacles such as sand or mud banks. The presence of benthic marine invertebrate communities or vegetation can be indicated by combination of codes from units 11.2, 11.3 or 11.4 with the relevant physiographic subdivisions of unit 21; the presence of benthic communities of athalassal affinities can similarly be indicated by addition of codes of units 23.12, 23.13 or 23.14, that of benthic or floating athalassal macrophytes by use of codes of unit 23.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea-connected lagoons
description: Coastal lagoons incompletely closed off from the sea, communicating with it through a channel or channels, such as those between barrier islands or around or through a barrier beach.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Isolated lagoons
description: Coastal lagoons closed off from the sea, without communicating channels sufficient to allow significant water passage.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Percolation pools
description: Coastal water bodies fed by the seeping of sea water.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Silled or sluiced ponds
description: Water bodies separated from the sea by sills or sluices that regulate their communication, often limiting it to entry by waves, high tides or storms.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coral reef lagoons
description: Water bodies of the interior of atolls; coastal waters enclosed by fringing or barrier reefs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal lagoon islets
description: Small islands in large coastal bodies of saline water, mostly important as sites for waterbird colonies. Associated terrestrial habitats can be indicated by addition of codes from units 3 and 4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Standing freshwater
description: Lakes, ponds and pools of natural origin containing fresh ([i.e]. nonsaline) or slightly brackish water. Seminatural aquatic communities occupying manmade freshwater bodies, including artificially created lakes, reservoirs and canals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Permanent freshwater ponds and lakes
description: Freshwater lakes, ponds, pools, or parts of such freshwater bodies, in which water is permanently retained, although its level may fluctuate; their associated pelagic (units 22.11-22.15) and benthic (unit 22.16) communities. The macrophytic, euhydrophytic based communities that colonize them are separately listed under unit 22.4. Features of the lake bed uncovered by low water such as gravel, sand, mud or rock banks and beaches, and the communities they support, are listed under unit 22.26. Permanently or almost permanently emerged features supporting terrestrial communities influenced by the presence of the water body are included in unit 22.6. Fringing belts or island rafts of rooted or floating tall emergent vegetation are listed under unit 53.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lime-deficient oligotrophic waterbodies
description: Lakes and pools with greenish to brownish clear waters, poor in dissolved bases (pH often 5-6).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesotrophic waterbodies
description: Lakes and pools with waters fairly rich in dissolved bases (pH often 6-7).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eutrophic waterbodies
description: Lakes and pools with mostly dirty grey to blue-green, more or less turbid, waters, particularly rich in dissolved bases (pH usually > 7).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dystrophic waterbodies
description: Lakes and pools with acidic waters of high humus content and often brown tinted (pH often 3-5).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lime-rich oligo-mesotrophic waterbodies
description: Lakes and pools with mostly blue to greenish, very clear, waters, poor (to moderate) in nutrients, base-rich (pH often > 7.5).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lacustrine benthic communities
description: Lake-bottom animal, green algal or lower algal communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temporary freshwater bodies
description: Freshwater lakes, ponds, pools, or parts of such freshwater bodies, which become periodically dry, with their associated animal, green algal or lower algal pelagic (units 22.21 - 22.25) and benthic (units 22.26, 22.27) communities. The macrophytic-based amphibious communities that may colonize them are separately listed under unit 22.3, terrestrial communities that may develop during their dry phase under unit 22.5, drawdown resistant euhydrophyte communities under unit 22.2, fringing belts or island rafts of rooted or floating tall emergent vegetation under unit 53. Permanently or almost permanently emerged features supporting terrestrial communities influenced by the presence of the water body are included in unit 22.6.  Grasslands, shrublands and woodlands which may at times be inundated but in which semicontinuous formations of grasses, shrubs or trees emerge at all times above the standing water surface are listed under units 37, 3A, 44 and 4A, not under unit 22.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lime-deficient oligotrophic temporary waterbodies
description: Temporary lakes and pools with greenish to brownish clear waters, poor in dissolved bases (pH often 5-6).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesotrophic temporary waterbodies
description: Temporary lakes and pools with waters fairly rich in dissolved bases (pH often 6-7).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eutrophic temporary waterbodies
description: Temporary lakes and pools with mostly dirty grey to blue-green, more or less turbid, waters, particularly rich in dissolved bases (pH usually > 7).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dystrophic temporary waterbodies
description: Temporary lakes and pools with acidic waters of high humus content and often brown tinted (pH often 3-5).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lime-rich oligo-mesotrophic temporary waterbodies
description: Temporary lakes and pools with mostly blue to greenish, very clear, waters, poor (to moderate) in nutrients, base-rich (pH often > 7.5).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lake muds, sands and shingles
description: Unvegetated lake-bottoms or lake-shores temporarily exposed by artificial or natural fluctuations of the water level, often important as feeding grounds for migrating waders. Unvegetated lacustrine beaches, formed by wind or wave action.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temporary waterbody benthic communities
description: Benthic communities developed in the wet phase of the cycle of temporary lakes and pools.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amphibious macrophyte communities
description: Macrophytic communities of the Palaearctic adapted to an alternance of emergence and complete submersion, colonizing lake bottoms or lake shores subjected to temporary exposure (unit 22.2) and other periodically or occasionally inundated muddy, sandy or stony basins. They include communities of annuals developing during the exposure phase as well as communities of perennials susceptible of temporary total immersion. Communities of prostrate plants adapted to alternances of floating on shallow water and creeping on wet muds are listed under unit 22.432, as shallow water floating communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian perennial amphibious communities
description: Carpets of perennial vegetation submerged for a considerable part of the year in oligotrophic or mesotrophic lakes, ponds and pools of the boreal and nemoral zones of the Palaearctic and of mountains of the southern Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shoreweed lawns, lobelia ponds, quillwort swards
description: [Littorella uniflora], [Lobelia dortmanna] and [Isoetes spp.] formations of oligotrophic waters of the boreal and nemoral zones of the Palaearctic and of mountains of the southern Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shoreweed lawns
description: Dense, almost monospecific [Littorella uniflora] lawns of lake shores subject to great annual variations of the water level and long emergence, and other [Littorella]-dominated associations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lobelia ponds
description: [Lobelia dortmanna] colonies of shallow oligotrophic, moderately acid ponds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian quillwort swards
description: Clear-water quillwort swards formed by the northern European and montane [Isoetes lacustris] and [Isoetes echinospora] or by the very local endemics [Isoetes tenuissima] of central western France and [Isoetes brochonii] of the eastern Pyrenees. Associated species may include [Lobellia dortmanna], [Sparganium angustifolium], [Littorella uniflora], [Hippuris vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Floating bur-reed communities
description: [Sparganium angustifolium]-dominated formations of small oligotrophic ponds, characteristic, in particular, of the upper montane and subalpine levels of the Alps and of the greater Hercynian ranges, locally recorded from sub-Atlantic heath regions of the Germano-Baltic plain, also capable of occurring, within the extensive Fennoscandian range of the species, and in coastal areas of Iceland, as a facies of the [Isoetes] communities of unit 22.3119.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic lake mud communities
description: Amphibious communities dominated by [Ranunculus reptans] and [Subularia aquatica] colonizing, sometimes on large surfaces, the bottom of water bodies of Fennoscandia, Iceland and the Faeroe Islands, mostly in situations characterized by relatively large fluctuations of the water level.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian spearwort-awlwort communities
description: [Ranunculus reptans]-[Subularia aquatica] amphibious communities of Fennoscandian woodland water bodies with relatively large fluctuations in the water level. [Ranunculus reptans]-rich variants of unit 22.312, distributed in northern continental Europe and the Alpine periphery constitute a transition towards this nordic unit.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic spearwort-awlwort communites
description: [Ranunculus reptans]-[Subularia aquatica] amphibious flag communities of the lowlands of Iceland and the Faeroe Islands, with [Littorella uniflora], [Alopecurus aequalis] ssp. [natans], [Ranunculus hyperboreus], [Ranunculus aquatilis] var. [diffusus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic [Koenigia] lake mud communities
description: Flag communities colonizing fine material deposits of low arctic and northern boreal lakes and ponds of the Palaearctic region, known in particular from Iceland, the Faeroes and Greenland, with [Koenigia islandica], [Sagina nodosa], [Sagina procumbens], [Montia fontana], [Cerastium fontanum], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Equisetum arvense], lakeshore and wet flat eqivalent of the flowing water-linked communities of unit 24.54.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Myriophyllum alterniflorum] communities
description: Oligotrophic pool and pool fringe communities of the northern Palaearctic dominated by [Myriophyllum alterniflorum], characteristic of weakly acid clear waters on limestone-free substrates, sometimes with [Ranunculus reptans], [Littorella uniflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spike-rush shallow-water swards
description: [Eleocharis acicularis] beds of the Palaearctic, characteristic of more organic soils and mesotrophic waters than the communities of unit 22.311.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acid pool fringe shallow-water swards
description: [Eleocharis multicaulis], [Scirpus fluitans], [Juncus bulbosus], [Hypericum elodes], [Pilularia globulifera], [Deschampsia setacea], [Ranunculus flammula], [Littorella uniflora] communities of shallow acid pools of the Palaearctic and their margins susceptible to short periods of emersion.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eleocharis multicaulis] communities
description: Oligotrophic pool fringe communities of the western Palaearctic dominated by [Eleocharis multicaulis], [Deschampsia setacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune slack shoreweed swards
description: Communities of humid sands and pool fringes in oligotrophic dunes of the Atlantic, the North Sea and the southern Baltic, with [Samolus valerandi] and [Littorella uniflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Pilularia] swards
description: Oligotrophic pool fringe communities of western and central Europe, north to Denmark and southern Fennoscandia, east to Poland, the Czech Republic and the Balkan peninsula, dominated by the fern [Pilularia globulifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Juncus bulbosus] communities
description: Oligotrophic pool fringe communities of sub-Atlantic Europe dominated by [Juncus bulbosus], often accompanied by [Ranunculus flammula], [Agrostis canina], [Glyceria fluitans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Scirpus fluitans] communities
description: Pool fringe communities dominated by [Scirpus fluitans] ([Eleogiton fluitans], [Isolepis fluitans]), characteristic of mesotrophic to dystrophic heath pools on sands or muds, particularly within the [Quercion] domaine, with periods of drying usually short, sometimes permanently inundated.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Apium inundatum] communities
description: Pool fringe communities of western and central Europe dominated by [Apium inundatum], characteristic of oligotrophic to mesotrophic fluctuating pools, in particular, dune slack pools and forest pools.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Baldellia] shore swards
description: Communities of the shores of shallow oligotrophic pools of the Atlantic domaine of Europe susceptible to prolonged summer dessication, usually developed on peaty or parapeaty soils, dominated by, or rich in [Baldellia ranunculoides], with [Hydrocotyle vulgaris], [Hypericum helodes]. They are recorded, in particular, from the Paris Basin, Normandy, the New Forest, Cornwall, southern Scandinavia, and, on the shores of of limestone pools, in the Burren of western Ireland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shore hairgrass swards
description: [Deschampsia littoralis] agg. formations of peri-Alpine lakes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine shore hairgrass swards
description: [Deschampsia littoralis] swards of the shores of Lake Geneva and of a few lakes of the southern Alpine periphery (Lago di Poschiavo, Lago di Cavazzo).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lake Constance shore hairgrass swards
description: Amphibious hairgrass swards of Lake Constance, formed by the endemic, endangered, [Deschampsia rhenana], also harbouring [Myosotis rehsteineri], very local, endangered, [Ranunculus reptans], local, gravely threatened, and [Armeria purpurea], near-endemic, gravely threatened, extinct in Switzerland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian dwarf annual amphibious swards
description: Dwarf oligomesotrophic annual communities of recently emerged muds and sands of the nemoral, boreonemoral and boreal regions of the western and central Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf spike-rush communities
description: Rare communities colonising the fluid muds of drying ponds of nemoral, boreonemoral, boreal, and, locally, steppic, Palaearctic Eurasia, characterised by [Eleocharis ovata], [Eleocharis carniolica], [Carex bohemica], [Lindernia procumbens], [Scirpus supinus], [Limosella aquatica], [Cyperus fuscus], [Peplis portula], [Juncus tenageia], [Elatine hexandra], [Elatine hydropiper], and [Coleanthus subtilis]; the latter species has a highly disjunct distribution, principally in western France, the Czech Republic and adjacent southeastern Germany and northern Austria, the Lake Ladoga region of Russia and Amurland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune-slack centaury swards
description: Pioneer formations of humid calcareous sands of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Europe, recorded from the North Sea coasts of northern France, Belgium, the Netherlands, England, Germany and Denmark, and from the Baltic coast of Germany, with [Samolus valerandi], [Centaurium littorale], [Centaurium erythraea], [Centaurium pulchellum], [Gentianella amarella], [Blackstonia perfoliata], [Juncus bufonius], characteristic of humid dune slacks and dune pool fringes, on soils with low salinity.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf toad-rush communities
description: Associations, often very limited in extent, appearing in the drying phase of temporary pools, flooded ruts of forest paths, wet heath paths, humid forest cuts, seeping mowed lawns and other sufficiently lit temporarily inundated, most often acidic, soils of nemoral, boreonemoral, boreal, and, locally, steppic, Palaearctic Eurasia, characterised by [Juncus bufonius], [Scirpus setaceus], [Cyperus flavescens], [Centunculus minimus], [Spergularia segetalis], [Centaurium pulchellum], [Blackstonia perfoliata], [Samolus valerandi], [Cicendia filiformis], [Radiola linoides] and [Illecebrum verticillatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Toad-rush swards
description: Communities of temporary pools, flooded ruts of forest paths, and other sufficiently lit temporarily inundated or moist soils of nemoral, boreonemoral and boreal Palaearctic Eurasia dominated by [Juncus bufonius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small galingale swards
description: Medio-European communities dominated by the annual galingales [Cyperus flavescens], [Cyperus fuscus] and [Cyperus michelianus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wet ground dwarf herb communities
description: Varied communities, some very rare and threatened, of small annuals of wet ground of nemoral and boreonemoral Palaearctic Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bur marigold communities
description: Taller annual communities colonizing nitrogen-rich muds of dry ponds and lakes of the boreal and nemoral zones of the Palaearctic, and locally of the Eurasian steppe zone, formed by [Bidens spp.], [Rorippa palustris], [Rorippa islandica], [Chenopodium spp.], [Polygonum spp.], [Rumex maritimus], [Rumex palustris], [Ranunculus sceleratus], [Senecio congestus], [Catabrosa aquatica], [Leersia oryzoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic amphibious communities
description: Perennial and annual communities of mediterranean, thermo-Atlantic and Macaronesian temporary ponds, river banks and spring sides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Short Mediterranean amphibious swards
description: Formations of Mediterranean, thermo-Atlantic and Macaronesian entirely or partially summer-dry ponds, pools and ditches with [Isoetes spp.], [Marsilea quadrifolia], [Marsilea strigosa], [Pilularia globulifera], [Pilularia minuta], [Mentha pulegium], [Lythrum hyssopifolia] [s.l.], [Trifolium filiforme], [Peplis erecta], [Teucrium cravense], [Serapias lingua], [Juncus bufonius], [Juncus capitatus], [Juncus pygmaeus], [Juncus fasciculatus], [Scirpus savii], sometimes (rocky edges of fast rivulets), [Spiranthes aestivalis] and [Anagallis tenella].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Terrestrial quillwort communities
description: [Isoetes histrix], [Isoetes durieui] formations of Mediterranean ephemeral waters.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean aquatic quillwort swards
description: Communities formed by [Isoetes boryana], [Isoetes delilei], [Isoetes heldreichii], [Isoetes velata], [Isoetes azorica] or [Isoetes malinverniana] in fluctuating waterbodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean quillwort swards
description: Endemic [Isoetes azorica] communities of pools and small lakes of the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean small galingale swards
description: Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic formations dominated by [Cyperus fuscus], [Cyperus flavescens] or [Cyperus michelianus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Fimbristylis] swards
description: Formations dominated by [Fimbristylis bisumbellata], often with [Cyperus spp.], in particular, [Cyperus flavescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Chaetopogon] swards
description: Formations dominated by [Chaetopogon fasciculatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog pimpernell-summer lady's tresses communities
description: Formations of the sandy, rocky edges of rivulets of the Mediterranean region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean amphibious small herb communities
description: Formations of Mediterranean temporarily inundated or wet terrain, including karstic pools, often highly ephemereal, dominated by annual small herbs, among which [Elatine spp.] ([Elatine macropoda], [Elatine gussonei], [Elatine pedunculata]), [Damasonium bourgaei], [Nananthea perpusilla], [Morisia monanthos], [Blackstonia perfoliata], [Samolus valerandi], [Radiola linoides], [Myosurus minimus], [Laurentia gasparrinii], [Laurentia tenella].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean dwarf [Scirpus] swards
description: Formations of the Mediterranean basin occupying temporarily inundated or wet terrain, dominated by small club-rushes of section [Isolepis] ([Scirpus setaceus], [Scirpus pseudosetaceus], [Scirpus cernuus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean [Eleocharis] swards
description: Formations of temporarily inundated or wet terrain, dominated by spike-rushes ([Eleocharis palustris]), accompanied by small annual herbs and grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean tall amphibious swards
description: Formations of Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic entirely or partially summer-dry ponds, pools, ditches and springs, developed on terrain covered by deep waters during long periods, composed of an admixture of small annuals and of tall perennials or annuals, in particular, of genera [Mentha] ([Mentha cervina], [Mentha longifolia]) and [Eryngium] ([Eryngium corniculatum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean amphibious crypsis swards
description: Slighly halophile and nitrophile post-estival vegetation of temporarily inundated terrains, with [Crypsis schoenoides], [Crypsis aculeata], [Crypsis alopecuroides] and [Centaurium spicatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Serapias] grasslands
description: Meso-hygrophile grasslands of crystalline Provence, with [Carex divisa] ssp. [chaetophylla], often dominant, [Briza minor], [Oenanthe lachenalii] and numerous [Serapias] species ([Serapias lingua], [Serapias neglecta], [Serapias vomeracea]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian amphibious communities
description: Annual dwarf sedges, rushes and [Elatine spp.] communities of recently emerged muds and sands, characteristic of the Pannonic plain, the Black Sea lowlands and adjacent areas of the Balkan peninsula, outside of the Mediterranean influence. Communities of units 22.321 and 22.323 occur locally in the same region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Pannonic riverbank dwarf sedge communities
description: Communities of nitrogen-rich muds and inundation zones of watercourses and lakes of the western central Eurasian steppe and presteppe zones, in particular of Pannonic and sub-Pannonic plains and hills, with [Cyperus fuscus], [Cyperus flavescens], [Cyperus michelianus] ([Dichostylis michelianus]), [Juncus bufonius], [Echinochloa crus-galli], [Filaginella uliginosa] ([Gnaphalium uliginosum]), [Elatine hungarica], [Ammannia verticillata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Pannonic rice-field dwarf sedge communities
description: Communities of rice field muds and of river and lake inundation zones of the western central Eurasian steppe and pre-steppe zones, distributed in particular in the Pannonic region, Russia, the Balkans and central Asia, with [Elatine hungarica], [Elatine triandra], [Eleocharis acicularis], [Scirpus supinus], [Lindernia procumbens], [Peplis portula], [Marsilea quadrifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Pannonic halo-nitrophile amphibious swards
description: Communities of the western central Eurasian steppe and presteppe zones, extending from Pannonic and sub-Pannonic plains and hills to the Caucasus, developed on clayey, nitrogen-rich saline or somewhat saline soils. Characteristic species include [Lythrum hyssopifolia], [Lythrum tribracteatum], [Lythrum linifolium], terrestrial forms of [Elatine alsinastrum], [Elatine triandra], [Elatine hydropiper], [Elatine hungarica], [Mentha aquatica], [Hippuris vulgaris] and crowfoots of subgenus [Batrachium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical and tropical amphibious communities
description: Fresh water amphibious communities of the tropics, the subtropical desert belt and of warm-temperate humid eastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lacustrine euhydrophyte communities
description: Communities of permanent or semipermanent fresh or slightly brackish lakes, ponds, pools or canals of the Palaearctic realm formed by free-floating, floating-leaved rooted, or submerged macrophytes and their associated epiphytic biocoenoses. Tall emergent-dominated formations, rooted in the substratum or constituting soil-retaining floating islands, are excluded and listed in unit 53.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Free-floating vegetation
description: Free-floating surface communities of more or less nutrient-rich waters of the Palaearctic realm.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Duckweed covers
description: Free-floating surface communities of duckweed ([Lemna], [Spirodela], [Wolffia]), small ferns ([Azolla]) or liverworts ([Riccia], [Ricciocarpus]) of  Palaearctic waters.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Frogbit rafts
description: Free-floating surface communities of Palaearctic waters rich in [Hydrocharis morsus-ranae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water-soldier rafts
description: Free-floating communities of Palaearctic waters dominated by [Stratiotes aloides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bladderwort colonies
description: Free-floating communities of more or less nutrient-rich Palaearctic waters dominated by bladderworts ([Utricularia australis], [Utricularia vulgaris]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Salvinia] covers
description: Free-foating communities of Central and Eastern Europe dominated by the free-floating nonindigenous fern [Salvinia natans], often forming dense and extensive mats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Aldrovanda] communities
description: Rare aquatic formations of Central and Eastern Europe, dispersed from southern Brandenburg and Lake Constance east to the Ukraine, with a former outpost in eastern Lithuania, harbouring the carnivorous, free-floating Droseraceae [Aldrovanda vesiculosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water lettuce beds
description: Colonies of the free-floating, rosette-forming [Pistia stratiotes] of tropical and subtropical regions of the southern Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water hyacinth rafts
description: Formations of the introduced Neotropical [Eichornia crassipes] established in seminatural situations, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions of the southern Palaearctic, locally in west-central Portugal.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rooted submerged vegetation
description: Formations of Palaearctic water bodies constituted by submerged, rooted, perennial phanerogams with often emerging flower spikes, in particular entirely immersed pondweeds of genus [Potamogeton].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Large pondweed beds
description: Associations of large pondweeds ([Potamogeton lucens], [Potamogeton praelongus], [Potamogeton zizii], [Potamogeton perfoliatus]) characteristic of deep, open Palaearctic waters.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small pondweed communities
description: Formations of smaller pondweeds, in particular, [Potamogeton crispus], [Potamogeton filiformis], [Potamogeton pusillus], [Potamogeton obtusifolius], [Potamogeton berchtoldii], [Potamogeton trichoides], [Potamogeton acutifolius], [Potamogeton pectinatus], [Potamogeton nitens], [Potamogeton friesii] ([Potamogeton mucronatus]), [Groenlandia densa], waterthymes and waterweeds ([Elodea spp.], [Hydrilla spp.], [Ottelia spp.]), horned pondweeds ([Zannichellia palustris] [s.l.]), naiads ([Najas spp.]), tapegrass ([Vallisneria spiralis]), water crowfoots ([Ranunculus circinatus]) that colonize shallower, more sheltered Palaearctic waters. Eurasian formations dominated by usually free-floating hornworts of genus [Ceratophyllum], in particular by [Ceratophyllum demersum], are included because of closer ecological and physiognomic similarity with communities of this unit than with those of unit 22.41.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fine-leaved pondweed communities
description: Submerged pondweed beds of Palaearctic waters dominated by small pondweeds of genera [Potamogeton] and [Groenlandia], in particular, [Potamogeton crispus], [Potamogeton filiformis], [Potamogeton pusillus], [Potamogeton obtusifolius], [Potamogeton berchtoldii], [Potamogeton trichoides], [Potamogeton acutifolius], [Potamogeton pectinatus], [Potamogeton nitens], [Potamogeton friesii] ([Potamogeton mucronatus]), [Groenlandia densa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Submerged hydrocharid communities
description: Submerged pondweed beds of Palaearctic waters dominated by waterthymes and waterweeds of genera [Elodea], [Hydrilla], [Ottelia] or by tapegrass ([Vallisneria spiralis]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Naiad communities
description: Submerged pondweed beds of Palaearctic waters dominated by naiads ([Najas spp.]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Horned pondweed communities
description: Submerged pondweed beds of Palaearctic waters dominated by horned pondweeds ([Zannichellia palustris] [s.l.]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Submerged water crowfoot communities
description: Submerged pondweed beds of Palaearctic waters dominated by water crowfoots ([Ranunculus circinatus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hornwort communities
description: Submerged pondweed beds of Palaearctic waters dominated by usually free-floating hornworts of genus [Ceratophyllum], in particular by [Ceratophyllum demersum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rooted floating vegetation
description: Formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by rooted aquatic plants with floating leaves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Floating broad-leaved carpets
description: Formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by rooted aquatic plants with large floating leaves, often with a stratum of submerged species ([Ceratophyllum], [Myriophyllum], [Potamogeton]) and occasionally free-floating [Utricularia spp.], characteristic of large, permanent water bodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Waterlily beds
description: Floating-leaved formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by magnonymphaeids of family Nymphaeaceae, in particular of genera [Nymphaea], [Nuphar], [Euryale].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Nuphar] beds
description: Floating-leaved formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by magnonymphaeids of genus [Nuphar], in particular [Nuphar pumila] and [Nuphar lutea], characteristic of temperate and cold regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Nuphar lutea] beds
description: Dense communities of the large thick-leaved [Nuphar lutea] characteristic of nutrient-rich waters of ponds, lakes and canals with depths up to 4 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Nuphar pumila] beds
description: Relict communities of arctic-continental distribution mostly characteristic of relatively oligotrophic acid ponds surrounded by, or adjacent to, bogs or woods, dominated by small-leaved [Nuphar spp.], mostly [Nuphar pumila] or [Nuphar intermedia], often accompanied by [Potamogeton natans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern [Nymphaea] beds
description: Floating-leaved formations of boreal, temperate and Mediterranean Palaearctic waters dominated by magnonymphaeids of genus [Nymphaea], in particular [Nymphaea alba], [Nymphaea candida], [Nymphaea tetragona], [Nymphaea pygmaea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Transylvanian hot-spring lotus beds
description: Formations of [Nymphaea lotus] of geo-thermal waters (unit 66.94) of Petea Lake, western Romania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical waterlily and lotus beds
description: Formations of [Nymphaea lotus], [Nymphaea caerulea], [Nymphaea maculata] of the subtropical desert belt of the Palaearctic region and of the Sahel.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern [Nymphaea] beds
description: [Nymphaea] formations of warm-temperate humid, subtropical and tropical regions of the Far Eastern Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Euryale] beds
description: Large-leaved [Euryale ferox] formations of China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water chestnut carpets
description: Floating-leaved formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by the trapid [Trapa natans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fringed waterlily carpets
description: Floating-leaved formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by magnonymphaeids of genus [Nymphoides], in particular by [Nymphoides peltata] or [Nymphoides indica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Broad-leaved pondweed carpets
description: Floating-leaved formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by the parvonymphaeid [Potamogeton natans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amphibious bistort carpets
description: Floating-leaved formations of Palaearctic waters dominated by the parvonymphaeid [Polygonum amphibium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sacred lotus beds
description: Formations of [Nelumbo nucifera], occurring in the Volga delta and from the south Caspian lowlands to the Far East, with a naturalized population in Romania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Long-leaved bur-reed carpets
description: Aquatic formations of the boreal zone dominated by species of genus [Sparganium] with long, strap-like floating leaves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sparganium gramineum] floating carpets
description: Aquatic formations of oligotrophic boreal woodland and mire lakes of Fennoscandia, Russia, the Baltic States and Belarus dominated by [Sparganium gramineum], with 1- to 2-metre long floating leaves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sparganium hyperboreum] floating carpets
description: Aquatic formations of mesotrophic small, shallow heath and mire lakes of low alpine and northern lowland regions of Iceland, dominated by [Sparganium hyperboreum], with 10- to 20-cm long floating leaves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shallow-water floating communities
description: Communities of Palaearctic waters dominated by water starworts ([Callitriche]), water crowfoots ([Ranunculus spp.], subgenus [Batrachium]) or water violet ([Hottonia palustris]), characteristic mostly of shallow waters with fluctuating water levels, susceptible to occasional drying.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water crowfoot communities
description: Communities dominated by water crowfoots, [Ranunculus peltatus], [Ranunculus aquatilis], [Ranunculus trichophyllus] ([Ranunculus confervoides], [Ranunculus aquatilis] var. [diffusus]), [Ranunculus baudotii], [Ranunculus hederaceus], [Ranunculus rionii], [Ranunculus ololeucos], [Ranunculus omiophyllus] ([Ranunculus lenormandi]), [Ranunculus tripartitus], with both submerged and floating leaves, characteristic mostly of shallow Palaearctic waters with fluctuating water levels, susceptible to occasional drying. Crowfoot- dominated communities of unit 22.433 are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water starwort communities
description: Communities of shallow stagnant Palaearctic waters with fluctuating water levels, susceptible to drying, dominated by [Callitriche spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water violet beds
description: Communities of shallow Palaearctic waters dominated by [Hottonia palustris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oligotrophic pondweed communities
description: Sparse formations of narrow-leaved floating pondweeds, in particular, [Potamogeton polygonifolius] ([Potamogeton oblongus]), [Potamogeton gramineus], [Potamogeton alpinus], with [Callitriche spp.], [Ranunculus ololeucos], [Ranunculus omiophyllus], [Ranunculus tripartitus], [Luronium natans], [Sparganium minimum], [Apium inundatum] of shallow, oligotrophic, clean, fluctuating, but usually permanent, often small, waterbodies of the Palaearctic region. Communities of this unit often form in close proximity to those of unit 22.313 and evolve into them with regular or prolonged dessication.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chandalier algae submerged carpets
description: Charophyte (genera [Chara], [Nitella], [Tolypella], [Nitellopsis], [Lamprothamnium], [Lychnothamnus]) algal carpets of the bottom of unpolluted, oligotrophic to mesotrophic lakes and pools of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Chara] carpets
description: Charophyte carpets developed on the bottom of basic, lime-rich, unpolluted, oligotrophic to mesotrophic, lakes and pools of the Palaearctic region, formed mostly by species of genus [Chara].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Deep water [Chara] carpets
description: Charophyte carpets developed on the bottom of unpolluted basic, lime-rich, oligotrophic to mesotrophic, deep, permanent waterbodies of the Palaearctic region, formed by, in particular, [Chara aspera], [Chara hispida], [Chara tomentosa], [Chara fragilis], [Chara strigosa], [Chara intermedia], [Nitellopsis obtusa], [Tolypella glomerata]. Many of the diverse communities formed by these species have a highly fragmented, relict range and are severely threatened.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shallow water [Chara] carpets
description: Charophyte carpets developed in shallower, often ephemereal pools of the Palaearctic region, formed by [Chara vulgaris], [Tolypella intricata], [Tolypella prolifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Nitella] carpets
description: Charophyte carpets developed on the bottom of unpolluted acid, neutral or slightly basic, lime-poor, oligotrophic to mesotrophic, lakes of the Palaearctic region, mostly formed by species of genus [Nitella].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acidocline [Nitella] carpets
description: Charophyte carpets developed on the bottom of unpolluted, slightly acid to neutral, lime-poor, oligotrophic or dystrophic, lakes and pools of oceanic and suboceanic lowland and collinar regions of the Palaearctic region, formed by, in particular, [Nitella gracilis], [Nitella capillaris], [Nitella flexilis], [Nitella translucens], [Chara braunii], [Chara fragifera], [Chara delicatula]. Many of the diverse communities formed by these species have a highly fragmented, relict range and are severely threatened.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Neutrocline [Nitella] carpets
description: Charophyte carpets developed on the bottom of unpolluted, neutral to slightly basic, oligotrophic to mesotrophic, lakes and pools of the Palaearctic region, mostly characteristic of premontane and moraine areas in zones of contact between siliceous and calcareous substrates, formed by, in particular, [Nitella opaca], [Nitella mucronata], [Nitella syncarpa], [Nitella tenuissima], [Nitella hyalina], [Chara coronata], [Tolypella prolifera], sometimes accompanied by the chrysophyte alga [Vaucheria dichotoma] of class Xanthophyceae. Many of the diverse communities formed by these species have a highly fragmented, relict range and are severely threatened.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peatmoss and bladderwort pools
