description: Floating, in part infra-aquatic, formations of [Sphagnum spp.], [Scorpidium scorpioides], [Utricularia minor], [Utricularia intermedia], [Utricularia ochroleuca], [Utricularia bremii], [Sparganium minimum], of dystrophic, oligotrophic or sometimes mesotrophic, bog pools, fen pools, heath pools, woodland ponds of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peatmoss-bladderwort pools
description: Floating formations of [Sphagnum spp.] ([Sphagnum auriculatum], [Sphagnum contortum], [Sphagnum cuspidatum], [Sphagnum fallax], [Sphagnum inundatum], [Sphagnum subsecundum], [Sphagnum crassicladum], [Sphagnum rufescens]), [Utricularia minor], [Utricularia ochroleuca], of dystrophic or oligotrophic, lime-poor bog pools, acid fen pools, heath pools, woodland ponds of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brownmoss-bladderwort pools
description: Floating formations of brown mosses ([Scorpidium scorpidioides], [Calliergon stramineum], [Calliergon giganteum], [Calliergon trifarium], [Calliergon cordifolium], [Campylium stellatum], [Drepanocladus aduncus], [Drepanocladus revolvens], [Drepanocladus intermedius], [Drepanocladus exannulatus]), [Utricularia minor], [Utricularia intermedia] of basic, neutral or weakly acid, oligotrophic or sometimes mesotrophic, often lime-rich, fen pools, transition mire pools and ponds of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sparganium minimum] pools
description: Rare aquatic formations of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Palaearctic dystrophic to mesotrophic, basic to mildly acid, rich fen, transition mire and heath pools, dominated by the rooted, floating-leaved [Sparganium minimum], usually accompanied by [Utricularia intermedia], sometimes by [Potamogeton polygonifolius], [Potamogeton gramineus], [Juncus bulbosus], [Littorella uniflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Turlough and lake-bottom meadows
description: Terrestrial communities colonizing the bottom of waterbodies that are completely and recurrently emptied of water for part of the time, such as Irish turloughs. The characteristics of each stage of the cycle can be defined by use of codes of units 22.1, 22.2, 22.3, 22.4, and, if appropriate, those of units 37, 38, 53, 54, or 8.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lacustrine islets
description: Permanently or usually emergent features of the bed or shores of permanent or temporary freshwater lakes or ponds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lake ice
description: Permanent or almost permanent ice formations of lakes, constituting continuous ice sheets that may cover the entire surface for all of the year or recede to part of the lake during summer and be accompanied or replaced by floating ice blocks, rafts and hummocks. They may, locally, seasonally or permanently, extend to the whole depth of the lake. They are characteristic of high latitude and high altitude lakes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Standing brackish and salt water
description: Athalassal decidedly brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, pools and ditches, their features, their associated pelagic and benthic communities, their beds of macrophytic submerged or offshore vegetation. Included are the large inland "seas", in particular, the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea, the Dead Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Athalassic saline lakes
description: Athalassic, permanent or temporary, brackish, saline or hypersaline waterbodies and their associated animal, charophyte, green algal or lower algal pelagic and benthic communities. The macrophytic, euhydrophytic based communities that colonize them are separately listed under 23.2, the macrophytic amphibious communities and the terrestrial communities that may develop during dry phases or in drying and dried portions under 15, fringing belts or island rafts of rooted or floating tall emergent vegetation under 53.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salt basins and salt basin pelagic communities
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools and their pelagic animal, green algal or lower algal communities, including marine mammal, bird and pelagic fish communities of the large inland seas of central Eurasia and of the big brackish lakes of the boreal zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal, nemoral and arctic salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools of the boreal, nemoral and arctic zones, including, in particular, the great brackish lakes of northern Europe (Ladoga), the ponds and pools associated with the inland salt communities of unit 15.4 and the waterbodies adjacent to the Yakutian salt steppes of unit 15.A7.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools of the Mediterranean zone, with major waterbodies limited to northern-central and southern Iberia, Sicily and Mediterranean North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Pannonic salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools of the Pannonic and Ponto-Sarmatic regions, associated with the salt steppes and salt marshes of 15.A1 and 15.A2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools of the Aralo-Caspian and Kazakh steppe and desert regions, including the Caspian Sea, the Aral Sea, Lake Balkash, Issyk Kul, Lake Tengiz, Ala Kul, Lake Zayzan and many other large or small waterbodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools of of the East Asian steppe and desert regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools of the Irano-Anatolian steppe and cold desert regions, including Tuz Golu, Lake Van, Lake Urmia and the great temporary khevirs of central Iran, as well as many smaller waterbodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Mediterranean and Saharo-Sindian salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline permanent or temporary lakes, ponds or pools of the subtropical desert belt and its transitions to the Mediterranean regions, including the great North African chotts, the Dead Sea, and many lesser waterbodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical salt lakes
description: Athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools of sub-Saharan Africa and the tropical Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salt basin charophyte carpets
description: Charophyte (mostly [Chara spp.]) formations of athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salt basin benthic communities
description: Benthic animal, green algal or lower algal communities of permanent athalassic brackish, saline or hypersaline lakes, ponds or pools; benthic communities developed in the wet phase of the cycle of temporary brackish, saline or hypersaline athalassic waterbodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salt basin muds or shingles
description: Unvegetated bottoms or shores of athalassic saline water bodies temporarily exposed by artificial or natural fluctuations of the water level, often covered with salt efflorescences.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Athalassic saline euhydrophyte communities
description: Communities of athalassic brackish or saline lakes, ponds, pools or basins, formed by submerged, floating-leaved, or slightly emergent macrophytes and their associated zoocoenoses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Submerged formations
description: Communities of athalassic brackish or saline lakes, ponds, pools or basins, formed by submerged macrophytes and their associated zoocoenoses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Athalassic tasselweed communities
description: [Ruppia maritima], [Zannichellia spp.] and [Najas spp.] beds, with associated [Potamogeton pectinatus], [Potamogeton crispus] and other submerged macrophytes, of athalassic brackish or saline lakes, ponds, pools or basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Athalassic seagrass communities
description: [Zostera noltii] formations of the Caspian Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Athalassic dwarf spike-rush beds
description: Emergent [Eleocharis parvula] or [Eleocharis acicularis] formations of brackish lakes and inland seas, their inlets, estuaries, lagoons, mud or sand flats, and other inland brackish waterbodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Athalassic brackish water floating communities
description: Communities of brackish lakes, ponds and pools, formed by free-floating or floating-leaved rooted macrophytes, in particular, brackish [Lemna] and [Wolffia] carpets, brackish [Callitriche] communities and formations of inland lakes and basins of very low salinity dominated by water crowfoots such as [Ranunculus baudotii] or [Ranunculus rionii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salt lake islands
description: Permanently or usually emergent features of inland seas and of permanent or temporary saline lakes or ponds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salt lake beaches
description: Beaches of inland seas and of large saline lakes, formed by wind or wave action.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salt lake estuaries
description: Estuaries formed by rivers emptying into inland seas and large saline lakes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Running water
description: All rivers and streams, permanent or temporary, fresh or saline, including rivers, streams, brooks, rivulets, rills, torrents, wadis or oueds, waterfalls, cascades and rapids.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rivers and streams
description: Flowing water courses of the Palaearctic region, permanent or temporary, and their associated animal and microscopic algae pelagic and benthic communities. Rivers, streams, brooks, rivulets, rills, torrents, wadis or oueds, waterfalls, cascades and rapids are included. The macrophytic, euhydrophytic communities that colonize them are separately listed under unit 24.4. Features of the river bed, uncovered by low water or permanently emerging, such as gravel, sand, mud or rock islands and bars are listed under units 24.2, 24.3, 24.5 and 24.6. The macrophytic amphibious communities and the terrestrial communities that may develop on them are listed under the relevant sections when specific to watercourses, are otherwise indicated by codes from units 15, 22.3, 3 or 4. The fringing belts of tall or short emergent vegetation are listed under unit 53, the spring vegetation under unit 54.1, the riverside veils of tall herbs and lianas under unit 37.71, riverine arbustive and arborescent vegetation under unit 44. The subdivisions of this unit are based on slope, width and water temperature, according to usual ichthyological practice. Classifications based on flora, such as that of Holmes (1983) for British streams, give broadly similar results. For each of the divisions below, subdivisions can be introduced to take into account regional characteristics, as well as the morphodynamics of the stream, as proposed, for instance, by Malavoi (1989).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Springs and rivulets
description: Gushing springs (rheocrenes), spring basins (limnocrenes), seepages (helocrenes) and crenal streams, rivulets formed in and near the source area of streams, characterized by high stability of temperature, near the annual average of the ground water, best developed in mountain situations. The presence of specialized vegetation associated with the spring is indicated by use of divisions of unit 54.1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Epirhitral and metarhitral streams
description: Upper and middle reaches of Palaearctic mountain streams ("Gebirgsbach", "alpine", "mountain" and "upland" streams), characterized by turbulent, irregular flow, by diurnal and annual temperature variations higher than in the crenon, and, by aquatic biocoenoses largely dominated by Turbellaria, Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, Trichoptera, Diptera, by Bryophyta and epilithic Bacillariophyta, Cyanophycaea, Rhodophyta and Chlorophyta algae, with few, specialized, immerged macrophytes (unit 24.3). The unit corresponds to the "Trout zone" or "Salmonid zone" of western European ichthyological classifications.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyporhitral streams
description: Lower reaches of Palaearctic mountain streams ("Gebirgsbach", "alpine", "mountain" and "upland" streams), often representing the middle course of rivers. The unit corresponds to the "Grayling zone" of western European ichthyological classifications.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Epipotamal streams
description: Upper reaches of Palaearctic lowland streams ("Niederungsbach", "lowland" and "plain" streams), characterized by calmer flow, higher annual temperature variation and aquatic biocoenoses comprising more standing water species, among them immerged macrophytes (unit 24.3). The unit corresponds to the "Barbel zone" of western European ichthyological classifications.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Metapotamal and hypopotamal streams
description: Middle and lower reaches of Palaearctic lowland streams ("Niederungsbach", "lowland" and "plain" streams), with aquatic biocoenoses very similar to those of standing water. The unit corresponds to the "Bream zone" of western European ichthyological classifications.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intermittent streams
description: Palaearctic watercourses of which the flow is interrupted for part of the year, leaving a dry bed or pools; conditions during the period of flow can be indicated by one of the previous codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Waterfalls
description: More or less vertical descent of a water course over irregularities of the streambed.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River gravels
description: Deposit beds of Palaearctic streams formed of pebbles, gravels, boulders or a mixture of gravels and finer sediments, with the communities that occupy them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River gravel deposits
description: Deposit beds of Palaearctic streams formed of pebbles, gravels, boulders or a mixture of gravels and finer sediments, occupying the edges of the stream, forming islands in the channel or supporting the arms and rivulets constituting the stream, together with their associated animal communities. The presence of vascular vegetation is indicated by use of the appropriate code from unit 24.22. Water-fringing communities, in particular of units 53, 37.7, 37.8, 37.9, may contribute to the colonisation of the deposits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River gravel banks
description: Deposit beds of Palaearctic streams formed of pebbles, gravels, boulders or a mixture of gravels and finer sediments strewn along the sides of the stream or constituting islands in its channel.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River gravel fans and sandar
description: Large beds of gravels, pebbles, boulders or mixed coarse and fine sediments constituting outwash fans, alluvial fans, sandar (sandur), deposited and criss-crossed by braided rivers of the Palaearctic region, characteristic, in particular, of boreal and arctic lands with intense fluvio-glacial deposition.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River gravel communities
description: Vascular plant communities occupying gravel deposits of Palaearctic rivers, including pioneer vegetation and subsequent stages in the colonization sequence. Early-stage communities of Alpide, boreal and Mediterranean watercourses are specialized, those of nemoral lowlands and hills are related to other formations, in particular those of unit 37.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine stream gravel communities
description: Open assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants, rich in alpine species, colonizing gravel beds of Palaearctic streams with an alpine, summer-high, flow regime, formed in northern boreal and lower arctic mountains, hills and sometimes lowlands, as well as in the alpine and subalpine zones of higher, glaciated, mountains of more southern regions, sometimes with abyssal stations at lower altitudes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine willowherb river gravel communities
description: Open assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants colonizing  alluvial and glacial gravels and sands inundated by rivulets and streams of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Alps. Characteristic plants include [Epilobium fleischeri], [Saxifraga bryoides], [Gypsophila repens], [Rumex cutatus], [Trifolium pallescens], [Astragalus sempervirens], [Rhacomitrium canescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic alluvial gravel communities
description: Open assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants colonizing gravel beds of streams of northern boreal and lower arctic Eurasian mountains, hills and sometimes lowlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic mountain sorrel river gravels
description: Low open assemblies of grasses and herbs colonising the lower parts of stony, boulder-strewn shingle banks of rivers in the mountains of boreal and arctic Scandinavia and in Iceland dominated by [Oxyria digyna] and [Cerastium alpinum] or by [Calamagrostis stricta], [Deschampsia cespitosa] and [Oxyria digyna]. There are very few lichens and mosses present, except in the [Calamagrostis] communities, in which [Hypnum lindbergii] may be abundant, and in the Norwegian and Icelandic representatives of the [Cerastium] communities, in which they play an important part, in particular the mosses [Rhacomitrium canescens] and [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic riverbeauty gravel communities
description: Often sparse and lacunar assemblies of herbaceous plants dominated by the spectacular, low-growing, [Epilobium latifolium], a species restricted in the Palaearctic to Iceland, Greenland and Siberia, variously accompanied by [Silene uniflora], [Festuca richardsoni], colonizing shingle, gravel and sand deposits of river beds of lowlands and lower mountains of Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic [Rhacomitrium] river gravels
description: Extremely dry, level, gravelly and stony terraces situated above the water line of rivers of Iceland and of the alpine and arcto-alpine regions of Scandinavia, colonized by a continuous moss and lichen cover dominated by [Rhacomitrium canescens], [Stereocaulon spp.], and, in Iceland, [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], with few vascular plants.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian alpine river gravel communities
description: Open assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants colonizing  alluvial and glacial gravels and sands inundated by rivulets and streams of the alpine and subalpine levels of central Eurasian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern alpine river gravel communities
description: Open assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants colonizing  alluvial and glacial gravels and sands inundated by rivulets and streams of the alpine and subalpine levels of mountains of eastern Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane river gravel communities
description: Open or closed assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants, colonizing, within the montane or submontane levels, gravel beds of streams with an alpine, summer-high, flow regime, born in high mountains of the Alpine system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River gravel chondrilla communities
description: Open and often unstable assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants, rich in casual immigrants from higher altitudes, colonizing gravel beds of the montane reaches of unregulated Alpine streams, with [Chondrilla chondrilloides], often accompanied by [Erucastrum nasturtiifolium], [Gypsophila repens], [Dryas octopetala], [Aethionema saxatile], [Epilobium dodonaei], [Erigeron acer], [Leontodon berinii], [Buphthalmum salicifolium], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Fumana procumbens], [Agrostis gigantea], [Anthyllis vulneraria] ssp. [alpestris], [Campanula cochlearifolia], [Hieracium piloselloides], [Calamagrostis pseudophragmites], [Conyza canadensis], [Pritzelago alpina], and seedlings of [Salix elaeagnos], [Salix purpurea], [Salix daphnoides] and [Myricaria germanica].  Because of widespread interference with natural flow regimes, these formations are gravely endangered.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small-reed river gravel communities
description: Closed or lacunar assemblies of often large herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants colonizing montane and submontane gravel beds loaded with finer sands or silts of unregulated streams of the Alpine system and its vicinity.  [Calamagrostis pseudophragmites] is usually dominant, seedlings of montane and dealpine willows, characteristic of 24.2221, often absent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpatho-Alpine small-reed river gravel communities
description: [Calamagrostis pseudophragmites]-dominated communities of rivers originating  in the Alpine and Carpathian arcs complex. Characteristic plants include [Epilobium dodonaei], [Agrostis gigantea], [Phalaris arundinacea], [Tussilago farfara]. Like those of unit 24.2221, these communities are gravely threatened by widespread watercourse alterations affecting natural flow regimes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Cantabric small-reed river gravel communities
description: Assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants colonizing gravel beds of streams with an alpine, summer-high, flow regime in the montane zone of the Pyrenees and the Cantabrian chain, with [Calamagrostis pseudophragmites] and [Erucastrum nasturtiifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Figwort river gravel communities
description: Thermophile pioneer communities of river gravels, mostly characteristic of the upper Rhine, with [Scrophularia canina], [Epilobium dodonaei], [Hieracium piloselloides], [Silene prostrata], [Inula conyza], [Centaurea stoebe] ssp. [stoebe], [Arenaria serpyllifolia], [Echium vulgare], [Salix elaeagnos] seedlings.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caucasian river gravel communities
description: Open or closed assemblies of herbaceous or suffrutescent pioneering plants, colonizing, within the montane or submontane levels, gravel beds of streams with an alpine, summer-high, flow regime, born in the high Ponto-Caucasian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane river gravel low brush
description: Communities of low shrubby pioneers invading the herbaceous formations of units 24.221 and 24.222 on gravel deposits rich in fine silt of mountain and northern boreal Palaearctic streams with an alpine, summer-high, flow regime. [Myricaria germanica] and [Salix spp.] are characteristic. Precise communities can be indicated by use of codes from unit 44, in particular unit 44.11.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gravel bank thickets and woods
description: Thickets or woods of, among others, [Salix spp.], [Hippophae rhamnoides], [Alnus spp.], [Betula spp.], on stream gravels of mountain and northern boreal Palaearctic streams with an alpine, summer-high, flow regime. Precise communities can be indicated by use of codes from unit 44, in particular unit 44.11.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean river gravel communities
description: Communities colonizing gravel deposits of Palaearctic rivers with a Mediterranean, summer-low, flow regime, with, in particular, [Myricaria germanica], [Erucastrum nasturtiifolium], [Glaucium flavum], [Oenothera biennis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern lowland river gravel communities
description: Communities, less specialized than those of high mountain, boreo-arctic and Mediterranean watercourses, colonizing river gravels of lowland and hill rivers of the Palaearctic nemoral, boreonemoral and adjacent zones. Precise formations can be indicated by use of codes from unit 3, in particular unit 37.1, and from unit 44.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River sands
description: Sand deposits of Palaearctic streams, with the communities that occupy them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River sand deposits
description: Sand deposits of Palaearctic streams, occupying the edges of the stream, forming islands in the channel or supporting the arms and rivulets constituting the stream, together with their associated animal communities. The presence of vascular vegetation is indicated by use of unit 24.32. Water-fringing communities, in particular of units 53, 37.7, 37.8, 37.9, may contribute to the colonisation of the deposits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River sand banks
description: Sand deposits of Palaearctic streams formed along the sides of the stream or constituting islands in its channel.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River sand fans and sandar
description: Large sand deposits constituting outwash fans, alluvial fans, sandar (sandur), deposited and criss-crossed by braided rivers of the Palaearctic region, characteristic, in particular, of boreal and arctic lands with intense fluvio-glacial deposition.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River sand communities
description: Sparsely-vegetated to wooded sand banks of large Palaearctic rivers. Appropriate codes from units 22.3, 31 and 44 can be used to specify habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euhydrophytic river vegetation
description: Beds of water crowfoots, pondweeds, water starworts and other euhydrophytes, including mosses and macroscopic algae, of Palaearctic streams, comprising in particular [Butomus umbellatus] f. [valisneriifolius], [Callitriche cophocarpa], [Callitriche hamulata], [Callitriche obtusangula], [Callitriche stagnalis], [Groenlandia densa], [Potamogeton coloratus], [Potamogeton helveticus], [Potamogeton natans] var. [prolixus], [Potamogeton nodosus], [Ranunculus fluitans], [Ranunculus penicillatus], [Ranunculus trichophyllus], [Sagittaria sagittifolia] var. [vallisneriifolia], [Schoenoplectus lacustris] var. [fluitans], [Sparganium emersum] ssp. [fluitans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acid oligotrophic river vegetation
description: Euhydrophyte communities of Palaearctic streams poor in nutrients and in lime, with, in particular, [Myriophyllum alternifolium], [Potamogeton polygonifolius], [Callitriche hamulata], [Littorella uniflora], [Juncus bulbosus], [Scirpus fluitans] or acidophilous mosses and algae. In Iceland, [Montia fontana], [Potamogeton filiformis], [Ranunculus trichophyllus] ([Ranunculus confervoides], [Ranunculus aquatilis] var [diffusus]) and [Fontinalis antipyretica] characterize the community in clear, slowly flowing waters.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lime-rich oligotrophic river vegetation
description: Euhydrophyte communities of Palaearctic streams poor in nutrients but rich in lime, characterized in particular by [Potamogeton coloratus] and [Chara hispida] or by tufa-forming mosses and algae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calciphile oligotrophic river vegetation
description: Euhydrophyte communities of Palaearctic streams poor in nutrients but rich in lime, in which tufa formation is absent or very limited, with [Potamogeton coloratus] and [Chara hispida].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tufa stream vegetation
description: Euhydrophyte moss and algae communities of Palaearctic streams poor in nutrients but rich in lime, forming infra-aquatic tufa deposits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tufa cascade vegetation
description: Euhydrophyte moss and algae communities of Palaearctic streams poor in nutrients but rich in lime, forming large, structuring, tufa deposits, with a complex arrangement of subcommunities, characteristic, in particular, of the karst region of the eastern Adriatic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesotrophic river vegetation
description: Euhydrophyte communities of Palaearctic streams moderately rich in nutrients, characterized in particular by [Berula erecta] ([Sium erectum]), [Mentha aquatica] f. [submersa], [Potamogeton perfoliatus], [Potamogeton natans], [Groenlandia densa], [Ranunculus peltatus], [Ranunculus penicillatus], [Ranunculus trichophyllus], [Ranunculus fluitans], [Ranunculus aquatilis], [Callitriche truncata], [Callitriche stagnalis], [Nymphaea alba], [Myriophyllum spicatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eutrophic river vegetation
description: Euhydrophyte communities of Palaearctic streams rich in nutrients, characterized in particular by [Ranunculus fluitans], [Ranunculus circinatus], [Zannichellia palustris] f. [fluviatilis], [Potamogeton nodosus], [Potamogeton lucens], [Potamogeton pectinatus], [Potamogeton crispus], [Sparganium emersum], [Sagittaria sagittifolia], [Callitriche obtusangula], [Nuphar lutea] and the moss [Fontinalis antipyretica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River muds and silts
description: Silt and mud deposits of Palaearctic streams, with the communities that occupy them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: River silt deposits
description: Silt deposits of Palaearctic streams occupying the edges of the stream, forming islands in the channel or supporting the arms and rivulets constituting the stream, together with their associated animal communities. The presence of vascular vegetation is indicated by use of the appropriate codes from units 24.52, 24.53 or 24.54. Water-fringing communities, in particular of units 53, 37.7, 37.8, 37.9, may contribute to the colonisation of the deposits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian annual river mud communities
description: Pioneer formations of tall annuals colonizing nitrogen-rich muds of lowland rivers of the boreal and nemoral zones of the Palaearctic, and locally of the Eurasian steppe zone, with [Bidens spp.], [Rorippa spp.], [Chenopodium spp.], [Polygonum spp.], [Xanthium spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean river mud communities
description: Nitrophilous annual and perennial grass and sedge formations of the alluvial banks of Mediterranean permanent or temporary water courses, most characteristic of great Mediterranean rivers, with [Paspalum paspalodes], [Paspalum vaginatum], [Polypogon viridis] ([Agrostis semiverticillata]), [Cyperus fuscus], [Catabrosa aquatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Arctic river mud communities
description: Communities colonizing fine material deposits of low arctic and northern boreal rivers and springs of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arcto-Atlantic river mud communities
description: Communities colonizing fine material deposits of arctic and northern boreal rivers of Iceland, the Faeroe Islands and Greenland with [Koenigia islandica] and [Sedum villosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic boreo-Arctic river mud communities
description: Communities colonizing fine material deposits of Icelandic and Faroese rivers and springs with [Koenigia islandica], [Sedum villosum], [Spergula arvensis], [Polygonum viviparum], [Epilobium palustre], [Euphrasia frigida], [Juncus biglumis], [Juncus triglumis], [Triglochin palustre], [Limosella aquatica], [Deschampsia alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland river mud communities
description: Communities colonizing fine material deposits of arctic rivers, springs and seeps of Greenland with [Koenigia islandica], [Juncus triglumis], [Sagina intermedia], [Ranunculus glacialis], [Saxifraga hirculus], [Saxifraga aizoides], [Eriophorum scheuchzeri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian boreo-Arctic river mud communities
description: Communities colonizing fine material deposits of low arctic and northern boreal rivers of continental Europe and Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Riverbed rocks, pavements and blocks
description: Hard rock features permanently emerging from, or temporarily uncovered by, Palaearctic water courses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scrub and grassland
description: Shrub-, grass- or forb-dominated communities constituting either zonal climax communities under nondesert climates unsuitable for forest, or zoogenic or anthropogenic, regressive or progressive, transitional stages in forest successions on well-drained, seasonally inundatable or poorly drained but nonmarshy soils. Included are deciduous, ericaceous, sclerophyllous or lauriphyllous shrub communities of boreal, temperate, mediterranean, tropical and high mountain climates, steppes, alpine and other orogenous grasslands, secondary dry, mesophile or humid grasslands and forblands of boreal, temperate, mediterranean and tropical climates, shrub and grass communities of permafrost.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate heath and scrub
description: Shrub communities of nemoral affinities. They include winter-deciduous scrubs or brushes of the subarctic, subantarctic, nemoral, steppe, warm-temperate humid and mediterranean zones, ericoid or coniferous scrubs of the subarctic, subantarctic, nemoral, steppe and warm-temperate humid zones and scrubs, heaths, cushion-heaths or brushes of the cold, extrasylvatic or supradesertic altitude belts of subarctic, subantarctic, nemoral, mediterranean and subtropical high mountains. In the Palaearctic realm, Atlantic heaths, high montane and boreomontane heaths and conifer scrubs, subalpine bush communities, oro-Mediterranean and Irano-Turanian tragacanthic communities, deciduous forest and temperate conifer forest recolonisation communities belong to this unit.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: European wet heaths
description: Wet or humid ericoid-shrub dominated heaths of the Atlantic and sub-Atlantic domaines of the western Palaearctic region, developed on peaty or semipeaty soils, waterlogged for at least part of the year, sometimes temporarily inundated, and usually moist even in summer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern wet heaths
description: Wet heaths of the northern Atlantic and sub-Atlantic domaine and of boreal enclaves in the southern Atlantic and sub-Atlantic domaine. They mostly comprise wet and humid heaths of anmoors, gleypodzols and thin peats of the British Isles, the Germano-Baltic plains and neighbouring Hercynian hills, northern and northwestern France, southern Scandinavia, dominated by [Erica tetralix] or [Calluna vulgaris], sometimes in association with [Scirpus cespitosus] or [Molinia caerulea], usually accompanied by nonpeatbuilding sphagna, in particular, [Sphagnum compactum], [Sphagnum molle], [Sphagnum tenellum]. They also include peaty heaths of more southern regions, in western France, the periphery of the Paris Basin and northwestern Iberia, mostly developed in the central, most humid, part of depressions, often in contact with somewhat less humid formations of unit 31.12.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Germano-Baltic [Erica tetralix] wet heaths
description: Wet heaths and humid heaths of the British Isles, the Germano-Baltic plains and northern France, with principal areas of occurrence in the drier, eastern, lowlands of Britain and in the North Sea plain between northern Belgium and Schleswig-Holstein, extending to southwestern Belgium and northwestern France, to the confines of Normandy, to the montane level of the western Hercynian hills, in particular, the Ardennes, and, in the northeast, to the Prignitz, the Lausitz and western Poland, always rich in, and generally dominated by, [Erica tetralix], sometimes by [Calluna vulgaris], often in association with [Molinia caerulea], accompanied by nonpeat-building sphagna, in particular, [Sphagnum compactum], [Sphagnum molle], [Sphagnum tenellum], and by [Zygogonium ericetorum]; the cortŠge may include [Gentiana pneumonanthe], [Juncus squarrosus], [Narthecium ossifragum], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Scirpus cespitosus] ssp. [germanicus], [Carex panicea], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Dicranum scoparium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Erica tetralix]-[Empetrum] dune slack swamp-heaths
description: Wet heaths or swamp-heaths of wet depressions of the acidified coastal dunes of the Wadden Sea islands of the Netherlands, Lower Saxony and Schleswig-Holstein, and of the southern Baltic coasts, east to eastern Germany, dominated by [Erica tetralix], accompanied by [Empetrum nigrum], [Salix repens], [Calluna vulgaris], [Carex trinervis], [Juncus balticus] ([Juncus arcticus] ssp. [balticus]), [Juncus anceps] ([Juncus alpinoarticulatus] ssp. [atricapillus]), [Calamagrostis epigeios], [Vaccinium macrocarpum] ([Oxycoccus macrocarpus]), [Drosera rotundifolia], [Sphagnum compactum], [Sphagnum molle].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Erica tetralix]-[Scirpus cespitosus] wet heaths
description: Wet heaths of Ireland, western and northern Britain, western Norway, southern Norway and Sweden, western, northern and northeastern Jutland, mostly developed on shallow peats, sometimes on peaty mineral soils, under highly oceanic climates, dominated by [Erica tetralix] and/or [Calluna vulgaris], in association with [Scirpus cespitosus] or [Molinia caerulea], accompanied by, in particular, [Potentilla erecta], [Polygala serpyllifollia], [Narthecium ossifragum], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Carex panicea], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Myrica gale], [Cornus svecica], [Sphagnum palustre], [Sphagnum capillifolium], [Sphagnum subnitens], [Dicranum scoparium], [Hypnum jutlandicum], [Leucobryum glaucum], [Cladonia spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian [Calluna]-[Scirpus cespitosus] wet heaths
description: Wet and humid heaths of anmoors of middle European Hercynian hills and their periphery, in particular, of the Black Forest and the Vosges, at the continental limit of the range of the Western European wet heaths, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris] in association with [Scirpus cespitosus] ssp. [germanicus] accompanied by [Juncus squarrosus], [Sphagnum compactum], [Sphagnum tenellum], [Leucobryum glaucum], [Scirpus cespitosus] ssp. [cespitosus], [Molinia caerulea]. Facies may be dominated by [Scirpus cespitosus] with little or no [Calluna vulgaris] and constitute oligotrophic humid grasslands included in unit 37.32.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lizard [Erica vagans]-[Schoenus nigricans] heath
description: Tall heaths of moist, shallow depressions of the Lizard in Cornwall, dominated by [Erica vagans] and [Schoenus nigricans] with [Erica tetralix], [Molinia caerulea], [Serratula tinctoria] and often [Ulex gallii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallo-Iberian peaty heaths
description: Peaty heaths of western France, the periphery of the Paris Basin and northwestern Iberia, mostly developed in the central, most humid, part of depressions, often in contact with somewhat less humid formations of unit 31.12.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern wet heaths
description: Humid and meso-hygrophile heaths of gley-podzols and semipeaty soils of the northwestern Iberian peninsula, Atlantic France, the Paris Basin and its periphery, extreme southern England, dominated by [Erica tetralix] or [Erica ciliaris], with [Erica scoparia], [Erica ciliaris], [Calluna vulgaris], [Ulex minor], [Ulex gallii] or [Genista anglica]. They may, in particular, form transition belts between peaty heaths of unit 31.11 and dry heaths of unit 31.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian wet heaths
description: Wet heaths and humid heaths of the northwestern Iberian peninsula, in the Atlantic and Carpetano-Iberico-Leonese provinces and, very locally, in the Luso-Extremadurian province, particularly characteristic of the beech and deciduous oak levels of the Cantabrian chain and Galicia, dominated by [Erica tetralix], [Erica ciliaris] or [Erica mackaiana] with [Genista anglica], [Genista micrantha], [Ulex gallii], [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica cinerea], [Daboecia cantabrica], [Juncus squarrosus], [Cirsium filipendulum], and sometimes [Euphorbia polygafolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aquitano-Ligerian wet heaths
description: Humid and meso-hygrophile heaths of gley-podzols with hydromor of Aquitanian and Ligerian France north to Brenne and the Le Mans region, dominated by [Erica tetralix], [Erica scoparia] or [Erica ciliaris], with [Molinia caerulea], [Scorzonera humilis], [Carum verticillatum], [Ulex minor], [Genista anglica], [Pseudarrhenatherum longifolium] ([Arrhenatherum thorei]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britanno-Gallic dwarf gorse wet heaths
description: Humid and meso-hygrophile heaths of semipeaty gley podzols of eastern Britanny, Normandy, the southern Paris Basin, the Morvan, extending very locally to England in southern Dorset, dominated by [Erica tetralix] or [Erica ciliaris], generally with [Ulex minor], accompanied by [Calluna vulgaris], [Genista anglica], [Salix repens], [Ulex europaeus], [Molinia caerulea], [Scirpus cespitosus], [Danthonia decumbens], [Carex panicea], [Polygala serpyllifolia], [Potentilla erecta], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Lobelia urens], [Carum verticillatum], [Scorzonera humilis], [Pedicularis sylvatica], [Ajuga occidentalis], [Sphagnum compactum], [Cladonia spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anglo-Armorican western gorse wet heaths
description: Humid and meso-hygrophile heaths of semipeaty gley podzols of hyper-Atlantic lower Brittany, Cornwall and Devon, dominated by [Erica tetralix] or [Erica ciliaris], generally with [Ulex gallii], accompanied by [Genista anglica], [Salix repens], [Molinia caerulea], [Scirpus cespitosus], [Juncus squarrosus], [Potentilla erecta], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Pinguicula lusitanica], [Viola palustris], [Narthecium ossifragum], [Lobelia urens], [Wahlenbergia hederacea], [Anagallis tenella], [Hydrocotyle vulgaris], [Cirsium dissectum] ([Cirsium anglicum]), [Carum verticillatum], [Dactylorhiza ericetorum] ([Dactylorhiza maculata] ssp. [ericetorum]), [Sphagnum spp.] and sometimes [Myrica gale].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Purple moorgrass wet heaths
description: Degraded facies of wet heaths, humid heaths and swamp-heaths of the Atlantic and sub-Atlantic domaines of the western Palaearctic region, dominated by [Molinia caerulea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: European dry heaths
description: Xerophile or meso-xerophile heaths on siliceous, podsolic soils in moist Atlantic and sub-Atlantic climates of the plains and low mountains of Western and Central Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-montane [Vaccinium]-[Calluna] heaths
description: Submontane, or sometimes lowland or coastal, heaths rich in [Vaccinium spp.], usually with [Calluna vulgaris], of the northern and western British Isles, of the North Atlantic islands, of Fennoscandia, of the Hercynian ranges and the lower levels of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Pyrenees and the Cordillera Cantabrica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North Atlantic [Vaccinium]-[Empetrum]-[Rhacomitrium] heaths
description: Low altitude heaths of boreomontane affinities developed under euoceanic climates along the coasts of low Arctic and northern temperate North Atlantic islands and of boreal and arctic Scandinavia, generally characterized by the prominence of [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum] or [Vaccinium vitis-idaea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Isles ling-crowberry heaths
description: Low altitude heaths of boreomontane affinities of the Faeroe, Shetland and Orkney islands, mostly characteristic of exposed headlands under euoceanic conditions, with [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum]. They are floristically closely related to montane heaths of unit 31.45, in particular, the Scottish Highland heaths of units 31.451 and 31.452.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic crowberry-northern bilberry heaths
description: Low altitude prostrate, open, moss-rich heaths of boreomontane affinities of the coasts and islands of oceanic southern boreal, oceanic middle boreal and arcto-alpine Norway, dominated by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum] and [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], accompanied by [Calluna vulgaris], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Cladonia spp.], [Sphagnum spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic crowberry-northern bilberry heaths
description: Moss-rich, closed [Vaccinium uliginosum]-[Vaccinium myrtillus]-[Empetrum hermaphroditum] heaths of Iceland, of boreomontane affinities, developed under humid euoceanic climate conditions at mostly low altitudes, typically from sealevel to 460 m. The three erico‹d shrubs dominate in any combination and may be accompanied by [Calluna vulgaris] or [Loiseleuria procumbens]. Common nonerico‹d vascular plants include [Alchemilla alpina], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Salix herbacea], [Viola palustris], [Galium boreale], [Galium normanii], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Carex bigelowii], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Avenella flexuosa]. Orchids include [Dactylorhiza islandica], [Coeloglossum viride], [Listera cordata]. The moss layer is very developed, with a cover of 20% to 70%, and a rich and diverse bryophyte and lichen cortŠge in which [Rhacomitrium canescens], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Rhytidiadelphus squarrosus], [Rhytidiadelphus loreus], [Hylocomium splendens], [Dicranum scoparium], [Polytrichum alpinum] may be particularly prominent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subboreal [Vaccinium] heaths
description: [Vaccinium]-dominated, [Vaccinium]-rich and [Empetrum]-rich heaths of boreomontane affinities characteristic of northern and western uplands of Britain and of western and southern Scandinavia, with extensions in the Germano-Baltic plain, particularly in Jutland, Poland, southern Finland and the Baltic States. [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Empetrum nigrum], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Pleurozium schreberi] and [Hylocomium splendens] are strongly represented among the associates of [Calluna vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subboreal [Vaccinium]-[Deschampsia] heaths
description: Usually low, relatively open submontane or subboreal heaths of the uplands of northern and western Britain, of southern Fennoscandia and Denmark, usually dominated by [Vaccinium myrtillus], in association with [Empetrum nigrum], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Calluna vulgaris], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] or [Vaccinium uliginosum] and with a moss-rich or grass-rich cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Vaccinium]-[Deschampsia] heaths
description: Usually low, relatively open submontane heaths of the uplands of northern and western Britain, particularly widespread in the central and eastern Highlands, usually dominated by [Vaccinium myrtillus], often in association with [Empetrum nigrum] or [Empetrum hermaphroditum], variously accompanied by [Calluna vulgaris], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Vaccinium uliginosum] and with a generally moss-rich or grass-rich cortŠge that includes, in particular, [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Festuca ovina], [Agrostis capillaris], [Nardus stricta], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Danthonia decumbens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic moss-rich crowberry-bilberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium myrtillus] heaths of the Highlands, with outposts in the Southern Uplands, the Lake District, and northern Wales, with abundant [Empetrum hermaphroditum] and bryophytes, mostly associated with large shallow snow beds at relatively high altitudes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Alchemilla] bilberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium myrtillus] heaths of the western and central Highlands, with outliers in the Southern Uplands and Wales, with [Alchemilla alpina] and abundant grasses, characteristic of lower altitudes, sunnier stations and lesser snow cover than those of unit 31.21211.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic lichen-rich crowberry-bilberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium myrtillus]-[Empetrum spp.] heaths of the southern Highlands, the Southern Uplands, the Lake District, the Bowland Fells, the Pennines, Wales and Dartmoor, with [Cladonia] lichens, [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Galium saxatile], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Festuca ovina], [Carex bigelowii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nordic [Vaccinium]-[Deschampsia] heaths
description: Usually low, relatively open, subboreal heaths of southern Fennoscandia and Denmark, usually dominated by [Vaccinium myrtillus] and [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], in association with [Calluna vulgaris] and mosses or with [Deschampsia flexuosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Scandian bilberry-ling heaths
description: Open [Vaccinium myrtillus]-[Vaccinium vitis-ideae]-[Calluna vulgaris] heaths characteristic of southern Scandinavia, distributed in Denmark, along the coast of Norway, north to central Norway, and in southwestern Sweden, developed under somewhat humid, mild-winter climates, with a field layer species cortŠge comprising [Galium saxatile], [Maianthemum bifolium], [Potentilla erecta], [Trientalis europaea], [Danthonia decumbens], [Deschampsia flexuosa], and a ground layer dominated by [Pleurozium schreberi] accompanied by [Dicranum polysetum], [Hypnum cupressiforme], [Hylocomium splendens], [Rhytidiadelphus triquetum] and lichens of genus [Cladonia]; [Juniperus communis] may be present; [Blechnum spicant] and [Rhytidiadelphus loreus] may be the important constituents of communities of oceanic Norway.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian bilberry-cowberry heaths
description: Grass-rich [Vaccinium myrtillus]-[Vaccinium vitis-ideae] heaths of central Sweden and southwestern Finland, with a species cortŠge comprising [Deschampsia flexuosa], which may codominate with the ericoid shrubs, [Calamagrostis arundinacea], [Luzula pilosa], [Lathyrus linifolius], [Melampyrum spp.], [Viola riviniana], occupying dry, lightly grazed patches within birch-oak pastures often on boulder-strewn moraine land.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subboreal [Calluna]-[Vaccinium] heaths
description: Subboreal and upland [Calluna vulgaris]-dominated heaths of northern and western Britain, southern Scandinavia and Denmark, more or less rich in [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] or [Empetrum nigrum] and sometimes with [Erica cinerea], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], grasses or lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Calluna]-[Vaccinium] heaths
description: Subboreal, upland, [Calluna vulgaris]-dominated heaths of northern and western Britain, more or less rich in [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Erica cinerea] or [Empetrum nigrum], accompanied by grasses or by pleurocarps and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic ling-bilberry-crowberry heaths
description: Submontane and collinar heaths of the Highlands, the Southern Uplands, Orkney, Shetland, the Lake District, the Pennines, the North York Moors, Wales, the South-West Peninsula dominated by [Calluna vulgaris] associated with [Vaccinium myrtillus], which may sometimes be codominant, accompanied by [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Empetrum nigrum] and, sometimes, [Erica cinerea], and often by pleurocarps and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic grassy ling-bilberry heaths
description: Grassy submontane and collinar heaths of the eastern Highlands, the Southern Uplands, Orkney, the Lake District, Wales, the South-West Peninsula dominated by [Calluna vulgaris] associated with [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Festuca ovina], [Festuca rubra], [Nardus stricta], [Anthoxanthum odoratum] and with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Empetrum nigrum], [Erica cinerea]. Grassy [Calluna]-[Vaccinium] heaths, in particular, those rich in [Nardus stricta] and associated grasses, or in [Juncus squarrosus], include communities transitional to grasslands of units 35 and 37.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dano-Scandian [Calluna]-[Vaccinium] heaths
description: Subboreal [Calluna vulgaris]-dominated heaths of southern Scandinavia and Denmark, rich in [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] or [Empetrum nigrum], in mosses and lichens, and sometimes grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dano-Scandian ling-crowberry-cowberry heaths
description: Very open heaths of Denmark, southern Sweden, southern Norway and, very locally, southwestern Finland, developed on podzols in humid, mild-winter climates, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], [Empetrum nigrum] and [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], with a rich moss and lichen cortŠge usually dominated by [Pleurozium schreberi], sometimes with a prominent occurrence of [Molinia caerulea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dano-Scandian subboreal ling heaths
description: Open heaths of western and northern Jutland, northern Zealand, Scania, the coasts and near-coastal hills of southern Sweden and southern Norway, of oceanic Norway north to the oceanic middle boreal zone, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris] accompanied by [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] and/or [Vaccinium myrtillus], and with [Pleurozium schreberi] usually dominant in the moss layer; [Blechnum spicant] may be the main accompanier of [Calluna vulgaris] in some communities of the oceanic southern boreal zone of Norway.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Faeroes [Calluna]-[Vaccinium] heaths
description: Subboreal heaths of the Faeroe Islands, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris],  [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] and [Empetrum nigrum] or [Vaccinium myrtillus], accompanied by [Pleurozium schreberi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Calluna]-[Vaccinium]-[Sphagnum] heaths
description: Tall [Calluna vulgaris]-[Vaccinium myrtillus] heaths with a ground layer dominated by bryophytes, in particular, leafy liverworts, hypnaceous mosses and sphagna, mostly [Sphagnum capillifolium], sometimes [Sphagnum quinquefarium], [Sphagnum russowii], [Sphagnum girgensohnii], [Sphagnum tenellum], characteristic of the northwest Highlands, with outliers in the southwestern Southern Uplands, in the Lake District and in Orkney.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subboreal [Calluna]-[Arctostaphylos] heaths
description: Heaths of the east-central Highlands of Scotland, Jutland, western Norway, the coastlands of the Skagerrak and Kattegat, the southeastern and central Baltic regions dominated by [Calluna vulgaris] and [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], often with [Erica cinerea], [Genista anglica], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] or [Vaccinium myrtillus], accompanied by a distinctly boreal species cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Calluna]-[Arctostaphylos] heaths
description: Moderately tall heaths of base-poor to near-neutral soils and moderate altitudes of the east-central Highlands, usually dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], usually accompanied by prominent [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi] and [Erica cinerea], often with [Genista anglica], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Vaccinium myrtillus] and a rather boreal species cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Germano-Baltic [Calluna]-[Arctostaphylos] heaths
description: Heaths of Jutland, of oceanic southern boreal Norway, of the Swedish and Norwegian coasts of the Skagerrak and Kattegat, of the Baltic coastlands of boreonemoral Sweden and Finland, of the Baltic plains of northeastern Germany, northern and central Poland and of the Baltic States, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi] and [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], with [Carex ericetorum], [Peucedanum oreoselinum], [Trientalis europaea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian [Vaccinium] heaths
description: Montane or submontane [Calluna]-[Vaccinium] heaths of the Hercynian ranges of northern and middle Western and Central Europe and of their surrounding regions. They mostly include secondary heaths of the beech level of the Vosges, of the Black Forest, of the Ardennes and the Eifel, of the mid-German Hercynian ranges, of the Bohemian Quadrangle, including the Erzgebirge (Metallic Mountains), the Sudeten, the Bohemian Forest (Sumava) and the Czecko-Moravian Hills, of the Massif Central and, locally, the Morvan, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Vaccinium uliginosum] and montane lycopodes ([Diphasiastrum spp.]). They also comprise partly primary and sometimes threatened local formations of extrasylvatic areas, in particular the [Calluna vulgaris] heaths enclaved in alpine and subalpine [Pinus mugo] scrub and acidophilous grassland complexes of the high slopes and plateaux of the Giant Mountains (Sudeten), or the [Calluna vulgaris], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] heaths of the Brocken summit in the Harz with [Anemone micrantha] and [Hieracium alpinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Submontane Alpine [Vaccinium] heaths
