description: [Vaccinium spp.] heaths of the collinar and montane levels of the Alps with, [Calluna vulgaris], [Artemisia alba], [Silene otites], [Campanula spicata] and other thermophile species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Submontane Pyreneo-Cantabrian [Vaccinium] heaths
description: [Vaccinium]-rich heaths of the collinar and montane levels of the Pyrenees and the Cordillera Cantabrica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Collinar-montane Carpathian [Vaccinium] heaths
description: [Vaccinium myrtillus]-[Vaccinium vitis-ideae] and [Vaccinium]-rich [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of the collinar and montane levels of the Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Submontane western Carpathian bilberry-cowberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium myrtillus]-[Vaccinium vitis-ideae] heaths of the collinar and montane levels of the western and northern Carpathians of Moravia, Slovakia, Poland, with [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Melampyrum pratense], [Melampyrum sylvaticum], [Calamagrostis arundinacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane eastern Carpathian bilberry-ling heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of the beech and spruce levels of the eastern Carpathians, most widespread in the Apuseni mountains, rich in [Vaccinium myrtillus] and [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], with [Lycopodium clavatum], [Genista sagittalis], [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia], [Campanula abietina], [Campanula serrata], [Scorzonera rosea], [Viola declinata], [Nardus stricta], [Potentilla erecta], [Hieracium pilosella], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Agrostis capillaris], [Festuca rubra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths
description: Low [Calluna vulgaris] heaths often rich in [Genista spp.], mostly of the Germano-Baltic lowlands. Similar formations occurring in British upland areas, montane zones of high mountains of the western Mediterranean basin and high rainfall Adriatic influenced areas are most conveniently listed here.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths
description: Heaths of the northern Germano-Baltic plain and neighbouring regions, in Denmark, southern Sweden, Germany, northern Poland and the Netherlands north of the Rhine, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], with [Genista pilosa] and, in the west, [Genista anglica], and with a species cortŠge that reflects boreal influences, marked, in particular, by the frequent presence of [Empetrum nigrum] or [Vaccinium spp.] These formations have their main area of occurrence in northwestern Germany, Jutland and the Netherlands in Friesland, the Drente, and the Hoge Veluwe, extending northward to northern Jutland and coastal Halland, eastward to the Prignitz and to Poland. Outliers occupy restricted surfaces in the Hercynian upper Rhine hills, the Rhine Valley and middle Franconia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subcontinental [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths
description: Relatively thermophile, subcontinental [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of Central Europe, in central and southern Germany, eastern France, the Czech Republic, Austria, with [Genista germanica], [Genista tinctoria], [Chamaespartium sagittale] ([Genista sagittalis]), [Vaccinium myrtillus] and, in peri-Alpine habitats, [Lembotropis nigricans] ([Cytisus nigricans]), [Chamaecytisus supinus] ([Cytisus supinus]), [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae]. They have their main area of distribution in the Thuringian and Franconian ranges, the Upper Palatinate hills, the Danube-Isar hills, the Swabian Alb, the Baar plateau, the eastern Black Forest, the Rhenano-Burgondian hills, the foothills of the Bayerischer Wald, the hills and low mountains of the Bohemian uplands, in the Bavarian and Austrian Danube basin, in the southeastern foothills of the Alps, in Carinthia and Styria; they irradiate northward, in thermophilous enclaves, in the Elbe basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Campino-Flandrian [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths
description: Heaths of the southwestern Germano-Baltic plain, in the Netherlands, south of the Rhine, Belgium and northwestern France, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], with [Genista anglica], [Genista pilosa] and a species cortŠge that reflects Atlantic influences, marked, in particular, by the frequent presence of [Erica cinerea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Campino-Flandrian [Erica cinerea] heaths
description: [Erica cinerea]-dominated heaths of the southern Netherlands and Belgium, facies of the [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths of unit 31.223. They represent a transtition to the northern Atlantic heaths of unit 31.25.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths
description: Species-poor [Calluna vulgaris] lowland and hill heaths of England, limited to base-poor substrates in areas of local relative contintality.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Anglian [Calluna]-[Festuca] heaths
description: Lowland, species-poor [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of East Anglia and adjacent areas, now very local, characteristic mostly of the Breckland and East Anglian coast, extending to Lincolnshire, and southwards into the Home Counties, limited to base-poor, sandy soils under relatively continental climates, with [Festuca ovina] and the mosses [Hypnum cupressiforme], [Dicranum scoparium];  [Cladonia] lichens are abundant in some communities, [Carex arenaria] in others.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: English [Calluna]-[Deschampsia] heaths
description: Species-poor [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of the Pennine foothills, around polluted industrial areas, of the North Yorkshire Moors and of the West Midlands, developed on acid, impoverished soils, under less oceanic climates than those to which heaths of unit 31.23 are exposed, with [Deschampsia flexuosa] and [Pohlia nutans]; some of the communities are somewhat richer in bryophytes or lichens, others in grasses, constituting transitions towards acidophilous grasslands of 35.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths
description: Thermophile [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of the montane zone (beech forest level) of the Central Massif, the Pyrenees and the southwestern Alps, with [Genista anglica], [Genista pilosa], [Vaccinium myrtillus] and, often, [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern subboreal [Calluna]-[Empetrum] heaths
description: Subboreal heaths of the Netherlands and northern Germany, occupying enclaves within the range of heaths of unit 31.22, rich in [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], or in [Empetrum nigrum], characteristic, in particular, of the Hoge Veluwe, Drente and Friesland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern subboreal ling-bilberry heaths
description: Subboreal heaths of the Netherlands and northwestern Germany rich in [Vaccinium myrtillus] and [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], characteristic of cool enclaves, in particular, of north-facing hill and inland dune slopes, extending southwest to the Hoge Veluwe in the central Netherlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern subboreal ling-crowberry heaths
description: Subboreal heaths of the Netherlands and northern Germany rich in [Empetrum nigrum], characteristic, in particular, of shady slopes, shrubby heaths, woodland edges and inland dunes, southwest to southern Friesland and Drente in the Netherlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian heaths
description: Heaths of the southern periphery of the Pannonic basin and the lower montane level of the Dinarides, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica herbacea], [Genista germanica] ssp. [heteracantha], [Genista pilosa], [Juniperus communis], [Prunella laciniata], [Hieracium murorum] ([Hieracium silvaticum]), [Serratula tinctoria], [Nardus stricta], [Carex pilulifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Po basin heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of the fluvioglacial terraces that constitute the high plains of the Po river system, with [Genista pilosa], [Genista tinctoria], [Cytisus scoparius], [Polygala chamaebuxus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Genista sagittalis] heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris]-[Chamaespartium sagittale] ([Genista sagittalis]) heaths of the southwestern Alps, the Vosges, the Black Forest, the Jura, the Bavarian plateau and the southeastern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western [Genista sagittalis] heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris]-[Chamaespartium sagittale] ([Genista sagittalis]) heaths of the southwestern Alps, the Vosges, the Black Forest, the Jura and the Bavarian plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian [Genista sagittalis] heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris]-[Chamaespartium sagittale] ([Genista sagittalis]) heaths of the southeastern Carpathians, with [Bruckenthalia speculifolia], [Viola declinata], [Scorzonera rosea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European basicline heaths
description: Heaths of calcareous or somewhat calcareous substrates, and of low-precipitation continental enclaves, in particular, in Hercynian hills and on Pleistocene inland dunes, of Germany, the Czech Republic, Austria, Poland, southern Scandinavia, with southern representatives in the northern Dinarides of Croatia, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Cruciata glabra], [Peucedanum oreoselinum], [Prunella vulgaris], [Juniperus communis], [Carex caryophyllea], [Carex ericetorum], [Carex humilis], [Koeleria pyramidata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic herb-rich ling heaths
description: Relatively species-rich heaths of Scania, southeastern Sweden, ™land and Gotland, central G”taland, eastern Svealand, the central Baltic archipelagos, extreme southern Finland, northern Germany and northern Poland, with outposts in southwestern Norway, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Hieracium pilosella], [Cladonia spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian basicline ling heaths
description: Heaths of calcareous or somewhat calcareous substrates, and of low-precipitation continental enclaves, in particular, in Hercynian hills and on Pleistocene inland dunes, of Germany, the Czech Republic, Austria, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Hieracium pilosella], [Carex caryophyllea], [Carex ericetorum], [Carex humilis], [Koeleria macrantha], [Koeleria pyramidata], [Koeleria gracilis], [Cladonia alcicornis], [Cladonia rangiformis], [Cladonia foliacea], [Cladonia uncialis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric basicline ling heaths
description: Heaths of calcareous or somewhat calcareous substrates of the northern Dinarides of Croatia, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Genista germanica], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Cruciata glabra], [Juniperus communis], [Carex caryophyllea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic ling heaths
description: Heaths, often extensive, of the Stranja-Istranca mountains and of the coasts of the Sea of Marmora, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica arborea], [Erica manipuliflora], [Cistus incanus], [Cistus salvifolius], [Genista carinalis], [Teucrium polium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Erica]-[Ulex] heaths
description: Heaths rich in gorse ([Ulex spp.]) of the Atlantic margins of Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Maritime gorse heaths
description: Wind-swept heaths with prostrate, cushiony gorse or broom ([Ulex europaeus] f. [maritimus], [Ulex gallii] f. [humilis], [Cytisus scoparius] ssp. [maritimus]), [Erica vagans], [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris], and numerous other maritime ecotypes, of cliff tops of promontories and islands of Brittany, Cotentin, southern Ireland, Cornwall, Wales, the Cantabrian coast and Galicia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic [Calluna vulgaris]-[Ulex gallii] heaths
description: Oceanic heaths of Ireland, Wales, the Isle of Man, the South-West Peninsula and, locally, the Pennines and the coasts of East Anglia, dominated by [Ulex gallii], [Calluna vulgaris] and [Erica cinerea]. Basicline heaths, somewhat homologous to the continental formations of unit 31.22B, may form in zones of transition between some communities of this unit and calcareous grasslands of unit 34.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irish [Erica mackaiana] heaths
description: Western Irish heaths comprising the northern, isolated, populations of [Erica mackaiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern [Erica vagans] heaths
description: Heaths of well drained soils of the coasts and offshore islands of Ireland, Cornwall and Brittany, other than cushiony maritime formations, dominated by or rich in [Erica vagans], constituting isolated northern outposts of occurrence of the species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Armorican [Erica vagans] heaths
description: Heaths of well drained soils of the coasts and offshore islands of Brittany, other than cushiony maritime formations, dominated by or rich in the uncommon and local [Erica vagans], almost limited to the islands of Belle-Ile and Groix.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lizard [Erica vagans] heaths
description: Heaths of well drained soils of the Lizard, in Cornwall, with a mixed canopy usually formed by [Erica vagans], [Ulex europaeus], [Erica cinerea], [Ulex gallii], with [Carex flacca], [Viola riviniana], [Filipendula vulgaris], [Agrostis canina], [Stachys officinalis] ([Stachys betonica], [Betonica officinalis]), [Hypochoeris radicata], [Polygala vulgaris], [Potentilla erecta], [Dactylis glomerata], [Scilla verna].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anglo-Armorican [Erica cinerea]-[Ulex gallii] heaths
description: Heaths of well drained soils of Brittany, the Cotentin peninsula, the South-Western Peninsula and the south coast of Wales, dominated by [Ulex gallii], [Erica cinerea] and [Calluna vulgaris], often rich in grasses, in particular, [Agrostis curtisii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cantabro-Pyrenean [Erica mackaiana]-[E. cinerea] heaths
description: Heaths with [Ulex gallii], [Erica mackaiana], [Erica cinerea], [Daboecia cantabrica] of well drained soils of the beech level of the Pyrenees and the Cantabrian chain and, very locally, of Galicia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cantabro-Pyrenean [Erica vagans]-[E. cinerea] heaths
description: Heaths with [Ulex gallii], [Erica vagans], [Erica cinerea], sometimes [Erica aragonensis], and [Pseudarrhenatherum longifolium] of the French and Spanish Basque coast and of the beech level of the Atlantic Pyrenees and of the Cantabrian chain, mostly on mildly acid or sightly calcareous soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallo-Britannic dwarf gorse heaths
description: Heaths of sub-Atlantic France and of southern and southeastern England formed by [Ulex minor], [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris] and [Ulex europaeus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallic [Ulex minor]-[Erica cinerea] heaths
description: Heaths of well drained soils of interior and oriental Brittany, the Perche, Normandy, the Paris Basin, the Sologne, the southern Morvan, dominated by [Erica cinerea], [Ulex minor], [Calluna vulgaris] and [Ulex europaeus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Calluna vulgaris]-[Ulex minor] heaths
description: Heaths of southern and southeastern England, from east Dorset to Kent, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris] and [Ulex minor], accompanied by [Erica cinerea] and usually by [Deschampsia flexuosa], sometimes by [Vaccinium myrtillus] or [Molinia caerulea]; [Ulex europaeus] and [Agrostis curtisii] are uncommon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern English [Ulex minor]-[Agrostis curtisii] heath
description: Heants of Dorset and Hampshire dominated by [Ulex minor], [Erica cinerea] and [Agrostis curtisii], on relatively well drained soils; [Calluna vulgaris] is usually of low abundance, [Ulex europaeus] is usually present. They constitute an important habitat of [Viola lactea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aquitano-Ligerian dwarf gorse heaths
description: Heaths of well drained soils of Aquitaine, Saintonge, Poitou, Sologne and the Loire region formed by [Ulex minor] and [Erica cinerea], sometimes with [Erica scoparia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-Atlantic [Erica-Ulex-Cistus] heaths
description: Aquitanian heaths with rock-roses. Iberian heaths with numerous species of heathers (notably [Erica umbellata], [Erica aragonensis]) and brooms, rock-roses and often [Daboecia]. When the rock-roses and other Mediterranean shrubs become dominant they should be classified under sclerophyllous scrubs (unit 32).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Biscay heaths
description: Coastal and collinar [Erica]-[Ulex]-[Cistus] heaths of the periphery of the Bay of Biscay and of the slopes of the Garonne Gap.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aquitanian [Erica-Cistus] heaths
description: [Erica cinerea] and [Cistus salvifolius] heaths of the Aquitanian coast, with irradiations in the Landes and to the Montagne noire and Minervois.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gascony-Sologne arid heaths
description: Arid [Erica cinerea] heaths of interior sandy hills and dunes of the Landes of Gascony and of Sologne gravels, with [Halimium alyssoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Iberian heaths
description: Tall, dense heaths of the coasts, hills and lower montane areas of the Atlantic slope of Cantabria, the Asturias and Galicia, formed by [Erica vagans] and [Ulex europaeus], with [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris] and [Daboecia cantabrica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Luso-Galician heaths
description: Atlantic Galician and Portuguese [Erica cinerea], [Erica umbellata] and [Ulex europaeus] heaths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Luso-Galician collinar heaths
description: Coastal and collinar, thermo-Atlantic Galician and northern Portuguese heaths with [Erica cinerea], [Erica umbellata], [Ulex minor], [Ulex europaeus], [Ulex micranthus], [Cistus salvifolius] and [Halimium alyssoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Luso-Galician maritime heaths
description: Cushiony heaths with [Ulex europaeus] ssp. [latebracteatus] f. [humilis] and [Erica cinerea] of cliff tops of Galicia, north and central Portugal (southern vicariant of unit 31.231).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cabreran heaths
description: Low [Calluna vulgaris]-rich heaths of interior northwestern mountains, limited to the Sierra de la Cabrera and the neighbouring Sierra Segundera, Pena Trevinca and Sierra del Teleno.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cabreran dry whin heaths
description: Open, cushiony formations of [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica umbellata], [Genista sanabrensis], [Halimium umbellatum], [Halimium alyssoides] occupying dry, superficial soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cabreran mesophile whin heaths
description: Formations of [Calluna vulgaris], [Genista carpetana], [Genista anglica], [Genista micrantha] and [Thymelaea coridifolia] ([Thymelaea dendryobryum]) of wetter stations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Galicio-Leonese heaths
description: [Erica aragonensis] or [Erica umbellata] heaths of the interior slopes of the Cordillera Cantabrica, of interior Galicia and of the Leonese mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Galicio-Leonese [Erica aragonensis] heaths
description: Supra-Mediterranean [Erica aragonensis] heaths with [Chamaespartium tridentatum], [Calluna vulgaris], [Halimium alyssoides] of the interior slopes of the Cantabrian Cordillera, eastern Galician ranges, Leon mountains and the Sierra de Cabrera.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Galicio-Leonese [Erica umbellata] heaths
description: Lower altitude heaths on the confines of Galicia and Leon dominated by [Erica umbellata] accompanied by [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Chamaespartium tridentatum], [Halimium alyssoides], [Genista triacanthos], [Lavandula stoechas] ssp. [luisieri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Galicio-Leonese [Erica cinerea] heaths
description: Lower altitude heaths on the confines of Galicia and Leon, characteristic of slightly more uniform and humid climates than those of unit 31.2442, dominated by [Erica cinerea], accompanied by [Calluna vulgaris], [Chamaespartium tridentatum], [Erica umbellata], [Halimium umbellatum] and Mediterranean elements such as [Lavandula stoechas] ssp. [pedunculata], [Thymus mastichina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Castillan heaths
description: [Erica aragonensis] heaths of the Cordillera Central and the summits of the Montes de Toledo.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Cordilleran [Erica aragonensis] heaths
description: [Erica aragonensis] formations of the western Cordillera Central (Serra da Estrela, Sierra de Gata, Sierra de Pena de Francia) with [Erica umbellata], [Halimium alyssoides] and sometimes [Juniperus nana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ayllon [Erica aragonensis] heaths
description: [Erica aragonensis] formations of the Sierra de Ayllon with [Halimium viscosum], [Halimium ocymoides], [Genista pilosa] and, sometimes [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Villuercan [Erica aragonensis] heaths
description: Isolated summital [Erica aragonensis] heaths of the Montes de Toledo (Villuercas).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sorian heaths
description: [Erica aragonensis] and [Calluna vulgaris] heath communities of the northern Iberian Range, often with [Genista pilosa] or, on wetter soils, [Genista anglica] and [Genista micrantha].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sorian summital heaths
description: [Calluna] heaths of high peaks, with [Viola montcaunica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sorian [Erica aragonensis] heaths
description: Beech-zone [Erica aragonensis] heaths with [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sorian [Erica vagans] heaths
description: Formations of lower beech zone, with [Erica vagans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sorian collinar heaths
description: [Erica arborea], [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris] formations of the acidophilous oak zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cuencan heaths
description: [Erica aragonensis] heaths of the southern Iberian Range (Valdemeca, Serrania de Cuenca) with [Thymelaea subrepens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Luso-Extremaduran heaths
description: Formations rich in [Erica umbellata], or sometimes [Erica aragonensis], of the meso-Mediterranean and occasionally thermo-Mediterranean zones of the western parts of the Iberian peninsula, intermediate between heath and maquis.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Luso-Extremaduran [Erica umbellata] heaths
description: Formations rich in [Erica umbellata] of the meso-Mediterranean and occasionally thermo-Mediterranean zones of the western parts of the Iberian peninsula, intermediate between heath and maquis.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Luso-Extremaduran [Erica aragonensis] heaths
description: Formations rich in [Erica aragonensis] of the Serra de Monchique in Algarve.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Erica andevalensis] heaths
description: Formations constituted by the local endemic [Erica andevalensis] on soils rich in heavy metals of the rio Odiel basin in western Andalusia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic [Erica cinerea] heaths
description: Low, open heaths of northern hyper-Atlantic Europe, north of the range of gorses, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris] and [Erica cinerea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Scandinavian bell heather heaths
description: Low, open heaths of the oceanic southern boreonemoral zone of southern Norway and western Sweden, along the inner Skagerrak, with [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], sometimes with [Juniperus communis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Faeroe bell heather heaths
description: Low, open heaths of the Faeroe, with [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Hypericum pulchrum], sometimes with [Juniperus communis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British ling-bell heather heaths
description: Submontane heaths of Scotland, northern England, Wales and Devon, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], with varying amounts of [Erica cinerea], sometimes with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Empetrum nigrum], accompanied by [Potentilla erecta], [Carex binervis], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Festuca ovina], [Anthoxanthum odorantum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spring squill heaths
description: Maritime heaths of cliff tops of the South-West Peninsula, western Wales, Cumbria, western Scotland, the Hebredes, northern Scotland, the Orkneys, the Shetlands, northeastern Scotland and, very locally, northeastern England, very low, open, formed by [Calluna vulgaris] and, usually, [Erica cinerea] with [Festuca ovina], [Scilla verna], [Lotus corniculatus], [Thymus praecox], [Plantago maritima], [Hypochoeris radicata], [Holcus lanatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British [Calluna]-[Sieglingia] heaths
description: Species-rich basicline heaths of the Central Highlands, the Northern Pennines, the Inner Hebrides and the Orkneys dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], with [Erica cinerea], [Danthonia decumbens] ([Sieglingia decumbens]), [Festuca ovina], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Thymus praecox], [Linum catharticum], [Viola riviniana], [Carex pulicaris], [Carex panicea], [Prunella vulgaris], [Primula vulgaris], [Potentilla erecta], [Lotus corniculatus], [Agrostis canina], and sometimes with [Galium boreale], [Lathyrus montanus], [Viola lutea], [Pyrola media], [Rubus saxatilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irish bell heather-sedge heaths
description: Oceanic heaths of Ireland, with [Erica cinerea], [Calluna vulgaris] and [Carex binervis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian heaths
description: Heaths of the Canary Islands, Azores and Madeira.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian heaths
description: Low and medium-tall ericaceous formations of the cloud belt of the Canary Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian [Erica scoparia] heaths
description: Humid low heaths of high elevations of Tenerife (Anaga) and La Gomera (Incherada), with [Erica scoparia] ssp. [platycodon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian [Erica arborea] heaths
description: Low and medium-tall stages of the [Erica arborea], [Myrica faya] and [Ilex canariensis] formations (tall forest-like formations are listed as 45.9).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Madeiran cloud heaths
description: Sometimes fairly tall, 2-3 metre high, [Erica arborea], [Myrica faya], [Erica scoparia], [Laurus azorica], [Clethra arborea] and [Pteridium aquilinum] heaths of the cloud zone of Madeira.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Madeiran summital heaths
description: [Erica cinerea] var. [maderensis]-dominated heaths of the highest peaks of Madeira.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean lowland heaths
description: [Erica azorica], [Myrica faya] and [Laurus azorica] heaths of the lower altitudes of the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean "upper woods" heaths
description: Heath facies of the [Erica azorica] and [Juniperus brevifolia] "upper woods" of the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean summital heaths
description: [Calluna vulgaris], [Daboecia azorica] and [Thymus caespititius] communities of the highest altitudes of the Azores (1200-1500 m).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine and boreal heaths
description: Small, dwarf or prostrate shrub formations of the alpine and subalpine zones of the mountains of Eurasia, dominated by ericaceous species, [Dryas octopetala], dwarf junipers, brooms or greenweeds; [Dryas] heaths of the British Isles.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide dwarf ericoid wind heaths
description: Very low, single-stratum, carpets of trailing azalea, [Loiseleuria procumbens], prostrate [Vaccinium spp.] or other prostrate ericoid shrublets, accompanied by lichens, of windswept, mostly snowfree, localities in the alpine belt of the high mountains of the Alpine system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide dwarf azalea heaths
description: Dwarf alpine heaths of the western Alpides dominated by [Loiseleuria procumbens], often accompanied by [Vaccinium spp.], and rich in lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine dwarf azalea heaths
description: [Loiseleuria procumbens]-dominated dwarf heaths of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean dwarf azalea heaths
description: [Loiseleuria procumbens]-dominated dwarf heaths of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian dwarf azalea heaths
description: Local formations of the lowel alpine level on windswept localities in the eastern and southern Carpathian Mountains (Rodnei, Bucegi, Fagaras, Retezat, Tarcu), dominated by [Loiseleuria procumbens], with some regional species including [Senecio carniolicus], [Sesleria coerulans], [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda] and [Rhododendron myrtifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide dwarf [Vaccinium] wind heaths
description: Very low, single-stratum, carpets of prostrate [Vaccinium spp.] and lichens, of windswept, mostly snowfree, localities in the alpine belt of the high mountains of the Alpine system, for the most part [Vaccinium]-dominated facies of the trailing azalea communities, in which [Loiseleuria procumbens] often accompanies [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] or [Vaccinium uliginosum], the latter represented, as in 31.411, 31.44 and 31.4A, by the distinctive low, small-leaved, creeping, mat-forming entity variously referred to as [Vaccinium gaultherioides], [Vaccinium uliginosum] ssp. [microphyllum], [Vaccinium alpina], [Vaccinium pubescens], [Vaccinium uliginosum] ssp. [pubescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alps dwarf [Vaccinium] wind heaths
description: Prostrate [Vaccinium spp.] and lichen carpets of windswept localities in the alpine belt of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian dwarf [Vaccinium] wind heaths
description: Very local prostrate [Vaccinium spp.] and lichen carpets of high windswept summits and peaks, in the lower alpine belt of the Eastern and Southern Carpathians, dominated by [Vaccinium gaultherioides] ([Vaccinium uliginosum] ssp. [microphyllum]) and [Cetraria islandica] with [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Juncus trifidus], [Festuca airoides] and [Cetraria islandica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide and Balkan dwarf [Vaccinium] wind heaths
description: Communities of prostrate [Vaccinium uliginosum] and lichens of the alpine level of the mountains of the Rhodopide system and of the Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide dwarf [Vaccinium] wind heaths
description: Communities of prostrate [Vaccinium uliginosum] and lichens of the alpine level of the Rila and Pirin mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range dwarf [Vaccinium] wind heaths
description: [Vaccinium uliginosum] and lichen mats occupying windswept localities in the alpine belt of the Balkan Range, local and fragmented representatives of the Rhodopide communities of unit 31.41231.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dwarf [Vaccinium] heaths
description: Prostrate [Vaccinium uliginosum] ssp. [microphyllum], or rarely [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], and lichen mats of high windswept localities in the Pontic Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian dwarf [Vaccinium] heaths
description: Prostrate [Vaccinium spp.] and lichen mats of high windswept localities in the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan dwarf [Vaccinium] heaths
description: Prostrate [Vaccinium spp.] and lichen mats of high windswept localities in the Himalayas and associated ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan [Gaultheria] dwarf heaths
description: Carpets of prostrate shrubs of the ericaceous genus [Gaultheria], in particular [Gaultheria nummularioides], [Gaultheria trichophylla], [Gaultheria pyroloides], accompanied by lichens, of windswept, mostly snowfree, localities in the alpine belt of the Himalayas, up to altitudes of 4500 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide acidocline alpenrose heaths
description: [Rhododendron spp.]-dominated heaths of acid podsols in the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Dinarides, the Carpathians, the Balkan Range, the Pontic Range, the Caucasus and the Himalayan system, often with [Vaccinium spp.], sometimes with dwarf pines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine rusty alpenrose heaths
description: [Rhododendron ferrugineum]-dominated heaths of acid podsols in the Alps, often with [Vaccinium spp.], sometimes with [Pinus mugo]. They often alternate in mosaic with units 31.431 and 31.44.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean rusty alpenrose heaths
description: [Rhododendron ferrugineum]-dominated heaths of acid podsols in the Pyrenees, often with [Vaccinium spp.] and alternating in mosaic with units 31.431 and 31.44.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric rusty alpenrose heaths
description: [Rhododendron ferrugineum]-dominated heaths of the Dinarides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian Kotschy's alpenrose heaths
description: Heaths of the subalpine and lower alpine levels (1700-2000 m) of the eastern and southern Carpathian Mountains, common and widespread, but occupying small surfaces, dominated by [Rhododendron myrtifolium] ([Rhododendron kotschyi]), [Vaccinium gaultherioides] and [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], with some regional species such as [Soldanella hungarica] ssp. [major], [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda], [Melampyrum saxosum], [Campanula abietina] and [Campanula serrata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide and Balkan Kotschy's alpenrose heaths
description: [Rhododendron myrtifolium]-dominated heaths of the subalpine belt of the Balkan Range and the Rila.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range Kotschy's alpenrose heaths
description: [Rhododendron myrtifolium]-dominated heaths of the subalpine belt of the central Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rila Kotschy's alpenrose heaths
description: [Rhododendron myrtifolium]-dominated heaths of the subalpine belt of the eastern Rila.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic alpenrose heaths
description: Heaths of the Pontic Range, formed, mostly above treeline, by [Rhododendron caucasicum], [Rhododendron smirnovii], [Rhododendron ungernii], [Rhododendron x sochadzeae], sometimes with [Rhododendron ponticum], [Rhododendron luteum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian alpenrose heaths
description: Rhododendron heaths of the Caucasus, dominated, for the most part, by [Rhododendron caucasicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan alpenrose heaths
description: Rhododendron heaths of the alpine zone of the Himalayas dominated by [Rhododendron lepidotum], [Rhododendron setosum], [Rhododendron anthopogon], [Rhododendron nivale], [Rhododendron litangensis], [Rhododendron open-shawianum], [Rhododendron thymifolium], [Rhododendron capitatum], and of the lower transition zone to mountain woodland, with [Rhododendron campanulatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Palaearctic mountain dwarf juniper scrub
description: Usually dense formations of prostrate junipers of the higher levels of southern Palaearctic mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain [Juniperus nana] scrub
description: Thermophile [Juniperus nana]-dominated heaths of the upper levels, mostly of the subalpine or equivalent levels, of the Alps, mostly in the central and southern chains, of the northern and central Apennines, the Corsican and Sardinian mountains, the Forez, the Pyrenees, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Balkan Range, the Rhodopide Mountains, the Moeso-Macedonian Mountains, the Caucasus, the high mountains of the Iberian and Hellenic peninsulas, the Pontic Range, the Taurus, the Himalayan system, the temperate Far Eastern mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina] heaths of Iberia, the Alps, the Apennines, the Tell of North Africa, the southeastern Central European mountains, the Pontic Range, the Anti-Taurus, the western Caucasus, Crimea, the Elburz, the Altai.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: Oro-Mediterranean [Juniperus sabina] heaths of Iberia north to the Pyrenees, where they are limited to south-facing slopes in the montane and subalpine belt of the central part of the range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina] heaths of the montane level of inner Alpine valleys with sporadic fragmentary occurrence in the alti-Mediterranean subalpine level of the southwestern Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina] heaths of rare stations in the Marcho-Abruzzian Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinarid [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina] heaths of the Dinarides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpatho-Balkanic [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: Thermophile [Juniperus sabina]-dominated formation on limestone in the montane belt of the Apuseni Mountains of the southeastern Carpathians, accompanied by regional species [Rhamnus saxatilis] ssp. [tinctorius] and [Sesleria rigida], [Thymus comosus], and [Rhamnus catharticus]. Sporadic fragmentary [Juniperus sabina] formations of the Balkan Range and the Rila mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina]-dominated scrubs of the Anatolian plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina]-dominated scrubs of the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina]-dominated scrubs of Crimea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Elburz [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina]-dominated scrubs of the Elburz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tell [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: Rare [Juniperus sabina] heaths of limestone and dolomite crests of the Djurdjura.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Altai [Juniperus sabina] scrub
description: [Juniperus sabina] heaths of the Altai.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Juniperus hemisphaerica] scrub
description: [Juniperus hemisphaerica] heaths of Iberia, the southern Apennines, Sicily (Madonie, Nebrodi, Etna), Greece, the Caucasus and North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain [Juniperus oxycedrus] scrub
description: [Juniperus oxycedrus] heaths of high mountain slopes of Greece, the Near East and the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain [Juniperus squamata] scrub
description: [Juniperus squamata] heaths of high altitudes of the Himalayan system, west to Afghanistan, and of the mountains of China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain [Juniperus recurva] scrub
description: [Juniperus recurva] heaths of high altitudes of the Himalayan system, west to Afghanistan, and of the mountains of China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain [Juniperus indica] scrub
description: [Juniperus indica] heaths of dry iner valleys of the Himalayan system, east to Yunnan, ascending to an altitude of 5200 m.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain Persian juniper scrub
description: Prostrate scrub facies of the open juniper steppe-forests of high arid slopes of the Elburz, the mountains of Transcaucasia and of Tadzhikistan, the Zagros, the Irano-Afghan plateau, the western and eastern Himalayas and the southeastern and southwestern Arabian peninsula, dominated by junipers of the [Juniperus excelsa] group, often united in an eastern species, the Persian juniper [Juniperus macropoda], or divided into several closely related species, [Juniperus macropoda], [Juniperus seravschanica], [Juniperus turcomanica], but by some taxonomists judged undistinguishable from [Juniperus excelsa]. [Juniperus semiglobosa] may also accompany the other forms or dominate the community in Tadzhikistan, Uzbekistan and Afghanistan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenic high mountain [Empetrum-Vaccinium] heaths
description: Dwarf heaths dominated by [Empetrum hermaphroditum] and [Vaccinium uliginosum], with [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], lycopodes ([Huperzia selago], [Diphasiastrum alpinum]), mosses ([Barbilophozia lycopodioides], [Hylocomium splendens], [Pleurozium schreberi], [Rhythidiadelphus triquetrus]) and lichens ([Cetraria islandica], [Cladonia arbuscula], [Cladonia rangiferina], [Cladonia stellaris], [Cladonia gracilis], [Peltigera aphthosa]) of the subalpine belt of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Pyrenees, the Central Massif, the Sudeten, the Jura, the Northern Apennines, characteristic of relatively windswept, snow-free stations, in frost-exposure situations that are, however, less extreme than those prevailing where communities of unit 31.41 dominate. Unlike the formations of 31.41, those of 31.44 are clearly two-layered.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine and arctic heaths
description: Alpine and high-montane heaths of the highlands and islands of Scotland and, very locally, of the Lake District and of Ireland, alpine and lowland boreal heaths of Iceland, alpine heaths of boreal mountains, in particular of the mountains of Scandinavia, of the Urals, of the mountains of Siberia, alpine heaths of Far Eastern mountains at, or just south of, the limits of the boreal zone, with [Juniperus nana], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Phyllodoce caerulea], [Betula nana] and elements of alpine flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Scotian dwarf mountain heaths
description: Prostrate alpine and high-montane [Calluna vulgaris] or [Vaccinium myrtillus] heaths of windswept summits and ridges, with little snow cover, of the Highlands, the Inner Hebrides and, very locally, of the uplands of Ireland, England and Wales, with [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Arctostaphylos alpinus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Calluna]-[Cladonia] heath
description: Dwarf, prostrate, matted, wind-clipped, low-alpine [Calluna vulgaris] heaths, often with lichen mats, of windswept summits, ridges and mountain passes exposed to cold, continental climates, in the Highlands of Scotland, particularly the east-central Highlands, with very few fragmentary outposts in isolated upland areas of England and Wales, with [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Empetrum hermaphroditum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Calluna]-[Rhacomitrium] heaths
description:
Prostrate, wind-clipped, open, low-alpine [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of moderate to fairly high altitude windswept plateaux and ridges of the northwest Highlands of Scotland, with outposts in the Grampians, descending locally to lower altitudes on Skye, with an abundance of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], and with [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Arctostaphylos alpinus],
[Arctostaphylos uva-ursi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Calluna]-[Arctostaphylos] heaths
description:
Prostrate, open, low-alpine [Calluna vulgaris]  heaths of windswept ridges and crests of the northwest Highlands of Scotland, generally at slightly higher altitudes than those of unit 31.4512, though also extending locally to low altitudes, in particular, along the northern Scottish coast, with [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], 
[Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Empetrum nigrum], [Erica cinerea], sometimes [Salix herbacea]; lichens are often prominent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Vaccinium]-[Rhacomitrium] heaths
description: Prostrate [Vaccinium myrtillus]-[Empetrum hermaphroditum] heaths, with abundant [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], of fairly exposed slopes and summits at moderate to high altitudes of the northwestern Highlands of Scotland, with scattered representatives in the Grampians, and lower altitude occurrences along the west coast of Scotland and on Skye, with [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Alchemilla alpina], [Carex bigelowii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hibernian montane heaths
description: Subboreal [Calluna vulgaris]-[Vaccinium myrtillus] heaths of windswept summits and ridges of Ireland, with [Empetrum nigrum], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] and sometimes [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Salix herbacea], [Diphasiastrum alpinum] ([Lycopodium alpinum]); they are limited to small surfaces, mostly above 800 metres, with areas of concentrated occurrence in Munster and in Connemarra.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic chionophilous boreo-montane heaths
description: Low- to very low-growing low alpine and subalpine [Vaccinium myrtillus] heaths of the Highlands of Scotland, Skye, and, locally, the Southern Uplands and northern England, characteristic of somewhat more protected stations with longer snow cover than those of unit 31.451, with [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Cornus suecica], [Carex bigelowii], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Vaccinium]-[Cladonia] heaths
description: Very low, matted, low alpine heaths of moderately sheltered and snowbound slopes of the Grampians and, more locally, of the northwestern Highlands, with fragmentary outposts in the Southern Uplands and the Lake District, formed by [Vaccinium myrtillus] with [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Empetrum hermaphroditum] and abundant lichens, in particular, [Cladonia arbuscula], [Cladonia uncialis], [Cetraria islandica]. [Carex bigelowii], [Deschampsia flexuosa] and [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] are often abundant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Vaccinium]-[Rubus chamaemorus] heaths
description: Low, subalpine heaths of the central and northwestern Highlands, with outposts in the Moffat-Tweedsmuir hills and in the Cheviots, within the Southern Uplands, developed on peaty ground under oceanic climates with prolonged snow cover, formed by [Vaccinium myrtillus] with [Calluna vulgaris], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], and sometimes [Vaccinium uliginosum], associated with a moist carpet of bryophytes. [Rubus chamaemorus], [Cornus suecica] and [Carex bigelowii] are characteristic of the species cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scotian juniper heaths
description: Prostrate [Juniperus nana] mats of the Highlands of Scotland, restricted to a limited number of stations on the west side of mountains in the northwest Highlands and on Skye, with [Calluna vulgaris], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Arctostapylos alpina], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Cladonia uncialis], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] and oceanic hepatics.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian boreo-alpine heaths
description: Alpine heaths of the boreal mountains of Scandinavia, with [Juniperus nana], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Vaccinium spp.], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], dwarf [Salix spp.], [Betula nana] and elements of alpine flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian diapensia-azalea heaths
description: Open, scattered heaths of the mountains of Fennoscandia with [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Diapensia lapponica], [Arctostaphylos alpinus] and many lichens, occurring in variable species dominance, installed on patches in snow fields swept bare by the wind in winter, often on dry gravel, sometimes on solifluction, and with high insolation. Maritime and continental types can be identified by the lichen cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian dwarf birch heaths
description: Heaths of the alpine belt of Fennoscandia, dominated by [Betula nana] and [Empetrum hermaphroditum], with [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Arctostaphylos alpina], [Salix glauca], [Salix lapponum] and a ground layer often rich in lichens, growing on poor, gravelly and sandy soils, with a low pH.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian crowberry heaths
description: Xerophilous low heaths of the subalpine and lower alpine levels of Fennoscandia dominated by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Betula nana], with a richly developed lichen layer and few vascular plants. [Juncus trifidus] and [Luzula spicata] are also characteristic. There is little or no snow cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Cladonia] heaths
description: Subalpine and alpine heaths of the mountains of Fennoscandia under rather continental climate, composed of thick (up to 20 cm) lichen carpets, dominated by [Cladonia alpestris]. During periods of drought, lichen carpet often cracks into polygons and mosses and scattered vascular plants appear. Lichen heaths can carpet large areas in lower situations; higher, they are restricted to narrow zones between wind-heaths and snowpatch vegetation. They grow on sand, gravel and stone, under a thin, early thawing snow cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian calcicline bearberry heaths
description: Lower alpine heaths of southern Norway, with low, prostrate, [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], accompanied by  [Antennaria dioica], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Euphrasia frigida], [Betula pubescens], [Vacinium vitis-idaea], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Carex vaginata] with mosses and lichens. Occurs on dry, poor, sandy or gravelly soils containing richer elements, though not on pure limestone, with a thin humus layer, in localities with strong insolation and early thaw.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Phyllodoce]-bilberry heaths
description: Often low heaths of lower alpine levels of Fennoscandia dominated by [Phyllodoce caerulea] and [Vaccinium myrtillus], with [Betula nana], [Betula pubescens], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Juniperus nana], [Alchemilla alpina], [Trientalis europaea] and many mosses and lichens, on moist soils with a humus layer, protected by snow for short periods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian dwarf cornel-northern bilberry heaths
description: Heaths of the boreal and arctic zones of Fennoscandia, mostly under maritime climate, dominated by [Cornus suecica] and [Vaccinium uliginosum] accompanied by [Solidago vigaurea] and [Trientalis europaea], with [Calluna vulgaris], [Carex bigelowii] often covering extensive areas in alternance with grass heaths, on relatively poor soils, normally snow protected.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian fern-bilberry heaths
description: Lower alpine heaths of western Fennoscandia, dominated by [Gymnocarpium dryopteris] and [Vaccinium myrtillus], with [Salix herbacea], [Trientalis europea], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Rumex acetosa], occurring over small surfaces within the dwarf cornel-northern bilberry heaths of unit 31.4547, in the shelter of stones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian juniper-dwarf birch-bilberry heaths
description: Lower alpine heaths of Fennoscandia, dominated by low scrub (0.5-1m) of [Betula nana], [Juniperus nana], [Vaccinium myrtillus], with very common [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], on dry to mesic ground with low pH, somewhat snow protected.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North Atlantic boreo-alpine heaths
description: Lowland and alpine boreal heaths of Iceland, Spitzbergen and Greenland formed by low, compact or mat-forming shrubs of Ericaceae, [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Betula nana], [Juniperus nana] and [Salix spp.] and alpine flora elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic boreo-alpine heaths
description: Lowland and alpine boreal heaths of Iceland formed by low, compact or mat-forming shrubs of Ericaceae, [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Betula nana], [Juniperus nana] and [Salix spp.] and alpine flora elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic azalea heaths
description: Dwarf heaths of Iceland, often sparse, dominated by [Loiseleuria procumbens], usually associated with [Empetrum hermaphroditum] and [Vaccinium uliginosum].
