The ground layer is well developed, with a cover of the order of 30% to 50%, often dominated by [Rhacomitrium canescens] or [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], accompanied by a diverse cortŠge of lichens. The community is characteristic of the lower alpine zone of northern and eastern Iceland, usually developed on shallow soils, in wind-exposed situations with reduced snow cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic dwarf birch heaths
description: Dwarf heaths of Iceland dominated by [Betula nana], usually associated with [Salix phylicifolia], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], with [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Salix lanata], [Salix herbacea], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Juncus trifidus]. The muscinal layer is moderately developed, with a cover of the order of 30%. These heaths are mostly developed in the lowland and lower alpine zones, in wind-exposed situations with low snow cover, often on loess deposits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic crowberry heaths
description: Xerophilous dwarf heaths of Iceland dominated by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], variously associated with [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Calluna vulgaris], [Betula nana], [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Salix lanata], [Salix herbacea], [Polygonum viviparum], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Carex bigelowii], [Festuca vivipara], [Festuca richardsonii], [Poa alpina], [Equisetum variegatum], with an often richly developed lichen layer. They are developed in the lowlands and lower alpine levels on a variety of substrates, including lavas, with relatively shallow soils. Where they occur alongside [Empetrum]-[Vaccinium] heaths of unit 31.2113 they occupy more wind-exposed, more snowfree surfaces, and differ by the lower stature of the erico‹ds, the often more open structure of the shrub layer and the lesser prominence of [Vaccinium spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic ling heaths
description: Heaths of Iceland dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], usually associated with [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Salix herbacea], [Rubus saxatilis], [Polygonum viviparum], [Galium boreale], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Carex bigelowii], [Luzula multiflora], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Equisetum pratense] and, often, with [Thymus praecox] ssp. [arcticus], [Galium normanii], [Platanthera hyperborea], [Dactylorhiza islandica], [Festuca vivipara], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Agrostis tenuis]. The mucinal layer is poorly to moderately developed, with a total cover ranging between 0 and 40%. [Rhacomitrium canescens], [Lophozia sudetica], [Ptilidium ciliare], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Rhytidiadelphus squarrosus], [Rhytidiadelphus loreus] are the most common species. They are mostly limited to the lowlands, best developed in the central northern lowlands, apparently absent from parts of the northwestern peninsula, often developed on loess deposits.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic bearberry heaths
description: Heaths of Iceland dominated by [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], accompanied by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Calluna vulgaris], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Rubus saxatilis], [Thymus praecox] ssp. [arcticus], [Festuca vivipara], [Carex bigelowii], [Kobresia myosuroides]. The muscinal layer is practically nonexistent. These heaths are characteristic of steep, dry, sunny slopes in the lowland and lower alpine zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Phyllodoce]-bilberry heaths
description: Heaths of Iceland, often low-growing, dominated by [Vaccinium myrtillus] and [Phyllodoce caerulea], with [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Betula nana], [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Juniperus nana], [Rubus saxatilis], [Alchemilla vulgaris], [Galium verum], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Polygonum viviparum], [Ranunculus acris], [Pyrola minor], [Carex bigelowii], and many mosses and lichens, developed in the lowlands and lower alpine zone of northern and eastern Iceland, on moist soils with a humus layer, moderately protected by snow.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic dwarf cornel-northern bilberry heaths
description: Heaths of Iceland dominated by [Cornus suecica] and [Vaccinium uliginosum], accompanied by, among others, [Calluna vulgaris], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Carex bigelowii], limited to four areas of northern Iceland, the northwestern fjords, the Snaefell peninsula, the north coast around the mouth of Eyjafj”rdur, north of Akureyri, and the northeastern coast between Vopnafj”rdur and Herads. They are developed at generally low altitude, in strongly oceanic sectors, usually in snow protected sites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic fern-bilberry heaths
description: Heaths of Iceland dominated by [Gymnocarpium dryopteris], associated with [Vaccinium myrtillus] or [Vaccinium uliginosum], mostly limited to small surfaces in the shelter of stones, within lowland heath complexes, in particular, of the northwestern peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic juniper-dwarf birch-bilberry heaths
description: Heaths of Iceland dominated by [Betula nana], [Juniperus nana] and [Vaccinium myrtillus], with [Vaccinium uliginosum] and, sometimes, in the east and northeast, [Vaccinium vitis-idea], forming scrubs 0.5 to 1 m high on dry to mesic ground of the lowlands and the lower alpine zone, in somewhat snow-protected situations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic northern bilberry heaths
description: Heaths of Iceland, often low-growing, dominated by [Vaccinium uliginosum] and [Phyllodoce caerulea], with many mosses, developed in most lowland and lower alpine regions on moist soils with a humus layer. Northern bilberry heaths require less snow protection than the [Phyllodoce]-bilberry heaths of unit 31.45516 and often covers larger areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland boreo-alpine heaths
description: Boreoarctic heaths of Greenland, with [Salix glauca] ssp. [callicarpea], [Betula glandulosa], [Betula nana], [Alnus crispa], [Sorbus groenlandica], [Juniperus nana], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum] ssp. [microphyllum], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] ssp. [minus], [Phyllodoce caerulea], [Rhododendron lapponicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian boreo-alpine heaths
description: Mountain heaths of the Urals, with [Betula nana], [Salix glauca], [Salix pulchra], [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia], [Cassiope tetragona], [Cassiope hypnoides], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Vaccinium uliginosum] ssp. [microphyllum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Phyllodoce caerulea], [Ledum palustre] ssp. [decumbens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian boreo-alpine heaths
description: High mountain dwarf shrub communities of the Sayan mountains (Korotkov), as well as of the northeastern Siberian highlands, the Altai and possibly the Khangai.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern boreo-alpine heaths
description: Alpine heaths of Far Eastern mountains, south of the main lowland taiga zone, including prostrate [Vaccinium spp.] and lichen mats of high windswept localities of the mountains of China and Japan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic heaths
description: Heaths of arctic mountains, coasts and islands of the Palaearctic zone, mostly dominated by or rich in [Cassiope tetragona], often associated with [Dryas] heaths of unit 31.494.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Cassiope] heaths
description: Alpine heaths restricted to mostly oceanic climates of northwestern boreal and arctic Fennoscandia, dominated by dense carpets of [Cassiope tetragona], [Empetrum hermaphroditum] and [Dryas octopetala] with wax-leaved and cushion plants; participating species include [Salix lanata], [Salix myrsinites], [Salix polaris], [Salix reticulata], [Salix hastata], [Rhododendron lapponicum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Betula nana], [Silene acaulis], [Silene whalenbergella], [Astragalus alpinus], [Astragalus frigidus], [Equisetum scirpoides], [Carex parallela], [Cerastium alpinum] var. [glabratum], often covering stony, calcareous substrates with fine material. There is snow protection but early thaw; ground moisture is insignificant during the growing period.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spitzbergen [Cassiope] heaths
description: Heaths of Spitzbergen dominated by [Cassiope tetragona], with [Dryas octopetala] var. [minor], [Carex rupestris], [Silene acaulis] var. [arctica], [Drepanocladus uncinatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland [Cassiope] heaths
description: Heaths of Greenland dominated by [Cassiope tetragona], with [Dryas octopetala], [Carex bigelowii], [Silene acaulis], [Vaccinium uliginosum] ssp. [microphyllum], [Phyllodoce caerulea], [Drepanocladus uncinatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Bruckenthalia] heaths
description: Formations of [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia], often accompanied by [Juniperus nana], [Vaccinium myrtillus] and herbaceous alpine grassland species, occupying damp, noncalcareous substrates of high mountains of the Balkan peninsula and northern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide [Bruckenthalia] heaths
description: [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia] heaths of the alpine and subalpine belts of the Vitosha, the Rila, the Pirin, the Slovianka, the Rhodopes, the Vrondous, the Menikion and the Pangeon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Hellenide [Bruckenthalia] heaths
description: [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia] formations of the subalpine, alpine and  locally, montane, belts of the Pelagonian mountains, south to the Varnous, the Vitsi, the Piperitsa, the Voras, the Pinovon, the Tzena, of the Moeso-Macedonian mountains south to the Kerkini (Belles range), and of the Pieria in the northern Thessalian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpatho-Balkanic [Bruckenthalia] heaths
description: [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia] formations of the Balkan Range, with northern representatives in the southeastern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan range [Bruckenthalia] heaths
description: [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia] formations of the subalpine, alpine and locally, montane, belts of the Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian [Bruckenthalia] heaths
description: Sporadically distributed formations in the Apuseni Mountains and the southern Carpathians, dominated by [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia], accompanied by [Juniperus nana], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] and the endemic or near-endemic [Campanula patula] ssp. [abietina] ([Campanula abietina]), [Campanula serrata] and [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Bruckenthalia] heaths
description: Scattered dwarf shrub formations dominated by [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia], of the alpine and subalpine belt of high mountains of northern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide bearberry heaths
description: Mats of [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi] or [Arctostaphylos alpinus] of the alpine, subalpine and locally, montane, belts of the Alps, the Pyrenees, the northern and central Apennines, the Dinarides, the Carpathians, the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides (south to the Slavianka-Orvilos, the Menikion, the Pangeon, the Falakron and the Rhodopi), the Moeso-Macedonian mountains (including Athos), the Pelagonides (south to the Greek Macedonian border ranges Tzena, Pinovon and Kajmakchalan) and Olympus, in the Thessalian mountains, mostly on calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide hairy alpenrose-erica heaths
description: Forest substitution heaths, treeline fringe formations and alpine heaths or mats of calcareous soils in the Alps and the Dinarides, with [Rhododendron hirsutum], [Rhododendron intermedium], [Rhodothamnus chamaecistus] and [Erica herbacea], often accompanied by [Clematis alpina], [Daphne striata], [Daphne mezereum], [Globularia cordifolia], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi]. [Rhododendron hirsutum] and, mostly in the Austrian Alps, [Erica herbacea] are the most frequent dominants; other shrubs can locally play that r“le. [Arctostaphylos spp.]-dominated facies have, however, been been included in unit 31.47.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hairy alpenrose heaths
description: Forest substitution heaths, treeline fringe formations and alpine heaths or mats dominated by [Rhododendron hirsutum], of calcareous soils in the Alps and the Dinarides. [Rhododendron intermedium], [Rhodothamnus chamaecistus] and [Erica herbacea] may participate in the constitution of the heath, often accompanied by [Clematis alpina] and [Daphne mezereum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine erica heaths
description: Species-rich montane, subalpine and low alpine heaths of calcareous soils of the Alps and the Dinarids, dominated by [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]), mostly characteristic of the Austrian northern and southern calcareous Alps, south to the Dolomites and the Karawanken, with [Sesleria albicans], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Daphne striata], [Globularia cordifolia], [Globularia nudicaulis], [Polygala chamaebuxus]. Small shrubs other than [Erica herbacea], in particular [Globularia cordifolia], may locally dominate communities. Distinctive formations also exist on siliceous and on serpentine substrates. They are provisionally included in this unit.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain avens mats
description: Dwarf heaths formed by mats of the woody [Dryas octopetala] in high Palaearctic mountains, in arctic and boreal regions and in isolated Atlantic coastal outposts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenic high mountain [Dryas] mats
description: Mats of [Dryas octopetala] of the high levels of the mountains of the western Alpine system, the Jura and the Central Massif, in calcicolous alpine grasslands and on high mountain rocks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] mats of the high levels of the Alps, widespread pioneering communities on calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern high moutain [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] mats of the high levels of the Pyrenees and Central Massif, relatively uncommon pioneering communities of calcareous substrates distributed in the CorbiŠres (pic d'Ourthizet), in the eastern and central Pyrenees, and, very locally, on high summits of the Cental Massif ranges of Monts-Dore and Cantal.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Jura [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] mats of the high levels of the western Jura, mostly above 1300 metres, on, in particular, la D“le, le Reculet, le Creux-du-Van, le Chasseral, le Mont-d'Or, le Suchet, la Dent de Vaulion.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine [Dryas] mats
description: Rare [Dryas octopetala] mats of the high levels of the Apuan Alps, the Pistoiese Apennines (Mandromini), the Central Apennines (Sibillini, Terminillo, Mount Viglio) and the Abruzzian and Campanian Apennines (Monte Cassino, Monte Cairo).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpatho-Balkanide [Dryas] mats
description: Communities dominated by [Dryas octopetala], scattered in calcicolous subalpine and alpine grasslands of the Carpathians and the Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Carpathian [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] mats of calcareous substrates in the subalpine and alpine belts of the western Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Carpathian [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] communities widespread in calcicolous subalpine and alpine grassland of the Romanian Carpathians, having as endemics [Achillea oxyloba] ssp. [schurii] ([Achillea schurii]), [Oxytropis carpatica], and [Cerastium transsilvanicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range [Dryas] mats
description: Calciphile communities dominated by [Dryas octopetala] of subalpine and alpine grasslands of the Balkan Range, west to the Gethian mountains of eastern Serbia (Suva Planina).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaro-Hellenide [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] mats of calcareous substrates of the high levels of the Dinarides and the Pelagonides south to Mount Tzena.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide mountain avens mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] communities of the Rila, the Pirin, the Slavianka-Orvilos and the Falakron.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic maritime [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] dwarf heaths of the oceanic lowlands of northern Scotland, the Inner Hebrides and western Ireland, associated with Durness, Jurassic or Carboniferous limestone outcroppings and karstic pavements, or with shell sands blown over rocky or peaty headlands, with [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Thymus praecox], [Carex flacca], [Viola riviniana], [Plantago maritima], [Lotus corniculatus], [Festuca ovina], [Calluna vulgaris], [Carex rupestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Durness [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] dwarf heaths of the oceanic lowlands of northern Scotland, developed on Durness limestone outcroppings and karstic pavements, or on shell sands blown over headlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hebridean [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] or [Dryas octopetala]-[Arctostaphylos uva-ursi] dwarf heaths of the Inner Hebrides, recorded from Skye, Raasay and Rhum, associated with Durness or Jurassic limestone outcroppings.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Burren [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] or [Dryas]-[Arctostaphylos] dwarf heaths of western Ireland, characteristic of the Burren, where they cover extensive surfaces of bare or thinly peat-covered Carboniferous limestones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] heaths of the boreoalpine and arctoalpine levels of northern Palaearctic mountains of Scotland and Fennoscandia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Dryas] mats
description: High-altitude species-rich [Dryas] cliff-ledge communities of the mica-shist hills of the central Highlands of Scotland, with fragmentary outposts in Lakeland and Snowdonia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian boreo-alpine [Dryas] mats
description: [Dryas octopetala] heaths of the boreoalpine and arctoalpine levels of the mountains of Fennoscandia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Dryas]-[Arctostaphylos] heaths
description: Dense, closed, low heaths of Fenoscandian mountains dominated by [Dryas octopetala], with [Diphasiastrum alpinum], [Carex brunnescens] and [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), installed on dry calcareous gravels, sands and rock pavements. Accompanying species vary over the very broad range of this habitat and include [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Arctostaphylos alpina], [Betula nana], [Juniperus nana], [Salix reticulata], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Astragalus alpinus], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Cerastium alpinum], [Draba norvegica], [Silene acaulis], [Minuartia stricta], [Parnassia palustris], [Pedicularis flammula], [Pedicularis oederi], [Potentilla nivea], [Pyrola norvegica], [Viola rupestris] ssp. [relicta], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Leucorchis albida] ssp. [straminea] ([Leucorchis straminea]), [Oxytropis lapponica], [Carex atrata], [Carex capillaris], [Carex rupestris], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Thalictrum alpinum]. The [Dryas] sometimes is so dense that no other species are present. A ground layer is often absent; the humus layer is often around 5 cm.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Dryas]-[Kobresia] heaths
description: Very low, open heaths of boreal mountains dominated by [Dryas octopetala] and [Kobresia myosuroides] occupying weathered calcareous gravels or pavements on windswept exposures with a thin humus layer, negligible snow cover and early thaw. Codominating species include [Carex fuliginosa], [Carex nardina] and, locally, [Festuca ovina], acompanied by [Draba fladnizensis], [Draba nivalis], [Draba norvegica], [Saxifraga cespitosa], [Saxifraga nivalis], [Saxifraga opositifolia], [Arnica alpina], [Campanula uniflora], [Diapensia lapponica], [Euphrasia lapponica], [Gentianella tenella], [Minuartia rubella], [Potentilla nivea], [Poa glauca], and, locally, [Carex glacialis], rich in lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian moist [Dryas] heaths
description: Sparse [Dryas octopetala] heaths of the low to midalpine level of Fennoscandian mountains, with an abundant, often continuous ground cover of mosses, particularly [Tomentypmum nitens] and [Sphagnum warnstorfii], developed on calcareous substrates that are permanently moist or subjected to periodical near-surface ground water flow. [Viola biflora], [Carex norvegica], [Minuartia biflora], [Thalictrum alpinum] have a preference for this habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic [Dryas] heaths
description: Maritime or submaritime [Dryas octopetala] heaths of the arctic lowlands of the Palaearctic continent and of the low arctic and subarctic islands of the North Atlantic and the Northern Ocean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian arctic maritime [Dryas] heaths
description: Low, open, heaths of the western and northern coasts of arctic Scandinavia developed on sandy, calcareous soils in exposed coastal climates, dominated by [Dryas octopetala] and [Empetrum hermaphroditum], accompanied by short sedges and grasses, usually without a mucinal layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Dryas] heaths
description: [Dryas octopetala]-dominated heaths of Iceland. [Empetrum hermaphroditum] often dominates with the [Dryas]. Other accompaniers may include [Calluna vulgaris], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Thymus arcticus], [Silene acaulis], [Armeria maritima], [Cerastium alpinum], [Draba incana], [Rhinanthus minor], [Euphrasia frigida], [Parnassia palustris], [Tofieldia pusilla], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Carex bigelowii], [Carex capillaris], [Carex glacialis], [Carex rupestris], [Carex vaginata], [Festuca vivipara], [Festuca richardsonii], [Luzula multiflora], [Luzula spicata], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Botrychium lunaria], [Equisetum pratense], [Equisetum boreale]. The moss layer can be variously developed and include, in particular, [Rhacomitrium canescens], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Drepanocladus uncinatus]. [Dryas] heaths occupy a variety of substrates, in particular, loess deposits, gravels, moraines, sands, in mostly somewhat wind-exposed situations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spitzbergen [Dryas] heaths
description: [Dryas] heaths of Spitzbergen developed on shallow, well drained soils, dominated by [Dryas octopetala] var. [minor] or by [Dryas octopetala] and sedges ([Carex rupestris]), [Carex nardina], with [Salix polaris], [Luzula confusa], [Pedicularis dasyantha], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Stereocaulon alpinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland [Dryas] heaths
description: [Dryas] heaths of Greenland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern [Dryas] mats
description: Dwarf heaths formed by mats of the woody [Dryas octopetala] or [Dryas punctata] in high mountains of the far eastern Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide high mountain dwarf bilberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium]-dominated dwarf heaths of the subalpine belt of southern mountains, in particular, of the northern and central Apennines, the Balkan Range, the Hellenides, the Pontic Range and the Caucasus, with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium uliginosum] [s.l.], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea]  and, locally, [Empetrum nigrum]. They are richer in grassland species than the communities of unit 31.44 and often take the appearence of alpine grassland with dward shrubs. [Vaccinium myrtillus] also plays a much more dominant role, in lieu of [Vaccinium uliginosum] and [Empetrum hermaphroditum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean subalpine dwarf bilberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium] dwarf heaths of the subalpine or lower alpine belt of mountains of the Italian peninsula and of the large Tyrrhenian islands formed by [Vaccinium myrtillus] and [Vaccinium uliginosum] [s.l.], with a large admixture of alpine or subalpine grassland species and sometimes of megaforb elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine dwarf bilberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium]-dominated dwarf heaths of the subalpine or lower alpine belt of the northern and central Apennines, with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium uliginosum] [s.l.], and, locally, [Empetrum nigrum], mostly dwarf-shrub rich facies of alpine or subalpine grasslands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican dwarf bilberry heaths
description: [Vaccinium myrtillus] heath-grasslands of ubacs of the lower subalpine level of Corsica, limited to cliff-bordered corridors, ledges at the foot of high cliffs, ravines, torrent banks, the fringe of humid sweet alder brush, in cool shady situations with prolonged snow cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkano-Hellenic dwarf bilberry heaths
description: Communities of [Vaccinium myrtillus] and/or [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], rich in grass and herb species, of the subalpine level of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Pelagonides, the Pindus, the Thessalian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic Range dwarf bilberry heaths
description: Communities of [Vaccinium myrtillus] and/or [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] of the Pontic Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian dwarf bilberry heaths
description: Communities of [Vaccinium myrtillus] and/or [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] of the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide high mountain greenweed heaths
description: Low [Genista spp.] or [Chamaecytisus spp.] heaths of the subalpine, low alpine or montane belts of high southern nemoral mountains, in particular of the southern Alps, the Apennines, the Dinarides, the southern Carpathians, the Balkan Range, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Pelagonides, the northern Pindus, the Rhodopides, the Thessalian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rayed broom heaths
description: [Genista radiata], [Genista holopetala], [Genista hassertiana] heaths of the montane, subalpine and alpine belts of the southeastern Alps, in particular the Bergamesque Alps, the Dolomites, the Carnic Alps, the Julian Alps, of the Dinarides, with more localized stations in the Novarese Alps, the northern and central Apennines, the southern Carpathians, the Pelagonides, the northern Pindus, the Thessalian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkano-Rhodopide [Chamaecytisus absinthioides] heaths
description: Low shrub formations dominated by the Balkan peninsula endemic [Chamaecytisus eriocarpus] ([Chamaecytisus absinthioides]) characteristic of the subalpine and montane belts of the Balkan Range, of the Rhodopides (Rila, Pirin, Orvilos, Vrondous, Pangeon, Falakron, Rhodope) and of the Moeso-Macedonian mountains south to the Belasitza-Kerkini.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic [Chamaecytisus hirsutus] heaths
description: [Chamaecytisus hirsutus] heaths of the mountains of the southern Balkan and Hellenic peninsula, in particular, of the Pelagonides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf pine scrub
description: [Pinus mugo] brushes of the dry eastern inner Alps, of the northern and southeastern outer Alps, of the southwestern Alps and the Swiss Jura, of the eastern greater Hercynian ranges, of the Carpathians, of the Apennines, of the Dinarides and the neighbouring Pelagonides, of the Pirin, the Rila and the Balkan Range; [Pinus pumila] scrubs of eastern Siberia, northeastern China, Korea and the Japanese archipelago.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Alpine dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: [Pinus mugo] brushes of the dry eastern inner Alps, of local occurrence throughout the area, accompanied by [Rhododendron hirsutum], [Erica herbacea], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Rhodothamnus chamaecistus], or, on siliceous ground, [Rhododendron ferrugineum] and [Vaccinium myrtillus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Outer Alpine dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: Main range [Pinus mugo] brushes of well-drained, mostly calcareous, soils of the northern and southeastern outer Alps, usually with [Rhododendron hirsutum], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Arctostaphylos alpinus], [Sorbus chamaemespilus], [Lonicera caerulea], [Lonicera alpigena], [Calamagrostis varia], sometimes with [Erica herbacea] or [Rhodothamnus chamaecistus] and, in acidophilous variants, known in particular from the Karawanken, [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Rhododendron ferrugineum], [Empetrum hermaphroditum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: Very local [Pinus mugo] brushes of the southwestern Alps (Moyen-Valais, Haute-Roya, Ligurian Alps), with [Juniperus nana], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Daphne striata], [Erica herbacea], [Carex firma] and, in some stations, [Rhododendron hirsutum]; cold-block [Pinus mugo] formations of the Swiss Jura.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: Rare and local Apennine formations of the Parmian Apennines, the Abruzzi and the Campanian Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: [Pinus mugo] brushes of the Sudeten, the Erzgebirge, the Bayerischerwald, the B”hmerwald, with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Salix silesiaca] [s. l.], [Trientalis europaea], [Homogyne alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: [Pinus mugo] brushes of the Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian subalpine mountain pine scrub
description: [Pinus mugo] brushes forming an extensive belt in the upper subalpine zone of the higher mountains of the northwestern, eastern and southeastern Carpathians with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Ribes petraeum] var. [carpaticum], [Sorbus aucuparia] var. [glabrata], [Rosa pendulina], [Homogyne alpina], [Soldanella hungarica] ssp. [major] in siliceous stations, with tall herbs in calcareous ones. The southeastern Carpathian formations, particularly those of the Apuseni Mountains, harbour the regional endemic [Campanula patula] ssp. [abietina] ([Campanula abietina]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian alpenrose mountain pine scrub
description: Widespread formations of [Pinus mugo] accompanied by the regional endemic [Rhododendron myrtifolium], on shallow-soil slopes of the subalpine level of the southeastern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelago-Dinaride dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: [Pinus mugo]-dominated formations of the Dinarides and of neighbouring chains of the Pelagonides, in particular the Jakupica range, with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Rubus saxatilis], [Rubus idaeus], [Sorbus aucuparia], [Rosa pendulina], [Veratrum album] and [Polygonatum verticillatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkano-Rhodopide dwarf mountain pine scrub
description: [Pinus mugo]-dominated formations of the Pirin and the Rila, with remnants in the Balkan Range, including the Suva Planina. This habitat has been severely reduced by clearance for pastures, and its dirtribution area has regressed; in addition to the ranges where it still forms substantial stands, [Pinus mugo] is recorded from the western Rhodope, the Vitosha and, perhaps, Orvilos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern dwarf Siberian pine scrub
description: Scrubs of eastern Siberia, northeastern China, Korea and the Japanese archipelago formed by [Pinus pumilio].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine and oroboreal bush communities
description: Bushy facies of the tall herb communities of moist, rich soils of Eurasian mountains, mostly characteristic of the subalpine zone of the higher ranges of the Alpine system and its satellites, and of the slopes of lesser ranges in the boreal zone (cf. unit 37.8).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain alder brush
description: Dense thickets of bushy alders characteristic of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Balkan Range, Vitosha, Rila, Corsica and the mountains of northeastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Green alder brush
description: Green alder ([Alnus viridis] ssp. [viridis])-dominated formations of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Dinarides and the Balkan Range, Vitosha, Rila, rich in tall herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine green alder scrub
description: Green alder ([Alnus viridis] ssp. [viridis])-dominated formations, rich in tall herbs, of the subalpine and lower alpine belts of the Alps, on slopes with a good water-holding capacity, mostly on siliceous soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian green alder scrub
description: [Alnus viridis]-dominated formations of the Carpathian mountains, with, in some communities, [Pulmonaria filarszkyana], [Cirsium waldsteinii], [Rumex arifolius] ssp. [carpaticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric green alder scrub
description: [Alnus viridis]-dominated formations of the Dinarides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan range green alder brush
description: [Alnus viridis]-dominated formations, often with [Rumex alpinus], [Ligusticum mutellina], [Salix silesiaca], [Geum coccineum], [Veratrum album], of the Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide green alder brush
description: [Alnus viridis]-dominated brushes of the subalpine, 1300-2100 metre, level of Vitosha and Rila.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican sweet alder brush
description: One to three metre-tall brush of the Corsican endemic [Alnus viridis] ssp. [suaveolens], sometimes accompanied by a few [Sorbus aucuparia], [Acer pseudoplatanus] or [Rhamnus alpinus], limited to the moist, cool, north-facing slopes (ubacs) and, locally, to humid torrent galleries on the south-facing slopes (adrets) of the subalpine (1600-2100 m) belt of Corsica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian alder brush
description: Thickets of [Alnus viridis] ssp. [fruticosa], [Alnus kamtchatica], [Alnus sinuata] of the subalpine level of the Urals, of the mountains of Siberia, in particular the Putorany range, the Kamchatka range, the mountains of northern China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland alder brush
description: Thickets of [Alnus cripa] of southwestern Greenland, distributed from Brede Fjord near Narsaq north to Evighedsfjorden near Maniitsoq, up to 2 metre, occasionnally  3-4 metre, tall.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine and oroboreal willow brush
description: Willow-dominated communities of higher Eurasian mountains and of the boreal zone, mostly characteristic of the subalpine zone of the higher ranges of the Alpine system and its satellites, where many constitute facies of subalpine bush and tall herb communities, of the slopes of lesser ranges in the boreal zone, including the Scandinavian mountains, of Iceland and of the northern British Isles (cf. unit 37.8).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the mountains of the Alpine system and neighbouring ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenous small willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane brushes and low scrubs of the Alps, the Apennines, the Jura, the western great Hercynian ranges, dominated by small shrubby, generally 0.5-2 metre tall, [Salix] species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine small willow brush
description: Willow brushes and dwarf shrub heaths of the Alps, dominated by [Salix waldsteiniana], [Salix caesia], [Salix foetida], [Salix glabra], [Salix hastata], [Salix glaucosericea], [Salix helvetica], [Salix bicolor], [Salix hegetschweileri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine small willow brush
description: Willow brushes and dwarf shrub heaths of the northern Apennines, in particular, of the Apuan Alps, dominated by [Salix hastata] or the endemic [Salix crataegifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Hercynian small willow brush
description: Very local willow brushes and dwarf shrub heaths of the Central Massif, the Vosges, the Harz, dominated by [Salix hastata] or [Salix bicolor].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Hercynian lapland willow brush
description: Very local willow brush of the Central Massif dominated by the glacial relict [Salix lapponum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine prostrate willow brush
description: Dwarf shrub heaths, very low brushes and espaliers of the alpine and subalpine belts of the Alps, formed by prostrate or near-prostrate [Salix alpina], [Salix breviserrata], [Salix reticulata], [Salix retusa], and occasionally very small forms of [Salix] species characteristic of unit 31.6211; snow patch communities dominated by [Salix reticulata] or [Salix retusa] (unit 36.1221) are excluded.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenous tall willow brush
description: Tall [Salix]-dominated brushes of the mountains of the subalpine, sometimes alpine and montane, belts of the Alps, the Apennines, the Jura, the western greater Hercynian ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine tall willow brush
description: [Salix pentandra], [Salix appendiculata], [Salix laggeri], [Salix mielichhoferi], [Salix nigricans] ([Salix myrsinifolia]) thickets and tall brushes of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine mountain tall willow brush
description: Very local willow thickets and tall brushes of the subalpine and montane belts of the western great Hercynian ranges (the Central Massif, the Vosges, the Black Forest, the Bayerischerwald) and of other ranges adjacent to the western Alps, in particular, the French and Swiss Jura and the northern Apennines, dominated by [Salix pentandra], [Salix appendiculata], [Salix nigricans] ([Salix myrsinifolia]) or [Salix daphnoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Cantabric willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the Pyrenees and the Cordillera Cantabrica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean willow dwarf heath
description: Dwarf heaths of the subalpine and alpine levels of the Pyrenees and the Cordillera Cantabrica, dominated by the endemic [Salix pyrenaica], often accompanied by [Dryas octopetala].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Cantabric [Salix breviserrata] heaths
description: Dwarf heaths and espaliers of the subalpine and alpine levels of the Pyrenees and the Cordillera Cantabrica, dominated by the prostrate or near prostrate [Salix breviserrata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean small willow brush
description:
Uncommon willow brushes and dwarf shrub heaths of the Pyrenees, dominated by 
[Salix foetida], [Salix hastata] or [Salix bicolor].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean Lapland willow brush
description: Very local willow brush of the eastern Pyrenees dominated by the glacial relict [Salix lapponum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean tall willow brush
description: Uncommon thickets and tall brushes of the Pyrenees dominated by [Salix pentandra], [Salix appendiculata], [Salix nigricans] ([Salix myrsinifolia]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynio-Carpathian willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the Carpathians and the eastern Hercynian ranges of the Sudeten.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sudeten Lapland willow brush
description: Willow brush of the Sudeten dominated by the glacial relict [Salix lapponum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynio-Carpathian Silesian willow brush
description: Subalpine and montane willow brushes of the Sudeten, in the Krkonose and Hruby Jesenik, of the Northern Carpathians, in the Babia Gora, and of the Eastern and Southern Carpathians, dominated by the small or medium-small [Salix silesiaca], variously accompanied by [Alnus viridis], [Sorbus aucuparia], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Rubus idaeus], [Luzula sylvatica], [Luzula luzuloides], [Luzula alpinopilosa], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Calamagrostis villosa], of alpine and subalpine slopes and waterfalls, on siliceous soils with high moisture content.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynio-Carpathian small willow brush
description:
Willow brushes and dwarf shrub heaths of the Carpathians and the Sudeten dominated by small willows other than [Salix lapponum] or [Salix silesiaca], in particular by [Salix hastata], [Salix bicolor] or [Salix marrubifolia],
in particular, eastern Carpathian communities, of the subalpine and lower alpine level, developed on humid, calcareous slopes, dominated by [Salix hastata], with [Trisetum fuscum], [Festuca picta], [Hypericum alpigenum], [Deschampsia cespitosa] and [Rhododendron myrtifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern alpigenous willow brushes
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the Balkan Range, the Dinarides and the Hellenides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaride willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the Dinarides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the Balkan Range, dominated by [Salix waldsteiniana] or [Salix silesiaca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide willow brush
description: Thickets of shrubby willows of Vitosha, Rila, Pirin and Rhodope, dominated by [Salix lapponum], [Salix waldsteiniana] or other mountain willows.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide Lapland willow brush
description: Willow brush of Vitosha and Rila dominated by the glacial relict [Salix lapponum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide small willow brush
description: Subalpine or alpine brushes of low shrubby willows of Vitosha, Rila and Pirin, dominated by [Salix waldsteiniana] or [Salix hastata], the latter limited to Rila.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide tall willow brush
description: Tall or medium tall subalpine, alpine or montane brushes and thickets of shrubby willows of Vitosha, Rila, Pirin and Rhodope, dominated by [Salix silesiaca], [Salix appendiculata] (Rila only) or [Salix pentandra] (Vitosha only).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caucasian mountain willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the Pontic Range, the Caucasus and neighbouring ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of the Himalayan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern mountain willow brush
description: Subalpine, alpine and occasionally montane [Salix]-dominated brushes and low scrubs of Far Eastern mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal willow brush
description: Willow-dominated brushes of boreal mountains and mountainous regions, in particular of the Highlands of Scotland, the mountains of Iceland, the boreal mountains of Scandinavia, European Russia, Siberia, northern China, Korea and Japan. Mostly characteristic of a suprasylvatic belt in the lower arcto-alpine or oroboreal zone, they may extend into the taiga belt in exposed locations and edaphic enclaves, and ascend locally into the arcto-alpine zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scottish subarctic willow brush
description: Subarctic [Salix lapponum], [Salix lanata], [Salix arbuscula] or [Salix myrsinites] formations of ungrazed cliff ledges in the central and northern Highlands of Scotland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian montane willow brush
description: Willow-dominated formations of the subalpine and low alpine levels of the mountains of Scandinavia, dominated by [Salix glauca], [Salix hastata], [Salix lapponum], [Salix lanata], [Salix nigricans] ([Salix myrsinifolia]), [Salix phylicifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian montane tall herb willow brush
description: Low (to 2 m) thickets of the sub- and low alpine levels of the southern, central and northern mountains of Scandinavia composed of various species of low, prostrate willows, with alternating dominance, and an extensive, dense, variable, often species-rich herb layer the species composition of which is independent of the shrub layer. The willows may include [Salix glauca], [Salix hastata], [Salix lapponum], [Salix lanata], [Salix nigricans] ([Salix myrsinifolia]), [Salix phylicifolia]; the herb layer is dominated by [Geranium sylvaticum] with [Aconitum septentrionale], [Angelica archangelica], [Bartsia alpina], [Cicerbita alpina], [Cirsium helenioides], [Epilobium angustifolium], [Epilobium lactiflorum], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Geum rivale], [Lactuca alpina], [Melampyrum sylvaticum], [Myosotis sylvaticum], [Paris quadrifolia], [Polemonium caeruleum], [Pyrola minor], [Ranunculus acris], [Ranunculus repens], [Rhodiola rosea], [Rumex acetosa], [Veratrum album], [Viola biflora], [Polygonatum verticillatum], [Coeloglossum viride], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Deschampsia cespitosa]. Tall herb willow brushes occupy rich soils with near-surface water and need some snow cover. Formations on stony or gravelly slopes, with nutrient-poor substrates, may have an impoverished field layer, with almost bare soils; they are mostly located in the low and middle alpine levels.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian montane tufted hairgrass willow brush
description: Dense (to 2 m) thickets of level, regularly flooded sediments in the proximity of watercourses in high-rainfall areas of the sub- and low alpine levels of the southern, central and northern mountains of Scandinavia dominated by [Salix lanata] or [Salix phylicifolia], accompanied by [Salix nigricans] ([Salix myrsinifolia]), [Salix glauca], [Salix hastata], [Salix lapponum], [Betula pubescens], with a sparse field layer, occupying mainly openings, dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa] and [Filipendula ulmaria], with [Alchemilla glabra], [Alchemilla glomerulans], [Caltha palustris], [Paris quadrifolia], [Pedicularis sceptrum-carolinum], [Petasites frigidus], [Ranunculus auricomus], [Ranunculus repens], [Ranunculus reptans], [Rumex acetosa], [Trientalis europaeus], [Viola biflora], [Calamagrostis purpurea], [Calamagrostis stricta], [Deschampsia alpina], [Equisetum palustre].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian montane heath willow brush
description: Dense low (to 1 m) thickets of the low and middle alpine levels of the southern, central and northern mountains of Scandinavia dominated by [Salix glauca], accompanied by [Salix lapponum], [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia], with a heath and grass layer formed by [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Betula nana], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Hieracium alpinum], [Rumex acetosa], [Pyrola minor], [Trientalis europaea], [Cerastium alpinum], [Carex bigelowii], [Festuca ovina], with mosses and with lichens of genera [Cetraria] and [Cladonia]. These formations often occur as a wreath around windswept heaths, in more sheltered locations than those occupied by [Empetrum] heaths, mainly on north-facing slopes on stony, gravelly nutrient-poor sediments with some fine soil and high moisture, in conditions of some snow protection with early thaw.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic willow brush and heath
description: Thickets, scrubs and heaths of the mountains and lowlands of Iceland dominated by the medium-sized to small willows [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic tall herb willow brush
description: Willow thickets of Iceland, of low or medium stature, formed by [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia], [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii], with a tall herb, usually luxuriant, field layer. They are developed in the lowlands and in a few highland oases, colonizing in particular, small islands, islets, lake shores, river banks, streamsides, gullies, mostly in sheltered situations. The species cortŠge includes [Geranium sylvaticum], [Erysimum hieracifolium], [Angelica archangelica], [Alchemilla vulgaris], [Coeloglossum viride], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Deschampsia flexuosa], and, in the highlands, sometimes, [Leymus arenarius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic tufted hairgrass willow brush
description: Dense thickets of the lowlands of Iceland dominated by [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia] and [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]) developed on frequently inundatable sediments, primarily along lake shores and rivers, mainly in drier areas of the north central and northeastern regions, with a humid meadow species cortŠge in the herb layer, usually dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa] or [Filipendula ulmaria], often confined to openings within the thicket.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic willow-dwarf birch-bilberry brush
description: Thickets and scrubs of the lowlands of Iceland dominated by [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia], accompanied by [Betula nana], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], relatively low-growing, usually 0.5 to 1 m high. The herb layer may be rich in gramino‹ds, notably [Carex bigelowii], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Festuca vivipara], [Festuca richardsonii], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Calamagrostis stricta]. They may also colonize lava fields, with a ground layer dominated by carpets of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum]. Some communities are related to the [Betula nana]-[Juniperus]-[Vaccinium] heaths of unit 31.45519.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic dwarf willow heaths
description: Willow-dominated dwarf heaths of the highlands of Iceland, often fairly open,  with an upper layer that may not exceed 5 cm in height, and is usually less than 50 cm. A number of distinctive communities develop on sandy, gravelly or loess substrates. [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]) or [Salix lanata] can be the dominant shrub in the upper layer, the latter, in particular, on more sandy substrates. Frequent dominants or codominants in the lower layer are dwarf [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Carex bigelowii], [Dryas octopetala], [Salix herbacea] and, in particular, on sand deposits, [Festuca richardsonii] or [Armeria maritima]. Common associates may include dwarf [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Betula nana], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Polygonum viviparum], [Pedicularis flammea] and, in humidity-retaining areas, [Parnassia palustris], [Tofieldia pusilla], [Pinguicula alpina], [Calamagrostis neglecta], [Equisetum variegatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic prostrate willow mats
description: Willow-dominated formations of windswept detritic summits, slopes and plateaux of the highlands of Iceland, constituted, in a desert-like landscape, essentially of bare stony gravelly substrates, by scattered prostrate [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), associated with [Salix herbacea] and a few mostly cushion herbs, in particular, [Silene acaulis], [Thymus praecox] ssp. [arctica], [Armeria maritima], [Galium normanii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian willow brush
description: Subarctic low-alpine willow formations of the middle and southern Urals, with [Salix glauca], [Salix lapponum], [Salix glandulifera], [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian willow brush
description: Subarctic willow formations of the mountains of Siberia, with numerous species, in particular [Salix krylovii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland willow brush and heath
description: Thickets, scrubs and heaths of Greenland dominated by the medium-sized to small willows [Salix glauca] ([s.l.]), [Salix arctica]), [Salix arctophilia], up to 2 metre, occasionnally 3 metre, tall.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern British willow brush
description: Mixed [Salix aurita], [Salix atrocinerea], [Salix repens] and [Salix caprea]  scrub, with [Rumex acetosa], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Dryopteris spp.], [Oxalis acetosella], developed on ungrazed ledges, islands and gullies of Shetland, Orkney, Hebrides and the Northern Highlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine mixed brushes
description: Communities of the subalpine zone, of the tree-limit, and sometimes of the montane zone, of higher nemoral mountains of the western Alpine system and its associated ranges, dominated by tall or medium shrubs, for the most part Rosaceae species (of genera [Rubus], [Sorbus], [Amelanchier], [Potentilla]), [Betula] or tall [Vaccinium], often accompanied by tall herbs characteristic of the subalpine tall herb communities (unit 37.8), or by subalpine heaths, such as the [Juniperus nana]-[Arctostaphylos uva-ursi] heaths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine [Sorbus] brush
description: Thickets of the subalpine zone of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Jura, the Hercynian ranges, dominated by [Sorbus aucuparia] ssp. [glabrata], [Sorbus chamaemespilus], [Sorbus mougeotii], [Sorbus ambigua], [Sorbus austriaca] or other shrubby [Sorbus] species, in particular, tree-limit formations with [Betula carpatica], [Lonicera nigra], [Prunus padus] ssp. [borealis] ([Padus petraea]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine birch brush
description: Thickets or brushes of the subalpine zone of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Hercynian ranges, usually at the tree-limit, dominated by shrubby or krumholtz birches, in particular, [Betula carpatica], [Betula pubescens], often with [Sorbus aucuparia] ssp. [glabrata], [Lonicera nigra], [Prunus padus] ssp. [borealis] ([Padus petraea]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine bramble brush
description: Brushes of the subalpine zone of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Hercynian ranges, the Balkan Range, the Hellenides, dominated by [Rubus spp.], in particular, [Rubus idaeus], [Rubus saxatilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine cherry brush
description: Thickets or brushes of the subalpine zone of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Jura, the Hercynian ranges dominated by shrubby species of genus [Prunus] or related genera, in particular, [Prunus padus] ssp.
