description: Tall shrubby formations of the meso- and thermo-Mediterranean zones of the Iberian peninsula, France, Italy, the large western Mediterranean islands and Mediterranean North Africa with [Erica arborea], [Arbutus unedo], [Quercus ilex], [Phillyrea angustifolia], [Phillyrea media], [Viburnum tinus], [Rhamnus alaternus], [Juniperus oxycedrus], [Fraxinus ornus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Luso-Extremaduran high maquis
description: Western Mediterranean maquis with [Erica lusitanica], [Erica arborea], [Erica scoparia], [Cistus psilosepalus], [Cistus populifolius] developed in particular in the vicinity of lauriphyllus formations of ravines and water-course edges of the Montes de Toledo.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Mediterranean high maquis
description: Maquis of Greece and the Balkan peninsula, with [Erica arborea], [Arbutus unedo], [Arbutus andrachne], [Myrtus communis], [Pistacia terebinthus], [Phillyrea latifolia], [Juniperus oxycedrus], [Quercus coccifera], [Quercus ilex].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low ericaceous maquis
description: Lower (usually less than one metre) western Mediterranean maquis rich in [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica scoparia], [Erica cinerea] or sometimes low [Erica arborea], often accompanied by [Cistus spp.], [Lavandula stoechas] and various brooms.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall cistus maquis
description: Meso-, thermo- and occasionally supra-Mediterranean maquis of Iberia, southern France and western Mediterranean North Africa, in which the tall, large-flowered [Cistus ladanifer] is prominent. Included are more or less dense, homogeneous fields of [Cistus ladanifer], which can be identified by addition of digit 1 in the fourth decimal place of any of the subdivisions below, and more varied formations dominated by tall clumps of [Cistus ladanifer], which can be identified by addition of digit 2 in the fourth decimal place of these subdivisions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Iberian tall cistus maquis
description: [Cistus ladanifer]-dominated formations rich in gorses, spiny brooms or, occasionally, heathers, abundant on usually shallow soils in the thermo- and meso-Mediterranean zones of the southwest of the Iberian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Iberian tall cistus maquis
description: [Cistus ladanifer]-dominated formations with brooms, heathers and lavenders of siliceous soils, generally rather eroded and oligotrophic of the meso- and, locally, supra-Mediterranean zones of the Meseta, the Iberian Range and its satellites, the eastern Cordillera Central and southern Galicia and Leon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baetic tall cistus maquis
description: [Cistus ladanifer]-dominated formations of southern Andalusia, developed in siliceous or peridotite ranges in association with local Baetic floras.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tyrrhenian tall cistus maquis
description: Localized meso- and thermo-Mediterranean [Cistus ladanifer]-dominated formations of siliceous or decalcified soils and subhumid climates of the Tyrrhenian hinterland (crystalline Provence, Valencia), often with heath elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African tall cistus maquis
description: [Cistus ladanifer]-dominated formations of western mediterranean North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low cistus maquis
description: Western Mediterranean formations of small or medium [Cistus spp.], most characteristic of the siliceous soils of the meso-Mediterranean zone, but also widely occurring in the thermo-Mediterranean zone and in the siliceous supra-Mediterranean zone. Formations of mostly calciphile [Cistus] species (e.g. [Cistus albidus], [Cistus clusii]) and of indifferent species accompanied by strongly calciphile floras are listed under 32.4; formations of entirely thermo-Mediterranean species (e.g. [Cistus bourgaeanus], [Cistus palhinhae], [Cistus heterophyllus]) and of widespread species associated with co-dominant thermo-Mediterranean species have been listed under 32.2. Included here are all other formations; homogeneous, more or less dense cistus fields can be identified by addition of digit 1 in the fourth decimal place of the subdivisions below, more varied maquis of which the relevant cistus species is an essential element, by addition of digit 2 in the fourth decimal place of these subdivisions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus monspeliensis] maquis
description: Formations dominated by [Cistus monspeliensis], widespread in the Mediterranean region; homogeneous fields form in particular after fires.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus salvifolius] maquis
description: Formations dominated by [Cistus salvifolius], equally widespread, though less often dominant, in the entire Mediterranean region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus populifolius] maquis
description: Formations dominated by [Cistus populifolius], often taller, mainly of cooler, moister, shadier, siliceous or serpentine stations of the meso-Mediterranean zone of the southern half of the Iberian peninsula, in particular of Portugal, Extremadura, the Sierra Morena, the Montes de Toledo, the Iberian Range system, the mountains of Andalusia Occidental, entering in several areas into the supra- or thermo-Mediterranean zones and extending north locally to northern Iberia and Languedoc.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus laurifolius] maquis
description: Formations dominated by [Cistus laurifolius], often also of medium height, widespread on siliceous or decalcified soils in meso- and supra-Mediterranean Iberia and northwestern Africa, particularly in the [Quercus pyrenaica] realm, extending to the montane zone of the Pyrenees, and locally to sub-mediterranean areas of the southern Central Massif and the southwestern Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus psilosepalus] maquis
description: Formations dominated by [Cistus psilosepalus] of moist, lime-free soils of the western half of the Iberian peninsula, usually associated with southern heath elements, within the Atlantic influence, frequently located in depressions and gullies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus crispus] maquis
description: Formations of southern and eastern Iberia, southern France, western Sicily and Mediterranean North Africa dominated by [Cistus crispus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus incanus] maquis
description: [Cistus incanus] (including [Cistus incanus] ssp. [corsicus] and [Cistus incanus] ssp. [creticus]) formations of the Balearics, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, peninsular Italy and Mediterranean North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus albidus] maquis
description: Silicicolous formations with [Cistus albidus]. Most [Cistus albidus] formations have a pronounced garrigue character and should be listed under 32.4; however, some may be accompanied by a cortŠge so typical of silicolous maquis that they are better retained here.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low [Cistus-Lavandula stoechas] maquis
description: Usually varied west-Mediterranean maquis rich in [Lavandula stoechas], accompanied by [Cistus spp.], [Erica spp.], brooms ([Genista spp.], [Cytisus spp. i.a.]). The subspecies of [Lavandula stoechas] can be used to characterize regional groups of communities otherwise differing by the assembly of accompanying species. In all cases, pure or almost pure [Lavandula] formations can be identified by addition of digit 1 in the fourth decimal place, digit 2 denoting the varied formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean lavender maquis
description: Formations with [Lavandula stoechas] ssp. [stoechas] of northeastern Iberia, France, Italy and the west Mediterranean islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Iberian lavender maquis
description: Formations of central Iberia with [Lavandula stoechas] ssp. [pedemontana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Iberian lavender maquis
description: Formations of western Iberia with [Lavandula stoechas] ssp. [luisieri] or [Lavandula stoechas] ssp. [sampaiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low sparse maquis
description: Sparse, low silicicolous western Mediterranean maquis of [Helichrysum spp.], [Cistus spp.], [Erica spp.] physiognomically similar to calcicolous garrigues.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Broom-dominated maquis
description: Low, west-Mediterranean maquis dominated by leguminous shrubs ([Cytisus], [Teline], [Genista], [Adenocarpus], [Calicotome spinosa]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Genista hystrix] maquis
description: Formations, widespread in northwestern areas of the Iberian peninsula, with [Genista hystrix].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mixed brooms maquis
description: Leguminous formations, other than those dominated by [Genista hystrix], with numerous local variants.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western meso-mediterranean calcicolous garrigues
description: Shrubby formations, often low, on mostly calcareous soils of the meso- mediterranean zone of the Iberian peninsula, France, Italy and the large western Mediterranean islands, notably the Balearics, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, Malta and their satellites. Included here are those formations that reach their optimal development within the meso-mediterranean zone although they often enter the thermo- or supra-mediterranean levels. The subdivisions proposed are based on the physiognomically most significant dominants; co-dominance can be indicated by use of multiple codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Kermes oak garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin, usually relatively closed and tall, dominated by [Quercus coccifera] with no, or little, [Pistacia lentiscus] or other thermo-Mediterranean shrubs, very widespread in the meso-Mediterranean zone of the Iberian peninsula and southern France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rosemary garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin, usually relatively tall, dominated by [Rosmarinus officinalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cistus garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin, mostly meso-Mediterranean, but often also thermo- or supra-Mediterranean, dominated by the low, calciphilous [Cistus albidus] or [Cistus clusii], or occasionally by indifferent species, usually accompanied by a more varied flora than that of the silicicolous cistus maquis, though sometimes capable of forming dense cistus fields. These can be identified by use of digit 1 in the fourth decimal place, digit 2 being reserved for more varied formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus albidus] garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Cistus albidus], widespread in Iberia, France, the Balearics and Liguria, with local stations in other parts of northern Italy, in Corsica and Sardinia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cistus clusii] garrigues
description: Formations of [Cistus clusii], mostly widespread in rather warm, dry areas of the southern and eastern parts of the Iberian peninsula and in the Balearics, with a very limited representation on Monte Gargano, in Calabria, and in Sicily.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [C. monspeliensis, C. salvifolius, C. incanus] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the western Mediterranean basin with [Cistus monspeliensis], [Cistus salvifolius] or [Cistus incanus]. Many formations of these species are maquis or maquis-like communities, best listed under 32.3. Some, however, with a pronounced calciphile character and a garrigue structure, can be listed here.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spurge garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by bushy or robust perennial [Euphorbia] species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spiny spurge garrigues
description: [Euphorbia spinosa] or [Euphorbia melitensis] cushion garrigues of very dry soils of the meso- or thermo-Mediterranean zones of southern France, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, the Maltese Islands and peninsular Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Unarmed spurge garrigues
description: Formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by often woody-stocked, clump-forming [Euphorbia] species (e.g. [Euphorbia fragifera], [Euphorbia characias]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Prostrate juniper garrigues
description: Meso-Mediterranean garrigues of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Juniperus oxycedrus] or other low, shrubby junipers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lavender garrigues
description: Meso-, or sometimes thermo-, mediterranean garrigues of the western Mediterranean basin rich in calciphile [Lavandula latifolia] or, occasionally, [Lavandula angustifolia]; almost pure fields of [Lavandula latifolia] may form, in particular, as a facies of calcareous grasslands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lavender stands
description: Homogeneous, or almost homogeneous, [Lavandula latifolia] stands invading grasslands of the western Mediterranean basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lavender mixed garrigues
description: [Lavendula]-dominated formations of the western Mediterranean basin in which the main constituting species is accompanied by a varied cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western sage and other labiate garrigues
description: Garrigues of the western Mediterranean basin of which the main components are labiate shrubs or robust perennials (except [Lavandula] and [Rosmarinus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thyme, sage, small germander and other labiate garrigues
description: Characteristically very low, open garrigues of the western Mediterranean basin of which the main components are labiate shrubs of genera [Thymus] (e.g. [Thymus piperella], [Thymus funkii], [Thymus zygis], [Thymus vulgaris], [Thymus capitatus], [Thymus mastigophorus]), [Salvia] (e.g. [Salvia lavandulifolia], [Salvia officinalis]), [Teucrium] (e.g. [Teucrium polium], [Teucrium marum], [Teucrium subspinosum], [Teucrium aragonense], [Teucrium gnaphalodes], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Teucrium montanum]), [Sideritis] (e.g. [Sideritis scordioides], [Sideritis incana]), [Micromeria] (e.g. [Micromeria fruticosa], [Micromeria graeca], [Micromeria juliana]), [Satureja] (e.g. [Satureja montana]), [Stachys] (e.g. [Stachys glutinosa]), [Nepeta] (e.g. [Nepeta foliosa]) [Phlomis] (e.g. [Phlomis fruticosa]) or other genera (except [Lavandula] and [Rosmarinus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western tree germander garrigues
description: Garrigues of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by the tall or very tall [Teucrium fruticans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Genista] garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin characterized by the abundance of small, spiny brooms such as [Genista scorpius], [Genista hispanica], [Genista corsica], [Genista lucida].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Genista scorpius, G. hispanica] garrigues
description: [Genista]-rich garrigues of southern France and Spain, dominated by [Genista scorpius] or [Genista hispanica]; some Meseta formations are listed under unit 31.7 (hedgehog-heaths) or unit 32.6.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Genista corsica] garrigues
description: [Genista]-rich garrigues of Corsica and Sardinia, dominated by [Genista corsica]; many formations are hedgehog-heaths (unit 32.7).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Genista lucida] garrigues
description: [Genista]-rich garrigues of Mallorca dominated by [Genista lucida].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Calicotome] garrigues
description: Meso-Mediterranean shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Calicotome spinosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Composite garrigues
description: Meso-Mediterranean shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by members of various genera of the family Asteraceae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Helichrysum, Santolina, Phagnalon] garrigues
description: Usually low, open garrigues of the western Mediterranean basin formed by dwarf, shrubby composites, often with small grey or whitish leaves and showy yellow bloom, of genera [Helichrysum], [Staehelina] ([Staehelina dubia]), [Phagnalon] ([Phagnalon rupestre]), [Santolina], [Scorzonera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Artemisia] garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by the usually small-leaved and inconspicuously flowering species of genus [Artemisia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aromatic inula garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by the invasive [Inula viscosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Medium tall composite garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by large composites other than [Helichrysum] and their relatives (genera [Helichrysum], [Staehelina], [Phagnalon], [Santolina], [Scorzonera]), wormwoods ([Artemisia]) or inulas ([Inula viscosa]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Erica] garrigues
description: Meso-Mediterranean shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by the calciphile heathers [Erica multiflora] or [Erica manipuliflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Globularia] garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Globularia alypum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Helianthemum] and [Fumana] garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by small or dwarf shrubs of the genera [Helianthemum] (e.g. [Helianthemum asperum], [Helianthemum pilosum], [Helianthemum oelandicum], [Helianthemum marifolium], [Helianthemum cinereum], [Helianthemum lavandulifolium], [Helianthemum nummularium], [Helianthemum caput-felis]) or [Fumana] (e.g. [Fumana ericoides], [Fumana laevipes], [Fumana thymifolia]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gromwell garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Lithodora fruticosa], distributed in Spain and southern France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Thymelaea] garrigues
description: Meso-Mediterranean shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin rich in shrubs of genus [Thymelaea] (e.g. [Thymelaea tinctoria], [Thymelaea nitida], [Thymelaea pubescens]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Bupleurum] garrigues
description: Often tall, sometimes very tall, dense shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Bupleurum fruticosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gorse garrigues
description: Meso-Mediterranean shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Ulex parviflorus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Restharrow garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Ononis fruticosa], limited to Iberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Anthyllis] garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Anthyllis cytisoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Dictamnus] garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Dictamnus albus] ([Dictamnus hispanicus]), characteristic of stony terrains of eastern Spain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern garrigues
description: Shrubby formations, often low, of the meso-, thermo- and occasionally supramediterranean zones of continental Greece, its archipelagoes, of Cyprus, Asia Minor and the Levant, of extreme southern Albania in the Butrintit Lake basin. Included here are all sclerophyllous formations, regardless of substrate, except those with conspicuous cushion structure (phryganas [s.s.], listed in unit 33, and hedgehog-heaths, listed in unit 31.7), those with abundant [Pistacia lentiscus], [Myrtus communis] or other thermo-Mediterranean brush elements ([Phillyrea spp.], [Erica manipuliflora], [Styrax officinalis], [Genista fasselata], [Euphorbia dendroides], [Calicotome villosa], [Sarcopoterium spinosum]) listed in unit 32.2 and high maquis with [Erica arborea] and [Arbutus spp.], listed in unit 32.3. The subdivisions proposed are based on the physiognomically most significant dominants; codominance can be indicated by use of multiple codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern kermes oak garrigues
description: Shrub communities of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland, usually relatively closed and tall, dominated by [Quercus coccifera] with no, or little, [Pistacia lentiscus] or other thermo-mediterranean shrubs; kermes oak garrigues are by far the most widespread xerophyllous shrub formations in the eastern meso-mediterranean zone. They are also well represented in the supra-Mediterranean and thermo-Mediterranean zones. Formations pertaining to the latter, when rich in other, more restrictively thermophile shrubs, have been listed as unit 32.2193.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern rosemary garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland, usually relatively tall, dominated by [Rosmarinus officinalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Cistus] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by or rich in [Cistus] species. Dense cistus fields can be identified by use of digit 1 in the fourth decimal place, digit 2 being reserved for more varied formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Cistus incanus] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by the low to medium-tall, large-flowered, pink [Cistus incanus] ssp. [incanus] or [Cistus incanus] ssp. [creticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Cistus parviflorus] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland, usually low, dominated by the small-flowered, deep pink [Cistus parviflorus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Cistus salvifolius] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by the low to medium-tall, white-flowered, [Cistus salvifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Cistus monspeliensis] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by the usually medium-tall, white-flowered, [Cistus monspeliensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern spurge garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by bushy or robust perennial [Euphorbia] species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern spiny spurge garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian and Aegean coastlands and hinterland rich in the spiny, cushion-forming [Euphorbia acanthothamnos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern unarmed spurge garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by, or rich in often woody-stocked, clump-forming [Euphorbia] species (e.g. [Euphorbia characias] ssp. [wulfenii], [Euphorbia rigida]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern prostrate juniper garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by low, shrubby [Juniperus oxycedrus], [Juniperus communis] or [Juniperus phoenicea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern lavender garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland rich in [Lavandula stoechas] or, occasionally, [Lavandula angustifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern sage and other labiates garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland of which the main components are labiate shrubs or robust perennials (except [Lavandula] and [Rosmarinus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern tree germander garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by the tall or very tall [Teucrium fruticans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Jerusalem sage garrigues
description: Fairly tall garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by [Phlomis fruticosa]. Very degraded habitats occupied by almost monospecific fields of this species can be listed under 32.9.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Salvia] and [Stachys] garrigues
description: Fairly tall garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by shrubs or woody perennials of genera [Salvia] (e.g. [Salvia triloba], [Salvia argentea], [Salvia eichlerana], [Salvia pomifera]), [Stachys] (e.g. [Stachys cretica]) or others.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern dwarf labiate garrigues
description: Low, open garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland formed by dwarf shrubs or perennials of genera [Thymus] (e.g. [Thymus capitatus], [Thymus teucrioides], [Thymus atticus], [Thymus sibthorpii], [Thymus striatus], [Thymus comptus]), [Teucrium] (e.g. [Teucrium polium]), [Sideritis] (e.g. [Sideritis syriaca], [Sideritis clandestina]), [Micromeria] (e.g. [Micromeria juliana], [Micromeria graeca]), [Phlomis] (e.g. [Phlomis cretica], [Phlomis floccosa], [Phlomis lanata]) or others.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Christ's thorn eastern garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by [Paliurus spina-christi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern broom garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland characterized by the abundance of broom-like shrubs of genera [Genista], [Chamaecytisus], [Teline] or others.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Ebenus] brushes
description: Garrigues of Crete dominated by [Ebenus cretica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Helichrysum] and other composite garrigues
description: Usually low, open garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland formed by dwarf, shrubby composites of genera [Helichrysum], [Phagnalon] ([Phagnalon graecum]), [Scorzonera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Erica] garrigues
description: Mesomediterranean garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by the heather [Erica manipuliflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Andrachne garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland characterized by their richness in low bushes of [Arbutus andrachne].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Globularia] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by [Globularia alypum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Helianthemum] and [Fumana] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland dominated by small or dwarf shrubs of the genera [Helianthemum] or [Fumana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Thymelaea] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland rich in shrubs of genus [Thymelaea] (e.g. [Thymelaea tartonraira]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Bupleurum] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the eastern Ionian, Aegean and eastern Mediterranean coastlands and hinterland, dense and often tall, sometimes very tall, dominated by [Bupleurum fruticosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean garrigues
description: Low shrub formations with pronounced Mediterranean affinities formed as a degradation stage of thermophile deciduous forests ([Quercion pubescentis], [Ostryo-Carpinion]) or sometimes of [Quercus rotundifolia] forests in the supra-Mediterranean belt of the Mediterranean basin. Included here are only those formations that are characteristic of the supra-Mediterranean level; formations, particularly of the lower supra-Mediterranean, that are closely related to meso-Mediterranean communities have been included under units 32.4 and 32.5.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: True-lavender garrigues
description: Montane formations dominated by [Lavandula angustifolia] ("[Lavandula vera]") with [Genista cinerea] ssp. [cinerea], [Buxus sempervirens] (both sometimes co-dominant), [Astragalus purpureus], [Onobrychis supina], [Satureja montana], [Artemisia alba], [Catananche caerulea], [Aphyllanthes monspeliensis], [Thymus vulgaris] characteristic of great surfaces of the supra-Mediterranean level of southwestern Alps of France, also occurring on the southern flanks of the Pyrenees in northern Spain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Genista cinerea] garrigues
description: Supra-Mediterranean garrigues or grasslands of the southwestern Alps, Haute Provence, the southern Central Massif, the CorbiŠres and the eastern Pyrenees dominated by [Genista cinerea] ssp. [cinerea], including the broom-rich facies of the French lavender garrigues and the White Quercy broom-fields.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-Gallic supramediterranean dwarf-shrub garrigues
description: Low frutescent or suffrutescent formations of the supra-Mediterranean levels of the Iberian Meseta and its surrounding mountains and of northern Spain and southern France, rich in small labiate shrubs of genera [Thymus], [Teucrium], [Salvia], [Satureja], [Sideritis], [Lavandula], accompanied by leguminous shrubs ([Genista scorpius], [Genista pilosa], [Genista pseudopilosa], [Genista cinerea] ssp. [speciosa], [Coronilla minima], [Dorycnium pentaphyllum] ssp. [pentaphyllum]) and various grasses ([Stipa spp.], [Brachypodium spp.]). In the north they often have an important, sometimes predominant, grass element and their impoverished shrub component is sometimes reduced to an almost monospecific [Thymus] formation; southwards, they become progressively more dominated by a richer constellation of shrub species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean labiate garrigues
description: Supra-Mediterranean dwarf-shrub formations of the Iberian Meseta, its surrounding mountains, northern Spain and southern France, dominated by labiate shrubs or subshrubs of genera [Thymus] ([Thymus serpolifolium], [Thymus vulgaris], [Thymus loscosii], [Thymus mastigophorus]), [Teucrium] ([Teucrium aureum], [Teucrium aragonense], [Teucrium gnaphalodes], [Teucrium polium]), [Salvia] ([Salvia lavandulifolia], [Salvia phlomoides]), [Satureja] ([Satureja montana]), [Sideritis] ([Sideritis incana]), [Lavandula] ([Lavandula angustifolia], [Lavandula lanata], [Lavandula latifolia]), often constituting a species-rich assemblage, but, mostly in the north, sometimes limited to one or a few species of [Thymus]; associated shrubs often include greenweeds ([Genista spp.]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean greenweed garrigues
description: Supra-Mediterranean labiate and pea dwarf-shrub formations of the Iberian Meseta, its surrounding mountains, northern Spain and southern France, dominated by [Genista scorpius], [Genista pilosa], [Genista pseudopilosa] or [Genista cinerea] ssp. [speciosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean [Dorycnium] garrigues
description: [Dorycnium pentaphyllum] ssp. [pentaphyllum] ([Dorycnium suffruticosum])-dominated formations of the supra-Mediterranean [Quercus pubescens] zones of the Garonne gap and neighbouring regions of southwestern France, characteristic, in particular of the calcareous molasses of Gascony where they invade [Bromion] grasslands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supramediterranean box scrub
description: [Buxus sempervirens] thickets of the supramediterranean zone, occurring as facies within several formations of southern France such as true-lavender garrigues (unit 32.61) and supramediterranean steppic grassland complexes (unit 34.7), in northeastern Spanish ranges, in isolated stations of the Apennines and in Corsica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italic supramediterranean garrigues
description: Characteristically supramediterranean garrigues of Italy and the large central Mediterranean islands. In the supra-Mediterranean level of Italy and the large central Mediterranean islands, the substitution stages of the thermophile deciduous forests are mostly grasslands or shrubby grasslands, hedgehog heaths, deciduous shrubs, semimaquis or occasionally embryonic garrigues that differ little from those of the mesomediterranean level. A few formations, in particular with labiates of genera [Thymus], [Teucrium], [Salvia], [Lavandula] and others, with [Helichrysum spp.] or with [Euphorbia spp.], may warrant separate listing under this heading.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan peninsula supramediterranean garrigues
description: Formations of the supramediterranean level and submediterranean areas of the Balkan peninsula dominated by sclerophyllous shrubs or subshrubs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan peninsula supramediterranean shrub garrigues
description: Formations of the supramediterranean level and submediterranean areas of the Balkan peninsula dominated by sclerophyllous shrubs, impoverished irradiations of the communities of units 32.32 and 32.5, in particular unit 32.51. Included are, notably, the [Phillyrea latifolia] and [Quercus coccifera] thickets or scrubs of the middle Struma-Strimon and Mesta-Nestos valleys of Bulgaria, when monodominated by these species, as well as some [Buxus sempervirens]- or [Juniperus oxycedrus]-dominated formations of the supramediterranean [Ostryo-Carpinion aegeicum] region of northern Greece, southern Albania and the southern F.Y.R. of Macedonia; most of the communities that include them also comprise, however, a substantial admixture of deciduous species and thus belong to unit 32.7.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan peninsula supramediterranean subshrub garrigues
description: Formations of the supramediterranean [Ostryo-Carpinion aegeicum] zone of the southern Balkan peninsula, in particular, of northern Greece and the southern  F.Y.R. of Macedonia, dominated by subshrubs associated with supramediterranean dry grassland elements and generally forming a mosa‹c with such grasslands; they include, notably [Satureja montana] grassy, stony scrubs and [Genista nissana] heaths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pseudomaquis
description: Mixed sclerophyllous evergreen and deciduous shrub thickets of the periphery of the range of Mediterranean sclerophyllous scrublands. They include, in particular, shrub formations of the Balkan and Italic peninsulas intermediate between Mediterranean maquis and schibljak, resulting from the degradation of the [Ostryo-Carpinion], with a mixture of evergreen and deciduous bushes including [Quercus coccifera], [Juniperus oxycedrus], [Quercus trojana], [Carpinus orientalis], [Ostrya carpinifolia], [Pistacia terebinthus], [Buxus sempervirens], [Berberis cretica], [Paliurus spina-christi], [Pyrus spinosa], [Rosa spp.], similar Iberian formations with [Amelanchier ovalis], [Prunus lusitanica], [Ilex aquifolium], French and Italian formations with [Quercus pubescens] and [Quercus ilex], formations of Mediterranean Asia Minor and the Levant dominated by mixed deciduous and evergreen shrubs or small trees, in particular, [Quercus coccifera] ([Quercus calliprinos]) and [Pistacia palaestina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic pseudomaquis
description: Shrub formations intermediate between Mediterranean maquis and schibljak, resulting from the degradation of the [Ostryo-Carpinion] of the Helleno-Balkanic peninsula, distributed in particular in northern Greece, in the Maritsa, Tundja, Mesta, Struma and Vardar valleys of Bulgaria and the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, in the Lake Ohrid basin of Albania, along the Black Sea coasts of Bulgaria, and in the eastern Adriatic hills of Albania, Yugoslavia and Croatia, with a mixture of evergreen and deciduous bushes including [Quercus coccifera], [Juniperus oxycedrus], [Juniperus excelsa], [Quercus trojana], [Carpinus orientalis], [Ostrya carpinifolia], [Pistacia terebinthus], [Pistacia atlantica], [Berberis cretica], [Paliurus spina-christi], [Pyrus spinosa], [Buxus sempervirens], [Phillyrea media], [Prunus spinosa], [Prunus lusitanica], [Laurus nobilis], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Jasminum fruticans], [Crataegus monogyna], [Crataegus pycnoloba], [Pyracantha coccinea], [Rosa sempervirens], [Rubus ulmifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italo-French pseudomaquis
description: French and Italian mixed sclerophyllous evergreen and deciduous shrub formations dominated by [Quercus pubescens] and [Quercus ilex].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian pseudomaquis
description: Mixed sclerophyllous evergreen and deciduous shrub formations of Iberia, with [Amelanchier ovalis], [Prunus lusitanica], [Ilex aquifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian pseudomaquis
description: Formations of Mediterranean Asia Minor and the Levant dominated by mixed deciduous and evergreen shrubs or small trees, in particular, [Quercus coccifera] ([Quercus calliprinos]) and [Pistacia palaestina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermo-Atlantic xerophytic communities
description: Xerophytic scrub formations of the lower slopes of the Canary Islands, Madeira, the Salvagen Islands, the Cape Verde Islands and the western North African mediterraneo-Saharan transition zone rich in succulents, in particular cactiform or dendroid spurges [Euphorbia spp.], rosette-forming [Aeonium spp.] and composites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Canarian spurge communities
description: Open, varied formations of arid, stony slopes of the lower, 0-700 m, level of the western and central Canarian islands, characterized by the abundance of fleshy-stemmed, aphyllous, or small-leafed species, in particular [Euphorbia spp.], [Senecio kleinia], [Periploca laevigata], [Cneorum pulverulentum], [Messerschmidia fruticosa], [Echium giganteum], [Convolvulus floridus], [Allagopappus dichotomus], [Rhamnus crenulata], [Rubia fruticosa], [Argyranthemum spp.], [Artemisia canariensis], [Sonchus leptocephalus], [Asparagus arborescens], [Rumex lunaria], [Micromeria spp.], [Paronychia canariensis.]. They constitute a Macaronesian representation of the coastal desert formations of northwest Africa, listed under unit 74.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cardonales
description: Xerophytic scrub communities of the Canary Islands dominated by the cactiform spurge [Euphorbia canariensis] and [Aeonium percarneum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spurge tabaibales
description: Xerophytic scrub communities of the Canary Islands dominated by the tree-like spurges [Euphorbia aphylla], [Euphorbia obtusifolia], [Euphorbia balsamifera], [Euphorbia atropurpurea], [Euphorbia bravoana], [Euphorbia regis-jubae], [Euphorbia bourgaeana], [Euphorbia berthelotii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Kleinia tabaibales
description: Xerophytic scrub communities of the Canary Islands dominated by [Senecio kleinia] ([Kleinia neriifolia]), [Sonchus spp.] or other composites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dragon tree communities
description: Xerophytic scrub communities of the Canary Islands in which the forest relict [Dracaena draco] is present.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cneorum] cushion communities
description: Xerophytic scrub communities of the Canary Islands with [Neochamaelea pulverulenta] ([Cneorum pulverulentum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Plocama] communities
description: Xerophytic scrub communities of the Canary Islands with [Plocama pendula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Canarian saxicolous formations
description: Xerophytic scrub communities of the Canary Islands colonizing hard rock faces, lava flows and ravine walls within the xerophytic zone of the western and central Canary Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Canarian saxicolous labiate communities
description: Canary Island communities of small ligneous plants colonizing hard, dry rocks with [Micromeria spp.], [Lavandula canariensis], [Lavandula pinnata], and the fern [Cheilanthes catanensis] ([Cosentinia vellea], [Notholaena vellea]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cardoncillo communities
description: Formations colonizing lava flows, with the succulent asclepiad cardoncillos [Ceropegia dichotoma] and [Ceropegia fusca], [Phagnalon purpurascens] and [Sonchus leptocephalus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Canarian crassulid communities
description: Formations of dry, less sunny rocks dominated by succulent crassulids ([Aeonium spp.], [Greenovia spp.]) with [Sonchus gummifer], [Sonchus radiatus], [Picridium ligulatum], [Lavandula abrotanoides], [Asparagus scoparius], [Hypericum reflexum], [Lavatera acerifolia], [Lavatera phoenicea], [Vieraea laevigata] and many lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Canarian xerophytic communities
description: Open formations of semidesertic Fuerteventura and Lanzarote, with high endemism; characteristic of various groupings are [Euphorbia obtusifolia], [Senecio kleinia], [Asparagus pastorianus], [Kickxia heterophylla], [Echium bonnetii], [Caralluma burchardii], the cactiform spurge [Euphorbia handiensis], [Pulicaria burchardii], [Pulicaria canariensis], [Argyranthemum winteri], [Echium handiense], [Bupleurum handiense], [Sideritis massoniana], [Asteriscus sericeus], [Asteriscus schultzii], [Minuartia platiphylla], [Reichardia famarae], [Aichryson tortuosum], [Aeonium lancerottense], [Aeonium balsamiferum], [Limonium bourgaei], [Echium decaisnei] ssp. [purpuriense], [Argyranthemum ochroleucum], [Helichrysum gossypium], [Helichrysum monogynum], [Ferula lancerottensis], [Sedum lancerottense], [Thymus origanoides], [Lavandula pinnata], [Echium pitardii], [Limonium puberulum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian [Launaea] scrub
description: Steppic grasslands of the Canary Islands invaded and dominated by [Launaea arborescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Madeiran spurge formations
description: Shrubby formations of the low slopes (0-350 m) of Madeira with [Euphorbia piscatoria], [Globularia salicina], [Phyllis nobla], [Myrtus communis], [Chamaemeles coriacea], [Rubus ulmifolius], [Olea europaea] var. [maderensis], [Bencomia caudata], [Echium nervosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Madeiran saxicolous formations
description: Formations colonizing rocks and volcanic ash deposits in the xerophytic zone of Madeira with [Aeonium glutinosum], [Plantago arborescens] ssp. [maderensis], [Helichrysum spp.], [Sonchus ustulatus], [Phagnalon spp.], [Tolpis fruticosa], [Sedum brissemoretii], [Davallia canariensis] or [Musschia aurea] and [Aeonium glandulosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Desertas dry scrub
description: Formation with Madeiran endemics [Artemisia argentata], [Calendula maderensis], [Andryala glandulosa], [Jasminum odoratissimum] and introduced plants.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cape Verde spurge communities
description: Xerophytic scrubs and thickets of the Cape Verde Islands dominated by succulents, in particular the candalabra-shaped pachycaul dendroid [Euphorbia tuckeyana], accompanied by the pachycaul candelabra bugloss [Echium hypertropicum], and the small tree or shrub [Sideroxylon marmulano], with the lianas [Periploca laevigata] and [Sarcostema daltonii]. The three arborescent componants are in severe regression or in danger of extinction.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African spurge communities
description: Communities of the western Mediterraneo-Saharan transition zone, under strong Atlantic influence, dominated by tall cactiform or pachycaul dendroid spurges of genus [Euphorbia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Euphorbia resinifera] succulent shrubland
description: Communities of the mediterraneo-Saharan transition steppes and semideserts zone of northwestern Morocco dominated by the cactiform spurge [Euphorbia resinifera], often alone or with very scattered participation of larger woody plants, such as [Acacia gummifera], [Ceratonia siliqua], [Chamaerops humulis], [Olea europea], [Pistachia lentiscus], [Tetraclinis articulata], [Ziziphus lotus], with a cortŠge of smaller species composed typically of Mediterranean genera, located on shallow, often calcareous lithosols in areas north of the Great Atlas, mainly on the lower slopes of the western Middle Atlas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Euphorbia beaumierana] succulent shrubland
description: Communities of the mediterraneo-Saharan transition steppes and semideserts zone of northwestern Morocco dominated by the cactiform spurge [Euphorbia officinarum] var. [beaumierana], distributed mostly in the coastal [Argania] woodland zone, extending from 100 km south of Essaouira to the Souss, slightly south of Agadir, typically occupying steep, rocky slopes leading to the sea, or windswept, stony cliff tops, often with a few scattered, low, shrubby, windclipped woody species, in particular, [Acacia gummifera], [Argania spinosa], [Ceratonia siliqua], [Maytenis senegalensis], [Olea europea], [Phillyrea angustifolia], [Pistachia lentiscus], and sometimes the 2-metre tall soft-stemmed pachycaulous [Aeolium arboreum] and [Sonchus pinnatifidus], as well as climbers, [Periploca laevigata], succulent-stemmed [Senecio anteuphorbium], and small shrubs, [Helianthemum canariense], [Lavandula dentata], [Lavandula maroccana], [Lavandula multifida], [Withania fruticans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: African [Euphorbia regis-jubae] succulent shrubland
description: Communities of cliffs and ravines of the southern Moroccan coasts dominated by the pachycaul tree spurge [Euphorbia obtusifolia] ssp. [regis-jubae], characteristic of the zone of transition between mediterranean formations and coastal desert communities of the Atlantic Sahara, distributed between Safi and the western Anti-Atlas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Euphorbia echinus] succulent shrubland
description: Communities of the mediterraneo-Saharan transition steppes and semideserts zone of northwestern Morocco dominated by the cactiform spurge [Euphorbia echinus], mostly distributed in the coastlands, rarer in the interior, characteristic of the southern part of the mediterraneo-Saharan transition region, south of the Oued Souss, extending far south in the coastal desert belt, south to Cap Blanc in Mauritania, most common between the Oued Noun and the Oued Dra, occupying rocky hillsides and pebbly or gravelly lower slopes, on permeable soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ermes
description: Communities of forbs, grasses and shrubs resulting from over-browsing and over-grazing of garrigues and consisting of unpalatable plants, in particular Liliaceae ([Asphodelus], [Urginea]), thistles ([Carthamus], [Carlina], [Centaurea], [Onopordum]), [Phlomis], [Ferula], especially characteristic of the more arid areas of the Mediterranean basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Asphodel fields
description: Communities of degraded terrains of the Mediterranean basin overwhelmingly dominated by facies-forming Liliaceae of genus [Asphodelus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thistle fields
description: Communities of degraded terrains of the Mediterranean basin overwhelmingly dominated by facies-forming thistles, notably of genera [Carthamus], [Carlina], [Centaurea], [Onopordum], [Notobasis], [Galactites].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Phlomis brushes
description: Communities of degraded terrains of the Mediterranean basin overwhelmingly dominated by facies-forming tall labiates of genus [Phlomis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ferula stands
description: Communities of degraded terrains of the Mediterranean basin dominated by facies-forming tall, robust umbellifers of genus [Ferula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spanish-broom fields
description: Thickets and brushes of Spanish broom, [Spartium junceum], widespread in mediterranean and sub-mediterranean areas of the Mediterranean basin, particularly in western Mediterranean Europe and North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian garrigues
description: Shrubby formations, often low, of the meso- and occasionally supra-Mediterranean zones of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula from Istria to southern Albania. Included here are all sclerophyllous formations, regardless of substrate, except high maquis with [Erica arborea] and [Arbutus spp.], listed in unit 32.3. The subdivisions proposed are based on the physiognomically most significant dominants; codominance can be indicated by use of multiple codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian kermes oak garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula dominated by [Quercus coccifera], of limited distribution.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian rosemary garrigues
description: [Rosmarinus officinalis]-dominated communities of the Dalmatian coast and its islands, in particular, Hvar, Brac, Solta, Vis.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Cistus] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula dominated by [Cistus incanus] ssp. [creticus], [Cistus monspeliensis] or [Cistus salvifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Cistus incanus] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula dominated by [Cistus incanus] ssp. [creticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Cistus salvifolius] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula dominated by [Cistus salvifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Cistus monspeliensis] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula dominated by [Cistus monspeliensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian spurge garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands and hills of the Balkan peninsula dominated by the spiny cushions of [Euphorbia spinosa] or by nonspiny often woody-stocked, clump-forming species of [Euphorbia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian spiny spurge garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Dalmatian coast dominated by [Euphorbia spinosa], reaching altitudes of 1000 m and higher.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian unarmed spurge garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands and hills of the Balkan peninsula dominated by often woody-stocked, clump-forming [Euphorbia] species (e.g. [Euphorbia nicaeenisis]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian prostrate juniper garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands and hills of the Balkan peninsula dominated by low, shrubby [Juniperus oxycedrus] or [Juniperus phoenicea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian sage and other labiates garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands and hills of the Balkan peninsula of which the main components are labiate shrubs or robust perennials (except [Rosmarinus]), in particular [Salvia officinalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian Christ's thorn garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands and hills of the Balkan peninsula dominated by [Paliurus spina-christi], characteristic, in particular, of Inner Istria, of Ravni Kotari, of the lower reaches of the Neretva and of Herzegovina. [Punica granatum] is a frequent component.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian broom garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula dominated by leguminous shrubs, in particular by [Calicotome villosa], [Genista sericea] var. [rigida], [Genista sylvestris] ssp. [michelii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Helichrysum] and other composite garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands and hills of the Balkan peninsula formed by dwarf, shrubby composites of genus [Helichrysum] and related genera, in particular, [Scorzonera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Erica] garrigues
description: Garrigues of the Adriatic lowlands of the Balkan peninsula dominated by [Erica manipuliflora] or sometimes [Erica multiflora].
