source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxinian garrigues
description: Shrubby formations of the Mediterranean enclaves of the Black Sea coasts, in Crimea, southern Bulgaria, Turkey-in-Europe and northern Anatolia, as well as of the Mediterraneo-steppic zone of southern Thrace. Included here are all sclerophyllous formations, regardless of substrate, except high maquis with [Erica arborea] and [Arbutus spp.], listed in 32.3 and Phryganas, listed in 33.B.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean garrigues
description: Sclerophyte shrub communities of Mediterranean southern Crimea, with, in particular, [Cistus incanus] ssp. [incanus] ([Cistus tauricus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South-Euxinian garrigues
description: Sclerophyte shrub communities of Mediterranean enclaves along the Black Sea coast of Anatolia, with [Cistus incanus] ssp. [creticus], [Cistus salvifolius], [Arbutus andrachne], [Arbutus unedo], [Erica arborea], [Jasminum fruticans], [Myrtus communis], [Laurus nobilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian garrigues
description: Sclerophyte shrub communities of the Mediterraneo-steppic Evros-Merich-Maritsa and Ergene river basins of southern Thrace and of Mediterranean enclaves along the Black Sea coast of the Stranja and of Turkey-in-Europe, with [Cistus incanus] ssp. [creticus], [Cistus salvifolius], [Jasminum fruticans], [Phillyrea latifolia], [Quercus coccifera], [Asparagus acutifolius], [Asparagus verticillatus], [Paliurus spina-christi], [Anemone pavonina]. They extend northward to Harmanli on the Maritsa, and to Varna on the Black Sea coast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-steppic brushes
description: Sclerophyllous scrubs of the transition belts between the Mediterranean zone and the Irano-Turanian or pre-Saharan steppes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African mediterraneo-steppic brushes and scrubs
description: Sclerophyllous brushes and scrubs of the transition belts between the mediterranean zone of North Africa and the pre-Saharan steppes or semi-deserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African pre-desert brushes
description: Brushes with [Periploca laevigata], [Withania frutescens], [Pistacia lentiscus], [Chamaerops humilis], [Rhus pentaphylla], [Tetraclinis articulata] of the upper arid (Mediterranean arid) zone of North Africa. Communities of unit 32.25 are, in part, European outposts of this unit.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African mediterraneo-steppic garrigues
description: Open, often very sparse and lacunar, garrigues of mediterranean affinities of the upper arid (in part), middle arid and lower arid (in part) zones of North Africa, mostly dominated by [Thymus capitatus] ([Coridothymus capitatus]) or by [Rosmarinus officinalis], also by [Thymus algeriensis], [Globularia alypum], [Cistus clusii] or [Fumana thymifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian mediterraneo-steppic brushes
description: Sclerophyllous scrubs of the transition zone between Mediterranean and Irano-Turanian domaines in the Levant and Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian semisteppe bathas
description: Xerophile batha-like semisteppe formations of the borderland between the mediterranean and Irano-Turanian domaines of the Levant and northern Egypt, dominated by hemicryptophytes, accompanied by numerous annuals. [Ononis natrix], [Salvia dominica], [Ballota undulata], [Echinops polyceras], [Convolvulus dorycnium], [Psoralea bituminosa], [Alkanna strigosa], [Euphorbia hierosolymitana], [Centaurea damascena], [Thymelaea hirsuta] are among the dominants of various communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean pre-desert scrub
description: Low formations of [Ziziphus spina-christi], [Ziziphus lotus], [Acacia albida], [Capparis spinosa], [Rhamnus palaestina], [Rhus tripartita] of the Levant and southern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Phrygana
description: Cushion-forming thermo-mediterranean sclerophyllous formations, often thorny and summer deciduous. They are best developed in the eastern Mediterranean basin, especially in the Aegean, where they may occupy considerable surfaces in coastal areas and occasionally inland. They also include a few rare, relict associations of the west Mediterranean, mostly characteristic of the edge of seashores and of maritime cliffs, where they constitute an often narrow belt between the cliff communities and thermo-mediterranean brushes, incorporating, in addition to characteristic, often endemic or very rare, hemispherical cushion-forming species, an admixture of species belonging to these two vegetation complexes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Mediterranean clifftop phryganas
description: Rare, extremely local and isolated associations of clifftops and adjacent areas dispersed along the coasts of Provence, Cap Corse, the Straits of Bonifacio, Catalonia (Cabo de Creus) and extreme southwestern Portugal, characterized by the presence of [Astragalus massiliensis] or [Anthyllis hermanniae], variously accompanied by [Thymelaea hirsuta], [Helichrysum italicum], [Plantago subulata], [Armeria ruscinonensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Provence tragacanth phrygana
description: Very rare clifftop cushion formations of the calcareous Marseilles coast of Provence (les Goudes), with [Astragalus massiliensis], [Thymelaea tartonraira] and [Plantago subulata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Catalo-Provençal thymelaea phrygana
description: Cliff-top communities of the cristalline maritime fa‡ade of the Maures and the Est‚rel, with [Anthyllis barba-jovis], [Thymelaea hirsuta], [Limonium minutum], [Euphorbia pithyusa], and of Catalonia and Roussillon, with [Thymelaea hirsuta], [Polycarpon polycarpoides], [Plantago subulata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West-Mediterranean [Anthyllis] phrygana
description: Clifftop cushion formations of the western Mediterranean basin dominated by [Anthyllis hermanniae], distributed in particular on Cap Corse and the Maltese Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Straits of Bonifacio tragacanth phrygana
description: Formations of the southern tip of Corsica and the extreme northern coast of Sardinia, with [Astragalus massiliensis], accompanied by [Teucrium polium], [Asteriscus maritimus], [Plantago coronopus] ssp. [humulis], [Artemisia arborescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cabo de Creus tragacanth phrygana
description: Isolated formation of the Cabo de Creus promontory in Catalonia, with [Astragalus massiliensis], [Pistacia lentiscus], [Cistus albidus], [Cistus salvifolius], [Phillyrea angustifolia], [Juniperus oxycedrus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cabo de Sao Vicente tragacanth phrygana
description: Very isolated formations of the Cabo de Sao Vicente and the Ponta de Sagres, with [Astragalus massiliensis] and [Crithmum maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian [Centaurea horrida] phryganas
description: Highly threatened formations of the promontories of northern Sardinia, limited to the peninsulas of Stintino and Capo Caccia and the islands of Asinara and Tavola, dominated by the large, silvery-blue, hemispherical cushions of the endemic Tertiary relict [Centaurea horrida], associated with many other endemic or restricted relict species including [Astragalus massiliensis], [Erodium corsicum], [Limonium acutifolium], [Nananthea perpusilla], [Evax rotundata], [Armeria pungens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean phryganas
description: Low, thorny formations of hemispherical shrubs of the coastal thermo-Mediterranean zone of Aegean islands, of mainland Greece and the Ionian islands, of coastal Anatolia, with [Sarcopoterium spinosum], [Centaurea spinosa], [Satureja thymbra], [Thymus capitatus], [Genista acanthoclada], [Anthyllis hermanniae], [Euphorbia acanthothamnos], [Stachys spinosa], [Ballota pseudodictamnus], [Ballota acetabulosa], [Erica manipuliflora], [Rhamnus oleoides], [Lithospermum hispidulum], [Fumana arabica], [Fumana thymifolia], [Cistus creticus], [Cistus parviflorus], [Cistus salvifolius], [Pistacia lentiscus], [Teucrium brevifolium], [Teucrium divaricatum], [Teucrium polium], [Calicotome villosa], [Micromeria graeca], [Micromeria juliana], [Micromeria nervosa], [Salvia triloba], [Ononis spinosa], [Helichrysum italicum] ssp. [microphyllum], [Helichrysum italicum] ssp. [italicum], [Phagnalon graecum], much more widespread and diverse than the western Mediterranean formations. The subdivisions proposed are based on physiognomically significant dominants; codominance can be indicated by use of multiple codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean [Sarcopoterium] phryganas
description: [Sarcopoterium spinosum]-dominated formations, by far the commonest phrygana facies, widespread in the Aegean archipelagoes and Crete, with local outposts in peninsular Greece, the Ionian islands and coastal Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Maritime [Centaurea spinosa] phryganas
description: Rare, relict formations on coastal sands and gravels of Egina, Attica, Euboea, Skyros, Samos, Lesbos, Khios, Kos, Lemnos, Samothrace, Crete, the Sea of Marmara, the Dardanelles, western Anatolia, dominated by the large, silvery hemispherical cushions of [Centaurea spinosa] ssp. [spinosa], sometimes accompanied by [Sarcopoterium spinosum] or [Euphorbia acanthoclada].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesbian [Centaurea spinosa] phryganas
description: Phryganas often rich in [Centaurea spinosa] ssp. [spinosa], mixed with [Sarcopoterium spinosum], [Satureja thymbra], [Ballota acetabulosa] of Lesbos, extending from the coast to the highest hills in the arid western part of the island; covering a relatively vast expanse, they harbour a highly distinctive flora and fauna as well as remnants of fossil forest.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesbian [Centaurea-Sarcopoterium] phryganas
description: [Sarcopoterium] phrygana rich in [Centaurea spinosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesbian [Sarcopoterium] phryganas
description: [Sarcopoterium] phrygana with little or no [Centaurea spinosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesbian steppe-phrygana
description: Open, almost pure, stands of [Centaurea spinosa] on steppic hills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cycladian [Centaurea] phryganas
description: Formations of the Cyclades, rich in [Centaurea spinosa] ssp. [cycladum], extending from coastal areas to the highest elevations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean heather phryganas
description: Phryganas of the Aegean region in which [Erica manipuliflora] plays an important role, often associated with [Sarcopoterium spinosum], [Genista acanthoclada], [Pistacia lentiscus], [Ballota acetabulosa], [Cistus creticus], [Cistus parviflorus], [Cistus salvifolius], a facies of the [Sarcopoterium] phrygana developing locally, notably in eastern Crete and the Cyclades.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean thyme phryganas
description: Phryganas of the Aegean region dominated or formed by [Thymus capitatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean [Genista] phryganas
description: [Genista acanthoclada] formations of the thermo-Mediterranean zone Aegean islands and coasts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean savory phryganas
description: Facies of the Aegean phryganas in which [Satureja thymbra] becomes locally dominant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean spiny spurge phryganas
description: [Euphorbia acanthothamnos]-dominated formations of the Aegean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean gromwell phryganas
description: [Lithospermum hispidulum]-dominated phryganas, limited to southeastern Aegean islands and adjacent Anatolian peninsulas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean [Anthyllis] phryganas
description: [Anthyllis hermanniae]-dominated or -rich phryganas, widespread, in particular in the northern Aegean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean [Carlina] phryganas
description: Phryganas of the Karpathos group, of the southeastern Cyclades and of the Marmaris peninsula in southwestern Anatolia dominated by, or rich in, [Carlina tragacanthifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mid-elevation phryganas of Crete
description: Varied formations of supra- and oro- Mediterranean levels of Crete resulting from the broad contact between phryganas and hedgehog-heaths (unit 32.7), with [Euphorbia acanthothamnos], [Verbascum spinosum], [Berberis cretica], [Phlomis cretica], [Satureja biroi], [Sideritis syriaca], [Hypericum empetrifolium], [Origanum microphyllum], [Micromeria juliana], [Helichrysum italicum] ssp. [microphyllum], [Genista acanthoclada].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Hypericum] phryganas
description: Extremely rare, local colonies of hemispherical shrubs of [Hypericum aegyptiacum] forming open phryganas on calcareous rocks by the sea in the Ionian islands, western Crete, Sardinia and Lampedusa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean [Sarcopoterium] phryganas
description: Very local, impoverished [Sarcopoterium spinosum] formations of Capo St. Elia (southern Sardinian coast), of the Gulf of Taranto (Puglia, Calabria) and of the Maltese Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian [Genista acanthoclada] phrygana
description: Very local [Genista acanthoclada] ssp. [sardoa]-dominated communities of northwestern Sardinia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balearic clifftop phryganas
description: Formations of the coasts of Mallorca and Minorca dominated by the cushion-forming Balearic endemics [Launaea cervicornis], [Astragalus balearicus], [Centaurea balearica], [Anthyllis fulgurans], [Anthyllis hermanniae] ssp. [hystrix], [Teucrium subspinosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyrno-Sardinian [Genista] phryganas
description: Thermo-Mediterranean formations of headlands and peninsulas of Corsica and Sardinia dominated by cushion-forming spiny [Genista corsica] or [Genista morisii]. These endemic species participate in the constitution of hedgehog-heaths (unit 31.75) as well as in that of the coastal formations listed here, which assume an evident phrygana appearance; they may also enter in the composition of midelevation formations of less distinctive appearance which can be listed under unit 32.482.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pantelleria phrygana
description: Coastal formation of hemispherical shrubs with the Pantelleria endemics [Helichrysum saxatile] ssp. [errerae] and [Matthiola pulchella], vicariant of the west Mediterranean, Balearic and Sardinian clifftop phryganas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian phryganas
description: Thorny cushion communities of the Thracian wooded steppe zone enclaved between the Black Sea, the Sea of Marmora and the Aegean, with [Sarcopoterium spinosum] and [Astragalus thracicus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian [Sarcopoterium] phryganas
description: [Sarcopoterium spinosum]-dominated phryganas of the Thracian steppe zone of northeastern Greece and Turkey-in-Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Thracian collinar [Astragalus thracicus] phryganas
description: [Astragalus thracicus] phryganas of the Thracian steppe zone of northeastern Greece and Turkey-in-Europe, with local representatives in the xerothermic oak belt of the hills and rim of the Northern Thracian plain (East Rumelian plain) of southeastern Bulgaria, in particular, in the Bakadzicita hills of the Yambol Tundzja basin and in the foothills of the eastern Rhodopes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean bathas
description: Cushion-forming thermo-Mediterranean summer-deciduous, often thorny, sclerophyllous formations of Mediterranean areas of the Levant, north and west to the Gulf of Alexandrette, with local outposts in the Gulf of Antalaya and in Cyprus; they occupy large areas in the lowlands, ascending locally into the hills and, in Lebanon, to 1300 m in the mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian phryganas
description: Cushion-forming thermo-mediterranean summer-deciduous, often thorny, sclerophyllous formations of Cyprus, mostly characteristic of the central plains, of semisteppic batha appearance, outpost of the continental formations of units 33.C2 to 33.C5, and like them of Irano-Turanian affinities, formed by [Sarcopoterium spinosum], [Thymus capitatus] ([Coridothymus capitatus]), [Lithodora hispidula] ([Lithospermum hispidulum]), [Onosma fruticosum], [Galium suberosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian [Sarcopoterium] phryganas
description: Phryganas or bathas of Cyprus dominated by [Sarcopoterium spinosum], variously accompanied by [Thymus capitatus] ([Coridothymus capitatus]), [Lithodora hispidula] ([Lithospermum hispidulum]), [Galium suberosum], [Noaea mucronata], [Cistus salviifolius], [Cistus creticus], [Fumana thymifolia], [Salvia verbenacea], [Helichrysum rupicolum], [Pistacia lentiscus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian thyme phryganas
description: Phryganas or bathas of Cyprus dominated by cushions of [Thymus capitatus] ([Coridothymus capitatus]), accompanied by [Sarcopoterium spinosum], [Galium suberosum], [Noaea mucronata], [Fumana thymifolia], [Asphodelus microcarpus], [Hyparrhenia hirta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian gromwell and golden drop phryganas
description: Phryganas or bathas of Cyprus dominated by Boraginaceae, in particular, [Lithodora hispidula] ([Lithospermum hispidulum]) or [Onosma fruticosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian [Sarcopoterium] bathas
description: Thorny cushion formations of the Levant and southern Anatolia dominated by [Sarcopoterium spinosum] on calcareous substrates, including terra rossa, rendzina or sand, typically on hills near the coast; there is often a significant participation of annuals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian thyme bathas
description: Cushion formations of the Levant and southern Anatolia dominated by [Thymus capitatus] ([Coridothymus capitatus]), typically forming a sparse plant cover poor in annuals, on calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Levantine sage bathas
description: Cushion formations of the Levant dominated by labiates, in particular, [Salvia triloba] or [Satureja thymbra], typically developed on calcareous rocky substrates and red soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian gromwell bathas
description: [Lithospermum hispidulum]-dominated phryganas of southeastern Anatolia and the Levant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African phryganas
description: Thermo-mediterranean summer-deciduous, mostly thorny cushion formations of North Africa, scattered in the semiarid and arid zones, particularly on the margins of the Sahara, mostly dominated by [Sarcopoterium spinosum]. They are prevalent, in particular, in Cyrenaica, with [Sarcopoterium spinosum], [Thymus capitatus] ([Coridothymus capitatus]), [Genista acanthoclada], [Phlomis floccosa], [Ballota pseudo-dictamnus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Steppes and dry calcareous grasslands
description: Primary and secondary steppes, formations dominated by medium or tall perennnial tuft-forming grasses or suffrutescents, with lacunar ground cover, together with their associated therophyte communities; typical formations, with two periods of dormancy, in large part climactic, are characteristic of a steppe belt in continental Central Eurasia and on the western Asian plateaux, with irradiations in the nemoral zone; physiognomically similar formations, although perhaps largely anthropogenic, and mostly with a single period of dormancy, are widespread in the transition zone between the Mediterranean and Saharo-Sindian domaines and occur locally in the Mediterranean zone. By extension, 34 also includes dry thermophilous, mostly zoogenous, grasslands and thermophile forest fringe formations of the lowland, hill and montane altitudinal levels of the nemoral and Mediterranean zones, on mostly calcareous soils, sands, and decomposed rock surfaces.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European pioneer swards
description: Open, thermophile formations of sandy or detritic ground in temperate and, locally, boreal or submediterranean lowland to montane areas of Western Europe, Central Europe and, very locally, northern Eastern Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian rock debris swards
description: Open lowland and hill rock debris swards of suboceanic, temperate, boreal or submediterranean, climates of Western Europe and of Central Europe, east, sporadically, to Poland, the hills of the Pannonic plain and the Adriatic coasts of the northwestern Balkan peninsula, formed mostly by annuals and succulents or semisucculents on decomposed rock surfaces of edges, ledges or knolls, with calcareous or siliceous soils frequently disturbed by erosion or rabbits. They comprise a great variety of distinct and often very local, isolated communities harbouring many characteristic species, among which numerous rare forms including both relict and evolutionarily recent taxa. Together with more evolved grassland communities of unit 34.35, sometimes 34.31, 34.33 or 34.341, very paucispecific communities of units 62.1B or 62.29, and lacunar shrub formations of unit 31.8, they constitute the vascular vegetation of middle European inland cliffs and rock outcroppings of unit 62.4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European stonecrop swards
description: Open lowland and hill rock debris swards of suboceanic, temperate or submediterranean, climates of Western Europe and Central Europe, dominated by, or rich in, succulent species of genus [Sedum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European acidocline stonecrop swards
description: Open swards of lowland and hill siliceous rock debris of Western Europe and western and northern Central Europe dominated by, or rich in, species of genus [Sedum], in particular, [Sedum reflexum] ([Sedum rupestre]), [Sedum album], [Sedum acre], and, under Atlantic climates, [Sedum anglicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European calcicline stonecrop swards
description: Open swards of lowland and hill calcareous rock debris of nemoral Western Europe, western and northern Central Europe dominated by, or rich in, [Sedum album], [Sedum sexangulare], or other succulents of genus [Sedum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Houseleek communities
description: Open lowland and hill rock debris swards of suboceanic climates of Western Europe and western and northern Central Europe harbouring often rare and local lowland forms of [Sempervivum spp.] or [Jovibarba spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sempervivum tectorum] communities
description: Debris swards rich in [Sempervivum tectorum] of the Jura, the Lake Constance area, the Moselle Valley, Hesse.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Jovibarba sobolifera] communities
description: Debris swards rich in [Jovibarba sobolifera] of Franconia, Rhon, southern Saxony, Brandenburg, Bohemia, Latvia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amblève houseleek community
description: Unique, and highly vulnerable, debris sward of [Sempervivum funckii] var. [aqualiense] of the AmblŠve Valley in the eastern Condruzian Ardenne periphery.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European grassy rock debris communities
description: Open lowland and hill rock debris swards of suboceanic climates of Western Europe and western and northern Central Europe, eastwards sporadically to the hills of the Pannonic plain, in which perennial grasses such as [Poa badensis], [Melica ciliata] and [Festuca spp.] play an important physiognomic role.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Poa badensis] and garlic rock debris swards
description: Lowland and hill rock debris swards of northern Bavaria, Bohemia and Thuringe, dominated by [Poa badensis], by [Allium montanum] or by both species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Poa compressa] rock debris swards
description: Lowland and hill rock debris swards of the Rhenish Hercynian ranges, the Jura, the Bohemian Quadrangle and the eastern Alpine periphery, dominated by [Poa compressa] or [Poa angustifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Melica ciliata] rock debris swards
description: Open, sub-Mediterranean type, limestone rock grassland of the western part of the Hungarian Central Range, with [Asplenium ruta-muraria], [Melica ciliata] and harbouring the rare and protected [Ceterach javorkaenum], [Colchicum hungaricum], [Sedum neglectum] ssp. [sopianae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European rock debris small forb communities
description: Open lowland and hill rock debris swards of suboceanic, temperate or submediterranean, climates of Western Europe and Central Europe in which small annual or perennial forbs predominate over sparser crassulids or perennial grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian pioneer rock swards
description: Pioneer communities colonizing thin debris soils and cracks of rocks, cliffs and rock pavements of xerothermic enclaves of the boreonemoral and southern boreal zones of Norway, Sweden and Finland, mostly limited to coastal regions, southern slopes and alvars. Some of the communities share physiognomic and ecological characteristics with the Central European communities of unit 34.35.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alvar stonecrop swards
description: Open swards of lowland and hill calcareous rock debris of boreonemoral Europe, limited to alvar limestone outcroppings of ™land, Gotland, V„sterg”tland, the land archipelago and extreme southern Finland; they are very low [Sedum album] and [Tortella spp.]-dominated herb and moss communities  occupying open, level limestone pavements almost totally lacking in soil, surrounded by a system of fissures, under semiarid climatic conditions. [Tortella inclinata] and [Tortella tortuosa] dominate among the mosses and lichens; the species cortŠge also includes, among others, [Allium schoenoprasum], [Androsace septentrionale], [Arenaria serpyllifolia], [Apera interrupta], [Cerastium pumilum], [Geranium lucidum], [Linum catharticus], [Saxifraga tridactylites], [Sedum acre], [Melica ciliata], [Tortella rigens], [Tortella caeruleonigricans], [Barbula spp.], [Cladonia symphycarpia], [Collema spp.] They are associated with rock fissure communities of unit 62.1B1 and rock lichen communities of unit 62.4121.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Sedum]-[Viola]-[Aira] rock swards
description: Sparse communities of small annuals, short grasses and succulents colonizing thin soils covering acid or basic rocks, or forming in small cracks under extremely dry local climates in xerothermic enclaves of Scandinavia, north to the southern boreal zone, mostly in coastal areas and on south-facing slopes. They are a refuge for species of low competition potential and are often dominated by one or two species, in particular, [Sedum acre], [Aira praecox], [Viola tricolor], [Rumex tenuifolius]. Their species cortŠge includes [Arabidopsis thaliana], [Bromus mollis], [Geranium pusillum], [Jasione montana], [Lychnis viscaria], [Satureja acinos], [Saxifraga granulata], [Saxifraga tridactylites], [Scleranthus annuus], [Scleranthus perennis], [Sedum album], [Sedum telephium], [Trifolium arvense], [Veronica arvensis], [Veronica spicata], [Veronica verna], [Viola rupestris], [Ceratodon purpureus], [Rhytidium rugosum], [Thuidium abietinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Festuca]-[Viola] rock swards
description: Rock swards of the Atlantic coast of Norway developed in thermic enclaves on south-facing slopes under oceanic climates, richer in grass and poorer in xerophile species than the communities of unit 34.1152, with a species cortŠge that includes [Plantago lanceolata], often dominant, [Festuca vivipara], [Viola tricolor], [Alchemilla alpina], [Allium oleraceum], [Arabidopsis thaliana], [Conopodium majus], [Galium saxatile], [Hieracium pilosella], [Potentilla argentea], [Veronica officinalis], [Luzula campestris], [Orchis mascula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Norvegian rock swards
description: Rock swards of Tr”ndelag and northern Norway with [Astragalus alpinus], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Draba incana], [Erigeron borealis], [Gentiana nivalis], [Gentianella campestris], [Lotus corniculatus], [Poa alpina], [Potentilla crantzii], [Primula scandinavica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian pioneer calcareous sand swards
description: Open grasslands of strongly to slightly calcareous inland sands of Western Europe and of western and northern Central Europe, locally to Lithuania, Latvia and Belarus, with [Helichrysum arenarium], [Silene otites], [Silene chlorantha], [Dianthus deltoides], [Dianthus arenarius], [Gypsophila fastigiata] ssp. [arenaria], [Astragalus arenarius], [Androsace septentrionalis], [Onosma arenaria], [Jurinea cyanoides], [Koeleria glauca], [Festuca psammophila], [Festuca polesica], [Festuca duvalii] and the Brandenburg endemic [Stipa borysthenica] ssp. [germanica], sometimes interspersed with annual formations with [Cerastium semidecandrum], [Vicia lathyroides], [Silene conica], [Phleum arenarium], [Petrorhagia prolifera], [Arenaria serpyllifolia], [Sedum acre]. Dunal formations can be characterized by conjunction of this code with those of unit 64.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Heavy metal grasslands
description: Dry, short grasslands, often rich in lichens and mosses, colonizing western and central European soils with a high content in heavy metals such as zinc and lead, and comprising uniquely adapted species, ecotypes or populations mostly related to, or derived from, otherwise montane, boreomontane or steppic species; heavy metal grasslands of distinctly alpine affinities, though spanning an altitudinal range that extends from the montane level and lowland dealpine stations to the subalpine and alpine levels, are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic heavy metal grasslands
description: Heavy metal grasslands of the British Isles, with [Armeria maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British heavy metal grasslands
description: Formations, in particular of Wales and the Pennines, developed in the vicinity of former mining operations or on river gravels, with [Minuartia verna], [Thlaspi caerulescens], [Armeria maritima], [Viola lutea], [Festuca ovina] [s.l.], [Festuca rubra] [s.l.], [Agrostis capillaris] ([Agrostis tenuis]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irish heavy metal grasslands
description: Grasslands on copper-rich soils of Kilarney, with [Armeria maritima] and [Silene maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calaminarian grasslands
description: Open formations colonizing heavy metal soils, either natural or resulting from past mining operations, in rapid regression and limited to a few stations in eastern Belgium, western Rhineland, Westphalia and Lower Saxony, and to one station in the southern Netherlands, with outposts in northern France, comprised of a highly specialized flora with the endemics [Viola calaminaria], [Viola guestphalica], [Thlaspi caerulescens] ([Thlaspi alpestre] ssp. [calaminare]) and [Festuca aquisgranensis] ([Festuca ophioliticola] ssp. [calaminaria]), with [Minuartia verna] var. [hercynica], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [humilis] and [Armeria halleri], limited to this formation and the next, and with the steppic, central European [Festuca valesiaca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Viola calaminaria] grasslands
description: Formations of eastern Belgium, the extreme southern Netherlands and the Aachen area, with the yellow-flowered [Viola calaminaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Viola guestphalica] grasslands
description: Formations of northern Westfalia and of southern Lower Saxony, with the purple-flowered [Viola guestphalica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western calaminarian thrift grasslands
description: Western European calaminarian communities comprising [Armeria halleri] [s.l.] in the absence of [Viola lutea] or [Viola guestphalica], known from very isolated stations, in particular, in the Eifel, southwestern Belgium and northern France. [Cardaminopsis halleri] is characteristic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calaminarian pennycress grasslands
description: Fragmentary heavy metal grasslands of the Osnabrck region of Lower Saxony and of Sauerland, with [Thlaspi caerulescens] ([Thlaspi alpestre] ssp. [calaminare]), but without violets or thrift.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Osnabrück heavy metal grasslands
description: Fragmentary heavy metal grasslands of the Osnabrck region of Lower Saxony, with [Thlaspi caerulescens] ([Thlaspi alpestre] ssp. [calaminare]), [Minuartia verna] var. [hercynica], [Silene vulgaris] var. [humilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sauerland heavy metal grasslands
description: Fragmentary heavy metal grasslands of Sauerland, with [Thlaspi caerulescens] ([Thlaspi alpestre] ssp. [calaminare]) and [Cardaminopsis halleri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European heavy metal grasslands
description: Heavy metal grasslands of Saxony, of the Harz and of Upper Silesia, with the endemic or near endemic [Armeria halleri], [Armeria bottendorfensis], [Armeria hornburgensis] and with [Minuartia verna] var. [hercynica], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [humilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saxon [Armeria halleri] grasslands
description: Heavy metal grasslands of the Harz, of the Mansfelder Mulde and the Saale basin in Sachsen-Anhalt and of the Littfeld area in the Siegerland of Westfalia with [Armeria halleri], [Minuartia verna] var. [hercynica], [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [humilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Armeria bottendorfensis] grasslands
description: Heavy metal grasslands of Sachsen-Anhalt, with the endemic [Armeria bottendorfensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Armeria hornburgensis] grasslands
description: Heavy metal grasslands of Sachsen-Anhalt, with the endemic [Armeria hornburgensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Silesian [Armeria halleri] grasslands
description: Fragmentary heavy metal grasslands of Upper Silesia, with [Armeria halleri] and [Cardaminopsis halleri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calaminarian catchfly grasslands
description: Fragmentary heavy metal grasslands of which the distinctive cortŠge is essentially reduced to [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [humilis], characteristic, in particular, of cupreous shists of the Niedersmarsberg of Westfalia, of outlying heavy metal stations of southern Germany in the Wiesloch-Baiertal of northern Baden-Wrttemberg and the southern Black Forest, as well as of peripheral sites within the range of other heavy metal lowland and hill communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine heavy metal communities
description: Formations of heavy metal soils of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Alps and the Pyrenees, with, among others, [Dianthus sylvestris], [Galium anisophyllon], [Poa alpina], [Armeria arenaria], [Thlaspi caerulescens], and the very restricted southern Alpine endemic [Viola dubyana]; they descend to the montane level and occur in some dealpine stations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Alpine heavy metal grasslands
description: Heavy metal communities of the southern limestone Alps, limited to the Bergamasque Alps, with [Viola dubyana], [Dianthus sylvestris], [Galium anisophyllon], [Poa alpina], [Euphrasia salisburgensis] and [Thymus praecox] ssp. [polytrichus] ([Thymus alpigenus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carnic heavy metal grasslands
description: Heavy metal communities of the southeastern limestone Alps, limited to the Carnic Alps and the Gail Valley, with [Thlaspi rotundifolium] ssp. [cepaeifolium], [Dianthus sylvestris], [Galium anisophyllon], [Poa alpina], [Minuartia verna] var. [hercynica] and [Silene vulgaris] var. [humilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Alpine heavy metal grasslands
description: Fragmentary heavy metal communities of the calcareous Northern Alps, in particular of the Lechtaler Alps and the Mieminger chain, with [Minuartia verna] var. [hercynica], [Silene vulgaris] var. [humilis], [Dianthus sylvestris], [Galium anisophyllon] and [Thymus praecox] ssp. [polytrichus] ([Thymus alpigenus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dense perennial grasslands and middle European steppes
description: Dry closed thermophilous grasslands of middle European or Mediterranean lowlands and hills, up to the montane zone, dominated by perennial grasses; steppic grasslands of continental affinities occurring under subcontinental conditions within the middle European nemoral and boreonemoral forest zones, in the Alpine system and in the sub-Mediterranean zone of the Balkans.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-continental steppic grasslands
description: Open grasslands of subcontinental climate areas of the nemoral zone of Western, Northern, Central and northern Eastern Europe and of the sub-Mediterranean zone of the Balkan peninsula, with [Festuca valesiaca], [Festuca rupicola], [Festuca pseudovina], [Festuca duvalii], [Festuca trachyphylla], [Stipa capillata], [Stipa joannis], [Stipa pulcherrima], [Stipa tirsa] ([Stipa stenophylla]), [Stipa dasyphylla], [Chrysopogon gryllus], [Danthonia alpina], [Koeleria macrantha], [Agrostis capillaris], [Poa bulbosa], [Poa molinerii] ([Poa badensis] var. [xerophila]), [Poa perconcinna] ([Poa carniolica]), [Melica ciliata], [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Carex supina], [Carex stenophylla], [Carex humilis] and herbs such as [Adonis vernalis], [Pulsatilla montana], [Pulsatilla pratensis], [Pulsatilla grandis], [Pulsatilla patens], [Pulsatilla pusilla], [Veronica spicata], [Allium flavum], [Allium sphaerocephalon], [Silene otites], [Artemisia campestris], [Achillea collina], [Achillea nobilis], [Achillea setacea], [Centaurea rhenana] ([Centaurea stoebe]), [Inula spiraeifolia], [Verbascum phoeniceum], [Armeria alliacea], [Kochia prostrata], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Campanula sibirica], [Iris pumila], [Iris variegata], [Linum flavum], [Onosma taurica], [Onosma arenaria], [Silene otites], [Potentilla arenaria], [Potentilla cinerea], [Aster linosyris], [Onobrychis arenaria], [Oxytropis pilosa], [Oxytropis halleri], [Ononis pusilla], [Ononis cenisia], [Astragalus onobrychis], [Astragalus exscapus], [Astragalus danicus], [Astragalus vesicarius], [Astragalus austriacus], [Astragalus alopecuroides], [Eryngium campestre], [Dianthus carthusianorum], often of oriental, mostly Sarmatic, affinities. Communities of sub-Pannonic, sub-Pontic and sub-Sarmatic hills are included, while those of the main wooded steppe and steppe zones of the Pannonic basin and the Ponto-Sarmatic lowlands and plateaux are listed separately under unit 34.9.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic savory steppes
description: Perennial, steppelike grasslands of the sub-Mediterranean and sub-Pannonic [Quercion frainetto] and [Fagion moesiacum] zones of the Balkan peninsula, from Greece to Serbia and western Bulgaria, where they are particularly well represented on the Golo Bardo and adjacent hills, with, among others, [Festuca valesiaca], [Festuca rupicola], [Koeleria gracilis], [Stipa pulcherrima], [Stipa joannis], [Bromus erectus], [Poa bulbosa], [Melica ciliata], [Carex humilis], [Carex caryophyllea], [Satureja montana], [Galium purpureum], [Teucrium montanum], [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria], [Artemisia alba], [Galium album], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Teucrium chamaedrys].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European steppic grasslands
description: Xerophile or mesoxerophile grasslands, developed in areas with a locally high degree of continentality, of Alsace, the upper Rhine valley and hills, Franconia, Thuringe, Saxony, the lower and middle Oder basin, the lower Vistula valley, the upper Vistula basin and Lublin Uplands, Lithuania, the Bohemian basin, the eastern Alpine periphery and inner valleys.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European steppes
description: Arid grasslands of western and northern Central European areas of high continentality, with [Stipa capillata], [Stipa pulcherrima], [Stipa joannis], [Stipa tirsa] ([Stipa stenophylla]), [Festuca valesiaca], [Festuca rupicola], [Festuca trachyphylla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rheno-Franconian steppes
description: Arid subcontinental steppic grasslands of hills, plateaux and basins of the southern German and Alsatian Hercynian and Jurassic system, limited to small surfaces in areas of high continentality.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rheno-Franconian garlic-feathergrass steppes
description: Arid [Stipa capillata] grasslands developed in isolated islands of high continentality scattered between the Franconian Main plateau and the Rhine and Nahe basin, colonizing limestones, calcareous sands and loess-covered limestone-poor substrates, with [Stipa pulcherrima], [Stipa joannis], [Festuca valesiaca], [Festuca sulcata] (in Franconia) or [Festuca lemanii] and [Festuca heteropachys] (in Rhenish regions), [Bromus erectus], [Koeleria glauca], [Poa badensis], [Phleum phleoides], [Carex humilis], [Allium sphaerocephalon], [Pulsatilla vulgaris], [Potentilla arenaria], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Stachys recta], [Dianthus carthusianorum], [Artemisia campestris], [Trinia glauca] and [Cerastium semidecandrum] (on calcareous soils) or [Melica ciliata] and [Sedum album] (on siliceous substrates), [Achillea nobilis] (on Rhenish limestones).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nahe valley hairy greenweed feathergrass steppes
description: Rare, isolated subcontinental steppic grassland of the Nahe basin, dominated by [Stipa tirsa] ([Stipa stenophylla]) with [Festuca heteropachys], [Festuca lemanii], [Stipa joannis], [Genista pilosa], [Potentilla arenaria], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Stachys recta], [Centaurea scabiosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern cinquefoil feathergrass steppes
description: Subcontinental [Stipa capillata] steppic grasslands of Brandenburg, the lower and middle Oder basin, the lower Vistula valley, with [Stipa pulcherrima], [Carex supina], [Oxytropis pilosa], [Alyssum montanum], [Anthericum liliago], [Centaurea rhenana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Hercynian steppes
description: Arid grasslands of Central European areas of high continentality formed within the Hercynian Bohemian and Saale-Mulde basins, mostly in the rain shadow of the Harz, the Thringerwald, the Erzgebirge and other ranges of the Bohemian Quadrangle.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Hercynian feathergrass steppes
description: Steppic grasslands of the Bohemian basin and of the middle German Saale-Mulde basin and their fringing hills, dominated by [Stipa capillata] or [Stipa joannis], developed on relatively deep calcareous or loess substrates, usually two-layered, with [Festuca valesiaca], [Festuca rupicola], [Koeleria macrantha], [Melica transsilvanica], [Elymus hispidus] ([Agropyron intermedium]), [Carex humilis], [Carex supina], [Artemisia campestris], [Achillea pannonica], [Astragalus exscapus], [Eryngium campestre], [Verbascum phoeniceum], [Centaurea stoebe], [Erysimum crepidifolium], [Potentilla arenaria], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Stachys recta], [Dianthus carthusianorum], [Sedum maximum], [Adonis vernalis], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Teucrium montanum], [Hippocrepis comosa], [Bupleurum falcatum], [Anthericum liliago].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Hercynian valesian fescue steppes
description: Open, species-rich steppic grasslands of the Bohemian basin and of the middle German Saale-Mulde basin and their fringing hills, developed on rocky ground with shallow continuous soils, dominated by [Festuca valesiaca], with [Koeleria macrantha], [Erysimum crepidifolium], [Pulsatilla pratensis], [Centaurea stoebe], [Seseli hippomarathrum], [Artemisia campestris], [Potentilla arenaria], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Stachys recta], [Dianthus carthusianorum], [Carex humilis], [Achillea pannonica], [Eryngium campestre], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Sedum maximum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Hercynian grooved fescue steppes
description: Open, very species-rich steppic grasslands of the Bohemian basin, in particular of the volcanic Ceske Stredohori hills, the Doupov hills and the Bohemian karst, and of the adjacent middle German Saale-Mulde basin, rich in lichens and mosses, dominated by [Festuca rupicola], with [Koeleria micrantha], [Festuca valesiaca], [Poa angustifolia], [Carex humilis], [Scabiosa ochroleuca], [Dianthus carthusianorum], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Stachys recta], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Achillea millefolium], [Potentilla arenaria], [Pulsatilla pratensis], [Centaurea stoebe], [Aster linosyris], [Artemisia campestris]n  [Sedum sexangulare], [Sedum maximum], [Sedum reflexum], [Allium montanum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine steppes
description: Steppic grasslands of eastern Alpine inner valleys, east of the Brenner Pass, dominated by [Festuca rupicola] with [Stipa styriaca], [Festuca brevipila], [Koeleria pyramidata], [Phleum phleoides], [Brachypodium rupestre], [Centaurea stoebe], [Globularia punctata], [Potentilla rupestris], [Scabiosa triandra], [Potentilla arenaria], [Potentilla pusilla], [Artemisia campestris], [Helianthemum ovatum], [Thymus pulegioides], [Pimpinella saxifraga], [Peucedanum oreoselinum], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Dianthus carthusianorum], [Pulsatilla nigricans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern pre-Sarmatic steppes
description: Subcontinental steppic grasslands of Little Poland and western Wolhynia, with [Festuca valesiaca], [Festuca rupicola], [Stipa capillata], [Poa bulbosa], [Koeleria gracilis], [Phleum boehmeri], [Euphrasia tatarica], [Carex supina],  [Sisymbrium polymorphum], [Myosotis collina], [Thymus austriacus], [Thymus glabrescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European desert-oat steppes
description: Extremely local xerophile grasslands of the Ceske Strednohory in the northwestern Bohemian basin, of the Pavlov hills-Pollauer Bergen of southern Moravia and ajacent Austria and of the Hainburger Bergen of Austria, dominated by the relict [Helictotrichon desertorum] ssp. [basalticum] ([Avenastrum besseri]), of Central Asian affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bohemian crown vetch steppes
description: Arid grasslands of the Bohemian basin, with [Coronilla varia], [Anthemis tinctoria], [Festuca rupicola], [Dianthus deltoides], [Knautia arvensis], [Koeleria pyramidata], [Potentilla heptaphylla], [Verbascum lychnitis] ssp. [moenchii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bohemian couch-fescue steppes
description: Arid grasslands of the Bohemian basin, with [Elymus hispidus] ([Agropyron intermedium]), [Festuca valesiaca], [Poa angustifolia], [Achillea setacea], [Agrimonia eupatoria], [Astragalus danicus], [Carex praecox], [Echinops sphaerocephalus], [Inula britannica], [Ononis spinosa], [Podospermum laciniatum], [Salvia nemorosa], [Melica transsilvanica], [Potentilla argentea], [Thymus pannonicus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European meadow-steppes
description: Mesoxerophile grasslands of western and northern Central European areas of high continentality, with [Astragalus danicus], [Inula spiraeifolia], [Seseli annuum], [Linum austriacum], [Linum flavum], [Linum hirsutum], [Carex michelii], [Carex praecox], [Carex flacca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European pheasant'eye meadow-steppes
description: Subcontinental mesoxerophile grasslands of the Rhenish regions, Franconia, the Bavarian plateau, the mid-German Saale-Mulde basin, the Bohemian basin, the Oder terraces and Great Poland, with [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Brachypodium rupestre], [Thesium linophyllon], [Scorzonera purpurea], [Scorzonera hispanica], [Adonis vernalis], [Astragalus danicus], [Pulsatilla grandis] ([Pulsatilla vulgaris] ssp. [grandis]), [Pulsatilla patens], [Oxytropis pilosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine sub-continental meadow-steppes
description: Subcontinental mesoxerophile grasslands of the eastern Alpine periphery and inner valleys, in particular, of Tirol, the Karawanken, the Rosental and M”lltal of southern Carinthia, with [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Brachypodium rupestre], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Briza media], [Avenula pratensis], [Dactylis glomerata], [Luzula luzuloides], [Persicaria vivipara], [Thesium alpinum], [Trollius europaeus], [Campanula scheuchzeri], [Potentilla erecta], [Thymus pulegioides], [Trifolium europaeus], [Ranunculus acris], [Ranunculus bulbosus], [Trifolium montanum], [Trifolium pratense], [Carlina acaulis], [Cirsium pannonicum], [Centaurea jacea], [Cruciata glabra], [Polygala comosa], [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Achillea millefolium], [Alchemilla vulgaris] agg., [Lotus corniculatus], [Anthericum ramosum], [Asperula tinctoria], [Linum flavum], [Linum viscosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European feathergrass meadow-steppes
description: Subcontinental mesoxerophile grasslands of the mid-German Saale-Mulde basin, in particular, of the southern slope of the Kyffh„user, developed on degraded chernozem, dominated by [Stipa tirsa] ([Stipa stenophylla]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern pre-Sarmatic meadow-steppes
description: Subcontinental mesoxerophile grasslands of northeastern Central Europe and northern Eastern Europe, recorded, in particular, from Little Poland, Wolhynia and Lithuania, rich in endemic communities of Sarmatic affinities, with [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Sesleria oliginosa], [Calamagrostis clinopodium], [Elymus hispidus] ([Agropyron intermedium]), [Carex praecox], [Cirsium pannonicum], [Carlina onopordifolia], [Dorycnium sericeum], [Aster amellus], [Inula ensifolia], [Inula conyza], [Scorzonera purpurea], [Viola rupestris], [Linum flavum], [Linum hirsutum], [Asperula tinctoria], [Thalictrum simplex], [Agrimonia eupatoria], [Hypericum perforatum], [Salvia pratensis], [Stachys germanica], [Origanum vulgare], [Eryngium campestre], [Ranunculus illyricus], [Campanula bononiensis], [Coronilla varia], [Iris aphylla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern inner Alpine arid grasslands
description: Dry grasslands of the isolated, low-precipitation, high insolation, high summer temperature, inner Alpine valleys of the central and eastern Alps, in particular, of the Val Bregaglia, upper basin of the Adda, the Val Venosta (Vinschgau, upper Adige), the middle Adige-Isarco basin, the Val Pusteria, the Engadine, the Virgental, the M”lltal in Carinthia, the Mur Valley of Styria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western inner Alpine arid grasslands
description: Grasslands of the dry inner valleys of the southwestern Alps in the upper basin of the Durance, the upper valley of the Romanche, the Maurienne and the Tarentaise, the basins of the Dora Riparia (Susa) and of the Chisone, the upper basin of the Dora Baltea (Aosta) and the upper Rhone valley of the Valais.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pannonic steppic grasslands
description: Xerophile or mesoxerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the hills of the western, northern and southwestern periphery of the Pannonic basin and of the Hungarian Central Range, with irradiations into the Bohemian basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pannonic steppes
description: Xerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the hills of the western, northern and southwestern periphery of the Pannonic basin and of the Hungarian Central Range, with irradiations into the Bohemian basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Noric sub-Pannonic steppes
description: Relatively wide-ranging xerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the hills of the western and northern, predominantly pre-Alpine or pre-Carpathian, periphery of the Pannonic basin in Austria, Moravia and Slovakia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Bohemian sub-Pannonic steppes
description: Localized xerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the hills of the northwestern, pre-Bohemian, periphery of the Pannonic basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Hungarian sub-Pannonic steppes
description: Grasslands of dry slopes of the Hungarian Central Range and the Mecsek hills, harbouring many continental and regionally important species including the very rare [Ferula sadlerana], with [Festuca rupicola], [Stipa capillata], [Stipa crassiculmis] ssp. [euroanatolica], [Stipa dasyphylla], [Cleistogenes serotina] ([Diplachne serotina]), [Dracocephalum austriacum], [Lotus borbasii], [Adonis vernalis], [Iris pumila], [Pulsatilla nigricans], [Ranunculus illyricus], [Veronica austriaca], [Linum austriacum], [Convolvulus cantabrica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Illyrian sub-Pannonic steppes
description: Xerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the hills of the southwestern periphery of the Pannonic basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Andropogonid sub-Pannonic steppes
description: Xerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the hills of the western and southwestern periphery of the Pannonic basin, dominated by [Dichanthium ischaemum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pannonic rock steppes
description: Xerophile grasslands of the Hungarian Central Range, intermediate between the rock swards of the [Festucetalia pallentis] and the steppes of the [Festucetalia valesiacae], and often in contact with both, developed on shallow rendzina soils over dolomites, rich in species of sub-Mediterranean and Illyrian affinities, in addition to a continental, in part Pontic, cortŠge, including in particular [Festuca pallens], [Carex humilis], [Helianthemum canum], [Jurinea mollis], [Scorzonera austriaca], [Teucrium montanum], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Frysimum diffusum], [Fumana vulgaris], [Minuartia setacea], [Onosma visianii], [Paronychia cephalotes], [Allium moschatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pannonic meadow-steppes
description: Mesoxerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the hills of the western, northern and southwestern periphery of the Pannonic basin and of the Hungarian Central Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pannonic wooded steppe meadows
description: Secondary xeromesophile grasslands colonizing abandoned vineyards in the Hungarian Central Range rich in rare and fragile species, harbouring, in particular, [Stipa stenophylla] ([Stipa tirsa]), [Campanula macrostachya], [Helictotrichon compressum], [Danthonia alpina], [Stipa dasyphylla], [Seseli osseum], [Centaurea triumfett] ssp. [axillaris], [Iris pumila], [Peucedanum cervaria], [Carex humilis], [Inula hirta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesio-Carpathian steppic grasslands
description: Xerophile or mesoxerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the foothills, lower slopes and associated plateaux of the eastern Carpathian system, of the Balkan Range and of the Dinarides, in areas enclaved between the Pannonic and Ponto-Sarmatic regions or within their influence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesio-Carpathian steppes
description: Xerophile grasslands of Ponto-Pannonic affinities of the foothills, lower slopes and associated plateaux of the eastern Carpathian system, of the Balkan Range and of the Dinarides, in areas enclaved between the Pannonic and Ponto-Sarmatic regions or within their influence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesio-Carpathian feathergrass-fescue steppes
