description: Steppes of the plain of the western Black Sea, west of the Dniester, of its associated basins, including those of the lower Danube, of Transylvania and of northern Thrace, of the southern edge and valleys of the Podolian, Central Russian and Volga plateaux, with [Stipa capillata], [Kochia prostrata], [Koeleria lobata] ([Koeleria degenii]), [Stipa lessingiana], [Festuca valesiaca], [Dichanthium ischaemum] ([Bothriochloa ischaemum]), [Medicago minima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic steppes
description: Steppes of the plain of the western Black Sea, west of the Dniester, of the basin of the lower Danube and of the northern Thracian basin of the middle Maritsa and the Tundzha, with [Pimpinella tragium], [Thymus zygioides], [Stipa lessingiana], [Stipa capillata], [Agropyron pectiniforme].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic thyme steppes
description: Very open steppes of the western Pontic region, with chamaephytes, on leached shallow soils, with [Pimpinella lithophila], [Thymus zygioides], [Stipa lessingiana], [Koeleria lobata], [Potentilla bornmuelleri], [Satureja coerulea], [Ornithogalum amphibolum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic wormwood steppes
description: Very open, semidesert-like steppes of the western Pontic region and the Transylvanian basin, developed on soils with fluctuating moisture, dominated or codominated by [Artemisia spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic feathergrass steppes
description: Steppes of the western Pontic region and the Transylvanian basin developed on deeper chernozem soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic steppes
description: Steppes of the southern edge and valleys of the Podolian, Central Russian and Volga plateaux, forming a wooded steppe belt north of the Pontic plains, extending west to the upper Prut basin of Romanian Moldavia and east to the Volga-Kama trough, composed of [Stipa lessingiana], [Stipa joannis], [Stipa pulcherrima], [Stipa ucrainica], [Koeleria macrantha], [Agropyron cristatum], [Festuca valesiaca], [Astragalus onobrychis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic steppes
description: Steppes of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain, of the basins of the Dnieper and the Don, extending west to the Dniestr, northeast to the Volga, east to the Caspian deserts and semideserts, southeast to the pre-Caucasian hills in the basins of the Kouban, the Manytch, the upper Kuma and upper Terek.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian steppes
description: Steppes of the steppe and wooded steppe belts of extreme eastern Europe and western Siberia, extending from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east, including the Transvolgan steppes of Orenburg and Bachkiria, the Kurgan, Ishim, Baraba, Kulunda, Barnaul, Kirgiz, Kazakh steppes, and the mountain steppes of the Tarbagatai and the Altai.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian steppes
description: Steppes of Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, the Songnen Plain of Northeast China, the western Loess Plateau of North China, mountain steppes of the Tien Shan, from the rim of the Naryn and Isyk-K”l basins eastwards, of the Sayan and Tannu mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian steppes
description: Steppes of the Anatolian Plateau, of Transcaucasia, of the eastern cis-Caucasian hills of Daghestan and the Terek basin, of the Iranian Plateau, the Kopet Dagh, the Pamir-Alai, the extreme western Tien-Shan, around the rim of the Ferghana basin and along the spur of the Karatau, and of northern Mesopotamia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian steppes
description: Steppes of the western Anatolian Plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Irano-Anatolian steppes
description: Steppes of the eastern Anatolian Plateau, of Transcaucasia, of the eastern cis-Caucasian hills of Daghestan and the Terek basin, of the western Iranian Plateau and of northern Mesopotamia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Afghan steppes
description: Steppes of the central and eastern Iranian Plateau, of the Kopet Dagh, the Pamir-Alai and the extreme western Tien-Shan, around the rim of the Ferghana basin and along the spur of the Karatau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Yakutian steppes
description: Steppes of the middle Lena basin of eastern Siberia, formed in regions of extreme continentality near the southern edge of the permafrost and the northern limit of the taiga belt.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sand steppes
description: Formations dominated by medium or tall perennnial tuft-forming grasses or suffrutescents, with lacunar ground cover, together with their associated therophyte communities developed on moving or fixed sands within the range of the continental Eurasian steppes (unit 34.9) and their areas of influence, or of the Mediterranean and sub-Mediterranean steppes of the zones of transition between the Mediterranean and southern Palaearctic desert zones. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.7.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic sand steppes
description: Formations dominated by medium or tall perennnial tuft-forming grasses or suffrutescents, with lacunar ground cover, together with their associated therophyte communities developed on moving or fixed sands within the range of the Pannonic steppes (unit 34.91), thus in the Pannonic basin and the areas of preponderant influence of its communities. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.71.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic sand pioneer swards
description: Therophyte-dominated stages of the first succession phase in the colonisation of Pannonic sands, and in particular of Pannonic dunes (64.71), characterized by a very thin, low cover of mostly ephemereal, early-blooming annuals of small stature, among which [Bromus mollis], [Bromus tectorum], [Bromus squarrosus], [Medicago minima], [Cerastium brachypetalum], [Erophila verna], [Plantago indica], [Saxifraga tridactylites], [Poa annua], [Poa bulbosa], [Viola kitaibeliana], [Lithospermum arvense], [Corispermum nitidum], [Polygonum arenarium], with a few species of longer seasonal visibility, such as [Equisetum ramosissimum] var. [altissimum], [Alyssum tortuosum], [Sedum acre], [Cynodon dactylon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Drooping brome pioneer swards
description: Pioneer sand-swards of the northern Pannonic basin, dominated by [Bromus tectorum], with [Koeleria glauca], [Secale sylvestre], [Cynodon dactylon], [Polygonum arenarium], [Sedum urvillei], [Kochia laniflora], [Plantago arenaria], [Helichrysum arenarium], [Alyssum montanum] ssp. [gmelinii], [Alyssum alyssoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corispermum pioneer swards
description: Pioneer sand-swards of the southern Pannonic basin, in particular of the Deliblat sand-steppe, dominated by [Corispermum nitidum] and [Polygonum arenarium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic horsetail pioneer swards
description: Pioneer sand-swards of the Pannonic basin, well characterized in the Seewinkel, dominated by [Equisetum ramosissimum], with [Scirpus holoschoenus] and small herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic open sand steppes
description: More or less open grasslands constituting the second stage of succession in the colonisation of Pannonic sands, in particular of Pannonic dunes (unit 64.71), best characterized in Hungary and the Vojvodina, with representatives in southern Slovakia, northeastern Austria and western Romania, dominated by the perennial grasses [Festuca vaginata], [Stipa capillata], [Stipa borysthenica], [Cleistogenes serotina], [Koeleria glauca], [Koeleria cristata], [Carex liparocarpos], accompanied by [Euphorbia seguierana], [Alkanna tinctoria], [Alyssum montanum] ssp. [gmelinii], [Dianthus serotinus], [Dianthus diutinus], [Gypsophila paniculata], [Scabiosa ochroleuca], [Astragalus austriacus], [Astragalus onobrychis], [Erysimum diffusum], [Fumana procumbens], [Minuartia glomerata], [Minuartia verna].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic calciphile sand steppes
description: More or less open grasslands constituting the second stage of succession in the colonisation of calcareous Pannonic sands, in particular of Pannonic dunes (64.71), dominated by [Festuca vaginata] or feathergrasses ([Stipa capillata], [Stipa borysthenica]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic calciphile sand fescue steppes
description: More or less open grasslands of calcareous Pannonic sands dominated by [Festuca vaginata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Pannonic calciphile sand fescue steppes
description: Extremely dry, open, semidesertic grasslands of the Hungarian Little Alf”ld and the Slovakian Marchfeld, of the Mez”f”ld and of the Danube-Tisza interfluve, on calcareous sands, with a 50-60% cover at most, constituted by [Festuca vaginata], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Fumana procumbens], [Viola rupestris], [Alyssum tortuosum], [Minuartia fastigiata], and harbouring numerous rare or endemic taxa, including [Achillea ochroleuca], [Corispermum canescens], [Dianthus serotinus], [Colchicum arenarium], [Astragalus exscapus], [Astragalus varius], [Iris arenaria], [Sedum hillebrandtii], [Linum hirsutum] ssp. [glabrescens], [Onosma arenaria], [Centaurea arenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pannonic calciphile sand fescue steppes
description: Open sand steppes of the Carei area of northwestern Romania, in the Nyirseg system of the northeastern Pannonic basin, characteristic of semifixed continental sand, dominated by [Festuca vaginata], with [Poa bulbosa], [Poa angustifolia], [Linaria genistifolia], [Draba verna], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Carex stenophylla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Pannonic calciphile sand fescue steppes
description: Open sand steppes of the Deliblat plateau of the Vojvodina, developed on extremely calcareous sands on which the moss [Barbula ruralis] contributes to the formation of carbonate crusts, dominated by [Festuca vaginata] with [Koeleria glauca], [Poa bulbosa], [Alyssum tortuosum], [Alyssum montanum] ssp. [gmelinii], [Polygonum arenarium], [Centaurea arenaria], [Artemisia campestris]. Representatives of the community irradiate in eastern Serbia to  the confines of the Oltenian plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic feathergrass sand steppes
description: Pioneer perennial grasslands of Pannonic sands, slightly less open than the fescue sand steppes, of which they often constitute a development stage towards closed grasslands, dominated by the tall feathergrasses [Stipa capillata], [Stipa borysthenica] that confer to them a multistrata structure.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Pannonic feathergrass sand steppes
description: [Stipa]-dominated pioneer perennial sand grasslands of the Pannonic basin of Hungary and the Marchfeld of Austria and Slovakia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Pannonic feathergrass sand steppes
description: [Stipa]-dominated pioneer perennial sand grasslands of the Deliblat steppe of the Vojvodina.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic acidophile sand fescue steppes
description: Open grasslands of acidic sands of the Hungarian Little Alf”ld and the Slovakian Marchfeld, of the Mez”f”ld periphery, of the northern Danube-Tisza interfluve, of the Drava basin of Croatia and of the Nyirseg complex of northeastern Hungary and the Carei area of northwestern Romania, formed by an admixture of elements of sub-Atlantic [Corynephorus] swards and of continental, Pannonic, [Festuca vaginata] grasslands, dominated by [Corynephorus canescens], [Festuca vaginata], and with [Minuartia viscosa], [Anchusa officinalis] ssp. [pustulata], [Filago germanica], [Filago minima], [Cynoglossum hungaricum], [Thymus serpyllum], [Veronica verna], [Jasione montana], [Helichrysum arenarium], [Crepis  capillaris], [Equisetum ramosissimum], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Onosma arenaria], [Gypsophila paniculata], [Silene conica], [Koeleria glauca], [Scabiosa argentea] ([Scabiosa ucranica]). They constitute a preferential habitat for the rare and threatened [Pulsatilla hungarica], [Pulsatilla patens] and [Herniaria hirsuta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Festuca wagneri] sand steppes
description: Pannonic semiclosed sand steppes dominated by fescues of the [Festuca wagneri] group, and, in the more evolved stages, by [Stipa spp.], intermediate between the [Festuca vaginata] formations of 34.A12 and the closed [Festuca rupicola] grasslands of 34.A14, with a species cortŠge drawn from both the [Festucion vaginatae] and the [Festucion valesiacae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Pannonic [Festuca wagneri] sand steppes
description: Semiclosed sand steppes of the Hungarian Plains, developed on calcareous sands with a degree of cover reaching 70-80%, usually in contact with the more open swards of the [Festucetum vaginatae], dominated by the endemic [Festuca javorkae] ([Festuca wagneri] [p.]), accompanied by a species assemblage constituted partly of elements of the open perennial grasslands, but mainly of the steppic grasslands, with [Poa pratensis] ssp. [angustifolia], [Centaurea arenaria], [Eryngium campestre], [Galium verum], [Potentilla prenaria], [Verbascum lychnitis], [Silene otites] var. [pseudotites], [Carex liparocarpos], [Scabiosa ochroleuca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Deliblat [Festuca wagneri] sand steppes
description: Semiclosed sand steppes of the Deliblat steppe of the Vojvodina, developed on highly calcareous sands as a transition stage between the [Alysso-Festucetum vaginataea] and the [Chrysopogonetum pannonicum], dominated by the endemic [Festuca wagneri s.s.], with [Festuca rupicola], [Stipa capillata], [Poa bulbosa], [Peucedanum arenarium], [Potentilla cinerea], [Verbascum lychnitis], [Silene otites], [Scabiosa ochroleuca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic closed sand steppes
description: Relatively closed, primary or secondary, fescue or feathergrass swards of basophilous, humus- and nutrient-rich, sandy or mixed sand-loessy soils of the Pannonic basin of Hungary, eastern Austria, southern Slovakia and Transylvania, of relatively rare and sporadic occurrence, dominated by [Festuca rupicola], [Stipa joannis], [Stipa pulcherrima], [Carex humilis], [Stipa capillata], [Koeleria macrantha], [Dichanthium ischaemum], or, in some facies, [Chrysopogon gryllus], with [Carex liparocarpos], [Festuca vaginata], [Festuca wagneri] [s.l.], [Agropyron cristatum] ssp. [pectinatum], [Achillea ochroleuca], [Astragalus asper], [Astragalus onobrychis], [Astragalus exscapus], [Astragalus austriacus], [Oxytropis pilosa], [Potentilla cinerea], [Potentilla arenaria], [Linum austriacum], [Salvia nemorosa], [Alyssum tortuosum], [Alyssum montanum] ssp. [gmelinii], [Silene parviflora], [Silene viscosa], [Dianthus giganteiformis] ssp. [pontederae], [Asperula cynanchica], [Galium glaucum], [Galium verum],  [Pulsatilla grandis], [Pulsatilla nigricans], [Lotus corniculatus], [Onosma arenaria] ssp. [pseudoarenaria], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Euphorbia nicaeensis] ssp. [glareosa] ([Euphorbia glareosa], [Euphorbia pannonica]), [Artemisia alba], [Artemisia campestris], [Artemisia laciniata], [Artemisia pancicii], [Thymus glabrescens], [Daphne cneorum], [Cytisus ratisbonensis], [Muscari botryoides], [Muscari comosum], [Iris variegata], [Iris humilis] ssp. [arenaria], [Colchicum arenarium], [Ophrys sphegodes], [Anacamptis pyramidalis], [Botrychium lunaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic sand puszta
description: Fescue pastures of sandy alluvial soils of the Pannonic basin, distributed in the Austrian Seewinkel, the Hungarian plains, the Banat, the Crisana and Transylvania, forming a mosaic with saline pusztas (unit 15.A11) and water-edge vegetation to constitute the puszta landscape, formed by [Festuca pseudovina], [Potentilla arenaria], [Cynodon dactylon], [Carex stenophylla] and, in some stands, [Festuca valesiaca], with [Fragaria viridis], [Cerastium semidecandrum], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Eryngium campestre], [Thymus glabrescens], [Poa bulbosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Sarmatic sand steppes
description: Formations dominated by medium or tall perennnial tuft-forming grasses or suffrutescents, with lacunar ground cover, together with their associated therophyte communities developed on moving or fixed sands within the range of the Ponto-Sarmatic steppes (unit 34.92) and the regions of influence of their communities. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under units 64.72 and 64.73.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of the plains of the western Black Sea, west of the Dniester, and of the basin of the lower Danube. Most of the formations listed are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.72. Within the steppe region, differences between inland and coastal sand communities are attenuated, so that some of the formations listed here may also occur in coastal grey dunes; communities that are specific to these have, however, not been included in this unit, but only in unit 16.22B.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic sand pioneer swards
description: Therophyte-dominated stages of the first succession phase in the colonisation of western Pontic sands, with a thin, low cover of mostly ephemereal, early-blooming annuals of small stature.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic sand pioneer grass swards
description: Therophyte stages of the first succession phase in the colonisation of western Pontic sands, dominated by annual grasses, [Bromus tectorum], [Apera spica-venti] ([Apera maritima]), [Secale sylvestre], with [Cynodon dactylon], [Polygonum arenarium], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Centaurea arenaria], [Alyssum desertorum], [Silene conica], [Syrenia montana], [Convolvulus persicus], [Koeleria glauca], [Scabiosa argentea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic sand pioneer forb swards
description: Therophyte stages of the first succession phase in the colonisation of western Pontic sands, dominated by annual forbs, [Plantago arenaria] ([Plantago indica]), [Mollugo cerviana], with [Polygonum arenarium], [Viola kitaibeliana], [Viola hymettia], [Centaurea arenaria], [Achillea ochroleuca], [Syrenia cana], [Silene conica], [Bromus tectorum], [Apera spica-venti].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic open sand steppes
description: More or less open grasslands constituting the second stage of succession in the colonisation of western Pontic sands, dominated by perennial grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wallachian open sand steppes
description: Open perennial grasslands colonizing sands of Oltenia, Muntenia and southern Moldavia, dominated by [Festuca vaginata] with [Koeleria glauca], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Polygonum anarium], [Kochia laniflora], [Gypsophila paniculata], [Astragalus virgatus], [Astragalus varius], [Onosma arenaria], [Centaurea arenaria], [Tragopogon floccosus], [Echinops ruthenicus] and, in Oltenia, [Corispermum nitidum], [Teucrium polium], [Viola kitaibeliana], [Asperula tenella].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Danubiano-Pontic open sand steppes
description: Open perennial grasslands of the inland sands of the Danube Delta and the northern Dobrogea, characterized by [Festuca arenicola] ([Festuca beckeri]), [Stipa borysthenica], [Scabiosa argentea], [Syrenia montana] and with [Koeleria glauca], [Carex ligerica], [Fumana procumbens], [Minuartia setacea], [Ephedra distachya].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic fescue-feathergrass sand steppes
description: Open perennial grasslands of Danube delta inland sands, dominated by [Festuca arenicola] ([Festuca beckeri]) or [Stipa borysthenica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic scabiosa sand steppes
description: Open perennial grasslands of Danube delta, Dobrogea and northern Thrace inland sands, usually dominated by [Carex ligerica] ([Carex colchica]), with [Scabiosa argentea] ([Scabiosa ucranica]), [Alyssum borzaeanum], [Astragalus virgatus], [Secale sylvestre], [Koeleria glauca], [Festuca arenicola] ([Festuca beckeri]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic [Helichrysum] sand steppes
description: Open perennial grasslands of Danube delta and Dobrogea inland sands, dominated by [Festuca arenicola] ([Festuca beckeri]) and [Helichrysum ponticum], with [Secale sylvestre], [Peucedanum arenarium], [Achillea ochroleuca], [Centaurea arenaria], [Tragopogon floccosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic closed sand steppes
description: Relatively closed, primary or secondary, [Chrysopogon gryllus], [Festuca spp.] or [Stipa spp.] swards of humus- and nutrient-rich, sandy or mixed sand-loessy soils of Oltenia, Muntenia, southern Moldavia the Danube delta, the Dobrogea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic sand pastures
description: Fescue pastures of sandy alluvial soils of Oltenia, Muntenia and southern Moldavia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of the wooded steppe belt occupying, north of the Pontic and Caspian plains, the southern edge and valleys of the Podolian, Central Russian and Volga plateaux east to the Volga-Kama trough. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.73.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain, of the basins of the Dnieper and the Don, within the range of eastern Pontic steppes of unit 34.923, extending west to the Dniestr, northeast to the Volga, east to the Caspian deserts and semideserts, southeast to the pre-Caucasian hills in the basins of the Kouban, the Manytch, the upper Kuma and upper Terek. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.72.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian sand steppes
description: Formations dominated by medium or tall perennnial tuft-forming grasses or suffrutescents, with lacunar ground cover, together with their associated therophyte communities developed on moving or fixed sands of the steppe and wooded steppe belts of extreme eastern Europe and western Siberia, extending from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east, including the Transvolgan steppes of Orenburg and Bachkiria, the Kurgan, Ishim, Baraba, Kulunda, Barnaul, Kirgiz, Kazakh steppes, and the mountain steppes of the Tarbagatai and the Altai (unit 34.93). Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.74.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian sand steppes
description: Formations dominated by medium or tall perennnial tuft-forming grasses or suffrutescents, with lacunar ground cover, together with their associated therophyte communities developed on moving or fixed sands within the range of the East Asian steppes (unit 34.94) of Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, the Songnen Plain of Northeast China, the western Loess Plateau of North China, the mountain steppes of the Tien Shan, from the rim of the Naryn and Isyk-K”l basins eastwards, of the Sayan and Tannu mountains. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.75.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian sand steppes
description: Formations dominated by medium or tall perennnial tuft-forming grasses or suffrutescents, with lacunar ground cover, together with their associated therophyte communities developed on moving or fixed sands of the Anatolian Plateau, of Transcaucasia, of the Iranian Plateau and of northern Mesopotamia, in the Irano-Anatolian zone of transition between the continental Eurasian steppes and the Mediterranean and southern Palaearctic desert zones, of the eastern cis-Caucasian hills of Daghestan and the Terek basin, the Kopet Dagh, the Pamir-Alai, the extreme western Tien-Shan. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.76.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of the western Anatolian Plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Irano-Anatolian sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of the eastern Anatolian Plateau, of Transcaucasia, of the eastern cis-Caucasian hills of Daghestan and the Terek basin, of the western Iranian Plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Afghan sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of the central and eastern Iranian Plateau, of the Kopet Dagh, the Pamir-Alai and the extreme western Tien-Shan, around the rim of the Ferghana basin and along the spur of the Karatau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Mesopotamian sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of northern Mesopotamia, in the Irano-Anatolian zone of transition between the continental Eurasian steppes and the Mediterranean and southern Palaearctic desert zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African sand steppes
description: Sand steppes of the North African Hauts Plateaux, in particular, communities dominated by [Festuca deserti] ssp. [duriaei]. Most of these formations are associated with inland dune systems and define subdivisions of habitats listed under unit 64.77.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern steppic and calcareous grasslands
description: Steppic grasslands of continental affinities and dry thermophilous grasslands of the Far Eastern nemoral, boreonemoral and warm temperate forest zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dry siliceous grasslands
description: Short, mostly secondary, grasslands and therophyte communities colonizing acidic, well-drained soils of the lowland, hill and montane levels of the nemoral, boreal, mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones. In particular, Atlantic and sub-Atlantic mat-grasslands of strongly acid soils, grasslands and therophyte communities of decalcified sands, Mediterranean siliceous grasslands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic closed acidophilous grasslands
description: Closed, dry or mesophile, perennial grasslands occupying acid soils in Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of northern Europe, middle Europe and western Iberia, with [Nardus stricta], [Festuca filiformis] ([Festuca tenuifolia]), [Festuca ovina], [Festuca rubra], [Agrostis capillaris], [Danthonia decumbens], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Poa angustifolia], [Galium saxatile], [Polygala vulgaris], [Viola canina], [Meum athamanticum], [Arnica montana], [Centaurea nigra], [Dianthus deltoides], [Gentianella campestris], [Chamaespartium sagittale], [Jasione laevis], [Potentilla erecta], [Carex pilulifera]. Any of the grasses listed can dominate or codominate distinctive facies; [Calamagrostis epigejos] or [Carex arenaria] also can invade and dominate some formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mat-grass swards
description: Mesophile and xerophile [Nardus stricta]-dominated or -rich grasslands of Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of northern Europe, middle Europe and western Iberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Insular [Nardus]-[Galium] grasslands
description: Mesophile and xerophile [Nardus stricta]-dominated or -rich grasslands of the British Isles and the Faeroe Islands, with [Agrostis capillaris], [Galium saxatile], [Potentilla erecta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic [Nardus]-[Galium] grasslands
description: Mesophile and xerophile [Nardus stricta]-dominated or -rich grasslands of Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of the mainland of Europe, extending north to western Jutland, northern Jutland, nemoral and boreonemoral southern Sweden, nemoral southern Norway and oceanic southern boreal Norway, east to Poland, Lithuania, the Bohemian Quadrangle, the Carpathians and the Austrian pre-Alps, southwest to Asturias and Cantabria; the species cortŠge includes [Polygala vulgaris], [Hypericum maculatum] f. [glabrum], [Galium saxatile], [Carex panicea], [Hieracium umbellatum], [Hypochoeris maculata], [Genista tinctoria], [Arnica montana], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Plantago lanceolata], [Potentilla erecta], [Thymus pulegioides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Beskid [Calluna]-[Nardus] grassland
description: Endemic grassland community of the Beskid vicinity of Poland, dominated by [Nardus stricta], accompanied by [Danthonia decumbens] ([Sieglingia decumbens]), [Viola canina] var. [ericetorum], [Polygala vulgaris] and invaded to a varying degree by [Calluna vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bohemian orchid-matgrass swards
description: Rare grassland community of the Czech and Austrian Bohemian Forest (Sumava) and of the Austrian southeastern pre-Alps, dominated by [Nardus stricta] with [Carex pallescens], [Gymnadenia conopsea], [Orchis mascula], [Dactylorhiza majalis], [Platanthera bifolia], [Phyteuma nigrum], [Lychnis flos-cuculi], [Anemone nemorosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian mat-grass swards
description: Mesophile and xerophile [Nardus stricta]-dominated or -rich grasslands of relatively high-rainfall lowland, collinar and montane regions of the Dinarides of Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Yugoslavia, northwestern Albania, mostly characteristic of the [Fagion illyricum] beech level and of the heaths of the [Carpinion illyricum] environment, extending into the Adriatic-influenced western forests of the [Fagion moesiacum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands
description: Closed mesophile or dry grasslands of the nemoral and boreal zones of Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of Europe formed by [Agrostis spp.] and [Festuca spp.], in association with other grasses such as [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Hierochloe odorata], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Danthonia decumbens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands
description: Closed mesophile grasslands of Atlantic and, locally, of sub-Atlantic, middle Europe, mostly characteristic of the nemoral zone, extending north to the boreonemoral zone and, locally, to the boreal zone, formed by [Agrostis spp.] and [Festuca spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands
description: Widespread upland mesophile grasslands and sheep pastures of the British Isles, and especially the Scottish Highlands, with abundant [Agrostis capillaris], [Agrostis canina], [Festuca ovina], and with [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Holcus lanatus], [Carex pilulifera], [Alchemilla alpina] [s.l.], [Galium saxatile].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Galium] grasslands
description: Species-poor [Festuca]-[Agrostis] grasslands of the western and northern uplands of Britain, very widespread on base-poor mineral soils in regions of high rainfall, dominated by mixtures of [Festuca ovina], [Festuca rubra], [Agrostis capillaris], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], with frequent [Galium saxatile], [Potentilla erecta], [Luzula campestris], [Viola riviniana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Thymus] grasslands
description: Species-rich, weakly acidophile to basicline, [Festuca]-[Agrostis] grasslands of the northern and western submontane zone of Britain, south to damp north-facing slopes of the Mendips and Derbyshire, developed on locally base-rich brown earth under rainy climates with more than 1000 mm of annual rainfall, dominated by [Agrostis capillaris], [Festuca ovina], [Festuca rubra], [Nardus stricta], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Danthonia decumbens], with [Thymus praecox], [Plantago lanceolata], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Prunella vulgaris], [Viola riviniana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Alchemilla] grasslands
description: Grass-heaths of higher submontane altitudes of Scotland and locally of Cambria, developed at altitudes mostly above 500 m under rainy climates with precipitation of up to 2000 mm, in trophic conditions somewhat intermediate between those of the acidophile species-poor communities of unit 35.12111 and the basicline species-rich communities of unit 35.12112, in particular, on Dalradian metasediments, characterized by the prominence of [Alchemilla alpina], associated with [Agrostis capillaris], [Festuca ovina], [Festuca vivipara], [Nardus stricta], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], and with [Thymus praecox], [Galium saxatile], [Potentilla erecta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian boreo-nemoral [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands
description: Closed mesophile [Agrostis] and [Festuca] grasslands of nemoral, boreonemoral, Atlantic and, locally, lowland boreal, Scandinavia and the Faeroe Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Galium] grasslands
description: Species-poor acidophilous grasslands or heath-grasslands, parallel to the Britannic [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Galium] grasslands of unit 35.12111, distributed in southern Fennoscandia in the nemoral zone of Denmark and southern Sweden, in the boreonemoral zone of southeastern Norway and Sweden, in the oceanic southern boreal zone of Norway, in southern parts of the southern boreal zone of Sweden, in extreme southern Finland, and on the Faeroe Islands, dominated by [Festuca ovina] or [Agrostis capillaris], with frequent [Galium saxatile], [Achillea millefolium], [Stellaria graminea], [Veronica chamaedrys], [Veronica officinalis], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Luzula campestris]; [Festuca vivipara] and [Luzula multiflora] are frequent in the Faeroe communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Festuca]-[Lychnis]-[Thymus] grasslands
description: Short herb-rich [Festuca]-[Agrostis] grasslands of Scandinavia, distributed north to the midboreal zone, parallel to the Britannic [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Thymus] grasslands of unit 35.12112, variously dominated by [Festuca ovina], [Lychnis viscaria], [Luzula campestris] or [Thymus serpyllum], with [Achillea millefolium], [Agrostis capillaris], [Alchemilla glaucescens], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Dianthus deltoides], [Galium verum], [Lathyrus linifolius], [Polygala vulgaris], [Pulsatilla vulgaris], [Ranunculus bulbosus], [Ranunculus polyanthemum], [Saxifraga granulata], [Silene nutans], [Stellaria graminea], [Veronica chamaedrys], [Vicia tetrasperma].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Alchemilla] grasslands
description: Relatively short, moderately herb-rich [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands of nemoral, boreonemoral, Atlantic and, locally, lowland boreal, Scandinavia and of the Faeroe Islands, parallel to the Britannic [Agrostis]-[Festuca]-[Alchemilla] grasslands of unit 35.12113, dominated by [Agrostis capillaris] with [Alchemilla spp.], [Trifolium repens], [Achillea alpina], [Festuca ovina], [Rhytidiadelphus squarrosus], and a species cortŠge that varies within the area of occurrence; in particular, communities of oceanic western Norway comprise [Conopodium majus], [Festuca vivipara], [Galium saxatile], [Cardamine pratensis], [Hypochoeris maculata], [Luzula campestris], [Platanthera bifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallo-Britannic [Agrostis curtisii] grasslands
description: Mesoxerophile thermo-Atlantic acidophilous grasslands of France and southern England dominated by [Agrostis curtisii] or [Pseudarrhenatherum longifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Agrostis curtisii] grasslands
description: Acidophilous grasslands of southern England, mostly restricted to the South-West Peninsula with outliers in the southern part of the New Forest and in neighbouring areas, dominated by the strongly sespitose [Agrostis curtisii], substitution grasslands of heathlands favoured by burning and grazing. [Festuca ovina], [Danthonia decumbens], [Agrostis capillaris] are the most frequent accompanying grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallic [Agrostis curtisii] grasslands
description: Mesoxerophile thermo-Atlantic acidophilous grasslands of France dominated by [Agrostis curtisii] or [Pseudarrhenatherum longifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands
description: [Agrostis], [Festuca] and [Danthonia] grasslands of northwestern Spain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands
description: [Festuca], [Avena] and [Genista sagittalis] grasslands of the Black Forest, the High Palatinat, the Swabian Alb and the Swabo-Bavarian pre-Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic [Agrostis]-[Festuca] grasslands
description: Grasslands of subarctic affinities of the northern boreal and middle boreal zones of northern Scandinavia and northwestern Russia, of the alpine and arcto-alpine zones of the Caledonian chains of Scandinavia and of lowlands and hills of Iceland, composed of [Festuca spp.], [Agrostis capillaris], with  [Anthoxanthum odoratum], other grass species, often with [Polygonum viviparum] and other herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-subalpine [Agrostis] grasslands
description: Relatively short grasslands of lower mountain slopes of northern Scandinavia and of lowlands and hills of Iceland dominated by [Agrostis capillaris] or [Anthoxanthum odoratum], with [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]) and [Carex bigelowii]. These grasslands are strongly influenced by, and perhaps entirely dependent on, grazing or mowing.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian [Agrostis]-[Bistorta] grasslands
description: Relatively short grasslands of lower mountain slopes of northern Scandinavia dominated by [Agrostis capillaris], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Carex bigelowii], occupying quite stony though well-developed soils, with a sufficient moisture supplied by prolonged snow cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Anthoxanthum]-[Galium] grasslands
description: Relatively short grasslands of lowlands and hills of Iceland dominated by [Anthoxanthum odoratum], with [Agrostis capillaris], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Carex bigelowii], [Galium normanii], [Luzula multiflora], occupying well-developed soils on stoney substrates, with a sufficient moisture supplied by prolonged snow cover, also colonizing lava fields and alluvions, constituting good pastures and often intensively grazed.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Anthoxanthum]-[Hierochloe] grasslands
description: Grasslands of Iceland dominated by [Agrostis capillaris], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Hierochlo‰ odorata], with a species cortŠge similar to that of unit 35.1221, occurring under similar conditions but with a somewhat longer-lasting snow cover. Some stands are dominated by [Deschampsia flexuosa] and are included in unit 35.132.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern boreal [Festuca] grasslands
description: Herb-rich grasslands, 20-40 cm tall, developed on sandy soils, often on inundatable terrain, under cold-temperate climates, characteristic of the northern boreal zone of Fennoscandia and northwestern Russia, extending locally in the middle boreal zone of eastern Sweden and Finland and in the alpine and arcto-alpine zones of the Caledonian chains of Scandinavia, dominated by [Festuca ovina] with a cortŠge, rich in northern species, that includes [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Carex vaginata], [Achillea millefolium], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Galium boreale], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Rubus arcticus], [Solidago virgaurea], [Thalictrum simplex], [Trollius europaeus], [Veronica longifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Festuca] grasslands
description: Grasslands of lowlands and lower mountains of Iceland and of the Faeroe Islands dominated by fescues of the [Festuca rubra] group, in particular, [Festuca vivipara], with a species cortŠge otherwise similar to that of unit 35.12212, including, in particular, [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Kobresia myosuroides], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Carex bigelowii], developed on somewhat drier and sandier substrates than the grasslands of unit 35.12212.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Avenula pratensis]-[Festuca rubra] grasslands
description: Dry or mesophile calcareous grasslands of subarctic affinities, limited to the continental middle boreal zone of lowland Sweden and northern Finland and to the middle boreal and arcto-alpine zones of the Scandinavian mountains; they constitute a northern, less species-rich, variant of the communities of unit 32.111, dominated by [Festuca rubra], with [Botrychum boreale], [Botrychum lanceolatum], [Botrychum lunaria], [Carex brunnescens], [Carex ericetorum], [Cerastium alpinum], [Erigeron borealis], [Galium boreale], [Gentiana nivalis], [Gentianella amarella], [Gentianella campestris], [Gentianella tenella], [Poa glauca], [Primula scandinavica], [Primula striata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Deschampsia flexuosa] grasslands
description: Closed, dry or mesophile, perennial grasslands occupying acid soils in Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of northern Europe, north to Iceland and southern Scandinavia, middle Europe and western Iberia dominated by [Deschampsia flexuosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral [Deschampsia flexuosa] grasslands
description: Closed, dry or mesophile, perennial grasslands occupying acid soils in Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of nemoral Europe, north to southern Scandinavia, and south to western Iberia, dominated by [Deschampsia flexuosa], forming, in particular, as degradation stages of [Calluna vulgaris] and other heaths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-arctic [Deschampsia flexuosa] grasslands
description: Closed, dry or mesophile, perennial grasslands of subarctic affinities occupying acid soils in Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of Iceland and northern continental Europe, dominated by [Deschampsia flexuosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wood small-reed stands
description: Tall [Calamagrostis epigejos]-dominated facies of siliceous grasslands of Atlantic or sub-Atlantic northern and middle Europe of units 35.11 or 35.12.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sand sedge grasslands
description: Closed acidophilous grasslands of Atlantic or sub-Atlantic lowland, collinar and montane regions of northern Europe, middle Europe and western Iberia dominated by [Carex arenaria], invasion facies of grasslands of units 35.11 and 35.12.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Medio-European open siliceous grasslands
description: Open grassland formations of dry, siliceous soils, of Atlantic, sub-Atlantic and Mediterraneo-montane Europe, often species-poor and with a strong representation of annuals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf annual siliceous grasslands
description: Pioneer formations of typically dwarf annuals, often ephemeral and of very limited extent, characteristic in particular of fixed sands, of Atlantic, sub-Atlantic and supramediterranean Europe, with [Aira caryophyllea], [Aira praecox], [Micropyrum tenellum] ([Nardurus lachenalii]), [Vulpia bromoides], [Vulpia myuros], [Trisetum ovatum], [Filago arvensis], [Filago gallica], [Filago lutescens], [Filago minima], [Filago pyramidata], [Filago vulgaris], [Spergularia morisonii], [Hypochoeris glabra], [Evax carpetana], [Moenchia erecta], [Scleranthus polycarpos], [Teesdalia nudicaulis], [Myosotis discolor], [Myosotis stricta], [Linaria elegans], [Linaria amethystea], [Sedum lagascae], [Sedum pedicellatum], [Ornithopus perpusillus], [Trifolium striatum], [Trifolium arvense], [Trifolium dubium], [Trifolium campestre], [Trifolium micranthum], [Tuberaria guttata]; typical former crop-following species also find a refuge in these communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Perennial open siliceous grasslands
description: Open or semi-open grasslands of fixed sands and dry ground of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Europe dominated by perennial grasses such as [Agrostis capillaris], [Agrostis vinealis], [Agrostis delicatula], [Agrostis durieui], [Agrostis castellana], [Poa angustifolia], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Festuca filiformis], [Corynephorus canescens], [Calamagrostis epigejos] or [Carex arenaria], usually succeeding to formations of unit 35.23 or 35.21 and constituting a transition towards unit 35.1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Corynephorus] grasslands
description: Very open grasslands of mobile or poorly fixed sands of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Europe, dominated by [Corynephorus canescens], sometimes by [Leymus arenarius] or [Carex arenaria]; most are dunal and enter in the composition of subunits of unit 64 (Inland dunes).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean therophytic siliceous grasslands
description: West Mediterranean and Dalmatian annual-rich grasslands of siliceous gravelly, sandy or silty, usually shallow, soils that remain cohesive during the dry season; they are rich in small Fabaceae, in particular of genera,  [Trifolium], [Lathyrus], [Ornithopus], [Lupinus], [Anthyllis], [Coronilla] and grasses of genera [Corynephorus], [Aira], [Airopsis], [Molineria], [Vulpia], [Briza], [Anthoxanthum], [Micropyrum]; among characteristic species, shared by eastern and western formations, are [Tuberaria guttata], [Silene gallica], [Linaria pelisseriana], [Plantago bellardii], [Galium divaricatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Mediterranean siliceous grasslands
description: West Mediterranean annual-rich grasslands of siliceous gravelly, sandy or silty, usually shallow, soils that remain cohesive during the dry season; characteristic are [Tuberaria guttata], [Helianthemum sanguineum], [Jasione montana], [Paronychia cymosa], [Paronychia echinulata], [Pterocephalus diandrus], [Prolongoa pectinata], [Senecio minutus], [Tolpis barbata], [Filago gallica], [Filago minima], [Teesdalia coronopifolia], [Sedum caespitosum], [Sedum arenarium], [Sedum andegavense], [Crassula tillaea], [Saxifraga carpetana], [Radiola linoides], [Silene gallica], [Silene psammitis], [Silene portensis], [Linum gallicum], [Linaria pelisseriana], [Linaria arvensis], [Plantago bellardii], [Galium divaricatum], [Trifolium cherleri], [Trifolium strictum], [Trifolium suffocatum], [Trifolium arvense], [Trifolium bocconei], [Trifolium purpureum], [Lathyrus angulatus], [Ornithopus pinnatus], [Ornithopus sativus], [Lupinus hispanicus], [Lupinus angustifolius], [Anthyllis cornicina], [Coronilla dura] and the grasses [Corynephorus divaricatus], [Aira cupaniana], [Aira tenorii], [Aira caryophyllea], [Airopsis tenella], [Molineria minuta], [Molineria laevis], [Vulpia geniculata], [Vulpia membranacea], [Vulpia bromoides], [Vulpia myuros], [Briza maxima], [Anthoxanthum aristatum], [Micropyrum tenellum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dalmatian siliceous grasslands
description: Uncommon acidophile annual-rich grasslands of Dalmatia occupying small, insularised surfaces on colluvions and red earths of the Dalmatian karst and on southern Dalmatian sands; characteristic are [Tuberaria guttata], [Filago vulgaris], [Silene gallica], [Linaria pelisseriana], [Plantago bellardii], [Galium parisiense], [Hypochoeris radicata], [Cynanchum contiguum], [Crepis sancta], [Trifolium cherleri], [Trifolium lappaceum], [Trifolium subterraneum], [Trifolium stellatum], [Trifolium glomeratum], [Trifolium nigrescens], [Trifolium angustifolium], [Lathyrus sphaericus], [Ornithopus compressus], [Lupinus micranthus], [Lupinus lacromensis], [Luzula campestris] and the grasses [Aira elegans], [Vulpia ligustica], [Vulpia bromoides], [Vulpia myuros], [Briza maxima], [Anthoxanthum ovatum], [Gastridium ventricosum], [Gaudinia fragilis], [Phleum echinatum], [Psilurus aristatus]; the orchids [Ophrys apifera], [Ophrys oestrifera], [Spiranthes spiralis] are recorded.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean annual deep-sand communities
description: Open, spring-blooming communities of annuals developed on deep sands of Iberia, of Mediterranean North Africa and, very locally, of southern France and Italy, with [Malcolmia lacera], [Malcolmia ramosissima], [Anthyllis hamosa], [Maresia nana], [Erodium laciniatum], [Erodium cicutarium] ssp. [bipinnatum], [Arenaria emarginata], [Hymenostemma pseudanthemis], [Loeflingia baetica], [Loeflingia spartea], [Loeflingia tavaresiana], [Loeflingia hispanica], [Linaria donyana], [Linaria pedunculata], [Vulpia membranacea], [Ononis variegata], [Ononis baetica], [Ononis cossoniana], [Ononis subspicata], [Coronilla repanda], [Evax asterisciflora], [Evax lusitanica], [Leucojum trichophyllum]. Many are dunal and have been listed under unit 16.228; others occur on coastal gravel banks, in conjunction with unit 17.43.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supramediterranean perennial siliceous grasslands
description: Open perennial grasslands and pastures colonizing siliceous, usually poorly developed soils of the supramediterranean levels of Iberian mountains and the southern Balkan and northern Hellenic peninsulas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian fescue-plantain grasslands
description: Open perennial formations colonizing arenaceous or skeletal, often unstable, siliceous soils of the supra-Mediterranean levels of Iberian mountains, rich in cushion-forming, rosette-leaved chamaephytes ([Jasione crispa] ssp. [sessiliflora], [Plantago radicata], [Scleranthus perennis]) and cespitose, rough perennial grasses ([Festuca costei], [Festuca indigesta], [Festuca summilusitana], [Corynephorus canescens], [Koeleria caudata] ssp. [crassipes]). Various formations, characterized by, among others, [Hieracium castellanum], [Leucanthemopsis pulverulenta], [Dianthus merinoi], [Dianthus laricifolius], [Armeria caballeroi], [Armeria alliacea], [Thymus serpylloides] ssp. [gadorensis], [Teucrium aureum] are distributed in the Cantabrian range, the southern Galician and Leonese mountains, the Iberian Range, the Cordillera Central, the Montes de Toledo, the Sierra Nevada.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic supramediterranean siliceous grasslands
description: Open perennial grasslands and pastures colonizing siliceous, usually poorly developed soils of the supramediterranean levels of the southern Balkan peninsula and northern Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Balkanic clover dry siliceous grasslands
description: Perennial grasslands and pastures of siliceous soils of the 500-1000 m supramediterranean level of hills and mountains of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and northern Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Balkanic thrift-cinquefoil dry siliceous grasslands
description: Perennial grasslands and pastures of siliceous soils of the 1000-1250 m supramediterranean level of mountains of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and northern Greece, with [Armeria rumelica], [Potentilla argenta], [Potentilla inclinata], [Euphrasia liburnica], [Leontodon hispidus], [Veronica austriaca], [Helianthemum numularium], [Filipendula vulgaris], [Rhinanthus rhumelicus], [Plantago carinata], [Asperula cynanchica], [Koeleria macrantha], [Festuca dalmatica], [Agrostis byzanthina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian tall fescue grasslands
description: Perennial grasslands dominated by the tall cespitose [Festuca elegans] of the supra-Mediterranean [Quercus pyrenaica] level of the Cordillera Central and Sierra Nevada with, among others, [Geum heterocarpum], [Trifolium ochroleucon] and [Paeonia coriacea] of deep, siliceous soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-montane mat-grass swards
description: [Nardus stricta]-dominated grasslands and related communities of the supra-mediterranean level of the mountains of the Mediterranean peninsulas, either developed on siliceous soils, or, rarely, on calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian montane mat-grass swards
description: Supra-mediterranean acidophilous communities rich in [Nardus stricta] with an accompanying cortŠge similar to that of the Iberian subalpine [Campanulo-Nardion] (unit 36.36), rather than to that of the Atlantic and sub-Atlantic [Violion caninae] (unit 35.1), occurring in particular in the [Quercus pyrenaica] level of the Cordillera Central.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Italian mat-grass swards and related communities
description: Closed, mesophile grasslands of depressions, flats and snow patches of the beech level of the southern Apennines, with [Luzula multiflora], [Luzula pindica], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Festuca rubra], [Festuca varia] [s.l.], [Festuca violacea], [Bellardiochloa violacea] ([Poa violacea]), [Alopecurus gerardii], [Danthonia decumbens], [Phleum alpinum], [Carex leporina], [Hypochoeris laevigata], [Dianthus deltoides], [Nardus stricta], [Crocus vernus], [Sedum atratum], [Euphrasia minima], [Ajuga tenorii] ([Ajuga acaulis]), [Potentilla neumanniana] var. [rigoana], [Potentilla argentea] var. [calabra], [Ranunculus sartorianus], [Ranunculus polyanthemos] ssp. [thomasii], [Meum athamanticum], [Asphodelus albus] var. [pollinensis], [Plantago brutia], [Pedicularis petiolaris], [Omalotheca sylvatica] ([Gnaphalium sylvaticum]), [Cirsium vallis-demoni], [Viola calcarata], [Armeria majellensis]; they are widespread in the siliceous Sila range and also occur on deep decalcified soils of the piani of the calcareous Pollino range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkanic montane mat-grass swards
description: Closed [Nardus stricta]-dominated grasslands of the [Fagion moesiacum] zone of the Balkan peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern dry siliceous grasslands
description: Short, mostly secondary, grasslands and therophyte communities colonizing acidic, well-drained soils of the lowland, hill and montane levels of the nemoral, boreal and warm-temperate humid zones of the Far Eastern Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine and subalpine grasslands
description: Primary and secondary grass- or sedge- dominated formations of the alpine and subalpine levels of boreal, nemoral, warm-temperate humid and Irano-Turanian mountains, and of the oro- and cryoro-Mediterranean levels ([sensu] Peinado Lorca and Rivas-Martinez,1987) or the alti-Mediterranean level ([sensu] Ozenda, 1975, 1985) of Mediterranean mountains. Euro-Siberian formations comprise the grasslands of the Alps, Carpathians, Dinaric Alps, Pyrenees, Cantabrian range, Jura, Central Massif, northern Apennines, Balkan Range, Scandinavian mountains, Urals, Siberian mountains, and of Iceland, and have very fragmentary outposts in the great Hercynian ranges of middle Europe, including the Black Forest, the Harz and the mountains of the Bohemian Quadrangle, Bohemian Forest (Sumava), Metallic Mountains (Erzgebirge, Krusne Hory), the Sudeten (Krkonose, Karkonosze or Riesengebirge; Jesenik Mountains), and in the Caledonian system of Britain. Mediterranean formations include grasslands of the Iberian mountains, of the Apennines, of the Hellenic ranges, of the Taurus complex and of the Atlas system. Central Eurasian grasslands occupy the alpine and subalpine levels of the Caucasus, of the Crimea, of the Western and Central Asian mountains, of the Himalayan system. Sino-Japanese grasslands occupy the Far Eastern mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Snow-patch communities
description: Vegetation of areas that retain late-lying snow. These formations are very developed in boreal and arctic mountains and in subarctic lowlands; they are well represented, though on much smaller surfaces, in the alpine level of the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Carpathians, the Caucasus and the major Asiatic mountains; towards and into the Mediterranean region, they extend to the Paeonian mountains and are represented by relict outposts in the Sierra Nevada, the Cordillera Central, the Monti Sibillini and Abruzzi, North Africa; they occur locally in the Scottish Highlands and in the Sudeten.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Alpic acidocline snow-patch communities
description: Acidophile or acidocline snow-patch and snowbed communities of the boreal and arcto-alpine mountains, including the Caledonian mountains of Scotland, and of the western Alpids and their satellite Hercynian ranges, developed on siliceous substrates or on leached and podzolized soils over calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic acid snow-patch communities
description: Acid snow-patch communities of the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Carpathians, the Sudeten and high mountains of the Mediterranean peninsulas, with [Salix herbacea], [Soldanella pusilla], [Sibbaldia procumbens], [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), [Luzula alpinopilosa], [Cerastium cerastoides] and mosses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic acid moss snow-patch communities
description: Moss snow-patches of the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Rhodopides (Rila) and the Pelagonides, occupying areas free from snow for less than two months, with the mosses [Polytrichum sexangulare], [Polytrichum juniperinum], [Pohlia commutata], [Kiaeria falcata] ([Dicranum falcatum]), the liverwort [Anthelia juratzkana] or sometimes lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic acid dwarf willow snow-patch communities
description: Dwarf willow ([Salix herbacea]) snow-patches of the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Carpathians, the Dinarids, the Pelagonides, the Pirin and Rila mountains, occupying areas covered by snow for up to eight to ten months.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic acid cudweed snow-patch communities
description: Communities of areas covered by snow for six to eight months, with [Carex foetida], [Alopecurus gerardii], [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]) (including [Omalotheca supina] var.
