[pusilla]), [Lepidium stylatum], [Alchemilla pentaphyllea], [Mucizonia sedoides], ([Umbilicus sedoides], [Sedum candollei]), [Sedum alpestre], [Cardamine alpina], [Carex pyrenaica], of the Alps, the eastern Carpathian system, the ranges of the Balkan peninsula, the Pyrenees; they extend to the subalpine level and include the isolated cryoro-Mediterranean formations of the Cordillera Central and the Sierra Nevada.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Luzula spadicea] snow patch communities
description: [Luzula alpinopilosa] ssp. [obscura] ([Luzula spadicea])-dominated snow patch communities of moderate slopes of the Alps and the Carpathians submitted to prolonged snow cover, ecological variant of the [Luzula spadicea] scree communities of 61.113, more prevalent in the central and eastern Alps, the Tatras and the eastern Carpathians, characterized by an important representation of species of the [Salicetea herbaceae], among which [Poa granitica], [Ranunculus montanus], [Oligotrichum hercynicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian acid snow patch communities
description: Acidophilous snow patch communities of the higher Hercynian ranges, in particular the Sudeten, the Black Forest, the Vosges, with [Nardus stricta], [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), [Plantago atrata], [Salix herbacea], [Polytrichum gracile], [Polytrichum norvegicum], or with [Luzula desvauxii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal acidocline snowbed communities
description: Snow-patch communities of the high altitudes of the Fennoscandian mountains, the Urals, the Siberian mountains, Iceland, the Arctic basin islands, the Highlands of Scotland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal moss snowbed communities
description: Snow-patch communities of arctic and boreal mountains of Fennoscandia, the Scottish Highlands, Iceland, Greenland and other islands of the Norwegian and Greenland seas, formed of mats of mosses and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal [Polytrichum]-[Kiaeria] snowbed communities
description: Moss snow-patch communities of the Scottish Highlands and the mountains of western Norway formed of mats of bryophytes dominated by [Kiaeria starkei] ([Dicranum starkei]) and [Polytrichum sexangulare] ([Polytrichum norvegicum]), with [Kiaeria falcata], [Polytrichum alpinum], [Oligotrichum hercynicum], [Pohlia ludwigii], [Pleurocladula albescens], [Barbilophozia floerkii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Polytrichum sexangulare] snowbed communities
description: Snow-patch communities of the alpine levels of Scandinavian and Icelandic mountains formed of mats of bryophytes of varied species composition, usually dominated by [Polytrichum sexangulare] ([Polytrichum norvegicum]), characteristically accompanied by, notably, [Andraea spp.], ([Andraea blittii], [Andraea obovata]) and [Anthelia juratzkana]. Solitary vascular plants, including [Salix herbacea], [Cerastium cerastoides], [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), [Saxifraga stellaris], [Carex lachenalii], [Deschampsia alpina], and lichens occur scattered at few metre intervals. [Polytrichum] communities are physiognomically variable, depending on the nutrient deficient substrate, which varies from fine material to rough boulders or solifluction, and may be dry to moist during the growing season. They appear as thin crusts on stones in hollows, as dense moss carpets on fine soils, as patches on coarser material, alternating with bare stones and gravel, or in boulder fields as fragments between boulders.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Anthelia juratzkana] snowbed communities
description: Snow-patch moss communities of alpine levels of Iceland, Spitzbergen, Jan Mayen and Greenland formed by often continuous mats of the blue hepatica [Anthelia juratzkana], hardening and becoming crusty in summer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal moss-dwarf willow snowbed communities
description: Acidophilous snow-patch communities of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia, Iceland and the Scottish Highlands dominated by dwarf willows embedded in dense bryophyte carpets.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Salix]-[Rhacomitrium] snowbed communities
description: Moss and dwarf willow snow-patch communities of the Scottish Highlands, with fragmentary outposts in the Southern Uplands, with [Salix herbacea], [Saxifraga stellaris], [Silene acaulis], [Omalotheca supina], [Luzula spicata] and mosses [Rhacomitrium heterostictum], [Rhacomitrium fasciculare], [Gymnomitrium concinnatum], [Polytrichum norvegicum], [Oligotrichum hercynicum], [Nardia scalaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cassiope-dwarf willow snowbed communities
description: Moss and dwarf-willow snow-patch communities of the alpine level of boreal and arcto-alpine Scandinavian mountains and of Iceland, dominated by [Salix herbacea], alone or with [Cassiope hypnoides], [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), [Ranunculus glacialis], frequently rich in small liver-mosses and lichens. Formations of high alpine and upper middle alpine levels are characteristically with [Poa flexuosa], [Luzula confusa], [Cardamine bellidifolia], [Ranunculus glacialis], of lower alpine levels with [Omalotheca supina], [Sibbaldia procumbens] and [Veronica alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine [Deschampsia]-[Anthoxanthum] communities
description: Acidophilous snow-patch communities of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia, Iceland and the Scottish Highlands dominated by coarse tussocky grasses, in particular, [Deschampsia cespitosa], sometimes associated with large hypnaceous mosses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Deschampsia]-[Galium] communities
description: Snow-patch communities of the western and central Highlands, with outposts in the Southern Uplands, dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa] or by [Rhytidiadelphus loreus] associated with [Deschampsia cespitosa] and often with [Hylocomium splendens] or [Pleurozium schreberi], with [Rhytidiadelphus squarrosus], [Rhytidiadelphus triquetrus], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Carex bigelowii], [Galium saxatile], [Alchemilla alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nordic [Deschampsia]-[Anthoxanthum] communities
description: Snow-patch communities of the low and middle alpine levels of Scandinavian mountains and of the lowland to low alpine levels of Iceland dominated by [Deschampsia flexuosa] and [Anthoxanthum odoratum] on poor, nonflooded, substrates, with [Omalotheca norvegica] ([Gnaphalium norvegicum]), [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), [Diphasiastrum alpinum], [Carex bigelowii], [Carex brunnescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine herb-rich acid snowbed communities
description: Acidophilous or acidocline snow-patch communities of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia, Iceland, the Faeroes and the Scottish Highlands forming a low, often open, turf of mat- and cushion-forming herbs, short tufted grasses and bryophyte patches.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Alchemilla]-[Sibbaldia] snowbed communities
description: Species-rich, low and often somewhat open swards of the western and central Scottish Highlands characteristic of sheltered hollows and corries kept moist by snow-melt or snow-bed springs, often on podzolized soils over calcareous substrates, formed by [Alchemilla alpina], [Sibbaldia procumbens], [Thymus praecox], [Silene acaulis], [Nardus stricta], [Agrostis capillaris], [Festuca ovina], [Festuca vivipara], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Omalotheca supina], [Galium saxatile].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian buttercup snowbed communities
description: Herb-rich, well-developed, closed meadow communities of lower and middle alpine levels of Scandinavian mountains, in locations around snow patches on south-facing slopes with relatively early thaw, on stable, moist substrates with low pH, subject to periodic flooding, mainly in spring. The ground layer is dominated by mosses; dominant vascular species, depending on subtypes, are [Ranunculus acris], [Sibbaldia procumbens] or [Alchemilla glomerulans]; the cortŠge may include [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Cerastium cerastoides], [Epilobium angustifolium], [Rumex acetosa], [Taraxacum croceum], [Veronica alpina], [Oxyria digyna], [Carex bigelowii], [Carex lachenalii], [Calamagrostis neglecta], [Phleum alpinum], [Agrostis mertensii], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Equisetum arvense]; lime-loving species are absent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nordic saxifrage snowbed communities
description: Species-rich, extremely patchy, communities of lower and middle alpine levels of Scandinavian mountains, of Iceland and the Faeroe Islands, forming on flooded, extremely moist, late thawing, poor substrates in heavy rainfall areas, dominated by [Oxyria digyna] and various species of saxifrages ([Saxifraga stellaris], [Saxifraga caespitosa], [Saxifraga hypnoides], [Saxifraga tenuis], [Saxifraga rivularis], [Saxifraga oppositifolia]) or by [Deschampsia alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine fern snowbed communities
description: Acidophilous snow-bed communities of alpine and arcto-alpine levels of the Fennoscandian mountains, of Iceland and of the Scottish Highlands dominated by ferns, characteristic of screes with prolonged snow cover, related to the tall-herb communities of unit 37.8. [Cryptogramma crispa], [Athyrium distentifolium] ([Athyrium alpestre]), [Athyrium filix-femina], [Dryopteris expansa] ([Dryopteris assimilis]) or [Dryopteris filix-mas] can dominate the communities. [Galium saxatile], [Calamagrostis purpurea], [Barbilophozia floerkii], [Polytrichum alpinum] are among the associates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine acidocline sedge and rush snowbed communities
description: Acidophilous snowbed communities of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains and subarctic lowlands of Scandinavia and Iceland, mostly developed in areas of long snowcover, dominated by Cyperaceae or Juncaceae, usually with a prominent bryophyte or lichen ground layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rufine sedge-arctic haresfoot sedge snowbed communities
description: Acidophilous snowbed communities of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of  Scandinavia and Iceland forming on extremely wet sandy substrates, under prolonged snow cover and with near-surface water during the entire vegetation period, dominated by [Carex rufina], often in a single species situation, or with [Carex lachenalii], [Carex bigelowii], on a compact moss carpet dominated by [Calliergon cordifolium]. Occurs in western parts of mountain chains, under submaritime or maritime climates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Curved woodrush-glacier buttercup snowbed communities
description: Mostly open snowbed communities of the alpine belt of boreal and arctic Scandinavia and Iceland, developed, on north- and northwest-facing slopes, in conjunction with snow fields that may thaw only in some years, on often very bare stony, gravellly or boulder-strewn acid, nutrient-poor soils, with high moisture content but susceptible to summer dessication, dominated by [Luzula arcuata] or, in Scandinavia only, [Luzula confusa], with a ground layer formed by hepatics, mosses or [Cetraria islandica]; the species cortŠge includes [Ranunculus glacialis] as well as, among others, [Ranunculus pygmaeus], [Cassiope hypnoides], [Silene acaulis], [Cardamine bellidifolia], [Saxifraga rivularis], [Carex lachenalii], [Poa flexuosa], and, in Iceland, [Poa alpina], [Phleum alpinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian snowpatch communities
description: Snow-patch communities of the high altitudes of the Urals, devoid of [Salix herbacea]. [Lagotis uralensis], [Anemone biarmiensis], [Ranunculus borealis], [Ranunculus sulfphureus], [Alchemilla murbeckiana], [Rhodiola rosea] are charactermistic of distinctive associations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Asian oroboreal snow-patch communmities
description: Snow-patch communities of high mountains of boreal eastern Asia, in particular, of Kamchatka and Amurland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Alpic calcicline snow-patch communities
description: Basiphile or basicline snow-patch or snowbed communities of the boreal and arcto-alpine mountains, including the Caledonian mountains of Scotland, and of the western Alpids, developed on calcareous substrates, on calcschists, or on base-rich soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic small herb calcicolous snow-patch communities
description: Herbaceous snow-patch swards of the Alpids, characteristic of carbonated soils under snow for long periods, with [Arabis caerulea], [Carex atrata], [Ranunculus alpestris], [Saxifraga androsacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Arabis-Gnaphalium] snow-patch communities
description: Herbaceous snow-patch swards of humid, carbonated soils, of the Alps and the Pyrenees, under snow for long periods, with [Ranunculus alpestris], [Arabis caerulea], [Omalotheca hoppeana] ([Gnaphalium hoppeanum]), [Hutchinsia alpina], [Potentilla brauniana] ([Potentilla minima]), [Soldanella alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian saxifrage snow-patch communities
description: Endemic snow patch community of the high Tatras and nearby Carpathian ranges, characteristic of sites with very long snow cover, with the western Carpathian endemic [Saxifraga wahlenbergii] ([Saxifraga perdurans]), [Hutchinsia alpina], [Bucegia romanica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaro-Pelagonide calciphile herbaceous snow-patch communities
description: Uncommon, isolated herbaceous snow-patch swards of the southern Dinarides and the Pelagonides, on carbonated soils under snow for long periods, generally associated with dolines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Alpic calcicolous espalier willow snowbed communities
description: Espalier willow communities of calcareous stone fields submitted to relatively long snow-cover of the Alpids and the boreal mountains, with [Salix reticulata], [Salix retusa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic espalier willow snowbed communities
description: Espalier willow communities of snow-bound calcareous stone fields of the Alpids, with the net-leaved willow, [Salix reticulata], and the retuse-leaved willow, [Salix retusa], or with [Salix kitaibeliana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpide [Salix retusa-reticulata] snowbed communities
description: [Salix reticulata] or [Salix retusa] communities of calcareous stone fields with late-lying snow cover, of the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Apennines, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Pelagonides, the Rhodopides and their associated ranges, with [Gentiana bavarica], [Dryas octopetala], [Sesleria varia], [Sesleria rigida] var. [haynaldiana], [Carex parviflora], [Ranunculus alpestris], [Saxifraga androsacea], [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Saxifraga sempervivum], [Omalotheca hoppeana] ([Gnaphalium hoppeanum]), [Homogyne discolor], [Veronica alpina], [Veronica aphylla], [Plantago atrata] ([Plantago montana]), [Bartsia alpina], [Anemone narcissiflora], [Achillea schurii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian [Salix kitaibeliana] snowbed communities
description: Distinctive snow patch communities, endemic to the Eastern Carpathians, in particular, to the Rodnei Mountains, formed by the Carpathian endemics [Salix kitaibeliana] and [Soldanella hungarica] ssp. [hungarica], with [Luzula alpinopilosa], [Polygonum viviparum], [Oreochloa disticha], [Doronicum clusii], and, more sporadically, the Eastern Carpathian endemics [Poa deylii] and [Lychnis nivalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian espalier willow snowbed communities
description: Espalier willow communities of calcareous stonefields in mountains in heavy-rainfall areas of boreal and arctic Scandinavia dominated by [Salix reticulata], often exclusively, and [Poa alpina], with a sparser participation of, among others, [Salix polaris], [Antennaria alpina], [Pinguicula alpina], [Silene acaulis], [Tofieldia pusilla], [Viola biflora], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Festuca vivipara], [Equisetum variegatum], [Selaginella selaginoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-boreal calcicline snowbed communities
description: Calciphile or calcicline snowfield, snowbed and snow-patch communities of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains formed by small herbs, grasses or dwarf, underground-stemmed willows.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Polar willow snowbed communities
description: Chionophilous communities of boreal and arcto-alpine Palaearctic mountains and of islands of the polar basin dominated by, or rich in, [Salix polaris], associated with mosses and small forbs, developed, at least in the boreal and arcto-alpine regions, on calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian polar willow snowbed communities
description: Snowbed communities of the boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia, characteristic of the edges of snowfields on calcareous often stone-littered soils with near-surface ground water or moisture in early spring and little or no solifluction, constituted by dense carpets of mosses and forbs in which [Salix polaris] dominates, often totally; the species cortŠge includes [Salix reticulata], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Erigeron uniflora], [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), [Minuartia biflora], [Ranunculus pygmaeus], [Saxifraga aizoides], [Saxifraga cernua], [Saxifraga stellaris], [Saxifraga tenuis], [Silene acaulis], [Taraxacum croceum], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Tofieldia pusilla], [Veronica alpina], [Viola biflora], [Carex lachenalii], [Poa alpina] f. [vivipara] and mosses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spitzbergen polar willow snowbed communities
description: Snowbed communities of islands of the polar basin, in particular, of Spitzbergen with [Salix polaris], [Luzula confusa], [Pedicularis hirsuta], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Cerastium arcticum], [Dricranum elongatum], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Gymnomitrion coralloides], [Anthelia juratzkana], [Cetraria delisei], [Sterocolon alpinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Distichium capillaceum] snowbed communities
description: Moss dominated snowbed communities of calcareous gravel and stonefields, or moraine, of Scandinavian mountains, with, in particular, [Distichium capillaceum], [Pohlia albicans], [Pohlia drummondii], often pioneering on "new ground". Individual vascular plants, growing widely separated, include, notably, [Cardamine pratense] f. [dentata], [Cerastium arcticum], [Cerastium cerastoides], [Saxifraga oppositifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Snow buttercup snowbed communities
description: Open snowbed communities of the alpine level of the boreal and arcto-alpine zones of Scandinavian mountains forming on level calcareous substrates often waterlogged the whole year, in the proximity of melting snow or cold springs,  on north-facing slopes, with prolonged snow-lie. Vascular plants are characteristically scattered, with great variation in the ground layer, with an often broken moss carpet, bare patches of gravel and stones. Characteristic species, often hygrophilous, include [Ranunculus nivalis], [Ranunculus sulphureus], [Salix herbacea], [Arabis alpina], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Cerastium cerastoides], [Minuartia biflora], [Oxyria digyna], [Taraxacum croceum], [Viola biflora], [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Saxifraga rivularis], [Saxifraga nivalis], [Saxifraga tenuis], [Saussurea alpina], [Sibbaldia procumbens], [Juncus biglumis], [Poa alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Snow grass snowbed communities
description: Sparse communities of the alpine level of northern boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia and of Iceland dominated by the grass [Phippsia algida], with, notably, [Salix herbacea], [Cerastium arcticum], [Cerastium cerastoides], [Oxyria digyna], [Ranunculus glacialis], [Ranunculus nivalis], [Ranunculus pygmaeus], [Saxifraga cernua], [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Saxifraga rivularis], [Saxifraga stellaris], [Saxifraga tenuis], [Carex lachenalii], [Juncus biglumis], [Poa alpina] f. [vivipara], [Deschampsia alpina], [Sagina saginoides], with a fragmentary moss cover and no lichens, located on gravelly, sandy, sometimes totally waterlogged soils, calcareous in Scandinavia, with prolonged snow-cover. Snow grass communities frequently occur as pioneer vegetation on small surfaces, very common in the central part of southern Norway and in Sweden from Jamtland northwards.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic woodrush snowbed communities
description: Open, herb-rich, snowbed communities of the middle to high alpine level of the boreal and southern arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia, developed on level or gently sloping moist calcareous ground with solifluction tongues separated by gravelly expanses with a thin but prolonged snow cover, dominated by [Luzula arctica]. [Luzula confusa], [Ranunculus glacialis], [Ranunculus sulphureus], [Cerastium spp.] and [Draba crassifolia] are characteristic of the species cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal herb-rich calcicline snowbed communities
description: Herb-rich and often mosaic patterned snow-patch or near snow-patch communities of alpine levels of boreal and arctic Scandinavia, of the lower alpine belt of Iceland, of the Scottish Highlands and of the English Lake District, with many moss species and few lichens, occurring on calcareous, nutrient-rich, humid substrates. Characteristic species include [Ranunculus acris], [Poa alpina], [Poa arctica], [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Silene acaulis], [Oxyria digyna], [Potentilla crantzii], [Cerastium alpinum], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Saussurea alpina], [Primula stricta], [Viola biflora], [Carex norvegica], [Minuartia biflora], [Thalictrum alpinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nordic [Potentilla crantzii]-[Bistorta vivipara] communities
description: Extremely herb-rich moderately chionophilous communities of the low and middle alpine levels of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia and of the lower alpine belt of Iceland, developed on calcareous, nutrient-rich, humid substrates, with a ground layer formed by many moss species and few lichens, and a mosaic-like vascular plant dominance in which a few species characterize smaller patches in different microtopic sites. These dominants include [Potentilla crantzii], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Silene acaulis], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Cerastium alpinum] and, in Scandinavia, [Poa alpina], [Poa arctica], [Saussurea alpina], or, in Iceland, [Alchemilla vulgaris] [s.l.], [Bartsia alpina], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Ranunculus acris], [Rumex acetosa], [Rhodiola rosea] ([Sedum roseum]), [Taraxacum spp.] These communities constitute an important habitat for [Nigritella nigra] [s.s.], [Primula stricta], [Armeria maritima] ssp. [labradorica]. [Drepanocladus uncinatus] is often the dominant bryophyte.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Festuca]-[Alchemilla]-[Silene] communities
description: Moderately chionophilous communities of higher altitudes of the Highlands of Scotland, forming, over calcareous bedrocks, short, often fairly open, species-rich swards of grasses, forbs and bryophytes among which [Silene acaulis], [Minuartia sedoides], [Sibbaldia procumbens], [Alchemilla alpina], [Thymus praecox], [Festuca ovina], [Festuca vivipara], [Agrostis capillaris], [Nardus stricta], [Deschampsia cespitosa] are prominent. The species cortŠge, rich in arctoalpine species, some of them of locally very restricted distribution, includes [Luzula spicata], [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Polygonum viviparum], [Sagina saginoides], [Cerastium alpinum], [Antennaria dioica], [Saxlix herbacea], [Omalotheca supina], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Juncus trifidus], [Euphrasia frigida], [Alchemilla filicaulis] ssp. [filicaulis], [Myosotis alpestris], [Veronica alpina], [Poa alpina], [Draba norvegica], [Potentilla crantzii]. These communities are similar to the Fennoscandian communities of unit 36.12361; they are related also to the more acidocline communities of unit 36.11241.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Ranunculus acris]-[Poa alpina] communities
description: Herb-rich, moderately chionophilous, closed communities of the low and middle alpine levels of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia, developed over calcareous substrates with near-surface or subsurface seeping water, usually with deep soils that may be superficially decalcified, sometimes with lithosoils, with few dominants, mostly [Ranunculus acris] and [Poa alpina], sometimes [Petasites frigidus], and a mosaic of multispecific plant assemblies that include [Alchemilla glomerulans], [Arabis alpina], [Bartsia alpina], [Equisetum arvense], [Oxyria digyna], [Pedicularis hirsuta], [Pedicularis oederi], [Ranunculus nivalis], [Ranunculus pygmaeus], [Salix polaris], [Saussurea alpina], [Saxifraga cernua], [Saxifraga cespitosa], [Taraxacum croceum], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Trollius europaeus], [Veronica alpina], [Viola biflora], [Selaginella selaginoides]. These communities often occupy an intermediate position, in particular along streams, or at the bottom of hollows, between small herb communities of unit 36.12361 and tall herb communities of unit 37.8, dominated by [Trollius europaeus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian [Saxifraga oppositifolia]-[Oxyria] communities
description: Chionophilous, patchy communities of the low and middle alpine levels of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia, developed over calcareous substrates on moist, sometimes porous and unstable, mineral soils, dominated by [Saxifraga oppositifolia], accompanied by [Oxyria digyna], with a locally variable set of accompanying species and an often broken ground layer generally rich in marchantiaceid liverworts. The species cortŠge includes [Arabis alpina], [Cerastium alpinum], [Draba crassifolia], [Omalotheca supina], [Ranunculus pygmaeus], [Rumex acetosa], [Sagina saginoides], [Salix herbacea], [Saxifraga cernua], [Saxifraga tenuis], [Taraxacum croceum], [Veronica alpina], [Poa alpina], [Poa arctica], [Poa stricta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Highland [Saxifraga aizoides]-[Alchemilla] banks
description: Almost pure banks of [Saxifraga aizoides] growing on continuously irrigated steep, calcareous cliff faces and earth banks of the Scottish Highlands and the Lake District; the species cortŠge includes [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Alchemilla glabra], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Pinguicula vulgaris], [Selaginella selaginoides], [Blindia acuta], [Orthothecium rufescens]. This community is related to the Fennoscandian communities of unit 36.12364.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subarctic small-herb snowbed communities
description: Chionophilous communities of stony and gravelly ground of the islands of the polar basin developed in conditions of shorter snow cover than the polar willow communities, with a species cortŠge that includes [Trisetum spicatum], [Ranunculus nivalis], [Ranunculus pygmaeus], [Oxyria dygina], [Lidia biflora], [Poa arctica], [Potentilla hyparctica], [Carex lachenalii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caucasian snow-patch communities
description: Snow-patch communities of high mountains of the Pontic Range and of the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian snow-patch communities
description: Snow-patch communities of high mountains of the Tien-Shan and Altai systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan snow-patch communities
description: Snow-patch communities of high mountains of the Himalayan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Asian snow-patch communities
description: Snow-patch communities of high mountains of boreonemoral, nemoral, warm-temperate and subtropical eastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine weathered rock and outcrop communities
description: Stonecrop and houseleak pioneer communities colonizing small surfaces on shallow soils of mostly siliceous rocky outcrops in the subalpine, alpine or montane levels of higher mountains of sub-Atlantic to Atlantic climates, in particular, of the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Cantabrians and associated northwestern Iberian ranges, the Black Forest and the Slovakian Carpathians.   The communities are dominated by succulent [Sempervivum arachnoideum] ssp. [arachnoideum], [Sempervivum arachnoideum] ssp. [tomentosum], [Sempervivum montanum] ssp. [montanum], [Sempervivum montanum] ssp. [stiriacum], [Sempervivum wulfenii], [Jovibarba arenaria], [Sedum montanum], [Sedum anglicum] ssp. [pyrenaicum], [Sedum sexangulare], [Sedum album], [Sedum annuum], [Saxifraga aspera], accompanied by [Silene rupestris], [Scleranthus polycarpos], [Veronica fruticans], [Thymus praecox] ssp. [polytrichus], [Viola tricolor] ssp. [saxatilis], by small crucifers, lichens and mosses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Alpic acidophilous alpine grasslands
description: Alpine and subalpine grasslands developed over crystalline rocks and other lime-deficient substrates or on decalcified soils of the boreal mountains, including the Caledonian mountains of Scotland, and of the western Alpids and their satellite Hercynian ranges, with [Armeria alpina], [Armeria alliacea] ([Armeria montana]), [Euphrasia minima], [Gentiana alpina], [Geum montanum], [Juncus trifidus], [Lychnis alpina], [Pedicularis pyrenaica], [Phyteuma hemisphaericum], [Pulsatilla alpina] ssp. [sulphurea], [Ranunculus pyrenaeus], [Sempervivum montanum], [Botrychium lunaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic mat-grass swards and related communities
description: Closed grasslands of deep, acid soils of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Pyrenees, the northern Apennines, the Jura and the higher Hercynian ranges, the northern and central Dinarides, developed mostly and abundantly in the subalpine level, dominated or co-dominated by [Nardus stricta], [Festuca eskia], [Festuca nigrescens], [Festuca rubra], [Alopecurus gerardii], [Bellardiochloa violacea] ([Poa violacea]), [Carex sempervirens], [Anthoxanthum odoratum]. Similar [Nardus stricta] grasslands of the Moesian region of the Balkan peninsula, distributed at high elevations of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains and the Pelagonides, as southern extensions of the Alpigenous communities or as grazing-induced facies of the more varied communities of unit 36.39.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Alpine mesophile mat-grass swards
description: Subalpine and lower alpine mesophile grasslands dominated by, or rich in, [Nardus stricta], of the Alps, the Pyrenees and, very locally, the Central Massif, the Jura and the northern Apennines; for the most part, they are heavily grazed grasslands with much reduced species diversity and overwhelming dominance of mat-grass.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Alpine hygrophile mat-grass swards
description: Subalpine and alpine hygro-mesophile, chionophilous [Nardus stricta] swards of depressions and humid flats around lakes and marshes, where snow melts slowly.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Alpine hygrophile foxtail swards
description: Subalpine and alpine hygro-mesophile, chionophilous grasslands of depressions with prolonged snow cover dominated by [Alopecurus gerardii] and [Trifolium alpinum]; they constitute a transition between siliceous grasslands and snowpatch communities, which they often ring.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean closed [Festuca eskia] grasslands
description: Subalpine and lower alpine closed mesophile [Festuca eskia] grasslands of north-facing slopes (ubacs) and depressions in the Pyrenees with [Arnica montana], [Ranunculus pyrenaeus], [Selinum pyrenaeum], [Trifolium alpinum], [Campanula barbata], [Gentiana punctata], [Leucorchis albida], [Phyteuma betonicifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean [Poa violacea] swards
description: Subalpine [Bellardiochloa violacea] ([Poa violacea])-dominated grasslands of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian summital mat-grass swards
description: Summital swards of the greater Hercynian ranges dominated by, or rich in, [Nardus stricta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hautes Chaumes summital mat-grass swards
description: Formations of the Hautes Chaumes (high Vosges), with [Nardus stricta], [Gentiana lutea], [Arnica montana], [Pulsatilla alba], [Viola lutea] ssp. [elegans], [Selinum pyrenaeum], [Leontodon pyrenaicus], [Hieracium vogesiacum], [Hieracium olivaceum], [Hieracium alpinum] and abundant ericoid shrubs, [Erica tetralix], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Black Forest summital mat-grass swards
description: [Nardus stricta] grasslands of the Black Forest.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Harz summital mat-grass swards
description: Formations of the Harz dominated by, or rich in, [Nardus stricta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bohemian Forest summital mat-grass swards
description: [Nardus stricta] grasslands of the high altitudes of the Bayerischer Wald and of the central Bohemian Forest (Sumava).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sudeten summital mat-grass swards
description: [Nardus stricta] grasslands of the high altitudes of the Sudeten mountains (Krkonose, Hruby Jesenik), with [Carex bigelowii] ssp. [rigida] ([Carex rigida], [Carex fyllae]), [Hieracium alpinum], [Primula minima], [Potentilla aurea], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Lycopodium alpinum], and, in some formations, [Sphagnum nemoreum], [Sphagnum girgensohnii], [Polytrichum strictum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sudeten stiff sedge mat-grass swards
description: [Nardus stricta] grasslands of the high altitudes of the Sudeten mountains (Krkonose, Hruby Jesenik), with [Carex bigelowii] ssp. [rigida] ([Carex rigida], [Carex fyllae]), [Hieracium alpinum], [Primula minima], [Potentilla aurea], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Lycopodium alpinum], and, in some formations, [Sphagnum nemoreum], [Sphagnum girgensohnii], [Polytrichum strictum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sudeten flower-rich mat-grass swards
description: Flower-rich [Nardus stricta] grasslands of the high altitudes of the Sudeten mountains (Krkonose, Hruby Jesenik), with [Hieracium alpinum], [Campanula bohemica], [Viola sudetica], [Gentiana asclepiadea], [Homogyne alpina], [Potentilla aurea], [Pulsatilla alba], [Rhinanthus alpinus], [Solidago virgaurea], [Thesium alpinum], [Luzula sudetica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sudeten silene mat-grass swards
description: Upper montane to low alpine [Nardus stricta] grasslands of the Sudeten mountains (Krkonose, Hruby Jesenik), developed at altitudes of 700-1100 m, comprising elements of high altitude [Nardion] grasslands, as well as of montane mesophile [Polygono-Trisetion] grasslands and collinar [Galio-Nardion] grasslands, with [Silene vulgaris], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Crepis succisifolia], [Silene dioica] ([Melandrium rubrum]), [Potentilla aurea], [Potentilla erecta], [Ranunculus acris], [Campanula bohemica], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Galium saxatile], [Hypericum maculatum], [Polygonum bistorta], [Leucanthemum vulgare], [Leontodon hispidus], [Hieracium lachenalii], [Gymnadenia conopsea], [Luzula luzuloides], [Luzula multiflora], [Carex pilulifera], [Agrostis capillaris], [Anthoxanthum odoratum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian mat-grass swards
description: Grasslands dominated by, or rich in, [Nardus stricta] of the Carpathian system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Carpathian mat-grass swards
description: [Nardus] grasslands of the northwestern Carpathians, with [Carex pilulifera], [Hieracium vulgatum], [Hypochoeris uniflora], [Crepis conyzifolia], [Gentiana punctata], [Homogyne alpina], [Potentilla aurea], [Pulsatilla alpina], of western Carpathian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian mat-grass swards
description: Grasslands rich in, or dominated by, [Nardus stricta], with [Festuca nigricans], [Festuca airoides], [Poa media] and regional species [Viola declinata], [Scorzonera rosea], [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda] ([Potentilla ternata]), [Campanula abietina], [Campanula serrata], of flats and gentle slopes of the subalpine and lower alpine levels of the Eastern and Southern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Moesian mat-grass swards
description: Acidophilous grasslands dominated by [Nardus stricta] of higher, mostly subalpine, sometimes alpine, elevations of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains and the Pelagonides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaride mat-grass swards
description: [Nardus stricta]-dominated grasslands of the subalpine and alpine levels of the Dinaride system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaride arnica mat-grass swards
description: Closed grasslands of subalpine and alpine levels of the northern and central Dinarides of Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, south to the Vranica Planina in Bosnia, dominated or co-dominated by [Nardus stricta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montenegrine scabious mat-grass swards
description: Closed acidophilous grasslands of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Bjelsica mountains of Montenegro, developed on recent volcanic substrates, dominated by [Nardus stricta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal acidocline grasslands
description: Grass, sedge, rush, bryophyte and lichen acidophile or acidocline communities of the higher summits of the boreal and arcto-alpine Palaearctic mountains, southwest to the Highlands of Scotland, the Lake District, northern England and northern Wales, submitted to diverse, though generally moderate, levels of snow cover and wind exposure, with resulting affinities to both the fairly chionophilous Alpide grasslands of the [Caricetea curvulae] assembled in unit 36.31 and to the snowfield communities of unit 36.11; [Juncus trifidus] and [Carex bigelowii] are often present.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal [Carex bigelowii]-[Polytrichum] sedge-heaths
description: Communities of the low and middle alpine levels of boreal and arcto-alpine mountains of Scandinavia and of high altitudes of the cold, snow-bound Central and Eastern Highlands of Scotland, with outliers in the Northern Highlands, dominated by [Carex bigelowii], or, in Scandinavia, [Carex bigelowii] and [Carex lachenalii], emerging from an often almost continuous carpet of mosses, formed, in particular, by [Dicranum fuscescens] and [Polytrichum alpinum], with frequent but usually scarce lichens, notably [Cladonia uncialis], [Cladonia arbuscula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal [Carex bigelowii]-[Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths
description: Carpets of mosses of genus [Rhacomitrium], often thick, closed and extensive, sometimes fragmented with much bare ground, associated with usually scattered vascular plants, among which [Carex bigelowii] is often prominent, characteristic of wind-exposed, cloud-bound, relatively snowfree summital regions of the Scandinavian mountains and of Scotland, northern England and northern Wales, of Iceland, the Faeroe Islands, Greenland, Spitzbergen. For the most part they constitute habitats physiognomically dominated by bryophytes, the subdivisions of 36.322 defining communities integrated within units 62.3 or 66.3.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandio-Britannic [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths
description: Moss-heaths of the Scandinavian mountains, of the Scottish Highlands, of the Southern Uplands and of Cumberland, formed by often nearly continuous carpets of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], associated with lichens and often dotted by scattered vascular plants, mostly sedges, grasses and erico‹ds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [C. bigelowii]-[Rhacomitrium]-lichen moss-heaths
description: Moss-heaths of exposed summits of the Scottish Highlands, particularly the Central Highlands, with outposts in the Southern Uplands and Cumberland, formed by often nearly continuous, but sometimes open, carpets of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], at times very extensive, usually dotted by scattered [Carex bigelowii], [Festuca ovina], [Festuca vivipara], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Vaccinium myrtillus] and richer in lichens, mostly of genera [Cladonia] and [Cetreria], than moss-heaths of unit 36.3222.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths
description: Moss-heaths of Scandinavia, formed by carpets of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] up to 10 cm thick, usually accompanied by lichens, mostly of genera [Cetraria], notably [Cetraria nivalis], and [Cladonia], and by scattered vascular plants, among which [Carex bigelowii], [Festuca vivipara], [Empetrum hermaphroditum] may be dominant or well represented. They are limited to the low alpine and middle alpine levels of mountains under maritime climates of southern and middle Scandinavia, developing on mixed sands and gravels with low lime content, pH in the order of 4.5 to 6.5, and a thin humus layer. They typically occupy small surfaces, of the order of 1-4 mý.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [C. bigelowii]-[Rhacomitrium]-[Galium] moss-heaths
description: Carpets of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] of the Scottish Highlands, most characteristic of the maritime western plateaux and the inner Hebrides, extending south, in the western British uplands, to the Southern Uplands, the Lake District and northern Wales, richer in grasses ([Festuca ovina], [Festuca vivipara], [Deschampsia flexuosa]) and with a less overwhelming dominance of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] than in unit 36.32211, with a lesser abundance of lichens and a greater representation of subshrubs ([Vaccinium myrtillus], [Empetrum nigrum] ssp. [hermaphroditum]), characteristic of lower elevations and less exposed situations. Characteristic vascular plants include [Galium saxatile], [Potentilla erecta], [Carex pilulifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Atlantic [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths
description: [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths of the northwest Scottish Highlands, of the Faeroe Islands and of Iceland, with outposts in the Central Highlands and the Southern Uplands, developed in conditions of high rainfall, early snow-thaw, prevalent cloudiness and harsh winds, with a sparse vascular cortŠge richer in cushion-herbs, poorer in [Carex bigelowii], grasses and lichens, than those of units 36.3221 and 36.3222.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [C. bigelowii]-[Rhacomitrium]-[Silene] moss-heaths
description: [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths rich in cushion-herbs, often very open, with a fragmented moss carpet, a relative reduction of [Carex bigelowii] and few lichens, developed in conditions of high rainfall, early snow-thaw, prevalent cloudiness and harsh winds, most characteristic of the northwest Scottish Highlands, where they occupy exposed summits, ridges and spurs, also recorded in Ireland, with outposts in the Central Highlands and the Southern Uplands; [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] is the dominant moss; the characteristic cushion herbs and mat-formers include [Armeria maritima], [Silene acaulis], [Minuartia sedoides], [Thymus praecox] ssp. [arcticus], [Alchemilla alpina], [Salix herbacea]; other associates comprise [Carex bigelowii], [Juncus trifidus], [Polygonum viviparum], [Rhytidiadelphus loreus], [Aulacomnium turgidum], [Hypnum hamulosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths
description: [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths of Iceland, where they colonize river gravels, stoney terrain and lava fields; [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] is the dominant moss in the heavy rainfall lowland areas, especially on lava fields, [Rhacomitrium canescens] in relatively lower rainfall areas of the highlands. Associated vascular plants may include [Armeria maritima], [Silene acaulis], [Thymus praecox] ssp. [arcticus], [Salix herbacea], [Cardaminopsis petraea], [Cerastium alpinum], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Galium normanii], [Polygonum viviparum], [Carex bigelowii], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Juncus trifidus], [Luzula spicata], [Festuca richardsonii], [Festuca vivipara], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Calluna vulgaris]. Lichens are not numerous, represented mostly by species of genera [Cetraria], [Cornicularia], [Cladonia], [Stereocaulon], [Peltigera], and by [Thamnolia vermicularis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Faeroe [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths
description: [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] moss-heaths of the Faeroe Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subarctic [Rhacomitrium] moss-heaths
description: Carpets of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] of Greenland and Spitzbergen, developed under oceanic climates on well-stabilized noncalcareous stoney substrates, with an overwhelming dominance of mosses ([Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Dicranum elongatum], [Hylocomium alascanum]) and of lichens ([Thamnolia subuliformis], [Cladonia uncialis], [Cladonia gracilis], [Cetraria nivalis]), and few vascular plants, among which [Cardamine bellidifolia], [Luzula confusa], [Saxifraga cespitosa], [Salix polaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal [Juncus trifidus]-[Rhacomitrium] rush-heaths
description: Lichen-rich communities of the Scottish Highlands, the Scandinavian mountains and Iceland, limited to stoney, acid substrates in exposed situations, such as granitic summital plateaux, summit detritus, steep screes, summit ridges, dominated by [Juncus trifidus] and [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] with [Carex bigelowii], [Salix herbacea], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Alchemilla alpina] and, sometimes, ericoid shrubs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal [Juncus trifidus]-[Cladonia]-[Cetraria] rush-heaths
description: Communities of the Scottish Central Highlands, extensive in the Cairngorms where they are often at the upper limit of vegetation, of the Scandinavian mountains and of lowland and lower alpine areas of Iceland, occupying porous substrates, dominated by [Juncus trifidus], and [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], which often forms extensive carpets among the [Juncus] tufts; [Carex bigelowii] is generally present and there is a lichen-rich species cortŠge that includes, in particular, [Cetraria islandica], [Cladonia sylvatica], [Cladonia uncialis], [Cladonia gracilis], [Cladonia arbuscula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal [Juncus trifidus]-[Salix herbacea] rush-heaths
description: [Juncus trifidus] and [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum]-dominated communities, rich in [Carex bigelowii] and with a participation of [Salix herbacea], of the Scottish Highlands and the mountains of Scandinavia, occupying mostly south-facing slopes, typically on sandy-humus soil over gravel, sand or stoney substrates in areas of high snowfall and spring flooding.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal [Nardus stricta]-[Carex bigelowii] grass-heaths
description: [Nardus stricta] communities developed in areas of prolonged snow cover in the Scandinavian mountains, Iceland, the Faeroe Islands, Scotland, Cumbria, the northern Pennines and northern Wales, with [Carex bigelowii], [Alchemilla alpina], [Agrostis borealis], mosses and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic[Nardus stricta]-[Carex bigelowii] grass-heaths
description: [Nardus stricta] communities developed in areas of prolonged snow cover in Scotland, Cumbria, the northern Pennines and northern Wales, with [Carex bigelowii], [Galium saxatile], [Potentilla erecta], [Alchemilla alpina], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Agrostis capillaris], [Festuca ovina], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Diphasiastrum alpinum], [Cladonia uncialis], [Cetraria islandica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandinavian [Nardus stricta]-[Carex bigelowii] grass-heaths
description: [Nardus stricta] grasslands developed in areas of prolonged snow cover in the Scandinavian mountains, mostly on relatively acid sandy substrates and in hollows, moist in spring and dessicated in summer, formed by dense or scattered tussocks of matgrass, with an often species-rich cortŠge that includes [Carex bigelowii], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Agrostis borealis], [Sibbaldia procumbens], [Omalotheca supina] ([Gnaphalium supinum]), [Diphasiastrum alpinum], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Polytrichum commune].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Nardus stricta] grass-heaths
description: [Nardus stricta] grasslands of Iceland, with [Polygonum viviparum], [Viola palustris], [Alchemilla alpina], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Agrostis capillaris], [Rhacomitrium canescans], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Rhytidiadelphus squarrosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Faeroe [Nardus stricta]-[Carex bigelowii] grass-heaths
description: [Nardus stricta] grasslands of boreal affinities of the Faeroe Islands, with [Carex bigelowii] and [Polytrichum norvegicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian oroboreal fescue grasslands
description: Dense, closed grasslands of the low and middle alpine levels of the Scandinavian mountains dominated by patchy tussocks of [Festuca ovina] or, on the maritime fa‡ade of Norway, of [Festuca vivipara], in alternation with lichen carpets, accompanied by [Juncus trifidus], occupying dry, acid (pH 4-5.5) soils over nutrient-poor bedrock in areas generally without snow cover or flowing groundwater, under relatively cool and dry climates. The species cortŠge includes [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Luzula spicata], [Agrostis mertensi], [Antennaria alpina], [Antennaria dioica], [Carex bigelowii], [Carex rupestris], [Luzula confusa], [Trisetum spicatum], [Silene acaulis], [Solidago virgaurea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North-Atlantic arcto-alpine fescue grasslands
description: Grassland communities of the lowlands and lower alpine levels of Iceland and the Faeroe Islands, similar to the fescue grasslands of unit 36.325, with [Festuca vivipara] and [Festuca richardsonii], but without [Festuca ovina] and an accompanying species cortŠge that differs somewhat, including [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Luzula spicata], [Juncus trifidus], [Agrostis canina], [Agrostis capillaris], [Luzula multiflora], [Equisetum pratense], and, in Iceland, [Kobresia myosuroides], [Trisetum spicatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Kobresia]-[Juncus trifidus] grasslands
description: Low growing heath grasslands of relatively poor, stoney, porous substrates of the subalpine and low alpine levels of Iceland, dominated by [Kobresia myosuroides], with [Juncus trifidus], [Agrostis vinealis], [Agrostis capillaris], [Festuca richardsonii], [Thymus arcticus], [Stereocaulon spp].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian grasslands
description: Grasslands of the extrasylvatic and upper sylvatic levels of the Urals, developed on high plateaux with deep soils and relatively high precipitations, particularly in the subalpine level of the southern Urals, or as substitution stages of grazed montane tundra.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Siberian grasslands
description: Grasslands of the extrasylvatic and upper sylvatic levels of northeastern Siberian mountains, in particular of the Anadyr and Kamtschatka ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermo-Alpigenous subalpine acidophilous grasslands
description: Subalpine thermophile formations on often skeletal soils of the southern Alps, the Pyrenees and, very locally, the Central Massif and the Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermo-Alpigenous [Festuca paniculata] swards
description: Thermophile, luxuriant, relatively closed grasslands formed by the very tall, bluegrey [Festuca paniculata] ([Festuca spadicea]) on south-facing slopes (adrets) of the upper montane and lower subalpine levels of the Pyrenees, the southern Alps and, locally, the Central Massif and the Abruzzi; characteristic and often abundant accompanying species include [Centaurea uniflora], [Silene nutans], [Trifolium montanum], [Hieracium peleteranum], [Hypochoeris maculata], [Potentilla grandiflora], [Lilium martagon], [Eryngium alpinum], [Luzula pediformis], [Meum athamanticum], [Nigritella nigra], [Helictotrichon parlatorei], [Asphodelus albus], [Iris xiphioides], [Paradisea liliastrum], [Dianthus monspessulanus], [Carduus defloratus]. Many have been traditionally treated as hay meadows and are of extraordinary floristic richness; they are nowadays increasingly abandoned or left to grazing.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rocky slope thermo-Alpigenous [Festuca paniculata] swards
description: More xero-thermophile formations on siliceous, rocky soils of steep, warm slopes of the southwestern Alps, Pyrenees, Central Massif and Abruzzi.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Deep soil thermo-Alpigenous [Festuca paniculata] swards
description: More mesophile, dense formations on deep soils of gentler slopes, often over calcareous substrates with decalcified, slightly acid, topsoil; they are mostly characteristic of the sout-western Alps with representation in the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean [Festuca eskia] garland-grasslands
description: Open, thermophile, stripped grasslands organized in ribbons retaining stony, almost bare steps on the adrets of the upper subalpine and lower alpine zones in the Pyrenees, formed by the hard, sharp-pointed, slippery, bright green, tufted [Festuca eskia], sometimes associated with [Carex sempervirens] [s.l.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arverno-Alpine varicoloured fescue garland-grasslands
description: Open, thermophile, stripped grasslands of the adrets of the (mostly) southern Alps and Central Massif, formed by calcifuge species of the hard, sharp-pointed [Festuca varia] group ([Festuca varia], [Festuca scabriculmis]), often associated with [Carex sempervirens] [s.l.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenous acidophilous grasslands
description: Mostly closed [Carex curvula], [Festuca spp.], [Oreochloa spp.] or [Juncus trifidus] grasslands on siliceous soils of the alpine level of the Alps, the Carpathians and the Pyrenees, with very local outposts in the great Hercynian ranges and the Cantabrian Range. [Androsace obtusifolia], [Androsace carnea] ssp. [laggeri], [Campanula barbata], [Juncus jacquinii], [Juncus trifidus], [Silene exscapa], [Gentiana alpina], [Achillea erba-rotta], [Euphrasia minima], [Luzula lutea], [Luzula spicata], [Luzula hispanica], [Lychnis alpina], [Minuartia recurva], [Minuartia sedoides], [Pedicularis kerneri], [Pedicularis pyrenaica], [Phyteuma globulariifolium], [Phyteuma hemisphaericum], [Potentilla frigida], [Armeria alpina], [Senecio incanus], [Trifolium alpinum], [Veronica bellidioides], [Ranunculus pyrenaeus] are characteristic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenous crooked-sedge grasslands
description: Formations of the Alps, of the Pyrenees and of the Carpathians, to which the dominance of the crooked sedge, [Carex curvula], with twisted leaves whithering early at the tip, gives a highly distinctive texture and yellow-brown hue.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine [Carex curvula] grasslands
description: [Carex curvula] formations of the upper and middle alpine levels of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean [Carex curvula] grasslands
description: [Carex curvula] formations of the upper alpine level of the eastern Pyrenees and of the alpine level of the central and western Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian [Carex curvula] grasslands
description: Formations dominated by [Carex curvula] accompanied by [Juncus trifidus], [Oreochloa disticha], [Festuca airoides], [Primula minima] and characterized by regional species [Poa media], [Senecio carpathicus], [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda], of the middle alpine level of the Eastern and Southern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenous [Festuca halleri] grasslands
description: Formations of flats and gentle slopes of the lower alpine level of the Alps, dominated by [Festuca halleri] and [Juncus trifidus], particularly widespread in the southwestern Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigenous [Festuca airoides] grasslands
description: [Festuca airoides] ([Festuca supina])-dominated swards of the alpine zone of the eastern Pyrenees, the Northern Carpathians, the Eastern Carpathians and the Sudeten.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean [Festuca airoides] grasslands
description: Low, fairly dry swards of the alpine zone of the eastern Pyrenees dominated by [Festuca airoides] ([Festuca supina]), with [Carex ericetorum], [Avenula versicolor], [Silene ciliata], [Lychnis alpina], [Arenaria grandiflora], [Jasione humilis], [Hieracium breviscapum] ([Hieracium pumilum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian [Festuca airoides] grasslands
description: Swards of the alpine zone of the Northern and Eastern Carpathians, dominated by [Festuca airoides] ([Festuca supina]), with [Juncus trifidus], [Cerastium alpinum], [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Carpathian [Festuca airoides] grasslands
description: [Juncus trifidus-Festuca airoides] swards of the Babia Gora, in Poland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian [Festuca airoides] grasslands
description: Lower alpine and upper subalpine formations of the Romanian and Ukrainian Carpathians dominated by [Festuca airoides] and [Agrostis rupestris], accompanied by regional species [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda], [Poa media] and [Campanula patula] ssp. [abietina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian [Festuca airoides] grasslands

name: Alpine [Oreochloa disticha] swards
description: [Oreochloa disticha]-dominated formations of the Alps, developed in particular in the northern Alps (Allg„u) and northeastern Alps.

name: Carpathian [Oreochloa disticha] grasslands

name: Western Carpathian [Oreochloa disticha] grasslands

name: Eastern Carpathian [Oreochloa disticha] grasslands
description: Alpine formations of the eastern Carpathians of Romania and the Ukraine dominated by [Oreochloa disticha] ([Sesleria disticha]) accompanied by [Juncus trifidus], of windswept crests and shaded slopes, on shallow podzolic siliceous soils, accompanied by regional species [Potentilla aurea] ssp. [chrysocraspeda], [Senecio abrotanifolius] ssp. [carpathicus], [Poa media], [Campanula serrata], [Festuca bucegiensis], [Soldanella hungarica] ssp. [hungarica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynio-Carpathian [Juncus trifidus] swards
