source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian alpine grasslands
description: Extrasylvatic grasslands of the Elburz range of northern Iran, of limited extent and insularized, developed under humid alpine conditions, with [Dactylis glomerata], [Alopecurus spp.], [Sesleria phleoides], [Trifolium spp.], [Lotus corniculatus], [Polygonum bistorta], [Primula auriculata], [Pedicularis comosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian alpine grasslands
description: High altitude grass and sedge dominated communities of eastern Anatolian, Irano-Afghan and Central Asian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Altaic alpine grasslands
description: High altitude grass and sedge communities of the Altai and other central and eastern Asian boreal mountain ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan alpine grasslands
description: High altitude grass and sedge dominated communities of the Himalayan system, developed at the 3800 or 4200 to 4800 or 5500 m level in the main ranges and at the 4000-5100 m level on the dry Tibetan plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian alpine grasslands
description: High altitude grass and sedge dominated communities of the high mountains of the Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Humid grassland and tall herb communities
description: Unimproved or lightly improved wet meadows and tall herb communities of the boreal, nemoral, warm-temperate humid, steppic and mediterranean zones of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lowland tall herb communities
description: Dense stands of tall or medium-tall hygrophile herbs developed in strips on fertile alluvial stream banks of the boreal, nemoral and steppe zone lowlands, and, by extension, tall herb stands colonizing humid hay meadows and pastures after more or less long discontinuation of mowing or grazing. Higher altitude formations, most characteristic of the subalpine zone of mountains, are listed under unit 37.8; the highly distinctive, lowland and montane, very tall herb formations of the Pacific Far East are individualized under unit 37.9.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western nemoral tall herb communities
description: River bank, humid depression and abandoned meadow tall herb communities of the western deciduous forest region and its zones of influence, characteristically dominated by [Filipendula ulmaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western riverine meadowsweet stands
description: Hygrophile tall herb strips of fertile alluvial stream banks of Western Europe and western Central Europe, with irradiations in sub-Mediterranean regions and in the hills of the Pannonic plain, mostly dominated by [Filipendula ulmaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic and sub-Atlantic meadowsweet stands
description: Hygrophile tall herb strips of fertile alluvial stream banks of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Western Europe, western and northern Central Europe, with irradiations in sub-Mediterranean regions and in the hills of the Pannonic plain, mostly dominated by [Filipendula ulmaria], with [Achillea ptarmica], [Angelica sylvestris], [Cirsium palustre], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Epilobium hirsutum], [Geranium palustre], [Eupatorium cannabinum], [Lysimachia vulgaris], [Lythrum salicaria], [Phalaris arundinacea], [Polygonum bistorta], [Valeriana officinalis], [Rumex acetosa], [Urtica dioica], [Vicia cracca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyper-Atlantic [Iris]-[Filipendula] stands
description: Hygrophile [Filipendula ulmaria]-dominated tall herb strips, often luxurient and species-rich, of the regions of Europe submitted to the most extreme Atlantic influence, enriched in [Iris pseudacorus] and, except in the far north, [Oenanthe crocata], known, in particular, from the western seaboard of Scotland, the Hebrides and the Orkneys.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subcontinental riverine tall herb stands
description: Hygrophile tall herb strips of fertile alluvial stream banks of eastern Central Europe and Eastern Europe, richer in species, in particular of continental affinities, than their western counterparts of unit 37.111; [Filipendula ulmaria], notably [Filipendula ulmaria] ssp. [picbaueri], is accompanied by [Veronica longifolia], [Scutellaria hastifolia], [Euphorbia lucida], [Stachys palustris], [Thalictrum flavum]. They are associated with grasslands of the [Cnidion], as the formations of unit 37.111 are with those of the [Calthion] or the [Molinion].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Recolonisation meadowsweet stands
description: Tall herb stands ([Filipendula ulmaria], [Angelica sylvestris]) colonizing humid hay meadows and pastures after more or less long discontinuation of mowing or grazing.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Great horsetail stands
description: Stands of [Equisetum telmateia], often forming tall, dense, extensive colonies, pure or associated with humid tall herb community components such as [Filipendula ulmaria], [Heracleum sphondylium], [Galium palustre], [Achillea ptarmica], [Angelica sylvestris], [Cirsium palustre], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Epilobium hirsutum], [Geranium palustre], [Eupatorium cannabinum], [Caltha palustris], [Lysimachia vulgaris], [Lythrum salicaria], [Phalaris arundinacea], [Polygonum bistorta], [Polygonum hydropiper], [Pulicaria dysenterica], [Valeriana officinalis], [Juncus inflexus], [Carex remota], [Carex riparia], of damp clay substrates, often on slopes and canal or railway banks, or along hedgerows.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal tall herb communities
description: River bank and humid depression tall herb communities of the lowlands of the boreal zone dominated by [Filipendula ulmaria], with, among others, [Achillea ptarmica], [Dactylorhiza fuschii], [Galium uliginosum], [Geum rivale], [Lysimachia vulgaris], [Trollius europeaus], [Valeriana sambucifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental tall herb communities
description: River bank and fresh-water humid depression tall herb communities of the continental steppe zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern nemoral tall herb communities
description: River-bank and humid depression tall herb communities of the Far Eastern deciduous forest region and its zones of influence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eutrophic humid grasslands
description: Meadows developed on moderately to very nutrient-rich, alluvial or fertilized, wet or damp soils, often inundated at least in winter, and relatively lightly mowed or grazed, in deciduous forest and steppe zones of Eurasia. They form a transition between the mesophile meadows, the oligotrophic humid grasslands and the small sedge and large sedge communities. They include a large number of distinctive and often species-rich communities, many of which harbour specialized, rare and threatened species of plants and animals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic and sub-Atlantic humid meadows
description: Lightly managed hay meadows and pastures on both basicline and acidocline, nutrient-rich permanently or temporarily humid soils of middle European lowlands, hills and low mountains under Atlantic or sub-Atlantic climatic conditions, from the British Isles and northwestern Iberia east to Lithuania, in the Germano-Baltic plain, the Western and Central European Hercynian ranges, the Jura, the valleys and foothills of the Alps, the western Carpathians and the western Cantabro-Pyrenean range. Among the characteristic plant components of the highly diverse communities forming this unit are [Caltha palustris], [Cirsium palustre], [Cirsium rivulare], [Cirsium oleraceum], [Carduus personata], [Telekia speciosa], [Epilobium parviflorum], [Lychnis flos-cuculi], [Mentha aquatica], [Scirpus sylvaticus], [Stachys palustris], [Bromus racemosus], [Crepis paludosa], [Fritillaria meleagris], [Geum rivale], [Polygonum bistorta], [Senecio aquaticus], [Trollius europaeus], [Lotus uliginosus], [Trifolium dubium], [Equisetum palustre], [Equisetum telmateia], [Myosotis palustris], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Angelica sylvestris], [Oenanthe silaifolia], [Gratiola officinalis], [Inula salicina], [Succisella inflexa], [Dactylorhiza majalis], [Ranunculus acris], [Rumex acetosa], [Holcus lanatus], [Alopecurus pratensis], [Festuca pratensis], [Festuca gigantea], [Juncus effusus], [Juncus filiformis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cabbage thistle meadows
description: Tall-herb rich wet meadows dominated by, or with an abundance of, [Cirsium oleraceum], distributed in Western and Central Europe from Denmark, locally Scania, norhwestern Germany, Belgium, France, northwestern Spain, east to Poland, Lithuania, the Bohemian basin, Austria, best developed in the submontane level of the Hercynian ranges, the Jura and the pre-Alps on base-rich loams of river and brook floodplains and lakesides; [Cirsium oleraceum], [Angelica sylvestris], [Caltha palustris], [Lychnis flos-cuculi], [Ranunculus acris], [Polygonum bistorta], [Rumex acetosa], [Holcus lanatus], [Alopecurus pratensis], [Festuca pratensis], [Poa trivialis] are characteristic of their cortŠge; in northern Germany, Poland, Lithuania, the communities are enriched in [Polygonum bistorta] and lack several characteritics of their middle Hercynian cortŠge, in particular [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Colchicum autumnale], [Silaum silaus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Globe flower-brook thistle meadows
description: Wet meadows of montane areas of the higher Hercynian ranges, the Jura and the Alpine piedmont rich in [Trollius europaeus] and [Cirsium rivulare], replacing the cabbage thistle meadows of unit 37.212 at higher altitudes. Their cortŠge includes [Cirsium oleraceum], [Caltha palustris], [Lychnis flos-cuculi], [Myosotis palustris], [Geum rivale], [Festuca pratensis], [Galium album], [Ranunculus acris], [Holcus lanatus] and, sometimes, in particular in the Swiss Jura, [Fritillaria meleagris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western tufted hairgrass meadows
description: Coarse humid meadows of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Europe dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa], characteristic of permanently moist soils submitted to periodical inundation, favoured by grazing.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic tufted hairgrass meadows
description: Coarse grasslands of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Western, Northern and, locally, western Central Europe and northern Eastern Europe, overwhelmingly dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa], characteristic of permanently moist, gleyed and periodically inundated near-neutral soils, with a highly variable, usually species-poor, complement of species that includes the grasses [Holcus lanatus], [Festuca rubra], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Agrostis capillaris], [Poa trivialis], [Poa pratensis], [Dactylis glomerata], [Lolium perenne], [Alopecurus pratensis], sometimes forming closely grazed swards around the tussocks of the less palatable [Deschampsia], as well as, among others, [Juncus affinis], [Juncus inflexus], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Cardamine pratense], [Angelica sylvestris], [Achillea ptarmica], [Ranunculus acris], [Ranunculus repens], [Cirsium arvense], [Rumex acetosa], [Cerastium fontanum], [Plantago lanceolata], [Lathyrus pratensis], [Centaurea nigra], [Dactylorhiza fuchsii]. They are particularly well characterized in the English lowlands and in Fennoscandia,  but occur locally farther east and south, notably in the Netherlands, in Belgium, in the Campine, the loess region and the peri-Hercynian calcareous regions, in northern Germany, in the Bohemian basin, in Austria, particularly under the influence of grazing. Grassland communities dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa] of regions of more continental climates of eastern and southeastern Europe belong to the inundation communities of units 37.23 and 37.263.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal tufted hairgrass meadows
description: Wet meadows of the middle boreal, northern boreal, oceanic boreal, arctoalpine zones of Fennoscandia and of Iceland, where they colonize moist stoney slopes and land slips on mountainsides as well as valley bottom allluvions, dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Carex nigra], [Ranunculus acris] and, in Fennoscandia, [Cirsium helenioides], with, in particular, [Bartsia alpina], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Filipendula ulmaria], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Rumex acetosa]; the cortŠge of Fennoscandian communities includes [Rubus arcticus], [Saussurea alpina], [Trollius europaeus], [Viola epipsila], that of Icelandic communities [Agrostis canina], [Agrostis capillaris], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Cardamine pratensis], [Equisetum palustre], [Equisetum pratense], [Festuca rubra] [s.l.], [Festuca vivipara], [Juncus balticus], [Trifolium repens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marsh ragwort meadows
description: Wet meadows and water-meadows of the lowlands of Britain, northern Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, France and northwestern Spain, developed on nutrient-rich, acidocline alluvions of rivers and brooks with a fluctuating water regime in which [Senecio aquaticus] and [Bromus racemosus] are usually prominent, accompanied by a variable cortŠge; [Potentilla palustris] and [Menyanthes trifoliata] characterize mesotrophic stands, [Ranunculus auricomus] and [Primula elatior] somewhat more base-rich ones. [Carex disticha] is usually present and sometimes abundant, marking a transition towards [Magnocaricion] communities of unit 53.211. At higher altitudes, above 250 m, on base-poor soils, these communities evolve towards [Polygonum bistorta]-dominated communities of unit 37.215.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bistort meadows
description: Wet and humid meadows of sub-Atlantic Western and Central Europe dominated by, or very rich in, [Polygonum bistorta], most characteristic of montane or submontane regions of the Hercynian ranges and neighbouring regions. They include distinctive acidocline Hercynian communities in which [Polygonum bistorta] is associated with [Deschampsia cespitosa] or [Juncus filiformis], [Polygonum bistorta]-enriched submontane or montane variants of thistle or ragwort lowland communities of units 37.211 or 37.214, of the montane thistle-globeflower communities of unit 37.212, of the clubrush communities of unit 37.219, peri-Hercynian submontane and lowland thermophilous communities of the Danube basin, and montane communities of the Iberian peninsula. They constitute the principal habitat of the threatened fritillary [Proclossiana eunomia], and, at least locally, an important habitat for other threatened butterflies, in particular, the copper [Palaeochrysophanus (Lycaena) hippothoe].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thread rush meadows
description: Humid and wet meadows of sub-Atlantic Europe dominated by or rich in [Juncus filiformis], or, in Iceland, [Juncus balticus] ([Juncus arcticus]), often accompanied by [Carex nigra], [Carex echinata], [Molinia caerulea], [Potentilla erecta], mostly developed on lime-poor soils, of strong boreal affinities, most characteristic of Fennoscandia, Iceland, the northern Germano-Baltic plain and the neighbouring Hercynian ranges, rare farther south, limited to small surfaces in cold-pocket areas of the greater Hercynian ranges and the pre-Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Soft rush meadows
description: Wet and humid meadows of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Europe dominated by the tall tussock-forming [Juncus effusus] or [Juncus inflexus], with a usually species-poor accompanying flora, characteristic of relatively nutrient-rich, acidocline to basicline, permanently moist soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Blunt-flowered rush meadows
description: Calciphile wet meadows of Western Europe, Central Europe and northwestern Eastern Europe, northeast at least to Estonia, dominated by or rich in [Juncus subnodulosus], characteristic of very wet calcareous soils or soils flushed by calcareous waters, transitional to the small sedge fens of the [Caricion davallianae] (unit 54.2), surviving mostly in the British Isles, in the Alpine foothills, in the moraine land of northern Germany, in chalk hills of northwestern Germany, in northern Jutland, on Fyn, in southern and central Scania, on ™land, in wet dune slacks of the Atlantic and North Sea seaboard of the continent of Europe; many formations are rather oligotrophic and could equally be listed under unit 37.3. Typical of these communities are the [Juncus subnodulosus]-[Cirsium palustre] fen-meadows, widespread in the southern British lowlands, particularly in East Anglia, north Buckinghamshire and Angelsey, rich in [Juncus subnodulosus], [Cirsium palustre], [Equisetum palustre], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Holcus lanatus], [Lotus uliginosus], [Mentha aquatica], [Caliergon cuspidatum]; a characteristically variable species-rich cortŠge, influenced by the various grazing and mowing routines the meadows are subjected to, may include, among others, [Trifolium spp.], [Briza media], [Carex elata], [Iris pseudacorus], [Molinia caerulea], [Dactylorhiza fuchsii], [Dactylorhiza praetermissa], [Dactylorhiza incarnata]. Also particularly characteristic are the [Juncus subnodulosus] formations that succeed fen communities of unit 54.2 in the colonization of coastal wet dune slacks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wood clubrush meadows
description: Lowland to montane wet grassland of sub-Atlantic Europe, east to Lithuania, the Bohemian basin and Austria, developed on waterlogged siliceous loams or peats, dominated, often overwhelmingly so, by [Scirpus sylvaticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brook thistle meadows
description: Eutrophic wet meadows of the Carpathian region dominated by [Cirsium rivulare], eastern vicariant of the communities of unit 37.211, characteristically developed on loams, gleys or pseudogleys, often with anmoor characteristics, in higher, cooler elevations of the montane level. They extend to lowland and hill pre-Pannonic areas, to the pre-Alps of Styria, to the eastern Hercynian ranges, and to the eastern Germano-Baltic plain, northeast, as rare communities, to Lithuania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crested dog's tail-rush meadows
description: Humid grasslands of sub-Atlantic Europe submitted to a mixed regime of haycutting and grazing, in particular, single early-summer cutting followed by later prolonged grazing, occupied by a mixture of species of mesophile pastures, notably [Cynosurus cristatus], [Lolium perenne], [Trifolium repens], and [Molinietalia] species resistant to changes in the exploitation regime, such as [Juncus effusus], [Juncus inflexus], [Lychnis flos-cuculi], [Cirsium palustre]. These grasslands constitute transitions between mesophile grasslands of unit 38 and humid grasslands of 37.21, particularly of unit 37.214; they are also closely related to formations of unit 37.217.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marsh thistle meadows
description: Sub-Atlantic wet grasslands of brook banks and soggy slopes of rainy granitic and cristaline hills and low mountains of middle Europe, most characteristic of the eastern Hercynian ranges and the northern pre-Alps, extending west to the Hercynian ranges of sub-Atlantic western Europe, dominated by [Cirsium palustre], accompanied by [Angelica sylvestris] at the lower altitudes, [Polygonum bistorta] at the higher altitudes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Melancholy thistle meadows
description: Humid meadows of the montane level of the siliceous eastern Hercynian ranges, dominated by [Cirsium helenioides] ([Cirsium heterophyllum]) and [Cirsium palustre], accompanied by [Polygonum bistorta], [Crepis mollis], [Deschampsia cespitosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chervil wet meadows
description: Montane brook meadows of the higher mid-German Hercynian hills, and very locally, of the northern pre-Alps, developed on clayey siliceous alluvions, with [Chaerophyllum hirsutum], [Ranunculus aconitifolius], [Caltha palustris], [Crepis paludosa], [Myiosotis palustris], [Polygonum bistorta], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Angelica sylvestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calcareous dunal small reed fens
description: Communities of calcareous wet dune slacks dominated by [Calamagrostis epigejos], in particular, [Calamagrostis epigejos]-dominated facies and evolution stages of the [Juncus subnodulosus] formations of unit 37.218, characteristic of northern French and Belgian dunes and rare fen formations of the Dutch North Sea Islands formed by [Carex hartmanii], [Calamagrostis epigejos], [Carex trinervis], [Ophioglossum vulgatum], [Salix repens], evolution stage with light sand covering of the fen communities of unit 54.2H2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sharp-flowered rush meadows
description: Humid meadows of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Europe dominated by, or rich in, [Juncus acutiflorus]. They are floristically and phytosociologically very varied and many are as related to the oligotrophic [Molinion] communities of unit 37.3 as to the more eutrophic [Calthion] ones of unit 37.2. Sharp-flowered rush meadows are particularly characteristic of the oceanic and suboceanic regions of the western seaboard of Europe from northwestern Iberia to the Low Countries, extending locally in Hercynian ranges to the Harz and the Bohemian Quadrangle and in small sub-Atlantic enclaves of the Germano-Baltic plains to eastern Germany and Poland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subcontinental riverine meadows
description: Meadows of the valleys of great rivers of continental or subcontinental climate regions of Central Europe, submitted to repeated inundation periods in the year, characteristic of the Elbe, the Saale, the Main valleys of Germany, of Bohemia, Moravia, Austria and northeastern Croatia, with a disjunct outpost in the arid Rhine graben; they are usually dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa]; characteristic species include [Cnidium dubium] ([Cnidium venosum]), [Viola persicifolia], [Allium angulosum], [Iris sibirica], [Oenanthe lachenalii], [Oenanthe silaifolia], [Gratiola officinalis], [Juncus atratus], [Leucojum aestivum], [Carex praecox] var. [suzae], [Lythrum virgatum]. Because of universal river control schemes, these communities, dependent on natural or near natural flow regemes, are extremely threatened.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Flood swards and related communities
description: Grasslands of occasionally flooded river and lake banks, of depressions where rain water collects, of disturbed humid areas and of humid pastures submitted to intensive grazing.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall rush pastures
description: Rush ([Juncus effusus], [Juncus conglomeratus], [Juncus inflexus]) colonies of intensively grazed pastures, in part an extreme facies of [Juncus effusus] humid grasslands of unit 37.217, but also of other wet grasslands of unit 37.2 and of more mesophile grasslands of unit 38.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Flood swards
description: Flood swards of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Europe, developed on ground submitted to periodical or occasional inundation and subsequent drying under relatively maritime climates, with [Agrostis stolonifera], [Carex hirta], [Festuca arundinacea], [Juncus inflexus], [Alopecurus geniculatus], [Rumex crispus], [Mentha longifolia], [Mentha pulegium], [Potentilla anserina], [Potentilla reptans], [Ranunculus repens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marsh foxtail flood swards
description: Flood swards dominated by [Alopecurus geniculatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Creeping bent flood swards
description: Flood swards dominated by [Agrostis stolonifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall fescue flood swards
description: Flood swards dominated by [Festuca arundinacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Common couch flood swards
description: Flood swards dominated by [Elymus repens] ([Agropyron repens]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhenish [Deschampsia media] flood swards
description: Local flood swards of the Rhine valley dominated by [Deschampsia media].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small rush swards
description: Grasslands of occasionally flooded river and lake banks, of depressions where rain water collects, of disturbed humid areas and of humid pastures submitted to intensive grazing dominated by small rushes, in particular [Juncus compressus] or [Juncus tenuis] ([Juncus macer]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Transitional tall herb humid meadows
description: Recently abandoned hay meadows evolving towards the communities of unit 37.1 or towards woodland, with invasion of [Polygonum bistorta], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Phragmites communis], may, if useful, be coded under this subunit instead of unit 37.21.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental humid meadows
description: Meadows of moderately to very nutrient-rich, alluvial or fertilized, nonsaline, wet or damp soils in the steppe and wooded steppe zones of Eurasia and their areas of influence. They are widespread in southeastern Central Europe, in Eastern Europe and southern Siberia, extending west to the Pannonic plain and to areas of Pannonic or Pontic influence in southern Moravia, sub-Carpathian hills and the Balkans.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pannonic ashy thistle humid meadows
description: Humid grasslands of pre-Pannonic hills of Austria, Moravia, Hungary, Slovakia and Transylvania, rich in [Cirsium canum], usually dominated by [Alopecurus pratensis], [Festuca pratensis], [Deschampsia cespitosa], with [Polygonum bistorta], [Angelica sylvestris], [Scirpus sylvaticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Pannonic humid meadows
description: Humid meadows of river valleys of the eastern Carpathian ranges, their foothills and associated plateaux, of the southern pre-Pannonic foothills of the western Carpathians and of the Central Hungarian Range, similar to the sub-Atlantic meadows of the [Calthion palustris] and, like them, dominated by species such as [Scirpus sylvaticus], [Juncus effusus], [Cirsium rivulare], [Caltha palustris] ([Caltha laeta]), but developed under more subcontinental climatic conditions and accompanied by regional species, in particular [Valeriana simplicifolia], [Pedicularis limnogena], [Ligularia sibirica] and [Telekia speciosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian globe flower-cabbage thistle meadows
description: Humid meadows of the eastern Carpathian system rich in [Cirsium oleraceum] and [Trollius europaeus], with [Angelica sylvestris], [Equisetum palustre], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Molinia caerulea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Pannonic bistort meadows
description: Humid meadows of the eastern Carpathian system and of sub-Pannonic hills rich in [Polygonum bistorta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian thread rush meadows
description: Humid meadows of the eastern Carpathian system dominated by [Juncus filiformis], often accompanied by [Carex pyrenaica] and [Deschampsia cespitosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian soft rush meadows
description: [Juncus effusus]-dominated humid meadows of the eastern Carpathian system, with [Epilobium palustre].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Pannonic wood clubrush meadows
description: Humid grasslands of the eastern Carpathian system and of sub-Pannonic hills dominated by [Scirpus sylvaticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Pannonic brook thistle meadows
description: Humid grasslands of the eastern Carpathian system and of sub-Pannonic hills rich in [Cirsium rivulare], accompanied by montane boreal species, in particular [Trollius europaeus] and [Ligularia glauca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrio-Pannonic riverine and humid meadows
description: Flood-plain meadows of the great rivers of the Alf”ld and the Little Alf”ld, of the Pannonic Danumbe basin, of the Drava and Sava basins of Croatia, Hungary and Slovenia, of the Leitha and Danube basins of eastern Lower Austria and the Burgenland, of Transylvania and Oltenia, of the Illyrian oak and beech zones of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, subject to repeated flooding in the course of the year; wet or damp, nonsaline meadows of moderately to very nutrient-rich, alluvial or fertilized soils of the same regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Sarmatic humid meadows
description: Floodplain and humid meadows of the Ponto-Caspian basin and of the steppe and nemoral Russian plateaux and plains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic humid meadows
description: Humid meadows of the western Pontic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic temporary dune slack grasslands
description: Humid meadows of the Danube Delta, with [Molinia caerulea] ssp. [euxina], [Vicia biennis], [Cirsium alatum], [Erianthus adpressus], [Carex panicea], [Potentilla erecta], [Euphorbia lucida], [Symphytum officinale], [Pulicaria dysenterica], [Eleocharis palustris], [Orchis elegans] ([Orchis palustris] ssp. [elegans]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dune slack [Holoschoenus] grasslands
description: Humid formations of southern Moldavia, Oltenia and the Danube Delta, developed in broad interdunal depressions with an accumulation of calcic humus, dominated by [Scirpus holoschoenus] ([Holoschoenus vulgaris]), accompanied by a [Festucetalia vaginatae] cortŠge that includes [Plantago arenaria], [Anthemis ruthenica], [Euphorbia seguierana], [Dianthus polymorphus], [Carex ligerica], [Festuca arenicola], [Koeleria glauca], [Asperula setulosa], [Helianthemum nummularium], [Syrenia montana], [Minuartia setacea], [Salix rosmarinifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic riverine meadows
description: Floodplain meadows of northern Russia, Bashkiria, Bielorussian Polesia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caspian riverine meadows
description: Floodplain meadows of the semidesert regions of the Ponto-Caspian plains, in particular of the Don and Volga valleys.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian humid meadows
description: Meadows of moderately to very nutrient-rich, alluvial or fertilized, nonsaline, wet or damp soils of the Transvolgan, Kazakh, Kourgan, Ichim, Koulounda, Baraba, Barnaul steppe and wooded steppe regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental East Asian humid meadows
description: Meadows of moderately to very nutrient-rich, alluvial or fertilized, nonsaline, wet or damp soils in the Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, Songnen Plain and northern Chinese western Loess Plateau steppe and wooded steppe zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern humid meadows
description: Meadows of moderately to very nutrient-rich, alluvial or fertilized, wet or damp soils, often inundated at least in winter, often mowed or grazed, of the deciduous forest zone of eastern Eurasia and its areas of influence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oligotrophic humid grasslands
description: Humid grasslands on soils very poor in nutrients of the deciduous forest and steppe zones of Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Purple moorgrass meadows and related communities
description: Humid grasslands of soils poor in nutrients, unfertilized and with a fluctuating water level, of Western Europe, south to northwestern Iberia, of Northern Europe, of Central Europe, locally of western Eastern Europe, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Succisa pratensis], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Potentilla erecta], [Allium angulosum], [Allium suaveolens], [Stachys officinalis] ([Betonica officinalis]), [Cirsium dissectum], [Cirsium tuberosum], [Dianthus superbus], [Trollius europaeus], [Galium boreale], [Gentiana asclepiadea], [Gentiana pneumonanthe], [Gladiolus palustris], [Silaum silaus], [Selinum carvifolia], [Inula salicina], [Iris sibirica], [Laserpitium prutenicum], [Lathyrus pannonicus], [Tetragonolobus maritimus], [Serratula tinctoria], [Carex tomentosa], [Carex panicea], [Carex pallescens], [Parnassia palustris], [Platanthera bifolia], [Colchicum autumnale], [Ophioglossum vulgatum], [Dactylorhiza maculata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calcicline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous or calcicline soils of middle Europe, southern Fennoscandia and northwestern Iberia, with [Silaum silaus], [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Selinum carvifolia], [Stachys officinalis] ([Betonica officinalis]), [Cirsium tuberosum], [Carex tomentosa], [Tetragonolobus maritimus], [Galium boreale], [Serratula tinctoria], [Inula salicina], [Dianthus superbus] and abundant [Colchicum autumnale].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European calcicline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous or calcicline soils of Central Europe, northeast to eastern Germany, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, east to the Bohemian basin, Slovakia and the Ukraine, southeast to Austria, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Selinum carvifolia], [Succisa pratensis], [Galium uliginosum], [Serratula tinctoria], [Gentiana pneumonanthe], [Stachys officinalis] ([Betonica officinalis]), [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Laserpitium prutenicum], [Carex panicea], [Euphrasia rostkoviana], [Prunella vulgaris], [Ranunculus acris], [Silaum silaus], [Cirsium tuberosum], [Carex tomentosa], [Tetragonolobus maritimus], [Inula salicina], [Dianthus superbus], [Epipactis palustris], [Ophioglossum vulgatum], [Iris sibirica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Alpine calcicline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous or calcicline soils of the calcareous northern pre-Alps, the eastern Alps, the Jura, the Baar plateau, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with a species cortŠge characterized by the prominence of [Trollius europaeus], [Gentiana asclepiadea] or [Allium suaveolens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Alpine garlic-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous or calcicline soils of the eastern Alps and neighbouring regions, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Allium suaveolens], [Allium angulosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Alpine gentian-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous or calcicline soils of the calcareous northern pre-Alps, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with a species cortŠge characterized by the prominence of [Gentiana asclepiadea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine globeflower-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous or calcicline soils of the Jura and the Baar plateau, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with a species cortŠge characterized by the prominence of [Trollius europaeus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dealpine heavy metal purple moorgrass meadows
description: Wet grasslands of the banks of the Loisach dominated by [Molinia caerulea] accompanied by fragmentary heavy metal communities comprising [Minuartia verna] var. [hercynica], [Silene vulgaris] var. [humilis] and [Cardaminopsis halleri], with [Cladonia spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic calcicline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous and often alkaline soils of the Pannonic basin, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Lathyrus pannonicus], [Adenophora lilifolia], [Centaurea jacea], [Lotus maritimus], [Cirsium canum], [Inula britannica], [Succisa pratensis], [Serratula tinctoria], [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Silaum silaus], [Carex distans], [Carex flacca], [Carex hostiana], [Juncus subnodulosus], [Sesleria uliginosa]. These grasslands have become extremely rare in Austria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern calcicline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid [Molinia] or [Molinia]-[Sesleria] grasslands of the northern and western periphery of the range of the typical Central European communities of units 37.3111 and 37.3112, with a species cortŠge tending somewhat towards that of the sympatric, Atlantic or sub-Atlantic, acidocline communities of unit 37.32.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British [Molinia]-[Crepis] meadows
description: Submontane humid grasslands of the northern Pennines and the Lake District developed on moist moderately base-rich and calcareous peats and peaty mineral soils dominated by [Molinia caerulea] with [Carex nigra], [Carex panicea], with [Crepis paludosa], [Succisa pratensis], [Valeriana dioica], [Potentilla erecta], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Angelica sylvestris], [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Trollius europaeus], [Ranunculus acris], [Serratula tinctoria], [Carex pulicaris], [Carex flacca], [Carex hostiana], [Juncus acutiflorus], [Festuca rubra], [Briza media], [Equisetum palustre], [Calliergon cuspidatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scandio-Baltic calcicline purple moorgrass-blue moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich calcicolous wet grasslands of Scandinavia dominated by [Sesleria caerulea], [Molinia caerulea], [Carex panicea] and [Linum catharticum] with a ground layer dominated by [Campylium stellatum] and [Ctenidum molluscum]. They are distributed in the Danish archipelago, in extreme southern Scania, ™land and Gotland, coastal Estonia, along the coasts of the Skagerrak, the Kattegatt, and the Oslo Fjord, along the Atlantic coast of Norway north to the middle boreal zone, in west G”tland and east G”tland, in Södermanland and Uppland, in central J„mtland on moist gley-calcareous soils with a relatively thick, peaty sod, under humid to semiarid nemoral, boreonemoral, southern boreal, middle boreal and oceanic climate conditions. [Carex flacca] and [Primula farinosa] are characteristic of their species cortŠge which also includes [Carex flava], [Carex lepidocarpa], [Carex pulicaria], [Carex hostiana], [Carex nigra], [Cirsium acaule], [Parnassia palustre], [Pinguicula vulgaris], [Polygala amarella], [Potentilla erecta], [Primula vulgaris], [Scorzonera humilis], [Succisa pratensis], [Festuca rubra], [Hierochloe odorata], [Briza media] and many orchid species. These grasslands have affinities with the moister variants of unit 34.32, in particular the British [Sesleria] grasslands of unit 34.32142 and the moist Mesobromions of unit 34.324.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic calcicline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich calcicline wet grasslands of the western periphery of the northwestern European Hercynian ranges, known in particular from Belgium and northern France, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Silaum silaus], [Succisa pratensis], [Achillea ptarmica], [Selinum carvifolia], [Scorzonera humilis], [Cirsium palustre], [Colchicum autumnale] sometimes abundant, [Dactylorhiza incarnata], [Dactylorhiza majalis], [Epipactis palustris], [Carex panicea], [Carex tomentosa], [Carex hostiana], [Carex pulicaris], [Carex flava], [Juncus inflexus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermophile calcicline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Species-rich humid grasslands of oligotrophic calcareous or calcicline soils of southern France and northwestern Iberia dominated by, or rich in, [Molinia caerulea], with a species cortŠge that includes, in addition to typical [Molinion] species, such as [Succisa pratensis] and [Stachys officinalis], a number of thermo-Atlantic or Mediterraneo-Atlantic species, among which [Centaurea nigra] var. [radiata], [Serapias cordigera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acidocline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Relatively species-poor humid grasslands of oligotrophic acid moist gley soils, sometimes with stagnant water and peat formation, of middle Europe north to the southern boreal approaches in Fennoscandia and the Faeroe Islands, and south to northwestern Iberia, with [Succisa pratensis], [Potentilla erecta], [Potentilla anglica], [Viola persicifolia], [Viola palustris], [Galium uliginosum], [Cirsium dissectum], [Crepis paludosa], [Luzula multiflora], [Juncus conglomeratus] ([Juncus subuliflorus]), [Ophioglossum vulgatum], [Inula britannica], [Lotus uliginosus], [Dianthus deltoides], [Carex pallescens], [Carex demissa], [Carex canescens], [Carex echinata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic thistle-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline oligotrophic humid grasslands of southern and eastern Britain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, northwestern Germany and northern France dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Cirsium dissectum], [Succisa pratensis], [Potentilla erecta], [Lotus uliginosus], [Galium uliginosum], [Crepis paludosa], [Viola palustris], [Luzula multiflora], [Juncus acutiflorus], [Juncus conglomeratus] ([Juncus subuliflorus]), [Carex panicea], [Carex echinata], [Carex hostiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic rush-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline oligotrophic humid grasslands of the extreme Atlantic fringe of Europe, in western Britain and Ireland, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Potentilla erecta], [Cirsium palustre], [Succisa pratensis], [Juncus acutiflorus], [Juncus effusus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian acidocline purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline oligotrophic humid grasslands of Fennoscandia, north to the southern boreal zone and to the oceanic middle boreal zone of Norway, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Succisa pratensis], [Potentilla erecta], [Cirsium palustre]. Wetter, highly oligotrophic, communities, developed on permanently wet peaty ground, typically have a fairly tall sward, in which [Molinia caerulea] is the single dominant and a species cortŠge that includes [Juncus conglomeratus], [Juncus effusus], [Pinguicula vulgaris]; somewhat drier and more mesotrophic communities, occupying moist gley soils, often with stagnant water and peat formation, are short, grass and sedge dominated in which the dominance is shared between [Molinia caerulea], [Carex nigra] and [Carex panicea], with a species cortŠge of variable richness, transitional between the species-poor communities of unit 37.32 and the species-rich calcicline meadows of unit 37.311, often fairly similar to the latter, including [Filipendula ulmaria], [Galium palustre], [Geum rivale], [Juncus filiformis], [Viola palustris], and, on the continent, but absent in the Faeroes, [Platanthera bifolia]; communities of western Norway are distinct, comprising a number of species of Atlantic affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European rush-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline [Molinia caerulea]-dominated oligotrophic humid grasslands of Central Europe, distributed from Germany to Poland and Lithuania and from eastern France to Austria, of limited occurrence within the area of prevalence of the more continental, basicline communities of unit 37.311; their species cortŠge includes [Succisa pratensis], [Potentilla erecta], [Cirsium palustre], [Juncus conglomeratus] ([Juncus subuliflorus]), [Juncus effusus], [Juncus acutiflorus], [Agrostis capillaris], [Viola persicifolia] ([Viola stagnina]), [Inula britannica], [Achillea ptarmica], [Hydrocotyle vulgaris], [Deschampsia cespitosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallo-Atlantic caraway-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline oligotrophic humid grasslands of eu-Atlantic France dominated by [Molinia caerulea] with [Carum verticillatum], [Wahlenbergia hederacea], [Lobellia urens], [Scutellaria minor], [Pucedanum gallicum], [Pucedanum lancifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-Gallic sawwort-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline oligotrophic humid grasslands of thermo-Atlantic France and northwestern Iberia dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Serratula seoanei], [Cirsium filipendulum], [Allium ochroleucon], [Allium ericetorum], [Laserpitium prutenicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arverno-Pyrenaean bistort-purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline oligotrophic humid grasslands ofthe Massif Central and the eastern and central Pyrenees dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Polygonum bistorta], [Crepis paludosa], [Pediculara mixta], [Ligularia siberica], [Selinum pyreneum], [Myosotis lamottiana], [Tephroseris helenitis] ssp. [arvernensis], [Tephroseris helenitis] ssp. [helenitis], [Achillea pyrenaica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Giant moorgrass swards
description: Very tall [Molinia caerulea] ssp. [arundinacea] ([Molinia arundinacea])-dominated humid meadows of southern Central Europe, in particular, of the Illyrian zone, the peri-Pannonic and peri-Bohemian regions, the Danube, Lech and Isar basins, the upper Rhine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal purple moorgrass meadows
description: Acidocline oligotrophic wet, often inundated, grasslands of boreal Fennoscandia dominated by [Molinia caerulea], with [Achillea millefolium], [Bartsia alpina], [Galium boreale], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Lysimachia thyrsiflora], [Pinguicula vulgaris], [Parnassia palustris], [Scutellaria galericulata], [Trientalis europaea], [Viola epipsila], [Carex acuta], [Carex aquatilis], [Juncus filiformis], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Nardus stricta], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Hypnum lindbergii], [Mnium rugicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Heath rush meadows and humid mat-grass swards
description: Humid, often peaty or semipeaty swards of middle Europe, southwest to northwestern Iberia and east to Lithuania, with [Nardus stricta], [Juncus squarrosus], [Festuca ovina], [Gentiana pneumonanthe], [Pedicularis sylvatica], [Scirpus cespitosus] and sometimes [Sphagnum spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental oligotrophic humid grasslands
description: Nutrient-poor humid grasslands of the northern steppe zone of central Eurasia, eastern vicariants of the [Molinion] communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern oligotrophic grasslands
description: Nutrient-poor humid grasslands of the eastern deciduous forest zone of Eurasia and its regions of influence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean tall humid grasslands
description: Mediterranean humid grasslands of tall grasses and rushes with [Scirpus holoschoenus] ([Holoschoenus vulgaris]), [Agrostis stolonifera], [Agrostis reuteri], [Galium debile], [Molinia caerulea], [Briza minor], [Melica cupanii], [Cyperus longus], [Linum tenue], [Trifolium resupinatum], [Schoenus nigricans], [Peucedanum hispanicum], [Carex mairii], [Juncus maritimus], [Juncus acutus], [Asteriscus aquaticus], [Hypericum tomentosum], [Hypericum tetrapterum], [Inula viscosa], [Oenanthe pimpinelloides], [Oenanthe lachenalii], [Eupatorium cannabinum], [Prunella vulgaris], [Pulicaria dysenterica], [Tetragonolobus maritimus], [Orchis laxiflora], [Dactylorhiza elata], [Succisa pratensis], [Sonchus maritimus] ssp. [aquatilis], [Silaum silaus], [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Serratula tinctoria], [Genista tinctoria], [Cirsium monspessulanum], [Cirsium pyrenaicum], [Senecio doria], [Dorycnium rectum], [Erica terminalis], [Euphorbia pubescens], [Lysimachia ephemerum], widespread in the entire Mediterranean basin, extending, along the coasts of the Black Sea, in particular in dunal systems, north to the Dobrogea and the Danube Delta, and, in valleys of the Balkan peninsula, north to the Banat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean short humid grasslands
description: Very short grasslands of impermeable compact soils or marls, wet for a large part of the year, and dessicated in summer, characteristic of the Mediterranean basin, with irradiations north to the Illyrian zone of the northwestern Balkan peninsula, with [Deschampsia media], [Centaurium pulchellum], [Lotus tenuis], [Trifolium lappaceum], [Prunella hyssopifolia], [Plantago maritima] ssp. [serpentina], [Centaurea timbali].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Mediterranean humid meadows
description: Humid meadows rich in clover ([Trifolium spp.]) of sub- and supramediterranean regions remote from Atlantic influence, in particular, of the Balkan peninsula, of the Apennines, of Mediterranean Anatolia, of Mediterranean North Africa, mostly developed at collinar levels.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Moesian riverine and humid clover meadows
description: Meso-hygrophile grasslands of river flood plains and other high water-table sites of the southern Balkan peninsula, in particular of Bulgaria, the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and northern Greece, with outposts in the Croatian coastlands, formed by [Alopecurus pratensis], [Alopecurus rendlei] ([Alopecurus utriculatus]), [Festuca pratensis] ([Festuca elatior]) or [Poa trivialis] ssp. [sylvicola] ([Poa sylvicola]), and by numerous [Trifolium spp.] including [Trifolium resupinatum], [Trifolium incarnatum], [Trifolium filiforme], [Trifolium balansae], [Trifolium nigrescens], [Trifolium michelianum], [Trifolium subterraneum], [Trifolium striatum], [Trifolium meneghinianum], [Trifolium patens], [Trifolium fragiferum], [Trifolium cinctum], [Medicago hispida] ssp. [apiculata], [Lotus corniculatus] var. [hirsutus], [Hordeum murinum], [Ranunculus marginatus], [Ranunculus velutinus], [Cirsium canum] var. [macedonicum], [Oenanthe stenoloba], [Moenchia mantica], [Lychnis flos-cuculi] ssp. [subintegra], [Teucrium scordioides], [Podospermum canum], [Narcissus poeticus], [Leucojum aestivum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine humid meadows
description: Permanent humid grasslands of Apennine karstic basins, with [Ranunculus velutinus], [Bromus racemosus], [Hordeum secalinum], [Trifolium dubium], [Trifolium resupinatum], [Trifolium micranthum], [Trifolium patens], [Trifolium fragiferum], [Trifolium pratense], [Trifolium repens], [Carex distans], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Gaudinia fragilis], [Ophioglossum vulgatum], [Centaurea jacea], [Holcus lanatus], [Alopecurus rendlei] ([Alopecurus utriculatus]), [Orchis laxiflora], [Colchicum lusitanum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dalmatian riverine and humid meadows
description: Humid meadows of Illyrian Istria and Dalmatia, developed in a mild semihumid to semiarid climate, of pronounced sub-Mediterranean affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrio-Moesian riverine and humid clover meadows
description: Floodplain meadows of southern sub-Pannonic regions, within the eastern [Carpinion illyricum], the [Quercion frainetto] and the [Fagion moesiacum] zones of Bosnia, Serbia, Oltenia and northwestern Bulgaria, under semihumid to semiarid climates, mostly dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Alopecurus pratensis] or [Poa trivialis] ssp. [sylvicola], with [Trifolium pallidum], [Trifolium patens], [Trifolium fragiferum], [Trifolium cinctum], [Ranunculus stevenii], [Lathyrus nissolia], [Medicago arabica], [Clematis integrifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian supra-Mediterranean humid grasslands
description: Humid meadows rich in clover of sub- and supramediterranean regions of Mediterranean Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: African supra-Mediterranean humid meadows
description: Humid meadows rich in clover of sub- and supramediterranean regions of Mediterranean North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Humid tall herb fringes
description: Watercourse veil and shady woodland edge communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Watercourse veils
description: Screens or veils of perennial tall herbs, small bushes and lianas lining lowland watercourses, and sometimes other water bodies, often with many ruderal and exogenous plants.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Angelica archangelica] fluvial communities
description: [Angelica archangelica] ssp. [litoralis] formations of great northern rivers, presently rare and threatened.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Angelica heterocarpa] fluvial communities
description: [Angelica heterocarpa] formations of tidal estuaries of the Loire, the Charente and the Gironde; the species is a rare and very narrow endemic of southwestern France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marsh mallow screens
description: [Althaea officinalis] formations of river banks and marsh edges, particularly on somewhat saline soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Butterbur riverine communities
description: Formations of the alluvial banks of small streams, characteristic of collinar and low montane levels of the Alpine system and the Hercynian ranges of Western and Central Europe and of northern Eastern Europe, constituted by [Petasites hybridus] ([Petasites officinalis]), [Petasites albus], [Petasites kablikianus] ([Petasites glabratus]), sometimes by [Chaerophyllum hirsutum] or [Equisetum telmateia], occasionally accompanied by various tall herbs, in particular, [Cirsium oleraceum], or by ferns.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West European mixed riverine screens
description: Screens or veils of perennial tall herbs, [Senecio fluviatilis], [Eupatorium cannabinum], [Epilobium hirsutum], [Sonchus palustris], [Urtica dioica], small bushes and lianas, [Calystegia sepium], [Cuscusta europaea], lining lowland watercourses, and sometimes other water bodies, of Western, Central and northern Eastern Europe, outside of the steppe and wooded-steppe zones, with many ruderal and introduced plants, such as [Aster spp.], [Rudbeckia spp.], [Solidago spp.], [Helianthus spp.], [Impatiens spp.], [Reynoutria japonica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental mixed riverine screens
description: Screens or veils of perennial tall herbs, [Senecio fluviatilis], [Eupatorium cannabinum], [Epilobium hirsutum], [Sonchus palustris], [Urtica dioica], small bushes and lianas, [Calystegia sepium], [Cuscusta europaea], lining lowland watercourses, and sometimes other water bodies, of the steppe and wooded-steppe zones of Eurasia, including, in the west, the Pannonic basin and the lower Danube valley, with many ruderal and introduced plants, such as [Aster spp.], [Rudbeckia spp.], [Solidago spp.], [Helianthus spp.], [Impatiens spp.], [Reynoutria japonica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian mixed riverine screens
description: Screens or veils of perennial tall herbs lining lowland watercourses, and sometimes other water bodies, of the nemoral zone of eastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shady woodland edge fringes
description: Nitro-hygrophilous communities of usually large-leaved herbs developing along the shaded side of wooded stands and hedges, with [Galium aparine], [Glechoma hederacea], [Geum urbanum], [Aegopodium podagraria], [Silene dioica], [Carduus crispus], [Chaerophyllum hirsutum], [Lamium album], [Alliaria petiolata], [Lapsana communis], [Geranium robertianum], [Viola alba], [Viola odorata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subalpine and alpine tall herb communities
description: Luxuriant tall herb formations of deep, humid soils in the montane to alpine, but mostly subalpine, levels of the higher mountains, with [Cicerbita alpina], [Cicerbita alpina plumieri], [Cirsium helenioides], [Cirsium spinosissimum], [Cirsium flavispina], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Polygonatum verticillatum], [Ranunculus platanifolius], [Aconitum vulparia], [Aconitum napellus], [Aconitum nevadense], [Adenostyles alliariae], [Senecio elodes], [Veratrum album], [Trollius europaeus], [Peucedanum ostruthium], [Doronicum austriacum], [Pedicularis foliosa], [Eryngium alpinum], [Leuzea rhapontica] ([Centaurea rhapontica]), [Valeriana pyrenaica], [Tozzia alpina]. Groupings of these plants can invade the [Aceri-Fagion] and reappear, along streams, lower down in montane beech forests. If useful, their presence can be noted by combining a code of 37.8 with the appropriate forest code.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Jura, the great Hercynian ranges, the Central Massif and the Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine adenostyles communities
description: [Adenostyles alliariae]-dominated stands and very mixed stands of the tall herb communities of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine fern communities
description: Fern-dominated facies of the tall herb communities of the Alps, with [Athyrium distentifolium] ([Athyrium alpestre]), [Athyrium filix-femina], succession stages floristically often more related to the small reed communities of 37.82.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine monkshood communities
description: Tall herb communities of the Alps dominated by [Aconitum tauricum], [Aconitum napellus] or [Aconitum compactum], often in almost pure stands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine butterbur communities
description: [Petasites albus]-dominated tall herb communities of the Alps characteristic of damper stations and montane brook edges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine leopardsbane communities
description: [Doronicum spp.]-dominated tall herb communities of the Alps structured around [Doronicum cataractarum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine sow-thistle communities
description: [Cicerbita alpina]-dominated facies of the tall-herb communities of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine lady's mantle communities
description: [Alchemilla vulgaris] agg.-dominated facies of the tall herb communities of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine cranesbill communities
description: [Geranium sylvaticum]-rich stands of the tall herb communities of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine buttercup communities
