description: [Ranunculus platanifolius]-dominated stands of the tall herb communities of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine larkspur communities
description: [Delphinium elatum]-dominated stands of the tall herb communities of the eastern Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine Carnic thistle communities
description: Rare tall herb communities of the eastern Alps dominated by [Carduus carduelis] and [Cirsium carniolicum], associated with Trisetum flavescens and [Myrrhis odorata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine giant knapweed communities
description: [Leuzea rhapontica] ([Centaurea rhapontica], [Stemmacantha rhapontica])-dominated stands of the tall herb communities of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Jura tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Jura.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Central Massif and of the great ranges of the Hercynian arc, in particular, the Vosges, the Black Forest and the major ranges of the Bohemian Quadrangle, the Sudeten, the Erzgebirge, the Bohemian Forest (Sumava).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian adenostyles communities
description: [Adenostyles alliariae]-dominated stands and very mixed stands of the tall herb communities of the Vosges, the Black Forest, the Sudeten and the Central Massif.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian high montane fern communities
description: Fern-dominated facies of the tall herb communities of the great Hercynian ranges, in particular, the Bohemian Quadrangle, with [Athyrium distentifolium] ([Athyrium alpestre]), [Athyrium filix-femina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian high montane butterbur communities
description: [Petasites albus]-dominated tall herb communities of the upper montane and subalpine levels of the Sudeten.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian high montane leopardsbane communities
description: [Doronicum spp.]-dominated tall herb communities of the Sudeten structured around [Doronicum austriacum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian high montane sow-thistle communities
description: [Cicerbita alpina]-dominated facies of the tall-herb communities of the great Hercynian ranges, in particular of the Sudeten, the Erzgebirge and the Black Forest.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian high montane globe flower communities
description: [Trollius europaeus]-dominated tall herb communities of the southeastern Sudeten.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian high montane cranesbill communities
description: [Geranium sylvaticum]-rich stands of the tall herb communities of the southeastern Sudeten.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian adenostyles communities
description: Tall herb communities of the Carpathians formed by [Adenostyles alliariae], [Cicerbita alpina] ([Mulgedium alpinum]), [Epilobium alpinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian fern communities
description: Tall herb communities of the Carpathians dominated by [Athyrium distentifolium] ([Athyrium alpestre]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian monkshood communities
description: Tall herb communities of the Carpathians formed by [Aconitum] species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North Carpathian monkshood communities
description: Tall herb communities of the northwestern Carpathians formed by [Aconitum firmum] ([Aconitum callibotryon]), [Archangelica officinalis], [Delphinium oxysepalum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian monkshood communities
description: Tall herb communities of the subalpine and alpine levels of the Eastern and Southern Carpathians, occupying wet nutrient- and humus-rich colluvions of glacial cirque perimeters dominated by [Aconitum tauricum], with [Saxifraga heucherifolia] and a representation of species of the [Adenostylion].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian butterbur communities
description: Formations of the Carpathians dominated by [Petasites spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian white butterbur communities
description: [Petasites albus]-dominated formations of the upper montane and lower subalpine levels of the Carpathians, with species typical of the [Adenostylion].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian glabrous butterbur communities
description: [Petasites kablikianus]-dominated formations of shady streamsides of Carpathian mountain valleys, with [Orobanche flava], [Carduus personata], [Chaerophyllum hirsutum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian Austrian leopardsbane communities
description: Tall herb formations of the Carpathians formed by [Aruncus sylvestris] and [Aconitum variegatum] ([Aconitum gracile]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian thistle-hogweed communities
description: Subalpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the eastern and southern Carpathians dominated by [Heracleum palmatum] and [Cirsium waldsteinii], with other regional species including [Salix silesiaca], [Leucanthemum waldsteinii], [Achillea distans], [Pulmonaria filarszkyana] and [Aconitum moldavicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Dinarides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric adenostyles communities
description: Tall-herb communities of the Dinarides formed by [Adenostyles alliariae], [Cicerbita alpina], [Doronicum austriacum], [Scopolia carniolica], [Eryngium alpinum], in single dominance or mixed stands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric monkshood communities
description: Tall herb communities of the Dinarides dominated by [Aconitum napellus], with [Lamiastrum galeobdolon], [Angelica archangelica], [Petasites albus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric [Laserpitium] communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb communities dominated by [Laserpitium archangelicum], with [Poa hybrida], [Hesperis dinarica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpigene tall grass communities
description: Communities of the montane and subalpine levels of high and moderately high mountains of the Alpine system and neighbouring ranges, dominated by tall grasses, accompanied by a species cortŠge similar to that of the subalpine tall-herb communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small-reed tall grass communities
description: Communities of the montane and subalpine levels of high and moderately high mountains of the Alpine system and neighbouring ranges, dominated by tall grasses of genus [Calamagrostis], accompanied by a species cortŠge similar to that of the subalpine tall-herb communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rough small-reed tall grass communities
description: Thermophile, meso-xerophile species-rich, abundantly flowering, often primary   formations of steep adrets of the subalpine level of the Alps, the Jura, the great Hercynian ranges and the Central Massif, the Dinarides, the Pelagonides,  the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Rhodopides, the Balkan Range, mostly dominated by [Calamagrostis arundinacea], associated with plants such as [Senecio doronicum], [Digitalis grandiflora], [Hieracium aurantiacum], [Hieracium prenanthoides], [Aconitum vulparia], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Bupleurum longifolium], [Galium boreale], [Lilium martagon], [Pimpinella major], [Rosa pendulina], [Sorbus sudetica], [Sorbus aria], [Sorbus mougeotii], [Sorbus chamaemespilus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wooly small-reed tall grass communities
description: Communities of the montane and subalpine levels of the Alps, the Sudeten, the Carpathians, the Rhodopes, dominated by [Calamagrostis villosa], accompanied by a tall-herb species cortŠge usually less rich in woodland edge and short grassland species than those of the [Calamagrostion arundinaceae]; characteristic species include [Adenostyles alliariae], [Peucedanum ostruthium], [Geum montanum], [Homogyne alpina], [Ligusticum mutellina], [Potentilla aurea], [Phleum rhaeticum], [Agrostis schraderana], [Dianthus superbus] ssp. [alpestris], [Hieracium prenanthoides], [Hieracium aureum], [Molinia caerulea], [Ranunculus platanifolius], [Silene vulgaris], [Solidago virgaurea] ssp. [minuta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fescue tall grass communities
description: Communities of the montane and subalpine levels of the Carpathians dominated by tall fescues, accompanied by a species cortŠge similar to that of the subalpine tall-herb communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian fescue tall grass communities
description: Tall, two-layered, closed [Festuca carpatica]-dominated grasslands of the northwestern and eastern Carpathians, developed on shallow stony soils overlying basic rocks, on steep slopes subjected to long snow cover, in particular, in avalanche troughs, physiognomically and ecologically similar to small reed grasslands of the [Calamagrostion arundinaceae] [s.l.], but with a species cortŠge characteristic in part of the calciphile grasslands of the [Seslerion tatrae] and the [Festuco saxatilis-Seslerion bielzii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Festuca porcii] tall grass communities
description: Mesophile tall grass community of the subalpine and upper montane levels of the Romanian and Ukrainian Carpathians dominated by [Festuca porcii], with [Calamagrostis villosa], [Festuca picta], [Knautia longifolia] and regional species such as [Campanula patula] ssp. [abietina], [Hypericum richeri] ssp. [grisebachii], [Achillea distans], [Festuca pratensis] ssp. [apennina], [Scorzonera purpurea] ssp. [rosea] ([Scorzonera rosea]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hairgrass tall grass communities
description: Communities of the upper montane and subalpine levels of the Sudeten, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides and, locally, of the Alps, dominated by [Deschampsia cespitosa], accompanied by a species cortŠge similar to that of the subalpine tall-herb communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Purple moorgrass tall grass communities
description: Communities of the subalpine or alpine level of the Sudeten, in particular, of the Giant Mountains (Krkonose, Karkonosze) and the Jesenik Mountains, dominated by [Molinia caerulea], accompanied by a species cortŠge comprising representatives of the [Betulo-Adenostyletea], the [Molinietalia], the [Phragmitetalia] and the [Caricetalia fuscae], in particular, [Deschampsia caespitosa] and [Phragmites australis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Iberian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of the Pyrenees, the Cantabrian mountains, the Cordillera Central, the Iberian Range, with [Valeriana pyrenaica] and [Adenostyles alliariae] ssp. [hybrida] ([Adenostyles alliariae] ssp. [pyrenaica]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-Mauritanian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of southern Iberian and North African mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Iberian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb communities of the Sierra Nevada and other southern Iberian mountains, with the endemic [Cirsium flavispina], [Aconitum nevadense], [Senecio elodes].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlas tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Atlas system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican [Cymbalaria] tall herb communities
description: Tall-herb communities of the subalpine and lower alpine level of Corsica, limited to shady, strongly sloping corridors with prolonged snow cover and often with stabilized scree, formed by [Adenostyles briquetii], [Valeriana rotundifolia], [Peucedanum ostruthium], [Cymbalaria hepaticifolia], [Ranunculus platanifolius], [Aquilegia bernardii], [Viola biflora], and often several fern species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican [Adenostyles] tall herb communities
description: Tall-herb communities of the subalpine and lower alpine level of Corsica, limited to shady, strongly sloping corridors with prolonged snow cover and often with stabilized scree, formed by [Adenostyles briquetii], [Valeriana rotundifolia], [Peucedanum ostruthium], [Cymbalaria hepaticifolia], [Ranunculus platanifolius], [Aquilegia bernardii], [Viola biflora], and often several fern species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican [Aconitum] tall herb communities
description: Tall-herb communities of the subalpine level of Corsica, limited to the Pianu di Cuscione, dominated by the endemic [Aconitum napellus] ssp. [corsicum], of extremely limited distribution.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican tall woodrush communities
description: Dense herbaceous communities of the subalpine level of Corsica, characteristic of strongly sloping corridors with prolonged snow cover, in somewhat less shady situations than those colonized by the communities of unit 37.851, formed by [Luzula sylvatica] var. [sieberi], [Polygonum alpinum], [Solidago virgaurea], [Cymbalaria hepaticifolia], [Ranunculus platanifolius], [Adenostyles briquetii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican [Doronicum] tall herb communities
description: Tall herb riparian communities of stony and rocky torrents and of dripping rocks of the upper montane, subalpine and alpine levels of Corsica formed by [Doronicum corsicum], [Narthecium reverchonii], [Carex frigida], [Calamagrostris varia] ssp. [corsica], [Phalaris arundinacea] var. [rotgesii] ([Typhoides arundinacea] ssp. [rotgesii]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern oro-Mediterranean and Balkan tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Balkan Range, the Hellenides and the mountains of Mediterranean Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic tall herb communities
description: Riparian and spring-edge vegetation of the montane and subalpine level of the Pindus and the Thessalian mountains south to Giona and Parnassus, with [Cirsium appendiculatum], [Cirsium tymphaeum], [Heracleum sphondylium] ssp. [pyrenaicum] ([Heracleum pollinianum]), [Stachys alopecuros] ([Betonica jacquinii]), [Scrophularia umbrosa] ([Scrophularia samaritanii]), [Scrophularia scopolii], [Achillea grandifolia], [Campanula trachelium] ssp. [athoa], [Chaerophyllum aureum], [Epilobium obscurum], [Solidago virgaurea], [Veratrum album], [Geranium asphodeloides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian tall herb communities
description: Montane meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of small splashing mountain torrents, moist hollows and gullies of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains and the Pelagonides, irradiating southwards, in the montane, sylvatic, level of the northern Pindus and the Pieria. The formations of these units harbour many species of the genus [Alchemilla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian Balkan thistle tall herb communities
description: [Cirsium appendiculatum] tall herb formations of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Pelagonides, irradiating southwards, in the montane, sylvatic, level of the northern Pindus and the Pieria. The communities of the Balkan Range and the Rhodopides harbour several species endemic or rare in the region, including [Alchemilla plicatula], [Trollius europaeus], [Pinguicula vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian butterbur tall herb communities
description: [Petasites albus] or [Petasites hybridus] tall herb formations of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Pelagonides, with [Epilobium montanum], [Alchemilla  spp.], [Carex spp.], [Geum coccineum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian hogweed tall herb communities
description: Tall herb communities of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Pelagonides dominated by [Heracleum sphondylium] ssp. [verticillatum], or [Heracleum sphondylium] ssp. [ternatum], extending south to the Moeso-Macedonian and Rhodopide mountains of northeastern Greece, in particular, to Belles, Athos, the Pangeon, the Falakron and the Rhodopi.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian scarlet avens tall herb communities
description: [Geum coccineum] formations of the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Pelagonides, south to the Varnous, Vernon, Vermion and Voras-Tzena groups.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Taurus tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Taurus system of Mediterranean Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine dock communities
description: Alpine and subalpine meso-hygrophile nitrophilous tall herb formations of the Alpine system and the higher Hercynian ranges, in particular, the Sudeten, the Black Forest, the Fichtelgebirge, the Dinarides, characteristic of the vicinity of cattle and game resting places, with [Rumex alpinus], [Senecio alpinus], [Cirsium spinosissimum], [Aconitum napellus], [Geranium phaeum], [Peucedanum ostruthium], [Urtica dioica], [Phleum alpinum] and, in eastern Carpathian communities, [Senecio subalpinus], [Leucanthemum waldsteinii], [Achillea distans], [Heracleum sphondylium] ssp. [transsilvanicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-boreal tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine mesohygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the boreal mountains and of the Scottish Highlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Roseroot-cranesbill-woodrush oroboreal communities
description: Generally species-rich communities of North Atlantic boreal mountains and uplands dominated by forbs of moderate stature, in particular, [Rhodiola rosea], [Alchemilla glabra], [Geranium sylvaticum], associated with [Angelica sylvestris], [Angelica archangelica], grasses, woodrushes or geophytes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British roseroot-woodrush communities
description: Species-rich tall-herb communities of the Scottish Highlands, the Hebrides, Orkney and Shetland, with outposts in the Moffat Hills, the Lake District and North Wales, formed by [Rhodiola rosea], [Alchemilla glabra], [Rubus saxatilis], [Geum rivale], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Angelica sylvestris], [Heracleum sphondylium], [Saussurea alpina], [Luzula sylvatica], [Festuca ovina], [Festuca vivipara], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], colonizing steep crags out of range of grazing, on moist base-rich soils in sheltered situations of cold wet mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Faeroes roseroot-woodrush communities
description: Luxuriant tall-herb communities of the Faeroe Islands rich in [Rhodiola rosea], [Alchemilla faeroensis], [Luzula sylvatica], [Angelica sylvestris] and [Geranium sylvaticum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic roseroot communities
description: Herb-rich upland communities of south-facing escarpments and moraine slopes of Iceland rich in, or dominated by [Rhodiola rosea], developed on relatively moist soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic cranesbill-angelica communities
description: Luxuriant tall-herb communities of Iceland dominated by [Angelica archangelica] and [Geranium sylvaticum] accompanied by [Angelica sylvestris], [Alchemilla vulgaris] [s.l.] ([Alchemilla acaulis]), [Filipendula ulmaria], [Hieracium spp.], [Taraxacum spp.], [Ranunculus acris], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Agrostis capillaris], [Leymus arenarius], [Hierochloe odorata], [Salix phylicifolia], often associated with bird colonies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal wood cranesbill communities
description: Communities of submontane areas of the Fennoscandian mountains and of Iceland dominated by [Geranium sylvaticum], with [Dactylorhiza fuchsii], [Carex atrata], [Carex vaginata], [Geum rivale], [Melampyrum pratense], [Melampyrum sylvatica], [Rubus saxatilis], [Succisa pratensis], [Trientalis europaea] and, in Iceland, [Dactylorhiza islandica], [Plathantera hyperborea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British [Luzula]-[Vaccinium] tall-herb communities
description: Relatively species-poor tall-herb communities of the Scottish Highlands, the Southern Uplands, the Inner Hebrides and Orkney, with outposts in the Lake District and the Cheviots, formed by [Luzula sylvatica], usually abundant and sometimes overwhelmingly dominant, accompanied by [Vaccinium myrtillus] and other subshrubs, sometimes constituting a dominated layer, and by [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Galium saxatile], [Oxalis acetosella], [Blechnum spicant], sometimes [Dryopteris dilatata] and other ferns, [Cicerbita alpina], [Anthoxanthum odoratum] or [Festuca ovina], colonizing inaccessible rocky formations and slopes, on relatively moist base-poor substrates with humic soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal tall forb communities
description: Communities of the mountains of the boreal and subarctic zones of the Eurasian continent dominated by tall dicotyledonous herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian tall forb communities
description: Communities of the boreal and arctoalpine Fennoscandian mountains dominated by tall dicotyledonous herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian sow-thistle communities
description: Tall herb-dominated communities of Scandinavian mountains dominated by [Cicerbita alpina], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Cirsium helenioides] with [Aconitum septentrionale], [Angelica archangelica], [Ranunculus platanifolia], [Saussurea alpina], [Rumex acetosa], [Trollius europaeus], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Calamagrostis purpurea], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Poa alpina], [Equisetum arvense], [Equisetum pratense], [Athyrium filix-femina], [Matteuccia struthiopteris], [Rubus saxatilis], [Salix spp.]; they colonize slopes and steep hillsides at subalpine and lower alpine levels.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian globe flower communities
description: Species-rich, multitiered [Trollius europaeus]-dominated communities of lower alpine levels of Scandinavian mountains, colonizing lime and nutrient-rich soils with flowing subsurface water, often situated below snow fields. The species cortŠge includes [Trollius europaeus], [Viola biflora], [Polygonum bistorta], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Astragalus alpina], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Parnassia palustris], [Ranunculus acris], [Potentilla crantzii], [Saussurea alpina], [Solidago virgaurea], [Taraxacum croceum], [Poa alpigena], [Poa alpina], [Festuca vivipara], [Festuca rubra], [Carex bigelowii], [Thalictrum alpinum], [Selaginella selaginoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Urals and neighbouring boreal ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Siberian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the boreal mountains of northern Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal tall grass and fern communities
description: Communities of the montane and subalpine levels of mountains of the boreal and subarctic zones of the northern Eurasian continent, dominated by tall grasses of genera [Calamagrostis], [Deschampsia], [Festuca] accompanied by ferns and a dicot species cortŠge similar to that of the oroboreal tall-herb communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian small-reed communities
description: Chionophilous tall-herb communities of boreal and arctoalpine mountains of Fennoscandia dominated by [Calamagrostis purpurea], characteristic of screes with prolonged snow cover, related to the fern communities of unit 36.1125.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian tall grass communities
description: Communities of the montane and subalpine levels of the Urals dominated by tall grasses of genera [Calamagrostis], [Deschampsia], [Anthoxanthum] accompanied by ferns and a dicot species cortŠge similar to that of the Uralian tall-herb communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Siberian tall grass communities
description: Communities of the montane and subalpine levels of the boreal mountains of northern Siberia dominated by tall grasses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subboreal fern-tall grass communities
description: Communities of the mountains and uplands of nemoral and boreonemoral zones of the northern Eurasian continent, dominated by ferns or tall grasses, notably, local communities of the western and northern uplands of Great Britain, particularly common in cooler oceanic regions, formed by [Thelypteris limbosperma] and [Blechnum spicant].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caucasian tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine mesohygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Pontic Range, of the Caucasus, of the Crimean mountains and of the Elburz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Himalayan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Altaic tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Altai, of the Sayan and of other southern Siberian and eastern Asian boreal mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern subalpine tall herb communities
description: Subalpine and alpine meso-hygrophile tall herb formations of moist hollows and gullies of the Sino-Japanese mountains of eastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern giant herb communities
description: Luxuriant, dense stands of very tall herbs growing under oceanic climates with evenly distributed moderate to high precipitation and stable frost-protecting snowcover, of Kamchatka, the Kuriles, Sakhalin, Honshu, northern Hokkaido and coastal Amurland, extending from sea-level to 1000 m in Kamchatka and Sakhalin, to 2000 m on Hokkaido, to 2500 m on Honshu. They represent a relict form of vegetation entirely restricted to Pacific northeastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Filipendula camtschatica] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Filipendula camtschatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Angelica ursina] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Angelica ursina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Anthriscus sylvestris] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Anthriscus sylvestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Petasites amplus] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Petasites amplus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Senecio cannabifolius] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Senecio cannabilifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Heracleum lanatum] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Heracleum lanatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cacalia kamtschatica] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Cacalia kamtschatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Polygonum weyrichii] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Polygonum weyrichii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Reynoutria sachalinensis] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Reynoutria sachalinensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Urtica platyphylla] stands
description: Far-eastern giant herb communities dominated by [Urtica platyphylla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesophile grasslands
description: Lowland and montane mesophile pastures and hay meadows of the boreal, nemoral, warm-temperate humid, Irano-Turanian and mediterranean zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesophile pastures
description: Regularly grazed mesophile pastures of Europe, fertilized and on well-drained soils, with [Lolium perenne], [Cynosurus cristatus], [Poa spp.], [Festuca spp.], [Trifolium repens], [Leontodon autumnalis], [Bellis perennis], [Ranunculus repens], [Ranunculus acris], [Cardamine pratensis]; they are most characteristic of the Euro-Siberian zone, but extend to Atlantic Iberia and the Cordillera Central, the Apennines and the supra-Mediterranean zone of the Balkan peninsula and Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Unbroken pastures
description: Continuous pastureland of Euro-Siberian Europe, Atlantic Iberia and the Cordillera Central, the Apennines and the supra-Mediterranean zone of the Balkan peninsula and Greece, unrelieved by networks of ditches.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ryegrass pastures
description: Relatively species-poor grasslands of Euro-Siberian Western and Central Europe, Atlantic Iberia and the Cordillera Central, the Apennines and the supra-Mediterranean zone of the Balkan peninsula and Greece dominated by [Lolium perenne], often with [Cynosurus cristatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Cynosurus]-[Centaurea] pastures
description: More species-rich grasslands of the British Isles dominated by [Cynosurus cristatus] and with many flowering herbs, notably [Centaurea nigra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic hill pastures
description: Pastures mostly of uplands of Western Europe, Central Europe and Eastern Europe, less treated, rougher and more species-rich than those of unit 38.111, often with the cespitose [Festuca nigrescens] and a significant representation of nitrofuge species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental pastures
description: Pastures of Eastern Europe, in the southern part of the Russian forest zone, Bashkiria and the southern Urals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ditch-broken pastures
description: Grasslands drained by a network of ditches, fleets, streams or pools.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Overgrown pastures
description: Abandoned grasslands with ruderal species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lowland and collinar hay meadows
description: Mesophile hay meadows of low altitudes of Europe, fertilized and well-drained, with [Arrhenatherum elatius], [Trisetum flavescens], [Anthriscus sylvestris], [Heracleum sphondylium], [Daucus carota], [Crepis biennis], [Knautia arvensis], [Leucanthemum vulgare], [Pimpinella major], [Trifolium dubium], [Geranium pratense]; they are most characteristic of the Euro-Siberian zone, but extend to Atlantic Iberia, the Cordillera Central and Montseny, to the Apennines and to the supramediterranean zone of Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic hay meadows
description: Lowland mesophile hay meadows of the Atlantic domaine of Europe, characteristic of the British Isles and western France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Arrhenatherum] grasslands
description: Lowland mesophile hay meadows of the British Isles and western France rich in, or dominated by [Arrhenatherum elatius] accompanied by [Dactylis glomerata] and [Holcus lanatus] with [Centaurea debeauxii] ssp. [nemoralis] ([Centaurea nigra], [Centaurea nemoralis]), [Rhinanthus lanceolatus], [Oenanthe pimpinelloides], [Gaudinia fragilis], [Linum bienne], [Brachypodium pinnatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Alopecurus]-[Sanguisorba] grasslands
description: Lowland mesophile hay meadows of England, characteristic of areas where traditional hay meadow treatment has been applied to seasonally flooded alluvial soils, formed by [Alopecurus pratensis], [Festuca rubra], [Cynosurus cristatus], [Lolium perenne], with less abundant or less constant [Holcus lanatus], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Dactylis glomerata], [Trisetum flavescens], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Bromus hordeaceus], [Arrhenatherum elatius], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Festuca arundinacea], with many dicots, among which [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Leontodon spp.], [Taraxacum spp.] are often abundant and [Fritillaria meleagris] particularly noteworthy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic lowland hay meadows
description: Mesophile lowland hay meadows of sub-Atlantic Western Europe, of western and northern Central Europe, of the humid Illyrian region and of the eastern Carpathian system, with [Arrhenatherum elatius], [Daucus carota], [Crepis biennis], [Knautia arvensis], [Leucanthemum vulgare], [Pimpinella major], [Trifolium dubium], [Geranium pratense], [Alchemilla xanthochlora], [Campanula patula], [Pastinaca sativa], [Galium album], [Equisetum arvense], [Medicago sativa], [Picris hieracioides], [Sanguisorba officinalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Xeromesophile medio-European lowland hay meadows
description: Drier, more thermophile, swards of the lowland sub-Atlandic mesophile hay meadows of Western Europe and Central Europe, dominated by [Arrhenatherum elatius], and with a species composition that includes [Festuco-Brometea] dry grassland species, in particular, [Salvia pratensis], [Bromus erectus], [Ranunculus bulbosus], [Dianthus carthusianorum], [Pimpinella saxifraga], [Plantago media], [Galium verum], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Linum catharticum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hygromesophile medio-European lowland hay meadows
description: More humid, or temporarily more humid, swards of the lowland sub-Atlandic mesophile hay meadows of Western Europe and Central Europe, dominated by [Arrhenatherum elatius] and [Alopecurus pratensis], or by the latter alone, and with a species composition intermediate between that of mesophile and humid meadows (37) with [Cirsium oleraceum], [Angelica sylvestris], [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Ranunculus repens], [Myosotis palustris], [Glechoma hederacea], [Lychnis flos-cuculi], [Ajuga reptans], [Cardamine pratensis], [Lysimachia nummularia], [Geranium pratense], [Campanula patula], [Pastinaca sativa], [Heracleum sphondylium], [Anthriscus sylvestris]. Towards the east, in more continental climates, the [Alopecurus] meadows communities increasingly take the character of humid riverine meadows; they have been included in 37 from the Pannonic region eastwards, in the range of the mesophile meadows of 38.5.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Medio-European submontane hay meadows
description: Mesophile grasslands of middle European Hercynian hills, of the middle elevations of the greater Hercynian ranges, the Jura, the pre-Alps, the Dinarides, the Pelagonides, the Carpathians, the Pyrenees, the mountains of the northwestern Iberian peninsula, intermediate between the lowland meadows of unit 38.22 and the montane meadows of unit 38.3.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Hercynian submontane hay meadows
description: Hay meadows of higher elevations of the lesser Hercynian ranges, with [Meum athamanticum], [Festuca nigrescens], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Lathyrus montanus], [Phyteuma spicatum], [Potentilla erecta], [Galium saxatile], [Ranunculus bulbosus], [Pimpinella saxifraga], [Lotus uliginosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Hercynio-Baltic submontane hay meadows
description: Hay meadows of mid-elevations of the great Hercynian ranges of Central Europe and of the hills of the eastern Germano-Baltic Plain, in particular, of the Baltic States.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Hercynian submontane hay meadows
description: Hay meadows of mid-elevations of the great Hercynian ranges of Central Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic submontane acidocline hay meadows
description: Hay meadows of siliceous substrates of the hills of the eastern Germano-Baltic Plain, in particular, of the Baltic States.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic submontane calcicline hay meadows
description: Hay meadows of calcareous substrates of the hills of the Baltic States.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian submontane hay meadows
description: Hay meadows of the submontane level of the Carpathians, at about 600-700 m.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Carpathian gladiolus meadows
description: Endemic community of the western Carpathians, with [Alchemilla walasii], [Alchemilla micans], [Alchemilla pastoralis], [Centaurea oxylepis], [Gladiolus imbricatus], [Viola saxatilis] var. [decorata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Carpathian vetch-clover meadows
description: Species-rich hay meadows of the Pienini and the Beskides, limited to thermophilous stations on deep calcareous soils, with [Medicago falcata], [Polygala comosa], [Thymus pulegioides], [Salvia verticillata], [Ranunculus polyanthemos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian yellow oatgrass meadows
description: Submontane mesophile meadows of the Romanian Carpathians, developed on nutrient-rich acid brown soils, dominated by [Trisetum flavescens], accompanied by [Arrhenatherum elatius] and a species cortŠge characteristic of the [Arrhenatherion], including [Campanula patula], [Trifolium repens], [Leucanthemum vulgare], [Lotus corniculatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Iberian submontane hay meadows
description: Mesophile hay meadows of sub-Atlantic northern Spain, in particular, of the beech level of the oro-Cantabrian region, with [Arrhenatherum elatius] ssp. [bulbosum], [Trisetum flavescens], [Sanguisorba minor], [Malva moschata], [Knautia arvensis], [Pimpinella major], [Trifolium repens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic submontane hay meadows
description: Submontane mesophile hay meadows of the pre-Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Jurassian submontane hay meadows
description: Submontane mesophile hay meadows of the Jura.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian submontane hay meadows
description: Submontane mesophile hay meadows of the beech level of the Dinarides, within the range of the [Fagion illyricum], dominated by [Trisetum flavescens], with [Poa pratensis], [Arrhenatherum elatius], [Festuca pratensis], [Alchemilla xanthochlora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Moesian submontane hay meadows
description: Submontane mesophile hay meadows of the beech level of the Pelagonides, within the range of the [Fagion moesiacum], dominated by [Trisetum flavescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal and subboreal meadows
description: Herb-rich meadows of boreal affinities of the boreal and boreonemoral regions of the Palaearctic, with outposts in cool humid uplands of the northern nemoral zone, in particular, in the British Isles.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fenno-Scandian boreal and subboreal meadows
description: Herb-rich meadows of boreal affinities of Fennoscandia, distributed in the boreonemoral, southern boreal, middle boreal, northern boreal, boreoalpine and oceanic southern boreal zones of Finland, Sweden and Norway, formed by [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Festuca ovina], [Briza media], with, as dominant dicots, [Geranium sylvaticum], [Alchemilla spp.], [Rhinanthus minor], [Anemone nemorosa] and a cortŠge that includes boreal elements such as [Polygonum viviparum], [Rubus arcticus], boreonemoral species, in particular, [Hypochoeris maculata], [Veronica chamaedrys], as well as [Cirsium helenioides], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Potentilla erecta], [Ranunculus auricomus], [Trollius europaeus], [Hepatica nobilis], [Dactylorhiza maculata], [Dactylorhiza fuchsii], [Listera ovata], [Platanthera chlorantha].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic submontane meadows
description: Mesophile hay meadows of submontane areas of northern England, with affinities to both the Fennoscandian boreal meadows of unit 38.241 and to the submontane continental Western European meadows of unit 38.23.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Anthoxanthum]-[Geranium] grasslands
description: Upland mesophile hay meadows of northern England, essentially restricted to Teesdale and Weardale in Durham, Swaledale and Wensleydale in North Yorkshire,  and to the Lake District, with outposts along the Tay in Scotland, formed by a mixture of grasses, including [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Dactylus glomerata], [Festuca rubra], [Holcus lanatus], [Agrostis capillaris], [Poa trivialis], with [Geranium sylvaticum] abundant and sometimes dominant, [Sanguisorba officinalis], [Alchemilla glabra], [Alchemilla xanthochlora] and a number of rarer species of genus [Alchemilla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Filipendula]-[Arrhenatherum] grasslands
description: Tall mesophile hay meadows of northern England, limited to the Carboniferous Limestone of Derbyshire and Craven, with an isolated occurrence in the Cheviots, dominated by large tussocks of [Arrhenatherum elatius] and [Festuca rubra], accompanied by tall hemicryptophyte dicotyledons, in particular, [Filipendula ulmaria], [Heracleum sphondylium], [Valeriana officinalis], [Angelica sylvestris] and, in some communities, [Polemonium caeruleum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental meadows
description: Lowland and collinar mesophile grasslands of the Pannonic basin, the Transylvanian basin, the lower Danubian plain, the Thracian plain and their fringing foothills, of Eastern Europe and of southern Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Pannonic mesophile hay meadows
description: Lowland and collinar mesophile grasslands of the Pannonic basin, the Transylvanian basin, the lower Danubian plain, the Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain and their fringing foothills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Thracian mesophile hay meadows
description: Lowland, collinar and, locally, montane, mesophile grasslands of the northern Thracian plain and its fringing foothills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Thracian mesophile floodplain meadows
description: Mesophile floodplain hay meadows of the northern Thracian plain and its fringing foothills, on soils moistened by a high water table fed by riverine inundation, situated on higher ground than riverine meadows of unit 37, dominated by similar grass species, including [Poa pratensis], [Alopecurus pratensis]; [Alopecurus rendlei] ([Alopecurus utriculatus]), [Festuca pratensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Thracian mesophile foothill meadows
description: Mesophile hay meadows of the valleys and lower slopes of mountain ranges fringing the northern Thracian plain and its peripheral basins installed on soils moistened by underground or surface water supplied by slope runoff, dominated by the same grass species as in the floodplain meadows of 38.2521, accompanied by [Arrhenatherum elatius] and [Agrostis capillaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Thracian mesophile cold water meadows
description: Species-rich mesophile hay meadows of the lower slopes and foot of the southern flank of the Balkan Range, developed on calcareous substrates and with a supply of cold surface and ground water originating in the upper levels of the mountain, dominated by [Poa pratensis], [Alopecurus pratensis], [Alopecurus rendlei] ([Alopecurus utriculatus]), [Festuca pratensis] and with  orchids, [Clematis integrifolia], [Cladium mariscus], [Merendera sobolifera], [Galium rubioides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic mesophile hay meadows
description: Lowland and collinar mesophile grasslands of the Sarmatic region of Eastern Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South Siberian mesophile hay meadows
description: Lowland and collinar mesophile meadows of southern Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Balkanic mesophile meadows
description: Mesophile [Poa bulbosa]-meadows of well-drained, relatively fertile, mineral soils of submediterranean regions of the southwestern Balkan peninsula, recorded, in particular, from the lower altitudes of Albania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain hay meadows
description: Often species-rich hay meadows of the montane and subalpine levels of higher mountains of the western Palaearctic deciduous forest zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpic mountain hay meadows
description: Species-rich mesophile hay meadows of the montane and subalpine levels (mostly above 600 metres) of the Western Alpides and the greater Hercynian ranges, usually dominated by [Trisetum flavescens] and with [Heracleum sphondylium], [Viola cornuta], [Astrantia major], [Carum carvi], [Crepis mollis], [Crepis pyrenaica], [Polygonum bistorta], [Silene dioica], [Silene vulgaris], [Campanula glomerata], [Salvia pratensis], [Centaurea nemoralis], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Crocus albiflorus], [Geranium phaeum], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Narcissus poeticus], [Malva moschata], [Valeriana repens], [Trollius europaeus], [Pimpinella major], [Muscari botryoides], [Lilium bulbiferum], [Thlaspi caerulescens], [Viola tricolor] ssp. [subalpina], [Phyteuma halleri], [Phyteuma orbiculare], [Primula elatior], [Chaerophyllum hirsutum] and many others.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caucasian hay meadows
description: Meadows of the montane and subalpine levels of the Caucasus and the Pontic mountains of northern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian vallicares
description: Summer pastures of the Iberian peninsula, submitted to poor drainage, brief flooding and rapid dessication with the first heat, constituted by perennial and annual grasses, most commonly by [Agrostis castellana], [Agrostis pourretii] ([Agrostis salmantica]), [Gaudinia fragilis], [Festuca ampla], [Periballia involucrata], [Vulpia ciliata], [Vulpia myuros], [Vulpia bromoides], [Holcus setiglumis], [Molineriella minuta], [Anthoxanthum aristatum], [Anthoxanthum ovatum] and often with [Juncus capitatus] and clovers such as [Trifolium campestre].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Perennial vallicares
description: Perennial [Agrostis castellana]-dominated grasslands of the Iberian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Annual vallicares
description: Annual [Agrostis pourretii]-dominated grasslands of the Iberian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Andalusian thrift vallicares
description: Forb and grass communities of oligo-mesotrophic sandy soils of southwestern Iberia, with subsurface seasonal water saturation, in particular, of the edges of marshes and large lagoons, dominated by the endemic [Armeria gaditana], with [Gaudinia fragilis], [Centaurea exarata] and [Asphodelus aestivus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian mesophile grasslands
description: Secondary grasslands of the highest levels of the Atlantic islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Steppe meadows
description: Lowland and montane mesophile pastures and hay meadows of the steppe zone of central Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern meadows
description: Lowland and montane mesophile pastures and hay meadows of the boreal, nemoral and warm-temperate humid zones of the eastern Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tundra
description: Communities of grasses and shrubs developed over permafrost. They are limited to Greenland, Spitzbergen and northern Russia. Communities sometimes composed of the same species in oroboreal areas remote from the main permafrost region, such as those of continental Fennoscandia and Iceland are listed under units 36 and 31.4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shrub tundra
description: Tundras of the southernmost tundra belt of Eurasia, characterized by an abundance of medium small and small shrubs, including 1-2 m tall [Alnus fruticosa], 0.5-0.8 m tall [Salix lanata], [Betula nana], [Betula exilis], [Salix reptans], [Salix pulchra], and of dwarf shrubs, in particular, [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Ledum decumbens], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Empetrum nigrum], [Arctostaphylos alpina]. They extend south to the wooded tundra belt.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western shrub tundra
description: Southern tundras of Europe, comprising Kola tundras in the west, the southern part of the Eastern European tundras from the Kanin peninsula to the Ural piedmont, and the southern part of the Uralo-Va‹katchan tundras.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Siberian shrub tundra
description: Southern tundras of western Siberia, constituting the southern part of the Yamalo-west Taimyrian tundras extending from the lower Obi and the base of the Yamal peninsula to the central Taimyr peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern shrub tundra
description: Southern tundras of central eastern Siberia, from the Khatanga to the Kolyma, in which [Betula nana] is replaced by [Betula exilis], and the more maritime tundras of the Chukchotski peninsula, of Alaskan affinities, with the tussock-forming [Carex lugens], the shrub [Betula kajanderi], [Betula glandulosa], and relict arctic glacial steppes with [Carex duriuscula], [Helictotrichon krylovii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moss and lichen tundra
description: Tundras of the middle tundra belt of Eurasia, characterized by a thick cover of mosses, formed notably by [Hypnum splendens], [Aulacomnium turgidum], [Tomenthypnum nitens], [Ptilium ciliare], with dwarf shrubs, particularly [Dryas punctata], [Cassiope tetragona], [Salix reptans], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], sedges, among which the often dominant [Carex ensifolia]. Drier stands alternate in mosa‹c fashion with wetter areas dominated by sedges, in particular, [Carex stans], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Eriophorum scheuchzeri], and grasses, notably [Arctophila fulva], [Dupontia fischeri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cladonia]-espalier willow tundra
description: Moss and lichen tundras of the northern Kanin peninsula, Kolguiev island, the northeastern European Petchora tundras, the Kara sea tundras, the southern Yamal peninsula, the southern Gyda peninsula, the southern Ta‹myr peninsula,  in the Ienissei and Piasana basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moss tundra
description: Moss and lichen tundras of the middle Ta‹myr peninsula, on the southern flanks of the Byrranga Range, and in the Ta‹myr basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Yakutian [Alectoria] tundra
description: Moss and lichen tundras of the near-coastal hinterland of the Khatanga-Anabar-Olenek basins and of the Lena-Iana-Indighirka-Kolyma basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cetraria]-[Eriophorum]-[Ledum] tundra
description: Moss and lichen tundras of eastern Anadyrland and the Tchouktchi peninsula south to the shores of the Gulf of Anadyr.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Cetraria]-[Dryas] tundra
description: Moss and lichen tundras of the southeastern Ta‹myr peninsula, in the Khatanga basin and of the middle Anabar basin, south of the Laptev Sea and north of the Siberian plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic tundra
description: Tundras of the northern tundra belt of Eurasia, forming the transition to the polar deserts, with sparser, very open, vegetation formed in particular by [Salix polaris], [Alopecurus alpinus], [Luzula nivalis], [Luzula confusa], [Cerastium bialynickii], [Saxifraga hirculus], [Saxifraga platysepala], [Saxifraga caespitosa], [Saxifraga serpyllifolia], [Novosieversia glacialis], moss carpets along brooks, mosses and lichens on stony ground, small forbs, [Cerastium regelii], [Stellaria edwardsii], [Papaver spp.], on pebbly lake shores and [Puccinellia phryganodes] mats around salty lagoons.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic [Dryas] tundra
description: Tundras of the northern belt of tundras of the Sea of Laptev, mainly located between the Khatanga and the Olenek and in the Lena delta.
