source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian inland calciphile beech forests
description: Thermophilous Illyrian [Fagus sylvatica] forests of inland areas of the Dinarides and of associated ranges and hills, of the southeastern pre-Alps and  the mid-Pannonic hills, characterized by the presence of [Ostryo-Carpinion orientalis] or [Fraxino orni-Ostryion] species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian hop-hornbeam beech forests
description: Thermophilous Illyrian [Fagus sylvatica] forests of limestones and dolomites of the pre-Dinaric hills of Slovenia and of the southeastern pre-Alpine hills of Slovenia and Carinthia, with [Ostrya carpinifolia], [Fraxinus ornus], [Sorbus aria], [Sorbus torminalis] and a species-rich herb-layer comprising numerous [Quercetalia pubescentis] characteristics.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Helleborus odorus] beech forests
description: Thermophilous Illyrian [Fagus sylvatica] forests of the northern Dinarides and pre-Dinarides and of the southern mid-Pannonic or sub-Pannonic hills, north to the Hungarian Mecsec and Tolna hills, with [Tilia tomentosa], [Fraxinus ornus] and [Carpinus betulus] in the canopy, [Helleborus odorus], [Tamus communis], [Chaerophyllum aureum], [Ruscus hypoglossum], [Ruscus aculeatus], [Potentilla micrantha] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian [Acer obtusatum] beech forests
description: Thermophilous [Fagus sylvatica] forests of inland areas of the central Dinarides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian subalpine beech forests
description: Local [Fagus sylvatica] forests of the tree-limit in the upper montane or subalpine level of the high Dinarides, with extremely limited outliers in the southeastern Alps, not forming a clear belt, contrary to more western formations of the [Aceri-Fagion], though, like them, characterized by the frequent admixture of [Acer pseudoplatanus] in the canopy and of [Adenostyletalia] megaphorb species in the understorey. [Acer heldreichii], [Sorbus chamaemespilus], [Salix appendiculata], [Myrrhis odorata], [Cicerbita alpina], [Aconitum paniculatum], [Chaerophyllum hirsutum], [Petasites albus], [Stellaria nemorum] are noteworthy accompaniers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian beech forests
description: [Fagus sylvatica], or, locally, [Fagus orientalis], [Fagus moesiaca], [Fagus taurica], forests of the Romanian, Ukrainian and eastern Serbian Carpathians, east of the Uz and the Stry, and of the west Ukrainian pre-Carpathic hills and plateaux. Characteristic species include [Symphytum cordatum], [Cardamine glanduligera] ([Dentaria glandulosa]), [Hepatica transsilvanica], [Pulmonaria rubra], [Leucanthemum waldsteinii], [Silene heuffelii], [Ranunculus carpaticus], [Euphorbia carniolica], [Aconitum moldavicum], [Saxifraga rotundifolia] ssp. [heuffelii], [Primula elatior] ssp. [leucophylla], [Hieracium rotundatum], [Galium kitaibelianum], [Moehringia pendula], [Festuca drymeja].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian acidophile beech forests
description: [Fagus sylvatica] forests of the eastern Carpathians and pre-Carpathian hills, developed on acid soils, in particular podzols and brown acid soils, mostly limited to rather small surfaces within the more extensive neutrophilous forest complexes, characterized by a species-poor acidophilous flora that includes [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Hieracium rotundatum], [Calamagrostis hirundinacea], [Luzula luzuloides], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Galium rotundifolium], [Galium kitaibelianum], [Galium baillonii], [Veronica officinalis], [Blechnum spicant], [Pteridium aquilinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian woodrush-beech forests
description: Widely distributed acidophilous [Fagus sylvatica] forests of the eastern and southern Carpathians, accompanied by a cortŠge in which the acidophile species characteristic of the [Calamagrostio-Fagenion] clearly predominate over the edaphically less restricted species of the [Symphyto-Fagion]; [Luzula luzuloides], [Hieracium rotundatum], [Calamagrostis arundinacea], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Veronica officinalis], in particular, are often abundant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Galium kitaibelianum] beech forests
description: Acidophilous [Fagus sylvatica] forests of the central zone of the southern Romanian Carpathians, limited to small surfaces, characterized by the presence of thermophilous species such as [Galium kitaibelianum], [Galium baillonii] and [Potentilla micrantha].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Galium rotundifolium] beech forests
description: Acidophilous [Fagus sylvatica] forests, mostly of high mountains in the southwestern Carpathians, with [Galium rotundifolium] and an admixture of acidophilous and neutrophilous [Fagetalia] species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian neutrophile beech forests
description: [Fagus sylvatica], [Fagus sylvatica]-[Abies alba], [Fagus sylvatica]-[Abies alba]-[Picea abies] and [Fagus sylvatica]-[Carpinus betula] forests of the Romanian, Ukrainian and eastern Serbian Carpathians and pre-Carpathian hills, with typical [Fagetalia] species, developed on neutral, basicline and sometimes acidocline substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Symphytum] beech forests
description: [Fagus sylvatica], [Fagus sylvatica-Abies alba] and [Fagus sylvatica]-[Abies alba]-[Picea abies] forests of the Romanian, Ukrainian and eastern Serbian Carpathians and pre-Carpathian hills accompanied by a cortŠge of typical [Fagetalia] species supplemented by regional Dacian elements, including [Symphytum cordatum], [Cardamine glanduligera] ([Dentaria glandulosa]), [Ranunculus carpaticus], [Pulmonaria rubra], [Aconitum moldavicum], [Hepatica transsilvanica], [Silene heuffelii], [Ranunculus carpaticus], [Euphorbia carniolica], [Crocus heuffelianus], [Aremonia agrimonoides], [Festuca drymeja], widely distributed in all mountains and high hills of the region on neutral, basicline and sometimes acidocline substrates. [Fagus orientalis] and [Fagus taurica] may locally enter the canopy in sub-Carpathic ranges of Moldavia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Dentaria glandulosa] beech forests
description: Neutrophile [Fagus sylvatica] forests, sometimes with a small admixture of [Acer pseudoplatanus], [Picea abies] and [Abies alba], with a rich [Fagetalia] flora and regionally characteristic Dacian species including [Symphytum cordatum], [Cardamine glanduligera] ([Dentaria glandulosa]), [Pulmonaria rubra], [Hepatica transsilvanica], [Ranunculus carpaticus], widespread on rich soils throughout the Romanian and Ukrainian Carpathians, where they form the zonal forests of the lower and middle montane belt, between 600 and 1100 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Pulmonaria rubra] fir-beech forests
description: Neutrophile [Fagus sylvatica-Abies alba] forests with a rich [Fagetalia] flora and Dacian regional species such as [Pulmonaria rubra], [Cardamine glanduligera] ([Dentaria glandulosa]), [Symphytum cordatum], [Hepatica transsilvanica], [Ranunculus carpaticus], [Campanula abietina], widely distributed throughout the Romanian and Ukrainian Carpathians, on rich brown, leached or acid soils of steep slopes at altitudes comprised between 700 and 1300 m.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Leucanthemum] beech forests
description: Acidocline [Fagus sylvatica]-[Picea abies] forests of the high southeastern Carpathians, occupying the upper fringe of the montane beech forests, at altitudes between 800 and 1350 metres, on acid brown soils, with [Leucanthemum waldsteinii] and a cortŠge otherwise typical of the [Symphyto-Fagenion], including [Oxalis acetosella], [Symphytum cordatum], [Pulmonaria rubra], [Cardamine glanduligera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian hairy sedge beech-hornbeam forests
description: Forests of [Fagus sylvatica], or sometimes [Fagus moesiaca] and [Carpinus betulus], occasionally of [Fagus sylvatica] without [Carpinus betulus], of the montane level of the Romanian, Ukrainian and eastern Serbian Carpathians and pre-Carpathian hills, accompanied by an eastern [Carpinion] cortŠge that includes [Tilia cordata], [Prunus avium], [Lathyrus hallersteinii], [Melampyrum bihariense], [Aposeris foetida], [Stellaria holostea], [Ranunculus auricomus], [Galium schultesii], [Carex pilosa], [Dactylis glomerata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Galium schultesii] beech-hornbeam forests
description: Neutrophile forests of [Fagus sylvatica], or sometimes [Fagus moesiaca], and [Carpinus betulus], often with an admixture of [Quercus petraea], or, in more thermophile variants, [Quercus cerris], widely distributed in the lower montane belt of the Romanian and Ukrainian Carpathians and high pre-Carpathian hills, mostly above 500-600 metres, with a typical [Lathyro-Carpinion] cortŠge formed by, in particular, [Galium schultesii], [Carex pilosa], [Melampyrum bihariense], [Aposeris foetida], [Stellaria holostea], [Ranunculus auricomus], accompanied by Dacian elements such as [Cardamine glanduligera] ([Dentaria glandulosa]), [Symphytum cordatum], [Helleborus purpurascens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Lathyrus hallersteinii] beech-hornbeam forests
description: Neutrophile [Fagus sylvatica]-[Carpinus betulus] beech forests with [Lathyrus hallersteinii] in the herb layer, of limited distribution in the southern Apuseni Mountains and the Petrosani Depression.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian orchid beech-horhbeam forests
description: Orchid-rich [Fagus sylvatica-Carpinus betulus] forests developed on calcareous substrates with rendzina-type soils of the montane belt of the Romanian Carpathians and pre-Carpathian hills, Dacian vicariant of the northern and central Central European [Carici-Fagetum], with [Cephalanthera rubra], [Cephalanthera damasonium], [Epipactis microphylla], [Epipactis helleborine], [Helleborus purpurascens], [Daphne mezereum], [Cardamine bulbifera], [Hepatica nobilis], [Mycelis muralis], [Salvia glutinosa], [Campanula rapunculoides], [Melica nutans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Dentaria bulbifera] beech forests
description: Neutrophile [Fagus sylvatica] forests of high pre-Carpathian hills, with a distinct medio-European character and an impoverished Dacian floral element, somewhat transitional between more western communities of the [Fagion medio-Europaeum] and the Dacian [Lathyro-Carpinion] and [Symphyto-Fagion], an intermediate position illustrated by the prevalence of [Cardamine bulbifera] ([Dentaria bulbifera]) and [Carex pilosa] combined with the absence of [Carpinus betulus] and of Dacian montane elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian sub-alpine beech forests
description: Local [Fagus sylvatica] and [Fagus sylvatica]-[Picea abies] forests of the tree-limit in the upper montane or subalpine level of the high southern Carpathians, developed where subalpine [Picea abies] forests do not form an uninterrupted zone, less well individualized than more western formations of the [Aceri-Fagion], though, like them, characterized by the admixture of [Acer pseudoplatanus] in the canopy and of [Adenostyletalia] megaphorb species in the understorey.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian subalpine beech-spruce forest
description: Neutrophile to weakly acidophile [Fagus sylvatica-Picea abies] forests with a mixed cortŠge composed of [Fagetalia]  species, in particular [Symphyto-Fagion] characteristics, and of [Vaccinio-Piceetalia] and [Adenostyletalia] species, of the subalpine or upper montane level of high mountains of the southern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian subalpine gooseberry beech forests
description: [Fagus sylvatica] forests with [Acer pseudoplatanus] characterized by the presence of [Ribes uva-crispa], [Glechoma hirsuta], [Lamium maculatum] and [Ulmus glabra], on very damp slopes of the subalpine or upper montane level of  the southern and southwestern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian calciphile beech forests
description: [Fagus sylvatica] forests developed on limestones of the eastern and southern Carpathians and pre-Carpathian hills, harbouring a strongly calciphile and thermophile cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Epipactis] beech forests
description: Calcicolous [Fagus sylvatica] forests of mountains and high hills in the western part of the southern Carpathians and in the Apuseni mountains, developed on rendzinas, over limestone substrates, with an abundant representation of the calcicline segment of the [Fagetalia] cortŠge, in particular, [Mercurialis perennis], [Sanicula europaea], [Actaea spicata], accompanied by thermophile species such as [Fraxinus ornus] and [Aristolochia pallida], and by numerous orchids, among which [Epipactis helleborine], [Epipactis microphylla], [Cephalanthera rubra], [Cephalanthera damasonium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian [Sesleria] beech forests
description: Xero-mesophile, neutrophile to basiphile [Fagus sylvatica] woods developed on  rendzina soils over limestone rocks in low mountains of the western and southern Romanian Carpathians, characterized by the dominance of [Sesleria rigida] in the field layer, accompanied by calciphile herbs, notably [Epipactis atrorubens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South Carpathian thermophilous beech forests
description: [Fagus sylvatica] or [Fagus moesiaca] forests of the southwestern and southern Carpathians and pre-Carpathian hills, with southern European floristic elements, including [Aremonia agrimonoides], [Festuca drymeja], [Helleborus odorus], [Tilia tomentosa], [Corylus colurna], of Illyrian or Moesian affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South Carpathian [Aremonia] beech forests
description: Neutrophile or basicline montane [Fagus sylvatica] forests widespread in the southwestern Carpathians, characterized by the presence of thermophile species of Illyrian affinities, in particular, [Aremonia agrimonoides], [Potentilla micrantha], [Fraxinus ornus], [Tamus communis] and the extreme rarefaction of typical [Symphyto-Fagion] Carpathian species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South Carpathian [Corylus colurna] beech forests
description: Neutrophile low montane [Fagus moesiaca] forests with [Corylus colurna] and a cortŠge of southern species, including [Primula columnae], [Fraxinus ornus], [Lathyrus venetus], [Knautia drymeia], [Ruscus hypoglossum], occupying small surfaces in a few localities of the southwestern Carpathians, south to the Rtanj range of eastern Serbia; they are related to Moesian formations of unit  41.19, in particular unit 41.1934.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South Carpathian [Helleborus odorus] beech forests
description: Neutrophile to weakly acidophile [Fagus moesiaca] forests, of low mountains and hills of the southwestern Romanian Carpathians and pre-Carpathian ranges, with a cortŠge of southern, in part Illyrian, species, including [Helleborus odorus], [Asperula taurina], [Daphne laureola], [Ruscus aculeatus], [Tamus communis], [Tilia tomentosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South Carpathian [Festuca drymeja] beech forests
description: Weakly acidophile to acidophile [Fagus sylvatica] or [Fagus moesiaca] forests of the upper part of sunny slopes of the mountains and hills of the southern and southwestern Carpathians, with an herb layer dominated by [Festuca drymeja] and in which [Luzula luzuloides] is always present and the [Symphyto-Fagenion] species poorly represented.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trans-Carpathian beech forests
description: Forests of [Fagus sylvatica], [Fagus taurica] and [Fagus orientalis] of hills and low mountains of the eastern flank of the southeastern Carpathians, of the central plateau of Romanian Moldavia and the Republic of Moldova, of the Podolian plateau of the western Ukraine, mostly with a cortŠge comprised of southern European elements, including [Tilia tomentosa], [Cornus mas], [Potentilla micrantha], [Carex brevicollis], [Corydalis bulbosa] ssp. [marshalliana] ([Corydalis marshalliana]), [Lathyrus venetus], [Lathyrus aureus], [Cardamine quinquefolia] ([Dentaria quinquefolia]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moldavian [Tilia-Corydalis] beech forests
description: Tall neutrophile forests of hills and low mountain slopes of the eastern flank of the southeastern Carpathians, of the central plateau of Romanian Moldavia and the Republic of Moldova, at an altitude of 200-400 metres, with an upper canopy formed by [Fagus sylvatica], [Fagus taurica] and [Fagus orientalis], mixed with [Tilia tomentosa], [Tilia cordata], [Tilia platyphyllos], [Quercus petraea], [Acer pseudoplatanus], and a lower stratum of [Carpinus betulus], [Acer platanoides], [Acer campestre], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Prunus avium], varied shrub and liana strata comprising [Corylus avellana], [Hedera helix] and a species-rich herb layer with [Carex pilosa], [Carex brevicollis] and the regional differential taxa [Corydalis bulbosa] ssp. [marshalliana] ([Corydalis marshalliana]), [Lathyrus venetus], [Lathyrus aureus], [Cardamine quinquefolia] ([Dentaria quinquefolia]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moldavian [Cornus mas] beech forests
description: Neutrophile [Fagus sylvatica], [Fagus taurica] and [Fagus orientalis] forests with [Cornus mas] and other southern European floristic elements, including [Lathyrus venetus], [Potentilla micrantha], of rare occurrence in hills and low mountain slopes of the eastern Carpathians and pre-Carpathians, notably in Romanian Moldavia and the Republic of Moldova.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Low montane Podolic beech woods
description: Forests of [Fagus sylvatica] of the Podolian plateaux of the western Ukraine, in the region of the upper Dniester, of more northern affinities than those of units 41.D61 and 41.D62.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic beech forests
description: [Fagus orientalis] forests of the Pontic Range and its satellite chains, extending into southeastern Central Europe in the Stranja-Istranca Range and the eastern Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic beech forests
description: [Fagus orientalis] forests of the western Pontic Range, the Stranja-Istranca Range and the eastern Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Balkan Range oriental beech forests
description:
Beech forests of the eastern Balkan Range dominated by [Fagus orientalis] and with an understorey formed in part by a Euxinian cortŠge, impoverished in comparison to that of more southern and eastern communities, though fairly similar to that of unit 41.1E21, comprising, as most characteristic taxa, [Primula vulgaris] ssp. [sibthorpii] ([Primula rosea], [Primula sibthorpii]), [Trachystemon orientalis] and [Scilla bithynica].


 and the absence of other southern Euxinian elements that occur in the Stranja.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja oriental beech forests
description: [Fagus orientalis] forests of the Stranja-Istranca Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja bearberry tree-oriental beech forests
description: Beech forests of the Stranja-Istranca mountains dominated by [Fagus orientalis], less rich in lauriphyllous shrubs than those of 41.1E122, more similar to those of 41.1E11, although slightly richer in Euxinian elements, with a cortŠge that includes, locally, [Vaccinium arctostaphylos], otherwise formed primarily by [Primula vulgaris] ssp. [sibthorpii] ([Primula rosea]), [Trachystemon orientalis] and [Scilla bithynica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja rhododendron-oriental beech forests
description: Beech forests of the Stranja-Istranca mountains dominated by [Fagus orientalis], often accompanied by [Carpinus betulus], [Carpinus orientalis], [Tilia tomentosa], [Tilia cordata], [Tilia platyphyllos], [Quercus polycarpa], [Acer platanoides], [Acer campestre], [Ulmus glabra], [Sorbus torminalis], [Sorbus domestica], [Prunus avium], with an understorey rich in lauriphyllous shrubs of Euxinian affinities, comprising, in particular, [Rhododendron ponticum], [Daphne pontica], [Prunus laurocerasus] ([Laurocerasus officinalis]), [Pyracantha coccinea], [Ilex aquifolium], [Ruscus hypoglossum],   and with the Euxinian [Primula vulgaris] ssp. [sibthorpii] ([Primula rosea]), [Trachystemon orientalis], [Teucrium cuneifolium], [Cyclamen coum], [Epimedium pubigerum], [Hypericum calycinum] and [Scilla bithynica] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic rhododendron-oriental beech forests
description: Forests of the western Pontic Range dominated by [Fagus orientalis], accompanied by [Quercus iberica], [Acer cappodoccicum], [Acer trautvetteri], with a lauriphile-rich one- to six-metre high understorey of [Rhododendron ponticum], [Rhododendron flavum] and [Ilex colchica] with [Hedera colchica], [Smilax excelsa], [Ruscus hypoglossum], [Daphne pontica], [Vaccinium arctostaphylos], [Crataegus pentagyna], [Aristolochia pontica], forming a massive belt at altitudes extending from sea level to 1100-1200 metres, under precipitations of 1000-2000 mm and on siliceous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic calciphile beech forests
description: Rare forests limited to calcareous outcrops of the western Pontic Range dominated by [Fagus orientalis] accompanied by [Stephylea pinnata], [Buxus sempervirens], [Taxus baccata], [Euonymus latifolius] ssp. [caucanus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic neutrocline fir-beech forests
description: Forests of the western Pontic Range dominated by [Fagus orientalis] accompanied by [Abies bornmuelleriana] occupying sites at altitudes above the rhododendron-beech forests of unit 41.1E14, accompanied by a similar floral cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic calciphile fir-beech forests
description: Forests of the western Pontic Range dominated by [Fagus orientalis] with [Abies bornmuelleriana] limited to calcareous outcrops within the fir-beech belt formed by the forests of unit 41.1E15, and at altitudes above the rhododendron-beech forests of unit 41.1E14, with a species-rich cortŠge characterized by the presence of [Telekia speciosa], [Aristolochia bodomae], [Arum ponticum], [Hieracleum platytaenium], [Campanula lactiflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western sub-Pontic beech-oak forests
description: Forests of the western Pontic Range composed of [Fagus orientalis], often with [Quercus dshorochensis], [Quercus syspirensis], [Quercus anatolica] or [Quercus iberica], [Carpinus betulus] and a presence of [Abies bornmuelleriana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian beech-oak forests
description: Beech and oak forests of the western Pontic Range occupying limestones, marls, flyschs and, locally, volcanic substrates, in damp climate areas with 900-1200 mm precipitation, of the Istranca mountains, of the western Pontic chains to the level of Sinop, of the Samsun area and of the Kelkit Cay and Harsit valleys south of Trabzon, variously composed of [Quercus dshorochensis], [Quercus syspirensis], [Quercus anatolica], [Quercus iberica], [Fagus orientalis], [Carpinus betulus], [Carpinus orientalis], [Acer cappadocium], sometimes with a presence of [Abies bornmuelleriana], [Pinus sylvestris] or [Pinus pallasiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western inner Pontic beech forests
description: Forests of interior massifs of the western Pontic Range dominated by [Fagus orientalis], sometimes with [Abies bornmuelleriana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic beech forests
description: Forests dominated by [Fagus orientalis] of the eastern Pontic Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic montane speedwell beech forests
description: Montane forests dominated by [Fagus orientalis] of the westernmost chains of the eastern Pontic Range, between, in the upper Yesil and Bag basins, characterized by [Veronica melissaefolia], [Veronica filiformis], [Veronica peduncularis], [Cyclamen coum] ssp. [caucasicum], [Vicia cracca], [Luzula pilosa], [Paris incompleta], [Cardamine pectinata] and the nearly total absence of lauriphyllous species, located on siliceous substrates at altitudes of 1200-1700 m, with 1200-1500 mm precipitation and 2-4 months of snow cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic beech-spruce forests
description: Montane forests dominated by [Fagus orientalis] with [Picea orientalis] of the eastern Pontic Range, extending along the entire chain from the Yedig”z and Igdir massif eastwards, forming a continuation of the beech forests of unit 41.1E31, with an understorey that includes [Rhododendron ponticum], [Daphnae pontica], [Vaccinium arctostaphylos], located on siliceous substrates at altitudes of 900-1400 m, with 1200-2000 mm precipitation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic calciphile beech forests
description: Rare forests dominated by [Fagus orientalis] accompanied by [Stephylea pinnata], [Buxus sempervirens], [Taxus baccata], [Euonymus latifolius] ssp. [caucanus], limited to calcareous outcrops of the eastern Pontic Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern sub-Pontic beech forests
description: Forests dominated by [Fagus orientalis] of siliceous substrates of the Kastamontu and Gereda regions of the eastern interior Pontic Range, under cold climate with 5-6 months of snow cover, 2-3 months of drought and annual pricipation of 1700-1900 mm.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dobrogea beech forest
description: Relict beech forests of the Macin Mountains, of extremely insular distribution, isolated within the steppe climate of the Romanian Dobrogea, far from the main beech regions of the Carpathians, with [Fagus sylvatica], [Fagus taurica] ([Fagus taurica] var. [dobrogica]), [Tilia tomentosa], [Tilia cordata], [Fraxinus ornus], [Fraxinus angustifolia], [Fraxinus pallisiae], [Carpinus betulus], [Populus tremula], [Ulmus glabra], [Fagetalia] species and southern European species, including [Potentilla micrantha], [Scutellaria altissima], in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean beech forests
description: Beech forests of the northern slopes of the southernmost mountain range of the Crimean Peninsula at altitudes between 600 m and 1100 m, on Jurassic substrates, under a climate regime of cool temperatures and moderate precipitation; the beeches are in almost pure stands or occasionally mixed with [Carpinus betulus], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Tilia cordata], [Ulmus glabra], with a poorly developed understorey that may include [Euonymmus latifolius], [Taxus baccata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian beech forests
description: Beech, beech-hornbeam and beech-fir forests of the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian sweet-pea beech forests
description: [Fagus orientalis] forests of the 1200-1300 m level of the southern flank of the central Caucasus, with [Quercus petraea], [Tilia cordata], [Acer laetum], [Acer campestre], [Rhododendron luteum], [Corylus avellana], [Cornus australis], [Lonicera caprifolium], [Crataegus kyrtostyla], [Euonymus latifolia], [Rubus caucasicus], [Galium odoratum], [Aruncus sylvestris], [Salvia glutinosa], [Polygonatum multiflorum], [Polygonatum polyanthemum], [Viola reichenbachiana], [Epilobium montanum], [Pulmonaria dacica], [Orobus laxifolius], [Festuca drymaea], [Festuca altissima], [Brachypodium sylvaticum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian bittercress and fern beech-hornbeam forests
description: [Fagus orientalis]-[Carpinus caucasica] forests of the 1200-1700 m level of the southern flank of the central Caucasus, with [Rhododendron luteum], [Euonymus latifolia], [Rubus caucasicus], [Tamus communis], [Galium odoratum], [Aruncus sylvestris], [Salvia glutinosa], [Polygonatum multiflorum], [Polygonatum polyanthemum], [Viola reichenbachiana], [Epilobium montanum], [Pulmonaria dacica], [Dentaria bulbifera], [Cardamine impatiens], [Festuca drymaea], [Festuca altissima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian bittercress beech-hornbeam forests
description: [Fagus orientalis]-[Carpinus caucasica] forests of the 1200-1300 m level of the southern flank of the central Caucasus, with [Rubus caucasicus], [Salvia glutinosa], [Dentaria bulbifera], [Cardamine impatiens], [Paris incompleta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian fern beech-hornbeam forests
description: [Fagus orientalis]-[Carpinus caucasica] forests of the 1200-1700 m level of the southern flank of the central Caucasus, with [Polystichum braunii], [Polystichum lonchitis], [Phyllitis scolopendrium], [Matteuccia struthiopteris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian butterbur beech forests
description: [Fagus orientalis] forests of steep ubacs the 1800 m level of the southern flank of the central Caucasus, with [Rhododendron luteum], [Euonymus latifolia], [Rubus caucasicus], [Daphne alboviana], [Galium odoratum], [Aruncus sylvestris], [Salvia glutinosa], [Polygonatum multiflorum], [Polygonatum polyanthemum], [Polygonatum verticillatum], [Viola reichenbachiana], [Epilobium montanum], [Pulmonaria dacica], [Petasites albus], [Senecio platyphylloides], [Euphorbia macroceras], [Gentiana schistocalyx], [Valeriana tiliaefolia], [Festuca drymaea], [Festuca altissima],
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian timberline beech forests
description: Timberline [Fagus orientalis] forests of the subalpine level of the southern flank of the central Caucasus, with [Rhododendron luteum], [Euonymus latifolia], [Rubus caucasicus], [Galium odoratum], [Aruncus sylvestris], [Salvia glutinosa], [Polygonatum multiflorum], [Polygonatum polyanthemum], [Viola reichenbachiana], [Epilobium montanum], [Pulmonaria dacica], [Veratrum lobelianum], [Aconitum orientale], [Asperula caucasica], [Swertia iberica], [Delphinium bracteosum], [Festuca drymaea], [Festuca altissima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian rich dark fir-beech forests
description: [Fagus orientalis]-[Abies nordmannia] forests of ubacs of the 1400-2200 m level of the northern flank of the Great Caucasus, with [Ulmus glabra], [Rhododendron luteum], [Euonymus latifolia], [Rubus caucasicus], [Galium odoratum], [Aruncus sylvestris], [Salvia glutinosa], [Polygonatum multiflorum], [Polygonatum polyanthemum], [Viola reichenbachiana], [Epilobium montanum], [Pulmonaria dacica], [Geranium robertianum], [Paris incompleta], [Mycelis muralis], [Ranunculus astrantifolius], [Festuca drymaea], [Festuca altissima], [Dryopteris filix-mas], [Dryopteris carthusiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian bilberry beech forests
description: [Fagus orientalis]-[Abies nordmannia] forests of acid podzolized soils of the Great and central Caucasus, with [Daphne glomerata], [Vaccinium arctostaphylos], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Orthilia secunda], [Pyrola media], [Luzula sylvatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trans-Caucasian beech-hornbeam forests
description: Beech-dominated facies of the [Fagus orientalis]-[Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus caucasica] forests of the 1200-1300 m level of the southern flank of the Central Caucasus of central Georgia, with [Clinopodium vulgare], [Primula macrocalyx], [Salvia glutinosa], [Fragaria vesca], [Epilobium montanum], [Melica uniflora], [Poa nemoralis]. More mixed or hornbeam-dominated stands are listed in unit 41.H311.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caspian beech forests
description: Forests of [Fagus orientalis] on north slopes of the Elburz Mountains, at the 1400-1800 metre level, under the climatic influence of the Caspian Sea, with cool temperatures and moderate annual precipitation, typically with abundant snowfall; the beech is either accompanied by [Acer insigne], [Alnus subcordata], [Carpinus betulus], [Quercus castaneifolia], [Sorbus torminalis], [Taxus baccatus], [Ulmus glabra], or growing in pure formations, the presence of other tree species diminishing towards the upper altitudinal levels; a luxurient understorey includes [Ilex hyrcanica], [Daphne pontica], [Vaccinium arctostaphylos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern oro-Mediterranean beech forests
description: Isolated beech forests of the Taurus system in western and southern Anatolia (Muraldag, Garur Daglari).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian beech forests
description: Beech forests of the nemoral zone of the East Asian floral domaine, formed by [Fagus crenata] and [Fagus japonica] in Japan, by [Fagus multinervis] in Korea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Japanese beech forests
description: Beech forests of Japan, distributed on southern Hokkaido, on Honshu and, locally, on Kyushu, at elevations between about 500 and 1700 m, within the cool-temperate to subalpine transition zones, formed by [Fagus crenata] or [Fagus japonica], often associated with other broad-leaved trees including [Quercus crispula], [Acer spp.], [Betula ermanii], [Zelkova serrata], or with conifers, [Abies spp.], [Thujopsis dolobrata], [Picea spp.], [Cryptomeria japonica], with an understorey that may be formed of [Sasa kurilensis], [Sasamorpha purpurascens] or ferns.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Japanese [Fagus crenata] forests
description: Beech forests of Japan dominated by [Fagus crenata], sometimes associated with [Fagus japonica], widespread, in particular, in southwestern Hokkaido, on the Pacific side of northern Honshu, on mesic flat areas of the mountainous Pacific side of central Honshu, in southwestern Honshu and in the highlands of Kyushu.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Japanese [Fagus japonica] forests
description: Beech forests of Japan dominated by [Fagus japonica], recorded, in particular, from the central and southern parts of the Sea of Japan watershed of northern Honshu, where it associates with [Abies firma] and [Zelkova serrata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Korean [Fagus multinervis] forests
description: Forests of [Fagus multinervis] of the volcanic Ulisung Island situated 130 km to the east of the Korean mainland, developed under a humid temperate climate with a short cold period. The beech is accompanied by two Asiatic [Acer] species, by [Prunus takesimensis], [Tilia insularis], [Sorbus commixta], [Styrax obassia], [Cornus controversa]. The shrub layer includes [Ligustrum foliosum] and [Rhododendron brachycarpum], the herb layer, [Maianthemum dilatatum], [Hepatica maxima], [Smilax riparia], [Diosporum sessile], [Solidago virgaurea], [Phryma leptostachya], the bamboo [Sasa kurilense] and four species of genus [Viola].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oak-hornbeam forests
description: Atlantic, medio-European and eastern European forests dominated by [Quercus robur] or [Quercus petraea], on eutrophic or mesotrophic soils, with usually ample and species-rich herb and bush layers. [Carpinus betulus] is generally present. They occur under climates too dry or on soils too wet or too dry for beech or as a result of forestry practices favouring oaks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mixed Atlantic bluebell oak forests
description: Atlantic forests of the British Isles, western Belgium and northwestern France, mostly on more or less water-retaining soils, characterized by a diverse tree layer, dominated by [Quercus robur] and rich in [Fraxinus excelsior], and by an herb layer rich in species of the group of [Hyacinthoides non-scripta], in particular [Narcissus pseudonarcissus], [Gagea spathacea], [Tamus communis], [Primula vulgaris], [Luzula forsteri]. [Allium ursinum], [Primula elatior], [Ranunculus ficaria], [Anemone nemorosa], [Lamium galeobdolon] characterise variants linked to soil acidity and hygromorphy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aquitanian ash-oak and oak-hornbeam forests
description: Forests of [Quercus robur], [Fraxinus excelsior] and [Carpinus betulus] of valley bottoms and cool, damp lower slopes of southwestern France, south to the Pyrenean piedmont, with [Sorbus torminalis], [Ruscus aculeatus] and many thermocline, acidocline and Mediterraneo-Atlantic species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic oxlip ash-oak forests
description: Forests of [Quercus robur], sometimes [Quercus petraea], rich in [Fraxinus excelsior], with [Carpinus betulus], developed on more or less wet, meso-eutrophic soils, in regions of moderate Atlantic influence, from southern Champagne and Lorraine north to lower Rhenania, Westphalia and Hanover, characterized by the abundance of species of the ecological groups of [Primula elatior], of [Lamium galeobdolon], of [Anemone nemorosa] and by the absence of [Hyacinthoides non-scripta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arum ash-oak forests
description: Typical neutrocline and acidocline [Quercus robur]-[Fraxinus excelsior] forests with primrose, developed on silts, marls and clays, characterized by the presence of the ecological group of [Arum maculatum], including [Ranunculus ficaria], [Ranunculus auricomus], [Adoxa moschatellina], [Ribes rubrum], [Glechoma hederacea], [Listera ovata], or of the group of [Galium odoratum], with [Rosa arvensis], [Mercurialis perennis], [Sanicula europaea], [Melica uniflora], [Ornithogalum pyrenaicum], or by the abundance of [Lamium galeobdolon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corydalis ash-oak forests
description: [Quercus robur]-[Fraxinus excelsior] forests occupying damp colluvions at the bottom of slopes in valleys within sub-Atlantic forests, characterized by the presence of the group of [Anemone ranunculoides], [Corydalis solida], [Gagea lutea] and [Lathraea squamaria] or of [Aconitum vulparia], transitional to ravine or alluvial forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Garlic ash-oak forests
description: Sub-Atlantic [Quercus robur]-[Fraxinus excelsior] forests rich in [Allium ursinum], of alluvial terraces and adjacent colluvions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic stitchwort oak-hornbeam forests
description: Sub-Atlantic and medio-European forests of [Quercus robur] and [Quercus petraea], with [Carpinus betulus], developed on meso-oligotrophic soils, less hydromorphic than those occupied by the often sympatric forests of unit 41.23, characterized by the replacement of the groups of [Primula elatior] and [Lamium galeobdolon], well represented in the forests of unit 41.23, by those of [Deschampsia flexuosa] and of [Maianthemum bifolium], transgressives from the [Quercion]. They constitute the prevalent oak-hornbeam forests of the Mnster basin, the Rhenish and Mosan regions, the northwestern Hercynian lands, Lorraine and the eastern Paris basin, Burgundy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern oak-hornbeam forests
description: Typical sub-Atlantic [Quercus robur]-[Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of northern Europe, north to southern Norway, southern Sweden and southern Finland, and of the eastern Paris basin and Lorraine, with [Stellaria holostea], [Carex brizoides], [Narcissus pseudonarcissus], [Polygonatum verticillatum], [Potentilla sterilis], [Ranunculus nemorosus], [Poa chaixii], [Luzula sylvatica], [Luzula luzuloides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lorraine marl oak-hornbeam forests
description: Oak-hornbeam forests of Lorraine marls, with [Quercus robur], [Carpinus betulus], [Acer campestre], [Sorbus torminalis], [Lonicera xylosteum], [Galium odoratum], [Carex umbrosa], [Pulmonaria obscura] and [Ornithogalum pyrenaicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Burgundy collinar oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus robur]-[Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of the mesozoic hills and plateaux of northwestern Burgundy (Nivernais, Langres plateau, Barrois, Morvan piedmont).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Burgundy plain oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus robur]-[Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of the Sa“ne plain in southern Burgundy and Bresse, of the southern Lyonnais and of the Limagne basin, including the outstanding multicentury-old stands of CŒteaux and similar stations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Famennian oak-hornbeam forests
description: Sub-Atlantic forests of [Quercus robur] and [Quercus petraea], mostly low-canopied, with [Carpinus betulus], [Sorbus torminalis], [Betula pendula], [Populus tremula] in the subcanopy or the understorey, developed on soils with an alternating hydric regime, mostly clays derived from the alteration of Devonian schists, characterized by the abundance of [Carex flacca] and the coexistence of acidocline and calcicline species, typical of the sub-Hercynian Fagne-Famenne depression where they constitute a highly distinctive, almost continuous, forest-belt.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-continental oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus robur] or [Quercus petraea] forests of eutrophic or mesotrophic soils of subcontinental and continental northern and central Central Europe and of Eastern Europe. [Carpinus betulus] is generally present in their western representatives, widespread in Central Europe and western Eastern Europe. They are richer in lime, [Tilia cordata], than the sub-Atlantic forests of units 41.23, 41.24 and 41.25. They are of more northern character in their area of mutual approach than the Balkanic forests of unit 41.2C. Their southern limit of occurrence follows the Carpathian arc, the northern rim of the Podolian plateaux, and, farther east, the southern limit of nemoral forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wood bedstraw oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of regions with subcontinental climate within the central European range of [Fagus sylvatica], such as the Upper Rhine plain, the rain shadows of the Harz, Rh”n and Spessart, the Swabian-Franconian basin, the Bavarian plateau and Thuringe, the Austrian northern pre-Alps and the Wienerwald, the Polish central lowlands and adjacent hills of Silesia, Great Poland and Kujawy, dominated by [Quercus petraea] and with [Sorbus torminalis], [Sorbus domestica], [Acer campestre], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Convallaria majalis], [Carex montana], [Carex umbrosa], [Festuca heterophylla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mixed lime-oak-hornbeam forests
description: Lime-oak forests of Central and Eastern Europe developed in regions of continental climate east of the range of [Fagus sylvatica], but within that of [Carpinus betulus], in Poland, Lithuania, Belarus, Ukraine and Russia, with [Quercus petraea], [Quercus robur], [Tilia cordata], [Acer platanoides], [Carpinus betulus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreonemoral spruce-lime-oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus robur]-[Quercus petraea]-[Tilia cordata] forests of northern nemoral or boreonemoral regions of northeastern Central Europe and Eastern Europe, east of the range of [Fagus sylvatica], north of the range of the forests of unit 41.262 from which they differ by an admixture of [Picea abies] and other boreal species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Carpathian lime-oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus robur]-[Quercus petraea]-[Tilia cordata] forests of the northern flank of the northern and northeastern Carpathians (Poloninskij Chrebet), west to northern Moravia, differing from those of unit 41.262 by the presence of [Abies alba] and [Picea abies] in the tree layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bohemian oak-hornbeam and oak-lime forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of plains and low hills of the Bohemian basin and adjacent areas of northeastern Lower Austria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bohemian melampyrum oak-hornbeam forests
description: Oak-hornbeam forests widespread in the Bohemian basin and neighbouring regions, particularly in the plains and low hills of the Bohemian Elbe-Vltava system, in the southwestern Moravian hills and valleys of the Dyje system and of the Thaya valley, and in northeastern Lower Austria (Kamp valley, Thaya valley, eastern edges of Waldviertel), with northern outposts in the Bohemian foothills of the Krusne Hory (Metallic Mountains) and in the Smida basin, in the western approaches to the Jizerske (western Sudeten). The tree layer is dominated by [Quercus petraea] and [Carpinus betulus] variously associated with [Tilia cordata], [Quercus robur], [Fagus sylvatica], sometimes [Fraxinus excelsior], [Acer pseudoplatanus], [Acer campestre], [Abies alba]. The shrub layer is species-rich, mostly formed by young individuals of the tree-layer species, with [Acer campestre], [Crataegus oxyacantha]. The herb layer has a somewhat continental and thermophile species cortŠge in which [Anemone nemorosa], [Poa nemoralis], [Stellaria holostea], [Galium sylvaticum], [Convallaria majalis] may form facies. [Melampyrum nemorosum], although not usually dominant, reaches its highest frequency within forest habitats in this community.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Bohemian oak-lime forests
description: Local and threatened oak-lime forests of the central Bohemian basin, limited to the Elbe and lower Vltava basins where it occupies terrace sands, sandy aeolian deposits and decalcified loess loams under warm, dry subcontinental climate conditions. [Quercus petraea], or sometimes [Quercus robur], associated with [Tilia cordata], dominate the tree layer. [Carpinus betulus] is rare. The species cortŠge, of which [Poa angustifolia], [Carex palescens], [Holcus mollis], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Hypericum montanum], [Carex pilulifera], [Carex umbrosa] are characteristic, contains numerous acidophilous species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Bohemian stitchwort oak-lime forests
description: Local and threatened oak-lime forests of the southern Bohemian basin, limited to the middle Otava valley and the foothills of the Sumava, developed on relatively rich soils of plains or moderate to steep slopes at the collinar level. The tree layer is dominated by [Quercus robur] and [Tilia cordata], associated with [Sorbus aucuparia], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Acer platanoides]. [Carpinus betulus] is absent. [Corylus avellana] may be well represented in the shrub layer. The herb layer is usually dominated by hygro-mesophilous species, in particular, [Stellaria holostea], [Lamium galeobdolon], [Poa nemoralis]; acidophilous species, notably [Luzula luzuloides], [Carex brizoides] are frequent, the latter sometimes forming facies. Other characteristic species include [Hepatica nobilis], [Convallaria majalis], [Aegopodium podagraria], [Oxalis acetosella], [Milium effusum], [Lilium martagon], [Euphorbia dulcis], [Lathyrus vernus]. Some stands are dominated by [Tilia cordata] (unit 41.G1 x 41.2653).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian hairy sedge oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Tilia cordata]-[Carpinus betulus]-[Fagus sylvatica] forests of the collinar level of the Carpathians, of southern Moravia, of the flysch hills of northeastern Lower Austria, of the Hainburger Berge and Leitha hills of northeastern Burgenland and of the volcanic hills of northern Hungary.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pannonic primrose oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Quercus robur]-[Carpinus betulus]-[Acer campestre] forests of warm hills of the Pannonic domaine, in southern Moravia, southern Slovakia, the eastern Lower-Austrian Weinviertel and Marchfeld, the hills of western Transdanubia and the mid-Pannonic range of central Transdanubia, outside of the range of [Fagus sylvatica], with [Quercus cerris], [Cornus mas], [Sorbus torminalis], [Ulmus minor], [Rhamnus catharticus], [Viola mirabilis], [Viola alba], [Viola suavis], [Primula veris], [Polygonatum latifolium], [Polygonatum multiflorum], [Polygonatum odoratum], [Pulmonaria mollis] ssp. [mollis], [Pulmonaria murinii], [Chamaecytisus supinus], [Serratula tinctoria], [Convallaria majalis], [Carex curvata], [Carex michelii], [Melica uniflora], [Poa nemoralis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central sub-Carpathian oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-Quercus robur]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of hills, valleys and plateaux of the southern flank of the eastern section of the Western Carpathian arc, in Slovakia and northern Hungary, within the range of [Fagus sylvatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Waldsteinia oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Quercus robur]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of the Slovakian-Hungarian karst.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scorpion-vetch oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Quercus robur]-[Carpinus betulus] forests of eastern Slovakia, with [Coronilla elegans] ([Coronilla latifolia]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western boreal mixed deciduous forests
description: Forests of [Quercus robur], [Ulmus glabra], [Tilia cordata], [Acer platanoides], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Corylus avellana] and sometimes [Fagus sylvatica] and/or [Carpinus betulus], of the southern Fennoscandian and Baltic regions of transition and interdigitation between taiga and nemoral deciduous forests. They usually constitute deciduous forests enclaved in a taiga environment, near the limits of the ranges of [Fagus sylvatica] and/or [Carpinus betulus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern middle Russian oak-lime forests
description: Forests of [Quercus robur] of the northern nemoral zone and of enclaves in the southern boreal zone of Eastern Europe, with [Tilia cordata] and no [Carpinus betulus]. They are characteristic of the Baltic States, eastern Belarus, the Ukraine and Russia, east to the Volga, outside of the range of [Carpinus betulus]. They also occur within the geographical range of hornbeam on soils unfavourable to its growth. [Quercus robur] and [Tilia cordata] are accompanied by [Acer platanoides], [Populus tremula], [Picea abies], [Corylus avellana], [Sorbus aucuparia], [Euonymus europaeus], [Daphne mezereum], [Galium odoratum], [Anemone nemorosa] and boreal herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern middle Russian oak-lime forests
description: Forests of the southern nemoral zone of Russia and northeastern Ukraine, east of the range of [Carpinus betulus] and west of the Volga, dominated by [Quercus robur] and [Tilia cordata] with [Acer platanoides] and [Ulmus montana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trans-Volgan oak-lime forests
description: Forests of the nemoral zone of Russia, east of the Volga, with diminishing [Quercus robur] and augmenting [Tilia cordata], and an often luxuriant shrub layer comprizing, in particular, [Corylus avellana]. Many, or most, are dominated by lime and listed under unit 41.G.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian oak-lime forests
description: [Quercus robur]-dominated forests of the montane and submontane zones of the southern Ural, with [Tilia cordata], [Acer platanoides], [Populus tremula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic calciphile oak-hornbeam forests
description: Often low, open, xerophile forests dominated by [Quercus robur] or [Quercus petraea], developed on superficial to deep soils associated with calcareous substrates in Hercynian southern central Germany, eastern and southern Belgium, eastern and central France; located within the range of the [Pulmonario-Carpinenion], they offer similarities to the [Galio-Carpinenion] and generally constitute substitution forests of the [Cephalanthero-Fagion], either regressive phases brought about by coppicing or recolonisation phases permitted by abandonment of [Bromion] grasslands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic calciphile privet oak-hornbeam forests
description: Generally low forests and woods characteristic of superficial calcareous soils on often steep sunny slopes of Hercynian southern central Germany, southern Belgium and eastern France, with [Quercus robur] (usually dominant), [Quercus petraea], [Tilia platyphyllos], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Carpinus betulus], [Acer campestre], [Corylus avellana], [Cornus sanguinea], [Cornus mas], [Crataegus laevigata], [Crataegus monogyna], [Prunus spinosa], [Evonymus europaeus], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Viburnum lantana], [Daphne laureola], [Primula veris], [Viola hirta], [Mercurialis perennis], [Scilla bifolia], [Orchis mascula], [Carex digitata], [Carex montana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic xerophile [Anthericum] oak-hornbeam forests
description: Low, open forests and woods characteristic of steeep, sunny slopes on slightly calcareous schists in the Ardenne-Eifel periphery, with [Quercus petraea] (dominant), [Carpinus betulus], [Quercus robur], [Sorbus torminalis], [Sorbus aria], [Pyrus pyraster], [Malus sylvestris], [Prunus avium], [Amelanchier ovalis], [Stellaria holostea], [Anemone sylvestris], [Silene nutans], [Silene inflata], [Campanula persicifolia], [Anthericum liliago], [Melica nutans], [Carex montana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Atlantic calciphile squill ash-oak forests
description: Forests of [Quercus robur] and [Fraxinus excelsior], rich in ligneous species, in particular, [Fagus sylvatica], [Carpinus betulus], [Sorbus aria], [Sorbus torminalis], [Ulmus glabra] ([Ulmus scabra]), [Taxus baccata], [Acer campestre], [Cornus mas], [Pyrus pyraster], [Daphne laureola], characteristic of well-drained, often deep, sometimes rocky, moist or partly dry calcareous soils on gentle slopes of the south Paris basin and adjacent regions, with [Arum italicum], [Asarum europaeum], [Doronicum plantagineum], [Helleborus foetidus], [Hepatica triloba], [Orobanche hederae], [Lilium martagon], [Carex montana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Alpine oak-hornbeam forests
description: Fragmentary mesophile or mesohygrophile formations of the Insubrian pre-Alps, the northern Apennines, the Ligurian Apennines, the Esterel and the Tanneron and very locally, the southern French Alps (forˆt du Saou, Dr“me), with [Quercus petraea], [Quercus robur], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Tilia platyphyllos], [Tilia cordata] and [Carpinus betulus], developed on deep soils in conditions of sufficient atmospheric and edaphic humidity. They represent a transition between the medio-European formations of the [Pulmonario-Carpinenion] and [Galio-Carpinenion] on the one hand, the southeastern formations of the [Carpinion illyricum], and perhaps the southwestern formations of the [Polysticho-Corylenion], on the other hand.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Cantabrian oak-ash forests
description: Forests dominated by [Quercus robur], or, in parts of the Pyrenees and in the Oro-Cantabrian interior, [Quercus petraea], with [Fraxinus excelsior], [Tilia platyphyllos], [Corylus avellana], [Acer campestre], [Acer pseudoplatanus], [Prunus avium], [Ulmus glabra], many shrubs and lianas, abundant [Hedera helix], many ferns, such as [Polystichum setiferum], [Dryopteris affinis], [Dryopteris dilatata], [Asplenium scolopendrium], and with [Arum italicum], [Veronica montana], [Hypericum androsaemum], [Primula vulgaris], [Pulmonaria longifolia], [Helleborus viridis] ssp. [occidentalis], [Isopyrum thalictroides], [Ajuga reptans], [Carex sylvatica], [Bromus racemosus], [Melica uniflora], of the collinar, submontane and, in a somewhat impoverished form with [Crataegus laevigata], montane levels of the piedmont of the Cordillera Cantabrica, in Navarra, Guipuzcoa, Vizcaya, Cantabria, Asturias and Castilla-Leon, as well as  of the submontane level of the northern slope, and locally in Navarra and Catalonia, the southern slope of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian oak-hornbeam forests
description: Forests of [Quercus robur] or [Quercus petraea], sometimes [Quercus cerris], and [Carpinus betulus] occupying the basins of the Drava and Sava in Slovenia, Croatia, northern Bosnia-Herzegovina, with outliers in south Hungarian mid-Pannonic and peri-Pannonic hills, south of Lake Balaton, in southern Carinthia and Styria and in valleys and hills, particularly karst valleys, of the western Balkan peninsula south to Montenegro, Albania and the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, characterized by higher continentality than in the sub-Mediterranean and by higher temperatures than in middle Europe; they are intermediate between those of central Europe and those of the Balkans and merge northwards into the Pannonic oak woods. Constituting a centre of diversity, they have a much higher species richness than the Central European oak woods. [Acer tataricum], [Cyclamen purpurascens], [Epimedium alpinum], [Erythronium dens-canis], [Helleborus dumetorum] ssp. [atrorubens], [Knautia drymeia] are characteristic. Outliers of these forests also occur in Frioul and the northern Apennines; they have been included in unit 41.28.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian sessile oak-hornbeam forests
description: Forests of [Quercus petraea], sometimes mixed with [Quercus robur] or [Quercus cerris], and [Carpinus betulus] occupying well-drained ground in the basins of the Drava and Sava in Slovenia, Croatia, northern Bosnia-Herzegovina, extending to the southern Hungarian mid-Pannonic and peri-Pannonic hills, to southern Carinthia and Styria, Frioul and the northern Apennines, and to valleys and hills of the western Balkan peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian calcicline sessile oak-hornbeam forests
description: Forests of [Quercus petraea], sometimes mixed with [Quercus robur] or [Quercus cerris], and [Carpinus betulus] occupying limestones and rendzinas, often on skeletal soils, in the basins of the Drava and Sava, north to the hills of southwestern Transdanubia and the upper Drava basin of southern Carinthia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian neutrocline sessile oak-hornbeam forests
description: Forests of [Quercus petraea], sometimes mixed with [Quercus robur] or [Quercus cerris], and [Carpinus betulus], occupying brown soils in the basins of the Drava and Sava, north and west to Friuli Venezia Giulia and the northern Apennines, southern Styria and southern Hungary, extending south in valleys and hills of the western Balkan peninsula to Albania and the F.Y.R. of Macedonia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian acidocline sessile oak-hornbeam forests
description: Forests of [Quercus petraea], sometimes mixed with [Quercus robur] or [Quercus cerris], and [Carpinus betulus], occupying well-drained acid soils in the basins of the Drava and Sava.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian pedunculate oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus robur] and [Carpinus betulus] forests of the Illyrian basin, in particular, humid forests of noncarbonated pseudogleys and gleys of valleys of the Drava and Sava basins of Slovenia, Croatia and Hungary, forming in contact with riverine forests of the [Alno-Padion], but on somewhat higher ground, vicariants of the Pannonic forests of unit 41.2B1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian submediterranean oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea] and [Carpinus betulus] forests of submediterranean regions of the southeastern pre-Alps and karstic reliefs of Slovenia, northwestern Croatia and extreme northeastern Italy, where they occupy north-facing doline slopes and cool vales, much richer in thermophile elements than the forests of unit 41.2A1.
