description: Mesoxerophile, neutrophile mixed oak forests of [Quercus frainetto], accompanied by some [Quercus dalechampii], [Quercus polycarpa], [Quercus pubescens], [Quercus virgiliana], [Fraxinus ornus], [Carpinus orientalis], [Tilia tomentosa] in the tree layer, [Cornus mas], [Cotinus coggygria] in the shrub layer and many sub-Mediterranean species, including [Paeonia peregrina], [Mercurialis ovata], [Piptatherum virescens], [Lychnis coronaria], in the herb layer, limited to small insular surfaces in the lower Danube valley of Bulgaria and in the Romanian Dobrogea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesio-Danubian oriental hornbeam-durmast oak forests
description: Forests mostly dominated by [Quercus frainetto] and [Quercus petraea] [s.l.], of the upper level of the [Quercion frainetto] zone of the central and eastern Balkan peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Moesian [Quercus dalechampii]-oriental hornbeam forests
description: Xero-mesophile [Quercus dalechampii]-dominated forests, sometimes mixed with [Quercus cerris], [Quercus frainetto] or [Fraxinus excelsior], with [Carpinus orientalis], [Ostrya carpinifolia] or [Fraxinus ornus] often present and sometimes abundant, widespread in the durmast oak-hornbeam, 600-1200 metre, belt of the Balkan Range and neighbouring hills, drier than the [Carpinus betulus-Quercus dalechampii] forests of 41.2C35.  [Ruscus aculeatus] is often present and sometimes subdominant in the undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesio-Danubian bedstraw sessile oak forests
description: Acidophile [Quercus petraea] [s.l.] forests of the southern and southwestern pre-Carpathian foothills, with [Galium pseudaristatum], [Luzula luzuloides], [Veronica officinalis], [Poa nemoralis], [Festuca heterophylla] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dobrogean oriental hornbeam-lime-oak forests
description: Oak forests of the Romanian Dobrogea dominated by [Quercus dalechampii], [Quercus polycarpa] or [Quercus pedunculiflora], rich in [Carpinus orientalis], [Tilia tomentosa], [Fraxinus ornus], [Fraxinus excelsior], of mixed Moesian and Pontic affinities, developed in stations ecologically intermediate between those that support [Carpinion betuli] forests of 41.72 and those that harbour steppe forests of 41.7A.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dobrogean paeonia sessile oak forests
description: Neutrophile [Quercus dalechampii] forests, limited to low hills of the Romanian Dobrogea, accompanied by [Fraxinus excelsior] ssp. [excelsior], [Fraxinus excelsior] ssp. [coriariifolia] ([Fraxinus coriariifolia]), [Fraxinus ornus], [Tilia tomentosa], [Carpinus orientalis] in the tree layer, with [Cornus mas] in the shrub layer, and [Paeonia peregrina] and other sub-Mediterranean species, including [Mercurialis ovata], [Piptatherum virescens], [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dobrogean sessile oak-lime-oriental hornbeam-ash forests
description: Xero-mesophile, neutrophile [Quercus dalechampii] and [Quercus polycarpa] forests of the northern Dobrogean plateaux, with [Tilia tomentosa], [Carpinus orientalis], [Carpinus betulus], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Fraxinus coriariifolia], [Fraxinus ornus], accompanied by numerous sub-Mediterranean species including [Nectaroscordum dioscoridis], [Lychnis coronaria], [Digitalis lanata], [Myrrhoides nodosa], [Mercurialis ovata], [Piptatherum virescens], and a few [Fagetalia] species, such as [Zerna benekenii], [Pulmonaria obscura], [Cardamine bulbifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dobrogean [Quercus pedunculiflora]-lime-oriental hornbeam forests
description: Xero-mesophile, neutrophile mixed [Quercus pedunculiflora] forests of the northern Dobrogea plateaux, with [Tilia tomentosa], [Carpinus orientalis], [Carpinus betulus], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Fraxinus ornus] in the tree layer, numerous sub-Mediterranean species, including [Ornithogalum fimbriatum], [Viola jordanii], [Paeonia peregrina], [Myrrhoides nodosa], [Mercurialis ovata], [Piptatherum virescens], and a few [Fagetalia] species, [Zerna benekenii], [Pulmonaria obscura], in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic sub-continental thermophilous oak woods
description: Sub-continental thermo-xerophile [Quercus frainetto-Quercus cerris-Quercus petraea] forests of the foothills bordering the lower Danube depression of southern Romania, with the continental [Acer tataricum] and lacking typically sub-Mediterranean species such as [Carpinus orientalis] and [Ruscus aculeatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic white cinquefoil [Quercus cerris] forests
description: Xero-mesophile, weakly acidophile forests of [Quercus cerris], of the plains of southern Romania, with [Acer campestre], [Acer tataricum], [Crataegus monogyna], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Cornus mas], [Potentilla alba], [Lychnis coronaria], [Viola hirta], [Polygonatum latifolium], [Chrysanthemum corymbosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic early sedge [Quercus frainetto] forests
description: Xero-mesophile, acidophile [Quercus frainetto] forests of Muntenia and Oltenia, with [Acer campestre], [Pyrus pyraster], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Crataegus monogyna], [Carex praecox], [Genista tinctoria], [Veronica officinalis], [Poa angustifolia], [Lychnis coronaria], [Calamagrostis epigejos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic crocus [Quercus frainetto]-[Quercus cerris] forests
description: Xeromesophile, weakly acidophile forests of [Quercus cerris] and [Quercus frainetto] of the plains in the southern of Romania, with [Acer campestre] and [Acer tataricum],  accompanied by [Ligustrum vulgare], [Crataegus monogyna], [Crocus flavus], [Lychnis coronaria], [Genista tinctoria], [Lathyrus niger], [Chrysanthemum corymbosum], [Polygonatum latifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic [Q. frainetto]-[Q. cerris]-[Q. petraea] forests
description: Weakly acidophile forests of [Quercus cerris], [Quercus frainetto] and [Quercus petraea] [s.l.] of the southern and western pre-Carpathian foothills, accompanied by [Acer campestre], [Acer tataricum], [Fraxinus ornus], [Cornus mas], [Crataegus monogyna], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Lathyrus niger], [Lychnis coronaria], [Helleborus odorus], [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Sedum maximum], [Sedum cepaea], [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria] ([Cynanchum vincetoxicum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic [Quercus frainetto]-[Quercus petraea] [s.l.] forests
description: Weakly acidophile forests of [Quercus frainetto] and [Quercus petraea] [s.l.] of the southern pre-Carpathian foothills, with a shrub layer composed of [Acer campestre], [Acer tataricum], [Ulmus minor], [Cornus mas], and an herb layer of [Carex praecox], [Carex caryophyllea], [Genista tinctoria], [Potentilla micrantha], [Lychnis coronaria], [Galium pseudaristatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Carpathian [Quercus cerris]-[Quercus petraea] [s.l.] forests
description: Weakly acidophile to neutrophile forests of [Quercus petraea] [s.l.] and [Quercus cerris] of the southern pre-Carpathian foothills, with [Acer campestre], [Acer tataricum], [Sorbus torminalis], sometimes [Tilia tomentosa], [Cerasus avium], [Fagus sylvatica], [Fraxinus ornus], participating in the tree layer, accompanied by [Crataegus monogyna], [Ligustrum vulgare] in the shrub layer and [Genista tinctoria], [Lathyrus niger], [Silene viridiflora], [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Chrysanthemum corymbosum] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian sub-continental thermophilous oak woods
description: Subcontinental thermoxerophile oak forests of southeastern Bulgaria and European Turkey, developed in the Euxinian Stranja-Istranca and eastern Balkan Range and in the peri-Mediterraneo-steppic hills rising from the northern Thracian plain or fringing it.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxino-Thracian [Quercus frainetto]-[Quercus cerris] forests
description: [Quercus frainetto-Quercus cerris] forests of the northern Thracian plain and its fringing Balkan Range, eastern Rhodope or Stranja foothills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian [Quercus frainetto]-[Quercus cerris] forests
description: Mostly fragmentary forests of the northern Thracian plain, its isolated hills and the fringing foothills of the Balkan Range, the eastern Rhodopes and the northwestern Stranja dominated by [Quercus frainetto] or sometimes [Quercus cerris], accompanied by [Carpinus orientalis], [Crataegus monogyna] and a thermophile, sub-Mediterranean cortŠge that includes [Physospermum cornubiense], [Lathyrus niger], [Lychnis coronaria], [Heptaptera triquetra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Euxinian [Quercus frainetto]-[Quercus cerris] forests
description: Forests of the inner hills and eastern foothills of the Stranja dominated by [Quercus cerris] or [Quercus frainetto], sometimes with [Quercus hartwissiana], accompanied by [Carpinus orientalis], [Acer campestre], [Acer tataricum], [Crataegus monogyna], [Cornus mas], [Poa nemoralis], [Dactylis glomerata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian [Quercus frainetto]-[Quercus virgiliana] forests
description: Forests of [Quercus frainetto] and [Quercus virgiliana] of the northern thracian basin, located mainly on relatively dry hills up to 800 metres, and usually acompanied by a species cortŠge similar to those of 41.76A1, including [Carpinus orientalis], [Acer campestre], [Acer tataricum], [Crataegus monogyna], [Cornus mas], [Poa nemoralis], [Dactylis glomerata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian [Quercus pedunculiflora] forests
description: Mesophile [Quercus pedunculiflora] forests of the northern Thracian plain developed on moist nutrient-rich soils, with [Acer tataricum], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Crataegus monogyna], [Cotinus coggygria], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Physospermum cornubiense], [Lathyrus niger], [Lychnis coronaria]. They have been submitted to intensive clearing and are now represented only by very fragmentary stands or single trees in a very resricted area.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja [Quercus polycarpa] forests
description: [Quercus polycarpa] forests of the Stranja-Istranca Range and of high mountains of the eastern Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja [Primula rosea]-[Quercus polycarpa] forests
description: [Quercus polycarpa]- or [Quercus polycarpa] and [Quercus frainetto]-dominated forests of the Stranja-Istranca Range, accompanied by a cortŠge comprised of numerous Euxinian elements, rich in [Primula vulgaris] ssp. [rosea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja [Fagus orientalis]-[Quercus polycarpa] forests
description: [Quercus polycarpa-Fagus orientalis] forests of the Stranja-Istranca Range, accompanied by a species-rich cortŠge of the [Querceta polycarpae] that includes numerous Euxinian elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Thracian thermophilous oak forests
description: Subcontinental xerothermophile forests of the Istranca southern spurs, rich in Euxinian and Mediterranean elements, dominated by [Quercus petraea] ssp. [dschorochense] and [Quercus cerris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian sub-continental thermophilous oak woods
description: Sub-continental, supra-Mediterranean, thermo-xerophile oak forests of western Anatolia with [Quercus frainetto], [Quercus cerris], [Quercus pubescens] ssp. [anatolica], [Quercus dshorochensis], [Castanea sativa], [Tilia tomentosa], [Mespilus germanica], [Geranium asphodeloides], [Aristolochia pallida], [Achillea grandiflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian turkey oak woods
description: Sub-continental, supra-Mediterranean, xerothermophile oak forests of northwestern Anatolia with [Quercus cerris], [Salvia forskali], [Digitalis orientalis], [Trifolium medium], [Polygala supina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian Hungarian oak woods
description: Sub-continental, supra-Mediterranean, thermo-xerophile calcifuge oak forests of western Anatolia with [Quercus frainetto], [Quercus dshorochensis], [Tilia tomentosa], [Castanea sativa], [Trifolium heldreichianum], [Orobus niger], [Silene splendens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian turkey oak-white oak woods
description: Sub-continental, supra-Mediterranean, thermo-xerophile oak forests of the Sundinken Dag of western Anatolia with [Quercus cerris], [Quercus pubescens] ssp. [anatolica], [Paeonia peregrina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afro-Iberian thermophilous oak forests
description: Iberian and North African forests and woods dominated by [Quercus faginea],  [Quercus canariensis] or [Quercus afares]. The humid formations of southwestern Iberia (units 41.772 and 41.773) are forest types of unique character in Europe and of extreme biological importance; also highly distinctive and vulnerable are the North African communities (unit 41.776) and the Baetic formations listed under units 41.7714 and 41.7715.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spanish [Quercus faginea] forests
description: Xero-mesophile [Quercus faginea] formations of slopes and plateaux of middle elevations of the Spanish Meseta and associated ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Spanish [Quercus faginea] forests
description: [Quercus faginea] forests of the supra-Mediterranean, sub-humid level of the Cantabrian periphery and upper Ebro basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Spanish [Quercus faginea] forests
description: [Quercus faginea] forests of the meso-supra-Mediterranean levels of the Iberian Range, upper Douro basin and neighbouring regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Spanish [Quercus faginea] forests
description: [Quercus faginea] forests of the meso-supra-Mediterranean levels of the Maestrazgo, interior Catalonia and adjacent Aragon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baetic [Quercus faginea] forests
description: Southern forests of the sub-humid to humid supra-Mediterranean level of calcareous Baetic ranges, limited to a few enclaves in the Serrania de Ronda and the ranges of the upper Guadalquivir basin, dominated by [Quercus faginea] associated with [Acer granatense], [Acer monspessulanum], [Sorbus aria], [Sorbus torminalis], [Taxus baccata] and sometimes [Quercus pyrenaica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Valencian [Quercus faginea] forests
description: [Quercus faginea] forests of ubacs of the southern Valencian mountains (Aitana, Montcabrer, Benicadell), with [Acer granatense], [Fraxinus ornus] and [Taxus baccata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Portuguese [Quercus faginea] forests
description: Humid, epiphyte-clad, dense, relict [Quercus faginea] forests of Portugal, restricted to a very few isolated localities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Andalusian [Quercus canariensis] forests
description: Humid and hyper-humid, luxuriant [Quercus canariensis] forests of the sierras of extreme southern Spain, limited to the Aljibe and a very few localities in the Serrania de Ronda.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Catalonian [Quercus canariensis] stands
description: Formations of Catalonia rich in [Quercus canariensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balearic [Quercus faginea] woods
description: Relict formations of Mallorca dominated by, or rich in, [Quercus faginea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: African [Quercus canariensis] forests
description: Montane forests, sometimes tall and closed canopied, of [Quercus canariensis] ([Quercus faginea] ssp. [baetica], [Quercus mirbeckii], [Quercus nordafricana], [Quercus faginea] ssp. tlemcenensis]), pure, or accompanied by [Quercus suber] or [Quercus afares], occupying cool, rainy slopes and tops of the Rif, the Middle Atlas, the Oulmes plateau, the Tell, the Kroumirian mountains, and, very locally, the High Atlas and the Aures. The shrub layer is rather sparce and includes, besides saplings of the dominant species, [Erica arborea], [Crataegus monogyna], [Myrtus communis], [Arbutus unedo], [Cytisus villosus], [Rubus ulmifolius], [Daphne gnidium], [Lonicera etrusca], [Hedera helix], and in very humid valleys, [Laurus nobilis]. The herb layer is abundant and rich, comprising the vernal [Ranunculus ficaria] ssp. [ficariiformis] ([Ficaria grandiflora]) and [Chrysanthemum], as well as [Agrimonia eupatoria], [Achillea ligustica], [Cyclamen africanum], [Satureja vulgaris] Fritsch, [Polystichum aculeatum], [Galium aparine], [Prunella vulgaris], [Carex remota], locally, [Pteridium aquilinum], [Sanicula europaea] or [Hypericum androsaemum]. Epyphytic growth is moderate, notably of [Polypodium vulgare] and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: African [Quercus afares] forests
description: [Quercus afares] stands or forests, pure or associated with [Quercus canariensis], limited to high altitudes in the Tell and the eastern Kroumirian mountains, in somewhat drier situations than those occupied by [Quercus canariensis] forest, though more humid than those characteristic of [Quercus suber] forests; the understorey includes [Cytisus villosus], [Erica arborea], [Genista tricuspidata], [Ilex aquifolium], [Ruscus aculeatus], [Paeonia atlantica], [Sanicula europaea], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Ampelodesmos mauritanica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trojan oak woodland
description: Supra-Mediterranean, and occasionally meso-mediterranean woods dominated by the semideciduous [Quercus trojana] or its allies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic Trojan oak woods
description: Usually low formations dominated by [Quercus trojana], often with junipers or maples, of Macedonia, Thrace and Thessaly, north to Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania and the the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, in the Vardar valley.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apulian Trojan oak woods
description: Relict woods, sometimes of considerable height, of [Quercus trojana] and [Quercus pubescens], often with an admixture of [Quercus ilex] and its associated vegetation (Murge: e.g. bosco delle Pianelle, foresta Gaglione).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian Trojan oak woods
description: Woods or stands of [Quercus trojana] of the mesomediterranean or supramediterranean levels of western Anatolia, at altitudes below 900 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lebanese [Quercus look] forests
description: Supra-Mediterranean forests dominated by [Quercus look], established at or near the xeric fringes of the Mediterranean domaine, best developed on lthe eastern slopes of the Lebanon mountains, the Anti-Lebanon and Mount Hermon, with a cortŠge of mixed Mediterranean and Irano-Turanian species, including [Quercus boissieri], [Juniperus drupacea], [Sorbus graeca], [Amygdalus korshinskyi], [Prunus ursina], [Colutea cilicica], [Berberis cretica], [Eriolobus trilobatus], [Phlomis braevilaeris], [Picris strigosa], [Kundmannia syriaca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean valonia oak woodland
description: Woods dominated by the semideciduous [Quercus macrolepis], often fairly open, of the mostly meso-Mediterranean zone of Greece, Albania, western Asia, and, very locally, southern Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic valonia oak woods
description: [Quercus macrolepis] formations of continental Greece and its archipelagoes, as well as of ajacent Albania; well developed forests exist, in particular, in the Ionian islands and on Lesbos; more modified, grove-like, stands, exist on the maritime slopes of the low mountains bordering the gulf of Arta and in western Etolia, in the northwestern Peloponnese, in Thessaly, in Attica, in Thrace, in Crete.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apulian valonia oak woods
description: Relict [Quercus macrolepis] formations of Salento (Tricase).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian valonia oak woods
description: Forests, woods or stands of [Quercus macrolepis] of Anatolia, mostly limited to western Anatolia, with a few outlying patches east to Siirt, sometimes forming extensive, handsome forests, particularly in the lower montane zone and in intermountain plains; they are situated mostly between 0 and 500 metres altitude, occasionally higher.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tabor oak woods
description: [Quercus ithaburensis]-dominated forests of the mesomediterranean zone of southern Anatolia and the Near East, occupying extensive areas in Palestine and Jordan, occurring farther north in the Golan Heights, in the plain of Adana, in the plain of Hatay, in Maras province, and in a few localities of the Taurus mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian steppe oak woods
description: Xero-thermophile oak woods of continental affinities of the wooded steppe zone of Pannonia and the Ponto-Sarmatic region, and their irradiations into regions or sites of high local continentality west and north of the Ponto-Pannonic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: White cinquefoil oak woods
description: Xero-thermophile oak woods of central Europe, Pannonia and the northern approaches to the Ponto-Sarmatic wooded steppe zone with a flora of moderate thermophily and high continental affinities, mostly characteristic of sandy soil along the edges of the eastern steppeland and of clay soils in northern and western woodland areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western white cinquefoil sessile oak woods
description: Cinquefoil oak woods of the Rhine, Elbe, Oder, Vistula and upper Danube basins, including the northern and central Bohemian Basin and the southern flank of the Bohemian Massif and the Carpathians in Moravia, forming the northern and westernmost irradiations of the complex, with [Quercus petraea], [Quercus robur], [Pinus sylvestris], [Sorbus torminalis], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Lonicera xylosteum], [Viburnum lantana], [Corylus avellana], [Rhamnus catharticus], [Prunus spinosa], [Juniperus communis], [Carpinus betulus], [Pyrus communis], [Primula veris], [Campanula persicifolia], [Polygonatum odoratum], [Lathyrus niger], [Geranium sanguineum], [Potentilla alba], [Pulmonaria angustifolia], [Ranunculus polyanthemos], [Serratula tinctoria], [Silene nutans], [Veronica officinalis], [Veronica chamaedrys], [Hieracium silvaticum], [Carex montana], [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Calamagrostis arundinacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic turkey oak-sessile oak woods
description: Well-developed woods of the Pannonic basin, in Hungary, southern Slovakia, western Romania and Serbia, installed on deep brown forest soil, between 200 m and 500 m altitude, dominated by [Quercus petraea], [Quercus dalechampii], [Quercus polycarpa] and [Quercus cerris], with an underdeveloped shrub layer and a grassy understorey composed most frequently of [Festuca beterophylla], [Poa nemoralis], [Melica uniflora], accompanied by [Lychnis coronaria], [Potentilla alba], [Vicia cassubica], [Serratula tinctoria], [Chrysanthemum corymbosum], [Digitalis grandiflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic hairy greenweed sessile oak woods
description: Uncommon thermophilous [Quercus petraea] woods of the Pannonic basin, developed in Hungary, in particular in the Central Hungarian Range, extending to Lower Austria, southwestern Moravia, southern Slovakia and western Romania, on andesite, granite or slate substrates and slightly acidic soils of south-facing slopes, somewhat transitional to acidophilous oak woods of unit 41.57. [Quercus petraea] is monodominant in the tree layer or associated with [Quercus polycarpa]; the understorey, almost devoid of a shrub layer, is composed of an admixture of oak forest species and siliceous rock sward elements; [Lembotropis nigricans] ([Cytisus nigricans]), [Veronica officinalis], [Hieracium bauhinii], [Hieracium silvaticum], [Calamagrostis arundinacea], [Anthericum ramosum], [Sedum sexangulare] are frequent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic cinquefoil oak woods
description: Xerothermophile oak woods dominated by [Quercus petraea] or [Quercus robur], of the central Sarmatic regions in Podolia, the central Russian plateaux, Bashkiria and the southern Urals, north of, and along the northern edge of, the Sarmatic wooded steppe zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic thermophilous sessile oak forests
description: Thermophile [Quercus petraea] forests of hills and low mountains of central and southern Romania accompanied by a mixed sub-Mediterranean flora including [Aremonia agrimonoides], [Festuca drymeja], [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria] ([Cynanchum vincetoxicum]), [Ruscus aculeatus], [Carex sylvatica], [Dentaria bulbifera], [Viola reichenbachiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic-pre-Carpathic [Festuca drymeia] oak forests
description: Acidophile [Quercus petraea] forests with an herb layer dominated by [Festuca drymeja], of hills and low mountains of central and southern Romania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic-pre-Carpathic [Aremonia] oak forests
description: Weakly acidophile [Quercus petraea] forests of the southwestern hills and low mountains of Romania, with [Acer campestre], [Sorbus torminalis] in the tree layer, [Crataegus monogyna], [Ligustrum vulgare] in the shrub layer and [Aremonia agrimonoides], [Helleborus odorus], [Ruscus aculeatus], [Sedum cepaea], [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria] ([Cynanchum vincetoxicum]), [Silene viridiflora], [Lychnis coronaria], [Carex sylvatica], [Dentaria bulbifera] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moravian serpentine oak woods
description: Xero-thermophile oak woods of serpentines of the middle Jihlava Valley of southwestern Moravia, dominated by [Quercus petraea] and [Pinus sylvestris] with well developed shrub and field layers; the former comprises, in particular, [Prunus mahaleb] and [Berberis vulgaris], the latter species of thermophilous oak forests and forest edges, species of dry grasslands, in particular, [Carex humilis], [Festuca pallens] and [Koeleria macrantha], serpentinophilous ferns, notably [Asplenium cuneifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tartar maple steppe oak woods
description: Xero-thermophile oak woods constituting the climax woodland element of the Pannonian and Ponto-Sarmatic wooded steppe biome, with a flora richer in southern, Euxinian and Sarmatic elements than that of the cinquefoil oak woods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic steppe oak woods
description: Oak woods of the geographically isolated Pannonic basin wooded steppe zone, separated from the main Ukraino-Russian belt by the Carpathian arc.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic loess steppe oak woods
description: Oak woods on black or brown soils over loess substrates of the Pannonic basin and its hills, dominated by [Quercus cerris], [Quercus pubescens], [Quercus robur] or [Quercus petraea]; the upper part of the well-stratified shrub layer is composed mainly of [Acer tataricum] and [Acer campestre], the herb layer of [Festuca rupicola], [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Melica altissima], [Nepeta pannonica], [Phlomis tuberosa], [Pulmonaria mollissima], [Doronicum hungaricum], [Polygonatum odoratum], [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]). Formerly extending in the entire Pannonic basin, from Hungary and southern Slovakia to the Srijem area of northeastern Croatia and northwestern Serbia and the Deliblat region of northeastern Serbia, these forests have been reduced to a few dozen remnant stands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic alkali steppe oak woods
description: Rare oak woods of the Danube basin lowlands developed in the transition zone between inundation areas and loess plateaux, on soils with a higher water table in spring. [Acer tataricum], growing with great vitality, reaches the second tree layer. Characteristic understorey species are [Carex michelii], [Pulmonaria mollissima], [Doronicum hungaricum] accompanying [Alopecurus pratensis], [Melica altissima], [Festuca rupicola], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Geranium robertianum], [Polygonatum latifolium], [Corydalis bulbosa] ([Corydalis cava]), [Ranunculus ficaria], [Viscaria vulgaris]; tall herbs ([Peucedanum officinale], [Galatella punctata]) and other species ([Artemisia pontica], [Limonium gmelinii i.a.])  penetrate the wood from the bordering grasslands on alkaline soil.  Only a few stands of this community remain, in Hungary and Transsylvania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic sand steppe oak woods
description: Oak woods of sandy substrates of the Pannonic plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic dry sand steppe oak woods
description: Low, open woods of [Quercus robur] on lowland sands with a very low water table, sometimes accompanied by [Acer campestre] and [Pyrus pyraster]. The shrub layer is most commonly of [Acer campestre], [Sambucus nigra], [Ligustrum vulgare] and [Prunus spinosa] and is accompanied by a grassy, xylophilous herb layer including [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Poa angustifolia], [Trifolium alpestre], [Dictamnus albus], [Peucedanum oreoselinum], [Veronica spuria] ssp. [foliosa], [Pulmonaria mollissima]. These woods, restricted to Hungary, have been greatly reduced.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic mesophile sand steppe oak woods
description: Well developed oak woods on lowland sands with a higher spring water table, of Hungary and northwestern Romania. [Quercus robur] is sometimes accompanied by [Quercus cerris], [Fraxinus angustifolia] ssp. [pannonica], [Populus alba], [Populus tremula] and has a rich shrub layer including [Cornus sanguinea], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Corylus avellana], [Euonymus europaeus]. The understorey comprises flood plain elements ([Agropyron caninum], [Rubus tomentosus]); mesophilous species ([Stachys sylvatica], [Salvia glutinosa], [Circaea lutetiana]) and xerophilous elements [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Asparagus officinalis], [Vicia pisiformis], [Geranium sanguineum]. The floristic richness of these woods is jeopardized by a lowering water table.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Voivodinian sand steppe oak woods
description: [Quercus pubescens] woods of dry sands of Deliblat, with [Tilia tomentosa], [Prunus mahaleb], [Fraxinus ornus], [Acer campestre], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Crataegus monogyna], [Thalictrum minus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moravian sand steppe oak woods
description: Tall, open woods of [Quercus robur] developed on siliceous sands of southern Moravia deposited over calcareous clays and with base-rich ground water, with a sparse shrub layer and species-rich field layer that includes thermophilous oak forest and forest-edge species, species of intermittently wet soils, species of mesophile grasslands and acidophilous species of mesic or xeric habitats, among them [Geranium sanguineum], [Iris variegata], [Trifolium alpestre], [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria], [Molinia caerulea], [Potentilla alba], [Ajuge reptans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Sarmatic steppe oak woods
description: Xero-thermophilous oak woods of the southern wooded steppe zone, extending from northern Bulgaria and eastern Romania through the Ukraine and southern Russia to the Urals and the lower Volga.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic [Acer tataricum]-[Q. pedunculiflora] steppe woods
description: Subcontinental, xerophile-thermophile wooded steppe oak woods on leached chernozem soils of low hills and plains of southern and southeastern Romania and northeastern Bulgaria, with [Quercus pedunculiflora], [Acer tataricum], [Pyrus pyraster] in the tree layer, [Crataegus monogyna], [Ligustrum vulgare] in the shrub layer and [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria] ([Cynanchum vincetoxicum]), [Pulmonaria mollis], [Thalictrum minus], [Fragaria viridis], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Viola hirta], [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]) in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic [Acer tataricum]-[Quercus pubescens] steppe woods
description: Subcontinental, xerophile-thermophile wooded steppe oak woods, on leached chernozem soils, of low hills and plains of eastern and southern Romania, with [Quercus pubescens], [Acer tataricum], [Pyrus pyraster] in the tree layer, [Cotinus coggygria] in the shrub layer and [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Carex michelii], [Thalictrum minus], [Festuca rupicola], [Vicia tenuifolia] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic [Acer tataricum]-[Q. cerris]-[Q. pedunculiflora] steppe woods
description: Subcontinental, xerophile-thermophile woods of [Quercus pedunculiflora], [Quercus cerris], [Acer tataricum], [Pyrus pyraster] on leached chernozem soils of the plains of southern Romania, with [Prunus spinosa], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Crataegus monogyna] in the shrub layer and [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria] ([Cynanchum vincetoxicum]), [Iris variegata], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Fragaria viridis], [Polygonatum latifolium], [Lychnis coronaria] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Acer tataricum]-[Quercus robur] steppe woods
description: Continental xerophile woods of [Quercus robur] and [Acer tataricum] on leached chernozems of low hills of northeastern Romania, with [Acer campestre], [Pyrus pyraster], [Prunus avium] in the tree layer, [Prunus spinosa], [Euonymus europaeus], [Cornus sanguinea], [Prunus fruticosa], [Amygdalus nana] in the shrub layer and [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Viola hirta], [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria] ([Cynanchum vincetoxicum]), [Sedum maximum], [Fragaria viridis] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic [Acer tataricum]-[Q. robur]-[Q. petraea] steppe woods
description: Subcontinental forests of [Quercus robur], [Quercus petraea], [Acer tataricum] on grey soils of north-facing low hills of the wooded steppe region of northeastern Romania, with [Carpinus betulus], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Prunus avium], [Acer campestre], in the tree layer, [Cornus sanguinea], [Euonymus europaeus], [Rhamnus catharticus] in the shrub layer and [Carex pilosa], [Stellaria holostea], [Asarum europaeum], [Mercurialis perennis] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern [Acer tataricum]-[Quercus robur] steppe woods
description: Woods of [Quercus robur], [Tilia cordata], [Malus sylvestris], [Pyrus pyraster] with [Acer tataricum], [Prunus fruticosa], [Prunus spinosa], developed mostly on shady slopes and in humid gorges of the wooded steppe zone of the Ukraine and southern Russia, in particular in the Don region and the Busuluk depression east of the Volga, on marly and loess black earths (chernozems).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Quercus robur] bairaks
description: Ultimate woodland representation at the southern edge of the wooded steppe zone, formed by low, crooked [Quercus robur] occasionally associated with [Acer campestre], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Ulmus minor], covered with lichens and interspersed with thorny bushes, [Prunus spinosa], [Crataegus monogyna], [Rhamnus catharticus], [Rosa spp].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic tartar maple steppe oak woods
description: Xero-thermophile oak woods of the pre-Carpathian hills fringing the lower Danube and Prut basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic [Lithospermum] white oak woods
description: Neutrophile [Quercus pubescens] woods of the sylvosteppic plains and low hills of southern Romania and the Moldova Republic, with [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), and other sub-Mediterranean species, including [Cotinus coggygria], [Achillea coarctata], [Asparagus verticillatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Getic [Prunus mahaleb] white oak woods
description: Neutrophile [Quercus pubescens] woods of Muntenia, with [Prunus mahaleb], [Acer campestre] in the tree layer, [Cornus mas], [Crataegus monogyna], [Ligustrum vulgare] in the shrub layer, [Buglossoides purpurocaerulea] ([Lithospermum purpurocaeruleum]), [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria] ([Cynanchum vincetoxicum]), [Origanum vulgare], [Poa angustifolia] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Euxinian steppe woods
description: Thermophilous oak woods of the wooded steppe zones of northern Crimea and the northern piedmont of the Caucasus, in the transition region from the Euro-Siberian steppes to the Euxinian montane vegetations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian steppe oak woods
description: Xero-thermophile oak woods of the Mediterraneo-steppic transition zone of central and eastern Anatolia and Iran.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Xero-Euxinian oak steppe forests
description: Steppe forests of Anatolia in which dominant trees of Mediterranean affinities are accompanied by mostly Irano-Turanian steppe elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Presteppic [Quercus anatolica] woods
description: [Quercus anatolica]-dominated forests and woods of presteppic regions of Anatolia, under semiarid climate conditions of 300-600 mm annual precipitation, 3 dry months and 2-4 months of snow cover, usually occupying calcareous substrates between 800-900 m and 1100-1300 m; the species cortŠge is rich in leguminous plants, including [Vicia cracca] ssp. [stenophylla], [Trifolium panormitanum] ssp. [elongatum], [Coronilla varia], [Lathyrus digitalis], typically with [Pyrus elaeagnifolia], [Colutea cilicia], [Jasminum fruticans], [Paliurus australis], [Falcaria rivini], and frequently infiltrated by spiny [Astragalus] steppe elements; on compacted andesites, notably north and northeast of Ankara, the oaks are accompanied by [Viburnum lantana], [Trifolium medium], [Primula vulgaris], [Fragaria vesca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Anatolian steppe oak woods
description: Oak forests and woods of the presteppic periphery of the Anatolian plateau, mostly characteristic of the southern piedmont of the Anti-Taurus, with representatives in the central Pontic valleys, developed under semiarid climate conditions of 5-7 dry, cool or cold months, characterized by submediterranean elements, including [Quercus calliprinos], [Arbutus andrachne], [Rhamnus graecus], [Rhamnus alaternus], [Jasminum fruticans], [Rhus coraria], [Asparagus aphyllus], [Juniperus oxycedrus]; in the great interior valleys [Juniperus excelsa] and [Juniperus foetidissima] play an important role, associating with [Quercus syspirensis], [Pistacia atlantica], [Crataegus orientalis] in the interior valleys of the Pontic range, or with [Pinus brutia] in the Taurus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian [Quercus pedunculiflora] steppe woods
description: Very open steppe woods of Inner Anatolia, limited to altitudes between 700-800 m and about 2000 m, strongly affected by human action, formed of often stunted, widely spaced [Quercus pedunculiflora], with, among others, notably in the Ankara area, [Celtis australis], [Crataegus lacinata], [Prunus spinosa], [Prunus divaricata], [Amygdalus balansae], [Pyrus elaeagrifolia], [Pyrus boissieriana], [Colutea cilicica], [Ephedra major], [Astragalus oleifolius], [Agropyron cristatum], [Agropyron divaricatum], [Melica cupani], [Rosa canina], [Acantholimon acerosum], [Asparagus verticillatum], [Thymus squarrosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tauro-Zagrosian oak steppe forests
description: Steppe forests of the eastern Taurus system of east central and eastern Anatolia, of the Zagros and of neighbouring regions, dominated by oaks of Irano-Turanian affinities, [Quercus brantii], [Quercus boissieri], [Quercus libani].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Anatolian steppe oak woods
description: Steppe woods of central eastern Anatolia formed of [Quercus brantii] associated with [Quercus libani] and [Quercus boissieri] with [Cotoneaster racemiflora], [Sorbus umbellata], [Crataegus arnica], [Cerasus microcarpus], [Paliurus spina-christi], various [Juniperus spp.] and an herb layer rich in steppe species, subjected to a cold semiarid climate with 3-5 months of snow cover and 500-700 mm precipitation, on limestone or volcanic, usually very eroded, substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Anatolian steppe oak woods
description: Very open, residual, woods of southeastern Anatolia and northern Iraq, subjected to cold semiarid climate conditions with 3-5 months of snow cover and 500-700 mm precipitation, occupying limestone or volcanic, usually very eroded, substrates, formed of [Quercus brantii], [Quercus iberica] and, locally, [Pistacia atlantica] occupying steppes rich in Irano-Turanian elements, including [Astragalus spp.], [Cousinia sp.], [Phlomis sp.] and gramineous species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Zagros steppe oak woods
description: Steppe woods of the Zagros dominated by [Quercus brantii], [Quercus boissieri] or [Quercus libani] with [Acer cinerascens], [Amygdalus communis], [Amygdalus orientalis], [Amygdalus horrida], [Amygdalus kotschyi], [Amygdalus reuteri], [Amygdalus salicifolia], [Amygdalus arabica], [Pyrus cordata], [Pyrus syriaca], [Prunus mahaleb], [Prunus microcarpa], [Cotoneaster racemiflora],  [Crataegus aronia], [Crataegus ambigua], [Crataegus monogyna], [Cerasus microcarpus], [Pistacia atlantica], [Pistacia khinjuk], [Paliurus spina-christi], [Rhamnus kurdicus], [Celtis caucasica], [Berberis intergerrima], [Colutea persica], [Daphnae angustifolia], [Lonicera arborea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mixed thermophilous forests
description: Nonalluvial deciduous or semideciduous forests or woods of submediterranean climate regions and supramediterranean altitudinal levels, and of western Eurasian steppe and substeppe zones, dominated by [Ostrya carpinifolia], [Carpinus orientalis], [Acer spp.], [Fraxinus spp.], [Tilia spp.] or [Celtis australis]; like the thermophilous oak woods of unit 41.7, they may, under local microclimatic or edaphic conditions, replace the evergreen oak forests in mesomediterranean or thermomediterranean areas, and irradiate far north into medio-European or sub-Atlantic regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hop-hornbeam woods
description: Forests or woods of submediterranean, sometimes mesomediterranean, climate regions and supramediterranean altitudinal levels dominated by [Ostrya carpinifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesomediterranean Gallo-Italic hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated ravine forests of the mesomediterranean [Quercus ilex] zone of the Maritime and Ligurian Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supramediterranean hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the supramediterranean zone of the Maritime and Ligurian Alps, the Mediterranean and Adriatic slope of the southeastern Alps, the Dinarides, the Hellenides, the Apennines and the large central Mediterranean islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Alpine supramediterranean hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the supramediterranean zone of the Maritime and Ligurian Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Alpine supramediterranean hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the supramediterranean zone of the Mediterranean and Adriatic slope of the southeastern Alps, in the Gardesano- Dolomitic and Veneto-Julian sectors of Italy and extreme northwestern Slovenia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Adriatic supramediterranean hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the supramediterranean [Ostryo-Carpinion orientalis] zone of the Adriatic region of the western Balkan peninsula and of Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine supramediterranean hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the supramediterranean zone of the northern and central Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican supramediterranean hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the supramediterranean zone of Corsica, limited to the northeastern part of the island.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Tyrrhenian supramediterranean hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the supramediterranean zone of the southern Appenines, Sardinia and Sicily.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the montane [Fagion medio-europaeum], [Fagion illyricum], [Fagion moesiacum], [Fagion dacicum], [Fagion hellenicum],   developed at the upper limit of the altitudinal range of the forests of units 41.812 or 41.814, with an accompanying flora usually formed by a combination of beech forest and thermophilous oak forest species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated woods of the [Carpinion illyricum] zone of the Sava and Drava basin, with irradiations into the southeastern Alps, in particular, in the Karawanken and in the eastern Dinarides, extending from southern Austria to Bosnia-Herzegovina.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian white oak hop-hornbeam woods
description: Mostly low woods of sunny, shallow-soil limestone and dolomite slopes of the [Carpinion illyricum] zone of northern Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia, dominated  by [Ostrya carpinifolia], facies of the [Querco-Ostryetum carpinifoliae] hop-hornbeam oak woods of unit 41.73751.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian spring heath hop-hornbeam woods
description: [Ostrya carpinifolia] woods of generally steep dolomite or limestone slopes and screes of the [Carpinion illyricum] region of Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, extending north to Austria in the Drava basin, the Karawanken and, very locally, the middle Inn Valley, with [Fraxinus ornus], [Sorbus aria], [Acer obtusatum], a rich shrub layer formed by [Viburnum lantana], [Juniperus communis], [Berberis vulgaris], [Rosa spp.], [Amelanchier ovalis], [Clematis vitalba] and an herb layer dominated by [Sesleria albicans] and [Carex humilis] on rocky slopes, by [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]) on scree slopes; [Helleborus niger] ssp. [macranthus] is often abundant and [Daphne blagayana] is notable in some stands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian hop-hornbeam woods
description: Uncommon [Ostrya carpinifolia]-dominated facies of thermophilous woods of the Taurus, the Amanus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oriental hornbeam woods
description: [Carpinus orientalis]-dominated facies of the thermophilous woods of units 41.73, 41.74, 41.76, particulary abundant in Greece, the middle Balkan peninsula, Anatolia and the Caucasus. Often of secondary nature, they replace oak forests on eroded soil after deforestation, especially on calcareous soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Illyrian oriental hornbeam woods
description: Thermophilous [Carpinus orientalis]-dominated woods of the [Carpinion betuli illyricum] and [Fagion illyricum] regions of northern and central Bosnia-Herzegovina, where they occupy sunny calcareous slopes, and of the Sava-Drava interfluve hills, between the Papuk Range and the Fruska Gora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic oriental hornbeam woods
description: [Carpinus orientalis]-dominated facies of thermophilous woods of the Balkan peninsula, south to Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Pelagonide oriental hornbeam woods
description: Low woods of northern Greece, Albania, the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and southwestern Bulgaria, including the northern and eastern foothills of the Rhodopes, dominated by [Carpinus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian oriental hornbeam woods
description: Low woods of Serbia and central Bulgaria, in particular, the foothills of the Balkan Range, dominated by [Carpinus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lilac oriental hornbeam woods
description: Low woods of eastern Serbia, western Bulgaria and the Banat, Oltenia and Muntenia in southwestern Romania, dominated by [Carpinus orientalis], rich in [Syringa vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oryzopsis oriental hornbeam woods
description: Low woods of northern Bulgaria, the Banat and Oltenia, dominated by [Carpinus orientalis], with [Fraxinus ornus], [Cotinus coggygria], [Oryzopsis holciformis], [Oxytropis virescens], [Stachys leucoglossa], [Paeonia peregrina], [Salvia ringens], [Cornus mas], [Quercus pubescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Adriatic oriental hornbeam woods
description: Woods of the [Ostryo-Carpinion orientalis] region of the western Balkan peninsula, developed in the supramediterranean level of the Triestine Riviera, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Montenegro, northern Albania, dominated by [Carpinus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolio-Caucasian oriental hornbeam woods
description: [Carpinus orientalis]-dominated facies of thermophilous woods of the Caucasus, the foothills of the Pontic Range, the Taurus, the Amanus and Alaouites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermophilous maple woods
description: Supra-Mediterranean thermophilous woods dominated by [Acer spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Andalusian [Acer granatense] woods
description: Supra-Mediterranean formations of the mountains of the upper Guadalquivir, with [Acer granatense], [Acer monspessulanum], [Quercus faginea], [Quercus pyrenaica], [Sorbus aria], [Sorbus torminalis], [Taxus baccata], [Daphne laureola], [Paeonia officinalis] ssp. [humilis]. Vestiges of this type of vegetation also survive in the Serrania de Ronda.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balearic [Acer granatense] woods
description: Formations, extremely rare if not extinct, of the mountains of Majorca (Puig de Ma‡anella, Puig Major), dominated by [Acer granatense], with [Quercus faginea], [Amelanchier ovalis] ssp. [comafredensis], [Ilex aquifolium] var. [balearica], [Helleborus foetidus] var. [balearicus], [Sorbus aria], [Primula acaulis] var. [balearica], [Rubus ulmifolius], [Tamus communis], [Taxus baccata], [Hedera helix], [Smilax aspera] var. [balearica], [Paeonia cambessedesii], several of which are relict endemic taxa of very limited distribution and low numbers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African [Acer monspessulanum] forests
description: Low (eight metres tall) [Acer monspessulanum]-dominated forest of the Djebel Zaghouan in the Tunisian Dorsale, with a dominated stratum of [Quercus ilex].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian thermophilous maple woods
description: Low [Acer monspessulanum]- or [Acer campestre]-dominated woods of the xerothermic oak belt of the Balkan peninsula, in Albania, the western F.Y.R. of Macedonia, southern Serbia and western and southern Bulgaria, in particular, of the northeastern Rhodope foothills and the northwestern Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermophilous lime woods
description: Supra-, sub- or mesomediterranean and Euro-Siberian steppe woods dominated by [Tilia spp.], for the most part, supra-, meso- or sub-Mediterranean [Tilia spp.] -dominated facies of the thermophilous woods of units 41.73, 41.74, 41.76, 41.7A.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Silver lime woods
description: [Tilia tomentosa]-dominated facies of mixed deciduous forests of southern Central Europe and the northern and middle part of the Balkan peninsula, mostly within the [Quercion frainetto] environment, but also locally developed in conjunction with eastern [Carpinion betuli] forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian silver lime woods
description: [Tilia tomentosa]-dominated facies of mixed deciduous forests of Moesian hills of the Balkan peninsula, in particular, [Tilia tomentosa] woods of the sub-Mediterranean hornbeam-durmast oak belt of Bulgaria and Northern Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Silver lime-hornbeam woods
description: [Tilia tomentosa] lime forests of the plains of Muntenia, near Bucharest, evolution stages of mixed forests of [Quercus robur] ([Quercus petraea]), [Carpinus betulus], [Tilia tomentosa], [Fraxinus spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Voivodinian sand steppe lime woods
description: [Tilia tomentosa] steppe woods of Pannonic affinities developed on dry sands of Deliblat, with [Quercus robur], [Prunus mahaleb], [Fraxinus ornus], [Acer campestre], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Crataegus monogyna], [Viburnum lantanum], [Lonicera xylosteum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Pannonic steppe ash-lime woods
description: Loosely closed forests mainly of [Tilia platyphyllos] and [Fraxinus excelsior] developed on shallow soils of exposed crests of limestone mountains (more rarely on andesite rocks) of the Northern Hungarian Range, with an herb layer of [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Galium erectum], [Cruciata glabra], [Digitalis grandiflora], [Erysimum odoratum], [Sisymbrium strictissimum], [Aconitum anthora], accompanied by endemics among which [Hesperis vrabelyiana], [Carduus collinus] and by other regionally rare species with disjunct distribution, such as [Waldsteinia geoides], [Melica altissima], [Carex brevicollis]. They constitute relict forests, most probably of the Boreal era, and are of great biological value.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nettle-tree woods
description: Thermophilous woods dominated by, or rich in, [Celtis australis]. Forests dominated by [Celtis australis] may have been an important component of Mediterranean woodland, in particular in North Africa, but appear to have been destroyed almost everywhere and to be represented only by individual trees and small stands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermophilous ash woods
description: Nonalluvial, non-ravine meso-, supra- or sub-Mediterranean thermophilous woods dominated by [Fraxinus angustifolia] or [Fraxinus ornus], often mixed with [Quercus pubescens] or [Quercus pyrenaica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sicilian narrow-leaved ash woods
description: [Fraxinus angustifolia] woods of western Sicily.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian narrow-leaved ash woods
description: [Fraxinus angustifolia] woods of the Iberian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Manna tree woods
description: Thermophilous [Fraxinus ornus] woods, characteristic, in particular, of the Banat hills and the pre-Balkanic plateaux and hills of the lower Danube basin, dominated by [Fraxinus ornus] with [Cornus sanguinea], [Tilia platyphyllos], [Tilia tomentosa], [Ulmus minor], [Carpinus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African ash woods
description: [Fraxinus dimorpha] woods of the Aures where they mostly occur in a narrow belt between [Quercus rotundifolia] and [Cedrus atlantica] forests, and of the Tunisian Dorsale where they are limited to higher slopes at around 1300 m, near Maktar.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic juniper-poplar steppe woods
description: [Populus alba] woods of sands, in particular sand dunes, of the Danube-Tisza confluence of the Pannonic plain. The shrub layer includes [Juniperus communis], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Rhamnus catharticus], [Crataegus monogyna], [Prunus spinosa], [Prunus mahaleb], [Rubus caesius], [Euonymus verrucosus], [Berberis vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic privet juniper-poplar steppe woods
description: Closed [Populus alba] forests of the Pannonian Danube-Tisza interfluvial region with a species-rich and strongly developed shrub layer and an herb layer comprising [Lithospermum officinale], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Asparagus officinalis], [Vincetoxicum hirundinaria], [Polygonatum odoratum], [Poa angustifolia], [Euphorbia cyparissias], [Poa pratensis], [Senecio integrifolius], [Silene nutans], [Verbascum lychnitis] and [Solanum dulcamara] var. [pusztarum], frequently with the mosses [Dicranum scoparium] and [Hypnum cupressiforme].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic sedge juniper-poplar steppe woods
