description: [Populus alba] woods of the Pannonian Danube-Tisza interfluvial region with an herb layer dominated by [Carex liparocarpos], accompanied by [Potentilla arenaria], [Thesium ramosum], [Viola rupestris] var. [arenaria], [Galium verum], [Lithospermum officinale], [Medicago falcata], [Phleum phleoides], [Pimpinella saxifraga], [Calamagrostis epigejos], [Taraxacum officinale], [Colchicum arenarium], [Iris humilis] ssp. [arenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic gypsophila juniper-poplar steppe woods
description: [Populus alba] woods of the Pannonian Danube-Tisza interfluvial region with an herb layer formed by [Gypsophila fastigiata] ssp. [arenaria], [Stipa capillata], [Ephedra distachya], [Alkanna tinctoria], [Potentilla arenaria], [Scabiosa ochroleuca] and sometimes stands of [Calamagrostis epigejos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Mediterranean and Pannonic mixed woods
description: Nonalluvial deciduous or semideciduous thermophilous forests or woods of submediterranean or supramediterranean regions of the Mediterranean basin, and of the Pannonic plain, formed by [Tilia spp.], [Fraxinus spp.], [Quercus spp.], [Carpinus spp.], [Ostrya carpinifolia], [Acer spp.], [Sorbus spp.], [Populus spp.], [Celtis australis] and occasionally, [Fagus spp.], in varied combinations and dominance.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Mediterranean mixed woods
description: Mixed woods of [Tilia spp.], [Fraxinus spp.], [Quercus spp.], [Carpinus spp.], [Ostrya carpinifolia], [Sorbus spp.], [Populus spp.] and occasionally, [Fagus spp.] of the Mediterranean, supra-Mediterranean and sub-Mediterranean [Quercion pubescenti-petraeae], [Ostryo-Carpinion] and [Quercion frainetto] zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic mixed karstic woods
description: Mixed woods of dolomitic substrates of the periphery and hills of the Pannonic plain, in Hungary, southern Slovakia and Croatia, characterized by the juxtaposition of beech wood and thermophile oak wood species, rich in relict species of disjunct distribution such as [Calamagrostis varia], [Allium victorialis], [Rubus saxatilis], [Primula auricula] ssp. [hungarica], and therefore of great biogeographical significance.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian mixed steppe woods
description: Varied steppe forests or woods of submediterranean climate regions and supramediterranean altitudinal levels of western and central Asian steppe and substeppe zones, including eastern Anatolia, Iran, Syria and Afghanistan, the western Himalayan systems and adjacent regions, and semiarid zones of mediterranean North Africa, formed of fruit or nut-bearing trees, including [Pistacia spp.], [Amygdalus spp.], [Malus spp.], [Pyrus spp.], [Prunus spp.], [Juglans regia] and often with [Acer spp.], [Rosa spp.], [Crataegus spp.], [Ulmus spp.], [Celtis caucasia], [Vitis hissarica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian wild fruit tree steppe woods
description: Usually open or very open stands of [Pistacia spp.], [Amygdalus spp.], [Malus spp.], [Pyrus spp.], [Prunus spp.], [Juglans regia] and other fruit or nut-bearing trees, often associated with [Acer spp.], [Rosa spp.], [Crataegus spp.], of the steppes and subdesert fringes of eastern Anatolia, Iran, Syria and Afghanistan, with a probable outpost in the central plains of Cyprus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian almond-terebinth steppe woods
description: Mixed open or very open stands of [Pistacia atlantica], [Amygdalus orientalis], and other arborescent or shrubby Rosaceae of genera [Amygdalus], [Malus], [Pyrus], [Prunus], [Rosa], [Crataegus], with [Juglans regia], [Acer spp.], of the steppes and subdesert fringes of eastern Anatolia, Iran, Afghanistan, Syria and the Levant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian terebinth steppe woods
description: Mixed open or very open stands of [Pistacia atlantica], accompanied by shrubby Rosaceae of genera [Amygdalus], [Malus], [Pyrus], [Prunus], [Rosa], [Crataegus], by [Juglans regia], or by [Acer spp.], of the steppes and subdesert fringes of western Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian almond-pear steppe woods
description: Mixed open or very open stands of [Amygdalus orientalis], or other arborescent Rosaceae of genera [Amygdalus] and [Pyrus], of the steppes and subdesert fringes of western Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian terebinth steppe woods
description: Open or very open stands of [Pistacia atlantica], [Ziziphus lotus], [Noaea mucronata], [Amygdalus communis], [Crataegus aronia], [Pyrus syriaca], associated with batha shrubs, of the semisteppic central plain of Cyprus, possible relict of a former climax community.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian deciduous steppe forests
description: Broad-leaved deciduous woodland formations of the slopes of the Tien Shan, Pamir-Alai and western Himalayan systems, and of neighbouring hills and plateaux, with [Juglans regia], [Acer spp.], [Ulmus spp.], [Malus siviersii], [Celtis caucasia], [Prunus spp.], [Amygdalus spp.], [Pistacia vera], [Vitis hissarica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tien Shan maple-elm-walnut woods
description: Formations of [Acer spp.], [Ulmus spp.], [Juglans regia] of humid slopes and gorges of the arid western Tien Shan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pamir-Alai mixed maple woods
description: [Acer turkestanicum], [Acer pubescens], [Juglans regia], [Vitis hissarica] formations of the higher levels of the Pamir-Alai.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian walnut woods
description: [Juglans regia]-dominated semi-humid forests of the Central Asian mountains, in particular of the western and central Tien-Schan, mostly developed in the 1500-2000 m level.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian wild fruit woods
description: Formations of [Malus sieversii], [Prunus spp.], [Amygdalus spp.], [Pyrus spp.], with [Elaeagnus spp.], [Sorbus spp.], [Pistacia vera], [Punica granatum] and other wild fruit trees of the Central Asian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian pistachio steppe woods
description: [Pistacia vera]-dominated formations of the slopes of the Kopet Dagh, and of the Pamir-Alai and Tien Shan systems, and of neighbouring plateaux and hills of northeastern Iran, Afghanistan, Tadzhikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Kirgizia and Kazakhstan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African [Pistacia atlantica] steppe woods
description: [Pistacia atlantica]-dominated formations of the semiarid level of Mediterranean North Africa, perhaps formerly constituting steppe forests similar to those of Western Asia, now apparently extinct in that form and represented only by individual trees or stands of the terebinth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Mediterranean chasm woods
description: Brushy liana-rich woods of deep ravines of Crete, formed by [Ficus carica], [Pistacia terebinthus], [Celtis tournefortii], [Cotinus coggygria], [Rhus coriaria], [Amelanchier ovalis] ssp. [cretica], [Sorbus aria] ssp. [cretica], [Sorbus umbellata], restricted to a few calcareous cliffs. They appear to have affinities with the Irano-Turanian steppe woods of unit 41.89 and with the southern Palaearctic ravine and valley tropical dry woodland of units 4B.4 and 4B.5.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chestnut woods
description: Supramediterranean and submediterranean [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and old established plantations with seminatural undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of the [Quercion frainetto] zone of the Balkan peninsula, of northern Greece, including the Chalkidike peninsula, with irradiations in the [Ostryo-Carpinion orientalis aegeicum] zone. They appear to represent the main area of indigenousness of the species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of the Peloponnese, the Aegean islands, Crete and western Asia Minor, occupying scattered, relatively rare localities in the supramediterranean level of mountains ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Adriatic chestnut forests
description: Submediterranean [Castanea sativa]-dominated acidophilous forests of the [Ostryo-Carpinion orientalis adriaticum] zone of the Balkan peninsula, distributed, in particular, in the Slovenian coastal mountains, in Istria, on the islands of Krk and Cres, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Montenegro, within an area of undoubted indigenousness of the species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Adriatic heath chestnut forests
description: Submediterranean [Castanea sativa] forests of the northwestern Balkan peninsula rich in [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]), recorded, in particular, from the coastal mountains of Slovenia, where accompanying trees include [Quercus petraea], [Quercus cerris], [Quercus pubescens], [Pinus nigra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Adriatic broom chestnut forests
description: Submediterranean [Castanea sativa] forests of the northwestern Balkan peninsula rich in brooms, including [Genista pilosa], [Genista germanica], [Genista tinctoria], [Chamaespartium sagittale], recorded, in particular, from the coastal mountains of Slovenia, where accompanying trees include [Quercus petraea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Adriatic alder chestnut forests
description: Submediterranean [Castanea sativa] forests of humid flysch substrates of the northwestern Balkan peninsula rich in [Alnus glutinosa], with a very limited distribution in the coastal mountains of Slovenia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of the [Carpinion betuli illyricum] zone, locally, notably in Bosnia-Herzegovina, extending into the [Fagion illyricum] zone, apparently constituting, with the subthermophilous oak region of the Balkans, a center of indigenousness of the species. Extensive stands are recorded, in particular, from northwestern Croatia, neighbouring Slovenia, northern, central and eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Liguro-Insubrian chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of the collinar level of the southern slope of the Alps of Italy and southern Switzerland, with a cortŠge characteristic of medio-European acidophilous oak forests; resulting from ancient introductions, they are particularly abundant  on the margins of the Piedmont plains, where they constitute, in some valleys, an almost continuous forest mantle, extending up to 800 m, sometimes 1000 m, and in the Insubrian region. They occur more sparsely west to the Ligurian Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italo-Sicilian chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of the supramediterranean zone of the Apennines, of lesser hill ranges of the Italian peninsula and of Sicily, at the 200-800 m level and mostly on siliceous soils, for the most part resulting from ancient introductions, probably indigenous in some areas, in particular, Etna and the Euganean hills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyrno-Sardinian chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of Corsica and Sardinia, where they may be indigenous and are fairly widespread, particularly in the San Petrone massif of Corsica and in eastern central Sardinia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Galloprovincial chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of southeastern France, in particular, of the Maures, the C‚vennes and the eastern Pyrenees, where they may be, in part, indigenous and are characteristic of the supramediterranean level, with a cortŠge of acidophilous [Quercion pubescenti-petraeae] forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gallo-Iberian chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of the Iberian peninsula, southwestern and central France, probably entirely resulting from ancient introductions, common in northwestern Iberia, in Catalonia, in the mountains of central and western Iberia, in Andalucia and, mostly as substitutes of southwestern Atlantic medio-European oak forests in the northwestern piedmont of the Pyrenees and southwestern France, fairly rare in the rest of the Iberian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxinian chestnut forests
description: [Castanea sativa]-dominated forests and naturalized plantations of the foothills and piedmont of the Pontic Range and the Caucasus, characteristic, in particular, of the 100-1100 m level of the Colchidian hills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hornbeam forests
description: Woods of the western Palaearctic region dominated by [Carpinus betulus], alone or with a small admixture of other species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western hornbeam woods
description: Woods of Western Europe and northern and central Central Europe, north to southern Denmark, Bornholm and southeastern Sweden, within the range of the [Fagion medio-europaeum] and the [Carpinion betuli], dominated by [Carpinus betulus], alone or with a small admixture of other species, uncommon, generally low, habitually secondary. Scandinavian stands, characteristic of diabases, basalts and greenstones, often dominated by tall [Carpinus betula], have a field layer dominated by abundant [Anemone nemorosa], [Stellaria nemorum] and [Hedera helix].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern hornbeam forests
description: Forests of southeastern Central Europe and of Eastern Europe, within the range of the [Carpinion illyricum], of the [Fagion moesiacum] and of the [Fagion dacicum], as well as of areas east of the range of [Fagus sylvatica], dominated by [Carpinus betulus], alone or with a small admixture of other species, more widespread and developed than those of unit 41.A1, sometimes primary.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian hornbeam forests
description: Forests of southeastern Central Europe, within the range of the [Carpinion illyricum], dominated by [Carpinus betulus], alone or with a small admixture of other species, in particular [Carpinus betulus]-dominated communities of the Carinthian [Helleboro nigri-Carpinetum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacio-Moesian hornbeam forests
description: Neutrophile or weakly acidophile forests of southeastern Central Europe, within the range of the [Fagion moesiacum], the [Fagion dacicum] and, locally, of the [Quercion frainetto], dominated by [Carpinus betulus], alone or with a small admixture of other species, with [Carpinion] species in the herb layer; they occur in various conditions on hills and in plains, as substitution for mixed forests of [Quercus robur] or [Quercus petraea], [Carpinus betulus], [Tilia spp.], [Fraxinus excelsior].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic hornbeam forests
description: Forests of Eastern Europe, east of the range of [Fagus sylvatica], dominated by [Carpinus betulus], alone or with a small admixture of other species, in particular, [Carpinus betulus] forests of the Podolian plateaux.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of the western Palaearctic region dominated by [Betula pendula], [Betula pubescens], their allies, or other arborescent [Betula spp.], on nonmarshy terrain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic lowland and collinar birch woods
description: Pioneer and subclimax [Betula pendula] or [Betula pubescens] formations of the North Sea-Baltic plains, the lower Hercynian slopes, the periphery of the Paris Basin, southwestern France, northwestern Iberia, Insubria and Illyria, within the range of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic acidophilous oak woods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Humid birch woods
description: Formations usually formed by [Betula pubescens], with [Molinia caerulea] and sometimes [Deschampsia flexuosa], developed on podzolized or hydromorphic soils, as substitution facies of oak and birch woods, or colonization stages, in particular, of [Molinion] grasslands or humid heaths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern humid birch woods
description: Widespread [Betula pendula]-dominated formations characteristic of the North Sea-Baltic plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aquitano-Ligerian humid birch woods
description: Southern [Betula pendula] formations common, in particular, in the Sologne and neighbouring areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Medio-European dry acidophilous birch woods
description: Formations usually formed by [Betula pendula], or, in the British Isles, [Betula pubescens], with [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Agrostis capillaris] ([Agrostis tenuis]), [Festuca ovina], [Vaccinium myrtillus], developed notably on sands, gravels, moraines and decalcified alluvions of nemoral northern and middle European plains and hills, as substitution facies of acidophilous oak woods ([Fago-Quercetum], [Blechno-Quercetum petraeae], [Rusco-Quercetum], [Luzulo-Quercetum]), occasionally of oak-hornbeam woods (particularly mixed Atlantic bluebell oak forests, [Endymio-Carpinetum]), or colonization stages of dry heaths and decalcified dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian acidophilous birch woods
description: Medio-European acidophilous birch woods of the collinar and lower montane levels of northwestern Iberia, formed by [Betula pendula] or [Betula celtiberica] as substitution stages of acidophilous oak woods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Insubrian acidophilous birch woods
description: Birch woods of the collinar and lower montane levels of northern Italy, dispersed in the Alpine foothills where they constitute substitution stages of the Insubrian acidophilous oak woods ([Castaneo-Quercetum] [p.]), on the fluvioglacial terraces of the Po system, as facies of the acidophilous pine-birch-oak woods, and in the Euganean hills.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Heavy-metal birch woods
description: Subclimax birch woods occupying soils intoxicated by heavy metals, with an herb layer that may include metallophytes and habitually calciphile species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dune birch woods
description: Birch woods formed by [Betula pubescens], [Betula pendula] and [Populus canescens] with [Viola hirta], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Polygonatum odoratum], in calcareous North Sea and Baltic dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian birch woods
description: [Betula pendula]-dominated woods of the basins of the Drava and Sava in Slovenia, Croatia, northern Bosnia-Herzegovina and of neighbouring regions, in part birch facies of the acidophilous [Betula pendula]-[Quercus petraea] forests of unit 41.5734, in part pioneer formations in forest clearings and other recolonization areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British sub-boreal birch woods
description: Birch woods, often extensive and pure, formed by [Betula pubescens] ([Betula odorata], [Betula carpatica]) or [Betula pendula], beyond and above the present range of oak woods in Scotland and northern England.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynio-Alpine birch woods
description: Birch stands of the montane and subalpine levels of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Apennines, the Pyrenees, the Jura, the Hercynian ranges and the mountains of the Balkan peninsula, mostly subclimax formations of stations with anomalous edaphic and microclimatic conditions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine timberline birch woods
description: Tree-limit birch stands, of local distribution in the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Birch block forests
description: Birch stands, mostly of [Betula pubescens] ([Betula carpatica], [Betula tortuosa]), occupying, in the Alps, the Jura and the Hercynian ranges, cold stations on cliff-base rocky screes and boulder-falls through which cold air flows.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean birch woods
description: Birch-dominated formations of the Pyrenees, locally frequent in all vegetation levels.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine birch woods
description: Isolated birch stations of the Apennines, in the Abruzzi, bosco di Manziana (Latium), monti Alburni, monti Picentini.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyro-Moesian montane birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] stands of the montane and subalpine levels of mountains of the Balkan Peninsula, including the Balkan Range, the Rhodopides, the Dinarides and the northwestern Hellenides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkano-Rhodopide birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] stands of the montane and subalpine levels of the Balkan Range and the Rhodopides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] stands of the Rhodopide mountains, substitution facies of [Fagus sylvestris], [Abies alba], [Picea abies] and [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the upper beech-fir levels of the Rhodopes, Rila, Pirin and Vitosha of Bulgaria, with isolated outposts in the southern Rhodopes of northern Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] woods of the montane and subalpine levels of the Balkan Range, substitution and recolonisation facies of [Fagus sylvestris], [Abies alba], [Picea abies] and [Pinus sylvestris] forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaro-Pelagonide birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] stands of the montane and subalpine levels of mountains of the western Balkan Peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] woods of montane level of the eastern Carpathian system forming as pioneer stands in felled areas of spruce, beech and mixed beech-fir and beech-fir-spruce forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian rowan birch woods
description: [Betula pendula]-dominated woods of the upper montane level of the Southern Carpathians and the Eastern Carpathians, on superficial brown acid soils of steep slopes in the zone of mixed spruce forests, rich in [Sorbus aucuparia] and accompanied by [Picea abies], [Oxalis acetosella], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Pulmonaria rubra], [Salix silesiaca], [Calamagrostis arundinacea] and some [Fagetalia] species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian aspen birch woods
description: [Betula pendula]-dominated woods situated on sandy brown weathered soils of steep slopes and hilltops of the lower montane level of the Apuseni mountains, in particular of the Plopis and Gilau mountains, with [Populus tremula] and representatives of the [Epilobion angustifolii], and of the [Fagetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intra-Carpathian dune oak-birch woods
description: Woods dominated by [Betula pendula] accompanied by [Quercus robur] with psammophyllous species in the herb layer, characteristic of the inland dunes of the eastern rim of the eastern intra-Carpathian basin of Romania, in the region of St. Gheorghe, at Reci in the Kovasna district.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] formations of the upper montane level of Corsica, forming extensive subclimax belts on rocky, rapidly eroding soils at the upper forest limit, as well as transition communities in the evolution of laricio pine or beech forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane [Betula celtiberica] woodlands
description: Formations of the upper montane and supra-Mediterranean levels of Iberia dominated by the endemic [Betula celtiberica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cantabrian [Betula celtiberica] woodlands
description: Climax tree-limit [Betula celtiberica] woods of the Cantabrian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western [Betula celtiberica] woodlands
description: Upper montane and supra-Mediterranean climax formations of the western Cordillera Central (Serra da Estrela) and the Orensano-Sanabrian mountains, limited to tree-limit situations and humid ravines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sorian and Guadarraman [Betula celtiberica] woodlands
description: Humid supra-Mediterranean climax formations of the eastern Cordillera Central (Guadarrama) and of the Northern Iberian Range (Sorian mountains), restricted to relict stations on rainy ubacs and in humid ravines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mount Etna birch stands
description: Endemic [Betula aetnensis] formations of Mount Etna lavas, limited to the 1200-2000 metre level, mostly within the 1600-1750 metre range, at northern to eastern exposures. The accompanying cortŠge includes [Adenocarpus complicatus], [Genista aetnensis], [Juniperus hemisphaerica], [Festuca circummediterranea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oroboreal birch woods and thickets
description: Timberline birch woods and thickets dominating the subalpine belt of the mountains of the boreal taiga zone or the transition zone between taiga and tundra or polar deserts in the Atlantic or Pacific influenced extreme western and extreme eastern regions of the northern Palaearctic, formed by [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] ([Betula pubescens] ssp. [tortuosa], [Betula kusmisscheffii]) or [Betula ermani].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic birch woods and thickets
description: Boreal and subarctic [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods and thickets of Iceland, extreme southwestern Greenland and oceanic western Norway, distributed in lowlands, in valleys and at the foot of mountain slopes, in relatively humid, sheltered situations. In Iceland and Greenland they constitute the only form of boreal woodland. Their stature varies with microclimates, dense low scrubs prevailing along the coasts, in wind-exposed localities and in the most oceanic areas, taller brushes and woods forming further inland and in more continental districts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic crowberry-bog bilberry birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of Iceland and western Norway with an ericoid-dominated undergrowth, formed mainly by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], dominant in Iceland, and [Vaccinium uliginosum], dominant in Norway, accompanied by [Calluna vulgaris], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Betula nana], [Deschampsia flexuosa], mosses and, in Iceland, [Juncus trifidus], [Kobresia myosuroides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic crowberry birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of Iceland, with a mostly ericoid undergrowth, dominated by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], accompanied by [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Calluna vulgaris], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Betula nana], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Juncus trifidus], [Kobresia myosuroides], mosses and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Norwegian bog bilberry birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of western Norway, with a mostly ericoid undergrowth dominated by [Vaccinium uliginosum], accompanied by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Calluna vulgaris], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Betula nana], [Deschampsia flexuosa] and mosses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic small fern birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of Iceland and of the oceanic southern boreal and oceanic middle boreal zones of Norway, developed on moist moraine podsols, with a field layer dominated by ferns.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic small fern birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of Iceland, developed on moist moraine podsols, dominated by [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii], with a fern field layer formed predominantly by [Gymnocarpium dryopteris], sometimes accompanied by [Dryopteris assimilis] or [Thelypteris phegopteris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Norwegian small fern birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of the oceanic southern boreal and oceanic middle boreal zones of Norway, developed on moist moraine podsols, with a fern field layer formed predominantly by [Gymnocarpium dryopteris] accompanied by [Dryopteris assimilis], [Thelypteris phegopteris], [Blechnum spicant] or [Dryopteris expansa] and with [Oxalis acetosella], [Lophocolea bidentata], [Rhytidiadelphus loreus], [Rhytidiadelphus triquetrus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic bog bilberry-hairgrass birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of the lowlands of Iceland, occupying thick, relatively rich soils, with a heath-grassland undergrowth dominated by [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Agrostis capillaris], [Deschampsia flexuosa], accompanied by [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Salix callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Salix lanata], [Salix phylicifolia], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Galium verum], [Hierochloe odorata], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Festuca rubra] [s.l.], [Juncus trifida], [Kobresia myosuroides], [Lycopodium annotinum], [Equisetum pratense].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic cranesbill birch woods
description: Herb-rich woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] occupying relatively rich mull sandy moraine soils in climatically favourable regions of western Norway and Iceland, with affinities to the oro-Scandinavian calcicline mountain birch woods of unit 41.B725.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic cranesbill birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of the lowlands of Iceland, characterized by a luxuriant shrub and herb layer rich in [Geranium sylvaticum] and [Rubus saxatile]. They mostly occupy hollows where snow lingers in spring, and are covered with snow in winter. Their species cortŠge may include [Salix spp.], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Populus tremula], [Juniperus communis], [Alchemilla vulgaris], [Campanula rotundifolia], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Fragraria vesca], [Galium verum], [Geum rivale], [Hieracium spp.], [Melampyrum sylvaticum], [Prunella vulgaris], [Trientalis europaea], [Elymus caninus] ([Roegneria canina]), [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Festuca rubra] [s.l.], [Hierochloe odorata], [Poa nemoralis], [Poa pratense], [Coeloglossum viride], [Dactylorhiza islandica], [Carex bigelowii], [Carex vaginata], [Luzula multiflora], [Equisetum arvense], [Equisetum pratense], [Athyrium filix-femina], [Gymnocarpium dryopteris] and mosses. These woods constitute, in their northern area of occurrence, the northernmost, dwarfed (0.5-1 m), stands of birch in Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Norwegian cranesbill birch woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] of rich mull soils in climatically favourable stations of oceanic boreal Norway with a forb-dominated herb layer that includes, among others, [Geranium sylvaticum], [Blechnum spicant], [Cornus suecica], [Thelypteris limbosperma], and a canopy and shrub layer that comprise [Alnus incana], [Populus tremula], [Corylus avellana], [Salix spp.], [Vaccinium spp.], [Juniperus communis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic holy-grass birch woods
description: [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods and thickets of the lowlands of Iceland, with a grass-dominated field layer formed by [Hierochloe odorata], [Agrostis capillaris] ([Agrostis tenuis]), [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Festuca richardsonii], [Deschampsia flexuosa] and accompanied by [Poa pratensis], [Poa nemoralis], [Luzula multiflora], [Carex vaginata], [Equisetum pratense].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic willow birch woods
description: [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods and thickets of moist soils of the lowlands of Iceland, with a willow-dominated undergrowth formed mainly by [Salix phylicifolia] and [Salix lanata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland birch woods
description: Boreal and subarctic [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods and thickets of extreme southwestern Greenland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian birch woods
description: [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods and thickets of the boreo-alpine and arcto-alpine mountains of Fennoscandia, distributed mostly in the subalpine, subfj„ll belt, which they dominate.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian crowberry-lichen birch woods
description: Low (2-3 m) [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods of the subalpine belt of northern, western and inner mountains of Fennoscandia with a lichen-rich ericoid-dominated undergrowth formed by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Phyllodoce caerulea], accompanied by  junipers ([Juniperus nana]), dwarf birch ([Betula nana]), willows ([Salix spp.]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian bilberry-hairgrass birch woods
description: Medium-tall (4-7 m) [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods of sandy moraine podsols of the subalpine belt of the mountains of Fennoscandia, with a moss-rich grass and heath undergrowth formed by [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Empetrum hermaphroditum] and [Deschampsia flexuosa], accompanied by [Dicranum fuscescens], [Dicranum scoparium], [Hylocomium splendens], [Pleurozium schreberi]; their cortŠge includes [Betula nana], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Linnaea borealis], [Pedicularis lapponica], [Solidago virgaurea], [Trientalis europaea], and sparse taller shrubs, in particular, of [Juniperus communis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian bilberry-dwarf cornel birch woods
description: Low to medium tall (to 6 m) [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods of the mountains of Norway and northern Finland, extending from the subalpine belt down, in western Norway, to the fjords, developing in somewhat warmer and wetter areas and occupying thick humus layers on weak podsols of sandy more nutrient-rich moraines than those of units 41.B721 and 41.B722, with an undergrowth dominated by [Cornus suecica], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Deschampsia flexuosa], accompanied by taller shrubs, primarily of [Juniperus communis] and [Salix spp.]; accompanying species include [Linnaea borealis], [Solidago virgaurea], [Trientalis europaea], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Molinia caerulea], [Luzula sylvatica], [Thelypteris limbosperma], [Gymnocarpium dryopteris], [Blechnum spicant], [Dryopteris expansa], [Dicranum scoparium], [Dicranum majus], [Hylocomium splendens], [Pleurozium schreberi], [Cladonia spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian small-fern birch woods
description: [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods of the subalpine belt of Fennoscandian mountains, often with some spruce or pine, and with an understorey dominated by [Gymnocarpium dryopteris]; accompanying species include [Dryopteris assimilis], [Thelypteris phegopteris], [Oxalis acetosella], [Cerriphyllum piliferum], [Hylocomium umbratum], [Lophocolea bidentata], in addition to the cortŠge of the woods of unit 41.B722.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian cranesbill-stone bramble birch woods
description: Tall (10-11 m) woods of [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii], accompanied by [Salix spp.], [Sorbus spp.], of the subalpine belt of mountains of Fennoscandia, occupying relatively rich mull soils of sand moraines in climatically favourable regions, with a low herb-rich undergrowth dominated by [Geranium sylvaticum] and [Rubus saxatilis]. There is an often well developed understorey of taller shrubs, in particular, [Juniperus communis] and [Salix spp.] and a poorly developed moss and lichen layer. The species cortŠge comprises [Campanula rotundifolia], [Alchemilla vulgaris], [Cornus suecica], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Fragraria vesca], [Galium boreale], [Galium verum], [Geum rivale], [Hieracium spp.], [Melampyrum sylvaticum], [Prunella vulgaris], [Poa nemoralis], [Poa pratensis], [Hierochloe odorata], [Agrostis capillaris], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Festuca rubra] [s.l.], [Melica nutans], [Trientalis europaea], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Elymus caninus] ([Roegneria canina]), [Carex bigelowii], [Carex vaginata], [Coeloglossum viride], [Dactylorhiza maculata], [Luzula multiflora], [Gymnocarpium dryopteris], [Athyrium filix-femina], [Equisetum arvense], [Equisetum palustre], [Hylocomium splendens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian tall-herb birch woods
description: Tall (up to 12 m) woods of the subalpine belt of Fennoscandian mountains dominated by [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii], with [Salix spp.], [Sorbus aucuparia], [Prunus padus] and an undergrowth dominated by tall herbs, comprising, together with abundant [Geranium sylvaticum], [Trollius europaeus], [Rubus saxatilis], [Aconitum septentrionale] ([Aconitum licoctonum]), [Cirsium helenioides], [Cicerbita alpina], [Epilobium angustifolium], [Ranunculus platanifolius]. The  well-developed taller shrub understorey is dominated by [Juniperus communis], accompanied by [Salix spp.]; dwarf shrubs are often absent and the moss and lichen layer is very poorly developed; ferns are common. The species cortŠge includes [Alchemilla spp.], [Astragalus alpinus], [Myosotis decumbens], [Paris quadrifolia], [Silene dioica], [Solidago virgaurea], [Stellaria nemorum], [Valeriana sambucifolia], [Vicia biflora], [Milium effusum], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Calamagrostis purpurea], [Anthoxanthum odoratum], [Carex vaginata]. These woods occupy well-drained, mull-rich soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Scandian tall-fern birch woods
description: Tall [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] woods of the subalpine belt of Fennoscandian mountains, occasionally accompanied by [Alnus incana], [Prunus padus], [Salix spp.], with a fern-rich field layer dominated by [Athyrium filix-femina], [Matteuccia struthiopteris], [Dryopteris expansa], accompanied by [Athyrium distentifolium], [Phegopteris connectilis], [Thelypteris limbosperma] and tall herbs; the species cortŠge includes [Aconitum septentrionale] ([Aconitum lycoctonum]), [Solidago virgaurea], [Stellaria nemorum], [Viola biflora], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Geranium sylvestris], [Ribes rubrum], [Rubus idaeus], [Rubus saxatilis], [Calamagrostis purpurea], [Deschampsia cespitosa]; tall-fern hirch woods are developed on sandy moraines with good water supply.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Khibiny birch woods
description: [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] ([Betula pubescens] ssp. [tortuosa], [Betula kusmisscheffii]) woods and thickets of the mountains and tundra timberline of the Kola peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian oroboreal birch woods and thickets
description: Timberline birch woods and thickets of the Urals formed by krumholz [Betula pubescens] [s.l.] ([Betula tortuosa] [s.l.]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern oroboreal birch woods
description: [Betula ermani] or [Betula middendorffii] woods and thickets forming at the timberline of the mountains of eastern Siberia, Kamchatka, Sakhaline and Hokkaido.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Betula ermani] woods and thickets
description: [Betula ermani] woods and thickets forming at the timberline of the mountains of Kamchatka, Sakhaline and Hokkaido.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Betula middendorffii] woods and thickets
description: [Betula middendorffii] woods and thickets forming at the timberline of the mountains of eastern Siberia, in particular the Verkoiansk Range, the Anadyr Range, the mountains of the Ba‹kal area and of Transba‹kalia, the Greater Khingan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eurasian boreal birch woods
description: Birch woods of the taiga belt, of the wooded tundra belt, and of the taiga-nemoral forest transition zone of Eurasia, formed by [Betula pendula], [Betula pubescens] [s.l.] or [Betula platyphylla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Eurasian boreal birch woods
description: Birch woods of the taiga and wooded tundra belts and of the transition zones between taiga and nemoral forests of Fennoscandia, the northern Sarmatic region and western Siberia, formed by [Betula pendula], or, sometimes, [Betula pubescens], with [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Agrostis capillaris], [Festuca ovina], [Trientalis europaea], [Melampyrum pratense], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Juniperus communis], [Rubus idaeus], [Equisetum sylvaticum] and, in some communities, [Cornus suecica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Eurasian boreal birch woods
description: Birch woods of the taiga and wooded tundra belts of eastern Siberia and the eastern Siberian mountains, formed by [Betula platyphylla] or, sometimes, [Betula pendula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian steppe birch woods
description: Open, often parklike, woods of [Betula pendula], [Betula platyphylla] or [Betula pubescens] [s.l.] of the transition zone between steppe and taiga of Siberia, east of the range of the nemoral deciduous forests of the Sarmatic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Siberian [Betula pendula] steppe woods
description: Open, often parklike, woods of [Betula pendula] and [Populus tremula] (listed under 41.D7 when dominated by the latter) of the transition zone between steppe and taiga of Siberia, east of the range of the nemoral deciduous forests of the Sarmatic region. The shrub layer includes [Lonicera altaica], [Lonicera tatarica], [Thelycrania alba] ([Cornus alba]), [Ribes nigrum], [Ribes rubrum], [Spiraea hypericifolia], [Cotoneaster multiflorus]; the meadow-like herb layer is formed by [Agrostis alba], [Calamagrostis arundinacea], [Poa pratensis], [Bromus inermis], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Astragalus danicus], [Campanula bononiensis]].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Siberian [Betula platyphylla] steppe woods
description: Open, often parklike, woods of [Betula platyphylla] of the transition zone between Eastern Siberian steppes and the taiga of northern Siberia or of the Siberian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Kazakh downy birch steppe woods
description: [Betula kirghisorum] ([Betula pubescens] [s.l.]) woods, enclaved, south of the wooded steppe zone of Eurasia, within the northern steppe zone, on saline soils of northern Kazakhstan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caspian birch woods
description: Birch forests of the northern Black Sea basin, Anatolia, the Caucasus and neighbouring regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caspian silver birch woods
description: [Betula pendula] woods of the Ponto-Caspian basin, the Caucasus, Anatolia, western Iran and Mesopotamia, widespread south of the Ponto-Caspian depessions, represented by rare outposts north of the basin, in particular in Crimea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caspian downy birch woods
description: [Betula litwinowii] and [Betula litwinowii-Betula pendula] woods of eastern Anatolia, the Caucasus and the Ponto-Caspian basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Anatolian downy birch woods
description: Woods of [Betula litwinowii], usually with [Betula pendula], of the regions of Tunceli, Erzurum and Kars, at between 1500 and 2500 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian downy birch woods
description: [Betula litwinowii]-dominated woods of the Bol'shoy and Malyy Kavkaz ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Ponto-Caspian downy birch woods
description: [Betula pubescens] woods of the steppe regions of the northern Ponto-Caspian basin, characteristic in particular of the sand terrasses of the lower Dnjepr.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian [Betula raddeana] woods
description: Birch woods of the Caucasus dominated by the scarce [Betula raddeana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trans-Caucasian [Betula medwediewii] woods
description: Woods and thickets of [Betula medwediewii], pure or mixed with [Quercus pontica], [Sorbus subfusca], [Rhododendron caucasicum], [Laurocerasus officinalis], [Ilex aquifolium], [Vaccinium arctostaphylos], characteristic of the 800 to 2300 m level of Transcaucasia, with isolated outposts in the eastern Black Sea region of Turkey.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian [Betula megrelica] woods
description: Birch woods of the Caucasus system dominated by [Betula megrelica], local and limited to the subalpine level.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian birch woods
description: [Betula turkestanica], [Betula tadzhikistanica], [Betula chitralica] formations of the Tien Shan and Pamir Alai systems, and of the northeastern Afghan mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan birch woods
description: [Betula utilis] ([Betula jacquemontii]) woods and thickets constituting or participating in the timberline formations (2700-3350 m) of the Nuristan Himalayas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern birch woods
description: [Betula spp.]-dominated formations, most characteristic of the timberline, of the borea-nemoral, nemoral and warm temperate zones of Eastern Asia. Birch woods of the larch, larch-pine and larch-pine-spruce zones of the southern boreal mountains of eastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alder woods
description: Nonriparian, nonmarshy woods of the western Palaearctic region dominated by [Alnus spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Alnus cordata] woods
description: [Alnus cordata]-dominated formations of slopes with deep, loose, moist soils, endemic to the Campanian, Lucanian and Calabrian Apennines and the Castaniccia and San Petrone ranges of Corsica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral and boreonemoral alder woods
description: Nonriparian, nonmarshy formations of the nemoral or boreonemoral zones dominated by [Alnus glutinosa] or [Alnus incana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic [Alnus glutinosa] woods
description: Nonriparian, nonmarshy formations of Atlantic regions of the nemoral zone dominated by [Alnus glutinosa] or [Alnus incana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Alnus]-[Urtica]-[Sambucus] woods
description: Tall, closed [Alnus glutinosa] woods of Britain developed on relatively dry, generally alluvial, eutrophic soils, in particular, on old river terraces, with [Sambucus nigra], [Salix cinerea], [Crataegus monogyna], [Prunus spinosa], [Urtica dioica], [Poa trivialis], [Dryopteris dilatata], [Galium aparine], [Rubus fruticosus] [s.l.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Norwegian herb-rich alder-elm woods
description: Woods of coastal southern Norway dominated by [Alnus glutinosa] and [Alnus incana], accompanied by [Ulmus glabra] and [Fraxinus excelsior], with an herb-rich undergrowth dominated by [Melica nutans], [Poa nemoralis], [Ranunculus ficaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European dry alder woods
description: Dry [Alnus incana] or [Alnus glutinosa] woods of nemoral Central Europe, in particular, great horsetail dry alder woods of Poland, dense alder stands of steep valley slopes of Great Poland, dominated by [Alnus incana] alone or by [Alnus glutinosa] and [Alnus incana] together, with a rich undergrowth composed predominantely of ruderal and riparian species; characteristic or abundant species include [Equisetum telmateia], [Lamium maculatum], [Myosotis sparsiflora], [Corylus avellana], [Chaerophyllum temulentum], [Urtica dioica], [Cardamine amara], [Veronica hederifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic dry alder woods
description: Dry alder woods of the nemoral and boreonemoral regions of Lithuania, Russia, Belarus and Ukraine, in particular, nettle grey alder woods, tall herb-rich dry [Alnus incana] forests on comparatively fertile acid brown forest soils, recorded from the northern part of the Valday Upland and Lithuania, with [Urtica dioica], [Anthriscus sylvestris], [Mnium cuspidatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide grey alder woods
description: [Alnus incana] woods of the subalpine level of the western Rhodopes, substitution facies of [Picea abies] forests, usually developed in wetter stations than those occupied by [Betula pendula] or [Populus tremula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal alder woods
description: Nonriparian, nonmarshy formations of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic region dominated by [Alnus glutinosa] or [Alnus incana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal [Alnus glutinosa] woods
description: Nonriparian, nonmarshy formations of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic region dominated by [Alnus glutinosa]. They are related to the shore woods of unit 44.24 and have a similar composition.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal [Alnus incana] woods
description: Nonriparian, nonmarshy formations of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic region dominated by [Alnus incana], appearing, in particular, as first recolonisation stage on rich damp soils of central and northern Fennoscandia. They are related to the shore woods of unit 44.23 and have a similar composition.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aspen woods
description: Woods of the western Palaearctic region dominated by [Populus tremula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Alpine aspen woods
description: Woods of [Populus tremula] and [Corylus avellana], accompanied by a xerophile flora, of dry inner valleys of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lowland nemoral aspen woods
description: Pioneer and subclimax [Populus tremula] formations of plains and hills of nemoral Europe, in particular the North Sea-Baltic plain and lower Hercynian slopes, within the range of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic acidophilous oak woods, and of the adjacent large alluvial systems, such as that of the Po.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane aspen stands
description: [Populus tremula] formations of the montane level of nemoral and Mediterranean mountains of Europe, occurring, in particular, within the beech belt of high southern mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Mediterranean aspen stands
description: [Populus tremula] formations occurring within the sub- or supra-Mediterranean environment of the mixed deciduous broad-leaved forests of, in particular, the [Quercion frainetto].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal aspen woods
description: [Populus tremula] stands of the taiga zone and of the transition zone between taiga and nemoral woods of Fennoscandia and the northern Sarmatic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian aspen woods
description: [Populus tremula]-dominated forests of the southwestern spurs of the Ural Mountains, part of the easternmost extension of the oak-lime nemoral forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian steppe aspen woods
description: Open, often parklike, woods of [Populus tremula] and [Betula pendula] (listed under unit 41.B9 when dominated by the latter) of the transition zone between steppe and taiga of Siberia, east of the range of the nemoral deciduous forests of the Sarmatic region. The shrub layer includes [Lonicera altaica], [Lonicera tatarica], [Thelycrania alba] ([Cornus alba]), [Ribes nigrum], [Ribes rubrum], [Spiraea hypericifolia], [Cotoneaster multiflorus]; the meadow-like herb layer is formed by [Agrostis alba], [Calamagrostis arundinacea], [Poa pratensis], [Bromus inermis], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Astragalus danicus], [Campanula bononiensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian aspen forests
description: [Populus tremula] stands, sometimes vast, of the southern slopes of inner Pontic ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Asian aspen woods
description: [Populus davidiana]-[Betula platyphylla] woods of the 2500-3000 metre spruce-pine zone of the Nanshan range of eastern central Asia and of the larch, larch-pine and larch-pine-spruce zones of the Ta-hsing-an Ling range of northeastern China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rowan woods
description: Woods of the western Palaearctic region dominated by [Sorbus aucuparia], characteristic in particular of the Scottish Highlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eurosiberian elm and maple woods
description: Forests and woods dominated by [Ulmus spp.] or [Acer spp.] of dry, sometimes humid but nonriparian, stable soils of the nemoral western Palaearctic region. Ravine forests, on screes or colluvions, dominated by these species are listed in unit 41.3, riverine forests in unit 44.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small-leaved elm woods
description: [Ulmus minor] ([Ulmus carpinifolia], [Ulmus campestris]) or [Ulmus procera] woods of base- and nutrient-rich, often ruderal, terrain, dispersed along the western seaboard of Western Europe and in warm, dry, subcontinental areas of Central Europe, usually rich in species of southern affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sweet violet elm woods
description: Nitrophile [Ulmus minor] or [Ulmus procera] woods of the western seaboard of the European continent, from northern France to Poland, distributed, in particular, in the Paris Basin, in the maritime dunes of the Netherlands and Belgium, on the dikes of the Dutch fluviatile district and on the cretaceous low Meuse hills, sporadically also in suburban forests, parks and green spaces throughout its range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermo-Atlantic elm woods
description: [Ulmus minor] woods of the coasts of Normandy, Brittany and Vend‚e.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: British suckering elm woods
description: Woods of the British Isles, mostly of the [Fraxinus]-[Acer]-[Mercurialis] type, invaded and dominated by suckering elms of the [Ulmus minor] group ([Ulmus carpinifolia], [Ulmus procera]); postcultural small-leaved elm groves are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-continental field elm woods
