description: [Ulmus minor] woods of dry, warm stations in regions of subcontinental climate of Central Europe, mostly secundary colonists of agricultural land on loess, marls, degraded chernozems or alluvial terrain, distributed in particular in southern German dry enclaves, in peri-Pannonic areas and in Bulgaria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wych elm and fluttering elm woods
description: Nonriparian, nonravine [Ulmus glabra] or [Ulmus laevis]-dominated formations of northern and central Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eurosiberian maple woods
description: Forests and woods dominated by [Acer spp.] of dry, sometimes humid but nonriparian, stable soils of the nemoral western Palaearctic region, in particular, maple-dominated, pioneer, young and perturbed stands of the Atlantic and sub-Atlantic varied oak-hornbeam and ash forests of units 41.2 and 41.3.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euro-Siberian lime forests
description: [Tilia spp.]-dominated forests and woods of dry, sometimes humid but nonriparian, stable soils of the nemoral and boreal zones of western and central Eurasia. Ravine forests, on screes or colluvions, dominated by these species are listed in unit 41.3, riverine forests in unit 44.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western lime forests
description: Rare [Tilia]-dominated stands of nemoral western and central Europe, within the range of [Fagus sylvatica], often [Tilia]-dominated facies of lime-rich oak-hornbeam forests. They are distributed, in particular, in the Bohemian basin, in southern Scandinavia and in the British Isles.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-boreal lime forests
description: [Tilia]-dominated forests of the northern nemoral zone and of enclaves in the southern boreal zone of Fennoscandia, the Baltic States and Russia, east to the Volga, outside of the range of [Fagus sylvatica] and mostly of [Carpinus betulus]. [Tilia cordata] may be accompanied by [Quercus robur], [Acer platanoides], [Populus tremula], [Picea abies], [Corylus avellana], [Sorbus aucuparia], [Euonymus europaeus], [Daphne mezereum], [Galium odoratum], [Anemone nemorosa] and boreal herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East-European lime forests
description: [Tilia]-dominated forests of eastern Central Europe and the southern nemoral zone of Russia, east of the range of [Fagus sylvatica] and, for the most part, of that of [Carpinus betulus], and west of the Volga, with [Quercus robur], [Acer platanoides] and [Ulmus montana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trans-Volgan lime forests
description: Forests of the nemoral zone of Russia, east of the Volga, with an eastward trend of diminishing [Quercus robur] and augmenting [Tilia cordata], and an often luxuriant shrub layer comprizing, in particular, [Corylus avellana]. Many, or most, are dominated by lime and listed here rather than under unit 41.26C.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Uralian lime forests
description: [Tilia cordata]-dominated forests of the montane and submontane zones of the Ural, mostly to the north and west of the forests of unit 41.26D, with [Quercus robur], [Acer platanoides], [Populus tremula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean lime forests
description: [Tilia cordata]-dominated forests of the oak-hornbeam-lime forest complex occupying the central part of the Tauric chain of southern Crimea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Altai lime forests
description: [Tilia sibirica]-dominated forests of the Altai.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mongolian steppe lime forests
description: [Tilia mongolica]-dominated formations of sheltered valleys of Inner Mongolian steppes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxino-Hyrcanian mixed deciduous forests
description: Mixed summer-green broad-leaved forests limited mainly to the mountains bordering the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxinian mixed mesic forests
description: Mixed summer-green broad-leaved forests of the Pontic Range of northern Anatolia and the Stranja-Istranca of Thrace, with outlyers in the eastern Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Euxinian mixed forests
description: Species-rich mixed forests of mountains of the western Pontic Range and the mountains of the western and southwestern Black Sea region, including the eastern Balkan Range, the Stranja-Istranca, typically with a varied, multispecific shrub layer and herb layer comprising many Euxinian elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracio-Euxinian mixed forests
description: Species-rich mixed forests of mountains of the western and southwestern Black Sea region, including the eastern Balkan Range, the Stranja-Istranca, composed of [Quercus polycarpa], [Quercus cerris], [Carpinus betulus], [Carpinus orientalis], [Sorbus torminalis], [Fagus orientalis], with a varied, multispecific shrub layer and herb layer comprising many Euxinian elements.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja beech-hornbeam-lime forests
description:
Mixed forests of [Fagus orientalis], [Carpinus betulus] and [Tilia tomentosa]
on well moistured soils of the Stranja mountains of southeastern Bulgaria, sometimes accompanied by the Balkan endemic [Quercus hartwissiana] and many species typical of the western Pontic [Fagus orientalis] forests (41.1E122), including the rare [Fritillaria pontica], [Cyclamen coum], [Primula vulgaris] ssp. [rosea], [Trachystemon orientalis], and [Scilla bithynica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stranja beech-[Quercus polycarpa] forests
description: Mixed forests of [Quercus polycarpa], [Carpinus betulus], [Quercus cerris], [Sorbus torminalis], [Fagus orientalis] with [Quercus frainetto], [Carpinus orientalis], located on north-facing slopes, on moist, nutrient-rich soils of the Stranja mountains of southeastern Bulgaria, with an understorey comprising [Crataegus monogyna], [Mespilus germanica], [Rhododendron ponticum], [Daphne pontica], [Erica arborea], [Vaccinium arctostaphylos], [Calluna vulgaris], [Genista carinalis], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Festuca heterophylla], [Poa nemoralis], [Melica uniflora], [Primula vulgaris] ssp. [rosea], [Cyclamen coum], [Salvia forskaohlei], [Trachystemon orientalis], [Sesleria alba].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian mixed mesic forests
description: Mixed forests with a varied, multispecific shrub layer and herb layer comprising many Euxinian elements located within a narrow coastal fringe from sea level to about 1200 m in the western Pontic Range between the Bulgarian border and 32øE, east of Zonguldak. Species include [Quercus macranthera], [Quercus hartwissiana], [Quercus iberica], [Taxus baccata], [Ostrya carpinifolia], [Fraxinus ornus], [Prunus laurocerasus], [Staphylea pinnata], [Buxus sempervirens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Colchidian mixed mesic forests
description: Mixed forests located within a narrow coastal fringe from sea level to about 800-900 m in the eastern Pontic Range, within the zone of tea cultivation. The tree layer includes [Quercus iberica], [Castanea sativa], [Fagus orientalis], [Carpinus betulus], occasional [Pinus sylvestris], the understorey comprises [Iris lazica], [Hypericum xylostelofolium], [Omphalodes cappadocica], [Oplismenus undulatifolius], [Rubus platyphylos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Euxinian mixed oak-hornbeam forests
description: Mixed forests of inner slopes of the Pontic Range generally in conditions of lower humidity and temperature than those of the Euxianian mixed forests of unit 41.H1, rich in species of [Quercus] and usually accompanied by [Carpinus betulus] or [Carpinus orientalis], sometimes with conifers. Characteristic species include [Quercus dshorochensis], [Quercus syspirensis], [Quercus anatolica], [Quercus iberica], [Quercus macranthera], [Acer cappadocium], [Fagus orientalis], [Abies bornmuelleriana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracian oak-hornbeam forests
description: Isolated oak-hornbeam forests of the Stranja and the Belgrat-Ormani, similar to woodlands of middle Europe in structure and field layer, but with [Quercus polycarpa], [Quercus frainetto], [Quercus cerris], [Quercus infectoria], dominated by, or rich in, [Carpinus betulus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian mixed oak-hornbeam forests
description: Oak-hornbeam forests of the western Pontic Range comprising, in particular, on calcareous marls, formations with [Quercus syspirensis], [Quercus anatolica], [Quercus iberica], with [Dictamnus albus] or, in the Kastamonu basin, with [Quercus iberica], [Abies bornmuelleriana], [Pinus sylvestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Pontic mixed oak-hornbeam forests
description: Oak-hornbeam forests of the central Pontic Range, centered around Samsun, variable in composition depending on conditions of humidity, including, in particular, formations with [Quercus cerris], [Crataegus curvipetala] on schists, with [Quercus dshorochensis], [Quercus anatolica] on limestones or marls, with [Quercus syspirensis], [Fagus orientalis], [Daphne pontica] or, with [Carpinus betulus], [Carpinus orientalis], [Ruscus aculiatus] and an accompanying flora characteristic of rhododendron-beech forests that grade, at their upper limit, into the mixed [Fagus]-[Quercus iberica]-[Carpinus]-[Acer cappadocium] forests of higher altitudes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic mixed oak-hornbeam forests
description: Oak-hornbeam forests of the eastern Pontic Range, including the Kelkit Cay and Harsit valleys, south of Trabzon, including, in particular, formations with [Quercus syspirensis], and an admixture of [Pinus pallasiana] and [Chamaecytisus pygmaeus] or, east of Erbaa, [Cedrus libani].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Pontic mixed oak-hornbeam forests
description: Oak-hornbeam forests of the inner slopes of the Pontic Range, under cold climate conditions and low precipitation (450-800 mm) comprising formations with [Quercus iberica], [Quercus macranthera], [Daphne pontica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian oak-hornbeam forests
description: Mixed forests rich in hornbeam, oak or beech, of slopes of the Central Caucasus of Georgia, with [Prunus avium], [Pyrus caucasica], [Corylus avellana], [Euonymus europaea], [Euonymus verrucosa], [Lathyrus roseus], [Dactylis glomerata], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Melica nutans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Caucasus oak-hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus caucasica] forests of the 800-1300 m level of the Central Caucasus of central Georgia, with [Sorbus torminalis], [Acer laetum], [Acer campestre], [Ulmus foliacea], [Crataegus kyrtostyla], [Mespilus germanica], [Lonicera caprifolium], [Cytisus caucasicus], [Digitalis schischkinii], [Viola reichenbachiana], [Carex euxina], [Melica uniflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasus beech-hornbeam forests
description: Mixed, oak- and hornbeam-dominated facies of [Fagus orientalis]-[Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus caucasica] forests of the 1200-1300 m level of the southern flank of the Central Caucasus of central Georgia, with [Clinopodium vulgare], [Primula macrocalyx], [Salvia glutinosa], [Fragaria vesca], [Epilobium montanum], [Melica uniflora], [Poa nemoralis]. Overwhelmingly beech-dominated stands are listed in unit 41.1H7.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasus dogwood hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus caucasica]-[Carpinus orientalis] forests of the 800 to 1000 metre level of northern slopes of the Central Caucasus of central Georgia, with [Sorbus torminalis], [Acer laetum], [Swida australis], [Crataegus kyrtostyla], [Lonicera caprifolium], [Berberis vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasus rhododendron hornbeam forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus caucasica] forests of the 1100 to 1300 metres of northern slopes of the Central Caucasus of central Georgia, with [Rhododendron flavum], [Acer platanoides], [Tilia cordata], [Poa nemoralis], [Festuca montana], [Galium vernum], [Cardamine impatiens], [Sedum stoloniferum], [Veronica officinalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasus timberline hornbeam forests
description: Timberline [Carpinus caucasica]-[Quercus macranthera] forests of the 1800 to 2000 metre level of northeastern slopes of the Central Caucasus of central Georgia, with [Sorbus caucasigena], [Daphne mezereum], [Lonicera caucasica], [Astrantia maxima], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Pulmonaria dacica], [Astrantia major], [Euphorbia macroceras], [Pimpinella rhodanta], [Betonica grandiflora], [Scutellaria altissima], [Vicia truncatula], [Campanula latifolia], [Calamagrostis arundinacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Great Caucasus sessile oak forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus]-[Fagus orientalis] forests of the northwestern part of the Great Caucasus, at altitudes of 150-420 m, with [Acer laetum], [Prunus avium], [Pyrus caucasica], [Corylus avellana], [Frangula alnus], [Swida australis], [Hieracium umbellatum], [Serratula cinquefolia], [Lathyrus hirsutus], [Festuca drymeja].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Great Caucasus mixed slope forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus]-[Fagus orientalis] forests of steep slopes with brown soils on limestone of the 150-250 meter level of the northwestern Great Caucasus, with [Tilia caucasica], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Acer camperstre], [Ulmus glabra], [Viburnum lantana], [Cotinus coggygria], [Hedera helix], [Smilax aspera], [Clematis vitalba], [Philadelphus caucasicus], [Staohylea colchica], [Euonymus latifolia], [Tamus communus], [Primula vulgaris], [Paeonia caucasica], [Epipactis helleborine], [Carex sylvatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Great Caucasus rhododendron oak forests
description: [Quercus petraea]-[Carpinus betulus]-[Fagus orientalis] forests of the 350-420 m of the northwestern Great Caucasus, with [Rhododendron luteum], [Crataegus monogyna], [Mespilus germanica], [Rubus caucasicus], [Vinca herbacea], [Melampyrum elatius], [Lathyrus aureus], [Dorycnium herbaceum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian mixed mesic forests
description: Mixed summer-green broad-leaved forests of the region bordering the southern periphery of the Caspian Sea, including its coastal plain and the northern slopes of the Elburz system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian mixed alder forests
description: Species-rich mixed forests mostly of damp, poorly drained soils of the lowlands in the region of the southern end of the Caspian Sea, with an often dense, jungle-like understorey of tall shrubs, lianas, low shrubs and herbaceous plants. The species cortŠge includes, among others, the trees and tall shrubs [Alnus subcordata], [Alnus glutinosa], [Fraxinus excelsior], [Pterocarya fraxinifolia], [Populus caspica], [Diospyros lotus], [Ficus carica], [Salix fragilis], [Buxus sempervirens], [Albizia julibrissin], [Celtis australis], [Acer insigne], [Prunus caspica], [Prunus laurocerasus], [Mespilus germanica], [Paliurus spina-christi], [Punica granatum], lower shrubs, notably [Epimedium pinnatum], [Sambucus ebulus], [Andrachne calchiica], [Hypericum androsaemum], [Teucrium hercanum], [Ruscus hyrcanus], and climbers, in particular, [Periploca graeca], [Vitis sylvestris], [Clematis vitalba], [Hedera colchica], [Jasminum officinale], [Tamus communis], [Rubus caesus], [Solonum dulcamara].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian [Quercus castaneifolia] forests
description: Forests of the foothills and lower mountain zone of the northern Elburz Mountains dominated by [Quercus castanaefolia], with [Parrotia persica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian [Carpinus]-[Quercus] forests
description: Forest communities of the foothills and lower mountain zone of the northern Elburz Mountains dominated by [Quercus castanaefolia] and [Carpinus betulus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian [Castanea]-[Quercus] forests
description: Uncommon forests of the foothills and lower mountain zone of the western Hyrcanian region dominated by [Quercus castanaefolia] and [Castanea sativa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian [Acer]-[Quercus] forests
description: Forests of the foothills and lower mountains mainly of the eastern Hyrcanian region dominated by [Quercus castanaefolia], [Acer cappidocicum] and [Acer signe],
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian [Quercus macranthera] forests
description: Relatively xerophile forests of Hyrcanian mountains, at altitudes of 1600-2000 m, dominated by [Quercus macranthera], with shrubs of [Quercus therica], [Sorbus boissieri], [Sorbus umbellata], [Rhamnus catharticus], [Mespilus germanica], [Acer hyrcanum], [Acer opilus], [Crataegus melanocarpa], [Viburnum lantana], [Colutea persica], [Spirea crenata], [Juniperus communis], [Juniperus sabina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Asian mixed deciduous forests
description: Macrophyllous deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral and boreo-nemoral eastern Asia, distributed in Russian Amurland, in the Heilongjiang (Heilungkiang), Jilin (Kirin), Hebei (Hopei), Shanxi (Shansi), Sandong (Shantung), Henan (Honan) and Shaanxi (Shensi) provinces of China, in     Korea and in Japan; [Fagus]-dominated forests of Japan and offshore islands of Korea, listed in 41.1K, are excluded.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amur oak-lime forests
description: Macrophyllous deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests, species-rich, of boreo-nemoral continental eastern Asia, distributed in the Russian Far East, in eastern Heilongjiang (Heilungkiang), eastern Jilin (Kirin) and northeast Liaoning provinces of China, and in northern Korea, rich in lime.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amur dry slope oak-lime forests
description: [Quercus mongolica]-[Tilia amurensis] forests of dry slopes of Amurland, with [Tilia amurensis], [Fraxinus rhynchophylla], [Acer mono], [Maianthemum dilatatum], [Vicia unijuga], [Sedum aizoon], [Viola sustroussurienis], [Falcata japonica], [Granium maximoviczii], [Adenophora verticillata], [Aruncus dioicus], [Polygonatum odoratum], [Lespedeza bicolor].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amur rich oak-lime forests
description: Rich [Quercus mongolica]-[Tilia amurensis] forests of western and southern dry gentle slopes of Amurland, with [Doellingeria scabra], [Viburnum sargentii], [Corylus manshurica], [Polemonium racemosum], [Artemisia stolonifera], [Artemisia gmelini], [Carex siderostricta], [Campanula cephalotes], [Galium davuricum], [Euphorbia eucorum], [Filipendula palmata], [Pedicularis resupinata], [Veronica siberica], [Viola collina], [Aconitum stoloniferum], [Trisetum sibiricum], [Cardamine leucantha], [Pseudostellaria], [japonica], [Asparagus schoberioides], [Lychnis fulgens], [Sanicula shinensis], [Agrimonia pilosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amur poor oak-lime forests
description: Poor [Quercus mongolica]-[Tilia amurensis] forests of dry steep northern, or gentle slopes of Amurland with [Acer pseudosieboldianum], [Cacalia hastata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amur oligo-hygrophile lime forests
description: [Tilia amurensis] forests on cool, moist unfertile soils of north-facing slopes of Amurland, with [Carpinus cordata], [Philadelphis tenuifolius], [Arisaema amurensis], [Ajuga multiflora], [Ribes maximoviczianum], [Urtica laetevirens], [Pseudostellaria sylvatica], [Dryopteris crassirhizoma].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amur hornbeam-lime forests
description: [Carpinus cordata]-[Tilia amurensis] forests on northern slopes of Amurland, with [Acer pseudosieboldianum], [Acer tegmentosum], [Syringa amurensis], [Delphinium macickianum], [Adoxa moschatellina], [Smilacina hirta], [Aconitum albo-violaceum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Amur maple-lime forests
description: Maple-lime forests on northern gentle slopes of Amurland, with [Phlomis maximowiczii], [Lonicera ruprechtiana], [Urtica angustifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sino-Japanese deciduous forests
description: Macrophyllous deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral eastern Asia, distributed in the Hebei (Hopei), Shanxi (Shansi), Sandong (Shantung), Henan (Honan) and Shaanxi (Shensi) provinces of China, in Korea, in the Quelpart Islands, in southern Hokkaido, Honshu, montane Shikoku and Kyushu, mostly dominated by deciduous [Quercus spp.], or by [Quercus spp.] and [Fraxinus spp.], sometimes by [Tilia spp.]; [Carpinus spp.], [Acer spp.], [Celtis spp.], [Juglans spp.], [Phellodendron amurense], [Koelreuteria paniculata], [Betula spp.], [Castanea crenata], [Aphananthe aspera], [Styrax japonica], [Zelkova serrata], [Aesculus turbinata], [Ulmus spp.], [Alnus spp.] may be part of the deciduous tree cortŠge; [Fagus]-dominated forests of Japan and offshore islands of Korea, listed in 41.1K, are excluded.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chinese broad-leaved deciduous forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral eastern China, dominated by oaks [Quercus spp.], oaks and ashes [Fraxinus spp.] or limes [Tilia spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Quercus aliena]-[Fraxinus] forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral eastern China, mostly distributed below 700 m, dominated by [Quercus aliena], [Fraxinus chinensis] and [Carpinus turczaninowii], with [Quercus dentata], [Evodia danielii], [Acer mono].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Quercus variabilis] forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral eastern China, mostly distributed below 500 m, dominated by [Quercus variabilis], with [Fraxinus chinensis], [Biota orientalis], [Pistacia chinensis], [Carpinus turczaninowii], [Acer truncatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Quercus dentata] forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral eastern China, mostly distributed between 400 and 1000 m, dominated by [Quercus dentata] with [Fraxinus chinensis], [Quercus aliena], [Ulmus macrocarpa], [Carpinus turczaninowii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Quercus liaotungensis]-[Fraxinus] forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral eastern China, mostly distributed between 700 and 1000 m, dominated by [Quercus liaotungensis] and [Fraxinus chinensis], with [Betula fruticosa], [Acer mono], [Tilia mandshurica], [Tilia mongolica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chinese [Tilia]-[Betula] forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of nemoral eastern China, mostly distributed between 1100 and 1400 m, dominated by [Tilia mandshurica], [Tilia mongolica] with [Betula japonica] var. [mandshurica], [Quercus liaotungensis], [Populus tremula] var. [davidiana], [Salix phylicifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Korean broad-leaved deciduous forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of central Korea dominated by [Quercus mongolica], [Quercus serrata], [Carpinus laxiflora], [Carpinus tschonoskii], [Acer formosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Japanese broad-leaved deciduous forests
description: Deciduous or predominantly deciduous forests of Japan mostly characteristic of southern Hokkaido and northern Honshu, mostly dominated by [Quercus crispula], [Quercus dentata], [Quercus serrata], [Fraxinus spaethiana], sometimes [Ulmus davidiana], [Castanea crenata], [Aesculus turbinata], with [Acer spp.], [Celtis spp.], [Betula spp.], [Zelkova serrata], [Alnus spp.], [Cercidphyllum japonicum], [Pterocarya rhoifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate coniferous forests
description: Forests and woodland of native coniferous trees, other than floodplain and mire woods, of the boreal, nemoral, Irano-Turanian, warm-temperate humid and Mediterranean zones; formations dominated by coniferous trees, but comprising broad-leaved evergreen trees, are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Palaearctic fir forests
description: Fir ([Abies spp.])-dominated conifer forests of the nemoral and Mediterranean mountains and hills of western Eurasia and North Africa, in regions under Atlantic influence. They are formed either by [Abies alba], widespread in the Alpine system and its satelite ranges (units 42.11 to 42.16), or by a number of southern species, mostly of very restricted range (units 42.17 to 42.1A).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Neutrophile medio-European fir forests
description: Fir ([Abies alba]) and fir-spruce forests developed on neutral or near-neutral soils of the Alps, the Dinarides, the Carpathians, the Pyrenees, the Jura, the Hercynian ranges and the northern Apennines, in association with forests of the [Fagion medio-europaeum], of the [Fagion illyricum] or of the [Fagion dacicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Alpine neutrophile fir forests
description: Neutrophilous [Abies alba] and [Abies alba]-[Picea abies] forests developed on brown soils of the intermediate or inner Alps, outside of the climatic range of the beech ([Fagus sylvatica]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sorrel fir forests
description: Typical inner Alpine [Abies alba] forests with a predominance of mull-moder species such as [Veronica urticifolia] ([Veronica latifolia]), [Melampyrum sylvaticum], [Prenanthes purpurea], [Oxalis acetosella], [Luzula nivea]; all fir forests of the intermediate and inner Alps can be included in this category with the exception of those that present clearly acidophilous or calciphilous facies and of the well-characterized local types listed immediately below.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall herb fir forests
description: High altitude, upper montane, tall-herb rich inner-Alpine fir forests with [Adenostyles alliariae], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Cicerbita alpina], [Chaerophyllum villarsii], [Peucedanum ostruthium], [Alnus viridis] and [Sorbus aucuparia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trochischantes fir forests
description: [Abies alba] forests of the Maritime Alps, distributed in particular in the Quatre-Cantons forest in the Tournairet massif, in the Haute-V‚subie, in the Peira Cava massif, in the middle and high Roya, with [Trochiscanthes nodiflora], [Galium sylvaticum], [Luzula pedemontana], [Aquilegia atrata], [Phyteuma halleri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Neutrophile Hercynio-Alpine fir forests
description: Neutrophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the outer Alps, the Dinarides, the Carpathians, the northern Apennines, the Pyrenees, the Jura and the Hercynian arc, dominated by [Abies alba] with a varying admixture of [Picea abies], [Fagus sylvatica] or both.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine neutrophile fir forests
description: Neutrophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the northern, western, southwestern and southern outer Alps, the western Carpathians, the northern Apennines, the Pyrenees, the Jura and the Hercynian arc, within the area of distribution of the montane beech forests of the [Fagion medio-europaeum], dominated by [Abies alba] with a varying admixture of [Picea abies], [Fagus sylvatica] or both.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine neutrophile spruce fir forests
description: Neutrophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the northern, western, southwestern and southern outer Alps, the western Carpathians, the northern Apennines, the Jura and the Hercynian arc, developed in stations edaphically or microclimatically unfavourable to beech, dominated by [Abies alba] accompanied to a varying extent by [Picea abies] and with a species cortŠge composed by elements of the [Fagetalia] and of the [Piceetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine neutrophile beech fir forests
description: Neutrophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the northern, western, southwestern and southern outer Alps, the western Carpathians, the northern Apennines, the Pyrenees, the Jura and the Hercynian arc, developed in stations sufficiently favourable to beech, dominated by [Abies alba] accompanied to a varying extent by [Fagus sylvatica] and [Picea abies] and with a species cortŠge identical to that of the montane beech forests of units 41.13, 41.14, 41.17.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian neutrophile fir forests
description: Neutrophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the southeastern outer Alps and the Dinarides, within the area of distribution of the montane beech forests of the [Fagion illyricum], dominated by [Abies alba] with a varying admixture of [Picea abies], [Fagus sylvatica] or both.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian neutrophile spruce fir forests
description: Neutrophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the southeastern outer Alps and the Dinarides, developed in stations edaphically or microclimatically unfavourable to beech, dominated by [Abies alba] accompanied to a varying extent by [Picea abies] and with a species cortŠge composed by elements of the [Fagetalia] and of the [Piceetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian neutrophile beech fir forests
description: Neutrophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the southeastern outer Alps and the Dinarides, developed in stations sufficiently favourable to beech, dominated by [Abies alba] accompanied to a varying extent by [Fagus sylvatica] and [Picea abies] and with a species cortŠge identical to that of the montane beech forests of units 41.13, 41.14, 41.17.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian neutrophile montane fir forests
description: Neutrophile to acidophile forests of [Abies alba] and [Fagus sylvatica], often with [Picea abies], on very steep slopes of the montane level of the eastern and southern Carpathians, with a cortŠge of [Fagetalia] and [Symphyto-Fagenion] species, including [Pulmonaria rubra], [Dentaria glandulosa], [Symphytum cordatum], [Salvia glutinosa], [Actaea spicata], [Rubus hirtus], [Dryopteris filix-mas], [Athyrium filix-femina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean fir forests
description: Montane [Abies alba] forests of inner valleys of the Pyrenees, and of other stations of relative continentality, unfavourable to beech, more acidophilous than those of units 42.111 and 42.112, with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Goodyera repens], [Galium rotundifolium] and a good representation of species of the neutrophilous beech forests, intermediate between this unit and unit 42.13.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian high montane fir forests
description: Forests dominated by [Abies alba] and [Picea abies], accompanied by [Fagus sylvatica] and characterized by the presence of boreal elements in the herb layer, of gentle slopes of the upper montane level of the Eastern and Southern Carpathians, with [Hieracium rotundatum], [Orthilia secunda], [Moneses uniflora], [Goodyera repens], [Homogyne alpina], [Soldanella hungarica] ssp. [major], [Calamagrostis villosa], [Calamagrostis arundinacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calciphile medio-European fir forests
description: [Abies alba] and [Abies alba]-[Picea abies] forests developed on calcareous soils of the Alps, the Dinarides, the Pyrenees, the Jura and the Hercynian ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Alpine calcicolous fir forests
description: Calcicolous [Abies alba] and [Abies alba]-[Picea abies] forests of the intermediate Alps, with [Carex alba], [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Hepatica triloba], [Calamagrostis varia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Outer Alpine calcicolous fir forests
description: [Abies alba] facies of calcicolous [Picea abies]-[Abies alba] forests of the outer Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Jurasso-Hercynian calcicolous fir forests
description: [Abies alba]-[Picea abies] woods of calcareous soils of the eastern Black Forest foothills, the Baar Plateau and the piedmont of the Swabian Alb, rich in sedges and orchids.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric calcareous block fir forests
description: [Abies alba]-dominated fir forests of calcareous block slopes of the Dinarides of Slovenia, western Croatia, mostly in the Gorski Kotar, the Velebit and the Pljesevica, and Bosnia-Herzegovina, extending north to the Triglav range in the southeastern Alps of Slovenia and south in fragmentary form to the Piva Valley of Montenegro, with [Juniperus nana], [Calamagrostis hirundinacea], [Calamagrostis varia], [Cirsium erisithales], [Clematis alpina], ferns and mosses including [Leucobryum glaucum]. They include primaeval and near-natural forests of considerable biological and aesthetic value.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acidophile medio-European fir forests
description: [Abies alba] and [Abies alba]-[Picea abies] forests developed on acid soils of the Alps, the Dinarides, the Carpathians, the Pyrenees, the Jura, the Hercynian ranges and the northern Apennines, within the biogeographical range of beech forests of the [Fagion medio-europaeum], of the [Fagion illyricum] or of the [Fagion dacicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inner Alpine acidophile fir forests
description: Oligotrophic fir and fir-spruce forests of the intermediate or inner Alps, with [Luzula nivea], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Calamagrostis villosa], [Festuca flavescens], [Saxifraga cuneifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acidophile Hercynio-Alpine fir forests
description: Acidophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the outer Alps, the Dinarides, the Carpathians, the northern Apennines, the Pyrenees, the Jura and the Hercynian arc, dominated by [Abies alba] with a varying admixture of [Picea abies], [Fagus sylvatica] or both.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine acidophile fir forests
description: Acidophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the outer Alps, the western Carpathians, the Jura, the Bohemian Quadrangle, the Black Forest, the Vosges, the Central Massif, the Pyrenees, locally of other mid-German Hercynian ranges, in particular, the Thringer Wald, developed in stations edaphically or microclimatically unfavourable to beech, dominated by [Abies alba] accompanied to a varying extent by [Picea abies] and with a species cortŠge combining elements of the [Piceetalia] with those of the [Fagetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian acidophile fir forests
description: Acidophile fir forests of the montane or submontane levels of the Dinarides, developed in stations edaphically or microclimatically unfavourable to beech, dominated by [Abies alba] with a varying admixture of [Picea abies] and [Fagus sylvatica], with a species cortŠge composed by elements of the [Fagetalia] ([Fagion illyricum]) and of the [Piceetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dacian acidophile beech fir forests
description: Neutrophile to acidophile [Abies alba] or [Abies alba]-[Picea abies] forests of the montane beech-fir belt of the southeastern Carpathians and the Apuseni mountains, with a cortŠge comprising [Fagetalia] and [Symphyto-Fagenion] species including [Pulmonaria rubra], [Dentaria glandulosa], [Symphytum cordatum], [Salvia glutinosa], [Actaea spicata], [Rubus hirtus], [Dryopteris filix-mas], [Athyrium filix-femina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpenrose fir forests
description: High-altitude fir forests characteristic of ubacs of the Pyrenees and southwestern Alps, outside of the range of spruce, with [Rhododendron ferrugineum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Homogyne alpina], [Festuca flavescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean alpenrose fir forest
description: Fir forests of the lower subalpine level of the Pyrenees, with [Rhododendron ferrugineum], [Homogyne alpina], [Lonicera nigra], [Polystichum lonchitis], [Rosa pendulina] ([Rosa alpina]), [Huperzia selago].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine alpenrose fir forests
description: Fir forests of the lower subalpine level of the western Alps, with [Rhododendron ferrugineum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Homogyne alpina], [Lonicera caerulea], [Festuca flavescens], [Huperzia selago].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Block alpenrose fir forests
description: Block fir forests of the montane level of the Pyrenees and the southwestern Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Holy Cross fir forests
description: Upland fir, or fir-dominated fir-spruce or fir-pine-oak forests developed on mesotrophic acid soils of Little-Poland, in particular, of the Holy Cross mountains and of sub-Carpathic hills, with an undergrowth rich in ferns, bryophytes and lowland forest species shared with the deciduous forests of the [Tilio-Carpinetum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Bazzania] fir forests
description: Fir-dominated [Abies alba]-[Picea abies] forests of the German, Swiss and Austrian outer Alps and their piedmont, and of the Carpathians, recorded from the Slovakian Carpathians and the Apuseni mountains, with [Frangula alnus] and an herb and moss layer rich in [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Bazzania trilobata], [Blechnum spicant], [Dryopteris carthusiana agg.], [Oxalis acetosella], [Sphagnum palustre], [Sphagnum girgensohnii], [Hylocomium splendens], [Polytrichum formosum], [Thuidium tamariscinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican fir forests
description: [Abies alba] woods and forests locally replacing, mostly in cool stations, the acidophilous beech forests of the montane level of Corsica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Apennine fir forests
description: Relict [Abies alba] woods associated with the beech forests of the [Geranio versicolori-Fagion] of the Lucano-Calabrian Apennines (Pollino, Sila, Aspromonte).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian silver fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies alba] or of [Abies alba] mixed with [Fagus sylvatica], [Picea abies], [Pinus sylvestris] or [Pinus nigra] of the Rhodopides, the Balkan Range, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains and the Pelagonids, within the geographical range of [Fagion moesiacum] forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies alba] or of [Abies alba] mixed with [Fagus sylvatica], [Picea abies], [Pinus sylvestris] or [Pinus nigra] of the Rhodopes and the northeastern Greek mountains, Pirin, Rila, Vitosha, within the geographical range of [Fagion moesiacum] forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Falakron silver fir forests
description: Very local, calciphilous, [Abies alba] forests of Falakron and the southern flank of the Rhodopes of extreme northern Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodope fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies alba] or of [Abies alba] mixed with [Fagus sylvatica], of the main Rhodope range, within the [Fagion moesiacum] zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Rhodopide fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies alba] or of [Abies alba] mixed with [Fagus sylvatica], [Picea abies], [Pinus sylvestris] or [Pinus nigra] of Pirin, Rila and Vitosha.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Macedonian fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies alba] or of [Abies alba] mixed with [Fagus sylvatica], [Picea abies], [Pinus sylvestris] or [Pinus nigra] of the Moeso-Macedonian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies alba] or of [Abies alba] mixed with [Fagus sylvatica], [Picea abies], [Pinus sylvestris] or [Pinus nigra] of the Balkan Range system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonide silver fir forests
description: [Abies alba] forests of the the Pelagonid mountains south to extreme northern Greece, including the Varnous system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkano-Pontic fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies nordmanniana], [Abies borisii-regis], [Abies bornmuelleriana] of the southern Balkans peninsula, the Pontic range and the Caucasus, often mixed with beech, or adjacent to beech forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: King Boris's fir forests
description: [Abies borisii-regis]-dominated fir forests of the southern Dinaric Alps, the northern Pindus, the central Pindus, the southern Rhodopes of Bulgaria and Greece, the Slavanka and Belaciza, adjacent to beech and beech-fir forests of the [Fagion hellenicum] or [Fagion moesiacum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bornmueller's fir forests
description: [Abies bornmuelleriana]-dominated forests of the Pontic Range and outlying massifs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic rhododendron-Bornmueller's fir forests
description: [Abies bornmuelleriana]-dominated facies of the western Pontic fir-beech forests (41.1E15) of the western Pontic Range of Anatolia, developed above the western Pontic rhododendron-beech forests (unit 41.1E13) and largely sharing their associated flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic box-Bornmueller's fir forests
description: [Abies bornmuelleriana] forests, with an undergrowth of [Buxus sempervirens], developed on rare calcareous enclaves of the western Pontic Range, associated with the Western Pontic calciphile beech forests (unit41.1E14).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western sub-Pontic beech-Bornmueller's fir forests
description: Local [Abies bornmuelleriana]-dominated facies of the western inner Pontic beech forests (unit 41.1E22) of inner sub-Pontic ranges, the Ilgaz Daglari, in Paphlagonia, and the Uludag, south of Bursa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern sub-Pontic beech-Bornmueller's fir forests
description: [Abies bornmuelleriana]-dominated facies of the eastern sub-Pontic beech forests (unit 41.1E4), developed on siliceous soils in the cold inner ranges of the eastern Pontic Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western sub-Pontic subalpine Bornmueller's fir forests
description: [Abies bornmuelleriana] forests of the higher elevations of the Ilgaz Daglari and of the Uludag, developed above the forests of units 41.1E22 and 42.1723, on siliceous soils and under high pluviosity conditions, with [Pinus sylvestris], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Hieracium tossianum], [Pyrola chlorantha], [Orthilia secunda], [Moneses uniflora], [Saxifraga rotundifolia], [Goodyera repens], [Listera cordata], [Luzula sylvatica] and, in the higher levels, [Juniperus nana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nordmann's fir forests
description: [Abies nordmanniana]-dominated forests of the Caucasus and of the eastern Pontic Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic Nordmann's fir forests
description: [Abies nordmanniana]-dominated facies of the Pontic eastern spruce-beech forests of the eastern Pontic Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Pontic Nordmann's fir forests
description: [Abies nordmanniana] forests of inner slopes of the eastern Pontic Range).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyper-humid Caucasian fir forests
description: Dark, species-rich, neutrophilous [Abies nordmanniana] forests of the most humid parts of the western Great Caucasus Range, with [Ilex colchica], [Vaccinium arctostaphylos], [Rhododendron ponticum], [Galium odoratum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Neutrophilous Caucasian fir forests
description: [Abies nordmanniana]-dominated facies of neutrophilous fir-beech and fir-beech-spruce forests of the northern slope of the Great Caucasus Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acidophilous Caucasian fir forests
description: [Abies nordmanniana]-dominated fir-pine forests of the western part of the Great Caucasus Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean fir forests
description: [Abies]-dominated fir or fir-pine forests of the northeastern Mediterranean basin, developed outside of, but in the immediate vicinity of beech [Fagus spp.], by [Abies cephalonica] and [Abies equi-trojani], outlier species of the group of [Abies alba] and [Abies nordmanniana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Grecian fir forests
description: Endemic [Abies cephalonica] or mixed [Abies cephalonica] and [Abies borisii-regis] forests of the Peloponnese, Cephalonia, Parnassos, the southern Pindus, north to Panetolikon, Timfristos, Vardousia, Iti, Kallidromon and Othris, well outside of the range of beeches, [Fagus spp].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Trojan fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies equi-trojani] of the higher elevations of the Kaz Dag and of the Mustapha Kemal mountains in extreme western Anatolia, with [Epipogium aphyllum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afro-Asian fir forests
description: Fir or fir-cedar forests dominated by relict species of [Abies], including forests of [Abies pinsapo], [Abies marocana], [Abies numidica], [Abies cilicica] or [Abies nebrodensis], distributed along the rim of the southern Mediterranean basin, well outside the range of beech.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ronda pinsapo fir forests
description: Calcicolous forests and stands of the endemic [Abies pinsapo] of the supra-meso-Mediterranean level of Andalucia, limited to the Serrania de Ronda and associated ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bermeja pinsapo fir forests
description: Forests and stands of the endemic [Abies pinsapo] of the supra-meso-Mediterranean level of Andalucia, developed on ultra basic serpentine outcroppings of the Sierra Bermeja and isolated stands of associated ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moroccan fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies maroccana] or [Abies tazaotana], limited to very small areas of the northwestern and northern Rif mountains of Morocco.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Abies maroccana] forests
description: Forests of [Abies marocana] limited to an area of 150 kmý on calcareous soils of the northwestern Rif mountains of Morocco.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Abies tazaotana] forests
description: Stands of [Abies tazaotana], known only from the Djebel Tassaot in the northern Rif.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Algerian fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies numidica] of Mount Babor and Mount Tababor, limited to calcareous islands within the range of [Cedrus atlantica], in the Algerian Tell.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cilician fir forests
description: Forests of [Abies cilicica] of the Taurus system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Taurus Cilician fir forests
description: [Abies cilicica] ssp. [isaurica]-dominated forests of the eastern Lycian, Pisidian and western Isaurian Taurus of southwestern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Taurus Cilician fir forests
description: [Abies cilicica] ssp. [cilicica]-dominated forests of the Cilician Taurus, of the western Anti-Taurus and of the Amanus in southern Anatolia and Syria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lebanon Cilician fir forests
description: [Abies cilicica]-dominated forests of the mountains of Lebanon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Relict Nebrodi fir stands
description: Surviving stands of the endangered [Abies nebrodensis] in the Madonie mountains of Sicily.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fir reforestation
description: Plantations of western Palaearctic firs within or near their area of present or recent natural occurrence. Other plantations of these species and plantations of nonwestern-Palaearctic firs should be noted as unit 83.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Abies alba] reforestation
description: Plantations of [Abies alba] within its area of occurrence or north and west of it.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Abies borisii-regis] reforestation
description: Plantations of [Abies borisii-regis] in Greece and the southern Balkan peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Abies cephalonica] reforestation
description: Plantations of [Abies cephalonica] in Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Abies pinsapo] reforestation
description: Plantations of [Abies pinsapo] in Andalucia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Abies nebrodensis] reforestation
description: Plantations of [Abies nebrodensis] in the mountains of northern Sicily.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Near-eastern fir reforestation
description: Plantations of [Abies nordmanniana] in the Caucasus, of [Abies bornmuelleriana], [Abies equi-trojani] or [Abies nordmanniana] in the Pontic system, of [Abies cilicica] in the Taurus system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African fir reforestation
description: Plantations of [Abies marocana] or [Abies numidica] within their North African range of natural occurrence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Palaearcic orogenous spruce forests
description: Conifer forests of the Alps, the Carpathians, the Dinarides, the Balkan Range, the Rhodopes, the Apennines, the Jura, the Hercynian ranges, the Pontic Range and the Caucasus, dominated by [Picea abies], [Picea omorika] or [Picea orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine and Carpathian subalpine spruce forests
description: [Picea abies] forests of the lower subalpine level, and of anomalous stations in the montane level, of the outer, intermediate and inner Alps; in the latter, they are often in continuity with the montane spruce forests of unit 42.22. The spruces, often stunted or columnar, are accompanied by an undergrowth of decidedly subalpine affinities. [Picea abies] forests of the lower subalpine level of the Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bilberry spruce forests
description: Mostly acidophilous, mesophile, subalpine [Picea abies] forests of the outer, intermediate and inner Alps, with [Oxalis acetosella], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Calamagrostis villosa] and the moss [Hylocomium splendens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall herb subalpine spruce forests
description: Tall-herb rich, hygrophile or mesohygrophile, [Picea abies] forests of high altitude stations of the Alps, subjected to prolonged snow cover and frequent fogs, with [Adenostyles spp.], [Chaerophyllum hirsutum], [Peucedanum ostruthium], [Ranunculus aconitifolius], [Aconitum vulparia], [Aconitum paniculatum], [Stellaria nemorum], [Geranium sylvaticum], [Cicerbita alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Adenostyles glabra] subalpine spruce forests
description: [Picea abies] or [Picea abies]-[Larix decidua] forests of subalpine to high montane slopes of the Alps developed on base-rich and usually lime-rich substrates, in particular, on dolomites, limestones, calcschists, green schists, usually on steep rocky slopes, with an undergrowth dominated by [Adenostyles glabra] ([Adenostyles alpina]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Adenostyles alliariae] subalpine spruce forests
description: [Picea abies] forests of the subalpine level of the Alps developed in high precipition regions on usually calcareous bedrock, sometimes on base-rich siliceous substrates such as flysch, with an undergrowth dominated by dense formations of tall herbs, in particular, [Adenostyles alliariae], [Cicerbita alpina], [Rumex alpestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moist subalpine spruce forests
description: Sphagnum-rich [Picea abies] forests of the Alps, developed on more or less peaty, humid but not waterlogged substrates, with [Listera cordata], [Sphagnum acutifolium], [Sphagnum quinquefarium], [Sphagnum girgensohnii]. Spruce forests developed in fens or swamps at the periphery of raised bogs or on waterlogged soils in forests are included in swamp forests of class 44, as unit 44.A411.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Xerophile subalpine spruce forests
description: [Picea abies] forests on dry adrets of the northern and northwestern Alps, with [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] and a small admixture of [Vaccinium myrtillus] on siliceous soils over sandstones and carboniferous schists, with [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Carex humilis] on lustrous schists, with [berberis vulgaris], [Valeriana montana], [Valeriana tripteris] on stabilized calcareous screes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cold station spruce forests
description: [Picea abies] woods of anomalous stations at the montane or subalpine level of the Alps, in particular block forests of "ice cellars" (shaded rocky screes through which cold air flows), woods developed in valleys and depressions where cold air accumulates on clear nights, woods colonizing stabilised screes and narrow bands of rocks, woods on moist sites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian spruce forests
description: [Picea abies] forests, usually unmixed, forming, in most of the Carpathian arc, a lower subalpine belt between beech-fir or beech-fir-spruce forests of the montane level and the mugo pine upper subalpine zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Carpathian subalpine spruce forests
description: Subalpine [Picea abies] forests of the northwestern and northern Carpathians of Poland and Slovakia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Carpathian acidophilous spruce forests
description: Subalpine [Picea abies] forests of siliceous soils of the northwestern and northern Carpathians of Poland and Slovakia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian holly-fern spruce forests
description: Subalpine [Picea abies] forests of calcareous ranges in the northwestern and northern Carpathians of Poland and Slovakia, in particular of the calcareous Tatras.
