name: Pyrenean siliceous mesophile Scots pine forests
description: Silicicolous formations of [Pinus sylvestris] with [Sorbus aucuparia], [Salix caprea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Galium rotundifolium], [Melampyrum sylvaticum], [Melampyrum pratense], [Lathyrus linifolius] ([Lathyrus montanus]), [Potentilla erecta], [Helleborus viridis] ssp. [occidentalis], [Deschampsia flexuosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Massif Scots pine forests
description: Montane [Pinus sylvestris] forests of interior, relatively dry, regions of the Central Massif in the upper Loire basin (Velay and neighbouring regions) and the Causse M‚jean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Alpine mesophile Scots pine forests
description: Mesophile montane forests with wintergreens occupying a broad belt on the southwestern flank of the Alps from Dauphin‚ to the Maritime Alps, differentiated from the forests of unit 42.54 by the absence of [Erica herbacea]; the undergrowh usually comprises [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Centaurea scabiosa], [Tolpis staticifolia] ([Hieracium staticifolium]), [Calluna vulgaris], [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Monotropa hypopitys], [Goodyera repens], [Epipactis atrorubens], [Neottia nidus-avis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris]-dominated facies of the thermophilous, supra-Mediterranean oak woods (unit 41.7), alternated, mixed or imbricated with [Quercus pubescens] or [Quercus faginea] woods in the southwestern Alpine foothills, on the periphery of the Central Massif, along the southern flank of the Pyrenees and, locally, in the Ligurian and Insubrian Alps, in the western Alps of northern Dauphin‚ and Savoie, in the northern Apennines and on the northern flank of the Pyrenees. [Buxus sempervirens] is usually abundant in the undergrowth; other components of the shrub layer include [Corylus avellana], [Sorbus aria], [Sorbus torminalis], [Acer opalus], [Acer campestre], [Acer monspessulanum], [Evonymus latifolius], [Genista cinerea], [Juniperus communis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine box Scots pine forests
description: Supra-Mediterranean [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the western, southwestern and Insubrian Alps and their foothills, and of the Central Massif periphery.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Pyrenean box Scots pine forests
description: Supra-Mediterranean [Pinus sylvestris] forests, with abundant [Buxus sempervirens], forming a broad belt on the southern flank of the Pyrenees, with outposts on the northern flank, in the eastern Pyrenees and the east of the Pays de Sault.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Emilian Scots pine woods
description: Isolated [Pinus sylvestris] woods of the base of the Emilian Apennines, mostly on limestones and serpentines, comprising [Quercus cerris] and [Quercus pubescens] or [Carpinus betulus], [Corylus avellana], [Acer campestre], [Fraxinus ornus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian calcareous Scots pine woods
description: Montane and oro-Mediterranean, xerocline, calcicolous [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the Iberian Range, the Baetic ranges and the southern flank of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean hedgehog-heath Scots pine woods
description: Woods or prewoods of adrets in the montane level of calcareous ranges of the southern flank of the central Pyrenees, with usually low and contorted [Pinus sylvestris] accompanied by a hedgehog-heath (cf. unit 31.71) of [Echinospartum horridum], [Buxus sempervirens], [Juniperus hemisphaerica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Savin Scots pine forests
description: Oro-Mediterranean, calcicolous [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the Iberian Range and the Baetic ranges, often fairly open, and with a shrub layer that includes the prostrate [Juniperus sabina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian-Range calcicolous Scots pine forests
description: Oro-Mediterranean, calcicolous forests of [Pinus sylvestris] var. [iberica] of the Southern Iberian Range (Maestrazgo: Gudar, Jabalambre, Penyagolosa; serrania de Cuenca: sierra de San Felipe, Montes Universales), with a shrub layer constituted mainly by [Juniperus sabina]; secondary calcicolous Scots pine formations of lower altitude in the Iberian Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baetic calcicolous Scots pine forests
description: Oro-Mediterranean forests of [Pinus sylvestris] var. [nevadensis] of the Baetic ranges, Sierra Magina, Sierra de Baza, Sierra Tejeda, Sierra del Trevenque (calcareous periphery of the Sierra Nevada), with a shrub layer of [Juniperus sabina] and [Juniperus nana] accompanied by [Ononis aragonensis], [Genista lobelii] ssp. [longipes], [Daphne oleoides] and [Prunus prostrata], on limestones and dolomites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian silicicolous Scots pine forests
description: Montane and oro-Mediterranean, xerocline, silicicolous [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the Iberian Range, the Cordillera Central and the  southern flank of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean xerophile Scots pine forests
description: Montane and lower subalpine [Pinus sylvestris] or [Pinus sylvestris] and [Pinus uncinata] forests of dry adrets of the southern flanks of the Pyrenees and of the Val d'Aran, with a shrub layer comprising [Juniperus hemisphaerica], [Cytisus purgans], [Buxus sempervirens] and an herb layer dominated by [Deschampsia flexuosa], accompanied by, among others, [Veronica officinalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian-Range silicicolous Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of siliceous ground in the oro- and supra-Mediterranean levels of the Northern and Southern Iberian Ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Upper Sorian silicicolous Scots pine forests
description: Oro-Mediterranean, acidophilous forests of [Pinus sylvestris] var. [iberica] of the Northern Iberian Range (Soria), with [Juniperus nana], [Cytisus purgans], [Deschampsia flexuosa] ssp. [iberica], and abundant [Vaccinium myrtillus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lower Iberian-Range silicicolous Scots pine forests
description: Supra-Mediterranean, acidophilous [Pinus sylvestris] var. [iberica] woods of the Iberian Range, forming in particular as a substitution stage of [Quercus pyrenaica] woodland of which they largely retain the accompanying flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cordilleran silicicolous Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of siliceous ground in the oro- and supra-Mediterranean levels of the Cordillera Central.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Summital Guadarraman silicicolous Scots pine forests
description: Oro-Mediterranean, summital, silicicolous forests of [Pinus sylvestris] var. [iberica] of the Sierra de Guadarrama, with [Juniperus nana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lower Cordilleran silicicolous Scots pine forests
description: Supra-Mediterranean [Pinus sylvestris] var. [iberica] woods of the Cordillera Central (Guadarrama, Gredos), forming in particular as a substitution stage of [Quercus pyrenaica] woodland of which they largely retain the accompanying flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cantabrian Scots pine forests
description: Isolated [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the Cantabrian mountain system, in the Cordillera Cantabrica, the Montes de Leon and the Serra do Geres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern European Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the eastern Carpathians and of the mountains of the Balkan peninsula, south to northern Greece, formed by the largely isolated, disjunct, southeastern forms ([Pinus sylvestris] var. [rhodopaea], [Pinus sylvestris] var. [illyrica], [Pinus sylvestris] var. [romanica]) of [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [sylvestris], and often limited to azonal edaphic enclaves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thessalo-Macedonian Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the mountains of northern Greece (Pieria, Olympus, Vermion, Voras, La‹la, Elatia range), often with [Acer pseudoplatanus], [Sorbus aucuparia], and sometimes [Fagus sylvatica] or [Picea abies] in the tree layer and with [Vaccinium myrtillus] and [Rubus idaeus] in the shrub layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of Vitosha, the Rila, the Pirin and the Rhodope.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Moesian Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the Pelagonides and Moeso-Macedonian mountains of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and Bulgaria, in particular of ultrabasic trachytes and andesites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Macedonian Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the Moeso-Macedonian mountains of western Bulgaria, and of trachytes and andesites of the Moeso-Macedonian mountains of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, in the Bregalnica basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonian Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of trachytes and andesites of the Pelagonides of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, in the Mavrovo range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric spring heath Scots pine forests
description: Thermophile [Pinus sylvestris] woods of serpentines, dolomites and dolomite rendzinas of the Dinarides of Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and western and southern Serbia, with [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]), [Galium lucidum], [Aquilegia vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric serpentine Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] woods of serpentines of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina and western and southern Serbia, with [Daphne blagayana], [Rosa pendulina], [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]), [Galium lucidum], [Laserpitium krapfii], [Vicia villosa], [Symphytum tuberosum], [Erythronium dens-canis], [Pteridium aquilinium] and the serpentine plants [Asplenium cuneifolium] ssp. [serpentini], [Campanula cervicaria], [Crocus veluchensis], [Stachys scardica]. They are developed within the Illyrian and Moesian beech forest zones and generally occupy higher elevations and deeper soils than the serpentine [Pinus nigra] woods of unit 42.6212.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric dolomite Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] woods of dolomites and dolomite rendzinas of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia and Slovenia, with [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]), [Galium lucidum], [Genista januensis], [Aquilegia vulgaris], [Buphthalmum salicifolium], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Carex humilis], [Anthericum ramosum], [Cyclamen purpurascens], [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Hepatica nobilis], [Geranium sanguineum], [Helleborus niger] ssp. [macranthus], [Epipactis atrorubens], [Carex alba]. They are developed within the Illyrian beech forest zone and often occupy somewhat higher elevations than the similar dolomite [Pinus nigra] woods of unit 42.6214.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric calcicole Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] woods on limestones of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina, within the range of Illyrian beech forests, with [Abies alba], [Fagus sylvatica], [Picea abies], [Populus tremula], [Betula pendula], [Juniperus communis], [Cotoneaster nebrodensis], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Galium licidum], [Luzula sylvatica], [Brachypodium pinnatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric acidophile Scots pine forests
description: Dry acidophilous [Pinus sylvestris] woods of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina, within the range of Illyrian beech forests, with [Picea abies], [Abies alba], [Betula pendula] and an undergrowth dominated by [Leucobryum glaucum] accompanied by a species cortŠge characteristic of the [Vacinio-Piceetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian [Sesleria] Scots pine forests
description: Relict, preice age, forests developed on limestone substrates of the montane level of the Apuseni Mountains of the Southwestern Carpathians and of the Southern Carpathians, dominated by [Pinus sylvestris], with numerous calcicolous species such as [Sesleria rigida], [Helianthemum nummularium] ssp. [obscurum], [Thymus comosus], [Asperula capitata], [Dianthus spiculifolius], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Sorbus aria] and [Cotoneaster integerrimus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian bilberry Scots pine forests
description: Montane silicicolous [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the eastern and southern Carpathians, developped on superficial brown soil or bog soil, with a predominantly acidiphilous herb layer including [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Luzula luzuloides], [Oxalis acetosella], [Deschampsia flexuosa] and [Dicranum scoparium]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian [Daphne blagayana] Scots pine forests
description: Relict forests developed on amphibolitic substrates of the upper montane level of the Southern Carpathians, in particular the Cozia mountains, dominated by [Pinus sylvestris] and [Betula pendula], accompanied by regional species such as [Daphne blagayana], [Iris ruthenica], [Bruckenthalia spiculifolia] and [Anthemis carpatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Po terrace Scots pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus sylvestris] of the fluvioglacial terraces that constitute the high plains of the Po river system, with [Betula pendula], [Quercus pubescens], [Castanea sativa] and a ground layer with [Cytisus scoparius], [Calluna vulgaris], [Pteridium aquilinum], [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Molinia caerulea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: European Scots pine reforestation
description: [Pinus sylvestris] plantations inside or near the present or recent natural nemoral and Mediterranean European range of the species. Other and very artificial [Pinus sylvestris] plantations should be listed under 83.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caucasian Scots pine forests
description: Forests composed of pines of the [Pinus sylvestris] group, mostly included in [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [hamata] or its intermediates with [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [sylvestris], sometimes in species [Pinus kochiana], [Pinus hamata] or [Pinus armena], of the Pontic Range, its satellites and inner Anatolian outposts, of the mountains of the Crimea and of the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian Scots pine forests
description: Forests and woods of [Pinus sylvestris] of the Pontic Range, its inner ranges and northern Anatolian outposts south to 39øN, usually at high altitudes, of 1300 to 2500 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western sub-Pontic Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the inner ranges of the eastern part of the western Pontic system, of Galatia, southeastern Bithynia and southwestern Paphlagonia, developed between 1300 and 1900 metres, on siliceous substrates under a cold continental climate with five to eight months of snow cover, with [Pyrola chlorantha], [Moneses uniflora], [Orthilia secunda] and many [Hieracium spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern sub-Pontic Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of inner Pontic ranges of the Sivas basin, from northeastern Cappadocia to the upper Euphrates region of Erzincan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian subalpine Scots pine forests
description: Acidophilous [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the inner ranges of the western half of the eastern Pontic system of southern Lazistan, comprising forests with [Lilium ciliatum], [Euphorbia djimylensis], [Vicia freyniana], [Ranunculus brachylobus], as well as more open formations on warmer slopes accompanied by an undergrowth of [Daphne glomerata], [Rhododendron flavum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Geum coccineum], [Avena planiculmis], [Luzula campestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Anatolian Scots pine pre-steppe forests
description: Open [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the eastern flanks of the Pontic Range, developed in the 1500 m to 2400 m altitudinal range, under cold continental climatatic conditions with five to seven months of snow cover, with an undergrowth of [Juniperus nana], several species of [Rhododendron] and a substantial representation of the Euxinian flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Pontic Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] forests of the extreme east of the Pontic Range, developed mostly on southern exposures between 1800 m and 2100 m, within the environment of the eastern Pontic beech-spruce forests; [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Rhododendron flavum], [Juniperus nana], [Luzula campestris], [Hieracium spp.], [Pyrola chlorantha], [Orthilia secunda] participate in the usually well-lit understorey.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lazic Scots pine forests
description: Remarkable [Pinus sylvestris] f. [lazica] forest of the Black Sea coastal lowlands of the region of Of, on damp soils, with [Epimedium pinnatum] ssp. [colchicum], [Catabrosa pontica], [Berberis integerrima], [Carex latifolia], [Lycopodium chamaecyparissus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [hamata] ([Pinus kochiana]) forests of the Caucasus, in particular, treelimit formations of drier localities than those occupied by [Betula litwinowii] and [Betula raddiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [hamata] ([Pinus kochiana]) forests of the upper forest belt of the high mountains of Crimea, often with beech [Fagus orientalis], and with [Viola sieheana], [Viola alba] and [Galium mollugo] present in the understorey.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean beech-Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [hamata] ([Pinus kochiana]) forests with beech ([Fagus orientalis]) situated at the 650-1200 m level of well illuminated slopes of the mountains of Crimea, accompanied by [Mercurialis perennis], [Euphorbia amygdaloides], [Polygonatum polyanthemum], [Carex digitata], and sometimes with representatives of the genera [Convallaria] or [Epipactis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean north slope Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [hamata] ([Pinus kochiana]) forests situated at the 550-1250 m level of northern slopes of the mountains of Crimea, accompanied by [Orthilia secunda], [Hieracium gentile], and sometimes with representatives of the genera [Cephalanthera] or [Genista].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean south slope Scots pine forests
description: [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [hamata] ([Pinus kochiana]) forests situated at the 1130-1400 m level of southern slopes of the mountains of Crimea, accompanied by [Pimpinella lithophila], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Filipendula vulgaris], [Hieracium glaucescens], [Salvia tomentosa], [Acachmena cuspidata], [Galium verum] , [Fragaria vesca], [Festuca valesiaca], [Plantago media], [Clinopodium vulgare], and sometimes with representatives of the genera [Echinops] or [Sanicula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Black pine forests
description: Forests dominated by pines of the [Pinus nigra] group.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpino-Apennine [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] [s.s.] forests of the eastern Italian, Austrian and Slovenian Alps, of the Apennines and of Adriatic coasts of northern Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Alpine [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra] ([Pinus nigra], [Pinus austriaca]) forests of dry, sunny, rocky steep slopes and cliffs of the southeastern pre-Alps (Carnian pre-Alps, Julian pre-Alps, Carso), between 200 and 1200 m altitude, with [Cyclamen purpurascens] and [Aquilegia einseleana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine [Pinus nigra] forests
description: Relict "Villetta Barrea pine" ([Pinus nigra] ssp. [italica]) stations of the Abruzzi (Costa Camosciara, Villetta Barrea), the Campanian Apennines (monti Picentini), the Pollino system (Orsomarso).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lower Austrian [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra] forests of dry, sunny, often rocky and steep dolomite or sometimes limestone slopes and cliffs of the eastern pre-Alps of Lower Austria, between 300 m and 1200 m altitude, with [Amelanchier ovalis], [Cotoneaster spp.], [Berberis vulgaris], [Erica herbacea], [Daphne cneorum],  [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Melampyrum angustissimum], [Epipactis atrorubens], [Cyclamen purpurascens], [Carex humilis], [Euphorbia saxatilis], [Sesleria albicans], [Calamagrostis varia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Adriatic [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] [s.s.] forests of the Adriatic coasts of northern Italy, in the gulf of Venice, apparently indigenous, and of glacial relict character.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Balkanic black pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra] or [Pinus dalmatica] of the Dinarides, the Pelagonides and the Dalmatian coastal areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaro-Pelagonian [Pinus nigra] forests
description: Forests of [Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra] of the Dinarides and the Pelagonides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Hellenic montane [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] [s.s.] ([Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra]) pine woods of ultrabasic substrates, generally trachytes and andesites, of the Pelagonides of northwestern Greece, Albania and the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, in the Mavrovo range, as well as of the Moeso-Macedonian mountains of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, in the Bregalnica basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian serpentine [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] [s.s.] ([Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra]) woods of serpentines of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina and western and southern Serbia, with [Daphne blagayana], [Rosa pendulina], [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]), [Galium lucidum], [Laserpitium krapfii], [Vicia villosa], [Symphytum tuberosum], [Erythronium dens-canis], [Pteridium aquilinium] and the serpentine plants [Asplenium cuneifolium] ssp. [serpentini], [Campanula servicaria], [Crocus veluchensis], [Stachys scardica], [Helleborus multifidus] ssp. [serbicus]. They are developed within the Illyrian and Moesian beech forest zones and generally occupy steeper, stonier slopes and lower elevations than the serpentine [Pinus sylvestris] woods of unit 42.5C51.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian limestone [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] [s.s.] ([Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra]) woods on limestones of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina, within the range of Illyrian beech forests, uncommon black pine facies of the calcicole [Pinus sylvestris] woods of unit 42.5C6.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian dolomite [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] [s.s.] ([Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra]) woods of dolomites and dolomite rendzinas of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia and Slovenia, with [Erica herbacea] ([Erica carnea]), [Galium lucidum], [Genista januensis], [Aquilegia vulgaris], [Buphthalmum salicifolium], [Teucrium chamaedrys], [Carex humilis], [Anthericum ramosum], [Cyclamen purpurascens], [Polygala chamaebuxus], [Hepatica nobilis], [Geranium sanguineum], [Helleborus niger] ssp. [macranthus], [Epipactis atrorubens], [Carex alba]. They are developed within the Illyrian beech forest zone and often occupy somewhat lower elevations than the similar dolomite [Pinus sylvestris] woods of unit 42.5C52.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian submediterranean [Pinus nigra] forests
description: [Pinus nigra] [s.s.] ([Pinus nigra] ssp. [nigra]) pine woods on dolomites and limestones of the submediterranean [Ostryo-Carpinion adriaticum] zone of the Dinarides, extending from sea level to about 1400m, and from the Velebit in the north to Montenegro in the south.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Pinus dalmatica] forests
description: Forests of [Pinus dalmatica] of Dalmatian coastal areas, limited to the sub-Mediterranean level of the Biokovo range and the Mediterranean zone of the Peljesac peninsula and of the islands of Brac and Hvar.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Salzmann's pine forests
description: [Pinus salzmannii] ([Pinus nigra] ssp. [salzmannii], [Pinus nigra] ssp. [clusiana], [Pinus nigra] ssp. [mauretanica]) forests of Spain, the Causses and North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Causses Salzmann's pine forests
description: Isolated [Pinus salzmannii] var. [cebennensis] woods of the southern edge of the Causses, with an undergrowth typical of supra-Mediterranean white oak forests at the upper limit and of evergreen oak forests at lower altitudes; [Buxus sempervirens] is usually abundant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Pyrenean Salzmann's pine forests
description: Meso- and supra-Mediterranean [Pinus salzmannii] var. [pyrenaica] forests of Pyrenean foothills; they are extensive in the southeastern foothills, with outposts in the central foothills, in Catalonian ranges and, very locally, on the north side of the range (Valley of the Tˆt, Conflent). The understorey is formed by the cortŠge of [Quercus ilex] ([Juniperus oxycedrus], [Rosmarinus officinalis], [Quercus ilex]) at low altitudes, and by that of [Quercus pubescens] ([Buxus sempervirens], [Juniperus communis], [Amelanchier ovalis], [Cornus sanguinea], [Lonicera etrusca]) at higher altitudes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern-Iberian Salzmann's pine forests
description: Isolated [Pinus salzmannii] var. [pyrenaica] woods of the northern Iberian Range (Soria).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cordilleran Salzmann's pine forests
description: Isolated silicicolous [Pinus salzmannii] var. [iberica] woods of the Cordillera Central, limited to small enclaves in the Sierra de Gredos and associated ranges, in the Rio Tietar-Rio Alberche area.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern-Iberian Salzmann's pine forests
description: Supra- and, locally, oro-Mediterranean [Pinus salzmannii] var. [hispanica] forests of the Southern Iberian Range, occupying extensive areas in the Serrania de Cuenca, the Maestrazgo and associated ranges, mostly on limestones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baetic Salzmann's pine forests
description: Supra- and, locally, oro-Mediterranean [Pinus salzmannii] var. [hispanica] forests of the Baetic and sub-Baetic ranges, covering vast expanses, mostly on limestones, in the sierras de Cazorla, Segura and Alcaraz, with outposts in the Sierra de Baza, the Sierra de Filabres and the calcareous periphery of the Sierra Nevada.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean Baetic Salzmann's pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus salzmannii] accompanied by a cortŠge similar to that of thermophilous oak forests, including [Quercus rotundifolia], [Juniperus oxycedrus], [Lavandula latifolia], [Erinacea anthyllis], [Rosmarinus officinalis], [Genista scorpius], [Crataegus monogyna], [Berberis hispanica], [Rosa pouzinii], [Daphne laureola], [Acer granatense], [Paeonia officinalis], of the sierras de Cazorla, Segura and Alcaraz, the erra de Baza, the Sierra de Filabres and the calcareous periphery of the Sierra Nevada.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Mediterranean Baetic Salzmann's pine forests
description: Oro-Mediterranean woods of [Pinus salzmannii], more open than those of 42.6361 and occupying very limited areas in the sierras de Cazorla, Segura and Alcaraz, with a shrub layer of [Juniperus sabina] and [Juniperus nana], accompanied by [Ononis aragonensis], [Genista lobelii] ssp. [longipes], [Daphne oleoides] and [Prunus prostrata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African Salzmann's pine forests
description: [Pinus salzmannii] ssp. [mauretanica]) forests of North Africa, limited to very few stands, in particular, on limestones of the Djurdjura and on altered dolomites of the Rif, east of Chefchaouen, at altitudes comprised between 1300 and 1700 m.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican laricio pine forests
description: [Pinus laricio] forests of the mountains of Corsica. The nuthatch [Sitta whiteheadi] is endemic to these forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dense montane laricio forests
description: [Pinus laricio] forests of the montane level of Corsica, where they replace beech forests, either entirely in some ranges or mostly on adrets and as subclimax communities elsewhere. The undergrowth, fairly similar to that of beech forests, includes [Ilex aquifolium], [Daphne laureola], [Pteridium aquilinum], [Allium pendulinum], [Helleborus lividus] ssp. [corsicus], [Galium odoratum]. Epiphytic lichens are often abundant, including [Cetraria glauca], [Hypogymnia bitteriana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Open montane laricio forests
description: Open [Pinus laricio] forests of Corsica, growing at the upper forest limit or on steep rocky slopes, often with birches, [Betula pendula].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean laricio forests
description: [Pinus laricio] forests of the supra-Mediterranean level of Corsica, with an often dense understorey of [Erica arborea] and [Erica scoparia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calabrian laricio pine forests
description: [Pinus laricio] var. [calabrica] forests of the Sila, the Aspromonte and Etna.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sila and Aspromonte laricio forests
description: [Pinus laricio] forests of the Sila Greca, the Sila Grande, the Sila Piccola and the Aspramonte, where they replace beech forests in drier areas within the montane zone, forming at times, particularly in the Sila Grande, imposing expanses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Etna laricio forests
description: [Pinus laricio] forests of the north flank of Mount Etna.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Banat and Pallas' pine forests
description: Montane forests of [Pinus pallasiana], or of [Pinus banatica] ([Pinus nigra] var. [banatica]), of the southern Carpathians, the Balkan peninsula, Cyprus, Anatolia and Crimea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic Pallas' pine forests
description: Montane forests of [Pinus pallasiana] of Greece and the Balkan peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Taygetos Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana]-dominated forests occupying steep rocky slopes of the montane level of the Taygetos mountains of the Peloponnese.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Parnon Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana]-dominated forests of the montane level of the Parnon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Peloponnese Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana]-dominated forests of the montane level of the Killini, Chelmos mountains of the northern Peloponnese.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Pindus Pallas' pine forests
description: Isolated [Pinus pallasiana]-dominated forests of the montane level of mountains of the southern Pindus complex, in particular of the Giona group, and of outlying ranges in Beotia and Eubaea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Olympian Pallas' pine forests
description: Forests dominated by [Pinus nigra] ssp. [pallasiana] occupying slopes and ridges of the 500 metre to 1500 metre belt of the Thessalian Mount Olympus, Pieria and Vourninos, extending from the upper limit of the Mediterranean forest and shrub level to, and into, the beech forest zone, accompanied by species characteristic of both the Mediterranian and montane levels, most extensive on the northern side, constituting the most important forest element of the Olympic system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Pindus Pallas' pine forests
description: Forests dominated by [Pinus nigra] ssp. [pallasiana] of the northern and central Pindus system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonide Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus nigra] ssp. [pallasiana]-dominated forests of the Pelagonides of north-central Greece, Albania and the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, north to the middle Treska Valley.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide Pallas' pine forests
description: Scattered [Pinus nigra] ssp. [pallasiana]-dominated forests of the Rila, Pirin, Slavianka, Rhodopes, Vrondous and Falakron, most widespread in the Rhodope, in part accompanied by [Quercus dalechampii], [Ostrya carpinifolia] (southern Rhodopes), [Abies alba] or [Pinus sylvestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range Pallas' pine forests
description: Uncommon [Pinus nigra] ssp. [pallasiana]-dominated forests of the beech and durmast oak levels of the western and central Balkan Range and its associated southern chains, sometimes accompanied by [Abies alba], by [Quercus dalechampii], or by [Ostrya carpinifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moeso-Macedonian Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus nigra] ssp. [pallasiana]-dominated forests of the Moeso-Macedonian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus nigra] ssp. [pallasiana]-dominated forests of the Aegean islands of Thasos and Samos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Banat pine forests
description: Relict thermophile forests of [Pinus banatica] ([Pinus nigra] var. [banatica]) developed on calcareous substrates of the montane level of the Southern Carpathians, in particular, of the Banat, with [Genista radiata], [Fraxinus ornus], [Cotinus coggygria], [Biscutella laevigata], [Ceterach officinarum], [Festuca xanthina], [Seseli rigidum], [Campanula kladniana], [Centaurea rhenana] and [Campanula divergens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian Pallas' pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus pallasiana] var. [caramanica] of the cold, snowy, high altitudes, above 1400 metres, of the Troodos Range, with [Euphorbia cassia] and numerous Cyprian endemics or near-endemics, among which [Platanthera holmboei], [Epipactis troodi], [Thlaspi cyprium] and [Jurinea cypria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lower Cyprian Pallas' pine forests
description: Lower altitudinal belt of [Pinus pallasiana] forests of Mount Troodos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Upper Cyprian Pallas' pine forests
description: Upper altitudinal belt of [Pinus pallasiana] forests of Mount Troodos, with [Juniperus foetidissima], [Sorbus umbellata] ssp. [oblongifolia], and the Cyprian endemics [Alyssum troodii], [Nepeta troodi], [Cynoglossum troodi], [Scorzonera trooda].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests of northwestern, southwestern and southern interior Anatolia, occurring between 1200 and 1800 metres altitude, in areas of only a few months of snow cover, moderate to low precipitation and up to six months of summer drought a year.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Phrygian Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests of northern and northwestern interior Anatolia, and of interior ranges of the western Pontic system, located at altitudes between 1200 and 1800 metres, in areas of two to four months of snow cover and four to five months of summer drought a year, with an understorey of [Cistus laurifolius], [Chamaecytisus pygmaeus], [Genista lydia], [Hypericum montbretii], [Iris chatii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Phrygian Pallas' pine forests
description: Western interior Anatolian forests of [Pinus pallasiana] accompanied by [Quercus cerris], [Populus tremula] and [Ferulago galbanifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Phrygian [Sesleria] Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests of western Anatolia, on marly calcareous and green rocks, with [Sesleria argentea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Pontic Pallas'pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests of the northwestern Anatolian pre-Pontic region, with [Lathyrus czeczottianus], situated on andesites, with marginal, more open, formations, extending locally to the southern side of the Pontic chain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carian Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests of southwestern Anatolia, located on superficial soils, at altitudes between 1200 and 1800 metres, in the region lying between Fetihye-Mugla and Izmir, in areas with two to three months of snow cover and four to five months of summer drought a year; the understorey comprises [Adenocarpus complicatus], [Chamaecytisus eriocarpus], [Genista anatolica], [Genista lydia], [Chronanthus orientalis], [Hypericum adenocarpum], [Teucrium kotschyenum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Igneous Carian Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests established on eruptive rock, with [Symphytum brachycalyx].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenstone Carian Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests established on greenstone, with [Teucrium sandrasicum] and [Centaurea ensifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dolomite Carian Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests established on dolomitic rock, with [Agropyron panormitanum] and [Sesleria anatolica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Taurus Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests of the Taurus and the Amanus mountains, sometimes accompanied by [Juniperus excelsa] or [Cedrus atlantica], located at altitudes between 1200-1400 metres and 1900-2100 metres, in areas with two to three months of snow cover, 500-1500 mm of rain and three to six months of summer drought a year, occupying more xeric sites than the cedar and fir forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calcareous Taurus Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests occupying calcareous substrates of the Taurus Mountains, with [Thlaspi oxyceras].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sandstone Taurus Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests occupying marly sandstones of the Taurus Mountains, with [Symphytum palaestinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean Pallas' pine forests
description: [Pinus pallasiana] forests forming a narrow altitudinal belt on the southeastern slope of the southern part of the Crimean mountains, below the  forests of [Pinus sylvestris] ssp. [hamata] ([Pinus kochiana]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Black pine reforestation
description: Plantations of pines of the [Pinus nigra] group, accompanied by seminatural undergrowth formations. These are usually calciphilous communities when accompanying [Pinus nigra], acidophilous ones when with [Pinus laricio]. In all cases they can be specified by codes borrowed from other units, used in conjunction with unit 42.67.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High oro-Mediterranean pine forests
description: Woods of [Pinus heldreichii], [Pinus leucodermis] or [Pinus peuce].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: White-barked pine forests
description: Local treeline formations of [Pinus heldreichii] or [Pinus leucodermis] restricted to the southern Balkans, northern Greece and southern Italy, usually open and with an undergrowth formed by stripped grasslands on dry, often stony or rocky soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italian white-barked pine forests
description: Rare white-barked pine formations of high southern Italian mountains, limited to the Abruzzian Appenines (Montagna della Maiella), the Campanian Apennines (monti Picentini) and the Lucano-Calabrian Apennines (Pollino, monti Alpi di Latronico, monte la Spina, monti di Orsomarso, monte Montea, serra delle Ciavole).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pindus white-barked pine forests
description: White-barked pine formations of high elevations of the Pindus, mostly on ophiolites, at altitudes above 1600 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Olympus white-barked pine forests
description: White-barked pine formations of Mount Olympus, mostly on jurassic and triassic limestones at altitudes above 1350 metres, with an undergrowth including [Juniperus nana], [Daphne laureola], [Daphne mezereum], [Daphne oleoides], [Genista radiata], [Buxus sempervirens], [Cotoneaster integerrimus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonide white-barked pine forests
description: White-barked pine formations of high elevations of the Pelagonides of Albania, the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and northern Greece, south to the Vourinos and the Vermion.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: South Dinaric white-barked pine forests
description: White-barked pine formations of high elevations of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Montenegro and northern Albania, extending from the Prenj range to the Prokletije and other ranges immediately north of the Metohija depression.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide white-barked pine forests
description: [Pinus leucodermis] forests of the Pirin and the Slavianka Mountains, on calcareous substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macedonian pine woods
description: [Pinus peuce] formations, restricted to the subalpine zone of the high mountains of the Balkan peninsula south to extreme northern Greece (Voras, Varnous, Rhodope).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonide Macedonian pine woods
description: [Pinus peuce] forests of the subalpine zone of the high Pelagonides of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia, Albania and northern Greece, recorded, in particular, from the Rudoka, Voras-Nidze and Varnous ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Dinaric Macedonian pine woods
description: [Pinus peuce] forests of the subalpine zone of the southern Dinarides of Montenegro and northern Albania, in the Prokleti and Metochi mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rila and Pirin Macedonian pine forests
description: Forests dominated by [Pinus peuce] of high altitudes of the Rila and Pirin ranges of Bulgaria, forming a belt of mixed or pure stands within the 1650 to 2100 metre zone and harbouring the largest populations of the species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodope Macedonian pine woods
description: [Pinus peuce]-dominated forests of the western Rhodope mountains of Bulgaria and of the Elatia region of Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Macedonian pine woods
description: [Pinus peuce] forests of the central Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean pine woods
description: Mediterranean and thermo-Atlantic forests of thermophilous pines, mostly appearing as substitution or paraclimactic stages of forests of the [Quercetalia ilicis] or [Ceratonio-Rhamnetalia].  Long-established plantations of these pines, within their natural area of occurrence, and with an undergrowth basically similar to that of paraclimactic formations, are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Maritime pine forests
description: Forests and plantations of [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [atlantica] of southwestern France and the western Iberian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Charente pine-holm oak forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [atlantica] forests with a subcanopy of [Quercus ilex],  [Arbutus unedo] and sometimes [Quercus pubescens] or [Quercus robur] and an undergrowth of [Rubia peregrina], [Cistus salvifolius], [Daphne gnidium] and, in the more acid stands, [Ulex europaeus], [Cytisus scoparius], [Erica scoparia] or, in more calcareous ones, [Hedera helix], [Ruscus aculeatus], developed on mostly calcareous inner dunes of the low-rainfall coasts of Vend‚e, Charente-maritime and northern Gironde, including the islands of Noirmoutier, Yeu, R‚ and Ol‚ron.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aquitanian pine-cork oak forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [atlantica] forests with a subcanopy of [Quercus suber], [Arbutus unedo] and sometimes [Quercus robur] and an undergrowth of [Erica cinerea], [Pteridium aquilinum], [Frangula alnus], [Rubia peregrina] and, in the more open stands, [Cistus salvifolius], [Cytisus scoparius], [Erica scoparia], [Calluna vulgaris] or, in more closed ones, [Hedera helix], [Ruscus aculeatus], [Ilex aquifolium], developed on acidocline inner dunes of the warmer, more humid coasts of the Marensin, between the Eyre and the Adour river mouths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Landes maritime pine plantations
description: [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [atlantica] woodland of southwestern France other than the dunal formations listed in units 42.811 and 42.812.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian maritime pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [atlantica] forests of Galicia, Portugal and neighbouring areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesogean pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [pinaster] ([Pinus mesogeensis]) of the western Mediterranean, mostly in siliceous meso-Mediterranean, upper meso-Mediterranean and supra-Mediterranean situations of Spain, Portugal, Corsica, southeastern France, northwestern Italy, Sardinia and Pantelleria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] forests of the Iberian peninsula, appearing mostly as substitution communities of [Quercus rotundifolia], [Quercus pyrenaica] or, locally, [Quercus suber], [Quercus faginea] woodlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern-Iberian mesogean pine forests
description: Very extensive [Pinus pinaster] forests of the Northern Iberian Range and neighbouring areas, occupying siliceous, often sandy substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cordilleran mesogean pine forests
description: Extensive [Pinus pinaster] forests of the Cordillera Central and neighbouring areas, particularly developed on the southern slope of the range, occupying siliceous substrates, mostly gneiss and granite.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern-Iberian mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] forests of the Southern Iberian Range and plateaux of eastern New Castile.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siliceous Southern-Iberian mesogean pine forests
description: Widespread and extensive silicicolous [Pinus pinaster] forests, mostly occupying reddish sandy soils (rodenales).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calcicolous Southern-Iberian mesogean pine forests
description: Less common calcicolous [Pinus pinaster] forests of Jurassic and Cretaceous limestones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cazorlan mesogean pine forests
description: Extensive [Pinus pinaster] forests of the Sierras de Cazorla, Segura, Alcaraz and Sagra, mostly on Mesozoic limestones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Andalusian mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] forests of southern mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aljibe mesogean pine forests
description: Silicicolous thermo-Mediterranean [Pinus pinaster] forests of the Aljibe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Andalusian peridotite mesogean pine forests
description: Peridotite [Pinus pinaster] forests of Western Malaga.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Andalusian dolomite mesogean pine forests
description: Dolomite [Pinus pinaster] forests of Malaga and Granada mountains, with a calciphilous undergrowth formed by [Buxus balearica], [Ulex argenteus], [Cistus libanotis], [Thymelaea tartonraira], [Linum suffruticosum], [Thymus erianthus], [Thymus longiflorus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Andalusian calcicolous mesogean pine forests
description: Limestone [Pinus pinaster] forests of eastern Andalusia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Andalusian silicicolous mesogean pine forests
description: Siliceous [Pinus pinaster] forests of eastern Andalusia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Leonese mesogean pine forests
description: Isolated [Pinus pinaster] woods of Nogarejas and Castrocontrigo in southern Leon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Catalonian mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] forests of Catalonia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corbières mesogean pine forests
description: Isolated [Pinus pinaster]-dominated woods of the CorbiŠres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Franco-Italian mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] forests of siliceous lower meso-Mediterranean areas of Provence, of marls and limestones of the upper meso-Mediterranean level of the Maritime Alps and the Ligurian Alps, and of mostly siliceous or clayey soils of the hills of Liguria and Tuscany.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster]-dominated forests of the meso- and supra-Mediterranean levels of Corsica, mostly on granitic substrates; they are very developed, accompanied by a maquis-like understorey, in the meso-Mediterranean zone, mostly at its upper tier; they occur locally within the supra-Mediterranean zone, on adrets and at lower altitudes, as facies of laricio pine forests.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] formations on granitic substrates of northern Sardinia, with [Arbutus unedo], [Quercus ilex], [Rosmarinus officinalis], [Erica arborea], [Genista corsica], [Lavandula stoechas], [Rubia peregrina], [Calicotome spinosa], [Pistacia lentiscus], [Teucrium marum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pantellerian mesogean pine forests
description: [Pinus pinaster] woods of Pantelleria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pantellerian mesogean pine-[Genista] forests
description: Dominant, probably subclimactic woodlands of Pantelleria, constituted by [Pinus pinaster], with [Genista aspalathoides], [Erica multiflora], [Cistus salvifolius], [Lavandula stoechas], [Rosmarinus officinalis], [Daphne gnidium], [Arbutus unedo], [Myrtus communis], [Erica arborea], [Carex illegitima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pantellerian mesogean pine-holm oak forests
description: Mixed [Pinus pinaster] and [Quercus ilex] formations of Pantelleria Grande and Monte Gibele, with [Arbutus unedo] and [Erica arborea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moroccan mesogean pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [hamiltonii] of the humid and semihumid levels of mountains of Morocco, from 1019 metres in the Rif and between 1500 and 2200 metres in the middle and high Atlas. [Cedrus atlantica] and, in the Rif, the North African endemic [Abies marocana] and [Pinus salzmannii] ssp. [mauretanica] may enter in the composition of the forest.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Numidian mesogean pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus pinaster] ssp. [renoui] of Numidian sandstones of the humid littoral zone of eastern Algeria and extreme western Tunisia, with [Arbutus unedo], [Erica arborea], [Erica scoparia], [Pistacia lentiscus], [Halimium halimifolium], [Teucrium fruticans], [Ampelodesmos mauritanica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stone pine forests
description: Mediterranean forests and old naturalized plantations of [Pinus pinea].  Antique introduction in many areas makes the distinction between spontaneous forests and long-established formations of artificial origin often difficult. These are thus included, while recent, obviously artificial groves are not.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the Iberian peninsula, where they reach their greatest development.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Andalusian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the lowlands of western Andalusia and adjacent areas, with [Halimium halimifolium], [Halimium rosmarinifolium], [Calicotome villosa], [Cistus salvifolius], [Cistus crispus], [Erica scoparia], [Corema album], [Rhamnus oleoides], [Chamaerops humilis], [Juniperus phoenicea].
