source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lusitanian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the coasts of Portugal, notably the Setubal peninsula, pure or with [Pinus pinaster].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Castilian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the plateaux of Old Castile in the provinces of Valladolid, Zamora, Avila and Segovia, pure or with [Pinus pinaster]; the undergrowth includes [Cistus laurifolius], [Cytisus scoparius], [Crataegus monogyna], [Salvia officinalis], [Lavandula latifolia], [Juniperus communis], [Juniperus thurifera] and tufts of [Corynephorus canescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cordilleran stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the foothills of the Cordillera Central, particularly in areas between Guadarrama and Gredos, pure or with [Pinus pinaster]; the undergrowth, similar to that of evergreen oak forests, includes [Juniperus oxycedrus], [Retama sphaerocarpa], [Cytisus scoparius], [Pistacia terebinthus], [Lavandula pedunculata], [Helichrysum serotinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Catalonian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of coastal and lowland Catalonia, often natural, and with an abundant shrub layer comprising [Arbutus unedo], [Erica arborea], [Ulex australis], [Calicotome spinosa], [Cistus albidus], [Cistus monspeliensis], [Cistus salvifolius], [Cistus laurifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Morena stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the Sierra Morena, largely represented by plantations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Manchegan stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the foothills of the Southern Iberian Range and the plateaux of La Mancha, also mostly of artificial origin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balearic stone pine woods
description: [Pinus pinea] formations of the Balearic Islands, native only on Ibiza and Formentera.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Provence stone pine woods
description: [Pinus pinea] formations of Provence, possibly spontaneous on coastal sands and in the Maures area.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal Provence stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] woods of coastal sands, particularly of the Camargue, where it is associated with [Juniperus phoenicea] ssp. [lycia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Permian Provence stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] woods of the Permian depression encircling the Maures, and a few neighbouring localities, associated mostly with maquis of [Cistus monspeliensis], [Cistus salvifolius], [Cistus ladanifer], [Erica scoparia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican stone pine woods
description: [Pinus pinea] formations of the littoral of Corsica, some of which may be of natural origin, in particular on old dunes of the east coast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] formations of Sardinia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iglesiente near-natural stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forest of coastal dunes of Iglesiente, west of Monte Linas, comprising plurisecular trees and of undoubted indigenous origin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian seminatural stone pine forests
description: Other [Pinus pinea] woods of Sardinia, some particularly in the vicinity of Monte Linas, of possible native origin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sicilian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] formations of the Monti Peloritani, northwestern Sicily, of probable native origin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italic stone pine forests
description: Large [Pinus pinea] forests and ancient plantations of the Tyrhenian and  Adriatic coasts of the Italian peninsula, in Liguria, Toscany, Latium, Campania, Emilia-Romagna (Ravenna) and Friuli-Venetia Giulia (Grado). At least the forests of the Adriatic coast, between Ravenna and the P“, are of natural origine, with a continuous record since post-glacial times.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] woods of the littoral and coastal hills of the Peloponnese, Chalcidice, Crete and Aegean islands, rather local but probably in part, at least, spontaneous; a splendid example exists, in particular, on Skiathos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Albanian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the southern Adriatic and Otranto Canal coastlands of Albania, where they form, in particular, considerable forests of varied composition on coastal sands between the Shkumbin and Seman rivers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dalmatian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the eastern Adriatic coastlands, distributed, in particular, in Istria and the Gulf of Rijeka and in southern Croatia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of Mediterranean enclaves on the southern Black Sea coast of Anatolia in extreme eastern Paphlegonia and in western and eastern Lazistan, some, at least, apparently indigenous. In Lazistan, they occur, in particular, on hill slopes, from sea level to the top of the coastal range, on eruptive rocks, with a rich undergrowth including [Cistus creticus], [Pistacia palaestina], [Juniperus oxycedrus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean Anatolian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the Aegean and east Mediterranean coasts of Anatolia and of their Mediterranean hinterland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of the Aegean hinterland of Anatolia in Mysia, Lydia and Caria, in places extensive, probably indigenous and possibly climax, in particular on sandstones away from the immediate coastal vicinity.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pamphylian stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] formations of sandy soils of the east Mediterranean coast of southwestern Anatolia, in the Gulf of Antalya, probably indigenous.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cilician stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] formations of the mesomediterranean hills of the periphery of the Cilician plain in southern central Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Phenician stone pine forests
description: [Pinus pinea] forests of Lebanon, isolated at the southeastern limit of the range of the species. They may have formerly extended to the coastal plain of Philistaea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aleppo pine forests
description: Woods of [Pinus halepensis], a frequent colonist of thermo- and calcicolous meso-mediterranean scrubs. The distinction between spontaneous forests and long-established formations of artificial origin is often difficult. The latter are thus included here, while recent, obviously artificial groves are not.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] forests of Spain, considered native for at least two-thirds of their considerable expanse; they are mostly restricted to eastern regions on the Mediterranean slope of the Catalonian mountains, the Maestrazgo, the pre-Baetic ranges of the upper Guadalquivir basin, the southern Andalusian mountains; they penetrate farther inland in the Ebro basin and around the headwaters of the Tagus and Guadalquivir systems. They appear to extend north along the coast of the French Golfe du Lion to the region of Agde.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balearic Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] formations of the Balearics, present and probably native on all the major islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Provenço-Ligurian Aleppo pine forests
description: Mostly lower meso-Mediterranean [Pinus halepensis] forests of Provence and of the lower slopes and coastlines of the Maritime and Ligurian Alps, extensive and undoubtedly native.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican Aleppo pine woods
description: Rare and local [Pinus halepensis] woods of the Corsican coasts, some, at least, possibly natural.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian Aleppo pine woods
description: [Pinus halepensis] formations of Sardinia, where certainly native woods occur on Isola di San Pietro and the Sulcis coast of Iglesiente.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sicilian Aleppo pine woods
description: [Pinus halepensis] formations of Sicily and peripheral islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mainland Sicilian Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] woods of mainland Sicily, where native formations occur on the southwestern slope of the Iblei massif (Vittoria).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Egadi Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] woods of the Egadi islands (Marettimo, Isla Grande, San Pantaleo).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lampedusa Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] woods of the Pelagie (Lampedusa).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pantelleria Aleppo pine forests
description: Uncommon [Pinus halepensis]-dominated facies of the pine woods of Pantelleria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Maltese Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] forests of the Maltese Islands. Natural forests, formerly widespread, were cut to extinction. A near-natural self-regenerating woodland,  originating from replantation exists on Malta (Buskett). It has a rich undergrowth of [Quercus ilex], [Olea europaea] var. [sylvestris], [Ceratonia siliqua], [Pistacia lentiscus] and other thermomediterranean shrubs, herbs and climbers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italic Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] formations of the Italian peninsula; extensive, probably at least partially native ones, are individualized in the subdivisions below.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gargano Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] forests of monte Gargano and the Tremiti islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Metapontine Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] forests of the Gulf of Taranto area, in particular of the Metapontine littoral.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Umbrian Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] forests of southern Umbria, in the Narni and Spoleto-Terni areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italic Aleppo pine reforestation
description: Other [Pinus halepensis] formations of peninsular Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] formations of Greece, where the species is relatively widespread, particularly in Attica, Thessaly, the coasts of the Peloponnese and of central continental Greece, the Ionian islands, Chalcidici, the northern Sporades, Euboea and Skiros.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian Aleppo pine forests
description: [Pinus halepensis] forests and woods of the southern and central part of the meso-Mediterranean [Orno-Quercetum illicis] zone of the Balkan peninsula, extending in a narrow coastal and archipelagic band from the Gulf of Sarand‰ to northern Dalmatia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean Aleppo pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus halepensis] of the Mediterranean coastal regions of the Middle East. Extensive and varied in the southern part of the region, they are represented further north by isolated outposts in the coastal region of Syria and in south central Anatolia, where [Pinus halepensis] occurs in the thermo-Mediterranean zone of the Cilician plain, apparently mixed with [Pinus brutia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African Aleppo pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus halepensis] of Mediterranean North Africa, extending from sea level to 2000 metres in the semiarid zone and the drier part of the subhumid zone. They occupy considerable surfaces in Tunisia and in southern Oran. In Morocco extensive forests occur only in the High Atlas, with scattered smaller stands elsewhere, in particular on the Mediterranean slope of the Rif and in the central Middle Atlas. A few formations exist in Cyrenaica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests of Crete, the eastern Aegean islands, extreme southeastern continental Europe, Anatolia, Cyprus and the eastern Mediterranean coastal regions. Eastern vicariants of Aleppo pine forests (unit 42.84), they comprise, however, taller, more luxuriant, and often extensive, formations. Disjunct formations of this pine or of related species, described from Crimea and the Caucasian region ([Pinus pityusa], [Pinus stankewiczii], [Pinus eldarica]) have been included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests of Crete
description: [Pinus brutia]-dominated forests of Crete and its satellite islands Gavdos and Gaidaronisi, pure or mixed with [Cupressus sempervirens]; they are widespread in particular in the White Mountains, the Psiloriti range, the Dikti range and, locally, in the Sitia mountains and the Asterousia mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cretan lentisc Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests with garrigue undergrowth of [Pistacia lentiscus], [Cistus creticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cretan phrygana Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests with a phrygana undergrowth of [Sarcopoterium spinosum] or [Thymus capitatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cretan grassy Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests with sparce grassy undergrowth on stony ground.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests of Lesbos
description: Extensive [Pinus brutia] forests of Lesbos, occupying Mount Olympus and surrounding hills in the south-eastern quadrant of the island, as well as parts of the Kuratsonas range in the northwest; these forests harbour the only European population of the nuthatch [Sitta krueperi] and the most significant one of the orchid [Comperia comperiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesbian humid montane Aegean pine forests
description: Humid montane [Pinus brutia] forests of Lesbos, with a high, fairly dense [Quercus coccifera]-dominated understorey and abundant lichen growth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesbian cistus Aegean pine forests
description: Dry collinar [Pinus brutia] forests of Lesbos, with low, sparse undergrowth formed mostly by [Cistus salvifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesbian heath Aegean pine forests
description: Dry collinar [Pinus brutia] forests of Lesbos, with continuous ericaceous undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests of Samos
description: [Pinus brutia] forests covering large expanses of Samos, in particular in the Ambelos range, the Kerki mountains, the southern hills and the northeastern peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Samian collinar Aegean pine forests
description: Lower altitude [Pinus brutia] forests of Samos, with [Pistacia lentiscus], [Cistus salvifolius], [Cistus parviflorus], [Sarcopoterium spinosum], [Quercus coccifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Samian montane Aegean pine forests
description: Higher altitude [Pinus brutia] forests of Samos, sometimes including [Pinus pallasiana], and with an undergrowth comprising [Quercus coccifera], [Prunus cocomilia] ([Prunus pseudarmeniaca]), [Crataegus spp].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine woods of Chios
description: Remnant forests of Chios with a composition and stratification similar to those of the forests of Samos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests of Thasos
description: Broad [Pinus brutia] belt on the lower reaches of Thasos, up to about 400 to 500 metres, mixed with [Pinus pallasiana] in the higher areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thasian kermes Aegean pine forests
description: Thasos [Pinus brutia] forests with a dense [Quercus coccifera] undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thasian bracken Aegean pine forests
description: Thasos [Pinus brutia] forests with sparse undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thasian heath Aegean pine forests
description: Thasos [Pinus brutia] forests with dense ericaceous undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine woods of Samothrace
description: Mostly sparse [Pinus brutia] formations of the lowlands of Samothrace.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests of Rhodes
description: Remnant [Pinus brutia] forests of Rhodes, still represented by some relatively natural formations with rich scrub undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests of Karpathos
description: Fairly extensive [Pinus brutia] forests of Karpathos, distributed, in particular, in the northern coastal area, the southern interior and the middle elevation of Kali Limni.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean pine forests of the Dodecanese
description: [Pinus brutia] formations of the islands of Simi, Kos, Leros and Ikaria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thracio-Macedonian Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests of Greek Thrace, of the Chalkidi peninsula and of the Black Sea region of Turkey in Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests of Anatolia and of the Dardanelles, covering extensive areas in western and southwestern Anatolia, with isolated outposts in northern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: Extensive [Pinus brutia] forests of the thermo-Mediterranean, meso-Mediterranean and, locally, supra-Mediterranean level of Caria, Pisidia, Pamphylia, Isauria, Cilicia in southwestern and south central Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Serpentine southern Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests on serpentines of the region of Koycegiz and around the Gulf of Alexandrette.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marl southern Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus brutia] on marls of the central Taurus system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Limestone southern Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: Supramediterranean forests of [Pinus brutia], accompanied by [Centaurea babylonica] or [Centaurea ptosimoppapoides], located on limestones of the Atsaki region and on ultrabasic rocks the region of Marsin and Pos, of the southern Taurus system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ultrabasic southern Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: Forests of [Pinus brutia], accompanied by [Quercus microphylla], on ultrabasic rocks around the Gulf of Alexandrette.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: Extensive [Pinus brutia] forests of the mostly meso-Mediterranean level of Mysia, Lydia, western Bithynia, western Phrygia of western Anatolia, with eastern garrigue undergrowth and dominated semideciduous or deciduous oaks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Anatolian Aegean pine forests
description: Enclave [Pinus brutia] forests of the Euxine region of northern Anatolia, characteristic, in particular, of transverse inner valleys of the Pontic Ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests of the thermo-Mediterranean, meso-Mediterranean and supra-Mediterranean levels of Cyprus, where it associates in particular with [Cupressus sempervirens] and with [Juniperus phoenicea]; it forms, in particular, great forests in the Pendadahtilos Range, in the regions of Karpassia and Akamas and in the Troodos Ranges where it replaces [Quercus alnifolia] on dry soils derived from eruptive basic rocks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean Aegean pine forests
description: [Pinus brutia] forests of Lebanon, coastal Syria and the southeast coasts of the Gulf of Alexandrette in southern central Anatolia. [Pinus halepensis] may be associated with [Pinus brutia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesopotamian Aegean pine forests
description: Isolated [Pinus brutia] forests of western slopes of the mountains lying between the Tigris and the Zab rivers, on the northern rim of the Mesopotamian high plains, in northern Irak.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean [Pinus pityusa] forests
description: Forests of [Pinus brutia] [s.l.] ([Pinus pityusa], [Pinus stankewiczii]) of the  mountains of southwestern Crimea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian Aegean pine woods
description: Formations of [Pinus brutia] or its allies in the Caucasus system, in particular stands of [Pinus eldarica], apparently limited to a single mountain site in Georgia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canary Island pine forests
description: Forests of endemic [Pinus canariensis], of the dry montane level at around 800 to 2000 metres (locally down to 500 and up to 2500 metres) in Tenerife, La Palma, Gran Canaria and Hierro, with [Chamaecytisus proliferus], [Adenocarpus foliolosus], [Cistus symphytifolius], [Lotus campylocladus], [Lotus hillebrandii], [Lotus spartioides], [Daphne gnidium], [Juniperus cedrus], [Micromeria spp.]; these forests, of which well-preserved examples have become rare, are the only habitat of [Fringilla teydea], [Dendrocopos major canariensis] and [Dendrocopos major thanneri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canary pine-rockrose forests
description: Climax [Pinus canariensis] forests of the main zone of altitudinal occurrence of the species, with an undergrowth characterized and often dominated by [Cistus symphytifolius] and comprising [Chamaecytisus proliferus], [Lotus campylocladus], [Lotus hillebrandii], [Lotus spartioides], [Juniperus cedrus], [Bystropogon origanifolius], [Argyranthemum adauctum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tenerife pine-rockrose forests
description: [Pinus canariensis] forests of Tenerife, with [Lotus campylocladus], [Chamaecytisus proliferus]; they are the main habitat of the endangered [Dendrocopos major canariensis] and of [Fringilla teydea teydea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: La Palma pine-rockrose forests
description: [Pinus canariensis] forests of La Palma, with [Lotus hillebrandii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gran Canaria pine-rockrose forests
description: [Pinus canariensis] forests of Gran Canaria, with [Cistus symphytifolius] var. [leucophyllus] and [Lotus spartioides]; they are the main habitat of the threatened [Dendrocopos major thanneri] and [Fringilla teydea polatzeki].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hierro pine-rockrose forests
description: [Pinus canariensis] forests of Hierro, with [Lotus hillebrandii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canary pine-dry scrub forests
description: Forests of dry, south-facing slopes of the Canary islands developed in the lower part of the [Pinus canariensis] belt, transitional towards juniper formations and their degradation scrubs, with an undergrowth often formed by [Cistus monspeliensis], [Euphorbia obtusifolia] ssp. [regis-jubae], [Salvia canariensis], [Micromeria hyssopifolia], [Echium aculeatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tenerife pine-dry scrub woods
description: Pine forests with a dry scrub undergrowth developed on dry, south-facing slopes of the lower part of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of Tenerife.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: La Palma pine-dry scrub woods
description: Pine forests with a dry scrub undergrowth developed on dry, south-facing slopes of the lower part of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of La Palma.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gran Canaria pine-dry scrub woods
description: Pine forests with a dry scrub undergrowth developed on dry, south-facing slopes of the lower part of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of Gran Canaria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hierro pine-dry scrub woods
description: Pine forests with a dry scrub undergrowth developed on dry, south-facing slopes of the lower part of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of Hierro.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canary pine-heath forests
description: Forests of humid, fogbound north- and northwest-facing slopes in the lower reaches of the [Pinus canariensis] belt, with an abundance of [Erica arborea] and [Myrica faya], and occasionally with [Ilex canariensis] and [Arbutus canariensis]; epiphytic lichens are abundant, as are dense carpets of mosses, in particular, [Hypnum cupressiforme]. These woods are the main habitat of [Regulus teneriffae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tenerife pine-heath forests
description: Fogbound heath-rich pine forests of the lower reaches of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of Tenerife.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: La Palma pine-heath forests
description: Fogbound heath-rich pine forests of the lower reaches of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of La Palma.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gran Canaria pine-heath forests
description: Fogbound heath-rich pine forests of the lower reaches of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of Gran Canaria, harbouring the endemic [Micromeria pineolens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hierro pine-heath forests
description: Fogbound heath-rich pine forests of the lower reaches of the [Pinus canariensis] belt of Hierro, harbouring the almost extinct [Adenocarpus ombriosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canary pine-broom woods
description: Forests of the highest altitudes of the [Pinus canariensis] belt, invaded by species of the supra-Canarian level, in particular [Adenocarpus viscosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tenerife pine-broom woods
description: High-altitude pine forests of Tenerife, with [Adenocarpus viscosus] var. [viscosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: La Palma pine-broom woods
description: High-altitude pine forests of La Palma, with [Adenocarpus viscosus] var. [spartioides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canary pine-juniper woods
description: [Pinus canariensis] and [Juniperus cedrus] forests of steep, rocky slopes of high altitudes of Tenerife and La Palma.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tenerife pine-juniper woods
description: [Pinus canariensis] and [Juniperus cedrus] forests of the edges of Las Canadas del Teide.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: La Palma pine-juniper woods
description: [Pinus canariensis] and [Juniperus cedrus] forests of the summits of La Palma.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Palaearctic cypress, juniper and yew forests
description: Woods dominated by [Cupressus sempervirens], [Juniperus spp.], [Platycladus orientalis] or [Taxus baccata] of the nemoral and Mediterranean mountains and hills of western Eurasia and North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Palaearctic cypress forests
description: Montane forests of the Mediterranean basin, of the Elburz and of the Sahara dominated by [Cupressus sempervirens], [Cupressus atlantica] or [Cupressus dupreziana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cypress forests of Crete
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] and [Cupressus sempervirens-Pinus brutia] forests of Crete occupying a wide altitudinal range, but a restricted geographical area, in the White Mountains (notably Samaria) with outposts in the Idi and Dikti mountains. Tall, closed, luxuriant forests exist, with cypresses up to 30 metres, as well as more open stands. Accompanying the cypress and [Pinus brutia] may be [Quercus coccifera], [Acer sempervirens], [Zelkova abelicea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cypress forests of Rhodes
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] and [Cupressus sempervirens]-[Pinus brutia] forests of Rhodes, represented on most mountain ranges and locally at lower altitudes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cypress woodland of Syme
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] formations of Syme, rather open and with impoverished undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cypress woodland of Kos
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] forest remnants of middle elevations of Kos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cypress woodland of Samothrace
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] formations of steep slopes of the southeastern side of Samothrace.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian cypress forests
description: [Cupressus sempervirens], [Cupressus sempervirens]-[Pinus brutia], [Cupressus sempervirens]-[Juniperus phoenicea] and [Cupressus sempervirens]-[Acer obtusifolium] forests of northern Cyprus, distributed in the 0-1200 m level, mostly on hard substrates, dense and extensive on the highest slopes of the Pendadahtilos (Kyrenia) Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian cypress forests
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] and [Cupressus sempervirens-Pinus brutia] forests of southwestern Anatolia, limited to the lower slopes of the Lycian and Isaurian Taurus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian cypress forests
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] forests scattered in the Hyrcanian zone of the Elburz range of northern Iran, with [Acer monspessulanum], [Quercus iberica], [Crataegus monogyna], [Cerasus microcarpa], [Carpinus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Levantine cypress forests
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] forests of Syria, Lebanon and Jordan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyrenaican cypress forests
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] forests of the Jebel Akhdar of northeastern Lybia, a community now apparently extinct, though the leading species may survive as isolated individuals in a few sites, including el Caf wadi.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Numidian cypress forests
description: [Cupressus sempervirens] var. [numidica] forests of the Dorsale of central Tunisia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moroccan cypress forests
description: [Cupressus atlantica] forests of the Oued N'fis basin in the semiarid level of the High Atlas of Morocco, with a few scattered stations in other parts of the range, all between 900 and 1400 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharan cypress forests
description: Relict [Cupressus dupreziana] formations of dry mountains of the Tassili-N'Ajjer, restricted to gorges and thalwegs of the Oued Tamrit and Oued Amazar and constituted by less than three hundred old trees, with little or no natural regeneration.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spanish juniper woods
description: Forest formations dominated by [Juniperus thurifera] of Spain, southern France, Corsica and North Africa. Many communities may be better described as arborescent matorrals, and listed under unit 32.136; geographical divisions can nevertheless be retained by appending the suffixes of units 42.A2 to 32.136.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian Spanish juniper forests
description: [Juniperus thurifera] forests on calcareous substrates in the supra- Mediterranean levels of the Iberian Range and neighbouring plateaux, dispersed throughout the entire system, in an arc extending from the province of Burgos to the Serrania de Cuenca and the mountains of Teruel; these constitute the main range of the species. [Pinus sylvestris] and [Pinus salzmannii] may accompany the juniper; [Juniperus hemisphaerica] and [Berberis hispanica] may be common in the undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Guadarraman Spanish juniper woods
description: Relict [Juniperus thurifera] woods of enclaves on the periphery of and within the Sierra de Guadarrama, occurring both on rare local limestone deposits and in a few siliceous stations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Guadarraman calciphilous Spanish juniper woods
description: Formations of [Juniperus thurifera] linked to local limestone deposits of the Sierra de Guadarrama area.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Guadarraman silicicolous Spanish juniper woods
description: Anomalous silicicolous [Juniperus thurifera] formations of the Sierra de Guadarrama area, with [Juniperus oxycedrus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cantabrian Spanish juniper woods
description: Relict, open [Juniperus thurifera] woodlands of dry, warm, rocky, calcareous southern slopes of the Cordillera Cantabrica, between the Rio Pisuerga and the Rio Luna, with [Juniperus nana], [Juniperus sabina], [Berberis vulgaris] ssp. [cantabrica], [Rhamnus alpinus], [Viburnum lantana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Monegros Spanish juniper woods
description: [Juniperus thurifera] woodlands on gypsiferous soils of the Ebro basin, with [Rhamnus lycioides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Manchegan Spanish juniper woods
description: [Juniperus thurifera] woods on La Mancha clay soils of the Campo de Montiel.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baetic Spanish juniper woods
description: Relict, open [Juniperus thurifera] formations of the pre-Baetic system in the Sierra Taibilla (Albacete, Murcia).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean Spanish juniper woods
description: Relict [Juniperus thurifera] wood of the supra-Mediterranean level of the Montagne de Rie, on the northern flank of the central Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Alpine Spanish juniper woods
description: [Juniperus thurifera] formations of warm calcareous supra-Mediterranean slopes of the southwestern Alps, in Dr“me, Hautes-Alpes and Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, between 700 and 1200, occasionally 1400, metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Isère Spanish juniper woods
description: [Juniperus thurifera] formations of warm calcareous supra-Mediterranean slopes of the IsŠre valley, in the western Alps, between 300 and 500 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican Spanish juniper woods
description: Open montane forests of [Juniperus thurifera], sometimes mixed with [Pinus laricio], restricted to a few valleys in the interior of Corsica with extreme temperature ranges (Pinnera, Rudda, Pruniccia)
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlas Spanish juniper woods
description: [Juniperus thurifera] woods of the Atlas system of North Africa, mostly widespread in Morocco, where they reach their greatest development on the southern slopes of the High Atlas and are also present in the Middle Atlas and in the eastern Anti-Atlas, limited in Algeria to the Aures. They are confined to the 1800 to 3150 metre cold semiarid level, mixed in the lower part of the range with [Cedrus atlantica]. The undergrowth usually includes [Bupleurum  spinosum], [Prunus prostrata], [Daphne laureola], [Crataegus laciniata], [Buxus sempervirens], [Lonicera arborea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Grecian and Persian juniper woods
description: Forest formations dominated by [Juniperus excelsa] or the closely allied [Juniperus macropoda] ([Juniperus polycarpos], [Juniperus seravshanica]) of the Irano-Turanian plateaux and mountains of Anatolia, Iran, Afghanistan, extending to Lebanon, the Caucasus, Crimea, Cyprus and the Balkanic peninsula, in the periphery of the Pelagonides and Rhodopides. Arborescent matorrals, somewhat more widespread in Mediterranean and sub-Mediterranean regions, have been listed under unit 32.1331; montane prostrate scrubs, often difficult to segregate sharply from the mountain juniper woods in unit 31.438.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Hellenic Grecian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus excelsa] forests of the [Ostryo-Carpinion] zone of the southern periphery of the Pelagonides, in particular of the mountains surrounding Lake Prespa in northern Greece where they occur up to 900-1000 m.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Rhodopide Grecian juniper woods
description: Woods of [Juniperus excelsa], of the western and northern periphery of the Rhodopides, localized in the southwestern Bulgarian Struma trough, and in the northern foothills of the central Rhodope mountains near Krichim and Bachkovo, usually open, with deciduous forest elements including [Fraxinus ornus], [Pistacia terebinthus], [Carpinus orientalis], sometimes [Quercus pubescens], and many Mediterranean species, such as [Phillyrea latifolia], [Asparagus acutifolius], [Lonicera etrusca], [Achnatherum bromoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Paeonian Grecian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus excelsa] forests of the [Ostryo-Carpinion] zone of the northern periphery of the Pelagonides, in particular of the Vardar and Crna Reka valleys of the northern F.Y.R. of Macedonia, at an altitude of 100-400 metres.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian Grecian juniper woods
description: Forests of [Juniperus excelsa] of the Troodos Range, where the species locally (Madari Peak, Papoutsa Peak) replaces [Pinus pallasiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian Grecian juniper woods
description: Presteppic, meso-Mediterranean and subalpine [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forests of Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane Taurus Grecian juniper forests
description: High altitude presteppic [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forests of the Taurus and Anti-Taurus of southern Anatolia, in the 1900-2200 meter range, in which the juniper may be accompanied by [Cedrus libani], [Abies cilicica], [Pinus pallasiana] with an undergrowth formed by [Berberis crataegina], [Berberis cretica], [Lonicera nummulariifolia], [Amygdalus orientalis] and [Rosa orientalis], or by tragacanthic hedgehog heaths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Treeline Taurus Grecian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated open woodland formations of the highest forested elevations of the Taurus system, above 2300-2400 metres, with an understorey formed by grasslands of the [Tanacion preteriti] in the west, of the [Agropyro-Stachyon] in the center and the east, representing many narrowly endemic communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian Grecian juniper steppe-woods
description: Presteppic [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forest formations of the semiarid (xero-Euxinian) belt surronding the Anatolian plateau, in particular of the inner valleys and inner slopes of the Pontic Ranges and of the Taurus system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Anatolian Grecian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forest formations, accompanied by Mediterranean brush, maquis or garrigues in the undergrowth, forming locally bin Meso-Mediterranean enclaves of the Pontic Ranges as well as in Aegean and East-Mediterranean southern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caucasian Grecian juniper woods
description: [Pistacia mutica-Juniperus excelsa] forests of terra rossa dry slopes of the Black Sea coastal regions of the Great Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crimean Grecian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forests of the southern Crimean coast and of the Crimean mountains, accompanied by [Elytrigia nodosa], [Achnatherum bromoides], [Jurinea sordida], [Teucrium polium], [Jasminum fruticans], [Pistacia mutica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western coastal Crimean Grecian juniper forests
description: [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forests of the southwestern part of the southern Crimean coast, with [Cistus tauricus], [Fibigia clypeata], [Arbutus andrachne].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern coastal Crimean Grecian juniper forests
description: [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forests of the eastern part of the southern Crimean coast, with [Linosyris villosa], [Bothriochloa ischaemum], [Agropyron ponticum], [Carex caryophyllea], [Eryngium campestre], [Pimpinella lithophila].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane Crimean Grecian juniper forests
description: [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forests of the Crimean mountains, with [Phleum phleoides], [Potentilla taurica], [Campanula taurica], [Melica monticola], [Lappula barbata], [Alyssum rostratum], [Filipendula vulgaris], [Alopecurus vaginatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Levantine Grecian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated forests of high altitudes, 1200-2000 metres, of the Lebanon Mountains and Ansariye Mountains, occupying generally more xeric sites than [Cedrus libani] and [Abies cilicica], including eastern, steppe-facing, slopes, though also mixed with them locally.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Persian juniper montane steppe forests
description: Open forest formations constituting a belt on high arid slopes of the Elburz, with more isolated occurrences in the mountains of Transcaucasia, of Tadzhikistan, of the Zagros, of the Irano-Afghan plateau, of the inner valleys of the western and eastern Himalayas and of the southeastern and southwestern Arabian peninsula, dominated by junipers of the [Juniperus excelsa] group, often united in an eastern species, the Persian juniper [Juniperus macropoda], or divided into several closely related species, [Juniperus macropoda], [Juniperus seravshanica], [Juniperus turcomanica], but by some taxonomists judged undistinguishable from [Juniperus excelsa]. [Juniperus semiglobosa] may also accompany the other forms or dominate the community in Tadzhikistan, Uzbekistan and Afghanistan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stinking juniper woods
description: Forest formations dominated by [Juniperus foetidissima] of the Balkan peninsula, Cyprus, Anatolia, Transcaucasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic stinking juniper woods
description: Forest formations dominated by [Juniperus foetidissima] of the mountains of Greece, developed locally at high altitudes, on adrets of the upper supra-Mediterranean level, in particular, in the northern Pindus, in the region of the Vicos gorge. Arborescent matorrals, somewhat more widespread in Greece, including the Aegean archipelagoes (Samos), have been listed under unit 32.1332.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian stinking juniper wood
description: Forest of [Juniperus foetidissima] of the upper level of Hionistra Peak in the Troodos Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian stinking juniper woods
description: Presteppic, meso-Mediterranean or subalpine [Juniperus foetidissima]-dominated forests of Anatolia and neighbouring areas, of apparently very local occurrence, considerably less widespread than the [Juniperus excelsa]-dominated formations of the same regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Syrian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus drupacea] woods of Greece and Asia Minor. Part of the formations take the appearence of arborescent matorral, listed under unit 32.135.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic Syrian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus drupacea] woods of the northern slopes of Mount Parnon and of the Karlik mountain in Thrace.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Taurus Syrian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus drupacea] woods of the Taurus and Amanus ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Levantine Syrian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus drupacea] woods of the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arbor-vitae forests
description: Forests of [Tetraclinis articulata], a species restricted to North Africa, southeastern Spain and the Maltese Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian arbor-vitae forests
description: Xerothermophile forests of [Tetraclinis articulata], restricted to extreme southeastern Spain, are extinct in forest form. The relict formations dominated by this species, of exceptional biogeographical and historical importance, constitute arborescent matorrals and have been listed under unit 32.151.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African arbor-vitae woodland
description: [Tetraclinis articulata]-dominated woodland of the lower Mediterranean slopes of the Rif and of the Oran and Algiers Tell and littoral, of the lower northern slopes and rain shadow valleys of the Middle Atlas and High Atlas, of the northern slopes of the Anti-Atlas, with outposts in maritime ranges of Tunisia, in particular, Ichkeul and Cap Bon and on the Tunisian Dorsale. They are limited to oceanic and maritime semiarid levels. Many formations are degraded to arborescent matorrals, listed under unit 32.152.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern African arbor-vitae forests
description: [Tetraclinis articulata]-dominated woodland of Morocco and western Algeria, distributed on the lower Mediterranean slopes of the Rif and of the Oran and Algiers Tell and littoral, of the lower northern slopes and rain shadow valleys of the Middle Atlas and High Atlas, of the northern slopes of the Anti-Atlas, with an exceptional representative on coastal sands in the fixed dunes of Essaouira on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tunisian arbor-vitae forests
description: Isolated [Tetraclinis articulata]-dominated woodland of the maritime ranges of Tunisia, in particular, Ichkeul and Cap Bon and of the Tunisian Dorsale.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Maltese arbor-vitae forests
description: Forests of [Tetraclinis articulata] of the Maltese Islands, extinct in woodland form, only represented by arborescent matorrals of unit 32.153.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Palaearctic yew woods
description: Woods dominated by [Taxus baccata], often with [Ilex aquifolium], of very local occurrence in plains, hills and mountains of the Western Palaearctic nemoral zone and in the mountains of the Mediterranean basin, with isolated outliers in the southern and eastern Carpathian system and the northern Rhodopides (Mount Vitosha).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic yew woods
description: [Taxus baccata] woods with [Sorbus aria] or [Mercurialis perennis] of dry valleys and scarps of the Chalk of southeastern England, and, very locally of the Durham Magnesium limestone; relict formations of Jutland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican yew woods
description: Formations of [Taxus baccata], [Ilex aquifolium], [Buxus sempervirens], restricted to cool, montane areas in the Tenda range, the San Pedrone range and the Cap Corse mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian yew woods
description: [Taxus baccata] and [Ilex aquifolium] woods of the Catena del Marghine and the Mount Limbara system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italic yew woods
description: [Taxus baccata] and [Ilex aquifolium] of the Macerata region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian yew woods
description: Occasional pure [Taxus baccata] formations of Spanish mountains, most often on steep shady slopes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Provence yew woods
description: [Taxus baccata] formations of southern France, similar to those of unit 42.A75.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpino-Carpathian yew woods
description: [Taxus baccata] woods of the Alpine system and of the Carpathians, in part rare facies of the yew-beech formations, in part amphibolite-colonizing woods with [Picea abies] and [Fraxinus excelsior] and [Juniperus sabina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric yew woods
description: Yew-dominated forests of the Dinarides, mostly yew-lime steep slope forests of northwestern Croatia, developed between 400 and 800 m on 30ø-80ø calcareous rock slopes with very shallow rendzina soils, also, locally, block forests within calcicolous fir forests of the Dinaric karst.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baltic yew woods
description: Pre-Sarmatic [Taxus baccata] formations of central Poland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Vitosha yew woods
description: Isolated [Taxus baccata] grove of Mount Vitosha, in Bulgaria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian juniper woods
description: Juniper-dominated formations of the Atlantic islands. All such formations are listed here whether wood-like or scrub-like in physiognomy; ericoid-dominated facies of the same formations have been listed under 31.3.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian juniper woods
description: [Juniperus cedrus] formations of the high altitudes of Tenerife, La Palma, Gomera, Gran Canaria, restricted to steep rocky slopes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean juniper woods
description: Endemic [Juniperus brevifolia] formations of the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian Phoenician juniper woods
description: [Juniperus phoenicea] formations of Tenerife, La Palma, Hierro, Gran Canaria, Gomera.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Prickly juniper woods
description: Woods dominated by [Juniperus oxycedrus] [s.l.]. Most [Juniperus oxycedrus] formations are thickets, scrubs or, at most, arborescent matorrals, listed under units 32.131, 32.45, 32.55, 32.B5 or, in dunal formations, unit 16.271. A few, however, qualify as woodland.
