The most characteristic examples to remain are probably those of the Iberian peninsula, although fragments are still recorded in France, Italy, the Maltese Islands, Greece, Asia Minor and North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean riparian ash woods
description: Riparian galleries of the mediterranean regions of the Iberian peninsula, southern France, the Italic peninsula, the large Tyrrhenian islands, the Hellenic peninsula, mediterranean North Africa and their zones of transition to adjacent climatic zones, dominated by tall [Fraxinus angustifolia], mostly characteristic of less eutrophic soils than the elm and poplar galleries, and of drier stations, with shorter inundation periods, than those occupied by poplar woods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian supra-Mediterranean ash galleries
description: [Fraxinus angustifolia] and [Quercus pyrenaica]-dominated galleries of supra-Mediterranean watercourses of the Cordillera Central, the Leonese mountains and the Iberian Range, developed on siliceous, sandy soils with temporary hydromorphy (pseudogleys).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian meso-Mediterranean ash galleries
description: [Fraxinus angustifolia] -dominated galleries of western Iberia, developed in meso- and thermo-Mediterranean areas on siliceous sandy, rarely inundated soils; [Populus alba], [Populus nigra], [Salix atrocinerea], [Rubus ulmifolius], [Osmunda regalis], [Ranunculus ficaria], [Arum italicum] frequently accompany the ashes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baetic ash-maple galleries
description: Meso- and supra-Mediterranean riparian galleries of the siliceous Sierra Nevada formed by [Fraxinus angustifolia] and [Acer granatense].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tyrrhenian ash-alder galleries
description: [Fraxinus angustifolia]-dominated galleries, usually with [Alnus glutinosa], of southern France, Tyrrhenian northern and central Italy, Corsica and Sardinia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italic ash galleries
description: [Fraxinus angustifolia]-dominated galleries of the Adriatic slope of the Italic peninsula, the lower Po basin, the plain of Foggia, the Gulf of Taranto and Sicily, with [Ulmus campestris], [Salix alba], [Populus nigra], [Equisetum telmateia], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Carex pendula], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Rubus ulmifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic ash galleries
description: Uncommon [Fraxinus angustifolia]-dominated galleries of continental Greece, reported in particular from the lower Achelos and Pinios.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African ash galleries
description: Riparian galleries of the mediterranean regions of North Africa dominated by [Fraxinus angustifolia], relatively widespread, ascending in the mountains to altitudes of 2500 m.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean riverine hop-hornbeam galleries
description: Mesohygrophile forests of the southwestern Alps, limited to the edges of small streams in deep ravines and, sometimes, in wider valleys, dominated by [Ostrya carpinifolia], with [Ulmus minor], [Populus alba], [Salix elaeagnos], [Alnus glutinosa], [Fraxinus ornus], [Acer campestre], [Acer opalus], [Quercus pubescens], [Tilia cordata], [Ulmus minor], [Cornus sanguinea], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Laurus nobilis], [Tamus communis], [Hedera helix], [Viola reichenbachiana], [Euphorbia dulcis], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Melica uniflora], [Carex pendula], [Carex digitata] and the rare [Carex grioletii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Pontic riverine ash forests
description: Riverine forests of the Mediterranean enclaves of the southern Black Sea coast and of the Sea of Marmora, dominated by [Fraxinus angustifolia], with [Ulmus minor], [Carpinus betulus], [Alnus glutinosa], [Acer campestre].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Sarmatic mixed poplar riverine forests
description: Mixed riverine forests of the floodplains of rivers of the Pontic and Sarmatic steppes, wooded steppes and southern nemoral forests of southern Eastern Europe, in particular, of the lower Danube, the lower Prut, the lower Dniestr, the lower Dniepr basin, the lower and middle Don and Donetz system, the lower Volga basin, the Kouma and Terek basins, dominated by or rich in [Populus alba], [Populus nigra], [Populus canescens]. They extend west to the sub-Carpathian Getic region; poplar galleries described from the Pannonic margin of Moravia and the Bohemian basin occupy a similar ecological position and are listed with them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic poplar galleries
description: Poplar galleries of the western Pontic steppe region of Bulgaria, Romania and Moldova, and of adjacent Getic valleys, dominated by [Populus alba], [Populus nigra], [Populus canescens], developed along sandy strips of river flood plains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic white poplar galleries
description: Galleries of [Populus alba] with [Salix alba], [Salix fragilis] and [Ulmus laevis] along streams of the western Pontic plain, with [Viburnum opulus], [Cornus sanguinea], [Crataegus monogyna], [Frangula alnus] in the shrub layer and [Rubus caesius], [Lycopus europaeus], [Bidens tripartita], [Scutellaria galericulata] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic white-black poplar galleries
description: Galleries along streams of the western Pontic plain dominated by [Populus alba] and [Populus nigra], with [Salix alba], [Salix fragilis], [Ulmus laevis], [Quercus robur], with [Viburnum opulus], [Cornus sanguinea], [Frangula alnus] in the shrub layer and [Rubus caesius], [Lycopus europaeus], [Bidens tripartita], [Scutellaria galericulata] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Danube delta galleries
description: Galleries of interdunal depressions of the sandy islands of the Danube Delta with [Quercus robur], [Quercus pedunculiflora], [Fraxinus angustifolia], [Fraxinus pallisiae], [Populus alba], [Populus tremula] and [Populus canescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Danube delta periploca-poplar-oak-ash galleries
description: Galleries of [Populus alba], [Populus tremula], [Populus canescens], [Quercus robur], [Quercus pedunculiflora], [Fraxinus angustifolia], [Fraxinus pallisiae] and [Alnus glutinosa], of the Danube Delta, in particular of interdunal depressions of sandy islands, with lianas [Periploca graeca], [Humulus lupulus], [Vitis sylvestris], [Clematis vitalba], shrubs [Salix cinerea], [Viburnum opulus], [Frangula alnus], [Cornus sanguinea], [Crataegus monogyna], and an herb layer of [Rubus caesius], [Lysimachia vulgaris], [Lythrum salicaria], [Carex spicata], [Carex hirta], [Carex acutiformis], [Galium rubioides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Danube delta [Hippophae]-[Populus canescens] galleries
description: Open-canopied [Populus canescens] galleries of the Danube Delta, with a closed shrub layer of [Hippophae rhamnoides], in particular of sandy island dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Sarmatic poplar and elm galleries
description: Poplar and elm galleries, mostly formed by [Populus nigra] and [Ulmus laevis], of the Dniepr, Don and Volga-Kama systems within the wooded steppes and adjacent nemoral forests of the valleys of the Podolian plateau, of the  Central Russian plateau, of the Volga plateau, of Orenburg and of Bachkiria, north of the Pontic and Caspian plains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central and eastern Pontic poplar forests
description: Poplar galleries of the Dniepr, Don, Volga-Kama, Kouma and Terek systems, within the steppes and wooded steppes of the northern plains of the Black Sea and of the northwestern and western Caspian Sea, with, in particular, [Populus nigra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European poplar galleries
description: [Populus nigra], [Populus alba], [Quercus robur], [Fraxinus excelsior] galleries occupying, within the riverine forest systems of the Bohemian Elbe and the Morava, locations submitted to great annual fluctuations of the water table and relatively frequent inundation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian mixed riverine forests
description: Riverine forests of the Transvolgan, Kazakh, Kurgan, Ichim, Kulunda, Baraba, Barnaul steppe and wooded steppe regions and of the Kazakho-Dsungarian and Turanian semideserts and deserts, in particular, of the Kyzyl-Kum and Kara-Kum deserts, of the northern flank of the Tien-Shan and of the western Pamir-Alai, of the northern flank of the Caucasus, mostly dominated by [Populus diversifolia], sometimes associated with or replaced by other poplars of subgenus [Turanga], in particular, [Populus pruinosa], [Populus ariana], and, near Lake Balkasch, [Populus litwinowiana], occasionally by poplars of subgenus [Populus], notably [Populus macrocarpa] of the valley of the Naryn, where it is associated with [Fraxinus potamophila], [Populus alba] and [Populus hybrida] of the Aralo-Caspian deserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental East Asian mixed riverine forests
description: Riverine forests of the steppes of Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, the Songnen Plain of Northeast China, the western Loess Plateau of North China, of the deserts and subdeserts of the Mongolian and Tibetan regions, of the southern flank of the Tien-Shan and of the eastern Pamir-Alai, mostly dominated by [Populus diversifolia], sometimes associated with or replaced by other poplars of subgenus [Turanga], in particular, [Populus pruinosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian mixed riverine forests
description: Riverine forests of the Irano-Anatolian plateau of Turkey, Iran and Afghanistan, of the Koura basin of Transcaucasia and of the Hyrcanian lowlands, of the Hindu-Kuch and western Himalayas, with [Populus nigra], [Populus caspica], [Populus alba], [Populus euphratica], [Populus pruinosa], [Populus transcaucasica], [Juglans regia], [Platanus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian poplar forests
description: Riverine forests of the Irano-Anatolian plateau of Turkey, Iran and Afghanistan, of the Koura basin of Transcaucasia and of the Hyrcanian lowlands, of the Hindu-Kuch and western Himalayas, with [Populus nigra], [Populus caspica], [Populus alba], [Populus euphratica], [Populus pruinosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian plateau poplar forests
description: Riverine forests of the Irano-Anatolian plateau of Turkey, Armenia, Iran and Afghanistan, with [Populus nigra], [Populus caspica], [Populus alba], [Populus euphratica], [Populus pruinosa], [Populus transcaucasica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian lowlands poplar forests
description: Riverine forests of the Hyrcanian lowlands dominated by [Populus spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Transcaucasian poplar forests
description: Riverine forests of the Koura basin of Transcaucasia dominated by [Populus spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan poplar forests
description: Riverine forests of the Hindu-Kuch and western Himalayas, with [Populus alba], [Populus ciliata], [Populus balsamifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian walnut riverine forests
description: Riverine forests of the Irano-Anatolian plateau of Turkey, Iran and Afghanistan dominated by [Juglans regia], with [Populus spp.], [Fraxinus spp.], [Platanus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian Euphrates poplar galleries
description: [Populus euphratica] riverine galleries of the northern margins of the southern Palaearctic hot deserts, formed along the lower courses of the great rivers of southern Mesopotamia and the Near East and their tributaries and, more disjunctly, along freshwater or slightly saline streams and desert torrents of southwestern Asia and North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arabo-Sindian Euphrates poplar galleries
description: [Populus euphratica] riverine galleries of the great rivers of southern Mesopotamia and the Near East, and of freshwater or slightly saline streams and desert torrents of southern Afghanistan, southern Iran and the Near East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Saharan Euphrates poplar galleries
description: [Populus euphratica] riverine galleries of freshwater or slightly saline streams and desert torrents of rare and scattered sites of Saharan and sub-Saharan Morocco and western Algeria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siwa poplar stands
description: [Populus euphratica] stands of Siwa oasis in Egypt, presumed to have been introduced in Roman times.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oriental plane and sweet gum woods
description: Forests and woods, for the most part riparian, dominated by [Platanus orientalis] or [Liquidambar orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oriental plane woods
description: Forests of [Platanus orientalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic riparian plane forests
description: [Platanus orientalis] gallery forests of Greek and southern Balkanic watercourses, temporary rivers and gorges; they are distributed throughout the mainland of Greece and its archipelagoes, extending north to Albania, the southern F.Y.R. of Macedonia and the valleys of southern Bulgaria, colonizing poorly stabilized alluvions of large rivers, gravel or boulder deposits of permanent or temporary torrents, spring basins, and particularly, the bottom of steep, shady gorges, where they constitute species-rich communities. The accompanying flora may include [Salix alba], [Salix elaeagnos], [Salix purpurea], [Alnus glutinosa], [Cercis siliquastrum], [Celtis australis], [Populus alba], [Populus nigra], [Juglans regia], [Fraxinus ornus], [Alnus glutinosa], [Crataegus monogyna], [Cornus sanguinea], [Ruscus aculeatus], [Vitex agnus-castus], [Nerium oleander], [Rubus spp.], [Rosa sempervirens], [Hedera helix], [Clematis vitalba], [Vitis vinifera] ssp. [sylvestris], [Ranunculus ficaria], [Anemone blanda], [Aristolochia rotunda], [Saponaria officinalis], [Symphytum bulbosum], [Hypericum hircinum], [Calamintha grandiflora], [Melissa officinalis], [Helleborus cyclophyllus], [Cyclamen hederifolium], [Cyclamen repandum], [Cyclamen creticum], [Galanthus nivalis] ssp. [reginae-olgae], [Dracunculus vulgaris], [Arum italicum], [Biarum tenuifolium], [Brachypodium sylvaticum], [Dactylis glomerata] and may be rich in mosses, lichens and ferns, among which [Pteridium aquilinum] is often abundant. Various associations have been described, reflecting regional and ecological variation in the composition of the undergrowth. The plane tree galleries are particularly well represented along the Ionian coast and in the Pindus; other important local complexes exist in Macedonia, in Thrace, around the Olympus massif, in the Pelion, in the Peloponnese, particularly in the Taygetos, where luxuriant gorge forests reach 1300 metres, in Euboea and in Crete; local, distinctive, representatives occur in other Aegean islands, such as Rhodes, Samos, Samothrace, Thasos. Restriction to gorges is increasingly pronounced towards the south.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic slope plane woods
description: [Platanus orientalis] woods on colluvions, detritus cones, ravine sides or other poorly stabilized substrates, of Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sicilian plane tree canyons
description: Relict [Platanus orientalis]-dominated or -rich galleries of the Cassabile, the Anapo, the Irminio and the Carbo rivers, in the Iblei range of southeastern Sicily, of the gorge of the Sirmeto, in the vicinity of the Nebrodi. Some of these formations, in particular, in the gorges of the Cassabile and of the Anapo, are true plane tree woods. Others, such as on the Sirmeto, are [Populus alba], [Fraxinus angustifolia], [Salix spp.] formations with [Platanus orientalis]; as they grade into each other, and because of the very isolated occurrence, and great biogeographical and historical interest of [Platanus orientalis] in Sicily, they are all listed here. Plane tree woods have had a much greater extension in Sicily and probably in Calabria. A large forest has, in particular, existed on the Alcantara, where the species is now extinct.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian plane forests
description: [Platanus orientalis] forests of river courses of the submediterranean margin of the Anatolian plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian plane forests
description: [Platanus orientalis] formations of streams and gorges of Cyprus, in particular, of the Troodos range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Levantine plane forests
description: [Platanus orientalis] forests of river courses of the mediterranean plains and hills of the Levant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian planetree forests
description: [Platanus orientalis] forests of northern Irak, eastern Turkey, Iran and Afghanistan, in particular, of river gorges of the Kurdo-Zagrosian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sweet gum woods
description: Riverine forests dominated by the Tertiary relict [Liquidambar orientalis], with a very limited range in southern Asia Minor and Rhodes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodian sweet gum woods
description: [Liquidambar orientalis] gallery forest of the Petaloudhes Valley of Rhodes, with poorly developed undergrowth and a ground layer dominated by [Adiantum capillus-veneris] in damp areas. This forest constitutes the only European formation of this species and harbours a unique, concentrated, aggregation of Jersey Tiger Moths, [Panaxia quadripunctaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian sweet gum woods
description: Riverine forests of [Liquidambar orientalis] of Caria, Lycia, Pisidia and Pamphylia, including the extensive forest of the alluvial plain of Lake K”ycegiz and of the river Dalaman in which [Liquidambar orientalis] is associated with [Alnus orientalis], [Platanus orientalis], [Ulmus spp.], [Smilax excelsa], [Periploca graeca], [Vitis vinifera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern riparian galleries and thickets
description: Tamarisk, oleander, chaste tree galleries and thickets and similar low ligneous formations of permanent or temporary streams and wetlands of the thermo-Mediterranean zone and southwestern Iberia, and of the most hygromorphic locations within the Saharo-Mediterranean and Saharo-Sindian zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oleander, chaste tree and tamarisk galleries
description: Thickets and galleries of [Nerium oleander], [Vitex agnus-castus] or [Tamarix spp.] of the southern parts of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oleander galleries
description: [Nerium oleander] cordons and screens, often with [Tamarix spp.], [Vitex agnus-castus], [Dittrichia viscosa], [Saccharum ravennae], [Arundo donax], [Rubus ulmifolius], most typical of temporary water courses, but also lining small and sometimes large rivers, marking springs and areas of high water table in southern and eastern Iberia, very locally in eastern Provence, Liguria and Corsica (Saint-Florent), in southern Italy, Sardinia and Sicily, in southern and western Greece, the Aegean and Ionian archipelagoes, in Crete, in Albania, in the eastern Mediterranean, in North Africa, including northern Saharan regions, and in Mesopotamia. They are particularly abundant in the south and east of Iberia, in Sicily, in the Aegean and eastern Mediterranean region and in North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chaste tree thickets
description: [Vitex agnus-castus] formations of temporary water courses and other humid sites within, mostly, the thermo-Mediterranean zone. They occur, though uncommonly, in Mediterranean southern and eastern Spain and in the Balearics; they are local and rare in eastern Provence, the Tyrrhenian coast of Italy, Puglia, the gulf of Taranto, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily and the Maltese Islands. They are frequent in Greece, particularly along the Ionian coasts, where they can constitute dense thickets, uncommon again in the Aegean archipelagoes and Crete. They extend to the southern Balkans, Crimea, Mediterranean Asia Minor, Anatolia and North Africa, including the northern Saharan regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Macaronesian tamarisk thickets
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], including [Tamarix gallica], [Tamarix africana], [Tamarix canariensis], [Tamarix parviflora], [Tamarix tetrandra], [Tamarix dalmatica], [Tamarix smyrnensis], [Tamarix hampeana], [Tamarix boveana], associated with river banks, wet areas and coastal localities of the Mediterranean basin, of the mediterranean coasts of the Black Sea, of the thermo-Atlantic coasts and lowlands of southwestern Europe and of the Macaronesian Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Mediterranean tamarisk thickets
description: [Tamarix gallica], [Tamarix africana] or [Tamarix canariensis] thickets of watercourse galleries, humid depressions and slightly saline coastal flats in Iberia, southern and western France, peninsular Italy, the Balearics, Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, the Maltese Islands and mediterranean North Africa. The accompanying flora comprises [Scirpus holoschoenus], [Saccharum ravennae], [Arundo donax], [Brachypodium phoenicoides], [Piptatherum miliaceum], [Asparagus acutifolius], [Equisetum ramosissimum], [Rubia peregrina], [Rubia longifolia], [Rubia angustifolia], [Dittrichia viscosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian tamarisk thickets
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], including [Tamarix gallica], [Tamarix africana], [Tamarix canariensis], of the Canary Islands and Madeira.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian tamarisk thickets
description: [Tamarix canariensis] and [Tamarix africana] galleries and thickets of the lower zone of the Canary Islands, lining the low part of barrancos and occupying the deltas of greater water courses. They are particularly abundant in the eastern desert islands, Lanzarote and, mostly, Fuenteventura, where they constitute one of the principal ligneous habitats for the fauna. They have also important representatives along the north coast of Tenerife and on Gran Canaria (Charca de Maspalomas, La Aldea).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Madeiran tamarisk thickets
description: [Tamarix gallica] thickets of the lowlands of Madeira.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean tamarisk thickets
description: [Tamarix parviflora], [Tamarix tetrandra], [Tamarix dalmatica], [Tamarix smyrnensis], [Tamarix hampeana] and [Tamarix hohenackeri] thickets of lowland water-course galleries, humid depressions and slightly saline coastal flats of Greece and its islands, of the southern F.Y.R. of Macedonia, of Albania, of Cyprus, of southern Crimea, of mediterranean Asia Minor and of the Levant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyper-saline Mediterranean tamarisk stands
description: Thickets of [Tamarix boveana], [Tamarix canariensis] or, sometimes, [Tamarix gallica] of the Mediterranean basin, accompanied by typical salt marsh flora, in particular, [Arthrocnemum fruticosum], [Arthrocnemum glaucum], [Suaeda brevifolia], [Halimione portulacoides], [Atriplex halimus], [Atriplex hastata], [Limonium lactibracteatum], [Limonium eugeniae], [Limonium cossonianum], [Limonium angustibracteanum], [Limonium sinuatum], [Inula crithmoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian [Tamarix boveana] stands
description: Rare and vulnerable formations of the Ibero-African [Tamarix boveana], alone or associated with [Tamarix canariensis], characteristic of arid areas of eastern Iberia, limited to a few stations in the Iberian Southeast (Murcia, Almeria, Alicante), the Ebro depression (Salada de Chiprana), the Ebro delta and Mallorca (Alcudia).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saline [Tamarix canariensis] stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix canariensis], sometimes with [Tamarix gallica], characteristic of strongly saline sites of Iberia and the European shores of the western Mediterranean, in particular, of Iberian interior saline depressions (La Mancha) and of coastal areas of the Iberian Arid Southeast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saline eastern tamarisk stands
description: [Tamarix smyrnensis], [Tamarix hampeana], [Tamarix dalmatica] stands of the strongly saline part of Greek and east Mediterranean coastal marshes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African hypersaline tamarisk stands
description: Thickets of [Tamarix spp.] of mediterranean North Africa accompanied by typical salt marsh flora, in particular salt scrubs of genera [Arthrocnemum] or [Suaeda] and rosette plants of genus [Limonium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian tamarisk thickets
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], including [Tamarix smyrnensis] ([Tamarix pallasii], [Tamarix ramossissima] [auct.]), [Tamarix tetrandra], [Tamarix octandra] [i.a.], associated with river banks, wet areas and coastal localities of the Irano-Turanian floristic region and its irradiation areas within the steppe and cold desert zones of Eurasia, in particular, of the Pontic basin, of Central Eurasia, of East Asia, of Inner Anatolia, northern Iran and Afghanistan, of northern Mesopotamia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix smyrnensis] ([Tamarix ramossissima] [auct.]), of stream sides and coastal localities of the Pontic steppe region of western Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic fresh water [Tamarix smyrnensis] stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix smyrnensis] and/or [Tamarix tetrandra] on weakly saline sands of fresh water steppe streamsides of the western Pontic region, including river systems such as those of the lower Danube and the Maritza-Tunja basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Danubio-Tracian fresh water tamarix stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix smyrnensis] and/or [Tamarix tetrandra] on weakly saline sands of fresh water steppe streamsides of the western Pontic region, including the lower Danube basin, the Danube delta, the Maritza-Tunja basins and watercourses of the northeastern Tracian plain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Danube small reed fresh water tamarix stands
description: [Tamarix smyrnensis] stands occupying weakly saline sands of fresh water steppe streamsides of the lower Danube basin and the Danube delta, in Muntenia, Oltenia and Dobrogea, with much [Calamagrostis epigejos] and other herbs, including [Cynodon dactylon], [Agrostis stolonifera], [Cynanchum acutum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Pontic coastal [Tamarix smyrensis] stands
description: Shrub communities of [Tamarix smyrnensis], [Tamarix ramosissima] and/or [Tamarix tetrandra] occupying weakly saline marine sand dunes of western Black Sea coastal areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central and eastern Pontic tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix smyrnensis] ([Tamarix ramossissima] [auct.]), of stream sides and coastal localities of the northern and eastern Black Sea lowlands, within the range of central and eastern Pontic steppes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], including [Tamarix smyrnensis] ([Tamarix pallasii], [Tamarix ramossissima] [auct.]), [Tamarix tetrandra], [Tamarix octandra] [i.a.], of stream sides, wetlands and coastal localities of the Irano-Anatolian region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian fresh water tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix smyrnensis], [Tamarix tetrandra], [Tamarix octandra], [Tamarix hampeana] of fresh water stream sides and wetlands of Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian saline tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], including [Tamarix smyrnensis], [Tamarix octandra i.a.], of saline sites of Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mesopotamian tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], in particular [Tamarix smyrnensis] ([Tamarix pallasii], [Tamarix ramossissima] [auct.]), of stream sides, wadis and wetlands of the Mesopotamian steppe region of southeastern Turkey, interior Syria, northwestern Irak and extreme eastern Iran.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], including about 15 species, among them [Tamarix smyrnensis] ([Tamarix pallasii], [Tamarix ramossissima] [auct.]), [Tamarix laxa], [Tamarix hispida], of streamsides, wadis and wetlands of the Transvolgan, Kazakh, Kurgan, Ichim, Kulunda, Baraba, Barnaul steppe and wooded steppe regions and of the Kazakho-Dsungarian and Turanian semideserts and deserts, in particular, of the Kyzyl-Kum and Kara-Kum deserts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian tamarisk stands
description: Formations of [Tamarix spp.], including [Tamarix smyrnensis] ([Tamarix pallasii], [Tamarix ramossissima] [auct.]), [Tamarix laxa], [Tamarix hispida], of streamsides, wadis and wetlands of the steppes of Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, the Songnen Plain of Northeast China, the western Loess Plateau of North China, of the deserts and subdeserts of the Mongolian and Tibetan regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Sindian tamarisk thickets
description: Forests or thickets of [Tamarix spp.] forming in wadis of the subtropical deserts of the Palaearctic domaine. They include, in particular, formations of [Tamarix articulata] of the central Sahara, developed in large sandy wadis with a water table within 7 or 8 metres of the surface, sometimes constituting closed, fairly tall, up to 10 metres, riparian forests, otherwise, more open woodland stands or dense 2 to 3 metre tall thickets, with an undergrowth of [Stipagrostis pungens], [Leptadenia pyrotechnica], [Calligonum comosum] and chenopods. They also include [Tamarix gallica] galleries and thickets of wadis of the northern and northwestern Sahara that receive their water supply from the High Atlas or the Saharan Atlas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Iberian tamujares
description: Low, spiny, almost monospecific fringes formed by the Ibero-African shrubby spurge [Securinega tinctoria] on the outer edge of temporary or permanent water courses of great seasonal amplitude in the southwestern quadrant of the Iberian peninsula (Montes de Toledo, Sierra Morena, Extremadura, southwestern Andalusia, southern Portugal). Among the few associated plants, are the lianas [Bryonia cretica], [Tamus communis] and the endemic [Clematis campaniflora]. [Pyrus bourgaeana] may transgress from neighbouring communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oretanian lauriphyllous galleries
description: Supra- and upper meso-Mediterranean riparian galleries of the Montes de Toledo (Cordillera Oretana), constituted by the lauriphyllous [Prunus lusitanica] and [Viburnum tinus]; they line water courses on the inner edge of alder galleries of 44.551 and 44.552, which they sometimes entirely replace.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oretanian bog-myrtle willow scrub
description: Tall scrub of Montes de Toledo streams, with [Frangula alnus], [Salix atrocinerea], [Salix salvifolia] and [Myrica gale].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alder, willow, oak, aspen swamp woods
description: Woods and scrubs of marshy ground, waterlogged for most of the year, colonizing fens and marshy or permanently inundated alluvial terraces of rivers of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alder swamp woods
description: Marshy [Alnus glutinosa]-dominated woods and scrubs of the Palaearctic region, usually with shrubby willows in the undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Meso-eutrophic swamp alder woods
description: Mesotrophic and meso-eutrophic [Alnus glutinosa] swamp woods of middle European and western Siberian, nemoral and subboreal, marshy depressions, with [Carex elongata], [Thelypteris palustris], [Dryopteris cristata], [Osmunda regalis], [Solanum dulcamara], [Calystegia sepium], [Ribes nigrum], [Calamagrostis canescens] and often, in acidocline variants, [Betula pubescens]. The constancy of [Carex elongata] is characteristic on the continent, less so in Britain. Tall sedges, [Carex paniculata], [Carex acutiformis], [Carex elata], often dominate the herb layer in the most humid types.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic greater tussock-sedge alder woods
description: Eutrophic and mesotrophic alder woods of Atlantic Europe, distributed in the British Isles, western France, locally, northwestern Germany, poor in [Carex elongata], and harbouring, in particular, [Oenanthe crocata], [Osmunda regalis], [Carex laevigata], [Scutellaria minor]. They include all meso-eutrophic alder swamp woods of the British Isles and western France, as well as the less eutrophic woods of the zone of transition between the main range of this unit and the more continental range of unit 44.9112.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Elongated-sedge swamp alder woods
description: Mesotrophic and meso-eutrophic [Alnus glutinosa] swamp woods of sub-Atlantic and subcontinental regions of the European continent characterized in particular by the constant presence of [Carex elongata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East European swamp alder woods
description: Mesotrophic and meso-eutrophic [Alnus glutinosa] swamp woods of subcontinental and continental regions of eastern Europe, from Mazuria and Masovia east to Bashkiria, often rich in [Carex elongata], [Ribes nigrum], [Sphagnum spp.], [Dryopteris cristata]; in the Sarmatic region, they may occupy extensive areas of nutrient-rich swamps, in particular in the Pripyat area.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-boreal swamp alder woods
description: Mesotrophic and meso-eutrophic [Alnus glutinosa] or [Alnus glutinosa]-[Alnus incana] swamp woods of northeastern Poland, the Baltic states, Fennoscandia, the northern Sarmatic region and Siberia, with [Calamagrostis canescens], [Athyrium filix-femina], [Cardamine amara], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Lysimachia thyrsiflora], [Carex elongata], [Carex remota], [Brachythecium rivulare], [Calliergon cordifolium], [Climacium dendroides], [Thuidium tamariscinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian alder swamp woods
description: Meso-eutrophic [Alnus glutinosa] swamp woods of marshy intramontane depressions and floodplains, at the 500-800 m level of foothills of the eastern Carpathian system, in particular, the Harghita and Baraolt mountains, with [Carex elongata], [Calamagrostis canescens], [Thelypteris palustris], [Carex caespitosa], [Dryopteris carthusiana], [Calla palustris] and [Ligularia sibirica], most of which may dominate facies of the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Carpathian alder swamp woods
description: [Alnus glutinosa] swamp woods of the floodplains of southern Romania, developed along water bodies and in microdepressions on alluvial soils covered by stagnant or slowly moving water, with [Thelypteris palustris], [Festuca gigantea], [Lycopus europaeus], [Caltha palustris], [Veronica beccabunga], [Lythrum salicaria], [Oenanthe silaifolia], [Sium erectum], [Stellaria aquatica], [Carex acutiformis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intra-Carpathian elongated sedge alder swamp woods
description: Rare [Alnus glutinosa] swamp woods of peat bogs of central Romania, with [Spiraea salicifolia], [Euonymus nanus], [Frangula alnus], [Ribes nigrum], [Salix cinerea] in the shrub layer and [Carex elongata], [Calamagrostis canescens], [Ligularia sibirica], [Thelypteris palustris] in the herb layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oligotrophic swamp alder woods
description: Oligotrophic or meso-oligotrophic, acidocline [Alnus glutinosa] woods of fens and poorly drained banks of brooks or small rivers of western Europe, mostly characteristic of siliceous regions and Atlantic climates, south to Galicia. [Betula pubescens] and [Frangula alnus] often accompany the alders. The ground layer is usually rich in [Sphagnum spp.] and includes [Carex laevigata], [Equisetum sylvaticum] and many ferns, including [Oreopteris limbosperma], [Blechnum spicant], [Athyrium filix-femina], [Dryopteris cristata] and [Dryopteris carthusiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Helleno-Balkanic swamp alder woods
description: Rare swamp woods of the mediterranean and submediterranean zones of the southern Helleno-Balkanic peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic swamp alder woods
description: Rare swamp woods of the mediterranean evergreen oak zone of the Hellenic peninsula, such as the Athos peninsula swamp wood with [Arundo donax], [Equisetum telmateia], [Carex pendula], [Carex remota], [Humulus lupulus], [Osmunda regalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Paeonian swamp alder woods
description: Rare swamp woods of the submediterranean [Ostryo-Carpinion orientalis aegeicum] zone of the southern Balkan peninsula, recorded, in particular, from the southeastern F.Y.R. of Macedonia, with [Acer tataricum], [Frangula alnus], [Ligustrum vulgare], [Corylus avellana], [Rosa corymbifera], [Osmunda regalis], [Pteridium aquilinum], [Equisetum telmateia], [Thelypteris palustris] and a profusion of lianas, including [Periploca graeca], [Hedera helix], [Humulus lupulus], [Vitis vinifera] ssp. [sylvestris], [Calystegia sylvatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Steppe swamp alder woods
description: [Alnus glutinosa] mire woods of the steppe zones of Eurasia, west to the Pannonic basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic swamp alder-ash woods
description: Mesotrophic and meso-eutrophic [Alnus glutinosa] swamp woods of the Pannonic basin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic swamp alder woods
description: Meso-eutrophic alder woods of mires of the east European steppe zone, south of the subboreal and nemoral regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal swamp alder woods
description: Swamp woods of the Scandinavian lowlands dominated by [Alnus glutinosa] and [Alnus incana] with a shrub layer dominated by [Alnus spp.], [Betula pubescens] and various [Salix spp.] The field layer, sometimes very sparse, includes [Filipendula ulmaria], [Epilobium palustre], [Galium palustre], [Iris pseudacorus], [Lysimachia thyrsiflora], [Lysimachia vulgaris], [Viola palustris], [Calla palustris], [Thelypteris palustris], [Carex canescens], [Carex Elongata], [Carex rostrata], [Calamagrostis canescens], [Deschampsia caespitosa]. The ground layer, of mosses and sphagnums, is very poorly developed.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oriental swamp alder woods
description: [Alnus sibirica], [Alnus hirsuta], [Alnus trobeculosa] eutrophic mire woods of the eastern Palaearctic, sometimes with [Betula fruticosa], [Betula ovalifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Willow carrs and fen scrubs
description: Low woods and scrubs colonizing fens, marshy floodplains and fringes of lakes and ponds of the western Palaearctic, dominated by large or medium sized shrubby willows, generally [Salix aurita], [Salix cinerea], [Salix atrocinerea], [Salix pentandra], alone or in association with [Frangula alnus], [Rhamnus cathartica], [Alnus glutinosa] or [Betula pubescens], any of which may, at times, dominate the upper canopy, or, in boreal regions and on cold subboreal plateaux, by very small arcto-alpine willows associated with [Betula humilis] or [Betula nana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Grey willow carrs
description: Mesotrophic or eutrophic low woods and scrubs colonizing fens, marshy floodplains and fringes of lakes and ponds of the western Palaearctic, dominated by [Salix cinerea], [Salix aurita] or, sometimes, [Salix atrocinerea], alone or in association with [Frangula alnus], [Rhamnus cathartica], [Alnus glutinosa] or [Betula pubescens], any of which may, at times, dominate the upper canopy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western grey willow carrs
description: Mesotrophic or eutrophic [Salix cinerea], [Salix aurita], or, sometimes, [Salix atrocinerea], and [Alnus glutinosa] scrubs of mires, fens, and water fringes of western Europe and northern Central Europe, within the Atlantic and sub-Atlantic domaines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central European grey willow carrs
description: [Salix cinerea]-dominated scrubs of often relatively eutrophic mires of the warmer lowlands and submontane level of central, southeastern and eastern Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intra-Carpathian grey willow carrs
description: [Salix cinerea] carrs occupying fen margins of the Eastern Carpathians and the Apuseni mountains, with [Frangula alnus], [Spirea salicifolia], [Ribes nigrum], [Euvonymous nana], [Calamagrostis canescens], [Lysimachia vulgaris], [Filipendula ulmaria], [Poa trivialis], [Galium palustre], [Myosotis palustris], [Deschampsia caespitosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sphagnum willow carrs
description: Oligotrophic [Salix aurita] or [Salix cinerea] and [Betula pubescens] or [Betula carpatica] scrubs, rich in sphagnum, of bog edges and acid fens of nemoral Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bay willow carrs
description: Medium-tall woods and brushes colonizing fens, marshy floodplains and fringes of lakes and ponds, dominated by the relatively large [Salix pentandra], particularly characteristic of boreal, subboreal and subcontinental Europe, from northern England through Scandinavia, northeastern Germany, Poland, Lithuania to Bashkiria in the northeast, to the Bohemian quadrangle, the Alpine piedmont of Bavaria and Hungary in the south, with outposts in the Netherlands, in subcontinental western Europe to the Black Forest and the Baar plateau, in continental southern Europe to Bulgaria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf willow mire scrubs
description: Dwarf [Salix repens], [Salix rosmarinifolia] and [Betula humilis] scrubs of bogs and fens, of eastern nemoral and boreonemoral Europe, with outposts constituting rare glacial relicts in the higher middle German Hercynian ranges and on northern pre-Alpine plateaux.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal sedge willow carrs
description: Low woods and scrubs colonizing fens, marshy floodplains and fringes of lakes and ponds of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic dominated by large or medium sized shrubby willows, generally [Salix cinerea] or [Salix aurita], accompanied by [Salix phylicifolia], [Salix nigricans] ([Salix myrsinifolia]) and the boreal [Salix glauca], [Salix lapponum], with sedges, in particular, [Carex aquatilis], [Carex caespitosa], brown mosses and sphagna.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine willow fen scrubs
description: Willow thickets or scrubs of mires of the mountains of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic region, characteristically forming along fen margins, on their hummocks or strings, sometimes in their lawns, with an understorey of dwarf shrubs, herbs, mosses and sphagna.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine acidophile willow fen scrubs
description: Willow thickets or scrubs of oligotrophic, acidic fens of the mountains of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic region, characteristically forming along fen margins, on their hummocks or strings, sometimes in their lawns, with an understorey of dwarf shrubs, herbs, mosses and sphagna.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine ledum-ling willow scrubs
description: Willow scrub of mire margins and hummocks of poor, acid fens of boreal and arctic Scandinavia, dominated by [Salix glauca], [Salix lanata], [Salix lapponum], [Salix phylicifolia] accompanied by a relatively tall shrub layer dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], [Ledum palustre], [Diapensia lapponica], with [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Betula nana], an herb layer of [Carex bigelowii] and [Carex globularis] with [Molinia caerulea], [Calamagrostis lapponica], [Calamagrostis purpurea], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Pedicularis lapponica], [Polygonum viviparum] ([Bistorta vivipara]), [Rubus chamaemorus], sphagna ([Sphagnum fuscum], [Sphagnum russowii]) and mosses ([Pleurozium schreberi], [Dicranum elongatum]), characteristic of subalpine and lower alpine levels.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine sedge-sphagnum willow scrubs
description: Willow scrub of boreal and arctic Scandinavia formed of scattered dense stands of [Salix glauca], [Salix lapponum], [Salix phylicifolia] on extensive sphagnum lawns, constituting mire margin communities, with a species cortŠge that includes [Carex canescens], [Carex magellanica], [Carex rostrata], [Potentilla palustris], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Sphagnum fallax], [Sphagnum lindbergii], [Sphagnum riparium], [Sphagnum squarrosum], installed on thin peat of poor, acid fens of subalpine and lower alpine levels.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine neutrocline willow fen scrubs
description: Willow thickets or scrubs of neutrocline oligotrophic fens of the mountains of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic region, characteristically forming along fen margins, on their hummocks or strings, sometimes in their lawns, with an understorey of dwarf shrubs, herbs, mosses and sphagna.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine small sedge-brown moss willow scrubs
description: Willow scrub of boreal and arctic Scandinavia formed of 1-1.5 m high [Salix lapponum] and [Salix phylicifolia] with a species-rich herb layer characterized by the dominance or presence of [Equisetum palustre], [Carex nigra], [Juncus filiformis], [Viola epipsila] and [Viola palustris], accompanied by [Parnassia palustris], [Pyrola minor], [Ranunculus acris], [Agrostis canina], [Agrostis mertensii],  [Festuca ovina], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Carex dioica], [Carex canescens], [Luzula frigida], [Luzula sudetica], with a ground layer of [Climacium dendroides], [Drepanocladus exannulatum], [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Polytrichum commuune], developed on mire margins or strings, in medium-rich fen conditions of pH 5.5-6.5 with flowing water, at subalpine and lower alpine levels.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine tall sedge-brown moss willow scrubs
description: Willow scrub, 1-1.5 m high, of boreal and arctic Scandinavia, dominated by [Salix lapponum], with [Salix glauca], [Salix hastata], [Salix phylcifolia], [Betula nana], [Betula pubescens], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Andromeda polifolia], [Potentilla palustris], [Parnassia palustris], [Pedicularis lapponicum], [Pedicularis sceptrum-carolinum], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Saussurea alpina], [Saxifraga stellaris], [Viola biflora], [Viola epipsila], [Viola palustris], [Dechampsia cespitosa], [Calamagrostis stricta], [Carex aquatilis, [Carex canescens, [Carex chordorrhiza], [Carex juncella], [Carex magellanica], [Carex rostrata], [Carex rotundata], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Eriophorum vaginata], [Equisetum fluviatile], [Calliergon stramineus], [Calliergon sarmentosum], [Cinclidium subrotundum], [Sphagnum squarrosum, [Sphagnum teres] and [Sphagnum warnstorfii], developed at subalpine levels on both drier and wetter, relatively nutrient-poor, substrates, as mire margin lawn communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-alpine basiphile willow fen scrubs
description: Prostrate scrubs of calcareous, relatively nutrient-rich fens of the subalpine and low alpine levels of the mountains of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic region dominated by [Salix myrsinites], accompanied by an extremely rich species assembly that includes numerous representatives of the cortŠge of the [Dryas] heaths of unit 31.4932 or of the arctoalpine riverine swards of unit 54.3. [Carex atrofusca], [Equisetum variegatum], [Pinguicula vulgaris], [Thalictrum alpinum] are particularly characteristic; other species include [Betula nana], [Polygonum viviparum], [Pedicularis oederi], [Tofieldia pusilla], [Carex capillaris], [Carex dioica], [Carex saxatilis], [Carex vaginata], [Juncus triglumis], [Kobresia simpliciuscula], [Equisetum scirpoides] and the mosses [Campylium stellatum], [Drepanocladus revolvens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Swamp bog-myrtle scrub
description: [Myrica gale] thickets of fringes of fens, drying fens and nascent or regenerating bogs of middle Europe, mostly characteristic of the Atlantic sector and of northeastern Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Acidocline swamp bog-myrtle scrub
description: [Myrica gale] thickets of fringes of acidic fens, drying acidic fens and nascent or regenerating bogs of middle Europe, north to southern Fenno-Scandia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rich fen bog-myrtle scrub
description: [Myrica gale] scrubs colonizing fringes and drying areas of rich fens, probably limited to the British Isles.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oak swamp woods
description: [Quercus robur]-dominated woods of inundatable depressions of the Sarmatic region, west to eastern Poland, with an accompanying species cortŠge composed of elements of the [Alnetalia glutinosae], [Molinietalia], [Phragmitetalia], [Caricetalia fuscae] and, to a lesser extent, [Vaccinio-Piceetea] and [Querco-Fagetea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aspen swamp woods
description: [Populus tremula]-dominated swamp woods of the eastern European and western Siberian northern steppe zone subject to continental climate conditions, where they occupy pods, inundated endoreic circular depressions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Birch and conifer mire woods
description: Woods of [Betula pubescens], [Pinus spp.] or [Picea spp.] colonizing bogs and fens; they are characteristic of the boreal and subboreal zones, extending, mostly as boreal relicts, into the nemoral, wooded steppe and steppe zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sphagnum birch woods
description: Forests of [Betula pubescens] or [Betula carpatica] on peaty, humid and very acid soils, colonizing bogs of reduced peat building activity and acid fens of the boreal, subboreal and nemoral zones of the western Palaearctic, very locally of the wooded steppe and steppe zones, with [Molinia caerulea], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Empetrum nigrum], [Trientalis europaea] and many sphagna, mosses and liverworts.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cottonsedge sphagnum birch woods
description: Sphagnum-rich [Betula pubescens] or [Betula carpatica] woods of the boreal and nemoral, mostly subboreal, western Palaearctic in which bog species, in particular [Eriophorum vaginatum] and [Vaccinium oxycoccos], are prominent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sedge sphagnum birch woods
description: Sphagnum-rich [Betula pubescens] or [Betula carpatica] woods of the boreal and nemoral western Palaearctic in which [Molinia caerulea] is accompanied by a cortŠge of acid fen species, in particular, [Carex rostrata], [Carex nigra], [Carex echinata], [Juncus acutiflorus], [Agrostis canina], [Narthecium ossifragum], [Calamagrostis canescens] and by ericoid shrubs, in particular [Vaccinium uliginosum]. Depending on water level, regime of inundation, history of ligneous colonization and nature of the initial stage, the undergrowth may be dominated by [Molinia caerulea], by sedges [Carex spp.], by rushes [Juncus spp.], by [Scirpus cespitosus] or by ericoid shrubs, resulting in a number of rather distinctive habitats. Conifers, mostly [Picea abies], may participate in the canopy of boreal, northeastern nemoral, Hercynian subboreal and pre-Alpine communities; [Pinus sylvestris] has its westernmost relict stations in northwestern stands. Fennoscandian formations have a number of northern species, in particular [Calamagrostis purpurea], [Cornus suecica], [Empetrum spp.], [Rubus chamaemorus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Meso-acidophilous birch swamp woods
description: Sphagnum-rich [Betula pubescens] or [Betula carpatica] woods of the boreal and nemoral western Palaearctic in which the presence of species characteristic of subhumid mineral soils indicate a transition towards acidophilous birch and oak woods; [Salix cinerea], [Alnus glutinosa], [Lysimachia vulgaris], [Luzula sylvatica], [Oxalis acetosella], [Deschampsia flexuosa] may be prominent, next to [Molinia caerulea]. Conifers, mostly [Picea abies], may participate in the canopy of boreal and subboreal communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Scots pine mire woods
description: [Pinus sylvestris]-dominated woods of bogs, fens and swamps of western Eurasia, mostly characteristic of the boreal and subboreal zones, with very localized outposts in nemoral mountains and in the steppe zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral Scots pine mire woods
description: [Pinus sylvestris] formations of bogs and transition mires of the plains of subboreal and northern nemoral central and eastern Europe, with isolated stations in the Hercynian system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern bilberry Scots Pine mire woods
description: [Pinus sylvestris] formations of bogs and transition mires of the plains of northern Germany, northern Poland and the northern nemoral Sarmatic region, with [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Calluna vulgaris], [Andromeda polifolia], [Myrica gale].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland northern bilberry Scots Pine mire woods
description: [Pinus sylvestris] formations of bogs and transition mires of nemoral and boreonemoral eastern Europe and of inland sites in the Baltic lowlands of northern central Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal northern bilberry Scots Pine mire woods
description: [Pinus sylvestris] formations of dunal depressions of the southern and southeastern Baltic coasts, with [Empetrum nigrum], [Erica tetralix], [Deschampsia flexuosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynian Scots pine mire woods
description: [Pinus sylvestris] formations of bogs and transition mires of the Hercynian system, best represented in the Bohemian Quadrangle, with rare outposts farther west to the Vosges, with [Betula pubescens], [Betula carpatica], [Frangula alnus], [Sorbus aucuparia], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Andromeda polifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small reed Scots pine mire woods
description: Peri-Hercynian [Pinus sylvestris] formations of mires with species-poor undergrowth, comprising [Vaccinium myrtillus], usually dominant, [Calamagrostis villosa], [Sphagnum girgensohnii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Scots pine mire woods
description: Isolated relict Scots pine mire woods of the Balkan peninsula, often with [Picea abies] and [Betula pubescens] and a sometimes species-rich cortŠge of fen, bog or transition mire species, including sphagna and cottonsedges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian Scots pine mire woods
description: Scots pine mire wood of the Han-Kram range in southern Bosnia, in the Illyrian beech forest zone, with [Picea abies], [Betula pubescens] and [Salix pentandra], accompanied by [Frangula alnus], [Sorbus aucuparia], [Salix caprea], [Salix cinerea], [Sphagnum spp.], [Carex spp.], [Molinia caerulea], [Agrostis canina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moesian Scots pine mire woods
description: Scots pine mire woods of the western Rhodope of Bulgaria and of western and eastern Serbia, with occasional [Picea abies] and [Betula pubescens]; the accompanying cortŠge is related to that of acid fens and transition mires; [Eriophorum latifolium], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] characterize constituting communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal Scots pine bog woods
description: [Pinus sylvestris]-dominated woods of bogs of the boreal regions of western Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal Labrador tea Scots pine bog woods
description:
Scots pine bog woods of the western boreal region of the Palaearctic formed of
