source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Atlantic laurel-oak woodland
description: [Laurus nobilis]-dominated facies of evergreen oak forests characteristic of areas of warm-temperate humid conditions of the southern Atlantic coasts of the European continent and of humid microclimatic enclaves in the Mediterranean region, in particular, of coastal Asturias (cf.45.311), of Andalusia, of Istria and the Dalmatian coast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Hyrcanian lauriphyllous forests
description: Communities of the Ponto-Caspian warm-temperate humid zone of the southern shores of the Black and Caspian seas, dominated by lauriphyllous or xero-lauriphyllous evergreen tree species, in particular, [Laurus nobilis],  [Prunus laurocerasus] ([Laurocerasus officinalis]) and [Buxus hyrcanica], anomalous and often limited to exiguous enclaves within a predominantly deciduous forest environment.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Euxinian laurel and cherry-laurel woods
description: Tree-size [Laurus nobilis] or [Prunus laurocerasus] ([Laurocerasus officinalis])-dominated communities of the southern Black Sea coast of Anatolia and of sea-facing slopes of Colchis.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyrcanian box woods
description: [Buxus hyrcanica]-dominated woods of the southern Caspian lowlands and lower slopes of the Elburz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sino-Japanese lauriphyllous forests
description: Species-rich, multistratum, lauriphyllous forests of the southern half of Honshu, of Shikoku, Kyushu and the Ryukyu islands, of southern Korea, of the southeastern quadrant of continental China and of the mountains of Taiwan and Hainan, dominated by evergreen Fagaceae, in particular of genera [Castanopsis], [Cyclobalanopsis], [Pasania], [Quercus], Lauraceae, of genera [Cinnamomum], [Machilus], Theaceae ([Camellia japonica], [Schima wallichii]), Myricaceae ([Myrica rubra]), with an admixture of conifers of genera [Podocarpus], [Torreya], [Pinus], [Abies], [Tsuga], many epiphytes and lianas, and a rich undergrowth of broadleaved evergreen small trees, shrubs, small shrubs, of vines, ferns and herbaceous plants. Mixed deciduous and evergreen broad-leaved forests, similar to the evergreen forests in their extreme species richness and mixed dominance, and bamboo forests of the warm temperate zone, mostly dominated by the monopodial [Phyllostachys bambusoides], in northern areas, or [Phyllostachys pubescens], in southern areas, are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mixed deciduous-evergreen broad-leaved forests
description:
Mixed deciduous and evergreen broad-leaved forests of the northern part of the southeastern quadrant of continental China, forming a belt north of the Yangtze, in extreme southern Kansu, southern Shensi, southern Honan, northern Hupei, central Ahnwei, to the Pacific in central Kiangsu, similar to the evergreen forests of units 45.532 and 45.533 in their extreme species richness and mixed dominance, although with slightly fewer species. They are mostly limited to altitudes below 500 m. in the east, extend to 1800 m. in the west.  
The main broad-leaved evergreen constituents include [Quercus glauca], [Quercus gracilis], [Quercus myrsinaefolia], [Castanopsis sclerophylla], [Lithocarpus glabra], [Lithocarpus henryi], the Lauraceae [Cinnamomum camphora] and [Phoebe heareri], [Schima superba]), the broad-leaved deciduous components, [Quercus acutissima], [Quercus aliena], [Quercus variabilis], [Quercus fabri], [Quercus glandulifera], [Albizia kalkora], [Liquidanbar formosana], [Platycarya strobalicea], [Dalbergia huppeana], [Rhus chinensis], [Pistacia chinensis], [Diospyros kaki], [Sassafras tsuma]; associated conifers comprise [Pinus massoniana], [Cunninghamia lanceolata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Chinese evergreen broad-leaved forests
description: Broad-leaved evergreen forests of Yunnan, southwestern Sichuan and western Guizhou, mostly dominated by Fagaceae of genera [Castanopsis], [Cyclobalanopsis], [Pasania], [Quercus], with Magnoliaceae, Lauraceae, in particular, of genus [Machilus], Theaceae, in particular [Schima wallichii]) and conifers of genera [Pinus], [Ketleeria], [Torreya], [Picea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Chinese evergreen broad-leaved forests
description: Broad-leaved evergreen forests of the great Red Basin of Sichuan, of the highlands of Guizhou, of the southeastern coastal provinces of Zhejiang (Chekiang), Fujian (Fukien), Guangdong (Kwangtung) and Guangxi (Kwangsi), below 1000 m, mostly on acidic sandstones, shales or granite, but in the Red Basin and in the highlands of Guizhou, also on limestones, mostly dominated by Fagaceae of genera [Quercus], [Castanopsis] and [Pasania], associated with Theaceae of genera [Shima] and [Hartia], Lauraceae of genera [Machilus], [Phoebe], [Beilschmiedia], [Cinnamomum], Magnoliaceae of genera [Magnolia], [Maglietia], [Illicium], [Michelia] and Hamamelidaceae of genera [Altingia], [Bucklandia] and [Liquidambar]. Forests of Zhejiang (Chekiang) are composed primarily of the Fagaceae [Quercus glauca] ([Cyclobalanopsis glauca]), [Quercus myrsinaefolia], [Castanopsis sclerophylla], [Lithocarpus glabra], of the Lauraceae [Phoebe cheareri], [Machilus thunbergii], of the Theacece [Shima superba]; those of Guangdong (Kwangtung), in the south, are of [Quercus nubium], [Castanopsis fissa], [Castanopsis fordii], [Castanopsis fabri], [Castanopsis fargestii], [Castanopsis carlesii], [Machilus panhoi], [Cinnamomum japonicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Insular Chinese evergreen broad-leaved forests
description: Warm temperate broad-leaved evergreen [Castanopsis]-[Shima] forests of the higher elevations of Taiwan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Korean evergreen broad-leaved forests
description: Broad-leaved evergreen forests of southern Korea, distributed south of 35øN, in areas of mean annual temperatures greater than 14øC and on offshore islands, mostly formed by oaks [Quercus spp.] and camellias [Camellia spp.], with bamboos.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Japanese evergreen broad-leaved forests
description: Species-rich, multistratum, lauriphyllous forests of the southern half of Honshu, of Shikoku, Kyushu and the Ryukyu islands, dominated by evergreen Fagaceae, in particular of genera [Castanopsis], [Cyclobalanopsis], [Pasania], [Quercus], Lauraceae of genera [Cinnamomum], [Machilus], Theaceae ([Camellia japonica], [Schima wallichii]), Myricaceae ([Myrica rubra]), with an admixture of conifers of genera [Podocarpus], [Torreya], [Pinus], [Abies], [Tsuga], many epiphytes and lianas, and a rich undergrowth of broadleaved evergreen small trees, shrubs, small shrubs, of vines, ferns and herbaceous plants.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bamboo forests
description: Bamboo forests of the warm temperate zone of China, Korea and Japan, mostly dominated by the monopodial [Phyllostachys bambusoides], in northern areas, or [Phyllostachys pubescens], in southern areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian laurel forests
description: Humid to hyper-humid, mist-bound, luxuriant, evergreen, lauriphyllous forests of the cloud belt of the Macaronesian islands, extremely rich in floral and faunal species, among which many are restricted to these communities. Genera such as [Picconia], [Semele], [Gesnouinia], [Lactucosonchus], [Ixanthus] are entirely endemic to these communnities, while others, such as [Isoplexis], [Visnea] and [Phyllis] reach in them their maximum development; in addition, each of the formations of the various archipelagoes harbours distinctive endemic species. Laurel forests are the most complex and remarkable relict of the humid sub-tropical vegetation of the Mioceno-Pliocene late Tertiary of southern Europe. Areas of intact forests have been drastically reduced to a level below which the preservation of their elements could not be sustained.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean laurisilvas
description: Lauriphyllous forests of the Azores, with [Laurus azorica], [Myrica faya], [Frangula azorica], [Ilex perado] ssp. [azorica], [Juniperus brevifolia], [Picconia azorica], [Prunus lusitanica] ssp. [azorica], [Euphorbia stygiana], [Viburnum tinus] ssp. [subcordatum], [Vaccinium cylindraceum], [Smilax divaricata]. The humid forests of the coastal areas ("[Myrico-Pittosporietum undulati] [p.]") have been totally or almost totally degraded, largely invaded by the introduced Australian [Pittosporum undulatum]. A better representation survives of the hyperhumid forests ([Culcito-Juniperion brevifoliae] [p.]) of higher elevations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Madeiran laurisilvas
description: Lauriphyllous forests of Madeira with [Laurus azorica], [Persea indica], [Ocotea foetens], [Apollonias barbujana], [Pittosporum coriaceum], [Clethra arborea], [Visnea mocanera], [Picconia excelsa], [Prunus lusitanica] ssp. [hixa], [Heberdenia excelsa], [Vaccinium padifolium], [Ilex perado] ssp. [perado], [Ilex canariensis], [Myrica faya], [Erica arborea], [Hedera canariensis], [Isoplexis canariensis], [Euphorbia mellifera], [Sambucus lanceolata], [Teline maderensis] ([Cytisus maderensis]), [Sonchus fruticosus], [Senecio auritus] ([Senecio maderensis]), [Ruscus streptophyllus], [Rubus bollei], [Semele androgyna], [Smilax canariensis], [Tamus edulis], [Carex peregrina] and many ferns. These forests, which still occupy a relatively large surface, of the order of 10,000 ha (15% of their former surface), are the habitat of the threatened endemic Madeiran Pigeon, [Columba trocaz].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian laurisilvas
description: Lauriphyllous forests of the Canary Islands, with [Laurus azorica], [Picconia excelsa], [Persea indica], [Ocotea foetens], [Apollonias barbujana], [Visnea mocanera], [Pleiomeris canariensis] ([Myrsine canariensis]), [Ardisia bahamensis], [Prunus lusitanica], [Sambucus palmensis], [Euphorbia mellifera], [Ixanthus viscosus], [Rubus bollei], [Convolvulus canariensis], [Geranium canariensis], [Hedera canariensis], [Smilax aspera], [Smilax canariensis], [Canarina canariensis], [Semele androgyna], [Sideritis macrostachys], [Sideritis canariensis], [Cryptotaenia elegans], [Rubia peregrina], [Carex canariensis], [Asparagus fallax] and many ferns. They are the habitat of the threatened endemic laurel pigeons [Columba junionae] and [Columba bollei], now limited to La Gomera, Tenerife and La Palma. The laurel forests of each island harbour a distinctive set of endemic plants and animals, as exemplified by the species of the composite genus [Pericallis], the well-marked races of the chaffinch [Fringilla coelebs] or the carabid faunas. They are thus best listed separately. The total remnant surface of laurel forest for the four islands, La Gomera, Tenerife, La Palma and Hierro, does not exceed 5000 ha.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Laurisilvas of La Gomera
description: Laurel forests of La Gomera, best preserved and most extensive of the archipelago, with large areas of humid [Persea indica] -[Laurus azorica] forests ([Lauro-Perseetum indicae]), particularly in high areas, and good examples of [Ocotea foetens]-dominated forests, hyperhumid and very rich in ferns and epiphytes ([Athyrio-Ocoteetum foetentis]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Laurisilvas of Tenerife
description: Laurel forests of Tenerife, mostly restricted to the Anaga range and Los Silos, with a few smaller patches in Guimar ravines and at a few north slope sites in the La Esperanza-Agua Garcia area and the Barranco de San Antonio - Icod area. There are good representations of til ([Ocotea foetens]) forests (Anaga), as well as of drier [Picconia excelsa-Apollonias barbujana] forests (Los Silos).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Laurisilvas of La Palma
description: Laurel forests of La Palma essentially restricted to a few large, deep ravines of the northern slope, particularly in the Las Sauces area, including both [Lauro-Perseetum] vinyatigo-laurel and [Athyrio-Ocoteetum] til stands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Laurisilvas of Hierro
description: Laurel forests of Hierro, very small and limited to cliff sides in the Ensenada El Golfo area of the north coast.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Laurisilvas of Gran Canaria
description: Laurel forests of Gran Canaria, extinct. Very small, but fully expressed, fragments existed until very recently, notably at Los Tiles, but now appear to have been totally degraded.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Temperate palm groves
description: Woods, often riparian, formed by palm trees of the Mediterranean and Macaronesian zones, [Phoenix theophrasti] of Crete and western Anatolia, and [Phoenix canariensis] of the Canary Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cretan palm groves
description: Relict [Phoenix theophrasti] woods of Crete, restricted to damp sandy coastal valleys; they include the extensive forest of Vai, where the luxuriant palm growth is accompanied by a thick shrubby undergrowth rich in [Nerium oleander], and about four other smaller coastal groves, notably on the south coast of the prefectorate of Rethimnon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian palm groves
description: Relict [Phoenix canariensis] woods of the Canary Islands, mostly characteristic of the bottom of barrancos and of alluvial soils, below 600 metres. Palm groves are now very rare, but still exist in all the islands, with particularly representative examples at Haria on Lanzarote, Vega del Rio Palmas on Fuerteventura, Fataga, Maspalomas and the Barranco de Tirajana in Gran Canaria, Valle Gran Rey in La Gomera, Masca in Tenerife and Brena Alta in La Palma.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian palm groves
description: Relict [Phoenix theophrasti] woods of western Anatolia, restricted to a few coastal valleys.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Palaearctic holly woods
description: Woods dominated by tall arborescent [Ilex aquifolium]. They occur in the supra-Mediterranean level of Sardinia and Corsica and in Atlantic mountains of northwestern Spain, mostly as a facies of the relict yew-holly forests (unit 42.A7). Other scattered occurrences exist, in particular, in England, as a facies of Atlantic acidophilous beech-oak forests of unit 41.52, of Germano-Baltic beech forests of unit 41.121 or of Atlantic neutrophile beech forests of unit 41.132, in Scotland and in Ireland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian heath forests
description: Very tall, forest-like, formations dominated by [Erica arborea], [Myrica faya], [Arbutus canariensis] or [Visnea mocanera], occurring naturally in the most wind-exposed and the driest stations within the "monte verde" of the Canary Island cloud belt; they also form extensively as degradation stages of the laurisilva or as secondary colonists.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian fayal-brezal
description: Tall [Erica arborea]-dominated formations of Tenerife, La Palma, La Gomera, Gran Canaria and Hierro, with [Myrica faya], [Ilex canariensis], [Rhamnus glandulosa], [Viburnum tinus] ssp. [rigidum], [Cedronella canariensis], [Bystropogon canariensis], [Isoplexis canariensis], [Urtica morifolia], [Teline canariensis], [Sonchus abbreviatus], [Hypericum glandulosum], [Gesnouinia arborea] and many species of the genus [Pericallis], including several island or local endemics that characterize several differentiated communities; among these are [Pericallis tussilaginis] ([Pericallis] = [Senecio]), [Pericallis webbii], [Pericallis cruenta], [Pericallis steetzii], [Pericallis murrayi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hierran fayal
description: Tall [Myrica faya] formation of the southern slope of Hierro, almost devoid of [Erica arborea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Visnea-Arbutus] forests
description: Formations characterized by the abundance of [Arbutus canariensis] and [Visnea mocanera] occurring, in particular, in the Valle de Guimar and Los Silos of Tenerife, and in the Ladera de Jinama of Hierro.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan evergreen oak forests
description: Montane moist forests of the western Himalayas dominated by [Quercus semecarpifolia], [Quercus dilatata] or [Quercus ballota], limited, within the Palaearctic region as here defined, to Nuristan, and to the slopes and valleys of the Hindu Kush, west to central northern Afghanistan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nuristan  [Quercus dilatata] forest
description: [Quercus dilatata] forests mostly of the 2100 to 2400 metre level of the Nuristan Himalayas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nuristan [Quercus semecarpifolia] forests
description: [Quercus semecarpifolia] cloud forests of the 2500-3000 metre level, developed on scarp schist slopes of the Nuristan Himalayas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afghan [Quercus baloot] forests
description: [Quercus ballota] dry forests and steppe-forests of the 1000-2500 metre level of the lower slopes, dry inner valleys and submontane plateaux of the Hindu Kush and Safed Koh system of the western Himalayas, mostly within the watershed of the Indus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Evergreen rain forests
description: Multistrata broadleaved evergreen forests, of great species diversity, situated in the lowlands within hyperhumid, warm tropical climates lacking a dry or a cold season. Limited within the Palaearctic, as here defined, to southern Hainan and to very limited relicts on southern Taiwan and in extreme southern mainland China, in southern Guangxi and southern Yunnan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Semievergreen rain forests
description: Multistrata, species-rich, broadleaved forests of warm, very humid, tropical climates marked by seasonal moisture stress, composed of both evergreen and deciduous species in the upper storey. Species-richness in the canopy is less, gregarious occurrence is more prevalent, emergent trees are usually scarcer than in evergreen rain forests. Limited within the Palaearctic, as here defined, to Hainan, Taiwan, southern Guangxi and southern Yunnan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Monsoon forests
description: Seasonal forests of humid tropical and subtropical regions with a very protracted dry season, particularly characteristic of monsoonal climates, characterized by a mostly deciduous upper canopy, a predominantly evergreen lower canopy and well-developed shrub and herb layers. Species diversity of canopy trees is much less than in either evergreen or semievergreen rain forests and single dominance frequent, in particular, in Southeast Asia by [Tectona grandis] or [Shorea robusta]; bamboos often play a dominant role in the shrub layer. Limited within the Palaearctic, as here defined, to Hainan,  and to limited relicts on southern Taiwan, in southern Guangxi, southern Yunnan and, very locally, extreme southern Tibet.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical montane forests
description: Forests of the slopes of tropical mountains, less species-rich, lower, more even-canopied than lowland rain forests, richer in microphyllous, cool-adapted species, often loaded with bryophytes and ferns. Included are lower montane rain forests, upper montane rain forests, tropical coniferous woodland, montane bamboo woodland, elfin forest, tropical krummholz formations. Limited within the Palaearctic, as here defined, to Eritreo-Arabian communities of the southern Arabian peninsula and Egypt, and to montane formations of the tropical Far East, occurring in particular in very limited areas on Hainan and in southern Yunnan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eritreo-Arabian tropical montane woodland
description: Montane forests, of Afromontane affinities, of the extreme southwest of the Arabian peninsula and of the coastal Red Sea mountains of Egypt.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afromontane juniper forests
description: [Juniperus procera]-dominated formations of southwestern Arabia, northernmost outpost of a formation distributed from Arabia and the Red Sea hills of Sudan through the east African mountain archipelago south to the Nyika Plateau of Malawi. They are developed in the 1500 to 3000 metre level, and higher on Jebel Sabor, of the ranges that parallel the Red Sea coast in Yemen and near Taif. Accompanying the juniper are [Euryops arabica], [Dodonaea viscosa], [Themeda triandra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eritreo-Arabian montane olive woodland
description: Broadleaved evergreen, sclerophyllous tropical montane forests and thickets  of southwestern Arabian mountains, with an outpost in the Gebel Elba of the Red Sea coastal mountains of Egypt. [Olea chrysophylla], [Tarchonanthus camphoratus], [Myrsine africana], [Buddleja polystachya], [Barbeya oleoides], [Maesa lanceolata], [Nuxia dentata], [Rhus abyssinica], [Rhus retinorrhoea], [Euclea kellau], [Teclea nobilis], [Celtis spp.], [Ficus spp.], [Dracaena ombet] participate in the composition of various communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern tropical montane forests
description: Forests of the slopes of tropical mountains of the Far East, including lower montane rain forests, upper montane rain forests, tropical coniferous woodland, montane bamboo woodland, elfin forest, tropical krummholz formations, occurring in particular in Hainan and southern Yunnan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tropical swamp forests
description: Edaphically determined forests of the evergreen and deciduous tropical forest zones, developed on hydromorphic, nonsaline soils and often characterized by a strong tendancy to monophytism. They include peat swamp tropical forests, fresh water swamp tropical forests, fresh water periodic swamp forests, tropical riverine forests. They are limited within the Palaearctic, as here defined, to the tropical Far East, where they have, however, been almost entirely cleared for cultivation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dry tropical woodland
description: Forests and woodlands of dry tropical regions, of simpler structure and considerably lower species richness than rain and monsoon forests, often characterized by a relatively low, open canopy. Included are varied formations known as closed dry forests, open dry forests, savanna woodland, wooded savanna, thorn forest, thorn woodland, tropical scrub, bushland. They are limited, within the Palaearctic, as here defined, to the Saharo-Mediterranean, Saharo-Sindian, Sahelian and Sino-Tropical zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Argan woodland
description: [Argania spinosa] thorn forests, thorn woodland, scrub forests and "bushlands" of the arid and semiarid levels of southwest Morocco, with [Acacia gummifera], [Ziziphus lotus], [Olea europaea], [Pistacia lentiscus], [Pistacia atlantica], and often abundant succulent [Euphorbia beaumierana] or [Euphorbia echinus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical palm groves
description: Woods and stands, often riparian, formed by palm trees of the Mediterraneo-Saharan, Saharo-Sindian and Sahelian zones, including [Phoenix dactylifera], [Phoenix atlantica], [Nannorrhops ritchiana], [Hyphaene thebaica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Date palm communities
description: Indigenous or spontaneous stands and long-established oasis plantations of [Phoenix dactylifera] of the Saharo-Sindian and Saharo-Mediterranean regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Date palm stands
description: Indigenous or spontaneous stands of [Phoenix dactylifera] installed on rocky slopes, in canyons, on coastal dunes and in saline or brackish wadis and flats, of the Saharo-Sindian and Saharo-Mediterranean regions. The area of indigenousness is unknown but has been suggested to be restricted to Arabia, or to encompass a much larger area, including, in particular, North Africa's coastal dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Date palm oases
description: Long-established plantations of [Phoenix dactylifera] of the Saharo-Sindian and Saharo-Mediterranean regions, entirely replacing the natural vegetation of desert and subdesert oases, and providing an important substitution habitat for animal communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cape Verde palm groves
description: Formations of the endemic [Phoenix atlantica] of the Cape Verde archipelago.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Doum palm communities
description: [Hyphaene thebaica] woods and stands of wadis, mountain gorges, salt marshes, sand dunes and sometimes oases of the southern Sahara, the Sinai and the Arabian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Nannorrhops] stands
description: [Nannorrhops ritchiana] formations of southern Iran and eastern Afghanistan, characteristic of sheltered mountain valleys with a reasonably high water table.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Medemia argun] stands
description: Relict stand of the endangered [Medemia argun] of the Dungul Oasis of southern Egypt, involving only a few individuals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Sindian thorn woodland
description: Thorn forests, thorn woodlands and savanna woodlands of the Saharo-Sindian region, locally reaching the Mediterraneo-Saharan region, and of the Sahelian region of Mauritania, dominated by acacias ([Acacia], [Prosopis]), or species of genera [Ziziphus], [Balanites], [Maerua], [Maytenus], [Salvadora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Saharan thorn woodland
description: Acacia-dominated formations of the northern confines of the Sahara, in the Saharo-Mediterranean transition zone.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Saharan [Acacia raddiana] woodland
description: [Acacia raddiana]-dominated savanna woodland of the northern fringes of the Sahara, now limited to a very few relict formations in the Oued Dra basin of Morocco and adjacent Algerian regions and in the Djebel Bou-Hedma of central Tunisia, where it constitutes an essential potential habitat and restoration center for the endangered antelope [Oryx dammah], with [Ziziphus lotus], [Retama retam], [Periploca laevigata], [Aristida plumosa], [Aristida obtusa], [Digitaria nodosa], [Cenchrus ciliaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Acacia gummifera] woodland
description: Endemic [Acacia gummifera] woodland and scrub land of the plateaux of western Morocco, now reduced to remnant stands, in particular, at Haouz-Tadla. The acacias are accompanied by [Ephedra altissima], [Asparagus stipularis], [Lavandula multiflora], [Ballota hispanica], [Bryonia dioica], [Peganum harmala] and many therophytes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharan thorn woodland
description: Open woodland or savanna woodland, steppe woodland or desert woodland of the  Sahara, dominated by [Acacia raddiana], [Acacia ehrenbergiana], [Acacia seyal], [Ziziphus mauritiana], [Balanites aegyptiaca], [Maerua crassifolia], [Salvadora persica], [Calotropis procera], [Capparis decidua], with [Cassia italica], [Ziziphus lotus], [Caylusea hexagyna], [Lavandula stricta], [Seetzenia africana], [Panicum turgidum], characteristic of the rocky beds of wadis and the alluvial gravels of outwash fans.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sahelian thorn woodland
description: [Acacia]-dominated thorn woodlands of the Sahelian zone of Mauritania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mauritanian [Acacia] steppe woodland
description: Open formations of [Acacia raddiana], [Acacia senegal], [Acacia ehrenbergiana], [Maerua crassifolia], [Balanites aegyptiaca], [Ziziphus mauritiana], [Combretum aculeatum], accompanied by steppic tropical grassland or rainy season temporary grasslands with therophytes, of the Sahelian region of Mauritania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Acacia nilotica] woodland
description: [Acacia nilotica]-dominated communities, often closed, of the Senegal valley of Mauritania, developed in particular on dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arabian thorn woodland
description: Open woodland or savanna woodland, steppe woodland, savanoid desert or desert woodland of the Arabian Peninsula and the Sinai, dominated by [Acacia raddiana], [Acacia tortilis], [Acacia gerrardii], [Acacia hamulosa], [Balanites aegyptiaca] or [Ziziphus spina-christi], with [Maerua crassifolia], [Salvadora persica], [Calotropis procera], [Cordia gharaf], [Capparis decidua], [Capparis cartilaginea], [Hammada salicornica], [Anabasis articulata], [Gymnocarpos decander], [Cassia italica], [Panicum turgidum], mostly confined to wadis and depressions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nubio-Arabian thorn woodland
description: Open woodland or savanna woodland of the tropical southwestern and southeastern plains and hills of the Arabian Peninsula and of extreme southeastern Egypt, dominated by [Acacia tortilis], [Acacia ehrenbergiana], [Acacia asak], [Acacia mellifera], [Acacia senegal], [Acacia oerfota], [Acacia seyal], [Acacia hamulosa], [Acacia laeta], [Acacia etbaica], [Balanites aegyptiaca], [Maerua crassifolia], [Aristida plumosa], [Lasiurus hirsutus], [Panicum turgidum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Persian thorn woodland
description: Open woodland, savanna woodland or desert woodland of the subtropical desert zone of southern Iran, with [Acacia nilotica] ssp. [indica] ([Acacia flava]), [Acacia oerfota] ([Acacia aucheri]), [Prosopis farcta], [Prosopis spicigera], [Ziziphus spina-christi], [Ziziphus nummularia], [Calotropis procera], [Periploca aphylla], [Dodonaea viscosa], [Amygdalus arabica], [Capparis spinosa], [Hammada salicornica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sindo-Afghan thorn woodland
description: [Ziziphus nummularia] thorn woodland of the Jalalabad basin of eastern Afghanistan, northwesternmost extension of pre-Sindian middle Indus communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cape Verde thorn woodland
description: Woods, thickets or wooded pastures of the Cape Verde Islands dominated by naturally or probably naturally occurring African trees characteristic of dry woodland communities, in particular, [Acacia albida], [Ficus capensis], [Ficus sycamorus], [Tamarindus indica], [Calotropis procera].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-montane olive woodland
description: [Olea laperrinei] formations of wadis of the higher altitudes, above 1800 metres, of the Ahaggar, the Tafedest, the Mouydir, the Tassili N'Ajjer, with an admixture of Mediterranean, Saharan, Sahelian and Afro-montane species, including [Pistacia atlantica], [Rhus tripartita], [Artemisia campestris] ssp. [glutinosa], [Stipa parviflora], [Stipa capensis], [Oryzopsis coerulescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Arabian [Ficus] woodland
description: Mesophilous ravine and valley gallery forest of the southeast of the Arabian peninsula, with [Ficus sycomorus], [Ficus glumosa], [Ficus lutea], [Ficus populifolia], [Ficus salicifolia], [Rhus glaucescens], [Diospyros mespilliformis], [Tamarindus indica], [Trichylia emetica], [Olea chrysophylla] and [Grewia spp.], [Combretum trichanthum], [Dracena spp.], [Phoenix reclinata] and many lianas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Socotran dry tropical woodland
description: Evergreen bushland and thickets, semievergreen bushland and open woodland of Socotra, island outpost of East African evergreen and semievergreen bushlands and thickets, distributed on drier slopes of mountains and hills from central Tanzania to Eritrea and Ethiopia, with a maximum development in Ethiopian highlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Socotran dragon tree woodland
description: Open [Dracaena cinnabari]-dominated woodland of limestone slopes of the Hagghier Mountains and of the Hamadera Hills of Socotra, with [Boswellia ameero], [Boswellia elongata], [Boswellia socotrana], [Aloe perryi], [Adenium socotranum], [Mitolepis intricata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Socotran evergreen thickets
description: Formations of [Cephalocroton socotranus], [Carissa edulis], [Buxus hildebrandtii], [Dodonaea viscosa], [Ficus socotrana], [Indigofera sokotrana], [Ruellia insignis], [Boswellia ameero], [Euphorbia socotrana], of granite slopes of the Hagghier range of Socotra.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Socotran cucurbit forest
description: Open, succulent, Socotran woodland dominated by [Dendrosicyos socotrana], the only arborescent Cucurbitaceae, belonging to a monospecific genus endemic to the island, accompanied by [Euphorbia arbuscula], [Euphorbia spiralis], [Adenium socotranum], [Dorstenia gigas], [Kleinia scottii], [Kalanchoe robusta], [Aloe perryi], [Cissus subaphylla], developed on sandstone plateaux and on limestone cliffs and valley slopes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-Himalayan olive woodland
description: Dry open evergreen sclerophyllous woodland developed on sub-Himalayan and sub-Hindukushian hills and plateaux of the Indus watershed of eastern Afghanistan, of Indo-Himalayan affinities, with [Olea ferruginea] ([Olea cuspidata]), [Monotheca buxifolia] ([Reptonia buxifolia]), [Quercus ballota], [Pistacia integerrima], [Ficus palmata], [Cotinus coggygria], [Punica granatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern dry tropical woodland
description: Closed dry forests, open dry forests, savanna woodland, thorn forests of the tropical regions of mainland China, of Hainan, Taiwan and of tropical Pacific islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mangrove forests and scrubs
description: Tropical intertidal mud forests and thickets formed by mangroves and their associates. Worldwide, mangrove forests can be divided into two large ensembles, Atlantic-type mangals, species-poor formations characteristic of the west coast of Africa as well as of the tropical Pacific and Atlantic coasts of the Americas, and Oriental-type mangals, species-rich formations of the Indian Ocean, of the western and central Pacific and of their associated tropical seas. In the Palaearctic region, as here defined, Oriental mangals occur along the coasts of the Pacific, north to southern Japan, of the Arabian Sea, of the Red Sea, Atlantic mangals along the coasts of west Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic mangrove forests and scrubs
description: Species-poor [Rhizophora racemosa], [Rhizophora mangle], [Rhizophora harrisonii], [Avicennia nitida], [Avicennia schauerana] formations of the west coast of Africa and of the tropical Pacific and Atlantic coasts of the Americas, with [Laguncularia racemosa], [Conocarpus erectus], [Drepanocarpus lunulatus], [Acrostichum aureum], [Hibiscus tiliaceus]. The complex of formations is represented in the Palaearctic zone, as here defined, by extremely localized mangrove scrubs of the coast of Mauritania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oriental mangrove forests and scrubs
description: Species-rich [Rhizophora mucronata], [Rhizophora apiculata], [Rhizophora stylosa], [Rhizophora lamarckii], [Rhizophora mangle], [Avicennia marina], [Avicennia spp.], [Bruguiera spp.], [Ceriops spp.], [Kandelia spp.], [Sonneratia spp.], [Lumnitzera spp.], [Aegiceras spp.], [Xylocarpus spp.], [Acanthus spp.], [Nypa spp.] formations of the Indian Ocean, of the western and central Pacific and of their associated tropical seas, represented within the Palaearctic zone, as here defined, by mangrove communities of the Red Sea, of the Arabian Sea and of the western Pacific north to Hainan, Kwangtung, Kwangsi, Fukien, Taiwan and southern Japan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bogs and marshes
description: Mire communities, for the most part turfogenic, of sedges, grasses, rushes, bryophytes and their associated species; tall helophyte fringes of water bodies. Complex systems of raised bogs, blanket bogs, rich fens, acidic fens, transition mires, boreal marsh-fens, aapa, palsa and polygon mires characterized by the presence of these communities, but also including formations otherwise typical of sections 22, 31, 37, 44. Spring systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Raised bogs
description: Highly oligotrophic, strongly acidic communities composed mainly of sphagnum growing on, and forming, peat and deriving moisture and nutrients only from rainfall (ombrotrophic). They form only in cool climates with heavy rainfall. They are most widespread in the boreal zone and in the mountains and hills of the nemoral zone; they occur locally in the lowlands of the nemoral zone and rarely in the middle Eurasian steppe zone. Within the western Palaearctic region, they are characteristic of lowlands and hills of northwestern and northern Europe, the adjacent Hercynian ranges, the Jura, the Alps, the Carpathians. In the eastern Palaearctic, they are known from Amurland, West Kamchatka, East Kamchatka, Sakhalin, the Altai. Their independence from ground water is the result either of upward growth or of changes in the water table. Bogs harbour, in addition to various sphagnum species, which are abundant, dominant and the major component of their formation, a small number of acidophilous plants such as [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Scirpus cespitosus] ([Trichophorum cespitosum]), [Carex pauciflora], [Carex paupercula], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Andromeda polifolia], [Drosera rotundifolia] and lichens. Animal species are not numerous but those that are adapted to bogs are highly specialised. Among typical invertebrates figure dragonflies ([Leucorrhinia dubia], [Aeshna subarctica], [Aeshna caerulea], [Aeshna juncea], [Somatochlora arctica], [Somatochlora alpestris]), lepidopterans ([Colias palaeno], [Boloria aquilonaris], [Coenonympha tullia], [Vacciniina optilete], [Hypenodes turfosalis], [Eugraphe subrosea]), beetles, ants ([Formica exsecta]), bugs and spiders ([Pardosa sphagnicola], [Glyphesis cottonae]). Most of the species that bogs harbour are rare and their populations fragmented into isolated relictual elements; several are threatened. The remaining intact or nearly intact communities are exceptional.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Near-natural raised bogs
description: Undisturbed, or little disturbed, peat-forming bogs of the Palaearctic region, often taking the shape of a convex lens. Such intact or nearly intact systems have become very rare or even exceptional. They are composed of a number of communities, which form and occupy the topological features of the bog. These communities are interrelated and function as a unit, so that they cannot be regarded as separate subhabitats; their presence and combination, however, characterizes the various types of bogs. Simultaneous use of an appropriate selection of the subunits below can thus contribute to a description of individual bog systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog hummocks, ridges and lawns
description: Vegetation of the higher parts of the plateau of Palaearctic bogs and of its drier, marginal slope. Intact, typical, raised bogs of northern, lowland and low montane central and eastern Europe display an alternance of well-marked sphagnum hummocks, colonized or not, especially in their drier upper part, by small shrubs, lower, wetter, flat lawns and wet hollows or schlenken. Sphagnum hummocks with no, or few, shrubs are listed in unit 51.111, sphagnum hummocks, or parts of them, colonized by shrubs in unit 51.113, lawns in unit 51.112. In bogs under strong oceanic influence, in high-altitude bogs, in bogs subjected to mineralotrophic influences or anthropogenic degradation, a sparse cover of shrubs or tussock-forming graminoids may become ubiquitous and the distinction between hummock and lawn, or even between hummock, lawn and hollow, blurred, in bogs that are often somewhat intermediate towards blanket bogs. Such communities are listed in units 51.114 to 51.116, as well as in 51.17 and in 51.2; in some of them sphagna may be scarce or replaced by bryopsid mosses. Well-defined sphagnum hummocks of unit 51.111 may nevertheless develop in conjunction with them. The dominance role is played by deergrass, [Scirpus cespitosus], in montane central European bogs, or parts of bogs listed in unit 51.114. In Atlantic bogs listed in unit 51.115 it is played by [Erica tetralix]. Somewhat degraded bogs, in particular, bogs affected by anthropozoogenic influences in Atlantic climates, may be overwhelmingly dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum], usually with complete blurring of the structure. They are listed in unit 51.116. More severely degraded bogs, invaded by [Molinia caerulea], are listed in unit 51.2. The highly distinctive shrub and sphagnum or shrub and moss hummocks bog expanses of the montane, rapidly dessicating, bogs of the boreal and subarctic zones are listed in unit 51.17. Sphagnum hummocks forming in acidic fens (unit 54.4), transition mires (unit 54.5) or, sometimes, rich fens (unit 54.2), are also indicated by codes of units 51.111 or 51.113.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Colourful sphagnum hummocks (bulten)
description: Cushiony domes or buttes of Palaearctic bogs, mainly made of red, yellow or brown sphagna, with other mosses, in particular, [Campylopus pyriformis] ([Campylopus fragilis] var. [pyriformis]), liverworts, including [Odontoschisma sphagni], [Mylia anomala], lichens ([Cladonia spp.], [Cladina spp.]), [Andromeda polifolia], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Drosera rotundifolia], and a small admixture of vascular plants characteristic of the lawn, such as  [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Carex pauciflora], [Scirpus cespitosus], or of dwarf shrub hummocks, in particular, [Calluna vulgaris], [Ledum palustre], [Erica tetralix], communities which are, in any case, usually closely associated with these.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum magellanicum] hummocks
description: Bog hummocks formed by the swollen-leaved, brownish or greenish-red [Sphagnum magellanicum], characteristic of suboceanic bogs, notably of bogs of the Danish archipelago, of sub-Atlantic Scandinavia in southeastern Norway and western Sweden, of northern Central Europe, of the southeastern Baltic lowlands, of the middle European Hercynian ranges, from the Ardennes, the Central Massif, the Vosges, the Black Forest east to the Bohemian Quadrangle, of the northern pre-Alpine plateaux and the Alps south to the southern Alps, of Amurland, also reported from the subalpine level of the Altai.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum fuscum] hummocks
description: Shiny brown [Sphagnum fuscum] hummocks, dense, usually low and wide, characteristic of bogs of subcontinental boreal Europe from southeastern Norway, central and eastern Sweden eastwards, of continental boreal Europe and western Siberia, of Kamchatka, of Sakhalin, of nemoral Central Europe and of boreonemoral Eastern Europe, of the Alps and the Carpathians, occasionally prominent in more western, more Atlantic, bogs, in particular, in the British Isles, also occurring as ombrotrophic bog hummocks within acidic or neutrocline mires of the same regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum rubellum] hummock wreaths
description: Dark red [Sphagnum rubellum] ([Sphagnum capillifolium] var. [rubellum]) communities often encircling the bases of [Sphagnum magellanicum] or [Sphagnum fuscum] hummocks of nemoral European bogs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum rubellum] hummocks
description: Hummocks of western Palaearctic bogs, mostly characteristic of Atlantic to  sub-Atlantic nemoral bogs, recorded, in particular, from Jutland and southwestern Norway, the British Isles, the eastern Netherlands, eastern and southeastern Belgium, France, Germany and the Alps, dominated by [Sphagnum rubellum] ([Sphagnum capillifolium] var. [rubellum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum imbricatum] hummocks
description: Often tall, large, dense hummocks of European bogs formed by the large, orange-gold [Sphagnum imbricatum], limited to undisturbed bogs in areas of strong maritime influence, in particular, in the British Isles, southwestern Sweden, Hercynian Belgium, northwestern Germany, formerly common, today rare and increasingly so.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum papillosum] hummocks
description: Low hummocks of olive-brown or ocre [Sphagnum papillosum], formed mostly in bogs of western and northern Europe, in particular, of the British Isles, Denmark, northwestern Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium. Outside of bogs, [Sphagnum papillosum] hummocks may form in a variety of mires, particularly in Atlantic regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum capillifolium] hummocks
description: Hummocks of Palaearctic bogs formed by the reddish [Sphagnum capillifolium] ([Sphagnum capillifolium] var. [capillifolium]), known, in particular, from the southeastern Baltic coastal regions, from higher levels of the western and central European Hercynian ranges, from the Alps and from the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum angustifolium] hummocks
description: Hummocks of Palaearctic bogs formed by [Sphagnum angustifolium], recorded, in particular, from northeastern Europe and France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog cottonsedge-sphagnum lawns and green hummock bases
description: Communities dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] and sphagna, in particular, green or yellow [Sphagnum cuspidatum], [Sphagnum recurvum] ([Sphagnum apiculatum], [Sphagnum fallax]), [Sphagnum pulchrum], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum balticum], [Sphagnum tenellum], also [Sphagnum magellanicum], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum fuscum] and others, constituting extensive carpets or lawns, or, sometimes with a lesser prominence of [Eriophorum vaginatum], forming in the transition zone between hollows and hummocks of Palaearctic bogs; [Drosera rotundifolia], [Andromeda polifolia], [Vaccinium oxycoccos] are often common.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum tenellum] lawns
description: Communities of bog lawns and of areas intermediate between hollows and hummocks in which often small loose cushions of [Sphagnum tenellum] dominate the ground layer, usally in association with [Sphagnum balticum], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum subnitens], and with an emergent layer of [Eriophorum vaginatum], characteristic, in particular, of Finland, the southeastern Baltic coastlands, also recorded from Scandinavia, Britain and Ireland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum pulchrum] lawns
description: Hollow-side and lawn communities of Palaearctic bogs dominated by the bright orange [Sphagnum pulchrum] associated with [Eriophorum vaginatum], recorded, in particular, from northwestern Central Europe, Ireland and western Britain.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum papillosum] lawns
description: Lawns and hummock-to-hollow transition communities of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Sphagnum papillosum] associated with [Eriophorum vaginatum], most characteristic of maritime and submaritime regions of the western and eastern Palaearctic, often constituting the dominant lawn community in Atlantic and sub-Atlantic bogs of nemoral Europe. [Erica tetralix] is a usual member of the community in western regions; when its cover exceeds that of [Eriophorum vaginatum] the stands should be listed under unit 51.115. In boreal Europe [Sphagnum papillosum] carpets are more characteristic of minerotrophic acidic fens than of bogs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum capillifolium] lawns
description: Lawns of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] associated with [Sphagnum capillifolium] ([Sphagnum capillifolium] var. [capillifolium]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum recurvum] lawns
description: Lawns of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] associated with [Sphagnum recurvum], often highly prevalent in moderately wet bogs of nemoral Central Europe and Hercynian Western Europe. In boreal Europe, [Sphagnum recurvum] communities are mostly limited to fens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum fuscum] lawns
description: Lawns of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] associated with [Sphagnum fuscum] characteristic of subcontinental Fennoscandia, from eastern Sweden eastwards, of the eastern Baltic bog province of western Russia, of the Eastern Carpathians, of western Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum rubellum] lawns
description: Lawns of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] associated with [Sphagnum rubellum] ([Sphagnum capillifolium] var. [rubellum]) characteristic of relatively maritime climates, recorded, in particular, from southeastern Norway, western Sweden and the Danish archipelago, where [Sphagnum balticum] is a frequent accompanier, and from the Central Massif of France, where [Sphagnum magellanicum] is an associate.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum balticum] lawns
description: Lawns of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] associated with [Sphagnum balticum] characteristic of bogs of the nemoral region, in particular, of large areas of Sweden, of Finland, the Baltic States, Russia, western Siberia. Accompaniers include [Scirpus cespitosus], [Eriophorum russeolum], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum tenellum], [Sphagnum lindbergii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum angustifolium] lawns
description: Lawns of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] associated with [Sphagnum angustifolium] characteristic of northeastern Europe and eastern Fennoscandia, mostly distributed in northern Karelia, the Lake and Bothnian gulf regions of Finland, rare in Sweden.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Eriophorum-Sphagnum magellanicum] lawns
description: Lawns of Palaearctic bogs dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum] associated with [Sphagnum magellanicum] and [Sphagnum rubellum], sometimes accompanied by [Sphagnum tenellum], [Sphagnum angustifolium], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum recurvum], [Sphagnum fuscum] or [Sphagnum warnstorfii], characteristic, in particular, of the British Isles, southern Scandinavia, in Denmark, Norway and southern Sweden, of the northern and southern Alpine piedmont, of the Eastern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf shrub hummocks
description: Dwarf shrub communities, mostly ericaceous, forming on the top of drying hummocks of bogs of the nemoral, boreonemoral, lowland boreal and low montane boreal regions of the Palaearctic, often with the moss [Polytrichum strictum], sometimes colonizing sphagnum hummocks forming in fens of the same regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ling dwarf shrub hummocks
description: [Calluna vulgaris]-dominated shrub hummocks, widespread in the nemoral and boreal zones of the western Palaearctic region, east to the Carpathians and western Siberia, south to the Alpine piedmont and the Pyrenees, most characteristic of Central European and sub-Atlantic Scandinavian bogs, in which [Calluna vulgaris] is often the only dominant hummock shrub.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cross-leaved heather shrub hummocks
description: [Erica tetralix]-dominated communities characteristic of the shrub hummocks of Atlantic bogs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Crowberry shrub hummocks
description: Shrub hummocks of lowland or low montane Northern Europe, of Western Europe, of lowland Central Europe, the Baltic region, the Hercynian ranges, the Alps, the Northern Carpathians dominated by [Empetrum nigrum] or, in boreal regions, in mountains and in eastern Central Europe, [Empetrum hermaphroditum], characteristic of suboceanic climates, of drier, taller hummocks or of slightly more mineral-influenced bogs of Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Vaccinium] shrub hummocks
description: Shrub hummocks of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic lowland or low montane boreal Europe, of the European Hercynian ranges, the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Carpathians, and their periphery, dominated by ericoid shrubs of genus [Vaccinium], mostly [Vaccinium uliginosum], also [Vaccinium vitis-idaea] or [Vaccinium myrtillus], locally, in particular, in Scandinavia and the Alps, associated with [Betula nana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Labrador tea shrub hummocks
description: Shrub hummocks of boreonemoral, subboreal, lowland boreal and low montane boreal regions of the Palaearctic dominated by [Ledum palustre], most characteristic of subcontinental regions of the southeastern Baltic hinterland, from eastern Germany, Poland, the Baltic States to boreonemoral Russia, and of the southern boreal Far East of Kamchatcka and northern Sakhalin, often marking tall hummocks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog myrtle hummocks
description: Shrub hummocks dominated by [Myrica gale], of local occurrence in nemoral Atlantic bogs, or by [Myrica tomentosa] in the southern boreal Pacific Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dwarf birch hummocks
description: Dwarf shrub hummock communities of nemoral Europe and of the lowland and hill bogs of boreal Europe, west to Fennoscandia and the Baltic States, dominated by, or rich in, [Betula nana]. In nemoral Europe they are limited to isolated enclaves on hills of the Germano-Baltic plains and to rare stations within the greater Hercynian ranges and the Alps, where they represent relict outposts of the communities of unit 51.17, with which they share, in particular, besides [Betula nana], [Vaccinium microcarpus], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Chamaedaphne calyculata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cloudberry hummocks
description: Dwarf shrub hummock communities of subcontinental and continental, lowland or low montane boreal and boreonemoral Europe dominated by, or rich in, [Rubus chamaemorus], associated with [Calluna vulgaris] or with [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Ledum palustre], [Chamaedaphne calyculata], characteristic, in particular, of eastern Fennoscandia, the southeastern and eastern Baltic regions, Russia, with outposts in the eastern Hercynian ranges, in the Giant Mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Leatherleaf hummocks
description: Shrub hummocks dominated by [Chamaedaphne calyculata], main shrub hummock type of the continental parts of the boreal and boreonemoral Palaearctic, in European Russia, Siberia, the Russian Far East, with outposts in Baltic regions and the eastern Hercynian ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog deergrass communities
description: [Scirpus cespitosus]-dominated bogs or parts of bogs, mostly characteristic of the subalpine level of Hercynian, pre-Alpine and Alpine ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog [Erica-Sphagnum] communities
description: Bogs or parts of bogs dominated by [Erica tetralix] and [Sphagnum papillosum], characteristic of raised bog systems of Atlantic regions, particularly the British Isles, the low countries, northwestern Germany.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Raised bog species-poor cottonsedge communities
description: Bogs or parts of bogs overwhelmingly dominated by [Eriophorum vaginatum], with a strongly impoverished species cortŠge, in particular, with very few sphagna, characteristic of degraded and, in particular, grazed, bog systems of Atlantic regions, notably of the Pennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog hollows (schlenken)
description: Temporarily or permanently rainwater-filled depressions of bogs, occupied by communities similar to those of larger intermediate mires of units 54.5 or 54.6.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sphagnum schlenken
description: Constantly submerged hollows carpeted by floating or bottom-hugging mats of often bright green sphagna, in particular, [Sphagnum cuspidatum], [Sphagnum recurvum], [Sphagnum majus] ([Sphagnum dusenii]), [Sphagnum balticum], sometimes accompanied by bryopsid mosses, in particular, [Drepanocladus fluitans], [Lophozia inflata], and with a vascular cortŠge that may typically be dominated by [Rhynchospora alba], [Scheuchzeria palustris], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Menyanthes trifoliata] or [Carex limosa], and include [Carex paupercula], [Carex pauciflora], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Andromeda polifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum cuspidatum] schlenken
description: Bog hollows dominated by [Sphagnum cuspidatum], characteristic of Atlantic and sub-Atlantic Western and Central Europe, of Baltic regions, of southern Fennoscandia; associates include [Sphagnum balticum] in Fennoscandia and Baltic regions, [Sphagnum recurvum] in more Atlantic regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum majus] schlenken
description: Bog hollows dominated by [Sphagnum majus] ([Sphagnum dusenii]), particularly characteristic of Fennoscandia and boreal Eastern Europe, also locally prominent in Central Europe; associates include, in particular, [Sphagnum balticum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum auriculatum] schlenken
description: Bog hollows dominated by [Sphagnum auriculatum], characteristic of Atlantic regions, in particular, of the British Isles, western Scandinavia, Lower Saxony, also recorded from the Alps; associates include [Sphagnum subsecundum] ssp. [inundatum] and the bright orange-yellow [Sphagnum pulchrum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum balticum] schlenken
description: Bog hollows dominated by [Sphagnum balticum], characteristic of subcontinental and continental regions of the boreal western Palaearctic, from northeastern Sweden and Finland to western Siberia, and of Baltic regions; associates include [Sphagnum lindbergii], [Sphagnum majus], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum magellanicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum lindbergii] schlenken
description: Bog hollows dominated by [Sphagnum lindbergii] or, in eastern regions, by the very similar [Sphagnum lenense], characteristic of continental and eastern regions of the boreal and subarctic zones of the Palaearctic, from the White Sea area to the Far East, with outposts in the Alps and the Bohemian quadrangle; associates include [Sphagnum balticum] and  [Sphagnum papillosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum jensenii] schlenken
description: Bog hollows dominated by [Sphagnum jensenii], characteristic, in particular, of bogs of boreal Russia, within the northeast European bog province; associates include, in particular, [Sphagnum majus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum angustifolium] schlenken
