description: Bog hollows dominated by [Sphagnum angustifolium], characteristic of subcontinental bogs, in particular, of bogs of the great Hercynian ranges and of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum tenellum] schlenken
description: Bog hollows dominated by usually small cushions of [Sphagnum tenellum], recorded from bogs of southern Fennoscandia, of the Baltic lands, of the Alpine periphery; associates include, in particular, [Sphagnum cuspidatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mud-bottom schlenken
description: Temporarily inundated shallow hollows, usually dominated by an often sparse cover of [Rhynchospora alba], with [Rhynchospora fusca], [Scheuchzeria palustris], [Drosera intermedia], [Lycopodiella inundata], sometimes dominated by [Eriophorum angustifolium] or [Eriophorum vaginatum], with a ground cover almost devoid of sphagna and often reduced to algae, in particular, the conjugate [Zygogonium ericetorum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog pools
description: Larger, deep, permanently filled depressions, usually distrophic, occurring near the centre of raised bogs or along tension lines. Their planctonic communities are original. Floating plant communities may sometimes develop, in particular those comprising [Sparganium minimum] and [Utricularia spp.] (unit 22.45) and, sometimes, beds of [Nymphaea spp.] (unit 22.4311).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog eye (kolk)
description: Large pools or lakes occurring near the centre of central European raised bogs, often with relatively firm, steep banks colonized by trees or scrub forming a ring of woodland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesser bog pools
description: Relatively large, deep, permanently filled depressions occurring along tension lines of raised bogs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog seeps and soaks
description: Paths of water runoff carving the marginal slope of the bog, carrying water from the centre to the lagg. They are in part colonized by intermediate mire or acid fen vegetation of units 54.5 or 54.4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog asphodel seeps
description: [Narthecium ossifragum] colonies in seep rivulets, mostly characteristic of western bogs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog myrtle soaks
description: [Myrica gale] thickets of Atlantic raised bog soaks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lagg
description: Ring of water surrounding raised bogs, often colonized by intermediate mire or acid fen communities of units 54.5 or 54.4, sometimes accompanied by more basicline species typical of neighbouring fens; [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Scirpus hudsonianus], [Carex rostrata], [Carex flava], [Parnassia palustris] are frequent components.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bog pre-woods
description: Parts of raised bogs colonized by shrubs or small trees of [Pinus rotundata], [Pinus sylvestris] var. [turfosa], [Picea abies], [Betula pubescens], [Betula carpatica], eventually leading to bog woods of unit 44.A.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreoalpine dwarf-shrub hummocks
description: Communities of the boreoalpine, subalpine, arctoalpine and northern lowland regions of Iceland, Fennoscandia, the Kola peninsula and the Urals formed by hummocks, banks or plateaux of sphagna or of bryopsid mosses associated with small shrubs, particularly [Betula nana], also [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Rubus chamaemorus], accompanied by [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Carex nigra]. They may associate with depressions occupied by lawn, hollow or mud bottom communities; they are prone to a rapid dessication. They show affinities with blanket bogs of unit 52, in particular, with upland blanket bogs of unit 52.2 and northern boreal blanket bogs of unit 52.4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreoalpine sphagnum dwarf-shrub hummocks
description: Communities of the boreoalpine, subalpine and arctoalpine regions of Fennoscandia, the Kola peninsula and the Urals formed by hummocks, banks or plateaux of sphagna dominated by [Sphagnum fuscum], sometimes with abundant lichens [Cladonia alpestris], [Cladonia rangiferina], [Cladonia sylvatica], with small shrubs, especially [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Betula nana], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], often with a presence or abundance of [Eriophorum vaginatum] and a species cortŠge that may include [Andromeda polifolia], [Arctostaphylos alpina], [Ledum palustre], [Loiseleuria procumbens], [Salix glauca], [Vaccinium microcarpus], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Pedicularis lapponica], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Carex bigelowii], [Carex dioica], [Carex rostrata], [Carex vaginata], [Eriophorum angustifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreoalpine moss dwarf-shrub hummocks
description: Communities of the boreoalpine, subalpine, arctoalpine and northern lowland regions of Iceland, Fennoscandia, the Kola peninsula and the Urals formed by hummocks, banks or plateaux of bryopsid mosses, including an abundance of [Dicranum bergeri], [Hylocomium splendens], [Pleurozium schreberi], [Polytrichum strictum], by small shrubs, especially [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Betula nana], [Vaccinium uliginosum] and, on the continent, [Ledum palustre], [Rubus chamaemorus], sometimes with an abundance of [Carex nigra] and [Eriophorum angustifolium]. The species cortŠge may include [Andromeda polifolia], [Empetrum nigrum], [Potentilla palustris], [Vaccinium microcarpum], [Agrostis canina], [Calamagrostis stricta], [Carex bigelowii], [Carex rariflora], [Carex rostrata], [Festuca rubra] [s.l.], and, in continental communities, [Cornus suecica], [Vaccinium vitis-ideae], [Eriophorum vaginatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Purple moorgrass bogs
description: Drying, mowed or burned bogs invaded by [Molinia caerulea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Blanket bogs
description: Communities similar to raised bogs, on flat or gently sloping ground with poor surface drainage, in oceanic climates with heavy rainfall. In the strictest sense, blanket bogs are a habitat endemic to northwestern Europe, characteristic of the western and northern British Isles, the Faeroe Islands and the western seaboard of Scandinavia. Extensive bogs developed in similar conditions of mild oceanic climate and high precipitations in Pacific Eurasia share several characteristics with the northwestern European blanket bogs and may be included in this unit. In spite of some lateral water flow, blanket bogs are mostly ombrotrophic. They often cover extensive areas with local topographic features supporting distinct communities. Sphagna ([Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum tenellum], [Sphagnum compactum], [Sphagnum magellanicum], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum fuscum]) play an important role in all of them, accompanied by [Narthecium ossifragum], [Molinia caerulea], [Scirpus cespitosus], [Schoenus nigricans], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Calluna vulgaris]. Geographically segregated types, high and low altitude forms and numerous variants can be distinguished. Intact examples of blanket bogs are relatively uncommon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bogs
description: Hyper-Atlantic blanket bogs of the western coastlands of Ireland, western Scotland and its islands, Cumberland, northern Wales and Devon, developed under very high rainfall climates. The main vascular plants are [Molinia caerulea], [Eriophorum angustifolium], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Scirpus cespitosus], [Schoenus nigricans], [Rhynchospora alba], [Narthecium ossifragum], [Carex panicea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica tetralix], [Myrica gale], [Pedicularis sylvatica], [Potentilla erecta], [Polygala serpyllifolia], [Pinguicula lusitanica], [Drosera rotundifolia]. The colourful mucinal layer comprises the black and crimson liverwort [Pleurozia purpurea], the black and gold moss [Campylopus atrovirens], the wooly fringe moss [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum]; it is often dominated by sphagna ([Sphagnum auriculatum], [Sphagnum magellanicum], [Sphagnum compactum], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum nemoreum], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum tenellum], [Sphagnum subnitens]), or, particularly in parts of western Ireland, mucilaginous algal deposits ([Zygogonium]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bog plateaux
description: Deep-peat lawn and hummock communities of blanket bog expanses of western Ireland, western Scotland and its islands, the Lake District, northern Wales and Devon, composed of graminoids, ericoid shrubs and sphagna, forming extensive, relatively featureless, fairly flat or gently undulating, tracts with a fine-grained alternation of dominance among species or, on bogs with stronger surface undulations, better defined hummocks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Irish black bog-rush blanket bogs
description: Deep-peat lawn and hummock communities of blanket bog expanses of western Ireland, particularly the Mayo, Galway and Donegal peninsulas, composed of [Erica tetralix], [Calluna vulgaris], [Myrica gale], [Molinia caerulea], [Narthecium ossifragum], [Rhynchospora alba], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Scirpus cespitosus], [Schoenus nigricans], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum magellanicum], with [Drosera rotundifolia], [Drosera anglica], [Menyanthes trifoliata], [Pinguicula lusitanica], [Pedicularis sylvatica], [Pleurozia purpurea] and [Zygogonium] algae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western British [Scirpus]-[Eriophorum] blanket mires
description: Deep-peat lawn and hummock communities of blanket bog expanses of western Britain composed of [Scirpus cespitosus], [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Molinia caerulea], [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica tetralix], [Myrica gale], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum tenellum], [Sphagnum subnitens], with [Drosera rotundifolia], [Juncus squarrosus], [Pleurozia purpurea], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Rhytidiadelphus loreus], [Cladonia spp.]
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bog sphagnum carpets
description: Waterlogged pool edges and bog surfaces of Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bogs marked by a scarcity of graminoids and shrubs, and a resulting physiognomic prominence of the sphagna, [Sphagnum magellanicum] or [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum cuspidatum], [Sphagnum auriculatum], [Sphagnum palustre], at times, particularly in Ireland, with [Zygogonium] algae deposits, often with [Drosera anglica], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Menyanthes trifoliata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bog deergrass heaths
description: [Scirpus cespitosus]-[Erica tetralix] wet heaths of Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bog slopes or tops of slopes, developed on shallower peats, in better drained situations, in more mineralotrophic conditions than the communities of unit 52.11. Sphagna are less prominent in the ground layer with, in particular, a lesser prominence of [Sphagnum papillosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Irish oblong-leaved sundew flush communities
description: Communities of western Irish lowland blanket bogs occupying slope areas submitted to surface water movement and shallow hollows, rich in [Drosera intermedia], with [Riccardia pinguis], [Rhynchospora fusca] or [Carex limosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Irish bulbous-rush flush communities
description: Communities of western Irish lowland blanket bogs occupying shallow drainage channels and shallow pools, rich in [Juncus bulbosus], [Eleocharis multicaulis] and [Carex panicea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bog hollows and pools
description: Wet depressions and seeps of Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bogs colonized by hollow communities similar to those of raised bog hollows of unit 51.121 or by other communities of the [Scheuchzerietalia palustris] (units 54.5, 54.6), communities of the [Caricetalia fuscae] (unit 54.4), of the [Utricularietalia intermedio-minoris] (unit 22.45), of the [Littorelletalia] (unit 22.31) or of the [Potamogetonetalia] (unit 22.43).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bog hollow communities
description: Wet depressions and seeps of Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bogs colonized by hollow communities similar to those of raised bog hollows of unit 51.121, in particular, of unit 51.1213, dominated by [Sphagnum auriculatum], with [Sphagnum subsecundum] ssp. [inundatum] and the bright orange-yellow [Sphagnum pulchrum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bog fen communities
description: Wet depressions and seeps of Hiberno-Britannic lowland blanket bogs colonized by communities of the [Scheuchzerietalia palustris] (units 54.5, 54.6), communities of the [Caricetalia fuscae] (unit 54.4), of the [Utricularietalia intermedio-minoris] (unit 22.45), of the [Littorelletalia] (unit 22.31) or of the [Potamogetonetalia] (unit 22.43), which can be noted by use of appropriate codes. Among important elements are [Potamogeton polygonifolius], [Eriocaulon aquaticum], [Lobelia dortmanna], [Menyanthes trifoliata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bogs
description: Blanket bogs of high ground, hills and mountains in Scotland, Ireland, western England and Wales. Characteristic species are [Eriophorum vaginatum], [Calluna vulgaris], [Erica tetralix], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Narthecium ossifragum], [Scirpus cespitosus], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] and abundant sphagnum mosses. Some of their communities show affinities with the boreoalpine hummocks of unit 51.17.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic cottonsedge-ling blanket bogs
description: Lawn and hummock communities of upland blanket bog expanses of Britain and Ireland, mostly distributed in the Scottish Highlands, the Southern Uplands, the Pennines, the Lake District, Wales, in Orkney, in northern, western, southwestern and upland eastern Ireland, dominated by an admixture of [Eriophorum vaginatum] and ericoid shrubs, with a varying amount of sphagna and hypnoid mosses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic cottonsedge blanket bogs
description: Species-poor upland blanket bog lawn communities of the Pennines overwhelmingly dominated by an open or closed canopy of low [Eriophorum vaginatum] tussocks, with few ericoid shrubs and a sparse and patchy ground cover in which sphagna are scarce; the most common vascular associates are usually [Eriophorum angustifolium] and [Deschampsia flexuosa]. They are characteristic of heavily grazed and burned expanses of blanket bog.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bog sphagnum mats
description: [Sphagnum papillosum], [Sphagnum magellanicum], [Sphagnum rubellum], [Sphagnum imbricatum], [Sphagnum fuscum] carpets and hummocks of the cottonsedge-ling blanket bogs, most characteristic of the moorlands of the Scottish Borders.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic dwarf shrub-cottonsedge upland bogs
description: Dwarf shrub-rich facies of Hiberno-Britannic upland cottongrass-ling blanket bogs, most characteristic of the eastern Scottish Highlands, with an abundance of [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Empetrum nigrum], [Betula nana], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Arctostaphylos alpinus] and [Sphagnum fuscum], with particularly close affinities to the boreoalpine hummocks of unit 51.17.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic wooly fringe moss upland bog hummocks
description: Lawn and hummock communities of Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bogs dominated by [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], mostly characteristic of eroded or dried surfaces.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bog wet heaths
description: [Erica tetralix] or, at lower altitudes, [Scirpus cespitosus]-[Erica tetralix] wet heaths of Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bog slopes or tops of slopes, developed on shallower peats, in better drained situations, in more mineralotrophic conditions than the communities of unit 52.21. [Eriophorum vaginatum] is less prominent in the sward, and sphagna sparser in the ground cover, while shrubs, [Juncus squarrosus] and [Nardus stricta] are more vigorous or commoner.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bog hollows and pools
description: Wet depressions and seeps of Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bogs colonized by hollow communities similar to those of raised bog hollows of unit 51.121 or by other communities of the [Scheuchzerietalia palustris] (units 54.5, 54.6), communities of the [Caricetalia fuscae] (unit 54.4), of the [Utricularietalia intermedio-minoris] (unit 22.45), of the [Littorelletalia] (unit 22.31) or of the [Potamogetonetalia] (unit 22.43). Pools and hollows are less prominent in these blanket bogs than in the western blanket bogs of unit 52.1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bog hollow communities
description: Wet depressions and seeps of Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bogs colonized by hollow communities similar to those of raised bog hollows of unit 51.121, in particular, of unit 51.1211, dominated by [Sphagnum cuspidatum] with [Sphagnum recurvum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bog fen communities
description: Wet depressions and seeps of Hiberno-Britannic upland blanket bogs colonized by communities of the [Scheuchzerietalia palustris] (units 54.5, 54.6), communities of the [Caricetalia fuscae] (unit 54.4), of the [Utricularietalia intermedio-minoris] (unit 22.45), of the [Littorelletalia] (unit 22.31) or of the [Potamogetonetalia] (unit 22.43), which can be noted by use of appropriate codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern boreo-Atlantic blanket bogs
description: Blanket bogs of oceanic southern boreal affinities distributed in maritime western Norway from Rogaland, in the south, north to the Arctic Circle, and in the Faeroe Islands, characterized by the dominance of [Calluna]-[Rhacomitrium] and [Calluna]-[Sphagnum rubellum] communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern boreo-Atlantic cottonsedge-ling bogs
description: Main bog-surface and hummock communities of southern boreal blanket bogs dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], [Eriophorum vaginatum] and [Sphagnum rubellum], with [Erica tetralix], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Andromeda polifolia], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Sphagnum magellanicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern boreo-Atlantic ling-wooly fringe moss bogs
description: Bog-surface and hummock communities characteristic of the southernmost southern boreal blanket bogs, in nemoral extreme southern Norway, oceanic southern boreal extreme western Norway, north to southern Tr”ndelag, and in the Faeroe Islands, dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], [Empetrum nigrum], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], with [Cornus suecica], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Dicranum elongatum], [Grimmia hypnoides], [Cladonia sylvatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern boreo-Atlantic blanket bog hollow communities
description: Hollow vegetation of southern boreal blanket bogs formed by [Sphagnum cuspidatum] and [Sphagnum tenellum], with [Rhynchospora alba], [Scheuchzeria palustris], [Drosera anglica], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Andromeda polifolia], [Carex limosa], [Eriophorum vaginatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern boreo-Atlantic blanket bogs
description: Blanket bogs of oceanic northern boreal affinities distributed in maritime western Norway, from southern Nordland to central Troms, characterized by the dominance of [Calluna]-[Empetrum]-[Sphagnum fuscum] communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ling-crowberry-[Sphagnum fuscum] blanket bogs
description: Bog-surface and hummock communities of the northern boreal blanket bogs dominated by [Calluna vulgaris], [Empetrum spp.], [Vaccinium uliginosum] and [Sphagnum fuscum] with [Andromeda polifolia], [Vaccinium microcarpum], [Drosera rotundifolia], [Betula nana], [Cladonia rangiferina], [Cladonia sylvatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern boreo-Atlantic blanket bog hollow communities
description: Hollow vegetation of northern boreal blanket bogs formed by [Sphagnum majus], with [Rhynchospora alba], [Scheuchzeria palustris], [Vaccinium oxycoccos], [Andromeda polifolia], [Carex limosa], [Scirpus cespitosus], [Drepanocladus fluitans].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific blanket bogs
description: Blanket bogs of Kamchatka and Sakhalin, with [Sphagnum fuscum], [Sphagnum lindbergii], [Sphagnum papillosum], [Empetrum nigrum], [Carex lyngbyei], [Carex middendorffii], [Cladonia spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water-fringe vegetation
description: Communities of the margins and of the floating rafts of lakes, rivers and brooks, or of eutrophic marshes and swamps, based on sociations of large graminoid, juncoid or broad-leaved plants, for the most part helophytes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Reed beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, inland seas and sea inlets, rivers and brooks, eutrophic marshes and swamps, based on sociations of tall helophyte Poaceae, [Scirpus], [Typha], horsetails or forbs, usually species-poor and often dominated by one species, growing in stagnant or slowly flowing water of fluctuating depths, and sometimes on waterlogged ground. They are classified according to dominant species which give them a distinctive appearance.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Common reed beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, inland seas and sea inlets, rivers and brooks, eutrophic marshes and swamps dominated by [Phragmites australis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Flooded [Phragmites] beds
description: [Phragmites australis] beds of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, inland seas and sea inlets, rivers and brooks inundated permanently or for prolonged annual periods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Freshwater [Phragmites] beds
description: [Phragmites australis] beds of the Palaearctic region permanently or usually inundated by fresh water lakes, ponds and watercourses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saline water [Phragmites] beds
description: [Phragmites australis] beds of the Palaearctic region beds permanently, usually or frequently inundated by the sea or by saline coastal lagoons, by athalassal saline lakes, by saline estuaries or saline rivers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dry [Phragmites] beds
description: [Phragmites australis] beds of the Palaearctic region dry for at least a large part of the year, often invaded by other species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dry freshwater [Phragmites] beds
description: Noninundated [Phragmites australis] beds of the Palaearctic region occupying mires, the landfilling zone of waterbodies, the edges of watercourses and other soils permeated by fresh water.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dry halophile [Phragmites] beds
description: Noninundated [Phragmites australis] beds of the Palaearctic region forming on the shores of saltwater bodies or on other saline soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Giant [Phragmites] beds
description: Formations of the very tall [Phragmites "maximus"], occurring locally in the Mediterranean basin, in particular on islets of lagoons of the east coast of Spain, where they harbour the very local, spectacular [Kosteletzkya pentacarpos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tidal reed beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic tidal rivers or sea inlets dominated by [Phragmites australis], in particular luxuriant [Caltha palustris] reedbeds of North Sea rivers, with [Ranunculus ficaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Common clubrush beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by [Scirpus lacustris], intolerant of drying, tolerant of water circulation, and thus forming the outer belts of reedbeds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Reedmace beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by [Typha latifolia], [Typha angustifolia], [Typha domingensis], [Typha laxmannii], [Typha elephantina] formations, usually extremely species-poor and sometimes almost pure, tolerant of extended periods of dryness, varying conditions of salinity, and of pollution.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Great reedmace beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by [Typha latifolia], of widespread occurrence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesser reedmace beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by [Typha angustifolia], like unit 53.131, of wide distribution.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Laxmann's reedmace beds
description: Reedmace beds formed by the small [Typha laxmannii] of southeastern Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern reedmace beds
description: [Typha domingensis] ([Typha angustifolia] ssp. [australis], [Typha australis], [Typha angustata])-dominated formations of fresh water and saline habitats, mostly characteristic of North Africa and southern Eurasia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Elephantine reedmace beds
description: Thickets of the tropical [Typha elephantina] occupying humid sands of torrent beds of the Saharo-tropical mountains of the central Sahara, up to about 1650 metres, the swamplands and adjacent sandy terraces bordering the lakes of Wadi El-Natrun in Egypt, and rare localities in the Tell.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Medium-tall waterside communities
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by shorter, mostly nongraminoid helophytes emerging from mesotrophic or eutrophic, stagnant or slow-moving, shallow water, and constituting fringes or patches within or alongside reedbeds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arrowhead communities
description: Formations of [Sagittaria sagittifolia] and [Sparganium emersum] of slowly flowing, and sometimes standing, meso-eutrophic waters of western Eurasia; formations of [Sagittaria sagittifolia], [Sagittaria natans] and [Caltha membranacea] of similar eastern Asian waterbodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Neglected bur-reed communities
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by [Sparganium neglectum], characteristic of standing or slowly flowing waters on mineral-rich, lime-poor muddy substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Erect bur-reed communities
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by or rich in [Sparganium erectum], characteristic of riparian reedbeds along standing waters on lime-rich, mineral-rich muddy substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sweet flag communities
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by the long-introduced thermophile [Acorus calamus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Flowering rush communities
description: Usually open communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by, or rich in, [Butomus umbellatus], characteristic of strongly fluctuating still or slow-flowing base- and mineral-rich waters.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water dropwort-great yellowcress communities
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks, often situated at the edges of reedbeds, rich in [Oenanthe aquatica] or [Rorippa amphibia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water horsetail beds
description: Low, often extensive, homogeneous, usually inundated communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by [Equisetum fluviatile].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water parsnip communities
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks dominated by or rich in the tall umbellifer [Sium latifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marestail beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks, usually of clear, cold to temperate nutrient-rich water, dominated by [Hippuris vulgaris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Common spikerush beds
description: Low, often extensive and very homogeneous formations of Palaearctic lakeshores, pools and ditches with strongly fluctuating water regime, dominated by [Eleocharis palustris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iris beds
description: Homogeneous [Iris pseudacorus] formations of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers and brooks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water-fringe grass beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, inland seas and sea inlets, rivers and brooks, eutrophic marshes, swamps and ditches dominated by medium or medium-tall helophyte Poaceae of genera [Glyceria], [Leersia], [Socolochloa] or [Calamagrostis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sweetgrass beds
description: Communities of eutrophic Palaearctic waters, often with variable level, dominated by fairly tall, robust grasses of genus [Glyceria] (section [Hydropoa]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Reed sweetgrass beds
description: Communities of eutrophic Palaearctic waters dominated by [Glyceria maxima], rather low, usually constituting strips in or along ditches or small streams, often in grasslands, requiring fairly constant inundation by eutrophic water and with a fairly rich associated flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Three-flowered sweetgrass beds
description: [Glyceria triflora] formations of periodically dry sites of Siberia and extreme northeastern Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eurasian [Leersia] beds
description: Communities of the terrestrialization zone of Palaearctic lakes, ponds, rivers, brooks and canals, mostly with turbid water, dominated by [Leersia oryzoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eurasian [Scolochloa] beds
description: Communities of the margins of muddy shores of lakes, slow-flowing rivers and alases of the Palaearctic domaine, from eastern Fennoscandia, eastern Germany, Lithuania and the Ukraine eastwards, including central Yakutia, dominated by [Scolochloa festucacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water-fringe [Calamagrostis] beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic mesotrophic acidicline lakes, rivers and swamps dominated by [Calamagrostis canescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Reed canary-grass beds
description: Communities of the margins of Palaearctic lakes, rivers, brooks and swamps dominated by [Phalaris arundinacea], pure or mixed with [Phragmites australis], very tolerant of drying, pollution and perturbance, susceptible of forming the landward belt of reedbeds and often characteristic of degraded systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Halophile clubrush beds
description: Formations of clubrushes ([Scirpus spp.]), often accompanied by rushes ([Juncus spp.]), fringing, to a depth of 1.5 metres, brackish, saline, or sometimes fresh, waters of coastal saltmarshes, coastal lagoons, athalassic saline waterbodies and tidal rivers of the Palaearctic region. [Scirpus tabernaemontani] ([Schoenoplectum tabernaemontani]), [Scirpus maritimus] ([Bolboschoenus maritimus]), [Scirpus triqueter], [Scirpus litoralis], [Scirpus pungens], with, in particular, [Juncus gerardi] and [Juncus maritimus], compose various communities in the western Palaearctic; [Scirpus iseensis] is one of the components of eastern Palaearctic formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Manchurian water rice beds
description: Formations of eastern Asia, north to southern Russian Amurland, dominated by [Zizania latifolia]; they occur, naturalized, in the Volga delta.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-tropical reed formations
description: Reedbed-like rooted or floating mats, beds, rafts and islands formed by tropical or subtropical herbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Large sedge communities
description: Formations of large Cyperaceae of genera [Carex] or [Cyperus] occupying the edge or the entirety of humid depressions, oligotrophic mires and rich fens of the Palaearctic region, on ground that can be dry for part of the year. They occur, in particular, on the landward side of reedbeds in waterside successions and as colonists of humid depressions on mineral soils, or of acid and alkaline fens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Large [Carex] beds
description: Palaearctic communities of social sedges of genus [Carex], usually dominated by one species that can be either tussock-forming or bed-forming. They are arranged according to dominant species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brown sedge beds
description: Formations of [Carex disticha] of Palaearctic humid alluvial meadows on clay and of temporarily drying peatbogs; often in contact with grasslands of the [Calthion] and sometimes placed in that alliance; they tolerate fairly long dessication and have a relatively rich accompanying flora.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Slender tufted sedge beds and related communities
description: Palaearctic formations of the terrestrialisation zone of marshes, ponds and lakes on mostly mineral, neutral, basic or weakly acid substrates, dominated by large bed-forming, rhizomatous, sedges, in particular, [Carex acuta], [Carex acutiformis] or their relatives.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Slender tufted sedge beds
description: Palaearctic formations of [Carex acuta] of wet, alkaline or slightly acid depressions with mineral soil; [Carex acuta] does not tolerate prolonged dessication. The community is distributed, in particular, in northern France, the Low Countries, Central Europe south to the Sava and Drava valleys of Croatia, the northern Morava valley of Serbia and Romania, north to Poland, the Kaliningrad District, Lithuania and Latvia, in southern Scandinavia, in the Dnieper basin of northern Ukraine and southern Belarus, in the lower Volga Valley.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesser pond sedge beds
description: Palaearctic communities dominated by [Carex acutiformis], more tolerant of dessication than [Carex acuta], forming beds on mesotrophic, base-rich, neutral to slightly acid, peaty or mineral soils. Large beds may form in fens, often with [Carex paniculata]; otherwise, they are widespread along watercourses on the landward side of [Carex acuta] or [Carex vesicaria] beds, in alluvial plains, ditches and depressions of humid meadow systems; they may occupy stations that almost totally escape periodical inundation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inn sedge beds
description: Formations of [Carex oenensis], restricted to oligotrophic, base-rich streamsides of the pre-Alpine Bavarian plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Banat sedge beds
description: [Carex buekii] formations of mesotrophic sandy or clayey soils in Franconia, eastern Bavaria, Saxony, northern Italy, eastern central Europe, eastern Europe and western Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Water sedge beds
description: Mesotrophic [Carex aquatilis] formations of northern Siberia and northern Europe, south to Lower Saxony, Friesland, Wales, Lakeland, Scotland, Ireland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brotero sedge beds
description: [Carex acuta] ssp. [broteriana] formations of Iberia, lining river courses on the inner side of alder galleries, or replacing them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Carex melanostachya] beds
description: Palaearctic swamp communities dominated by [Carex melanostachya] ([Carex nutans]), characteristic of slightly saline soils of the Pannonic region, habitat of the uncommon [Carex curvata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Carex hispida] beds
description: Formations of the terrestrialisation zone of Mediterranean marshes, ponds, lakes, ditches dominated by [Carex hispida].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greater pond sedge beds
description: Formations of [Carex riparia], mostly characteristic of larger valleys and southern regions of the Palaearctic domaine, intolerant of dessication. They form on mineral or thinly peaty substrates, often in areas almost permanently inundated by somewhat lime-rich water.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bottle, bladder and slender sedge beds
description: Palaearctic terrestrialization communities dominated by [Carex vesicaria], [Carex rostrata] or [Carex lasiocarpa], characteristic of moderately to strongly acid, fairly constantly inundated soils and poor fens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bottle sedge beds
description: Terrestrialization sedge beds of the Palaearctic domaine, characteristic, in particular, of continental regions, dominated by [Carex rostrata], forming dense, vigorous, fertile beds on usually very wet, meso-oligotrophic substrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bladder sedge beds
description: Palaearctic formations of [Carex vesicaria], usually characteristic of less oligotrophic situations than the previous ones. [Carex vesicaria], however, often accompanies [Carex rostrata], forming then the outer, drier edge of the sedge bed.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Slender sedge beds
description: Palaearctic terrestrialization communities dominated by [Carex lasiocarpa], characteristic of dystrophic to mesotrophic waters with low to moderate level fluctuations, on weakly to moderately acid peaty substrates or gyttyas, most widespread in northern and continental Eurasia, with representatives in Atantic Europe, in particular in Ireland, and, as rare glacial relicts, in Alpine lands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tufted sedge and sward sedge tussocks
description: Palaearctic formations dominated by the large, tussock-forming [Carex elata] or its relatives.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tufted sedge tussocks
description: Formations of large, often crowded tussocks of [Carex elata], of alkaline or eutrophic, peaty or organic soils of the Palaearctic domaine. [Carex elata] is, in particular, one of the constituents of species-rich sedge communities in alkaline fens. It is also typical of the flood plain of large, slow-flowing rivers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sward sedge tussocks
description: Formations of [Carex cespitosa], characteristic of nutrient- and base-rich, neutral to acid peaty soils of Siberia, Central Asia, northern and central Europe, west to the Netherlands, Bohemia, Wrttemberg and northern Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greater tussock sedge tussocks
description: Formations of large, usually well-spaced tussocks of [Carex paniculata], of alkaline to acid, usually mesotrophic, often somewhat shady, habitually peaty stations of the Palaearctic domaine, including marshy woods. [Carex paniculata] is also a constituent of species-rich alkaline fen sedge communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Smaller tussock sedge tussocks
description: Terrestrialization formations of Palaearctic lakes, ponds and swamps dominated by [Carex appropinquata] ([Carex paradoxa]) or [Carex diandra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fibrous tussock sedge tussocks
description: Terrestrialization formations of [Carex appropinquata] ([Carex paradoxa]), alone or mixed with [Carex paniculata], essentially of mesotrophic, basicline peaty or mineral soils of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lesser tussock sedge tussocks
description: Terrestrialization formations of Palaearctic lakes, ponds and swamps dominated by [Carex diandra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyperus sedge tussocks
description: Palaearctic sedge beds dominated by [Carex pseudocyperus], mostly characteristic of slightly acid peaty soils, in very wet situations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fox sedge tussocks
description: Palaearctic formations dominated by [Carex vulpina] or [Carex otrubae], of eutrophic humus-poor clay soils, inundated for part of the year.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: True fox sedge tussocks
description: Palaearctic formations of the very large [Carex vulpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: False fox sedge tussocks
description: Palaearctic formations of the often less robust [Carex otrubae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Club sedge beds
description: Beds of [Carex buxbaumii] of wet grasslands, lake shore swamps and fens, on temporarily inundated relatively nutrient-rich, somewhat acid peaty sandy or clayey soils of eastern France, southern and eastern Germany, Poland, Lithuania, the southern Alps and the central Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic sedge beds
description: Sedge beds of Iceland dominated by [Carex lyngbyei], forming, thanks to strong runners, large stands on lakesides, poolsides, open mires and in ditches.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian sedge beds
description: [Carex vesicata] beds of Yakutia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall galingale beds
description: Palaearctic formations dominated by large perennial Cyperaceae of genus [Cyperus], other than [Cyperus papyrus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Common galingale beds
description: [Cyperus longus] formations of Italy, southeastern Europe, North Africa and Asia Minor.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Slender galingale beds
description: Formations dominated by, or rich in, [Cyperus laevigatus], characteristic, in particular, of saline depressions in the Canary Islands, of thermal waterbodies on Pantelleria, and of damp, often saline, sites, such as lake, marsh and swamp margins, of North Africa. These formations are apparently extinct in the Maltese Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtropical galingale beds
description: Waterfringe formations of the southern Palaearctic deserts and their margins dominated by [Cyperus rotundus], [Cyperus capitatus] ([Cyperus kalli]) or other large subtropical perennial Cyperaceae of genus [Cyperus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Papyrus swamps
description: Formations of [Cyperus papyrus] of the Near East, Egypt and Sicily.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyane papyrus swamp
description: [Cyperus papyrus] ssp. [siculus] gallery of the Cyane river in southeastern Sicily. Taxonomic and historical evidence strongly suggest that this unique station is of natural origin, an extraordinary relict of an extensive Tertiary distribution.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Egyptian papyrus swamps
description: The Wadi El-Natrun relict stand of [Cyperus papyrus], apparently the only one remaining in Egypt, where the species was thought to have become extinct in the first half of the 19th century, before its rediscovery in 1968.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Jordan River papyrus swamps
description: [Cyperus papyrus] thickets of the Hula swamps in the Jordan River valley.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fen-sedge beds
description: [Cladium mariscus]-dominated formations of Europe north to 62ø N and the Mediterranean basin, mostly limited in the northern part of their range, where they have a distincty relict distribution, to alkaline and sometimes acid fens and to the land-building zone of calcareous lakes, somewhat more widespread in the Mediterranean region as a waterside vegetation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fen [Cladium] beds
description: Species-rich, fairly open [Cladium mariscus] beds of alkaline and sometimes acid Palaearctic fens, accompanied by cortŠges of the [Caricion davallianae] or of the [Caricion lasiocarpae]. These formations are in grave decline throughout their range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Valencia [Cladium] islands
description: Endangered endemic association of peaty islets of the Albufera de Valencia, with [Kosteletzkya pentacarpos].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Riparian [Cladium] beds
description: Species-poor [Cladium mariscus] formations of Palaearctic riversides or lakesides, with a [Phragmition] cortŠge, mostly characteristic of Mediterranean regions, including North Africa, where they are, however, uncommon.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small reed beds of fast-flowing waters
description: Formations of small helophytes, [Glyceria fluitans], [Glyceria plicata], [Glyceria nemoralis], [Glyceria declinata], [Leersia oryzoides], [Catabrosa aquatica], [Sparganium neglectum], [Sparganium microcarpum], [Nasturtium officinale], [Nasturtium microphyllum], [Veronica beccabunga], [Veronica anagallis-aquatica], [Apium nodiflorum], [Sium erectum] occupying, from the Euro-Siberian region, through the Mediterranean basin, to desert oases, the banks of Palaearctic small rivers, brooks, brooklets or springs on alluvial or peaty soils.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall rush swamps
description: Palaearctic formations of large [Juncus spp.] invading heavily grazed and trampled marshes or fens or (with [Juncus effusus]) eutrophized poor fens and bogs as in the vicinity of bird colonies. Similar formations developing within the environment of wet meadows have been listed under unit 37.241.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Riparian cane formations
description: Mediterranean, desert, sub-desert, sub-tropical and tropical Palaearctic beds of tall canes lining permanent or temporary water courses and water bodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Pontic Ravenna cane communities
description: Mediterranean and, locally, southern and southwestern Pontic, tall cane beds formed by [Imperata cylindrica], [Saccharum ravennae] ([Erianthus ravennae]), [Saccharum strictum], [Saccharum spontaneum] ([Saccharum aegyptiacum]), [Arundo plinii], [Hemarthria altissima], mostly lining temporary water courses, but also developing in damp depressions, in particular dune slacks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Provence cane beds
description: Very tall thickets of [Arundo donax] lining water courses of the Middle East and Central Asia; similar formations of the Mediterranean basin, where the species is an old introduction, are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Desert cane beds
description: Desert and sub-desert Palaearctic beds of tall canes lining permanent or temporary water courses and water bodies, with [Erianthus purpurascens], [Saccharum spontaneum], [Imperata cylindrica], [Sorghum halepense], [Phragmites communis], [Calamagrostis spp.], [Elymus multicaulis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-tropical riverine cane beds
description: Sub-tropical and, locally, tropical Palaearctic beds of tall canes lining permanent or temporary water courses and water bodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fens, transition mires and spring mires
description: Small-sedge and related communities of fens, transition mires and quaking bogs; vegetation of springs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spring mires
description: Plant communities closely associated with springs and seepages and dependant on the peculiar microclimatic and hydrological situation created by them. They comprise specialized spring communities ([Montio-Cardaminetea]) as well as fen communities ([Caricetalia davallianae], unit 54.2, [Caricetalia fuscae], unit 54.4) or other communities ([Caricion bicoloris-atrofuscae], unit 54.3, [Festuco-Brometea], unit 34.3), that are interwoven with them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Soft water spring mires
description: Spring mires of acid or neutral, oligotrophic to eutrophic noncalcareous springs of the Palaearctic domaine. The specialized spring communities belong to the various associations of the [Montio-Cardaminetea]. The associated swamp communities belong to the [Caricetalia fuscae] and their presence can be indicated by use, simultaneously with one of the codes of unit 54.11, of a code of unit 54.4.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Soft water bryophyte springs
description: Spring communities of lime-poor waters of the Palaearctic domaine dominated by bryophytes, mostly characteristic of northern upland and high montane, alpine or subalpine levels, also locally of well-lit lowland sites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Montane soft water moss springs
description: Spring communities of montane, sometimes collinar, lowland or subalpine, well-lit, lime-poor waters of the Palaearctic domaine dominated by mosses, in particular, [Philonotis fontana], with [Epilobium nutans], [Epilobium obscurum], [Epilobium palustre], [Epilobium parviflorum], [Montia fontana], [Stellaria alsine], [Galium uliginosum], [Ranunculus repens], [Veronica beccabunga], [Equisetum fluviatile].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European soft water moss springs
description: Spring communities of montane, sometimes collinar, lowland or subalpine well-lit, lime-poor waters of the Alpine system, the western and central European Hercynian ranges and neighbouring regions dominated by mosses, in particular, by [Philonotis fontana], with [Bryum pseudotriquetum], [Calliergonella cuspitata], [Dicranella palustris], [Drepanocladus exannulatus], [Galium palustre], [Montia fontana], [Stellaria alsine].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Ranunculus omiophyllus]-[Montia fontana] springs
description: Spring mires of soft-water springs of warm, oceanic, western lowlands of Britain, with an often crowded cover of vascular plants and bryophytes, formed by [Ranunculus omiophyllus], [Montia fontana], [Ranunculus flammula], [Potamogeton polygonifolius], [Sphagnum auriculatum], [Philonotis fontana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Philonotis]-[Saxifraga stellaris] springs
description: Bryophyte dominated spring communities of alpine, subalpine, boreoalpine, arctoalpine, and sometimes upland, well-lit, lime-poor cold waters of the northern Palaearctic mountains and hills, of the Alpine system and of the great Hercynian ranges, mostly dominated by [Philonotis seriata], [Bryum schleicheri] or, in the north and west, [Philonotis fontana], with a vascular species cortŠge marked by arcto-alpine species, among which [Saxifraga stellaris] is usually prominent. Somewhat intermediate between the communities of unit 54.1111 and those of units 54.1113 and 54.1114, they extend to relatively low upland regions in northern Europe, in the British isles, and, as glacial relicts, in the Hercynian ranges and their periphery.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fennoscandian [Philonotis]-[Saxifraga stellaris] springs
description: Bryophyte dominated communities of cold, oxygen-rich, soft-water springs of the lower, middle and upper alpine zones of the boreoalpine and arctoalpine mountains of Fennoscandia, formed by [Philonotis fontana], with [Pohlia drummondii] and [Scapania uliginosa], accompanied by a sparse formation of vascular plants, most prominent of which are [Ranunculus nivalis] and [Saxifraga stellaris]; the species cortŠge may also include [Carex lachenalii], [Cerastium cerastoides], [Juncus biglumis], [Oxyria digyna], [Poa alpina] ssp. [vivipara], [Ranunculus pygmaeus], [Saxifraga aizoides], [Saxifraga cernua], [Veronica alpina] and, in Finnmark, [Ranunculus sulphureus]. The [Philonotis] spring communities of this unit border onto the [Saxifraga oppositifolia]-[Oxyria digyna] snow-patch communities of unit 36.12364. Some bryophyte spring communities of boreal Fennoscandia are dominated by [Drepanocladus exannulatus] and/or [Sphagnum lindbergii], with [Sphagnum riparium], [Sphagnum teres], a sparse representation of [Philonotis seriata], and an absence of [Cratoneuron spp.]. The sparse vascular plant component may include individuals of [Andromeda polifolia], [Equisetum hornemannii], [Equisetum sylvaticum], [Salix glauca]; there is an absence of wet-fen species typical of other spring communities. These communities may be transitional towards the communities of unit 54.1111.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic [Philonotis]-[Saxifraga stellaris] springs
description: Bryophyte dominated communities of cold, oxygen-rich, soft-water springs and small mountain becks of alpine and lowland Iceland and of the Faeroe Islands formed by [Philonotis fontana], with, in Iceland, [Pohlia wahlenbergii] ([Pohlia albicans]), accompanied by a sparse formation of vascular plants in which [Saxifraga stellaris], [Cerastium cerastoides], [Epilobium alsinifolium], [Montia fontana] or [Agrostis stolonifera] may be dominant, while, at high altitudes, [Ranunculus pygmaeus] and [Saxifraga rivularis] are characteristic. The vascular cortŠge also includes [Caltha palustris], [Cardamine pratensis], [Epilobium anagallidifolium], [Epilobium hornemanni], [Epilobium lactiflorum], [Epilobium palustre], [Equisetum arvense], [Equisetum palustre], [Juncus biglumis], [Deschampsia alpina], [Phleum alpinum]. The spring communities of this unit often border onto the black sedge alkaline fen communities of unit 54.263, many of whose components may encroach on the spring community.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Britannic [Philonoto-Saxifragetum stellaris] springs
description: Mountain and upland bryophyte dominated spring communities of well-lit, lime-poor cold waters of Britain, mostly formed by [Philonotis fontana], [Dicranella palustris], [Scapania undulata], with [Sphagnum auriculatum], [Scapania uliginosa], [Calliergon sarmentosum], [Drepanocladus exannulatus], [Drepanocladus fluitans], [Jungermannia exsertifolia], and a vascular species cortŠge often dominated by [Saxifraga stellaris], with [Deschampsia cespitosa], [Deschampsia alpina], [Stellaria alsine] and sometimes [Montia fontana], [Chrysosplenium oppositifolia], or the arctoalpines [Epilobium alsinifolium], [Epilobium anagalidifolium], [Cerastium cerastoides], [Phleum alpinum]. On Skye, flushes adjacent to [Philonotus]-[Saxifraga stellaris] springs have related communities formed by [Scapania undulata], [Calliergon sarmentosum], [Blindia acuta], with [Carex demissa] and [Koenigia islandica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010
