source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Fennoscandian palsa mounds
description: Palsa domes, ridges and plateaux of Fennoscandia, restricted to the low alpine, subalpine and sometimes upper conifer forest levels of the northern, arctoalpine, Fennoscandian mountains of Troms, Finnmark, Swedish and Finnish Lapland, with outposts on the Dovre plateau in the boreoalpine mountains of Norway, occupied by dwarf shrub communities composed mainly of [Betula nana], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Ledum palustre], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Vaccinium myrtillus], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], with [Vaccinium microcarpum], the mosses [Dicranum elongatum], [Polytrichum alpestre], [Pleurozium schreberi] and lichens, in particular of genus [Cladonia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic palsa mounds
description: Palsa mounds of the periglacial arctoalpine highlands of central Iceland, 0.5-2.5 metres high, 2-10 metres long, 1-7 metres broad, surrounded by a narrow lake-like lagg or a minerotrophic mud-bottom mire, generally of the Icelandic [Carex rostrata]-[Carex rariflora] type (unit 54.6242), occupied, on the tops, by shrub communities dominated by [Empetrum hermaphroditum], with [Dryas octopetala], [Salix herbacea], [Armeria maritima], [Silene acaulis], [Kobresia myosuroides], the mosses [Drepanocladus uncinatus], [Rhacomitrium canescens], the sphagnum [Sphagnum teres] and the lichen [Cetraria islandica], and on the lower slopes by communities dominated by [Salix glauca] ssp. [callicarpaea] ([Salix arctica]), [Salix herbacea] and [Calamagrostis neglecta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Kola palsa mounds
description: Palsa mounds, mostly 2-3 metres high and with no mineral core, restricted to the tundra and forested tundra zones of the northern Kola Peninsula, occupied by dwarf shrub communities composed mainly of [Betula nana], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Rubus chamaemorus], mosses, including [Dicranum congestum], [Dicranum elongatum], [Polytrichum alpestre], and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lower Pechora palsa mounds
description: Palsa mounds of the lower Pechora lowlands, located north of the Arctic circle, mostly in the forested tundra zone, partly in the shrub tundra zone, in a 100 km-wide belt from the east coast of the White Sea and the Kanin Peninsula to the mouth of the Usa River, forming ridges or domes, occupied by [Betula nana], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum] and [Rubus chamaemorus], with mosses, including [Dicranum spp.], [Polytrichum spp.], [Sphagnum fuscum], and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northeast European palsa mounds
description: Palsa mounds of the northern taiga, forested tundra and southern tundra zones of the Kara coastlands and hinterland in the middle and upper reaches of the Usa River, and of southern Nova‹a Zemlia, varying from 0.5 m to 6 m in height, with a mineral core, occupied by communities composed of [Betula nana], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Rubus chamaemorus], mosses including [Hylocomium splendens], [Pleurozium schreberi], [Polytrichum strictum], [Sphagnum fuscum], [Sphagnum nemoreum], and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Siberian palsa mounds
description: Palsa mounds of the northern taiga and southern forested tundra zones of the West Siberian plain, between the Ob and the Yenissei, 2-4 m high in the north, 6-8 m in the south, occupied by by dwarf shrub communities composed mainly of [Betula nana], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Rubus chamaemorus] and hypnoid and sphagnoid mosses, or with sparse [Betula pubescens], [Larix sibirica], [Pinus sibirica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle Siberian palsa mounds
description: High palsa mounds, characteristically 4-8 m in height, of the middle Siberian northern taiga and forested tundra zones of the Yenissei, lower Tunguska and stony Tunguska basins and uplands, south to the mouth of the Angara, occupied by dwarf shrub communities composed mainly of [Betula nana], [Chamaedaphne calyculata], [Ledum palustre], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Rubus chamaemorus], [Sphagnum fuscum], [Sphagnum capillifolium] and lichens, commonly with a participation of trees, such as [Betula pubescens], [Larix sibirica], [Pinus sylvestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Sphagnum fuscum] pounikko hummocks
description: High hummocks of [Sphagnum fuscum] of palsa mires of the western palsa mire region of the Palaearctic domaine, often congregating in broad fields, resulting, like the palsa mounds, from frost action, but with a core in which the frost is only seasonal though long-lasting.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Palsa mire flarks
description: Pools, hollows and laggs of palsa mires of the subarctic and northern boreal zone of the Palaearctic domaine, mostly inundated, minerotrophic or partly minerotrophic, acidocline to basicline. They are predominantly colonized by transition mire communities of unit 54.5 or mud-bottom communities of unit 54.62.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mud-bottom palsa flarks
description: Pools, hollows and laggs of palsa mires of the subarctic and northern boreal zone of the Palaearctic domaine colonized by mud-bottom communities of unit 54.62.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Transition mire palsa flarks
description: Pools, hollows and laggs of palsa mires of the subarctic and northern boreal zone of the Palaearctic domaine colonized by transition mire communities of unit 54.5. Characteristic species include [Eriophorum russeolum], [Eriophorum angustifolum], [Carex limosa], [Carex rotundata], [Carex rostrata], [Carex aquatilis], [Menyanthes trifoliata], [Potentilla palustris], [Sphagnum lindbergii], [Sphagnum majus], [Sphagnum fimbriatum], [Sphagnum girgensohnii], [Sphagnum riparium], [Sphagnum obtusum], [Sphagnum squarrosum], [Sphagnum flexuosum], [Drepanocladus vernicosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Polygon mires
description: Complex mires of the Arctic and subarctic zones of the Palaearctic domaine  patterned by a surface microrelief of large, 10 to 30 metres in diameter, low-centre or high-centre polygons formed by the juxtaposition of dry, 0.3 to 0.5 metres high, ridges covered by shrubs, hypnoid mosses and sphagna, and of wet hollows occupied by grasses, sedges, mosses and sphagna. They are distributed, mostly in the tundra and forested tundra zones, from Va‹gatch Island and the Yugorskiy peninsula to the Chukotka peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Polygon mire ridges
description: Ridges and flat tops of polygons of polygon mires of the Arctic and subarctic zones of the Palaearctic domaine, covered by shrubs, hypnoid mosses and sphagna.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic polygon mire ridges
description: Ridges and flat tops of polygons of polygon mires of the Arctic zone of the Palaearctic domaine occupied by mostly graminoid communities, formed of sedges, woodrushes and grasses, with willows, in particular, [Salix pulchra], [Salix reptans], mosses, notably [Aulacomnium palustre], [Aulacomnium turgidum], [Homalothecium nitens], and the sphagna [Sphagnum fimbriatum], [Sphagnum girgensohnii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern subarctic polygon mire ridges
description: Ridges and flat tops of polygons of polygon mires of the northern subarctic zone of the Palaearctic domaine formed by the dwarf willows [Salix pulchra] and [Salix reptans], by [Dryas punctata], by the sedge [Carex stans], by grasses, in particular, [Arctagrostis latifolia], by mosses, notably [Aulacomnium palustre], [Aulacomnium turgidum], [Homalothecium nitens], [Hylocomium splendens] and by [Sphagnum fimbriatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern subarctic polygon mire ridges
description: Ridges and flat tops of polygons of polygon mires of the southern subarctic zone of the Palaearctic domaine formed by the dwarf shrubs [Betula nana], [Ledum decumbens], [Vaccinium vitis-idaea], [Rubus chamaemorus], the mosses [Dicranum spp.], [Polytrichum strictum], and the sphagna [Sphagnum lenense], [Sphagnum nemoreum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Polygon mire hollows
description: Hollows and cracks of polygon mires of the Arctic and subarctic zones of the Palaearctic domaine, occupied by the grasses [Arctophila fulva], [Dupontia fischeri], the sedges [Carex stans], [Carex chordorrhiza], [Carex rariflora], [Carex rotundata], the hypnoid mosses [Drepanocladus spp.], [Mnium spp.] and the sphagna [Sphagnum balticum], [Sphagnum majus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian mountain mires
description: Mires of the arid Central Asian mountains, in particular, of the Tyan Shan and the Pamir, of the Tibetan plateau and of the Himalyan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental East Asian fens
description: Mires of the continental regions of Siberia and the Far East, in particular, of the Central Siberian plateau, of northeast Siberia, of south Yakutia, of the Angara, of northern Dahuria, of Mongolia, of the Amur lowlands and of continental China, together with those of the Altai and Sayn mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Maritime Far Eastern mires
description: Fens and string mires of Kamchatka, of the Sikhote-Alin region, of the Kuriles, of Sakhalin, of Japan and of maritime China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Palaearctic fens
description: Peat lands of North African lowlands and of other subtropical desert fringe areas, dominated by, or rich in, tropical sedge species such as [Rhynchospora glauca], [Fuirena pubescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland rocks, screes and sands
description: Terrestrial habitats and landscapes, free of direct marine influence, in which the mineral substrate, algae, lichens, bryophytes or colonies of animals dominate the physiognomy, and the herb, shrub or woodland communities that occupy enclaves or restricted surfaces within their expanse, in particular rock faces and rock pavements, and the lichen, bryophyte or rock-crack communities that colonize them, unstable screes and lichen, moss, herb, or shrub scree communities, permanent snow and ice, nondesert inland sand systems and all the communities they may support, caves, volcanic features and the specialized bacteria, animal, algae, lichen, moss or herb communities that they support.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Screes, gravel and boulder fields
description: Accumulations of boulders, stones, rock fragments, pebbles, gravels or finer material, of non-aeolian depositional origin, unvegetated, occupied by lichens or mosses, or colonized by sparse herb- or shrub-dominated communities. Included are screes and scree slopes produced by slope processes, moraines and drumlins originating from glacial deposition, sandar, eskers and kames resulting from fluvio-glacial deposition, block slopes, block streams and block fields constructed by periglacial depositional processes of downslope mass movement, ancient beach deposits constituted by former coastal constructional processes. Deposits originating from aeolian depositional processes (dunes) or from eruptive volcanic activity are not included, nor are those developed under desert climates; they are included in sections 64, 66 and 7, respectively. Accumulations of rock debris of erosional origin, resulting from frost weathering, heaving, thrusting or cracking, from aeolian denudation, erosion or abrasion processes, or from glacial erosion are also excluded and placed in unit 62. High mountain, boreal and mediterranean unstable screes are colonized by highly specialized plant communities. They or their constituting species may also inhabit moraines and other depositional debris accumulations in the same areas. A very few communities form in lowland areas elsewhere.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine and northern siliceous screes
description: Siliceous screes of high altitudes and cool sites within the Alpine system and the Pyrenees, of the Jura and Hercynian ranges and of middle European uplands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine siliceous screes
description: Siliceous, cool, damp screes of the subalpine and alpine levels of the Alpine system, the Pyrenees and Corsica with [Androsace alpina], [Achillea nana], [Oxyria digyna], [Geum reptans], [Saxifraga bryoides], [Ranunculus glacialis], [Linaria alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain sorrel screes
description: Stabilized silicate screes, poor in humus, of the Alpine system, the Pyrenees  and Corsica, characterized by [Oxyria digyna] and with [Cerastium uniflorum], [Doronicum clusii], [Doronicum grandiflorum], [Poa laxa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine mountain sorrel screes
description: Siliceous, cool, damp [Oxyria digyna] screes of the subalpine and alpine levels of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Alpine mountain sorrel screes
description: Siliceous, cool, damp screes restricted to the southwestern Alps, comprising the endemic species [Viola valderia] and [Thlaspi limosellifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean mountain sorrel screes
description: Stabilized silicate screes of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican mountain sorrel screes
description: Silicate [Oxyria digyna] screes of high mountains of Corsica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian mountain sorrel screes
description: Silicate [Oxyria digyna] screes of the Tatras and the high southeastern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tatra mountain sorrel screes
description: Silicate mountain sorrel screes of the Tatras, with [Oxyria digyna], [Arabis alpina], [Cochlearia tatrae], [Saxifraga carpathica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian mountain sorrel screes
description: Silicate mountain sorrel screes of the eastern Carpathian system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian saxifrage mountain sorrel screes
description: Silicate mountain sorrel screes of the Eastern Carpathians (Rodnei mountains) and the Southern Carpathians (Fagaras mountains), with [Oxyria digyna], [Arabis alpina], [Saxifraga carpathica], [Doronicum carpaticum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Carpathian meadowgrass mountain sorrel screes
description: Silicate mountain sorrel screes of high peaks and cirques of the western extremity of the Southern Carpathians, with [Oxyria digyna], [Poa cenisia] ssp. [contracta], [Saxifraga bryoides], [Saxifraga moschata], [Alchemilla fissa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide mountain sorrel screes
description: Silicate [Oxyria digyna] screes of the high Rila and Pirin mountains, with [Poa cenisia] ssp. [contracta], [Geum reptans], [Satureja alpina], [Pedicularis verticillata], [Armeria alpina], [Luzula spicata], [Bellardiochloa violacea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rock jasmine screes
description: Communities of silicate screes of the high alpine and nival levels of the central Alps dominated by [Androsace alpina] or [Androsace wulfeniana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brown woodrush screes
description: Humid, humus-rich silicate screes of the Alps, the Carpathians and the Rhodopides, on slopes long-covered with snow, carpeted by the alpine woodrush, [Luzula alpinopilosa], accompanied by a cortŠge that constitutes an ecological variant of the snow patch communities of unit 36.1114, characterized by a stronger representation of scree species of the [Androsasetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine woodrush screes
description: Humid, humus-rich silicate screes of the Alps, on slopes long-covered with snow, carpeted by the alpine woodrush, [Luzula alpinopilosa], accompanied by a cortŠge that constitutes an ecological variant of the snow patch communities of unit 36.1114, characterized by a stronger representation of scree species of the [Androsasetalia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian woodrush screes
description: [Luzula alpinopilosa] ssp. [obscura] ([Luzula alpinopilosa] = [Luzula spadicea]) of the siliceous high Tatras and of the alpine level of the high southeastern Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide woodrush screes
description: Screes colonized by communities dominated by [Luzula alpinopilosa] ([Luzula spadicea]) and [Festuca picta] ([Festuca picturata], [Festuca violacea] ssp. [picta]), characteristic of slopes with prolonged snow-cover of Vitosha, Rila and Pirin.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cold silicate block screes
description: Communities of ferns and brambles, including [Gymnocarpium dryopteris] ([Dryopteris disjuncta]), [Cryptogramma crispa], [Athyrium distentifolium], [Dryopteris dilatata], [Cystopteris fragilis], colonizing nonstablized, shady subalpine silicate screes of the Alpine system with a high proportion of large blocks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpatho-Balkanic saxifrage-speedwell-ragwort screes
description: Stony silicate screes of the alpine level of the eastern Carpathian system and the high mountains of the Balkan peninsula, with [Saxifraga carpathica], [Saxifraga pedemontana] ssp. [cymosa], [Saxifraga adscendens], [Veronica baumgartenii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide ragwort screes
description: Stony silicate screes of the alpine level of the Pirin with [Senecio doronicum] ([Senecio glaberrimus], [Senecio transylvanicus], [Senecio rochelianus]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian saxifrage-speedwell acidophilous screes
description: Stony silicate screes of the alpine level of the eastern Carpathian system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian saxifrage-speedwell screes
description: Stony silicate screes of the alpine level of the Eastern Carpathians (Rodnei Mountains), with [Saxifraga carpathica], [Saxifraga pedemontana] ssp. [cymosa], [Saxifraga bryoides], [Veronica baumgartenii], [Poa laxa], [Doronicum clusii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Carpathian saxifrage-speedwell screes
description: Stony silicate screes of the alpine level of the Retezat Mountains in the Southern Carpathians, with [Saxifraga bryoides], [Saxifraga pedemontana] ssp. [cymosa], [Veronica baumgartenii], [Silene acaulis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Painted fescue screes
description: [Festuca picta] screes of the siliceous high Tatras, the high mountains of the eastern Carpathian system, the Rhodopides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European upland siliceous screes
description: Siliceous screes of hills of western and central Europe, with [Epilobium collinum], [Galeopsis segetum], [Senecio viscosus], [Anarrhinum bellidifolium], [Cryptogramma crispa]. Upland siliceous screes, often resulting from quarry activity, and colonized by very impoverished forms of the Alpine communities, usually rich in mosses, lichens and sometimes ferns, notably [Cryptogramma crispa], are included.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine calcareous screes
description: Calcareous and calcschist screes of high altitudes and cool sites of the Alps and, locally, of peri-Alpine ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine calcschist screes
description: Calcareous slate slope communities of the Alps, with [Draba hoppeana], [Campanula cenisia], [Saxifraga biflora], [Herniaria alpina], [Trisetum spicatum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine pennycress screes
description: Unstable, hard limestone and dolomite coarse screes of the alpine and nival levels of the Alps, with [Thlaspi rotundifolium], [Papaver rhaeticum], [Papaver sendtneri], [Viola cenisia], [Linaria alpina], [Arabis alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fine calcareous screes
description: Fine-element calcareous screes of the alpine, subalpine and high montane levels of the Alps and neighbouring ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Butterbur screes
description: High montane and subalpine, relatively humid, fine limestone and marl screes, with [Petasites paradoxus], [Valeriana montana], [Gypsophila repens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain hawkbit screes
description: Damp, marlo-calcareous screes of the alpine level of the Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Alpine mountain hawkbit screes
description: Screes of the northwestern and central Alps, with [Leontodon montanus], [Ranunculus parnassifolius], [Saxifraga biflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Berardia] screes
description: Screes of the southwestern Alps, with the spectacular endemics [Berardia subacaulis] and [Brassica repanda] ssp. [repanda].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian calcareous screes
description: Calcareous screes of the Carpathians, represented by diverse communities of mostly very local occurrence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Carpathian calcareous screes
description: Calcareous screes of high altitudes of the Tatras, with [Cerastium latifolium], [Cerastium tatrae], [Arabis alpina], [Hutchinsia alpina], [Sedum atratum], [Cystopteris montana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tatra catchfly screes
description: Calcareous screes of the lower alpine level of the high Tatras, with [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [prostrata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tatra poppy screes
description: Calcareous screes of the upper alpine level of the high Tatras, with [Papaver burseri] ([Papaver alpinum] ssp. [tatricum]), [Saxifraga cernua] and [Cerastium latifolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian calcareous screes
description: Calcareous screes of the eastern Carpathian system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian xerophile poppy screes
description: Heliophilous communities colonizing fine semistabilized strongly insolated calcareous screes of the eastern Carpathian Bucegi, Fagaras and Retezat mountains, with [Papaver corona-sancti-stephani] and the endemic [Cerastium arvense] ssp. [lerchenfeldianum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian sciaphile poppy screes
description: Sciaphile, mesophile communities colonizing mobile or semistabilized screes derived from limestones or amphibolites, located in glacial cirques and rubble fans of the Rodnei and Bucegi mountains, with [Papaver corona-sancti-stephani], [Doronicum carpaticum], [Cardaminopsis neglecta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian calamint screes
description: Communities colonizing fine, semistabilized strongly insolated calcareous screes of the montane and subalpine level of the eastern Carpathian Rodnei, Bucegi, Tarcu and Godeano mountains, formed by or rich in [Acinos alpinus] ssp. [majoranifolius].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian dock screes
description: Communities colonizing moving, humid calcareous screes of torrent corridors in the subalpine level of the eastern Carpathian Rodnei, Fagaras, Retezat, Tarcu and Godeanu mountains, with [Rumex scutatus], [Doronicum columnae], [Thymus pulcherrimus], [Senecio rupestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Carpathian calcareous saxifrage screes
description: Communities colonizing semistabilized poorly insolated calcareous screes of the subalpine and alpine levels of the eastern Carpathian Rodnei, Fagaras, Tarcu and Godeanu mountains, formed by [Saxifraga moschata] with [Cerastium arvense] ssp. [calcicola], [Arabis alpina], [Saxifraga aizoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide calcareous screes
description: Screes of the Rhodope Mountains, with [Morina persica], [Sideritis scardica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Mediterranean and thermophilous screes
description: Screes of warm exposures in the Alps and the Pyrenees, of calcareous substrates in the Pyrenees, of Mediterranean mountains, hills and lowlands and, locally, of warm, sunny middle European upland or lowland sites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine thermophilous screes
description: Mostly coarse, unstablized, sunny calcareous screes of the montane and subalpine levels of the Alps and of the uplands and lowlands of western and central middle Europe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rough-grass screes
description: [Achnatherum calamagrostis] screes of warmer, lower parts of Alpine valleys and of the southwestern outer Alps.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-montane calcareous screes
description: Forb- or fern-dominated sunny calcareous screes of the montane or collinar levels of peri-Alpine ranges, particularly characteristic of the Jura, locally also of the middle European Hercynian ranges and of the southern Alpine periphery.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hemp-nettle screes
description: Species-poor pioneer communities of warm sunny calcareous screes of the Jura, the Alpine system, the Carpathians and the middle European Hercynian ranges, dominated by [Galeopsis angustifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: French sorrel screes
description: Species-poor open pioneering communities of dry calcareous screes of the low to moderate altitudes of the Alpine system, the Jura and the middle European Hercynian ranges, dominated by [Rumex scutatus], often with [Silene vulgaris] ssp. [glareosa], [Silene hayekiana], [Hieracium bifidum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Limestone fern screes
description: Open to closed fern swards of [Gymnocarpium robertianum] colonizing often slightly damp, more or less calcareous screes of the Jura and the middle European Hercynian ranges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Vincetoxicum screes
description: Species-rich thermophile pioneer scree communities of natural and anthropogenic station of the Alpine system, the Jura, the middle European Hercynian ranges, in particular, the Hautes Fagnes, and their vicinity, dominated by [Vincetoxicum hirundinacea], often with [Brachypodium pinnatum], [Anthericum ramosum], [Knautia dipsacifolia] ([Knautia sylvatica]), [Calamagrostis varia], [Campanula rapunculoides], [Galium album], [Origanum vulgare].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Paris Basin screes
description: Calcareous screes of the Paris basin and its periphery, with [Leontodon hyoseroides], [Sisymbrium supinum], [Linaria supina], [Galeopsis angustifolia] and many rare or endemic plants, including [Viola hispida] (endangered endemic), [Galium timeroyi] ssp. [fleurotii], [Iberis violetii], [Iberis durandii], [Biscutella neustriaca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cevenno-Provençal screes
description: Supramediterranean screes of Mediterranean southern France, common in the coastal ranges of the Marseille region (Allauch, Carpiagne, Puget, Marseilleveyre), rare on the Sainte-Baume, also represented in the C‚vennes, with [Arenaria provincialis] ([Gouffeia arenarioides]), [Ptychotis heterophylla], [Linaria supina], [Centranthus ruber], [Centranthus lecoqii], [Crucianella latifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Alpine thermo-siliceous screes
description: Siliceous screes of warm slopes of the subalpine level of the Alps and of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Pyrenees, usually composed largely of big stones or boulders, with [Senecio leucophyllus], [Taraxacum pyrenaicum], [Galeopsis pyrenaica], [Xatardia scabra], [Armeria alpina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyrenean calcareous screes
description: Calcareous screes of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fine Pyrenean calcareous screes
description: Fine limestone or calcschists on gentle slopes of the alpine level, with [Iberis spathulata], [Papaver suaveolens], [Galium cometerhizon], [Plantago monosperma], [Viola lapeyrousiana], [Campanula jaubertiana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coarse Pyrenean calcareous screes
description: Coarse, relatively dry screes on steep slopes, forming debris cones at the foot of cliffs, with [Crepis pygmaea], [Doronicum grandiflorum], [Campanula cochlearifolia], [Carduus carlinoides], [Galium cespitosum], [Festuca glacialis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High Pyrenean calcareous screes
description: Flatish screes of high altitudes of the central Pyrenees, with [Androsace ciliata], [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Hutchinsia alpina], [Galium pyrenaicum], [Minuartia cerastiifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Humid Pyrenean calcareous screes
description: Damp, cool screes with prolonged snow cover, with [Saxifraga praetermissa], [Saxifraga aizoides], [Epilobium anagallidifolium], [Veronica alpina], [Taraxacum alpinum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-alpine Pyrenean calcareous screes
description: Calcareous screes developed at the foot of the cliffs of the great calcareous ranges, with [Crepis pygmaea], [Carduus carlinoides] and the endemics [Borderea pyrenaica], [Cirsium glabrum], [Lithospermum gastonii], [Iberis bernardiana], [Armeria pubinervis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Cantabrian calcareous screes
description: Basiphile screes of the Cordillera Cantabrica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Cantabrian mobile calcareous screes
description: Altimontane, subalpine and alpine unstabilized calcareous screes of the Cordillera Cantabrica, made of stones of medium size, with [Linaria filicaulis], [Arabis cantabrica], [Iberis lereschiana], [Ranunculus parnassifolius] ssp. [favargeri], [Crepis pygmaea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fine oro-Cantabrian calcareous screes
description: Fine screes of the collinar and montane levels, with [Iberis aperta] and [Rumex scutatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chionophilous oro-Cantabrian calcareous screes
description: Somewhat stabilized coarse screes of the subalpine and alpine levels, subjected to prolonged snow cover, characterized by [Epilobium anagallidifolium], [Doronicum grandiflorum] ssp. [braunblanquetii] and [Campanula arvatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Seeping oro-Cantabrian calcareous screes
description: Fine screes of the subalpine and alpine levels, submitted to prolonged snow cover and waterlogging, with [Saxifraga praetermissa], [Arabis cantabrica] and [Ranunculus alpestris] ssp. [leroyi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Cantabrian calcareous lapiaz screes
description: Screes developed on the surface of frost-broken rocks in areas of short snow cover in the alpine and subalpine levels, with [Salix breviserrata] and [Galium pyrenaicum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Cantabrian siliceous screes
description: Siliceous screes of the Cordillera Cantabrica; floristically rich formations of the "dark" screes of the Cordillera are related to those of unit 61.351, though somewhat intermediate towards 61.38; other more species-poor ones, characterized by [Trisetum hispidum] and [Rumex suffruticosus], belong to the latter.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian fern screes
description: Fern-dominated chaotic boulder fields of the altimontane, subalpine and oromediterranean zones of siliceous and calcareous Iberian mountains, north to the Cordillera Cantabrica and the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iberian calciphile fern screes
description: Fern-dominated chaotic boulder fields of the altimontane, subalpine and oromediterranean zones of calcareous Iberian mountains, in particular, of the Cordillera Cantabrica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-Pyrenean acidophile fern screes
description: Fern-dominated chaotic boulder fields of the altimontane, subalpine and oromediterranean zones of siliceous Iberian mountains, in particular, of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpetano-Iberian siliceous screes
description: Screes of the Cordillera Central, the Iberian Range, the Leonese mountains, with [Linaria saxatilis], [Linaria alpina], [Digitalis purpurea] var. [carpetana], [Senecio pyrenaicus] ssp. [carpetanus], [Rumex suffruticosus], [Santolina oblongifolia], [Conopodium bunioides], [Reseda gredensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nevadan siliceous screes
description: Siliceous screes of the high levels of the Sierra Nevada, very rich in endemics.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nevadan foxglove screes
description: Screes at the subsummital levels of the Sierra Nevada, between 1900 and 2900 metres, with [Senecio tournefortii] var. [granatensis], [Digitalis purpurea] var. [nevadensis], [Cirsium gregarium], [Solidago virgaurea] ssp. [alpestris], [Holcus caespitosus], [Crepis oporinoides], [Eryngium glaciale], [Linaria aeruginea] var. [nevadensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nevadan violet screes
description: Screes of the summital region of the Sierra Nevada, at around 2800-3000 metres, with a very sparse community formed by [Viola crassiuscula], [Linaria glacialis], [Rhynchosinapis cheiranthos] ssp. [nevadensis], [Ranunculus glacialis], [Ranunculus parnassifolius], [Saxifraga oppositifolia], [Papaver suaveolens], [Holcus caespitosus], [Crepis oporinoides] and, in more stabilized areas, [Erigeron frigidus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Iberian calcareous screes
description: Screes of the calcareous Baetic mountains of southern and southeastern Iberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean screes
description: Screes of the Italian peninsula, of Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily and their associated islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean calcareous screes
description: Calcareous screes of the Italian peninsula, of Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily and their associated islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean siliceous screes
description: Siliceous screes of the Italian peninsula, of Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily and their associated islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican montane screes
description: Siliceous screes of the montane, oromediterranean and, locally, subalpine levels of the mountains of Corsica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean siliceous fern screes
description: Fern-rich siliceous screes of the mountains of the Italian peninsula and of large Mediterranean islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Mediterranean siliceous alpine adret screes
description: Thermophile siliceous screes of adret slopes of high mountains of the central Mediterranean, in particular, of Corsica.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean screes
description: Screes of high mountains of southern Albania, mainland Greece, the Peloponnese, the Aegean, Cyprus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iono-Aegean limestone screes
description: Limestone screes of high mountains of southern Albania, mainland Greece, the Peloponnese, the Aegean, with [Drypis spinosa], [Ranunculus brevifolius], [Senecio thapsoides], [Aethionema saxatile].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern and central Pindus limestone screes
description: Calcareous screes of the northern and central Pindus of Greece and southern Albania, with [Geranium aristatum], [Achillea abrotanoides], [Arenaria conferta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Olympus limestone screes
description: Screes of Olympus, with [Asperula muscosa], [Rhynchosinapis nivalis], [Alyssum handelii], [Achillea ambrosiaca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Pindus limestone screes
description: Screes of Parnassus, Giona and other southern Pindus ranges, with [Astragalus hellenicus], [Corydalis bulbosa], [Sclerochorton junceum], [Euphorbia deflexa], [Geranium macrorrhizum], [Rumex scutatus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peloponnese limestone screes
description: Screes of the Taygetos, Kilini and other Peloponnese ranges, with [Valantia aprica], [Minuartia juniperina].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegean screes
description: Subalpine screes of Crete and Karpathos, with [Ranunculus brevifolius], [Silene variegata], [Cicer incisum], [Cynoglossum sphacioticum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iono-Aegean serpentine screes
description: Serpentine screes of high mountains of southern Albania and mainland Greece, less widespread than the limestone screes of unit 61.41, restricted to serpentines of the northern Pindus and of Mount Olympus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pindus serpentine screes
description: Serpentine screes of the northern Pindus, with [Campanula hawkinsiana], [Arenaria serpentini], [Cardamine glauca], [Viola magellensis], [Alyssum scardicum], [Silene haussknechtii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Olympus serpentine screes
description: Serpentine screes of Mount Olympus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian screes
description: Limestone and ophiolite screes of Cyprus, in particular, limestone and ophiolite screes of the Troodos range, limestone screes of the Kyrenia range, flysch, sandstone and conglomerate screes of the Kythrean formation. Endemic plants include [Alyssum troodi], of Troodos serpentine substrates, [Hedysarum cyprium] and [Salvia veneris] of the Kythrean formation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian screes
description: Calcareous and serpentine screes of the alpine, subalpine and, locally, montane, levels of the Dinarides, the Pelagonides and the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, and of the upper mesomediterranean and supramediterranean [Orno-Quercetum ilicis] and [Ostryo-Carpinion adriaticum] zones of Istria, the Dalmatian coast and Montenegro.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian montane screes
description: Calcareous screes of the alpine, subalpine and, locally, montane levels of the Dinarides, the Pelagonides and the Moeso-Macedonian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian fern screes
description: [Dryopteris villarii]-dominated formations of calcareous screes of the east Adriatic mountains, widespread in the Dinarides and Pelagonides, with [Doronicum columnae], [Ligusticum dinaricum], [Scrophularia bosniaca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian butterbur screes
description: [Petasites paradoxus]-dominated formations of the foot and grooves of calcareous scree slopes of the Dinarides and Pelagonides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian drypis screes
description: Screes of the Dinarides and northern Hellenides dominated by [Drypis spinosa] ssp. [linnaena], of more submediterranean affinities than the communities of units 61.511 and 61.512, with [Cardamine carnosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian candytuft screes
description: Wind-exposed, snow-free calcareous screes of the Dinarides, with [Bunium alpinum], [Iberis pruitii], [Thymus acicularis], [Degenia velebitica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian toadflax screes
description: High-altitude calcareous screes of the Dinarides, in particular of the Prenj in Herzegovina and the Durmitor in Montenegro, with [Moehringia ciliata], [Papaver kerneri], [Poa minor].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian mouse-ear screes
description: Calcareous screes of the Dinara and Velebit, with [Cerastium dinaricum], [Euphorbia capitulata], [Thlaspi dinaricum], [Rumex scutatus], [Valeria montana], [Achillea clavenae], [Arabis scopoliana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian geranium screes
description: Calcareous screes of the Piva basin of Montenegro, with [Corydalis ochroleuca], [Moehringia muscosa], [Geranium macrorrhizum], [Saxifraga rotundifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonide toadflax-valerian screes
description: Calcareous screes of the Pelagonides of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and Albania, in particular, of the Korab range, with [Valeriana bertisceae], [Sedum magellense], [Lamium bifidum], [Hieracium bifidum], [Ranunculus seguieri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian sub-Mediterranean screes
description: Thermophile calcareous screes of the upper mesomediterranean and supramediterranean [Orno-Quercetum ilicis] and [Ostryo-Carpinion adriaticum] levels of the Triestine Karst, Istria, the Dalmatian coast, Montenegro and Albania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian montane serpentine screes
description: Serpentine screes of the montane level of the Dinarides of Bosnia-Herzegovina, harbouring the endemic [Halacsya sendtneri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian rough-grass screes
description: [Achnatherum calamagrostis] screes of Albania and Montenegro, in particular, of the Piva basin, southeastern representatives of the peri-Alpine [Stipion calamagrostidis] screes of unit 61.311.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal and arctic screes
description: Screes of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic and arcto-Atlantic screes
description: Communities of noncalcareous screes of the mountains and uplands of the boreal zone of the western Palaearctic domaine, developed on siliceous substrates or on basic to ultrabasic igneous or metamorphic substrates. Included are the screes of Greenland, Iceland, the Faeroes and Fennoscandia, around the rim of the western polar basin, in regions of Atlantic climate influence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic rock speedwell screes
description: Open pioneer communities of nutrient-rich, noncalcareous screes of the subalpine and low alpine levels of the boreoalpine and arctoalpine mountains of Fennoscandia and of the foot of west- or southwest-facing slopes of alpine southwestern Iceland, often composed of a mixture of lowland and alpine species, with an absence of chalk-dependant species; characteristic species include [Veronica fruticans], [Epilobium angustifolium], [Convallaria majalis], [Poa glauca], [Poa nemoralis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fennoscandian shrub-rich rock speedwell screes
description: Shrub-rich scree communities of screes of the subalpine and low alpine levels of the boreoalpine and arctoalpine mountains of Fennoscandia, resulting from stabilization and shrub invasion of the screes of unit 61.611. Characteristic shrubs include the usually dominant [Juniperus communis] and [Cotoneaster integerrimus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Faero-Icelandic mouse-ear screes
description: Open pioneer communities of gravel and stone screes of Iceland and the Faeroes dominated by [Cerastium alpinum] or, on the Faeroes, [Cerastium arcticum], with [Festuca vivipara] and a number of mosses, especially [Rhacomitrium spp.], and lichens, in particular of genus [Stereocaulon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lady's mantle screes
description: Open communities of dry, more or less stabilised, screes of moderatly steep lower slopes of Icelandic mountains, characterized by the prominence of [Alchemilla alpina] and [Thymus arcticus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fennoscandian northern bilberry screes
description: Very open, scattered, communities of acidic, dry to humid, humus-poor, gravel, stone and block screes of the upper montane, subalpine, low alpine and middle alpine levels of Fennoscandian mountains, formed by heliophile species, with a prominence of [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Juncus trifidus] and lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic thrift screes
description: Very sparse communities colonizing gravelly soils on wind-swept, snow-free, dry, porous lava fields and upland plateaux of Iceland, from near sealevel to 800 m, with [Armeria maritima], [Silene acaulis], [Thymus praecox] ssp. [arcticus], [Cardaminopsis petraea], [Cerastium alpinum], [Festuca vivipara], and, in particular on lowland lava fields of the Reykjanes peninsula, [Arenaria norvegica], [Silene uniflora]. Bryophytes are almost absent, [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] achieving a less than 1% cover on southwestern Icelandic lava fields.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic roseroot screes
description: Sparse scree communities of tussock-forming [Rhodiola rosea] and [Silene acaulis] of south-southeastern slopes of mountains of Iceland, of very local distribution.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Faero-Icelandic dwarf willow screes
description: Sparse communities of snow-bound upland and mountain screes of Iceland and the Faeroes, extending, as pioneer formations, to the lowlands, dominated by [Salix herbacea], mosses, especially [Rhacomitrium spp.], and lichens, in particular, of genus [Stereocaulon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Greenland screes
description: Screes of the mountains and uplands of Greenland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic sandwort calcicline screes
description: Pioneer open communities of unstable, gravelly, humus-poor, highly calcareous screes of the subalpine, low alpine and middle alpine levels of the boreoalpine and arctoalpine mountains of Fennoscandia formed by [Arenaria norvegica] and a number of endemic species or species of restricted range, including [Arenaria humifusa], [Arenaria pseudofrigida], [Artemisia norvegica], [Papaver] species of the [Papaver radicatum] group, [Papaver relictum], [Papaver laestadianum], [Braya linearis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-continental and arcto-continental screes
description: Communities of screes of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the central Palaearctic domaine. Included are the screes of the Chibiny range, of the Urals, of the chains of northern central Siberia, from the Putorany to the Tscherski range, of the mountains of southern Siberia, from the Altai to the Stanowoi range, situated in areas of high to very high continentality.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Pacific and arcto-Pacific screes
description: Scree communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the eastern Palaearctic domaine. Included are the screes of the Anadyr, Tschuktschi, Korjak, Kamchatka, Amurland and Sakalin mountains, situated in regions of Pacific climate influence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian screes
description: Scree communities of the mountains and steppe hills of Anatolia, the Levant, the Kurdo-Zagrosian and Irano-Turanian regions, Crimea, of the Pontic range, the Caucasus, the Elburz, the Central Asian mountains, the Himalayan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anatolian screes
description: Screes of the mountains and steppe hills of the mediterranean and submediterranean regions of Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supra-Mediterranean Anatolian screes
description: Screes of the supramediterranean level of the mountains and hills of Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Mediterranean Anatolian screes
description: Screes of the oromediterranean level of the mountains and hills of Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Levantine alpine screes
description: Screes of the high mountains of the Levant.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian screes
description: Screes of the mountains and steppe hills of the Kurdo-Zagrosian and Irano-Turanian regions of southwestern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caspian screes
description: Scree communities of the mountains and steppe hills of Crimea, of the Pontic range, of the Caucasus and of the Elburz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian screes
description: Scree communities of the mountains and steppe hills of Central Asia, including those of the Tian Shan, Pamir-Alai and Kopet Dag systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan screes
description: Scree communities of the Himalayan system, west to the Hindu-Kush.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African screes
description: Screes of thermomediterranean, mesomediterranean, supramediterranean and oromediterranean hills, mountains and high mountains of North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern screes
description: Screes of mountains and hills of the nemoral and warm-temperate zones of the Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland cliffs and exposed rocks
description: Unvegetated, sparsely vegetated, and bryophyte- or lichen-vegetated cliffs, rock faces, rock pavements and rock accumulations formed by erosional processes, of fluvial, glacial, aeolian, frost or past marine origin, not presently adjacent to the sea, and not resulting from recent volcanic activity. Rock accumulations resulting from depositional processes are excluded and listed under unit 61. Plant communities developing in parts of seacliffs free from the influence of wave or wind transported marine salt are included and may be noted by combined use of a code from unit 18.1 with a code from unit 62.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Rock-crack communities of dry, calcareous inland cliffs. Specific plant associations colonize montane and Mediterranean cliffs. Most of the subdivisions below refer to them. Northern lowland cliffs usually support fragments of communities listed in other units.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tyrrheno-Adriatic eumediterranean calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the mediterranean level of mainland Spain, of the Balaearics, of the thermo- and meso-mediterranean levels of mainland France, of Corsica and Sardinia, of peninsular Italy, of Sicily and associated islands, of the Adriatic coastal regions of the Balkan peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Petrarch-spleenwort cliffs
description: Calcareous and dolomitic cliff and rock communities of the Mediterranean hills and mountains of Spain, from Catalonia to the Serrania de Ronda, and of the thermo- and lower meso-Mediterranean levels of the Balearics, the coastal chains of Provence and Bas-Languedoc, of the southern C‚vennes, of Corsica and Sardinia, with [Asplenium petrarchae], [Phagnalon sordidum], [Sarcocapnos enneaphylla], [Biscutella frutescens], [Hieracium stelligerum], [Lavatera maritima], [Campanula macrorhiza], [Melica minuta], [Melica bauhinii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southeastern Iberian chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the arid southeastern regions of Spain, with large shrubs; [Scabiosa saxatilis], [Teucrium buxifolium], [Rhamnus lycioides] ssp. [borgiae] are characteristic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balearic calcareous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Balearics, with many endemics, including [Brassica balearica] and [Helichrysum rupestre] var. [cambessedesii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Insular cabbage cliffs
description: Calcareous rock communities of the mesomediterranean level of Corsica, Sardinia and Pantellaria, with [Brassica insularis], [Ruta graveolens], [Stachys glutinosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sicilo-Italic [Dianthus] cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the thermo- and mesomediterranean levels of Sicily, the Egadi Islands, the Maltese Islands, southern Calabria, southern Tyrrhenian Italy, rich in large subshrubby plants, with [Dianthus rupicola], [Iberis semperflorens], [Lithodora rosmarinifolia], [Antirrhinum siculum], [Brassica rupestris], [Brassica incana], [Scabiosa limonifolia], [Pimpinella anisoides], [Seseli bocconi] ssp. [bocconi], [Silene fruticosa], [Asperula rupestris], [Cymbalaria pubescens], [Odontites bocconei], all of them endemic to these communities or having in them their area of greatest diffusion.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010
