name: Panormitan knapweed cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of northwestern Sicily, between Alcara li Fusi and Trapani, of the continental shelf Egadi Islands, of Favignana and Levanzo, developed between 50 and 1000 metres, mostly on north-facing slopes, with the endemics [Centaurea ucriae], [Centaurea umbrosa], [Helichrysum rupestre] var. [rupestre], [Convolvulus cneorum] ssp. [cneorum], [Matthiola incana] ssp. [rupestris] and with [Scabiosa cretica]. Very local endemics characterize local subassociations, in particular, on Monte Gallo, near Mondello, with [Helichrysum rupestre] var. [stramineum], [Anthemis ismelia], [Hieracium lucidum], [Limonium panormitanum], on Monte Catalfano, east of Palermo, with [Centaurea todari], on Monte Cofano, betweeen Castellamare and Trapani, with [Erica sicula] ssp. [sicula], [Helichrysum rupestre] var. [cophanense], [Phagnalon metlesicsi], [Hieracium cophanense], on Monte Erice, above Trapani, with [Brassica drepanensis], on the Egadi Islands, with [Brassica macrocarpa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Egadean scabious cliffs
description: Calcareous rock-crack communities of the Egadean Island of Marettimo, developed above 200 metres, with [Scabiosa limonifolia] and the island endemics [Bupleurum dianthifolium], [Scilla hughii], [Thymus nitidus], [Helichrysum rupestre] var. [messerii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Busambran knapweed cliffs
description: Calcareous and dolomitic cliff and rock communities of interior mountains of northwestern Sicily, known from a few ranges within the Madonie and from the mountains to the south of Palermo, in particular, Rocca Busambra, Monte Kumeta, Monte La Pizzuta, between 500 and 1600 metres, with the endemic [Anthemis cupaniana], [Centaurea busambarensis], [Helichrysum rupestris] var. [pendulum]. Species characteristic of local representatives of these communities include the African [Viola munbyana], represented in Sicily only at Rocca Busambra and La Pizzuta, and the very restricted endemics [Bupleurum elatum] of the Madonie, and [Armeria gussonei] of the highest crests of Rocca Busambra.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyblaean putoria-micromeria cliffs
description: Cliff communities of Miocene limestones of the Iblei Mountains in southeastern Sicily, with [Putoria calabrica], [Micromeria microphylla], [Asperula aristata] ssp. [scabra] and the Iblei endemics [Trachelium lanceolatum] and [Urtica rupestris]. The [Dianthion rupicolae] cortŠge is reduced to [Dianthus rupicola], [Antirrhinum siculum], [Silene fruticosa], [Brassica incana], [Odontites bocconei], [Cymbalaria pubescens], [Pimpinella anisoides]. An isolated representative of the community exists on the Maltese Islands, located in a wadi of the central part of the main island, at Misram Gnonoq, dominated by [Putoria calabrica], but with an otherwise reduced cortŠge that includes [Micromeria microphylla] and [Antirrhinum siculum] but not [Dianthus rupicola]. [Chiliadenus bocconei], characteristic of the next unit, is present.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Maltese rdum communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Maltese Islands, characteristic of the western coasts of Malta, of Gozo, and of the vertical walls of wadis, harbouring many vulnerable, rare or endemic species. Endemic, often palaeoendemic, species include [Chiliadenus bocconei], [Palaeocyanus crassifolius], [Cremnophyton lanfrancoi], [Darniella melitensis], [Limonium melitensis]. Subendemic species comprise [Crucianella rupestris], [Senecio pygmaeus], [Daucus rupestris]. Among characteristic or physionomically important species are [Hypericum aegyptiacum] ([Triadenia aegyptiaca]), [Salsola vermiculata], [Capparis orientalis] ([Capparis spinosa] var. [inermis]), [Arthrocnemum glaucum], [Inula crithmoides], [Crithmum maritimum], [Asphodelus microcarpus]. Communities in Gozo are perhaps even more diverse and include endemic [Helichrysum melitense], [Hyoseris frutescens], [Matthiola incana] subsp. [melitensis] and subendemic [Senecio leucanthemifolius], with [Daucus gingidium] and [Allium arvense]. More impoverished communities of Comino are mainly characterized by [Darniella melitensis] with [Daucus rupestris], [Senecio leucanthemifolius] and [Inula crithmoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Agrigentan [Diplotaxis] cliffs
description: Chasmophyte communities of gypseous, calcareous, marly or arenaceous gypso-sulphuriferous rocks of central and central western Sicily, developed  in the provinces of Enna, Caltanissetta and Agrigento, both near the sea and in the interior, at altitudes comprised between 100 and 800 metres, with the primarily North African [Diplotaxis crassifolia] and [Erysimum suffruticosum], the endemic [Brassica villosa], and a reduced [Dianthion rupicolae] cortŠge, limited to [Silene fruticosa] and [Antirrhinum siculum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peloritano-Calabran [Erucastrum] cliffs
description: Cliff and rock communities of the Peloritani Mountains of northeastern Sicily and the mountains of southern Calabria, in a region of ancient siliceous crystalline rocks, including schists, granites, gneisses, marls and a limited representation of limestones and dolomites, with few cliffs and limited rock wall surfaces. The relatively reduced rupicolous flora is nevertheless rich in remarkable endemics. Characteristic of the community is the endemic [Erucastrum virgatum], associated with [Dianthus rupicola], [Antirrhinum siculum], [Silene fruticans], [Brassica incana], [Pimpinella anisoides] and [Sesili bocconi] subsp. [bocconi]. Very local endemics characterize subassociations, in particular, at Capo d'Ali, between Taormina and Messina, with [Limonium sibthorpianum], around Taormina with [Centaurea tauromenitana], on the crystalline schists of Capo Tindari with [Centaurea todari] f. [seguenzae], on the coast of southern Calabria, between Scilla and Bagnara with [Senecio gibbosus] and [Centaurea scyllae], on the Ionian slope of Calabria with [Centaurea ionica], [Campanula fragilis] var. [ionica], [Ptilostemon gnaphaloides] ssp. [gnaphaloides], [Leontodon intermedius], [Alyssum orientale].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Campanian knapweed cliffs
description: Chasmophyte communities of calcareous and dolomitic cliffs, and of araneceous tufas of the coastal mountains of the Tyrrhenian slope of northern Calabria, of Campania, and of southern Latium, with [Campanula fragilis] var. [fragilis], [Centaurea cineraria] and a reduced [Dianthion rupicolae] cortŠge comprising [Lithodora rosemarinifolia], [Dianthus rupicola], [Brassica incana], [Iberis semperflorens], [Pimpinella anisoides]. The communities of Capri and the Sorrento peninsula include the endemic [Seseli polyphyllum] and [Asperula crassifolia], as well as the rare [Convolvulus cneorum] ssp. [latifolium]. Those of the Cilento, between Capo Palinuro and Praia a Mare, harbour, in the most coastal stations, the archaic endemic [Primula palinuri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrian chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Adriadic meso-mediterranean zone of northeastern Italy and the Balkan peninsula. Some of them grade into maritime cliff communities of unit 18.221.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Istrio-Triestine karst chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff communities of the karst region of northeastern Italy and northern Istria with [Campanula pyramidalis], [Cheiranthus cheri], [Teucrium flavum], [Euphorbia wulfenii], [Micromeria thymifolia], harbouring the very rare, threatened endemics [Centaurea kartschiana] and [Moehringia tommasinii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Karst knapweed cliffs
description: Cliff communities of the karst region of northeastern Italy, with the very rare Triestine endemic [Centaurea kartschiana], and with [Erysimum cheiri] ([Cheiranthus cheiri]), [Campanula pyramidalis], [Teucrium flavum], [Sesleria juncifolia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Istrio-Triestine spurge cliffs
description: Cliff communities of the karst region of northeastern Italy and Slovenia, with  [Campanula pyramidalis], [Micromeria thymifolia], [Sesleria juncifolia], [Teucrium flavum] and [Euphorbia wulfenii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Istrio-Triestine moehringia cliffs
description: Cliff communities of the karst region of northeastern Italy, southwestern Slovenia and extreme northwestern Croatia, in the Vena Mountains between Val Rosandra and Buzet, harbouring the rare, threatened [Moehringia tommasinii], known from a very restricted number of stations within an exiguous region, one of them in Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Liburnian chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Adriadic meso-mediterranean coast lands of the northern Dalmatian coast, in part constituting the upper levels of sea-cliffs of unit 18.2219.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dalmatian knapweed cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Dalmatian islands of Rab and Pag with the endemic [Centaurea dalmatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Austrian viper's grass cliffs
description:
Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Dalmatian archipelago
with [Scorzonera austriaca], [Sesleria juncifolia], [Seseli pallasii], [Allysum robertianum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Liburnian meadow rue-bellflower cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the central and southern Velebit coast lands, with [Campanula fenestrellata], in part constituting the upper levels of sea-cliffs of unit 18.2219.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dalmatian chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Adriadic meso-mediterranean coast lands of the central Dalmatian coast, in part constituting the upper levels of sea-cliffs of unit 18.221A.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Raguse knapweed cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Dalmatian mesomediterranean zone, with the endemic [Centaurea ragusina] and [Convolvulus cneorum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moltkia cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the central and southern parts of the Dalmatian mesomediterranean zone, with [Moltkia petraea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Centaurea cuspidata] cliffs
description: Calcareous cliffs of the southern Biokovo coastlands of central Dalmatia, with [Inula spp.], [Centaurea cuspidata], [Seseli tomentosum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Vardean chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Adriadic meso-mediterranean coast lands of the southern Dalmatian coast, in part constituting the upper levels of sea-cliffs of unit 18.221B, in particular, communities dominated by [Putoria calabrica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dalmatian fern-navelwort cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Dalmatian mesomediterranean zone, widespread on rocks and man-made structures, with [Umbilicus horizontalis] and asplenioid ferns.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Pyrenean calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the central and eastern Pyrenees, with [Saxifraga media], [Saxifraga longifolia], [Saxifraga aretioides], [Potentilla alchimilloides], [Potentilla nivalis], [Ramonda myconi], [Asperula hirta].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Liguro-Apennine calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Maritime Alps and northern Apennines, with [Saxifraga lingulata], [Primula marginata], [Primula allionii], [Phyteuma charmelii], [Phyteuma villarsii], [Silene campanula], [Potentilla saxifraga], [Ballota frutescens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western mediterraneo-montane cinquefoil cliffs
description: Cliff and rock communities of the supra- and oro-Mediterranean levels of calcareous Iberian mountains, of the central Apennines and of the calcareous mountains of the large Tyrrhenian islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-montane cinquefoil cliffs
description: Cliff and rock communities of the supra- and oro-Mediterranean levels of calcareous Iberian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Cantabrian calcareous cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Cantabrian Cordillera and a few other northwestern Iberian ranges, with [Asperula hirta], [Asplenium viride], [Erinus alpinus], [Globularia repens], [Hypericum nummularium], [Rhamnus pumilus], [Saxifraga aretioides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Baetic calcareous cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of high altitudes of Baetic and sub-Baetic ranges of eastern Andalusia, with [Linaria verticillata], [Potentilla caulescens], [Saxifraga camposii], [Saxifraga erioblasta], [Teucrium rotundifolium], [Silene boryi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Valencian calcareous cliffs
description: Shady calcareous cliff and rock communities of Valencian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyrno-Italic cinquefoil cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the montane or subalpine levels of the central Apennines and of the calcareous mountains of the large Tyrrhenian islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Corsican montane calcareous cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the cryo-oromediterranean and supramediterranean levels of Corsica, limited to rare limestone outcrops, in particular, of the Chapelle Sant'Angelu de Lanu summit and of the Punta di u Fornellu, with [Arenaria bertolonii], [Potentilla crassinervia], [Festuca sardoa], [Dianthus sylvestris] ssp. [godronianus], [Ptychotis saxifraga], [Elymus corsicus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Apennine montane calcareous cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the montane or subalpine levels of the central Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West-Mediterranean polypode cliffs
description: Cool, shaded calcareous cliff and rock communities of the west Mediterranean regions, formed mostly of bryophytes and ferns, including [Polypodium cambricum] ssp. [australe] ([Polypodium australe]), and with [Selaginella denticulata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine and sub-mediterranean cinquefoil cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Alps and the Carpathians, of lesser satellite ranges and of submediterranean areas of the northern Tyrrhenian periphery.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine calcareous cliff heliophile communities
description: Well-lit calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Alps and neighbouring regions, including upper Provence, upper Languedoc, the pre-Pyrenees and CorbiŠres, the Catalonian mountains, with [Potentilla caulescens], [Potentilla clusiana], [Potentilla nitida], [Primula auricula], [Hieracium humile], [Cardaminopsis petraea], [Androsace helvetica], [Minuartia rupestris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle-European calcareous fern cliffs
description: Communities of shady, cool, often moist rockfaces of the Alps and neighbouring regions, of the Carpathians, of the Jura, the Hercynian ranges, the British Isles, with many ferns, including [Cystopteris fragilis], [Cystopteris regia], [Asplenium viride], [Asplenium scolopendrium], [Asplenium trichomanes], and with [Carex brachystachys].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian calcareous cliff heliophile communities
description: Rock-crack communities of sunny rock faces of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Carpathian calcareous cliff heliophile communities
description: Rock-crack communities of sunny rock faces of the alpine and subalpine levels of the high northwestern Carpathians, of Alpine affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian calcareous cliff xero-heliophile communities
description: Rock-crack communities of sunny rock faces of the alpine and subalpine levels of the eastern Carpathian system, characterized by the prevalence of Dacian endemics.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian saxifrage-campion cliff communities
description: Rock-crack communities of sunny rock faces of the Eastern Carpathians, formed by [Silene zawadzkii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian wormwood-gypsophila cliff communities
description: Rock-crack communities of sunny rock faces of the southeastern Carpathians, formed by [Artemisia eriantha] and [Gypsophila petraea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian saxifrage-whitlowgrass cliff communities
description: Rock-crack communities of abrupt slopes and humid ubacs of the Bucegi and Ceahlau mountains of the Southern Carpathians, formed by [Saxifraga moschata] and [Saxifraga oppositifolia] with [Draba kotschyi].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian musky saxifrage cliff communities
description: Rock-crack communities of sunny rock faces of the Retezat mountains in the western Southern Carpathians, formed by [Saxifraga marginata] ssp. [rocheliana] with species of Dacio-Balkanic affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Carpathian orange saxifrage cliff communities
description: Rock-crack communities of semishady rock faces of the southeastern Carpathians, formed by the endemic [Saxifraga mutata] ssp. [demissa] and [Gypsophila petraea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hellenic eumediterranean calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the thermo- and meso-Mediterranean zones of mainland Greece and Albania, up to the [Abies cephalonica] belt, with [Campanula versicolor], [Campanula rupestris], [Sideritis roeseri], [Stachys candida], [Hypericum vesiculosum], [Asperula arcadiensis], [Galium boryanum], [Centaurea pelia], [Alkanna graeca], [Alyssum orientale], [Linaria microcalyx], [Onosma frutescens], [Inula candida], [Centranthus ruber], [Silene congesta], [Teucrium flavum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aegeo-east-Mediterranean basiphile chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous and ultrabasic cliff and rock communities of Crete, the Aegean archipelagoes, Cyprus, the Mediterranean coastlands of Anatolia and the Levant. They constitute one of the most diverse and endemic-rich groups of cliff communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cretan chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and chasm communities of Crete, with [Petromarula pinnata], [Galium fruticosum], [Centaurea argentea], [Ebenus cretica], [Verbascum arcturus] ([Celsia arcturus]), [Inula candida], [Eryngium ternatum], [Asperula incana], [Dianthus juniperinus], [Aster canus], [Campanula pelviformis], [Campanula saxatilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Cretan chasmophyte communities
description: Relatively widespread cliff and chasm communities of the lowlands and hills of western and central Crete.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Cretan chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and chasm communities of the arid lowlands and hills of eastern Crete.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High-altitude Cretan chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and chasm communities of the high altitudes of Crete.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Karpathos chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and rock communities of Karpathos, with [Teucrium heliotropifolium], [Silene fruticosa], [Galium incurvum], [Inula heterolepis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Aegean chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and rock communities of Rhodes, Samos, Ikaria, Lesbos with [Campanula hagielia], [Lactuca leburnea], [Dianthus rhodensis], [Inula heterolepis], [Rosularia serrata], [Sedum creticum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyclades chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and rock communities of the Cyclades, with [Fibigia lunarioides], [Eryngium amorginum], [Amaracus tournefortii], [Campanula amorgina], [Campanula heterophylla], [Helichrysum amorginum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Sporades chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and rock communities of the Sporades, with [Inula sophiae], [Capparis spinosa], [Dianthus arboreus], [Amaracus tournefortii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyprian chasmophyte communities
description: Limestone and ophiolite cliff and rock communities of Cyprus, in particular, limestone and ophiolite cliffs and gorges of the Troodos range, limestone cliffs and pinnacles of the Kyrenia range, flysch, sandstone and conglomerate rock-slopes of the Kythrean formation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Kyrenia chasmophyte communities
description: Limestone cliff and rock communities of the Kyrenia range. Endemic plants include [Delphinium caseyi], [Brassica hilarionis] and [Arabis cypria] of the Kythrean formation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troodos limestone chasmophyte communities
description: Limestone cliff and rock communities of the Troodos range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troodos serpentine chasmophyte communities
description: Ophiolite cliff and rock communities of the Troodos range and the Akamas peninsula. Endemic plants include [Alyssum troodi], [Alyssum akamasicum], [Alyssum chondrogynum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Kythrean chasmophyte communities
description: Calciphile cliff and rock crevice communities of the Kythrean formation, with several local endemics, including [Hedysarum cyprium] and [Salvia veneris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Hellenic cinquefoil cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of high altitudes of the Peloponnese, Giona and Parnassus, with [Silene auriculata], [Achillea umbellata], [Campanula rupicola], [Saxifraga sibthorpii], [Saxifraga marginata], [Saxifraga spruneri], [Minuartia stellata], [Valeriana olenaea], [Satureja parnassica], [Rosa glutinosa], [Viola poetica], [Edraianthus parnassicus], [Campanula aizoon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Hellenic cinquefoil cliffs
description: Calcareous and ultrabasic cliff and rock communities of the high altitudes of the central and northern Pindus and of the Thessalian Olympus system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Olympian chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff and rock communities of the Thessalian Olympus system and of Mount Ossa, with [Saxifraga scardica], [Saxifraga glabella], [Campanula oreadum], [Arabis bryoides], [Potentilla deorum], [Jankaea heldreichii], [Omphalodes luciliae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pindus calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous and ultrabasic cliff and rock communities of the Pindus, with [Galium degenii], [Edraianthus graminifolius], [Asplenium fissum], [Aubrieta gracilis], [Achillea clavennae], [Satureja parnassica], [Hypericum apollinis], [Gnaphalium roeseri], [Trifolium noricum], [Silene pindicola].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyrio-Helleno-Balkanic cinquefoil cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Dinarides, the southwestern foothills of the eastern Carpathian system, the Balkan Range, the Pelagonides, the Rhodopides, formed by often narrowly endemic species of Illyro-Balkanic affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Balkanic calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Balkan Range, the Pelagonides and the Rhodopides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonide calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliffs of the Pelagonides of northern Greece, the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and of Albania, in particular of the Kapina, the Galicica, the Bistra, the Korab, the Jakupica, the Voras-Nidze, the Vermion, with [Ramondia nathaliae], [Campanula formanekiana], [Alyssoides utriculata], [Jurinea consanguinea], [Micromeria cristata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodopide calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Rhodopides.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pirin calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Pirin and the Slavianka with [Leontopodium alpinum] ssp. [nivale], [Potentilla apennina] ssp. [stoianovii], [Kernera saxatilis], [Campanula cochlearifolia] var. [pirinica], [Saxifraga ferdinandi-coburgi], [Saxifraga luteoviridis], [Papaver degenii], [Aster alpinus] var. [dolomiticus], [Brassica jordanoffii], [Danthoniastrum compactum], [Festuca pirinica], [Sesleria rigida], [Sesleria korabensis], [Pinus heldreichii] and, in the Slavianka, [Viola delphinantha], [Convolvulus boissieri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rila calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Rila, of very limited extent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhodope calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Rhodopes with [Campanula orphanidea] ([Petkovia orphanidea]), [Saxifraga stribrnyi], [Scabiosa rhodopensis], [Sideritis scardica], [Seseli rhodopeum], [Haberlea rhodopensis], [Morina persica], [Trachelium jacquinii] ssp. [rumelianum] ([Trachelium rumelianum]), [Campanula lanata], [Sesleria rigida], [Ceterach officinarum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan Range calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Balkan Range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkan range ramonda cliffs
description: Very rare and restricted [Ramonda serbica] communities of cliffs of the foothills of the western Balkan range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Vrachansky karst chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Vrachaanska mountains in the western Balkan Range, developed around 1400 metres of altitude, with [Festuca balcanica] ssp. [balcanica], [Festuca xanthina], [Achnatherum calamagrostis], [Juniperus sabina], [Daphne oleoides], [Syringa vulgaris], [Saxifraga rocheliana], [Polygala murbeckii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaro-Carpathian calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the Dinarides and the southwestern foothills of the eastern Carpathian system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dinaric calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Cliff communities of calcareous rocks of the Dinarides, from Croatia to Montenegro, with [Micromeria croatica], and a number of specialized species of limited distribution, some of them narrow endemics, characterizing diverse communities, including the small western Balkanic borage shrub [Moltkia petraea], the Piva gorge [Daphne malyana], the crassulid [Jovibarba heuffelii], the saxifrages [Saxifraga marginata] ssp. [rocheliana], [Saxifraga paniculata], the cinqfoils [Potentilla clusiana], [Potentilla colescens] ssp. [persicina], the bellflowers [Campanula fenestrellata] ([Campanula garganica]), [Campanula pyramidalis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Banat collinar calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff communities of the southwestern foothills of the eastern Carpathian system, in the south of the Banat and, in particular, the Danube Iron Gates gorge, with [Micromeria pulegium], [Athamanta turbith] ssp. [hungarica], [Dianthus kitaibelii], [Silene saxifraga] ssp. [petraea], [Erysimum comatum], [Campanula crassipes].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Moist Dinaric calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Communities of humid cliffs of the northern Dinarides, subjected to tufa formation, with [Carex brachystachys], [Valeriana elongata], [Aster bellidiastrum], [Campanula cochlearifolia] ssp. [croatica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Balkano-Illyrian shaded calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Communities of shady, cool, often moist rockfaces of the Dinarides and neighbouring regions, Balkano-Illyrian vicariant of the [Cystopteridion] communities of unit 62.152, widespread at the montane beech level, with many ferns, including [Cystopteris montana], [Asplenium ruta-muraria], [Asplenium trichomanes], and with [Corydalis ochroleuca], [Moehringia muscosa], [Cardaminopsis croatica], [Saxifraga rotundifolia], [Campanula justiniana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lowland middle European calcareous cliff communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the plains and hills of nemoral northern and middle Europe, very species-poor, usually occupying small surfaces within the environment of more extensive communities of units 34.1 or 34.35.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fern nemoral lowland cliff communities
description: Species-poor pioneer communities of calcareous cliffs and rocks of the lowlands of middle and northern Europe dominated by ferns, in particular, [Asplenium ruta-muraria]-[Asplenium trichomanes] communities of limestone fissures known from the Jura, the Werra and Saale regions, the Sauerland Massenkalk, the Harz, Belgium, France, and the boreonemoral alvars of ™land, Gotland and V„sterg”tland, [Asplenium lepidum] formations of eastern Central Europe, [Cystopteris fragilis] formations of more shady rocks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Forb nemoral lowland cliff communities
description: Species-poor pioneer communities of calcareous cliffs and rocks of the lowlands of middle Europe dominated by small forbs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal calcareous cliff communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the boreal and arctic zones of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic calcareous cliff communities
description: Calcareous rock and cliff crevice communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the western Palaearctic domaine, in particular of the Fennoscandian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Green spleenwort calcareous boreal cliffs
description: Calcareous cliff crevice and rock communities of the alpine belt of boreal Fennoscandia formed by [Asplenium viride], [Woodsia glabella] and many xerophytes. [Saxifraga cotyledon], [Potentilla hyparctica], [Potentilla chamisonis], [Potentilla pulchella], [Kobresia myosuroides] are typical of various communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Brittle fern-roseroot calcareous boreal cliffs
description: Sparse calcareous rock and cliff crevice communities of Norway formed by [Cystopteris fragilis] and [Rhodiola rosea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-continental calcareous cliff communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the central Palaearctic domaine. Included are the communities of the Chibiny range, of the Urals, of the chains of northern central Siberia, from the Putorany to the Tscherski range and of the mountains of southern Siberia, from the Altai to the Stanowoi range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Pacific calcareous cliff communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the eastern Palaearctic domaine. Included are the communities of the Anadyr, Tschuktschi, Korjak, Kamchatka, Amurland and Sakalin mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterraneo-Anatolian calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the eastern Mediterranean hinterland and of mediterranean and submediterranean Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northwestern Anatolian calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Communities of calcareous rocks of the mediterraneo-montane and oromediterranean levels of northwestern Anatolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Taurus calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Communities of calcareous rocks of the mediterraneo-montane and oromediterranean levels of the western Taurus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Taurus calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Communities of calcareous rocks of the mediterraneo-montane and oromediterranean levels of the central eastern Taurus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of mediterranean North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Kurdo-Zagrosian and Irano-Turanian regions, of Crimea, the Pontic range, the Caucasus, the Elburz, the Central Asian mountains, the Himalayan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Kurdo-Zagrosian and Irano-Turanian regions of southwestern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caspian calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the mountains and steppe hills of Crimea, of the Pontic range, of the Caucasus and of the Elburz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the mountains and steppe hills of Central Asia, including those of the Tian Shan, Pamir-Alai and Kopet Dag systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the Himalayan system, west to the Hindu-Kush.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern calcicolous chasmophyte communities
description: Calcareous cliff and rock communities of the nemoral, warm-humid temperate and tropical Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Silicicolous and boreo-basaltic chasmophyte communities
description: Rock-crack communities of dry non-calcareous inland cliffs. Specific plant associations colonize montane and Mediterranean cliffs. Most of the subdivisions below refer to them. Northern lowland cliffs usually support fragments of communities listed in other chapters.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European montane siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the northwestern, northern, eastern and central Alps, the Pyrenees, the western Carpathians, the middle European Hercynian ranges, the Jura.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Middle European high-altitude siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the alpine and subalpine levels of the northwestern, northern, eastern and central Alps, with outliers in the Dinarides, of the Massif Central and of the Pyrenees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pyreneo-Alpine high-altitude siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the alpine and subalpine levels of the northwestern, northern, eastern and central Alps, of the Dinarides and of the Pyrenees, with [Androsace vandellii], [Artemisia umbelliformis], [Eritrichium nanum], [Minuartia cherlerioides], [Primula hirsuta], [Phyteuma scheuchzeri], [Erysimum rhaeticum], [Saxifraga aspera], [Saxifraga cotyledon], [Saxifraga iratiana], [Saxifraga retusa], [Saxifraga bryoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Massif subalpine siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the subalpine levels of the Central Massif, with [Minuartia verna], [Saxifraga lamottei], [Saxifraga hieraciifolia], [Dianthus gratianopolitanus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynio-Alpine montane and collinar siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the montane level of the middle European Hercynian ranges, the Jura, the Alps and their periphery, of Atlantic regions of the European continent and the British Isles, with [Saxifraga sponhemica], [Biscutella laevigata], [Asplenium septentrionale], [Asplenium adiantum-nigrum], [Asplenium billotii], [Asplenium foresiense].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hercynio-Alpine serpentine cliffs
description: Serpentine cliff and rock communities of the middle European Hercynian ranges and their periphery, of northern Styria, Low-Austria and the Burgenland, with [Asplenium adulterinum], [Asplenium cuneifolium], [Asplenium x alternifolium], [Cheilanthes marantae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian montane siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff communities of Alpine affinities of the Carpathians, formed principally by bryophytes and ferns.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpathian fern siliceous cliffs
description: Communities dominated by or rich in ferns of siliceous cliffs of the Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Carpathian [Jovibarba heuffelii] communities
description: Cliff communities occupying siliceous rock fissures of interior valleys at the foot of the Cibinului Mountains in the western Southern Carpathians, formed by [Jovibarba heuffelii] with [Veronica bachofenii], [Genista januensis], [Silene dubia], [Thymus comosus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Oro-Iberian siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of high altitudes of Iberian mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ibero-Carpetanian siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the Cordillera Cantabrica, the Iberian Range, the Cordillera Central and the Leonese mountains, with [Hieracium pallidum] ssp. [graniticum], [Murbeckiella boryi] ssp. [boryi], [Murbeckiella boryi] ssp. [herminii], [Saxifraga willkommiana], [Spergula viscosa] ssp. [pourretii].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nevadan siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the Sierra Nevada, with [Saxifraga nevadensis], [Sedum brevifolium], [Centranthus nevadensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southwestern Alpine siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the Maritime, Ligurian and Cottian Alps, with [Saxifraga pedemontana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cyrno-Sardinian montane and alpine cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the mountains of Corsica and Sardinia, distributed from the supramediterranean to the alpine level, with [Potentilla crassinervia], [Armeria leucocephala], [Silene requieniil, [Saxifraga pedemontana] ssp. [cervicornis]. Supramediterranean and montane communities have [Amelanchier ovalis] ssp. [rhamnoides],  cryomediterranean, subalpine and alpine communities have [Festuca sardoa], [Phyteuma serratum], [Helechryssum frigidum], [Aquilegia bernardii], [Leucanthemum corsicum], [Scabiosa corsica], upper alpine communmities are characterized by the presence of [Draba dubia], [Asplenium veride], [Draba loiseleurii], [Erigeron paolii] and the absence of thermophile species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Helleno-Carpatho-Balkanic campion siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff communities rich in Dacio-Balkanic endemics of the subalpine level of the eastern Carpathian system and the mountains of the Balkan peninsula, including the Dinarides, the Balkan Range, the Moeso-Macedonian mountains, the Pelagonides and the Rhodopides, of relict character.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Carpathian campion siliceous cliffs
description: Endemic siliceous cliff communities of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Southern  Carpathians.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fagaras campion siliceous cliffs
description: Endemic siliceous cliff communities of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Fagaras mountains of the Southern Carpathians, formed by [Silene dinarica], with [Festuca airoides], [Juncus trifidus], [Primula minima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Retezat campion siliceous cliffs
description: Endemic siliceous cliff communities of the alpine and subalpine levels of the Southern Carpathian Retezat and Tarcu-Godeanu mountains, formed by [Silene lerchenfeldiana], with [Senecio glaberrimus], [Juncus trifidus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Carpatho-Balkano-Rhodopide campion siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff communities of the Paring mountains in the Southern Carpathians, of the Balkan Range and of the Rhodopides, in particular, of the Rila and the Pirin, with [Silene lerchenfeldiana], [Potentilla haynaldiana], [Saxifraga juniperifolia] ssp. [juniperifolia] ([Saxifraga pseudosancta]), [Saxifraga pedemontana] ssp. [cymosa], [Rhodiola rosea] ([Sedum rosea]), [Dianthus henteri], [Minuartia bulgarica], [Haberlea rhodopensis], [Symphyandra wanneri], [Carex kitaibeliana] ([Carex laevis]), [Juncus trifidus], [Sesleria coerulans], [Festuca airoides], [Poa nemoralis], [Asplenium trichomanes], [Cystopteris fragilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pelagonide campion siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff communities of the Pelagonides of the F.Y.R. of Macedonia and northern Greece.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Pyrenean montane siliceous cliffs
description: Montane siliceous cliff and rock communities of the C‚vennes, the eastern and central Pyrenees and the Catalonian hills, with [Asarina procumbens] ([Antirrhinum asarina]), [Sedum hirsutum], [Centaurea pectinata], [Sempervivum arvernense], [Dianthus graniticus], [Saxifraga clusii], [Saxifraga hypnoides].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Iberian siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the meso-Mediterranean level of western Iberia, with [Cheilanthes tinaei], [Cheilanthes hispanica].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Mediterranean thermophile siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the thermomediterranean, mesomediterranean and lower supramediterranean levels of Provence, Corsica and eastern Spain, mostly constituted by ferns, in particular, of genus [Cheilanthes] (including [Cosentinia]) in xeric sunny situations, of genera [Asplenium] and [Polypodium] in more shady locations, accompanied by species of genus [Dianthus], in particular, [Dianthus sylvestris] ssp. [siculus], [Dianthus sylvestris] ssp. [godronianus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lowland middle European siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the hills of northern and middle nemoral Europe colonized by communities referable to units other than 62; their nature can be specified by addition of the relevant codes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal siliceous cliffs
description: Rock and cliff crevice communities of granites, gneisses and acidic rocks of the boreal and arctic zones of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic siliceous cliffs
description: Rock and cliff crevice communities of granites, gneisses and acidic rocks of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the western Palaearctic domaine, in particular of Fennoscandia and Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal spleenwort siliceous cliffs
description: Rock and cliff communities of boreal Fennoscandian and Icelandic granites, gneisses and acidic rocks, generally occurring in the humus accumulation of crevices and comprising few genuine chasmophytes, dominated by variable, usually paucispecific assemblies in which [Asplenium septentrionale], [Asplenium trichomanes], [Potentilla argentea] are often prominent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal rock campion-heather siliceous cliffs
description: Rock and cliff communities of southern and middle Fennoscandian granite, gneiss and acidic sediment glacier-fashioned flat-top rock outcrops with dense lichen carpets, formed, in particular, by [Cladonia rangiferina], mosses, scrubs and sometimes sparse grasses and forbs. [Calluna vulgaris], [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Silene rupestris] are characteristic. Part of the communities may constitute more or less open [Pinus sylvestris] woods of unit 42, or [Calluna vulgaris] heaths of unit 31.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal woodsia-sticky catchfly siliceous cliffs
description: Rock and cliff communities of southern and middle Fennoscandian granite or gneiss, sometimes with amphibolite or gabbro, glacier-fashioned flat-top rock outcrops with a varied lichen, moss and vascular plant cover, formed, in particular, by [Deschampsia flexuosa], [Woodsia ilvensis], [Lychnis viscaria]. Part of the communities may constitute more or less open [Pinus sylvestris] woods of unit 42, or [Juniperus communis] thickets of unit 31.8.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-continental siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous rock and cliff communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the central Palaearctic domaine. Included are the communities of the Chibiny range, of the Urals, of the chains of northern central Siberia, from the Putorany to the Tscherski range and of the mountains of southern Siberia, from the Altai to the Stanowoi range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Pacific siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous rock and cliff communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the eastern Palaearctic domaine. Included are the communities of the Anadyr, Tschuktschi, Korjak, Kamchatka, Amurland and Sakalin mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal serpentine and basaltic cliffs
description: Serpentine and basalt cliff and rock communities of the boreal and arctic zones of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Atlantic serpentine and basaltic cliffs
description: Serpentine and basalt cliff and rock communities of the boreal and arctic zones of the western Palaearctic domaine, in particular of Fennoscandia and Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal spleenwort-sandwort-mouse-ear serpentine cliffs
description: Scattered communities of serpentine cliffs and rocks of subalpine low alpine and middle alpine levels of the Fennoscandian mountains, colonizing crevices and weathered, frost-shattered rock debris; [Asplenium viride], [Arenaria norvegica] and serpentine varieties of several species of mouse-ears, in particular, [Cerastium alpinum] var. [serpentinicola], [Cerastium alpinum] var. [nordhagenii], [Cerastium fontanum] var. [kajanense], [Cerastium glabratum] var. div., are characteristic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal heath serpentine cliffs
description: Communities of serpentine cliffs and rocks of the upper montane, subalpine and low alpine levels of the Fennoscandian mountains rich in heath species, in particular, [Calluna vulgaris], [Empetrum hermaphroditum], [Vaccinium uliginosum], with much [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], on a thin humus layer.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Serpentine fern boreal cliffs
description: Communities of serpentine cliffs and rocks of oceanic southern boreal Norway, colonizing crevices and weathered rocks, with [Asplenium adulterinum] and [Cardaminopsis petraea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic basaltic cliffs
description: Basic cliff and rock communities of Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic green spleenwort cliffs
description: Cliff crevice and rock communities of basaltic lowlands of southern Iceland formed by [Asplenium viride], [Woodsia glabella] and many xerophytes. [Saxifraga cotyledon], [Potentilla hyparctica], [Potentilla chamisonis], [Potentilla pulchella], [Kobresia myosuroides] are typical of various communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic brittle fern-roseroot cliffs
description: Sparse crevice communities of basic rocks and cliffs of Iceland and the Faeroes formed by [Cystopteris fragilis] and [Rhodiola rosea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-continental serpentine and basaltic cliffs
description: Serpentine and basalt cliff and rock communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the central Palaearctic domaine. Included are the communities of the Chibiny range, of the Urals, of the chains of northern central Siberia, from the Putorany to the Tscherski range and of the mountains of southern Siberia, from the Altai to the Stanowoi range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-Pacific serpentine and basaltic cliffs
description: Serpentine and basalt cliff and rock communities of the mountains and uplands of the boreal and arctic zones of the eastern Palaearctic domaine. Included are the communities of the Anadyr, Tschuktschi, Korjak, Kamchatka, Amurland and Sakalin mountains.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: North African siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of mediterranean North Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the Kurdo-Zagrosian and Irano-Turanian regions, of Crimea, the Pontic range, the Caucasus, the Elburz, the Central Asian mountains, the Himalayan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the Kurdo-Zagrosian and Irano-Turanian regions of southwestern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Caspian siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of Crimea, of the Pontic range, of the Caucasus and of the Elburz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the mountains of Central Asia, including those of the Tian Shan, Pamir-Alai and Kopet Dag systems.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Himalayan siliceous cliffs

source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous cliff and rock communities of the nemoral, warm-humid temperate and tropical Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pavements, rock slabs, moss and lichen carpets
description: More or less level surfaces of rock of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic exposed by glacial erosion, by weathering processes, or by nondesert aeolian scouring, bare or colonized by mosses, algae or lichens. The hard rock surface may be apparent or partially or completely covered by indigenous erosional rock debris, in particular, those produced by frost weathering, heaving, thrusting or cracking. Included are, in particular, lapi‚s, karren, limestone pavements of karst landscapes, rock dome tops, whaleback, roche moutonn‚e, flyggberg and rock basin formations of periglacial areas, frost-shattered mountain-top detritus, golec and felsenmeer formations, level surfaces of dykes and old lava flows. Vascular plant communities may colonize cracks and superficially decomposed areas, in particular, [Sedo-Scleranthion], [Alysso-Sedion albi] or [Sedo albi-Veronicion dillenii] communities of units 34.11 and 36.2, occasionally scree communities of unit 61 or chasmophyte communities of units 62.1 or 62.2. More developed communities belonging to other units may also be present.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pavements, rock slabs, rock domes
description: Bare or sparsely vegetated more or less level surfaces of rock of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic exposed by erosion or weathering processes, physiognomically dominated by hard rock surfaces or indigenous erosional rock debris.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Limestone pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of calcareous rock of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic, including karstic pavements, lapi‚s, with their clints and grikes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High altitude and arctic limestone pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of calcareous rock of nondesert arctic regions and of the nival, or aeolian, level of mountains of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain limestone pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of calcareous rock of the alpine to montane levels of high mountains of the mediterranean, nemoral, boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-nemoral and boreal limestone pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of calcareous rock of of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, in particular alvars of the eastern Fenno-Scandian boreonemoral zone occupied by epilithic lichen communities of unit 62.32, associated with debris swards, calcareous grasslands and paucispecific nemoral fissure communities of units 34.1151, 34.317 and 62.1B1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral low altitude limestone pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of calcareous rock of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the nemoral zone of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010
