source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siliceous pavements, slabs and domes
description: More or less level surfaces of siliceous rocks of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High altitude and arctic siliceous pavements

source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-nemoral and boreal siliceous pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of siliceous rocks of lowlands and hills of the boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, in particular, flat tops of southern and middle Fennoscandian granite, gneiss and acidic sediment glacier-fashioned rock outcrops. source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral low altitude siliceous pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of siliceous rock of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the nemoral zone of the Palaearctic, in particular, sandstone slabs of north central and eastern France.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean siliceous pavements
description: More or less level surfaces of siliceous rock of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the Mediterranean region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

description: More or less level surfaces of basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rock of nondesert arctic regions and of the nival, or aeolian, level of mountains of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

description: More or less level surfaces of basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rock of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the Mediterranean region.

name: Rock pavement lichen communities
description: More or less level surfaces of rock of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic exposed by erosion or weathering processes, colonized by dense lichen mats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Arctic and arctoalpine lichen heaths
description: Lichen-dominated communities of level rock or erosional debris surfaces of arctic regions, outside of polar deserts, and of the arctoalpine level of the mountains of the northern boreal region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal and boreo-nemoral rock lichen heaths
description: Lichen-dominated communities of level rock or erosional debris surfaces of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the boreal and boreo-nemoral regions of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alvar lichen heaths
description: Epilithic lichen communities of alvars of the eastern Fenno-Scandian boreonemoral zone dominated by [Lecanora calcarea], with [Collema spp.] and [Verrucaria nigrescens], accompanied by the mosses [Grimmia pulvinata] and [Schistidium apocarpum], associated with debris swards, calcareous grasslands and paucispecific nemoral fissure communities of units 34.1151, 34.317 and 62.1B1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal rock outcrop lichen heaths
description: Carpets of lichens, often very dense, of flat tops of southern and middle Fennoscandian granite, gneiss and acidic sediment, sometimes amphibolite or gabbro, glacier-fashioned rock outcrops, usually dominated by [Cladonia rangiferina], sometimes associated with mosses and with scrub, grass and forb fissure communities of unit 62.2A.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral and alpine pavement lichen communities
description: Lichen-dominated communities of level rock or erosional debris surfaces of lowlands, hills and mountains of the nemoral regions of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean rock pavement lichen communities
description: Lichen-dominated communities of level rock or erosional debris surfaces of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the mediterranean regions of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rock pavement, plateau and summital moss heaths
description: More or less level surfaces of rock of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic exposed or shattered by erosion or weathering processes, colonized by dense moss carpets.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal and arcto-Atlantic moss heaths
description: Moss carpets, often thick and extensive, developed over more or less level surfaces of rock or erosional rock debris accumulations of lowlands, hills and mountains of boreal, boreo-nemoral or arctic regions of the Palaearctic, particularly characteristic of basaltic, siliceous, or sometimes calcareous, summits and plateaux of the North-Atlantic, in Iceland, the Faeroes, Scotland and, locally, the Scandinavian mountains, northern England and northern Wales, Greenland, Spitzbergen. These moss-heaths, dominated by [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] or [Rhacomitrium canescens] (unit 62.331 x 36.322), constitute, together with the lava-field formations of unit 66.312 (unit 66.312 x 36.3223), one of the most original landscapes of Iceland and the North Atantic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral moss carpets
description: Moss carpets of more or less level surfaces of rock or erosional rock debris accumulations of lowlands, hills and mountains of nemoral, steppe and mediterranean regions of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rock pavement and slab pools
description: Pools, usually temporary, forming in basins, hollows or depressions on more or less level surfaces of rock of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic. They may be colonized by highly specialized communities of units 22.2 and 22.3.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Limestone pavement pools
description: Pools, usually temporary, forming in karst pans, runnels, basins, pits of limestone pavements of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic. They may be colonized by highly specialized communities of units 22.25, 22.27 and 22.3. Remarkable, endemic-rich faunas occur, in particular, in temporary pools of Malta, of the Causses and of the Slovenian karst.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sandstone slab pools
description: Pools, usually temporary, forming on siliceous or basaltic pavements, slabs and domes of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic. They may be colonized by highly specialized communities of units 22.21, 22.22, 22.27 and 22.3. Particularly remarkable are the "platiŠre" pools of sandstone slabs of southern Ile-de-France harbouring a highly unique flora and fauna, particularly of crustaceans.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dry inland cliffs
description: Noncoastal cliffs and exposed rocks of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic. At high altitudes and high latitudes, they may be devoid of vascular vegetation; they are then usually colonized by lichen crusts and "ink stains". At lower altitudes in the mountains, as well as in Mediterranean and boreal regions, they comprise, besides lichen communities and bare surfaces, fissure communities of units 62.1 and 62.2. In nemoral and steppe lowland and hills, these specialized fissure communities are very impoverished, reduced to the extremely paucispecific communities of units 62.1B and 62.29; they share the cliffs with debris sward communities of unit 34.11, more evolved grassland communities of unit 34.35, sometimes 34.31, 34.33 or 34.341, and lacunar shrub formations of unit 31.8.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Limestone dry inland cliffs
description: Limestone rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic. Their lichen communities are composed of internal crustose lichens ([Protoblastenia], [Verrucaria], [Petractis], [Polyblastia]), external crustose lichens ([Caloplaca], [Xanthoria]) or gelatinous ([Collema]) and foliose ([Dermatocarpon]) lichens.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High altitude and arctic limestone cliffs
description: Limestone rocks, cliffs and nunataks of nondesert arctic regions and of the nival, or aeolian, level of mountains of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain limestone cliffs
description: Limestone rocks and cliffs of the alpine to montane levels of high mountains of the mediterranean, nemoral, boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, harbouring specialized alpine chasmophyte communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-nemoral and boreal limestone cliffs
description: Limestone rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, harbouring specialized boreal fissure communities, including near vertical surfaces of alvars of the eastern Fenno-Scandian boreonemoral zone occupied by epilithic lichen communities of unit 62.32, associated with debris swards, calcareous grasslands and paucispecific nemoral fissure communities of units 34.1151, 34.317 and 62.1B1.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral low altitude limestone cliffs
description: Limestone rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the nemoral zone of the Palaearctic, harbouring impoverished, paucispecific, fissure communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean limestone cliffs
description: Limestone rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the Mediterranean region, harbouring specialized Mediterranean chasmophyte communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siliceous dry inland cliffs
description: Siliceous rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic. Their lichen communities are composed of external crustose lichens ([Rhizocarpon]), navel lichens ([Umbilicaria]) and fruticose lichens ([Ramalina], [Cornicularia], [Rhizoplaca]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High altitude and arctic siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous rocks, cliffs and nunataks of nondesert arctic regions and of the nival, or aeolian, level of mountains of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous rocks and cliffs of the alpine to montane levels of high mountains of the mediterranean, nemoral, boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, harbouring specialized alpine chasmophyte communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-nemoral and boreal siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, harbouring specialized boreal fissure communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral low altitude siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the nemoral zone of the Palaearctic, harbouring impoverished, paucispecific, fissure communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean siliceous cliffs
description: Siliceous rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the Mediterranean region, harbouring specialized Mediterranean chasmophyte communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Basaltic and ultrabasic dry inland cliffs
description: Basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and mountains of nondesert regions of the Palaearctic, including basalts, gabbros, dolerites, andesites, ultramafites (serpentines, peridotites).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High altitude and arctic basaltic and ultrabasic cliffs
description: Basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rocks, cliffs and nunataks of nondesert arctic regions and of the nival, or aeolian, level of mountains of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mountain basaltic and ultrabasic cliffs
description: Basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rocks and cliffs of the alpine to montane levels of high mountains of the mediterranean, nemoral, boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, harbouring specialized alpine chasmophyte communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-nemoral and boreal basaltic and ultrabasic cliffs
description: Basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rocks and cliffs of the boreonemoral and boreal zones of the Palaearctic, harbouring specialized boreal fissure communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nemoral low altitude basaltic and ultrabasic cliffs
description: Basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the nemoral zone of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean basaltic and ultrabasic cliffs
description: Basic or ultrabasic noncalcareous rocks and cliffs of lowlands, hills and low mountains of the Mediterranean region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wet inland cliffs
description: Very wet, dripping, overhanging or vertical rocks of hills, mountains and Mediterranean lowlands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean wet inland cliffs
description: Wet inland cliffs of Mediterranean regions, with a specialized vegetation formed by [Adiantum capillus-veneris], mosses, [Borago pygmaea], [Pinguicula grandiflora] ssp. [coenocantabrica], [Pinguicula hirtiflora].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern wet inland cliffs
description: Wet inland cliffs of middle European hills and mountains. They are often colonized by unique plant assemblages, the components of which are, however, equally characteristic of other habitats; notable among such species are [Saxifraga paniculata], [Alchemilla glabra], [Viola palustris], [Phegopteris connectilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian inland cliffs
description: Inland cliffs of the Canary Islands, Madeira and the Azores, extremely rich in endemic species of both plants and animals, including vertebrates (the endangered [Pterodroma madeira]). The genus [Aeonium] is particularly representative.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eternal snow and ice
description: High mountain zones and high latitude land masses occupied by glaciers or by perennial snow. They may be inhabited by algae and invertebrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Snow packs
description: Quasipermanent snow packs, in particular in avalanche corridors.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rock glaciers, ice-core moraines, glacierets
description: Rock, stone or debris formations covering buried or underlying ice, small areas of uncovered permanent or semipermanent ice caused by relief features.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rock glaciers
description: Glacier-like tongues of angular talus extending out from a cirque and slowly moving downslope under the effect of gravity and of underlying, fully covered, interstitial ice.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ice-core moraines
description: Fairly large ridges or mounds of morainic material containing buried ice, originating from till deposited on former glacier ice or from morainic material deposited on a snow bank, adjacent to the ice front.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Glacierets
description: Small ice masses, permanent, or with an existence of a few years, derived in particular from snow-drifting, avalanches, or ice deposition in cold-bottom karst dolines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: True glaciers
description: Masses of snow and ice formed by the consolidation under pressure of snow falling on high ground, moving outward and downward from the zone of accumulation to lower ground.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ice sheets and ice caps
description: Dome-like ice masses unconstrained by topography, together with their outlet glaciers. They are characteristic of arctic regions. The largest ice sheet in the northern hemisphere is that of Greenland. Smaller ice sheets and ice caps occur in Iceland, Jan Mayen, Spitsbergen, southern Norway, Franz Josef Land, Severnaya Zemlya and the islands of the De-Longa group.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cirque and valley glaciers
description: Glaciers constrained by topography, including cirque glaciers, valley glaciers, mountain glaciers, piedmont glaciers. They are characteristic, in particular, of the large mountain ranges of the Alpine system, occurring also in arctic regions, notably on Novaya Zemlya, in the subpolar and polar Urals, in the east Siberian mountains and, locally, in Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dunes
description: Habitats, habitat complexes and landscapes dominated by accumulations of sand, rarely of silt or clay, deposited by aeolian processes and often possessing marked constructional relief, developed within the boreal, nemoral, steppic, warm-temperate humid, mediterranean or subdesert steppe zones, separated from the coast and its dune cordons by nondunal habitats. Unvegetated areas, algae-, lichen- or bryophyte-dominated pioneer communities and very sparse communities of higher plants are listed in this section. Other communities are noted by combination of units of this section with units from sections 3 or 4. Desert sands are excluded and listed under section 7.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Germano-Baltic fluvio-glacial dunes
description: Dunes of the North Sea and Baltic plains, formed of quartzic sands originating in redeposited and reworked glacial drift and outwash. They are highly siliceous in the Netherlands, northern Belgium and northwestern Germany, progressively slightly less oligotrophic and with a more continental cortŠge in northeastern Germany, Poland and the eastern Baltic plain. The dune systems, particularly the large ones, harbour a unique ensemble of interacting communities and harbour many specialized and restricted organisms. They have considerably regressed and the remaining examples are fragile and often threatened. The presence of the various elements of the ecosystem can be indicated by simultaneous use of the codes below and of those relevant to the types of plant communities they represent.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune pioneer grasslands
description: Formations of unstable Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland sands with [Corynephorus canescens], [Carex arenaria], [Spergula morisonii], [Teesdalia nudicaulis] and carpets of fruticose lichens ([Cladonia], [Cetraria]) (cf. unit 35.23). Communities of Jutland are rich in [Ammophila arenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune siliceous grasslands
description: Grasslands of more stabilized Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland dune systems with [Agrostis spp.] and [Corynephorus canescens] or other acidophilous grasses; their composition can be specified by use of codes of of 35 other than of unit 35.23.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune heaths
description: Heaths colonizing Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Drente crowberry heaths
description: Crowberry heaths (unit 31.2272) of the relict wandering dunes of Drente and southern Friesland, with [Empetrum nigrum], [Salix arenaria], [Lophochloa cuspidata], [Pseudoscleropodium purum], [Hylocomium splendens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune [Calluna]-[Genista] heaths
description: Sub-Atlantic [Calluna-Genista] heaths colonizing Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland dunes, other than those of 64.131; their composition can be specified by use of codes of unit 31.22.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune thickets
description: Formations of large shrubs colonizing Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune juniper scrubs
description: [Juniperus communis]-rich scrubs of Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland dunes (unit 31.882).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune mixed thickets
description: Thickets other than juniper scrubs in Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland dune systems; their composition can be specified by use of codes of unit 31.8.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Inland dune woods
description: Natural woods, usually birch-oak or, east of the Elbe, [Pinus sylvestris], installed within Germano-Baltic fluvioglacial inland dune systems. Their composition can be specified by use of codes of 41 or 42.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern river dunes
description: Formations of the immediate vicinity of great rivers within the North Sea-Baltic plain, comprising, besides the communities of 64.11 to 64.15, slightly calcareous grasslands of 34.12 and 34.34.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Breckland inland dunes
description: Remnants of the once vast Breckland inland dune system, of similar glacial origin to that of the continental fluvioglacial dunes of unit 64.1, and like them, colonized by acidophilous grasslands and heaths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Palaeo-coastal dunes
description: Dune cordons marking former, though post-glacial, seashores. They are strongly decalcified and the communities that occupy them are similar to those of continental dunes, though floristically more influenced by the proximity of the sea, and often related to the decalcified inner fringes of the coastal dunes. Subhabitats may be indicated by use of the same codes as in unit 64.1 (replacing the prefix 64.1 by 64.3), specified by those of units 35.2, 31.2, 31.8, 41, 42 or 16.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fluviatile dunes
description: Dunes of the great rivers of middle Europe (Seine, Loire, Saone, upper Rhine, upper Elbe). Like the fluvioglacial dunes of northern Europe, they carry specialized and rare ecosystems. They are much more calcareous than the northern inland dunes and their grasslands (units 34.12, 34.34, [i.a.]) have a substeppic character contrasting with that of neighbouring regions. They are highly vulnerable. A small remnant exists in the Po plain of northern Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lacustrine dunes
description: Unique dunes of the Savoie shore of Lake Geneva (Excenevex).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean inland dunes
description: Inland dunes of the mediterranean climate regions of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhône riverine dunes
description: Fossil dunes of the Camargue, built up by silty alluvial sands of the Rh“ne.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhône dune grasslands
description: Mediterranean tall cane beds and grassland communities of the Camargue inland dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhône dune cane beds
description: Tall cane communities of Camargue dune slacks and dune bases, with [Imperata cylindrica] and [Saccharum ravennae] (unit 53.61).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other Rhône dune grasslands
description: Dry grasslands of the [Malcomietalia] (unit 35.4), [Thero-Brachypodietea] (unit 34.5), [Brachypodietalia phoenicoidis] (unit 34.36) colonizing inland Camargue dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhône dune scrubs
description: Mediterranean scrubs of the Camargue inland dunes. Communities can be indicated by combination with unts of division 32.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rhône dune juniper woodland
description: [Juniperus phoenicea] ssp. [lycia] woodland of the bois des RiŠges in the Camargue.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Iberian inland dunes
description: Fossil dunes of the Coto Do¤ana and other areas of southwestern Iberia. They support very specialized brushes (32.2A) and open grasslands belonging to the [Malcomietalia] (35.4, 16.228).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental inland dunes
description: Inland dunes developed in the middle Eurasian, Irano-Anatolian and Saharo-Mediterranean steppe zones of the Palaearctic domaine, under continental climatic regimes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic inland dunes
description: Inland dunes of the Pannonic plain and of neighbouring basins, northwest to the Marchfeld.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic bare sands
description: Initial stage of renewal of the surface of wandering dunes, devoid or almost devoid of phanerogamic vegetation, in which the bare sand surface is usually covered by a thin film of soil algae and supports the fungus [Psatirella ammophyla].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic dune lichen communities
description: Lichen-dominated earliest stage of the first succession phase of colonisation of Pannonic dunes, with [Cladonia convoluta], [Cladonia furcata], [Cladonia magyarica] and the bryophytes [Syntrichia ruralis], [Tortula spp].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic dune pioneer grasslands
description: Therophyte-dominated later stages of the first succession phase in the colonisation of the Pannonic dunes, characterized by a very thin, low cover of mostly ephemereal, early-blooming annuals of small stature, among which [Bromus mollis], [Bromus tectorum], [Bromus squarrosus], [Medicago minima], [Cerastium brachypetalum], [Erophila verna], [Plantago indica], [Saxifraga tridactylites], [Poa annua], [Poa bulbosa], [Viola kitaibeliana], [Lithospermum arvense], [Corispermum nitidum], [Polygonum arenarium], with a few more perennials such as [Equisetum ramosissimum] var. [altissimum], [Alyssum tortuosum], [Sedum acre], [Cynodon dactylon].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic dune open grasslands
description: More or less open grasslands constituting the second stage of succession in the colonisation of Pannonic dunes, dominated by the perennial grasses [Festuca vaginata], [Stipa capillata], [Stipa borysthenica], [Cleistogenes serotina], [Koeleria glauca], [Koeleria cristata], [Carex liparocarpos], accompanied by [Euphorbia seguierana], [Alkanna tinctoria], [Alyssum montanum] ssp. [gmelinii], [Dianthus serotinus], [Dianthus diutinus], [Gypsophila paniculata], [Scabiosa ochroleuca], [Astragalus austriacus], [Astragalus onobrychis], [Erysimum diffusum], [Fumana procumbens], [Minuartia glomerata], [Minuartia verna]; arid sites on flattened plains are characterized by the abundance of lichens and have [Helechrysum arenarium] and [Kochia laniflora]; thermic slopes and tops of dunes support an open community with the shrub [Fumana procumbens], [Astragalus varius], [Helianthemum nummularium], [Scabiosa ochroleuca]; somewhat water-retentive depressions are characterized by [Scirpus holoschoenus] and [Linum hirsutum] ssp. [glabrescens]; shrub colonisation includes [Juniperus communis], [Berberis vulgaris] and [Salix rosmarinifolia]. Decalcified dune tops and slopes may support more acidophilous formations dominated by [Corynephorus canescens], with [Jasione montana] and [Rumex acetosella] ssp. [tenuifolia], but also with many species of the calcareous sandy grasslands, including [Festuca vaginata] and [Koeleria glauca].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic dune closed grasslands
description: Closed swards of basophilous, humus- and nutrient-rich, sandy or mixed sand-loessy soils of Pannonic fixed dunes, dominated by [Festuca rupicola], [Festuca wagneri], [Festuca pseudovina] or, in some facies, [Chrysopogon gryllus], with [Carex liparocarpos], [Festuca vaginata], [Agropyron cristatum] ssp. [pectinatum], [Achillea ochroleuca], [Astragalus asper], [Astragalus onobrychis], [Astragalus exscapus], [Potentilla cinerea], [Muscari botryoides], [Muscari comosum], [Linum austriacum], [Thymus glabrescens], [Iris variegata], [Iris humilis] ssp. [arenaria], [Colchicum arenarium], [Ophrys sphegodes], [Anacamptis pyramidalis], [Salvia nemorosa], [Alyssum spp.], [Silene parviflora], [Dianthus giganteiformis] ssp. [pontederae], [Lotus spp.], [Onosma arenaria] ssp. [pseudoarenaria].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic dune thickets and scrubs
description: Formations of large shrubs colonizing Pannonic dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic dune woods
description: Natural woods installed within Pannonic dune systems. Their composition can be specified by use of codes of 41.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic plain dune woods
description: Dune woods of the main Pannonic basin and its connected satellites
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intra-Carpathian dune woods
description: Woods of the sands of the border of the former Pannonic sea, along the internal part of the Carpathian bend, formed by [Betula pendula] and [Quercus robur] (unit 41.B37).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic inland dunes
description: Inland dunes of the Pontic plain and of neighbouring basins, including the lower Danube basin of Oltenia and Muntenia and the northern Thracian plain, the northern Black Sea-Sea of Azov plain with the basins of the Dnieper and the Don, northeast to the Volga, east to the Caspian deserts and semideserts, southeast to the pre-Caucasian hills in the basins of the Kouban, the Manytch, the upper Kuma and upper Terek (units 34.921 and 34.923).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic bare sands
description: Initial stage of renewal of the surface of wandering Pontic dunes, devoid or almost devoid of phanerogamic vegetation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dune lichen communities
description: Lichen-dominated earliest stage of the first succession phase of colonisation of Pontic dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dune pioneer grasslands
description: Therophyte-dominated later stages of the first succession phase in the colonisation of Pontic dunes, characterized by a very thin, low cover of mostly ephemereal, early-blooming annuals of small stature. Detailed communities can be indicated by addition of codes identifying subunits of 34.A211.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dune open grasslands
description: More or less open grasslands constituting the second stage of succession in the colonisation of Pontic dunes. Detailed communities can be indicated by addition of codes identifying subunits of 34.A212.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dune closed grasslands
description: Closed swards of basophilous, humus- and nutrient-rich, sandy or mixed sand-loessy soils of Pontic fixed dunes.  Detailed communities can be indicated by addition of codes identifying units 34.A213 or 34.A214.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dune thickets and scrubs
description: Formations of large shrubs colonizing Pontic dunes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pontic dune woods
description: Natural woods installed within Pontic dune systems. Their composition can be specified by use of codes of 41.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sarmatic inland dunes
description: Dunes of the wooded steppe belt occupying, north of the Pontic and Caspian plains, the southern edge and valleys of the Podolian, Central Russian and Volga plateaux east to the Volga-Kama trough (unit 34.922).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Eurasian steppe inland dunes
description: Dunes of the steppe and wooded steppe belts of extreme eastern Europe and western Siberia, extending from the Volga-Kama system in the west to the Tarbagatai and western Altai in the east, including the Transvolgan steppes of Orenburg and Bachkiria, the Kurgan, Ishim, Baraba, Kulunda, Barnaul, Kirgiz, Kazakh steppes, and the mountain steppes of the Tarbagatai and the Altai (unit 34.93).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian steppe inland dunes
description: Dunes of the East Asian steppes (unit 34.94) of Transbaikalia, Outer Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, the Songnen Plain of Northeast China, the western Loess Plateau of North China, the mountain steppes of the Tien Shan, from the rim of the Naryn and Isyk-K”l basins eastwards, of the Sayan and Tannu mountains, in particular, of the steppes of Inner Mongolia and Manchuria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian inland dunes
description: Inland dunes of the Anatolian Plateau, of Transcaucasia, of the Iranian Plateau and of northern Mesopotamia, in the Irano-Anatolian zone of transition between the continental Eurasian steppes and the Mediterranean and southern Palaearctic desert zones, of the eastern cis-Caucasian hills of Daghestan and the Terek basin, the Kopet Dagh, the Pamir-Alai, the extreme western Tien-Shan.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Afro-Mediterranean inland dunes
description: Dunes of the North African Hauts Plateaux.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreal inland dunes
description: Inland dunes of the boreal zone of the Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic inland dunes
description: Inland dunes, unvegetated or colonized by species-poor grassland communities dominated by [Leymus arenarius] or [Festuca cryophila], with [Equisetum boreale], [Silene uniflora], [Silene maritima], [Armeria maritima].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Boreo-lacustrine dunes
description: Lacustrine inland dunes of the northern boreal region, in particular, of Lake Inari in Finland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Far Eastern inland dunes
description: Inland dunes of the nemoral and warm-humid temperate zones of the eastern Palaearctic domaine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Standing stone inland dunes
description: Tertiary sands with upright stones and open psammophytic vegetation of the Varna district of Bulgaria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Caves
description: Natural caves, cave systems, underground waters and subterranean interstitial spaces. Caves and their associated waters (units 65.1-65.7) harbour varied, but paucispecific, communities of animals, fungi and algae that are restricted to them (troglobiont organisms), or are physiologically and ecologically capable of conducting their entire life cycle within them (troglophile organisms), or are dependent on them for part of the life cycle (subtroglophile organisms). Underground waters not associated with caves (stygon, unit 65.8) and interstitial spaces (units 65.9, 65.A) harbour distinctive faunas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont vertebrate caves
description: Caves harbouring communities that include troglobic amphibians or fish, limited worldwide to a very small number of highly distinctive organisms, mostly relict forms of extremely limited distribution, including 15 species of amphibians, limited to North America and Europe, and about 38 species of fishes belonging to 13 families, notably, Cyprinidae, Gobiidae, Bythitidae, Pimelodidae, Characidae, Cobitidae, Amblyopsidae, Clariidae, Ictaluridae, Trichomycteridae, Ophidiidae, Synbranchidae. Palaearctic representatives include a unique amphibian, as well as cyprinids and gobiid fishes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Olm caves
description: Caves of the Adriatic karst system of Italy, Slovenia, Croatia and Montenegro, harbouring the relict amphibian [Proteus anguinus], the most remarkable of all troglobiont vertebrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont fish caves
description: Caves harbouring communities that include troglobic fish, limited in the Palaearctic region to representatives of the Cyprinidae and Gobiidae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont cyprinid caves
description: Caves harbouring communities that include troglobic Cyprinidae, known, in particular, from Iran, Iraq, Oman and from China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Asian troglobiont cyprinid caves
description: Caves of the Near and Middle East harbouring communities that include troglobic Cyprinidae, mostly loaches or garrine fishes, known, in particular, from Iran, Iraq and Oman.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Asian garrine caves
description: Caves of the Near and Middle East harbouring communities that include troglobic garrine fishes, known, in particular, from Iran, Iraq and Oman.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Iranocypris] caves
description: Caves of the Iranian plateau harbouring the Cyprinid [Iranocypris typhlops].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Typhlogarra] caves
description: Caves of the Euphrates basin of Irak harbouring the Cyprinid [Typhlogarra widdowsoni].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Omani garrine caves
description: Caves of Oman harbouring communities that include troglobic garrine fishes of genus [Garra].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: [Caecocypris] caves
description: Caves of Iraq harbouring communities that include the troglobic cyprinid of unknown affinities [Caecocypris].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: West Asian loach caves
description: Caves of the Near and Middle East harbouring communities that include troglobic loaches, known, in particular, from Iran.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Asian troglobiont cyprinid caves
description: Caves of the eastern Palaearctic harbouring communities that include troglobic Cyprinidae, known, in particular, from China, with two species of loaches and one with garrine fishes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont gobiid caves
description: Caves harbouring communities that include troglobic Gobiidae, known from Japan, with two species, [Luciogobius albus] and [Luciogobius pallidus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental subtroglophile vertebrate caves
description: Caves of the main Eurasian and African landmasses essential to parts of the life-cycle of vertebrate subtroglophiles (elective periodic trogloxenes).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental subtroglophile herpeta caves
description: Caves of the main Eurasian and African landmasses providing an essential habitat of reptilian and amphibian subtroglophiles (elective periodic trogloxenes).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italo-French [Speleomantes] caves
description: Caves harbouring the salamanders [Speleomantes] ([Hydromantes]), [Speleomantes ambrosii] and [Speleomantes italicus] of southeastern France and northern and central Italy.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Alpine [Speleomantes] caves
description: Caves harbouring the salamander [Speleomantes ambrosii] ([Hydromantes ambrosii]) of southeastern France and northern Italy, with several races of extremely local distribution, in particular, in the Ligurian Alps, the Maritime alps, the Provence Alpes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Apennine [Speleomantes] caves
description: Caves harbouring the salamander [Speleomantes italicus] ([Speleomantes]  = [Hydromantes]) of northern and central Italy, with two races of local distribution in the Apuan Alps, the Modenan, Emilian, Toscan, Umbrian, Marchesian Apennines.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Reptile caves
description: Caves of the main Eurasian and African landmasses providing an essential habitat of reptilian subtroglophiles (elective periodic trogloxenes), in particular, geckos or snakes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental bat caves
description: Caves of the Eurasian and North African landmasses, under normally oxygenated, buffered microclimates, generally large and crossed by watercourses or excavated near epigean watercourses, with permanent or temporary colonies of bats, in majority belonging to the Vespertilionidae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Insular subtroglophile vertebrate caves
description: Caves of the islands of Eurasia and North Africa essential to parts of the life-cycle of vertebrate subtroglophiles (elective periodic trogloxenes).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Insular subtroglophile herpeta caves
description: Caves on islands off the main Eurasian and African landmasses providing an essential habitat of reptilian and amphibian subtroglophiles (elective periodic trogloxenes).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sardinian salamander caves
description: Caves of the calcareous massifs of Sardinia harbouring salamanders of the genus [Speleomantes] ([Hydromantes]) and constituting an essential habitat for their existence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Iglesiente salamander caves
description: Caves of the Sulcis and the Iglesiente of southwestern Sardinia, notably in the Domusnovas area of the Fiuminese massif, harbouring [Speleomantes genei].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Imperial salamander caves
description: Caves of the Gerrei and of the Salto di Quirra in the southeastern quadrant of Sardinia, harbouring [Speleomantes imperialis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Monte Albo salamander caves
description: Caves of the Monte Albo massif of eastern Sardinia, harbouring [Speleomantes flavus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Supramonte salamander caves
description: Caves of the massifs facing the Gulf of Orosei, notably of the Orosei, Dorgali, Oliena, Orgosolo, Baunei areas of eastern Sardinia, harbouring [Speleomantes supramontis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ryukyu gecko caves
description: Caves of the Ryukyu archipelago harbouring [Gymnodactylus yamashinae] or [Eublapheris splendens].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Insular bat caves
description: Caves of the islands of Eurasia and North Africa with permanent or temporary colonies of bats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont invertebrate caves
description: Caves harbouring communities that include no troglobiont amphibians or fish, but include troglobiont invertebrates, limited worldwide to a relatively small number of species belonging to a limited number of groups, and including remarkable relict species. In the Palaearctic region, the majority are situated in the northern Mediterranean basin and the peri-Pontic region. Gastropoda, Opiliones, Chilopoda (Lithobiidae), Collembol, Coleoptera (Bathysciinae and Trechinae subfamilies) among the terrestrial faunas, Turbellaria, Gastropoda and Urodela, among the aquatic faunas, are characteristic of their communities, and essentially restricted to caves of temperate regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont invertebrate temperate caves
description: Caves under normally oxygenated, buffered microclimates, dry, humidified by seeps or crossed by permanent or temporary watercourses, but not retaining glaciers, and harbouring communities of troglobiont invertebrates, often including remarkable relict species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont invertebrate ice caves
description: Caves under normally oxygenated, buffered microclimates, harbouring communities of troglobiont invertebrates, and in which past and present conditions permit the retention of glaciers; they are rare, known in particular from the Carpathians of Romania and Slovakia, the Alps and the Jura.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont invertebrate hydrothermal caves
description: Caves under normally oxygenated, buffered microclimates, warmed and humidified by geothermal waters, and harbouring communities of troglobiont invertebrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglobiont invertebrate sulphur caves
description: Deoxygenated, relatively warm caves, with atmospheres rich in carbon dioxide and sulphur vapour or methane and hydrogen sulfide, harbouring relict thermophile faunas of highly distinctive troglobiont and stygobiont invertebrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hydro-thermal sulphur caves
description: Caves harbouring ecosystems linked to sulphurous geothermal waters in a  relatively warm, deoxygenated methane- and hydrogen sulfide-rich atmosphere.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dobrogean hydro-thermal sulphur caves
description: Movile cave of the southern Romanian Dobrogea, harbouring a singular chemoautotrophically based ecosystem linked to sulphurous geothermal waters in a quasi-closed, relatively warm (20øC), deoxygenated methane- and hydrogen sulfide-rich atmosphere, comprising a unique, totally isolated, thermophile and thiophile relict fauna of highly distinctive troglobiont and stygobiont invertebrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Illyro-Pannonic hydro-thermal sulphur caves
description: Hydrothermal sulphur caves of Hungary, Croatia and Slovenia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Vapourthermal sulphur caves
description: Adam cave from Baile Herculane, Romania, relatively warm, deoxygenated, with very much carbon dioxide, partly influenced by sulphur vapours, harbouring a  relict thermophile fauna; a very rich trophic substratum (guano) is present.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Troglophile invertebrate caves
description: Caves harbouring communities that include no troglobiont organisms, but include troglophile invertebrates. Generally, they are caves crossed by watercourses or with rich trophic substratum, excavated in limestone afforested zones.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subtroglophile invertebrate caves
description: Caves essential to parts of the life-cycle (quiescence period) of invertebrate subtroglophiles (elective periodic trogloxenes), such as Lepidoptera, Diptera, Hymenoptera, Coleoptera; in general they are stably cool (or warm) and humid caves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atroglozoocoenotic caves
description: Caves, often small and dry, devoid of significant troglobiont or troglophile zoocoenoses, and not harbouring significant subtroglophiles.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Stygal biocenoses
description: Communities harboured by ground waters (stygon), not including those of cave waters. They are constituted by mostly small, elongated forms, in Europe principally bacteria, protozoans, turbellarians, rotifers, nematodes, copepods and amphipods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Anchihaline biocoenoses
description: Communities occupying anchialine (or anchihaline) habitats, underground bodies of more or less saline water, usually with a restricted exposure to open air, always with more or less extensive subterranean connections to the sea. They  show noticeable marine as well as terrestrial influences. They are varied, located within either volcanic or limestone bedrock. Distinctive communities of anchialine stygobionts, mostly crustaceans, have been discovered, in particular, in Italy, the western Balkan peninsula, the Sinai peninsula, the Canary Islands, the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Interstitial phreatic biocenoses
description: Communities of stygobiont invertebrates and vertebrates, highly distinctive, occupying eustygal habitats, interstitial water saturating porous sediments below the water table.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hyporheic interstitial biocenoses
description: Rhythrostygal (potamostygal) communities of stygobiont organisms, mostly fresh-water mites and small crustaceans, occupying interstitial water in sand and gravel sediments accompanying running water courses.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subterranean interstitial biocenoses
description: Communities occupying the compartment of the subterranean ecosystem in direct contact with the lower horizon of the soil, at a depth ranging from a few centimeters to a few meters, in the interconnected microspaces of the colluvions or the fissures of the superficial zones of the bedrock. Distinctive interstitial assemblies of troglobiont invertebrates, comprising coleoptera, myriapods, isopods, spiders, pseudoscorpions, have been described from the Pyrenees, the Alps, the Carpathians, the Canary Islands, the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Volcanic features
description: Hard rock surfaces, rock jumbles, loose material deposits, soils, water bodies resulting from recent or present volcanic activity, unvegetated, occupied by lichens or mosses, or colonized by specialized, relatively sparse herb- or shrub-dominated communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Orocanarian summital communities
description: Summital zone of the Teide volcano of Tenerife, above (2700) 3000 metres, colonized by very open communities of [Viola cheiranthifolia], [Silene nocteolens] and [Argyranthemum teneriffae].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Orovolcanic summital communities
description: Summital zone of very high volcanoes of the Eurasian land mass and its nearshore islands, in particular, of Mount Etna, above the level of hedgehog heaths, of the high volcanoes of western Asia and of those of the Far East.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Etna orovolcanic communities
description: Summital zone of Mount Etna, above the level of hedgehog heaths, between 2500 metres and the summit, where a very dispersed pioneer community is formed by endemics, notably [Rumex aetnensis], [Senecio aetnensis], [Anthemis aetnensis], [Hypochoeris robertia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian orovolcanic communities
description: Summital zone of very high volcanoes of western Asia, in particular, of Nemrut Dag in eastern Turkey, Damavand in northern Iran, Taftan in southern Iran, with [Polygonum radicosum], [Crepis demavendi], [Artemisia melanolipis], [Carex pseudofoetida].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific orovolcanic communities
description: Summital zone of very high volcanoes of the Far East, in particular, alpine communities of Mount Fuji-Yama, with, between about 2700 and 3450 metres, [Polygonum weyrichii] var. [alpinum], [Arabis serrata], [Artemisia pedunculosa], [Stellaria niponica], [Salix renii], [Carex stenantha], [Cassiope lycopodioides], and, between 3450 metres and the summit at 3776 metres, moss and lichen communities formed by [Rhacomitrium microcarpum], [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum], [Dicranum fuscescens], [Dicranum rugosum], [Stereocaulon vesubianum], [Rhizocarpon geographicum], [Alectoria lata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lava flows, lava fields, lava features
description: Hard or porous rocky surfaces and chaotic rock jumbles formed by solidified lava flows originating from volcanoes and fissures of the Palaearctic domaine, unvegetated, occupied by lichens or mosses, or colonized by specialized, relatively sparse herb- or shrub-dominated communities. They are restricted to the Mid-Atlantic ridge and its associated fracture zones, in Iceland and the Macaronesian islands, responsible for a large proportion of the volume of recent lava in the world, to the collision zones and constructive margins of southern Eurasia, in the Mediterranean and Tethyan basins along the folds of the Alpine system, to the Red Sea rim, on the Arabian peninsula, and to the western Pacific rim and island arcs. A range of surface characteristics is presented by lava of differing composition, viscosity and gas content, including pahoehoe or ropy lava, aa, scoria, pumice and pillow lava. A gradient of increasing acidity and viscosity extends from basalts through andesites and dacites to rhyolites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lava flows
description: Pleistocene lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of Iceland, concentrated in the neovolcanic zones that stretch along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge from northeast Iceland to the Reykjanes peninsula, branch south of it to the Vestmann Islands, and occupy the Snaefell peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Barren Icelandic lava flows
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of Iceland devoid of vegetation or sparsely vegetated by algae, lichens and mosses, which constitute the first stage of colonisation, with covers of up to 20-40%. The main constituents of the vegetation are the lichens [Stereocaulon vesubianum], [Stereocaulon alpinum], [Stereocaulon arcticum], [Alectoria ochroleuca], [Cladonia pyxidata], [Lecidea spp.], [Lecanora spp.] and the mosses [Grimnia spp.], [Andreaea rupestris], [Andreaea obovata], [Rhacomitrium canescans], [Polytrichum spp.] accompanied by a very few vascular plants, including [Festuca richardsonii], [Thymus praecox] ssp [arcticus], [Poa subcaerulea].
