source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lava flow moss heaths
description: Lava flows and lava fields of Iceland covered by continuous carpets of [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] (unit 36.3223 [p.]), forming thick mantles that cover very large surfaces over all parts of the relief, engulfing asperities, bridging gaps, draping protruding rocks with large cushions, or else, in less evolved complexes, forming preferentially in the depressions and concavities where some organic matter accumulates. Together with similar formations of the basaltic uplands (unit 62.331 x 36.3223), these moss heaths constitute a particularly original landscape of Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lava flow heaths and scrubs
description: Heaths, scrubs or low birch woods colonizing parts of lava flows and lava fields of Iceland, mostly in hollows where loess accumulates, within the [Rhacomitrium lanuginosum] carpets of unit 66.312. [Empetrum spp.], [Arctostaphylos uva-ursi], [Vaccinium uliginosum], [Betula nana] are the main heath components. At a later stage, [Betula pubescens] ssp. [czerepanovii] may invade and form scrubs and thickets. Subdivisions of division 3, in particular, of units 31.2113 and 31.4551, and of unit 41.B71, may be used in conjunction with unit 66.313 to describe the formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lava flow fissure communities
description: Communities colonizing fissures, cracks, overhangs and cave entrances formed in lava flows and lava fields of Iceland, and on the faces of dykes, stacks and other surfaces protruding from them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lava fissure bryophyte communities
description: Bryophyte-dominated communities colonizing fissures or cavities  of lava flows and lava fields of Iceland, in particular, sciaphile communities of [Distichium capillaceum], [Pohlia cruda], [Mnium marginatum], [Timmia austriaca], [Bartramia ityphylla], [Mnium stellare], [Plagiothecium roeseanum] and [Cystopteris fragilis] characteristic of loess-collecting lava vesicular cavities and of shady ledges.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lava fissure herb communities
description: Sparse vascular plant communities colonizing fissures and cracks of lava flows and lava fields of Iceland, and the faces of dykes, stacks and other surfaces protruding from them. Codes of division 62, in particular, of units 62.1C and 62.2A can be combined with unit 66.314 to further define the community.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian lava flows
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the Azores, the Canary Islands and the Cape Verde Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Barren Macaronesian lava flows
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the Azores, the Canary Islands and the Cape Verde Islands, unvegetated, occupied by usually discontinuous communities dominated by algae, lichens or mosses, sometimes colonized by very sparse vascular plants. Barren lava fields of Fuerteventura, Lobos and Lanzarote are the main habitat of the endemic and vulnerable Canary Shrew, [Crocidura canariensis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian lava flow scrubs and woods
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the Azores, the Canary Islands and the Cape Verde Islands, occupied by open or closed communities dominated by herbs, shrubs or trees, in particular, of units 31.7F, 31.31, 31.846, 32.8, 42.9, 42.A8, 45. Codes of these units can be combined with 66.322 to define habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian lava flow fissure communities
description: Rich and diverse fissure, crack and overhang communities colonizing lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the volcanoes of the Azores, the Canary Islands and the Cape Verde Islands. Codes of unit 62.6 can be combined with 66.323 to further define the community.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan lava flows
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the volcanoes of the Mediterranean Basin and of western Asia, including Etna, Vesuvius, the Phlegrean Fields, Ischia, the Lipari Islands, Pantelleria, the Aegean archipelago, Nemrut Dag in eastern Turkey, Damavand in northern Iran, Taftan in southern Iran, the volcanoes of Syria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Barren Tethyan lava flows
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the volcanoes of the Mediterranean Basin and of western Asia, unvegetated, occupied by usually discontinuous communities dominated by algae, lichens, notably [Stereocaulon vesubianum], or mosses, sometimes colonized by very sparse vascular plants.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan lava flow scrubs and woods
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the volcanoes of the Mediterranean Basin and of western Asia, occupied by open or closed communities dominated by herbs, shrubs or trees, in particular, of units 31.7, 31.845, 32, 34, 35, 36, 41.B6, 42. Codes of these units can be combined with 66.332 to define habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan lava flow fissure communities
description: Fissure, crack and overhang communities colonizing lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of the volcanoes of the Mediterranean Basin and of western Asia. Codes of unit 62 can be combined with 66.333 to further define the community.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Red Sea lava flows
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of volcanoes of the Red Sea rim, situated, within the Palaearctic region as here defined, in the region of Medina and near the southwestern extremity of the Arabian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific lava flows
description: Lava flows, fields, dykes, necks, domes, cones of volcanoes of the western rim of the Pacific Basin and its associated island arcs, situated, in particular, in Kamtchatka, the Kuriles, Japan, the Ryu-Kyu Islands, Manchuria and eastern Siberia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Volcanic ash and lapilli fields
description: Exposed deposits of pyroclastic rocks, fragmental volcanic material blown into the atmosphere by explosive activity, including ash, lapilli, bombs, pel‚es hair, or of detritic pumice and scoriae, together with the pioneer assemblies of specialized species that may colonize them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic ash and lapilli fields
description: Exposed deposits of pyroclastic rocks, including ash, lapilli, bombs, pel‚es hair, pumice and scoriae, of Iceland, together with the pioneer assemblies of specialized species that may colonize them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian ash and lapilli fields
description: Exposed deposits of pyroclastic rocks, including ash, lapilli, bombs, pel‚es hair, pumice and scoriae, of the Azores, the Canary Islands and the Cape Verde Islands, together with the pioneer assemblies of specialized species that may colonize them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan ash and lapilli fields
description: Exposed deposits of pyroclastic rocks, including ash, lapilli, bombs, pel‚es hair, pumice and scoriae, of the Mediterranean Basin and of western Asia, including Etna, Vesuvius, the Phlegrean Fields, Ischia, the Lipari Islands, Pantelleria, the Aegean archipelago, Nemrut Dag in eastern Turkey, Damavand in northern Iran, Taftan in southern Iran, the volcanoes of Syria, together with the pioneer assemblies of specialized species that may colonize them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Red Sea ash and lapilli fields
description: Exposed deposits of pyroclastic rocks, including ash, lapilli, bombs, pel‚es hair, pumice and scoriae, of the Red Sea rim, situated, within the Palaearctic region as here defined, in the region of Medina and near the southwestern extremity of the Arabian peninsula, together with the pioneer assemblies of specialized species that may colonize them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific ash and lapilli fields
description: Exposed deposits of pyroclastic rocks, including ash, lapilli, bombs, pel‚es hair, pumice and scoriae, of the western rim of the Pacific Basin and its associated island arcs, situated, in particular, in Kamtchatka, the Kuriles, Japan, the Ryu-Kyu Islands, Manchuria and eastern Siberia, together with the pioneer assemblies of specialized species that may colonize them.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Lava tubes
description: Caves formed in lava flows by open-ended tubes or passages resulting from the cooling of the surface whose moulten interior continued to flow. They may be colonized by anchihaline communities of unit 65.81.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic lava tubes
description: Lava tubes of Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian lava tubes
description: Lava tubes of of the Azores, the Canary Islands and the Cape Verde Islands. The very large tube created by the volcano La Corona of Lanzarote harbours unique communities of invertebrates, in particular, the decapode crustacean [Munidopsis polymorpha], endemic to that locality, and several crustaceans of the genus [Speleonectes].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tethyan lava tubes
description: Lava tubes of the Mediterranean Basin and of western Asia, including Etna, Vesuvius, the Phlegrean Fields, Ischia, the Lipari Islands, Pantelleria, the Aegean archipelago, Nemrut Dag in eastern Turkey, Damavand in northern Iran, Taftan in southern Iran, the volcanoes of Syria.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fumaroles, solfataras and mofettes
description: Orifices in volcanic areas emitting hot or cold gases and vapours. Their very extreme environment is colonized by paucispecific but highly distinct communities. Included are steam vents (fumaroles), vapour and hot sulphurous gas vents (solfatares), paint pots, porridge pots and mud volcanoes, as well as cold carbon dioxide, methane and nitrogen vents (mofettes), that emit directly into the open atmosphere; marine and subterraneous vents have been included in units 11 and 65, respectively.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Italian fumaroles
description: Fumaroles of the major area of active volcanism of the western Mediterranean basins, located on the Italian peninsula and its small islands, in particular those of Isola d'Ischia, with communities that include [Cyperus polystachyos]; other gas vent manifestations of the same region of volcanism are listed in the next two sections.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sicilian fumaroles
description: Fumaroles of Sicily and its nearshore islands, in particular of Mount Etna and the Lipari islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pantelleria fumaroles
description: Fumaroles of Pantelleria. Their walls, mouth  and immediate vicinity are colonized by a succession of microvegetation composed of bryophytes, ferns and a few angiosperms.  Constituting plants include the endemic moss [Calymperes sommieri], sole Mediterranean representative of a tropical genus, as well as [Radiola linoides], [Kickxia cirrhosa], [Trifolium angustifolium], [Centaurium maritimum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian fumaroles
description: Fumaroles of the Canary Islands and the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canarian fumaroles, solfataras and mofettes
description: Fumaroles of the Canary Islands and the communities that depend on the warm-humid microclimate they generate, in particular, communities of the summital zone of Teide comprising the endemic [Gnaphalium teydeum] and bryophytes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Azorean fumaroles and solfataras
description: Fumaroles of the Azores.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic solfataras
description: Fumaroles and solfataras of Iceland, surrounded by very sparse communities on warm, acid and clayey soils under a humid, warm microclimate, comprising Cyanophycea carpets in the immediate vicinity of the vent, hepatica belts farther out, first of the small [Riccia bifurca] and [Fossombronia dumortieri], then of the more robust [Preissia quadrata], finally, vascular plant assemblies in which [Ophioglossum azoricum], [Sagina procumbens], [Plantago major] var. [pygmaea] are prominent. Vast expanses of sulfur-poisoned ground in the general vicinity of the solfataras are almost devoid of vegetation, with a few vascular plants in less poisoned areas, in particular, [Achillea millefolium].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: East Mediterranean fumaroles and solfataras
description: Fumaroles and solfataras of the areas of active volcanism of the eastern Mediterranean basins, in particular, of the Aegean and the Levantine Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine fumaroles, solfataras and mofettes
description: Gas vents, fumaroles, solfataras, mofettes, related to late Tertiary volcanism of the western Alpine system, its periphery, its satellite mountain complexes and its interior basins, including the Pyrenees, the Alps, the Carpathians, and, notably, the Eastern Carpathians, the Jura, the Dinarides, the Hellenides, the Hercynian ranges, the Iberian mountains, the Atlas, the Taurus.  Included in particular are the extensive mofette systems of Bohemia and of the mountains constituting the Bohemian Quadrangle, in particular, those of the bogs of Soos, in the Cheb district of western Bohemia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Asian fumaroles and solfataras
description: Gas vents, fumaroles, solfataras, mofettes of the Caucasus and of western Asian mountains and plateaux, in particular, of the slopes of the Nemrut Dag in Turkey and of the Damavand and Taftan in Iran.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian fumaroles and solfataras
description: Gas vents, fumaroles, solfataras, mofettes of the the Central Asian mountains and their periphery.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Riftian fumaroles and solfataras
description: Gas vents, fumaroles, solfataras, mofettes related to active volcanism of the Rift, along the Arabian peninsula shores of the Red Sea and in neighbouring regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific fumaroles and solfataras
description: Hot or cold gas vents of the zones of volcanic activity lining the Pacific margins of Eurasia, in particular, of the Jigokudani volcanic site on Hokkaido.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharan fumaroles and solfataras
description: Gas vents, fumaroles, solfataras, mofettes of the North African desert ranges and their periphery.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Thermal springs
description: Acid or alkaline springs heated by geothermal energy, located in regions of present or past volcanic activity, producing a continuous flow of water at temperatures significantly above the air temperature. Springs and tepid pools at temperatures below 50ø C may host a few species of specialized animals, those at temperatures between 50ø C and 75ø C harbour bluegreen algae that may form conspicuous mats, those at temperatures above 75ø C are inhabited only by heterotrophic bacteria; the  margins of the springs and the water-saturated substrates may host distinctive biotic communities, including superior plants.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mediterranean thermal springs
description: Hot springs related to active volcanism of the islands, coasts and hinterland of the Mediterranean basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Mediterranean thermal springs
description: Hot springs of the islands, coasts and hinterland of the areas of active volcanism of the western Mediterranean basins, in particular, of the Tyrrhenian Sea and of the Strait of Sicily.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Mediterranean thermal springs
description: Hot springs of the islands, coasts and hinterland of the areas of active volcanism of the eastern Mediterranean basins, in particular, of the Aegean and the Levantine Sea.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Macaronesian thermal springs
description: Hot springs related to active volcanism of the southern north Atlantic, on the mid-Atlantic ridge islands of the Azores and on the Canary Islands, Madeira and the Cape Verde Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic thermal springs
description: Hot springs related to active volcanism of the northern North Atlantic, on the mid-Atlantic ridge islands, Iceland and Jan Mayen.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic thermal spring waters
description: Warm outflow water of Icelandic hot springs, often extremely basic, with a pH approaching 8-9, mostly devoid of macrophytic vegetation at temperatures above 35ø C, otherwise with species assemblies that vary with water temperature and conditions at each site, including altitude. Characteristic species include [Crassula aquatica], [Hydrocotyle vulgaris] and [Callitriche stagnatilis].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic thermal spring hot soil communities
description: Moss and vascular plants communities occurring on warm and moist soils around Icelandic hot springs. Soaked, very hot substrates nearest to the spring are colonized by Cyanophycea, small hepatics, in particular, [Fossombronia dumortieri] and a moss of genus [Archidium]; a more external belt is often characterized by the exuberant development of sphagna, while hypnoids develop beyond. Generally, bryophytes tolerate soil temperatures up to 50ø C, while vascular plants occur at lower temperatures. Vascular species assemblies are highly varied, depending on altitude and ground temperature, and comprise species limited in Iceland to these hot soil situations, in particular, [Filaginella uliginosa] ([Gnaphalium uliginosum]), [Hydrocotyle vulgaris], [Mentha aquatica], [Polygonum persicaria] ([Persicaria maculosa]), [Plantago major] var. [pygmaea], [Blechnum spicant] var. [fallax], [Ophioglossum azoricum].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Alpine thermal springs
description: Hot springs related to late Tertiary volcanism of the western Alpine system, its periphery, its satellite mountain complexes and its interior basins, including the Baetic mountains, the Rif, the Tell, the Atlas, the Pyreneo-Cantabrian range, the Alps, the Carpathians, the mountains of the Balkan peninsula, the Jura, the Hercynian ranges of Iberia, the Central Massif, the northern Hercynian arc. They include, in particular, Romanian geothermal waters harbouring formations of [Nymphaea lotus] (unit 22.43113).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Peri-Caucasian hot springs
description: Hot springs related to late Tertiary volcanism of the central Alpine system,  its periphery, its satellite mountain complexes and its interior basins, including the Caucasus, the Pontic range, the Anatolian plateau, the Taurus, the Zagros, the Elburz.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian thermal springs
description: Hot springs related to late Tertiary volcanism of the eastern Alpine system,  its periphery, its satellite mountain complexes and its interior basins, including the Himalayas and the connected ranges of the Pamir-Alai, the Tien Shan and the Hindu Kush.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Riftian thermal springs
description: Hot springs related to active volcanism of the Rift, along the shores of the Red Sea, the Jordan Valley and in neighbouring regions, in particular, springs of the shores of the Sea of Galilee.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific thermal springs
description: Hot springs of the zone of active volcanism of the Pacific ring of fire in Kamchatka, the Japanese archipelago and neighbouring areas of far-eastern Asia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharan thermal springs
description: Hot springs related to past or present volcanism of Saharan Africa.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Geysers
description: Springs from which heated water and steam is ejected, sometimes violently, at periodic intervals, in active or recently active volcanic regions. Major geysers are rare, known from only four areas in the world, and within the Palaearctic region, as here defined, only from Iceland and the northwestern Pacific rim. The proximal zone of geysers may host distinctive communities of lower plants and invertebrates.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Icelandic geysers
description: Geysers of Iceland, of which about 10 are presently active, in particular, in southern Iceland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pacific geysers
description: Geysers of the zone of volcanic activity riming the Pacific margins of Eurasia, including, for example, those of the Valley of the Geysers, Kamtchatka and of the Jigokudani volcanic site on Hokkaido.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Deserts
description: Unvegetated or sparsely vegetated formations of geographically significant extent, developed under arctic, temperate or tropical climates in extreme conditions of low precipitation and high evaporation. Included are all shrub-dominated, grass-dominated or succulent-dominated communities exposed to arid or very arid conditions, typically with annual precipitation inferior to 200 mm, and, as semideserts, shrub-dominated or succulent-dominated, including arborescent succulent-dominated, communities, usually strongly lacunar, formed under semiarid conditions, with annual precipitation that may reach 500 mm or 600 mm. Grass-dominated communities constituted under the latter conditions and representing encroachments of steppes characteristic of neighbouring regions are listed under 3, while all communities that comprise a reasonably continuous, closed or open, stratum of trees, other than arborescent succulents, are listed under 4, most often under 4B. Communities dependent on permanent or temporary surface water are excluded and listed in units 15, 2, 3 or 5; nonarborescent communities dependent on phreatic water are included in unit 7.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Polar deserts
description: Formations of the most extreme parts of the Arctic zone, characterized by mostly bare ground worked by solifluction and colonized by algae and very species-poor, extremely open communities constituded by lichens, mosses, liverworts and a very restricted number of vascular plants. They are restricted within the Palaearctic as here defined, to the northern tip of the Ta‹myr peninsula, to Greenland and to the islands of the Arctic Ocean.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Barents polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the Nordaustlandet of the Spitzbergen archipelago, Victoria Island, Franz Josef Land and the north end of Novaya Zemlya.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Spitzbergen polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the Nordaustlandet of the Spitzbergen archipelago.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Victoria polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the small ice-free part of Victoria Island, with an impoverished vegetation comprising a few species of mosses, lichens and ground-covering algae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern Franz Josef polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the northern part of the Franz Josef archipelago.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Unvegetated Franz Josef polar deserts
description: Stone fields, rock heaps and sandy-loamy deluviums of the Franz Josef archipelago devoid of all vegetation, mostly characteristic of areas with prolonged snow cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Open aggregation Franz Josef polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the Franz Josef archipelago occupied by uniform, species-poor assemblages of widely scattered higher and lower plants, constituting a negligible ground cover.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Nanocomplex Franz Josef polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the Franz Josef archipelago occupied by a continuous cover of higher and lower plants, broken by bare stones and patches of bare ground.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern Franz Josef polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the southern part of the Franz Josef archipelago.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Novaya Zemlya polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the north end of Novaya Zemlya.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the North Land Archipelago (Severnaya Zemlya), the extreme northern tip of the Taimyr peninsula and the de Longa Islands, north of the New Siberian Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern North Land polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of ice-free areas of the very glaciated northern islands of the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago, including Ostrov Komsomolets, Ostrov Pioner and the Ostrova Sedova.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern North Land polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the southern islands of the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago, including Ostrov Oktyabr'skoy, Ostrov Revolyutsii, Ostrov Bol'shevik, Ostrov Malyy Ta‹myr, Ostrov Starokadomskogo, less glaciated than the northern islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Taimyr polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the extreme northern tip of the Taimyr peninsula (Mys Chelyuskin).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: New Siberian polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the three islands of the Ostrova de Longa group (De Long Islands), north of the New Siberian Islands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Canadian polar deserts
description: Polar deserts of the Lincoln Sea coasts of extreme northern Greenland.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Continental cool deserts and semideserts
description: Interior continental deserts or semideserts of temperate areas beyond the reach of moisture-laden winds ("d‚serts d'‚loignement") and rain-shadow deserts or semideserts lying on the leeward side of high mountain ranges which intercept the rain-bearing winds ("d‚serts d'abri"). In the Palaearctic region they are represented by the deserts and semideserts of the Central Eurasian desert region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Aralo-Caspian cool deserts and semideserts
description: Interior continental deserts or semideserts of the Caspian lowlands, the northern Aralo-Caspian depression and Dzungaria, the Atrek basin, the Ustyurt Plateau, the Kyzyl-Kum and Kara-Kum, the Kopet Dag, the Central Asian mountains of the Tien-Shan system.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Afghan cool deserts and semideserts
description: Interior continental deserts or semideserts of the Iranian and Afghan plateaux, south of the Kopet Dag and the Pamir.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Central Asian cool deserts and semideserts
description: Interior continental deserts or semideserts of Mongolia, inner Mongolia and the Cis-Hsing-An region, including the Gobi, of the Pei Shan, of Kashgaria and the Tarim Basin with the Takla Makan, of the Ala Shan and the Ordos, of the Kansu corridor and the Tsaidam region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pamiro-Tibetan cool deserts and semideserts
description: High-altitude interior continental deserts or semideserts of the Pamir and the Tibetan plateau.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hot deserts and semideserts
description: Sunny deserts and arid shrublands developed under tropical or subtropical climates. Most characteristically and extensively, they are situated within the horse latitudes, the 30ø-35ø belts of high atmospheric pressure zones or Hadley cells producing low precipitation and high insolation. Under anomalous local conditions of rain shadow or trade wind regimes, arid shrublands or succulent and arborescent succulent communities may form in other parts of the tropics. They are physiognomically similar to the horse latitude semideserts and are included in this unit. In the Palaearctic region, this unit encompasses the extremely extensive horse-latitude Saharo-Sindian deserts and their semidesert transition to mediterranean habitats or other formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian deserts and semideserts
description: Hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, within the Saharo-Arabian floristic domaine; they include most of the Sahara Desert, the Sinai Desert, the Neguev, the Arabian Desert and the Southern Mesopotamian Desert.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian sand deserts and semideserts
description: Sand-covered hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, covering more than one-third of the surface of the western Sahara, a somewhat smaller portion of the eastern Sahara, huge expanses of the Arabian Desert, in particular, in the Rub'l Khali and the Nafud-Dahna, and substantial surfaces in the northern part and in the intermountain valleys and plains of the Sinai peninsula and in the northern Neguev. They include desert dunes as well as sandy regs and may be unvegetated, especially in the hyperarid zone or carry vegetation of greatly variable development. The communities of the sandy floors of wadis are excluded and listed in unit 73.14.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian ergs and barkhans
description: Species-poor communities of ergs and barkans of the Saharo-Sindian region, including less mobile dunes harbouring communities of graminids and shrubs with roots able to penetrate deeper, moisture retaing layers of sand, or rare communities of annuals, as well as highly mobile, constantly shifting, sands devoid of any vegetation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian erg and barkhan grass communities
description: Species-poor communities of ergs and barkhans of the Saharo-Sindian region dominated by gramino‹d species, especially drinn, [Aristida pungens] ([Stipagrostis pungens]), sometimes with [Cyperus conglomeratus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian erg and barkhan shrub communities
description: Shrub-dominated communities of dunes of the Saharo-Sindian region variously composed of, in particular, [Ephedra alata], [Retama retam], [Genista saharae], [Calligonum azel], the chenopod shrub [Cornulaca monacantha], sometimes with herbaceous plants, including [Cyperus conglomeratus], [Aristida pungens], or small shrubs, such as the borage [Moltkia ciliata].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian unvegetated ergs and barkhans
description: Large unvegetated ergs or barkhans of the Saharo-Arabian desert zone, prominent in areas where rainfall is very low, less than 20 mm per year, and episodic, with many consecutive rainless years, occupying extensive surfaces, in particular, in the eastern Sahara.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian erg and barkhan annual flushes
description: Ephemeral communities of dunes of the Saharo-Sindian region formed of annuals, such as [Malcolmia aegyptiaca], appearing after bouts of precipitation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian sandy regs
description: Communities of sandy regs, sandy areas protected from erosion by a cover of superficial slightly larger rock fragments, of the Saharo-Sindian region, particularly frequent in areas of hyperaridity, subject to episodic rains, with as little as 10-20 mm being sufficient to provoke the development of a flush of ephemeral vegetation; communities are homogeneous, comprised almost exclusively of therophyte species, including [Athenatherum forscalii] ([Danthonia]), [Plantago ciliata], [Polycarpaea repens] ([Polycarpaea fragilis]), [Monsonia nivea], [Ifloga spicata], [Fagonia glutimosa].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian regs
description: Gravel-covered hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, constituted of heterogeneous deposits of, in particular, coarse alluvions or conglomarates, from which fine material has been removed by wind action; beneath the often compacted suface a powdery mass of gypsum accumulates and may form a strong hardpan at somewhat greater depths.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian reg communities
description: Diffuse communities of gravel-covered hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula formed by shrubs, in particular, [Hammada scoparia] ([Haloxylon articulatum]) [Cornulaca monacantha], [Randonia africana], [Hammada elegans] ([Haloxylon salicornicum]), grasses, notably [Stipagrostis plumosa], [Stipagrostis obtusa], [Stipagrostis ciliata], [Lasiurus hirsutus], [Panicum turgidum], geophytes, [Androcymbium spp.], [Asphodelus], or annuals, [Daucus spp.], [Ammodaucus spp.].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian bare reg communities
description: Diffuse communities of gravel-covered hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula formed by shrubs, in particular, in the northern Sahara, the chenopod [Haloxylon scoparium], often degraded as a result of fuel-gathering. [Stipagrostis obrtusa] may form after rains on regs, notably of the Central Sahara.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian reg sand-cover communities
description: Regs covered by sands of variable depths, of hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, capabable of supporting communities, often with a denser cover than the bare regs of unit 73.1211, that may include grasses, notably swards of [Stipagrostis plumosa], [Stipagrostis obtusa], [Stipagrostis ciliata], geophytes, [Androcymbium spp.], [Asphodelus], and annuals, [Daucus spp.], [Ammodaucus spp.]; clay-rich sand covers may support shrub communites of the chenopod [Cornulaca monacantha] or the Resedaceae [Randonia africana].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian reg gully communities
description: Communities of water drainage channels transecting regs of hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, characteristic of the drier parts, where sand-filled gullies of bare regs support, notably in northeastern African pebble regs, sparse [Haloxylon salicornicum] stands on shallow deposits or formations with [Lasiurus hirsutus], [Panicum turgidum], [Zilla spinosa] on deeper sands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian unvegetated regs
description: Large unvegetated regs of the Saharo-Arabian desert zone, characteristic of gravel deserts with a surface so compacted that roots cannot penetrate, prominent in areas where rainfall is very low, less than 20 mm per year, and episodic, with many consecutive rainless years, occupying extensive surfaces, in particular, in the eastern Sahara.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian hamadas
description: Stone- or pavement-covered plateau-tops and rocky slopes of hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, where all fine products of weathering are swept away by the wind; included are Cretaceous and Tertiary stone pavements, very extensive in the Sahara. Accumulations of salts or gypsum may form in the layer beneath the surface stones, which are often varnished with blackish deposits of iron or magnesium compounds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian hamada communities
description: Often exiguous, but relatively species-rich, communities occupying the tops, flanks and rock crevices of hamadas and rocky slopes of hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, usally able to survive only in moisture-retaining depressions or rock fissures, or on steep rocky slopes deeply incised by drainage channels. Characteristic species include, in particular, [Forsskalea tenacissima], [Asteriscus graveolens], [Salvia aegyptiaca], [Farsetia aegyptiaca], [Reseda villosa], [Fagaria latifolia], [Enneapogon scaber], [Enneapogon desvoxii] ([Enneapogon brachystachya]), [Anastatica hierochuntica] in the northern northwestern, western and central Sahara, [Moricandia arvensis], [Cymbopogon schoenanthus], [Fagonia microphylla], [Haloxylon scoparium] in the northern Sahara, [Limoniastrum feei], [Pituranthos battandieri] in the northwestern Sahara.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian hamada top communities
description: Communities of the hamada floor of plateau tops of hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, in particular, northwestern Saharan communities of dense rounded cushions of [Fredolia aretioides] ([Anabasis aretioides]), up to 50 cm high, scattered alone across extensive plateau surfaces, or with, notably, [Limoniastrum feei], [Pituranthos battandieri].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian hamada flank and crevice communities
description: Communities of the flanks and rock crevices of hamadas of hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula, in particular, perennial communities of the rock flanks of unvegetated hamadas of the central Sahara, with [Anabasis articulata], [Aerva persica] and grasses including [Aristida spp.], [Stipagrostis spp.], [Enneapogon spp.], or communities of chasmophytes, including [Erodium glaucophyllum], [Reaumuria hirtella], [Helianthemum kahiricum], [Fagonia mollis], growing in crevices of rocks, sometimes lichen-covered, of the otherwise usually unvegetated Egyptian Desert hamadas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian unvegetated hamadas
description: Large hamada surfaces or rocky slopes of the Saharo-Arabian desert zone with no vascular plant life, in situations of insufficient moisture or relatively high salt content, prominent in areas where rainfall is very low.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian wadis
description: Usually dry valleys or stream courses of the Saharo-Arabian region, carrying water only during rare heavy rainfall, often retaining groundwater near enough to be reached by plant species. Wadis are the only desert habitat, apart from oases, occupied by trees or large shrubs, including, in particular, [Tamarix spp.] communities (unit 44.815) and [Acacia spp.] communities (unit 4B.3).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharomontane communities
description: Diverse woodlands, grasslands, [Erica arborea] or dwarf-shrub communities of high mountains, above about 1800 metres, of the Saharo-Arabian region, with a higher rainfall than that of surrounding lowlands, species-rich and often harbouring endemic species. Except in the most favoured locations or during periods of good rainfall, communities are often restricted to wadis.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saharo-Arabian halogypsophilous communities
description: Communities colonizing saline and gypseous evaporation soils of the hot deserts and semideserts of North Africa, the Sinai peninsula, Southern Mesopotamia and the Arabian peninsula.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Turanian hot deserts and semideserts
description: Hot deserts and semideserts of the Near East and northern Mesopotamia, within the Irano-Turanian floristic domaine; they include the Syrian Desert and the Northern Mesopotamian Desert.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sudano-Sindian hot deserts and semideserts
description: Hot deserts and semideserts of the southern Sahara, the Red Sea coastlands, the southern Arabian peninsula, the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman coastlands, within the Sub-Sudanian and Sudanian floristic domaines. On the southern fringes of the Sahara, their northern limit, separating them from the deserts of unit 73.1, is most conveniently situated at the transition between hyperarid regions with episodal, prevailingly winter, rains and arid regions with prevailing summer rains; they are thus limited, within the Palaearctic region, as here defined, to southern Mauritania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Coastal deserts
description: Deserts of the west coasts of continents, under the influence of cold ocean currents, mostly within subtropical or tropical regions, almost without measurable rainfall but with high relative humidity in the form of fogs and mists. Within the Palaearctic region, communities of the extreme western Sahara, between Saguia el Hamra, at the southern limit of the mediterraneo-Saharan succulent shrublands of unit 32.89, and the northern limit of the Sahel, are referable to this unit.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Agricultural land and artificial landscapes
description: Cultivated or built-up areas under the overwhelming influence of human activity; the natural vegetation cover has been totally replaced as a result of agricultural practices, urbanization or industrialization. A natural flora and fauna subsists mainly in areas of extensive and traditional cultivation and dwelling. Wild plants may grow among crops, in hedges, along roads, on walls and in fallow fields. Many animals have, during the course of the past few thousand years, adapted to these man-created habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Improved grasslands
description: Land occupied by heavily fertilized or reseeded permanent grasslands, sometimes treated by selective herbicides, with very impoverished flora and fauna, used for grazing, soil protection and stabilization, landscaping or recreation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dry improved grasslands
description: Dry or mesophile intensive pastures and grasslands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Humid improved grasslands
description: Humid intensive pastures, often scored with drainage ditches, and capable of harbouring breeding waders or wintering waterfowl, in particular, geese.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Cropland
description: Arable fields planted for annually or regularly harvested crops other than those that carry phanerophytic trees or shrubs. They include fields of cereals and other graminaceous plants, of sunflowers and other oil seed plants, of beets, legumes, fodder, potatoes and other forbs. If a tree layer is present, it can be indicated by simultaneous use of a code of 83 or 84 with the present one. Croplands comprise intensively cultivated fields, planted with native or exotic species or cultivars, involving moderate to high chemical or organic fertilization and/or systematic use of pesticides, with complete ground occupation, as well as traditionally and extensively cultivated crops, with little or no chemical or organic fertilization, generally without the use of pesticides. Faunal and floral quality and diversity depend on the intensity of agricultural use and on the presence of borders of natural vegetation between fields.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Unbroken intensive cropland
description: Intensive cultivation, involving moderate to high chemical or organic fertilization and/or systematic use of pesticides, with complete ground occupation on dry land.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Field crops
description: Cereal and other crops grown on large, unbroken surfaces in open field landscapes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Market gardens and horticulture
description: Intensive cultivation of vegetables, flowers, small fruits, usually in alternating strips of different crops.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Field margin cropland
description: Intensively treated crops interspersed with strips of spontaneous vegetation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Extensive cultivation
description: Traditionally and extensively cultivated crops, in particular, of cereals, harbouring a rich and threatened flora of field weeds including [Agrostemma githago], [Centaurea cyanus], [Legousia speculum-veneris], [Chrysanthemum segetum], [Calendula arvensis], [Adonis spp.], [Consolida spp.], [Delphinium spp.], [Nigella spp.], [Papaver spp.]; their varied range of associations can be indicated by subdivisions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Flooded crops
description: Rice fields and other inundated or inundatable croplands.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rice fields
description: Inundated or inundatable fields used for the cultivation of rice ([Oryza sativa]). When not too heavily treated, they may provide substitution habitats for some wetland faunal elements, in particular, birds, including ducks, rails, herons and icterids.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Watercress beds
description: Inundated or inundatable fields used for the cultivation of forbs, in particular, watercress, [Nasturtium officinale] ([Rorippa nasturtium-aquaticum]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Orchards, groves and tree plantations
description: Ligneous crops. Extensive orchards and old plantations may support a rich flora and fauna; it is in particular the case of ancient olive groves and old poplar plantations with tall herb undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: High-stem orchards
description: Stands of trees cultivated for fruit or flower production, with an avocation of permanent tree cover once mature.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Olive groves
description: Mediterranean formations of [Olea europaea] var. [europaea].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Traditional olive groves
description: Ancient olive groves, often made of very old trees shading herbaceous layer, extensively treated. Greek olive groves are an important habitat of the very restricted sylviid [Hippolais olivetorum], as well as of many orchids.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intensive olive groves
description: Intensively treated or young olive groves.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Chestnut groves
description: Land planted in broad-leaved winter-deciduous chestnuts ([Castanea]), of sub-Mediterranean affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Walnut groves
description: Land planted in broad-leaved winter-deciduous walnuts ([Juglans]), of temperate affinities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Almond groves
description: Land planted in broad-leaved winter-deciduous almond trees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fruit orchards
description: High-stem orchards of apple, pear, plum, apricot, peach, cherry and other Rosaceae.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Northern fruit orchards
description: High-stem orchards of apple, pear, cherry of temperate Europe, often extensively treated.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Southern fruit orchards
description: Thermophilous Mediterranean and sub-Mediterranean fleshy-fruit Rosaceae orchards, usually intensively treated.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Citrus orchards
description: Land planted in broad-leaved evergreen citrus trees.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Palm groves
description: Formations dominated by planted or introduced palms, in particular, date palm ([Phoenix dactylifera]).
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other orchards
description: Land planted in deciduous or evergeen trees, other than those of units 83.11 to 83.16, cultivated for fruit, leaves or flowers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other deciduous orchards
description: Land planted in deciduous trees, other than those of units 83.12, 83.13, 83.14, 83.15, cultivated for fruit, leaves or flowers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other evergreen orchards
description: Land planted in evergeen trees, other than those of units 83.11, 83.16, 83.17, cultivated for fruit, leaves or flowers.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shrub orchards and plantations
description: Plantations of dwarf trees, shrubs, espaliers or perennial ligneous climbers, mostly cultivated for fruit or flower production, with an avocation of permanent shrubby cover, or else for wood or small tree production, with a regular whole-plant harvesting regime.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Vineyards
description: Plantations of vine.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Traditional vineyards
description: Vineyards that have preserved their characteristic accompanying flora, generally lightly treated.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Intensive vineyards
description: Vineyards usually cleared of their herb layer, intensively treated.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fruit, flower and wood shrub crops
description: Plantations of dwarf trees, shrubs, espaliers or perennial ligneous climbers other than vineyards and tea plantations, as well as young stages of units 83.23 and 83.21.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shrub and low-stem tree orchards
description: Plantations of dwarf trees, shrubs, espaliers or perennial ligneous climbers, other than vineyards and tea plantations, cultivated for fruit or flower production, with an avocation of permanent shrubby cover. They include, among others, espaliers of various Rosaceae plantations and berry shrub patches.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shrub and dwarf tree plantations
description: Plantations of dwarf trees or shrubs cultivated for wood or small tree production, with a regular whole-plant harvesting regime, including, among others, osier beds, Christmas tree crops, horticultural nurseries. Young stages of units 83.23 and 83.21.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tea plantations
description: Plantations of [Camellia sinensis], widespread in southeastern mainland China, Formosa, on Formosa, southern Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu, more limited elsewhere in the Palaearctic, in particular, in the eastern Pontic range of Turkey, in the Caucasian periphery of Russia, Georgia and Azerbaijan, in northern Iran, in the Azores on Sao Miguel.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tall tree plantations
description: Cultivated tree formations planted most often for the production of wood, composed of exotic species or of native species out of their natural range and habitat. Early stages of such plantations are listed in unit 83.2.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Conifer plantations
description: Cultivated ligneous formations of exotic conifers or of native conifers out of their natural range and habitat.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Native conifer plantations
description: Plantations of Palaearctic conifers within their broad biogeographical area of occurrence, but outside of the conditions described under "reforestation" in the relevant subdivisions of unit 42.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Native fir, spruce, larch, cedar plantations
description: Plantations of Palaearctic conifers of genera [Abies], [Picea], [Larix] or [Cedrus] within their broad biogeographical area of occurrence, but outside of the conditions described under "reforestation" in the relevant subdivisions of unit 42.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Native pine plantations
description: Plantations of Palaearctic conifers of genus [Pinus] within their broad biogeographical area of occurrence, but outside of the conditions described under "reforestation" in the relevant subdivisions of unit 42.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Native cypress, juniper, yew plantations
description: Plantations of Palaearctic conifers of genera [Cupressus], [Juniperus], [Taxus] within their broad biogeographical area of occurrence, but outside of the conditions described under "reforestation" in the relevant subdivisions of unit 42.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Exotic conifer plantations
description: Plantations of non-Palaearctic species of conifers or of Palaearctic species outside of their broad biogeographical region of occurrence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Exotic spruce, fir, larch, douglas fir, deodar plantations
description: Plantations of conifers of genera [Abies], [Picea], [Larix], [Pseudotsuga] or [Cedrus] formed of non-Palaearctic species or of Palaearctic species outside of their broad biogeographical region of occurrence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Exotic pine plantations
description: Plantations of conifers of genus [Pinus] formed of non-Palaearctic species, or of Palaearctic species outside of their broad biogeographical region of occurrence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other exotic conifer plantations
description: Plantations of conifers of genera other than [Pinus], [Abies], [Picea], [Larix], [Pseudotsuga] or [Cedrus], formed of non-Palaearctic species or of Palaearctic species outside of their broad biogeographical region of occurrence.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Plantations of broad-leaved trees
description: Cultivated evergreen or deciduous broad-leaved tree formations planted for the production of wood, composed of exotic species, of native species out of their natural range, or of native species planted in artificial conditions with a considerably modified accompanying cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Poplar plantations
description: Plantations of species, hybrids or cultivars of the deciduous genus [Populus], in particular, [Populus nigra], [Populus nigra] cv. [italica], [Populus deltoides], [Populus xcanadensis], [Populus balsamifera], [Populus trichocarpa], [Populus candicans].
