source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Poplar plantations with megaphorb herb layer
description: Old poplar plantations with a tall herb-rich undergrowth, substitution habitat for some riparian forest species of plants and animals.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other poplar plantations
description: Poplar plantations devoid of tall herb-rich undergrowth.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eucalyptus plantations
description: Plantations of trees of the Australian genus [Eucalyptus], in particular, [Eucalyptus globulus], [Eucalyptus camaldulensis], [Eucalyptus cladocalyx], [Eucalyptus delegatensis], [Eucalyptus nitens], [Eucalyptus radiata], [Eucalyptus astringens], [Eucalyptus bicostata], [Eucalyptus brockwayi], [Eucalyptus regnans], [Eucalyptus gomphocephala], [Eucalyptus grandis], [Eucalyptus maidenii], [Eucalyptus cornuta], [Eucalyptus fastigata], [Eucalyptus pauciflora], [Eucalyptus viminalis]. These plantations offer little support for indigenous biological diversity and constitute biological deserts as far as the fauna is concerned.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Exotic oak plantations
description: Cultivated formations of deciduous trees of genus [Quercus] planted most often for the production of wood, composed of exotic species or of Palaeartic species out of their natural range.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Locust tree plantations
description: Plantations and spontaneous formations of [Robinia pseudacacia].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other broad-leaved tree plantations
description: Cultivated evergreen or deciduous broad-leaved formations of trees of genera other than [Populus], [Eucalyptus], [Quercus] and [Robinia], planted for the production of wood, composed of exotic species, of native species out of their natural range, or of native species planted in artificial conditions with a considerably modified accompanying cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Broad-leaved deciduous tree plantations
description: Cultivated deciduous broad-leaved formations of trees of genera other than [Populus], [Quercus] and [Robinia], planted for the production of wood, composed of exotic species, of native species out of their natural range, or of native species planted in artificial conditions with a considerably modified accompanying cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Broad-leaved evergreen tree plantations
description: Cultivated evergreen broad-leaved formations of trees of genera other than [Eucalyptus] planted for the production of wood, composed of exotic species, of native species out of their natural range, or of native species planted in artificial conditions with a considerably modified accompanying cortŠge.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tree lines, hedges, rural mosaics
description: Ligneous formations of small size, arranged in a linear, reticulated or insular manner, closely interwoven with grassy or cultivated habitats. Also, combinations of such elements and mixed agricultural formations, containing both ligneous and herbaceous layers. Very artificial, disturbed or heterogeneous systems, containing many planted or exogenous elements can be listed here while more natural ensembles utilising many natural elements and covering substantial surfaces are better classified under section 9 (units 91 and 92). Landscapes in which pastures, crops and plantation elements are intimately mixed (equivalent to unit 92) can be described by use of the first three codes below (if useful, specified by codes from units 31.8, 41, 42 and 83) in conjunction with other codes from section 8 and other open habitat sections. Surfaces characterized by mixed agricultural formations, and in particular, those that combine ligneous and herbaceous elements on the same surfaces (equivalent to unit 91) can be designated by one of the codes 84.4 or 84.5 and their elements specified by use of other codes from section 8 or any other.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Tree lines
description: Tall ligneous formations arranged in a linear manner, planted mostly for shelter or shading.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hedgerows
description: Ligneous formations arranged in a linear or reticulated manner, closely interwoven with grassy or cultivated habitats, usually serving functions of partition and shelter, characteristically formed of trees and shrubs in temperate oceanic regions of the western seaboard of continents, notably in the western Palaearctic, of cacti in arid and semiarid regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small woodlots
description: Ligneous formations of small size, arranged in an insular manner within cultivated environments.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rural mosaics
description: Reticulated landscapes of tree-lines, hedgerows, plantations, woodlots, pastures and crops.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Shaded crops and pastures
description: Crops or pastures developed under orchards or other cultivated ligneous formations.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Urban parks and large gardens
description: Usually varied formations, created for recreational use. The vegetation, usually composed mainly of introduced species or cultivars, can nevertheless include many native plants and supports a varied fauna when not intensively managed. The heterogeneity of the habitat engenders a high faunal diversity with, however, a preponderance of common species. The frequent presence of old trees favors the installation of rarer specialists.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Large parks
description: Large, varied green spaces. Their constituting elements can be specified by use of the codes below.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Park woodlots
description: Copses, groves or woods of native or introduced trees, with or without accompanying shrubbery and herbaceous undergrowth, constituting elements of urban parks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Park lawns
description: Grasslands, usually mowed, composed of native or sometimes exotic grasses, constituting elements of urban parks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Park basins
description: Bodies of water, including basins or more natural ponds or lakes, constituting elements of urban parks. Seminatural communities that might colonize them can be indicated by use of codes from sections 11, 15, 22, 23, 24 or 53.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Park flower beds, arbors and shrubbery
description: Plantations of ornamental forbs or shrubs constituting elements of urban parks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Park sub-natural communities
description: Elements of sub-natural communities enclaved in parks or colonizing their elements; codes from sections other than 8 are to be used to specify their nature.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Small parks and city squares
description: Small public urban green spaces usually with a simplified structure and suitable for only a very impoverished representation of rural faunas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gardens
description: Areas of land planted with ornamental or food-crop vegetation, and adjoining a dwelling.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ornamental gardens
description: Areas of land adjoining a house, planted with ornamental grass, shrubs, trees, flower beds.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Subsistance gardens
description: Areas of land used for the cultivation of fruit, vegetables, fruit trees or other domestic crops in the immediate vicinity of a dwelling.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: City block inner spaces
description: Complexes of gardens or other green spaces, often partitioned by walls, located inside city blocks and completely or almost completely surrounded by continuous architectural structures.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Towns, villages, industrial sites
description: Areas used for human occupation and industrial activities. A considerable fauna has adapted to buildings. Birds such as [Apus apus], [Tyto alba] and [Hirundo rustica] nest nearly exclusively in them, using mostly structures with traditional architecture. Other species, of montane rocky habitats, such as [Phoenicurus ochruros], have colonized lowlands in villages and towns. Bats roost in buildings. Rock plants colonize old walls and roofs.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Towns
description: Densely populated settlements integrated within a built-up ensemble of medium to large size, with limited access to surrounding rural areas.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Urban centers
description: Areas situated around the center or the subcenters of a town, characterized by continuous or nearly continuous spatial occupation by buildings destined for habitation or circadian occupation periods.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Suburban areas
description: Areas situated at the periphery of a town, characterized by relatively low density and strongly discontinuous spatial occupation by buildings.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Town features
description: Relatively large, outstanding structures incorporated within a town ensemble, characterized by a relatively low intensity of spatial or temporal human presence, such as religious edifices and monuments.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Town ruins and construction sites
description: Structures and spaces incorporated within a town ensemble, characterized by very low intensity of spatial or temporal human presence, such as ruins, abandoned buildings and construction sites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Villages
description: Small groups of houses in rural areas, susceptible to strong interconnection between usages by the fauna of the built-up and countryside habitats.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Village cores
description: Areas situated around the center of a village, characterized by continuous or nearly continuous spatial occupation by buildings.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Village peripheries
description: Areas situated at the near periphery of a village, with relatively low density and strongly discontinuous spatial occupation by buildings.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Village features
description: Relatively large, outstanding structures incorporated within a village ensemble, including its near periphery, characterized by a relatively low intensity of spatial or temporal human presence, such as religious edifices, monuments.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Village ruins and construction sites
description: Structures and spaces incorporated within a village ensemble, including its near periphery, characterized by very low intensity of spatial or temporal human presence, such as ruins, abandoned buildings and construction sites.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Active industrial sites
description: Areas built-up for the purpose of large-scale or relatively large-scale  industrial activities, including agro-industry and intensive stock raising, and presently in operation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Active extraction sites
description: Areas used for open-sky mining and quarrying activities and presently in operation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Active industrial constructions
description: Areas built-up for the purpose of industrial activities and presently in operation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Old industrial sites and open spaces
description: Abandoned industrial sites, open areas and byproducts of industrial activities susceptible of colonisation by seminatural communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Abandoned quarries
description: Permanently or temporarily unworked sites or parts of sites of open-sky extractive activities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sand, clay and kaolin quarries
description: Permanently or temporarily unworked sites or parts of sites of open-sky soft material extraction, often significant as reproduction sites of burrowing species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Gravel quarries
description: Permanently or temporarily unworked sites or parts of sites of open-sky pebble extraction.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Hard stone quarries
description: Permanently or temporarily unworked sites or parts of sites of open-sky hard material extraction, sometimes significant as reproduction or forraging sites of rupicolous species.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Slag heaps and other detritus heaps
description: Features of relief formed by byproducts of industrial activities, susceptible of colonisation by seminatural communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Marginal and disused industrial sites
description: Disused sites of industrial activities, including transportation, social recreation, waste dumping, as well as marginal and interstitial spaces developed within or alongside areas still used for such activities, susceptible of colonisation by seminatural communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Transport network margins and disused sites
description: Margins and interstitial spaces of transport infrastructures, including highways and their margins, railroad tracksides, switch yards and maintenance areas, airport runways, aprons and adjacent grounds, portside service areas, as well as disused surfaces of such infrastructures, susceptible of colonisation by seminatural communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Recreation area margins and disused sites
description: Margins and interstitial spaces of surfaces used for recreational activities, including sports playing fields, tracks for athletic events, horse and car racing, playgrounds, amusement parks, military exercise grounds, as well as disused areas of such surfaces, susceptible of colonisation by seminatural communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rubble and detritus tips
description: Sites where wasteproducts of human activity are dumped, including household, agricultural, nonmineral industrial and construction wastes, susceptible of colonisation by seminatural communities. Large landscape-shaping features holding industrial wastes are excluded and included in unit 86.42.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Disused industrial constructions
description: Areas built-up with superstructures for the purpose of industrial activities, presently inactive, susceptible of colonisation by seminatural communities.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Rural scattered constructions
description: Structures dispersed within the rural or natural environment established for the purpose of agricultural activities, permanent or temporary residences, small-scale commercial, artisanal or industrial activities, recreation, research, environmental protection. They include isolated greenhouses, animal shelters, harvest-drying structures, sheds and huts, field and pasture enclosures. High concentration batteries of such constructions are excluded and considered industrial structures listed in unit 86.32.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Archeological sites
description: Sites of former human activity, containing ruins of greater or lesser spatial coverage and vertical profile.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fallow land, waste places
description: Fields abandoned or left to rest, roadsides and other interstitial spaces on disturbed ground. They are colonised by numerous pioneering, introduced or nitrophilous plants. They sometimes provide habitats that can be used by animals of open spaces. Expanses occupied by colonies of forbs planted for purposes of soil protection, stabilization, fertilization or reclamation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fallow fields
description: Communities of segetal, pioneering, introduced or nitrophilous plants colonising fallow fields, disused farmland, vinyards, neglected flower beds and abandoned gardens of the Palaearctic region.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ruderal communities
description: Communities of pioneering, introduced or nitrophilous plants colonising waste places, disturbed natural or seminatural areas, roadsides and other interstitial spaces or disturbed ground within arctic, boreal, nemoral, mediterranean, steppic, desert or tropical regions of the Palaearctic.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Land reclamation forb fields
description: Expanses occupied by colonies of forbs, notably leguminous species, planted for purposes of soil protection, stabilization, fertilization or reclamation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Mines and underground passages
description: Artificial underground spaces. They may constitute important substitution habitats for cave-dwelling bats and for significant subterranean invertebrates such as crustaceans, planarians etc.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Industrial lagoons and reservoirs, canals
description: Very artificial aquatic habitats; seminatural communities that might colonize them can be indicated by use of codes from sections 11, 15, 22, 23, 24 or 53.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saline industrial lagoons and canals
description: Artificial watercourses and basins carrying saltwater or brackish water.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sea harbours
description: Seaside complexes of artificial basins and inlets constructed for the purposes of navigation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Saltworks
description: Active or recently abandoned salt-extraction evaporation basins. Detailed habitats can be specified by use of the subdivisions of 15 and 23 in conjunction with 89.12.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Other saline industrial lagoons and canals
description: Inland artificial saltwater bodies.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Fresh water industrial lagoons and canals
description: Artificial watercourses and basins carrying freshwater.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Navigable canals
description: Linear artificial freshwater bodies open to navigation.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ditches and small canals
description: Narrow linear artificial freshwater bodies, mostly used for irrigation or partition.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Industrial lagoons and ornemental ponds
description: Artificial freshwater basins used for the needs of navigation, industrial activities, recreation or ornamentation outside of city parks.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sewage farms and sewage works
description: Sewage treatment plants and their basins.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wooded grasslands and scrubs
description: Large ecosystems composed of a mosaic combination of woodland and grassland, of scattered trees growing within grass or shrub ecosystems, or of native trees shading surfaces transformed for grazing or cultivation, in which a stable equilibrium between the tree and grass or scrub formations is naturally or artificially maintained. They are characteristic of zonal ecotones, and of some regions where traditional extensive combined agro-pastoral methods are used. Their constituting elements can be specified by use of codes borrowed from sections 3 and 4, occasionally from section 8. Transition pre- and post-forest phases, covered in section 3, are excluded, as are very artificial rural mosaics included in section 8.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Parklands
description: Extensive surfaces characterized by mixed agro-pastoral formations, combining ligneous and herbaceous elements on the same surfaces.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Atlantic parkland
description: Extensive surfaces of Atlantic regions of nemoral Europe occupied by grassland dotted with widely planted trees, characteristic of the British Isles, where they are usually enclosed, used for cattle or deer grazing.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Dehesa
description: A characteristic landscape of the southwestern quadrant of the Iberian peninsula in which crops, pasture land or Mediterranean scrub, in juxtaposition or rotation, are shaded by a fairly closed to very open canapy of native oaks, [Quercus suber], [Quercus rotundifolia], [Quercus pyrenaica], [Quercus faginea]. It is an important habitat of raptors, including the threatened Iberian endemic eagle [Aquila adalberti], of the crane [Grus grus], of large insects and their predators and of the endangered felid [Lynx pardinus].
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Sub-continental parkland
description: Extensive surfaces of sub-continental regions of nemoral and steppe Europe occupied by grassland dotted with trees, characteristic, in particular, of Pannonic and peri-Pannonic regions.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Bocages
description: Reticulated landscapes of small linear, insular and semiinsular wooded habitats, tree-lines, hedgerows, closely interwoven with grassy or cultivated habitats. Also, combinations of such elements and mixed agricultural formations, containing both ligneous and herbaceous layers, characteristic of the British Isles, southern Fennoscandia, the Germano-Baltic plain, the northern piedmont of the Alps, western France, Galicia, Romania.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wooded steppe
description: Formations of the transition zone between forests and the middle Eurasian, Irano-Anatolian or Saharo-Mediterranean steppes, occurring in a vast swath extending from Pannonia to the Far East, south of and inland from the boreal and nemoral forest belts, in regions of reduced summer humidity, as well as in areas adjacent to, or under the influence of the Mediterranean and warm-temperate humid zones, represented by a macromosa‹c of steppe and connected, contiguous, disjunct or widely spaced woodland stands, the latter usually with a very developed grassy understorey, or by a scattering of trees within a steppe environment. The forest elements are often located on porous or slightly raised ground, valley sides or slopes, the grasslands occupying less well drained soils and lower places. Detailed habitats can be coded by combining subdivisions of prefixes of 4 and 3 with the relevant geographical or physiographic subdivisions of 93.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pannonic wooded steppes
description: Wooded steppes of the Pannonic plain and surrounding basins and hills, north to southern Moravia and Southern Slovakia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Ponto-Sarmatic wooded steppes
description: Wooded steppes of the plain of the western Black Sea, west of the Dniester, of its associated basins, including those of the lower Danube, of Transylvania and of northern Thrace, of the southern edge and valleys of the Podolian plateau, of the Central Russian plateau, of the Volga plateau, of Orenburg and of Bachkiria, forming a broad ecotonal belt between the western Palaearctic nemoral forests and the Ponto-Sarmatic steppes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Pre-Euxinian wooded steppes
description: Wooded steppes of northern Crimea and the northern piedmont of the Caucasus, forming the transition between the Ponto-Sarmatic steppes and the mediterranean or Euxino-Hyrcanian forests of Crimea and the Caucasus.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Western Siberian aspen-birch parkland
description: Wooded steppes of western Siberia, extending from the Urals to the Kusnezk-Alatau, in the transition zone between taiga and central Asian eastern Transvolgo-Kazakh steppes, including the Kourgan, Ichim, Koulounda, Baraba, Barnaul steppes. The forest element is constituted by woods of [Populus tremula], [Betula pendula] and [Betula pubescens], the steppe element is a [Stipa joannis]-[Stipa stenophylla]-[Helictotrichon desertorum] steppe.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Siberian larch parkland
description: Parkland landscape developed around the foothills of the Altai system, with groves of [Larix sibirica] and [Pinus sylvestris], in the zone of transition between Altai taiga and East Asian steppes of Transbaikalia and Outer Mongolia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Irano-Anatolian wooded steppes
description: Wooded steppes of the Anatolian Plateau, of Transcaucasia, of the Iranian Plateau and of northern Mesopotamia.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Khangai-Daourian wooded steppes
description: Montane wooded steppes of the Khangai-Daourian regions of southern Siberia and northern Mongolia, with [Larix sibirica] and [Pinus sibirica], developed in a transition zone between taiga and the western, Transbaikalian and Mongolian, segment of east Asian steppes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Eastern Asian wooded steppes
description: Wooded steppes of the Songarian depression, the southern Hingan mountains and the Schensi-Kansu loess plateaux, developed in the transition zone between taiga and Far-Eastern forests and the eastern section of east Asian steppes.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wooded tundra
description: Formations of the transition zone between taiga and tundra, characterized by a scattering of stunted coniferous trees or deciduous shrubs within a tundra environment, or by a macromosa‹c of tundra with scattered islands of forest, or by forest with scattered treeless tundra patches. They occur in a broad belt, up to several hundreds of kilometers wide, across the north of the Eurasian continent and in a narrow ecotone in Siberian mountains. Detailed habitats can be coded by combining subdivisions of prefixes 39 and 4 with the relevant physiographic subdivisions of 94.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Treeline ecotones
description: Formations of the timberline, or combat zone (Kampfzone, zone de combat) of mountains, in which subalpine forests give way to alpine or boreal heaths and scrubs, to alpine grasslands, or to tropical alpine communities; they are characterized by a scattering of stunted, gnarled trees punctuating an alpine shrub or grassland environment, by a macromosa‹c of alpine shrub and grass formations with scattered islands of forest, or by open or clear forest with an undergrowth composed of alpine elements such as ericaceous shrubs. They occupy a narrow belt, varying in altitudinal location according to latitude, exposure and other climatic or edaphic conditions.  Detailed habitats can be coded by combining subdivisions of prefixes 31, 36, 37, 3C, 41, 42, 43 or 49 with the relevant physiographic subdivisions of 95.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Savannas
description: Formations transitional between tropical grassland and dry tropical woodland or, sometimes, tropical forests, including both homogeneous surfaces of grassland with a more or less even, more or less dense, scattering of trees or tall shrubs, and macromosa‹cs of grasslands and isolated or connected stands of woodland. The grasslands involved may be savanna grasslands, tropical seasonally flooded grasslands, tropical permanently flooded grasslands or tropical steppes, the woodlands are usually dry tropical woodlands (dry forest, bushland, scrub forest, scrub woodland), sometimes fragments of monsoon forest, rain forest or tropical swamp forest. Savannas are limited within the Palaearctic, as here defined, to the Sahelian zone of Mauritania, to the southern fringe of the Saharo-Sindian zone, and to tropical China.
source: Devillers, P., Devillers-Terschuren, J. & Vander Linden, C., 2001. PHYSIS Palaearctic Habitat Classification, updated to 10 December 2001 (IRSNB); table TYPO_PAL_PHYSIS_2001, SPN-MNHN / INPN 2010

name: Wooded deserts and semideserts
description: Formations of the subtropical desert zones resulting from the colonisation by dry tropical woodland trees of shrubby or grassy semidesert or desert communities. Included are desert savannas, pseudosteppes and sand-dune open woodlands.
